History(歷史) is the continuation of life(生命) exerted by a subject(主體) that exists only once, so there can be no correct vitality(生命力) in a history(歷史) where another nationality(民族) has lived or where the subject(主體) itself could not take responsibility for the history(歷史).

In this regard, our history(歷史), which has been preserved solely by our Korean people(韓民族) as the legitimate subject(正統主體) for half a millennium, must have the most radiant and distinct vitality(活力) of subjectivity(主體性) than any other national history(民族史) in the world(世界).

## 2. The Context of Victory(勝利) of Subjectivity(主體性) in the Field(現場) of History(歷史)
The context of the subjectivity(主體性) that we have maintained has been too arduous and painful for thousands of years. Therefore, the field(現場) of subjectivity(主體性) that we must seek was nothing but a continuous and dreadful historical ordeal.

In our history(歷史), it meant the painful national crisis(國難) that the subject of nationality(民族) had experienced, but outside of history(歷史), it was a terrifying challenge to seize the subject(主體) of this country's history(歷史).

Whether it was a national crisis(國難) or a challenge(挑戰), it was all a historical wound(傷處) to our subjectivity(主體性), and the wounds recorded in history(歷史) alone amount to 931 times.

*   Ancient times(上古時代): 11 times (based on Chinese(中國) records only)
*   The Three Kingdoms(三國) and Unified Silla(統一新羅) periods: 143 times (110 times from the continent(大陸), 33 times from the sea(海洋))
*   The Goryeo(高麗) period: 417 times (125 times from the continent(大陸), 292 times from the sea(海洋))


--- (p. 45) ---

# The Joseon Dynasty (朝鮮朝) Era: 360 Incidents (360回) (360회) (360 Incidents on the Continent: 192 Incidents (192回), 168 Incidents (168回) at Sea)

Among these 931 incidents (931回) of national crisis (國難), the Mongol (蒙古) invasion lasted a total of 40 years, the Khitan (契丹) invasion lasted 27 years, and the Japanese (倭) invasion lasted over 20 years. Even just the Imjin War (壬亂) alone lasted a full 7 years. Therefore, the total time (總時間) of challenge (挑戰) that the 931 incidents (931回) of national crisis (國難) actually trampled upon this country's history (歷史) was not 931 years, but rather over a thousand years.

On the roughly 4,000-year history (歷史), a history (歷史) of suffering (受難) that exceeds a thousand years, this is a sad tale that our nation's history (民族史) was stained with the wounds of subjectivity (主體性) for more than a quarter of its existence. It is also a sorrowful and pitiful scene that our Korean people (韓民族) had to fight against national crises (國難) without exception every four years on the stage of history (歷史).

It is difficult to find such a painful national history (民族史) in world history (世界史). However, even in the face of such a tragic national history (民族史), there is one great conclusion (結論) that only we can clearly make. That is the great conclusion (結論) of the victory (勝利) of subjectivity (主體性), that we have never failed to overcome and defeat all 931 incidents (931回) of national crisis (國難) that have been imposed upon our history (歷史).

Nations (民族) have suffered endlessly before national crises (國難), but in the history (歷史) of victory (勝利) after overcoming those crises (國難), great vitality (生命力) always emerges. Therefore, nations (民族) that have not experienced such bitter national crises (國難) cannot confirm such a context (脈絡) of subjectivity (主體性), and nations (民族) that have faced such crises (國難) but ultimately failed to overcome them cannot confirm such a context (脈絡) of subjectivity (主體性).

Now, we need to return to the scenes (現場) of the national crises (國難) of our painful national history (民族史) to find the consistent context (脈絡) of our subjectivity (主體性).

In the 7th century AD, the invasion by Yangdi (楊帝) of the Sui Dynasty (隋) involved a direct combat force (戰鬪部隊) of 1.13 million infantry and cavalry alone, with a follow-up reserve force (豫備兵力) of over 2 million, which was double that number. Adding the 100,000 naval forces (水兵) that crossed the sea, the total force (兵力) exceeded 3 million.

Goguryeo (高句麗), which had to fight against such an unprecedented force (未曾有) in history (歷史), had a total population that did not even reach 2 million, let alone 3 million.

If this national crisis (國難) involved a small country like Goguryeo (高句麗), with a total population of only 1.8 million, having to face a powerful continental nation (大陸) like the Sui Dynasty (隋), with hundreds of millions of physical invaders (強國), who would


--- (p. 46) ---

It was already clear what the conclusion would be.
History shows that the small country of Goguryeo, with a population of only 1.8 million, defeated the Sui Dynasty, which had an invading force of over millions, three times in a row. This was the great victory of General Eulji Mundeok at the Battle of Salsu, where he repelled the last 300,000-strong detachment of the Sui Dynasty with just 30,000 troops. Here, we can clearly see the nation's victory in the face of immense national crisis.
The historical scene then turns to the 40-year-long struggle against the Mongols in the 13th century. The Mongols, known today as the strongest life form in the world, invaded this small land of Goguryeo for 40 years. The bitterness of this national crisis is beyond description.
However, here we must also clearly recognize the context of our subjectivity. In short, when the Mongols from the north swept across Asia, including our Joseon, in the 13th century, there were indeed many nations stronger than us and many great powers larger than our country. But it is important to note that among those Asian powers and great nations that were supposedly stronger than us, not a single one resisted the Mongols for even four years.
In the face of such a terrifying Mongol invasion, it was only this small country of Joseon in the East that fought for 40 years, demonstrating a historic power in defending the subject of history.
Therefore, we should not only feel and worry about the bitter scene of our land being trampled for 40 years by the Mongols in the 40-year struggle against them. Instead, we should seek out the traces of that tearfully great struggle, where we alone fought for 40 years while no other Asian power resisted for even four years, and thereby strengthen our subjectivity.
In short, this means that in the history of Asia at that time, the autonomous strength demonstrated by our Korean people was superior and greater than that of any other power or great nation.
However, even in the context of this great national history, among the 931 national crises,


--- (p. 47) ---

# Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong

There was once a tragic severance we had to endure because we failed to overcome it ourselves. This was the humiliating national crisis of the Manchu Invasion (병자호란) when our King Injo (인조) had to kneel down after 40 days of resistance at Namhansanseong (南漢山城) and submit a surrender document (降伏文書) to the Qing (淸) Dynasty's 200,000 troops.

On January 30, 1637 (丁丑), the gates of Namhansanseong (南漢山城), our last stronghold defended since the previous December, were opened, and King Injo descended to perform the ritual of three kneels and nine prostrations (三跪九叩頭) before the Qing Taizong (清太宗), presenting the surrender document (降伏文書). Our national history (民族史) suffered a humiliating blow to its subjectivity (主體性), an experience unprecedented in our 5,000-year history.

To this day, despite examining our history (歷史) for the past 300 years and scrutinizing the Manchus' history (歷史), we have found no record of retrieving or receiving back the surrender document (降伏文書) we submitted to the Qing (淸) Dynasty in the year of Dingchou (丁丑). We have genuinely failed to retrieve that document and have not found it until this moment.

What does this historical (歷史的) fact signify? It reveals a sorrowful and painful unresolved (未解決) grievance (恨) in our national history (民族史): the historical (歷史的) wound inflicted by submitting the surrender document (降伏文書) to the Qing (淸) Dynasty, a wound to our national subjectivity (主體性) that remains unresolved.

When a nation bears such a wound to its subjectivity (主體性), the pain endured by the people persists eternally, and the historical (歷史的) constraints imposed upon us limit the vitality (活力) of our nation endlessly.

Here, we face a double burden: the incomplete liberation (光復) from the humiliation inflicted by Japanese imperialism (日本帝國主義) just 50 years ago, and the unresolved historical (歷史的) wound from the surrender document (降伏文書) submitted to the Qing (淸) Dynasty 300 years ago. This double burden weighs heavily upon us today.

Yet, there is one clear conclusion: the Manchus, who once held our surrender document (降伏文書) and boasted before us, no longer exist on this Earth (地球).


--- (p. 48) ---

Although we, the Korean people, had to endure the agony of presenting a surrender document to them, the fact that we are now thriving as the main actors of history proves that we ultimately triumphed over the Manchus. This is a clear national victory. Therefore, we are now confirming this persistent victory, achieved 300 years later, over the Manchus.

Among the 931 national crises in our 5,000-year history, we had only failed to overcome one—the Manchu invasions of 1627 and 1636 (병자호란(丙子胡亂)). If we can now confirm this victory even over that crisis, our national history would mean that we have overcome all 931 national crises. This is where the true potential of our great historical subjectivity lies.

### 3. Overcoming National Crises and a New Global Perspective

The total force that a particular history can exert is the ultimate value and absolute conclusion that can be drawn from all histories. Therefore, our Goguryeo's victory over the powerful Sui Dynasty 1,300 years ago was because the total force of history that Goguryeo could muster was greater than that of the Sui Dynasty. Similarly, when the Mongol invasions occurred, while no other strong or great powers in Asia could resist for more than four years, only our Joseon Dynasty fought for 40 years and ultimately prevailed. This was because the total force of history that our Goguryeo could muster was greater than that of the other strong or great powers in Asia at the time.

In this context, we should not only be captivated by the glory of victory in the Battle of Salsu (薩水大捷) 1,300 years ago, where our small Goguryeo mysteriously defeated the powerful Sui Dynasty. We must take one more step forward and confirm the great power of our national history: that Goguryeo's total force of history was clearly superior to that of the Sui Dynasty at the time. Viewed in this light, the Manchus, who had even taken a surrender document from us 300 years ago, have disappeared without a trace. Meanwhile, we are now thriving and have become the victors.


--- (p. 49) ---

# Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

It also becomes clear that the total historical impact of the Manchus over 300 years was less than that of the Korean people (韓民族) over the same period. How could a small country like Goguryeo (高句麗), with a total population (總人口) of only 1.8 million, produce a greater historical impact than a powerful nation like the Sui Dynasty (隋), whose invading armies (侵略軍) numbered in the millions?

Here lies the final essence (要諦) of our subjectivity (主體性). It is the final active element (活力要素) in history (歷史), the +α factor (要因) that distinguishes our historical legacy. While the outward appearance (外觀) and physical dimension (物理的次元) of history may not be immediately apparent, the essential (本質的) foundation (根本) of history's composition (構成) and driving force (原動力) lies in the spiritual element (精神要素) +α of our total historical impact (歷史的總量). This is why Goguryeo (高句麗) was able to defeat the Sui Dynasty (隋).

Although the Sui Dynasty (隋) appeared physically stronger (物理的) in terms of national power (國力), the historical conclusion (歷史的結論) is clear: Goguryeo's (高句麗) total historical impact (歷史的總量) was greater. This conclusion is based on the superior (優越) historical +α factor (歷史的+α要因) that Goguryeo (高句麗) possessed at that time.

What, then, is the essence (本質) of our historical spiritual factor (歷史的精神要因) that has always allowed us to surpass our challengers (挑戰者) and triumph over national crises (國難)? It is the most precious subjectivity (主體性) that we must inherit here. Our subjectivity (主體性) is the spiritual element (精神要素) of history (歷史) that has always made us victors (勝利者) in the face of adversity (困難). It is the creative spirit (創造) and belief (信念) that connects us to our national vitality (民族生命力) today.

History (歷史) never allows others to live for us. Here, subjectivity (主體性) is reaffirmed as the final vitality (活力) of a nation (民族) preserving its history (歷史). On the other hand, a nation (民族) with strong subjectivity (主體性) will never collapse, no matter how difficult history (歷史) may be.


--- (p. 50) ---

It is not a matter of whether we can endure or not, but rather a matter of how we endure. This is why our Korean people have survived so vividly through the most severe national crisis in our 5,000-year national history. In one word, it is clear that this is a global historical representation that a nation with strong subjectivity before history will never collapse no matter how much it suffers. Here lies the true greatness of our national subjectivity in our national history that we can be proud of and find.

## Section 6: Social Movements Before the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 1. The Mythical Significance in Traditional Customs

While the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is defined as a movement for better living, this movement is not a unique concept that refers solely to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).
Looking back at our history, we can see that our ancestors had a strong desire to live well and made efforts to find ways to live well, reflecting the social characteristics of each era in which they lived.
In other words, as long as humans possess life, they will inevitably burn with their own desires, and as long as these desires coexist with life, seeking methods to satisfy these desires is a characteristic that cannot be abandoned for any reason.
When examining the methods of movement adopted under various names in a chronological order, they were not necessarily identical, but there was one unchanging common point: the meaning of seeking to live better did not change.
From this perspective, we can discover a clear logic that today's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) chosen by us must be understood in two aspects. One is the variable aspect, and the other is the invariable aspect.
The variable aspect is the point of how the movement was developed under what name, in what way, and on what scale, while the invariable aspect is the point that the essential nature of the movement for better living does not change regardless of the way and scale.
In other words, while the method oriented towards desire satisfaction can change, the desire itself does not bring about a fundamental change.


--- (p. 51) ---

# Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The various social movements (社會運動) before the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) had different ways of unfolding (展開) depending on the era (時代), but the essential nature (本質的) of their pursuit (追求) to live well has never changed.

While the specific content (內容) of the desires (欲求) they sought may have varied, the ultimate value (價値) they pursued was always centered on the goal of living better.

One clear example (實證的) of this is the Korean tradition (風習) of "Goshi-nae" (고시내), which has been passed down for over 5,000 years (五千年). "Goshi-nae" can also be written as "Gosil-na" (高失乃) or "Gosil-lae" (高失來), but all these terms refer to Gosil-si (高失氏).

According to "Gyuwonsahwa" (揆園史話), attributed to the author Buk-ae (北崖), "Gosil-si was the first to invent the fire-cooking (火食) farming method (農法) and taught the people how to cultivate crops (稼穑)." In "Hae-dong-jukji" (海東竹枝) by Choi Young-nyeon (崔永年), it is explained that even today, farmers call out "Goshi-nae" while eating a spoonful of rice in the fields as a prayer (祈祝) to invite the blessing (來臨) of Gosil-si, the god (始神) of agriculture (農事) (家家舍哺恩雖忘, 一飯必呼高失來).

Whether or not "Goshi-nae" originated from the existence (存在) of Gosil-si (高失氏), one clear fact is that this tradition has not disappeared from our daily lives (生活習俗) and clearly expresses the wish (祈願) to live well and be well-fed (飢饉).

In other words, "Goshi-nae" is an expression of the fundamental human desire (本質的欲求) to live well.

Now, let us trace the various ways (方式) in which this desire (欲求) to live well has been pursued (具顯) throughout history (時系列的).

## 2. Social Movement (社會運動) Activities in Ancient History (古代史)

Even today, we operate various organizations (組織) based on the traditional Korean social cooperation system (契), solving common interests (共同關心事) together. The origin (始源) of this system, known as "gye" (契, formerly written as 禊), can be traced back to the Three Han (三韓) period (時代), particularly in the kingdom of Byeon Han (弁韓).

According to "A Sang-nok" (雅賞錄) by Jeong Yak-bo (丁若鋪) and "Hae-dong-jukji" (海東竹枝) by Choi Young-nyeon (崔永年), Byeon Han (弁韓) was home to 9 tribes (部族), each led by a chief (酋長) known as "Cheon" (千).


--- (p. 52) ---

They said.
The leaders of the nine tribes (九個部族) were called Gu-gan (九干), and they gathered to discuss issues of coexistence (共存問題) and consultation (協議問題) among the tribes, which was called Jik (稷).

Based on this origin (始源), the tradition (傳來) of contracts (契) began and has continued to this day, thriving among various groups (各界) and like-minded communities (同類集團). A survey (調査) conducted in 1931 targeting 1,685 villages (個部落) (Table 5) shows how prevalent these contracts (契) were in society.

There were 232 types of kinship mutual aid contracts (同族相助契), which signified mutual aid (隣保相助) among members of a community (共同體) with blood ties (血緣關係). There were 807 types of ancestor worship contracts (祖先祭祀契), which promoted ethical values (倫理) based on the philosophy of filial piety (孝敬思想). There were 57 types of agricultural encouragement contracts (勸農契), which signified cooperative work (協業作業). There were 14 types of tax payment deadline adherence contracts (納稅期限嚴守契), which signified adherence to the law (遵法). There were 26 types of custom improvement contracts (風習改善契), which aimed to eliminate decadent trends (退廢風潮). There were 34 types of education promotion contracts (敎育獎勵契), which aimed to invigorate academic atmosphere (學風).

In short, contracts (契) were clearly a social movement (社會運動) based on the spirit of mutual aid (守望相助), a form of national activity (國民活動).

During the reign of the third king (第3代), Yuri of Silla (新羅儒理王), there was a women's collective (集團) called Dure Sam (積麻), led by a princess (公主), which was a production organization (生產組織) at the village level (三國史記). This gradually evolved into a cooperative body (協業體) at the village level called Dure.


--- (p. 53) ---

Each had its own flag (旗) symbolizing itself (自體), and the fruits (成果) were distributed (配分) according to each member's (成員) contribution (出資) ratio (比率). The surplus (剩餘分) was shared (共有) and used for expenses (費用) such as building bridges (橋) for the village, establishing night schools (夜學施設), or preparing shared agricultural tools (農機具) for common use (共同利用).

The *dure* (두레) had a distinct character (性格) as a production community (生產共同體) based on the local community (地緣) of shared living spaces (住居空間).

### 3. Social Movement (社會運動) through *Hyangyak* (鄕約)

*Hyangyak* (鄕約) had a range (範圍) at the county level (面單位) regional society (地域社會), which was a distinguishing feature (特徵) compared to *dure*. However, unlike *dure*, it was not a system (體制) where all members (成員) of the local community (地緣共同體) directly participated (直接參與). Participation (參與) was based on the principle (原則) of supporters (支援者), and at that time (當時), when there were class distinctions (班常階層), there were also status-based (身分的) restrictions (制約) on who could become a member (入約者).

However, *Hyangyak* (鄕約) strongly emphasized social education (社會敎育) by practicing moral codes (實踐徳目) as a lifestyle creed (生活綱領). Its fundamental ideology (基本理念) was "Hwaminseongsok" (化民成俗), which aimed to educate (敎化) the people (百姓) and create good customs (美風良俗). To achieve this ideology (理念), it proclaimed four main moral codes (主要實踐徳目): ① *Deok-eopsangsangwon* (徳業相勸), ② *Gwasilsanggye* (過失相規), ③ *Yesoksanggyo* (禮俗相交), and ④ *Hwan-nansangsoo* (患難相恤) as the four pillars (4大支柱). (Depending on the circumstances (境遇), the expression (表現) of these moral codes (徳目) might vary slightly, but their meanings (意味) all align (相通) with these four.)

It is said that *Hyangyak* (鄕約) began with the four brothers (兄弟) of the *Yeo* (呂) family who lived in the *Namjeon* (藍田) region during the Song (宋) dynasty in China (中國). The *Yeo* family's *Hyangyak* (呂氏鄕約) was supplemented (增補) by *Jumongong* (朱文公) (熹) and was introduced to Korea (傳來) as *Yi Hwang* (李滉)'s "Yeonan Hyangyak" (禮安鄕約) (1556). Before *Yi Hwang* (李滉)'s "Yeonan Hyangyak" (禮安鄕約), there was also the "Pungpye Hyangyak" (豊沛鄕約) initiated by *Taejong* (太祖) *Lee Seong-gye* (李成桂) (1398).

The "Pungpye Hyangyak" (豊沛鄕約) can be considered the beginning (嚆矢) of *Hyangyak* (鄕約) in Korea, as it primarily (主로) consisted of 41 articles (條目) regulating non-action obligations (不作爲義務). It is also known as the "41 Articles of Hyangyak" (鄕約 41조).


--- (p. 54) ---

It was done.

Later, it was expanded by Hyeongnyeongdaegun (孝寧大君) into 21 articles of good deeds (善目) and 35 articles of bad deeds (惡目), totaling 56 articles (條), hence it was also called the Pyongyang Hyangyak (平壤鄕約) 56 articles (條).

The Pyongyang Hyangyak (平壤鄕約) was created to be implemented in the Hamhung area (咸興地域), the birthplace of Taejo (李太祖), but why was it named Pyongyang (平壤)? Taejo (李太祖) did not follow the name of the birthplace of the Han Gaozu (漢高祖) of China (中國) and called it Hamhung Hyangyak (咸興鄕約), but instead named it Pyongyang Hyangyak (平壤鄕約).

However, Yi Hwang (李滉), who named his work the Yean Hyangyak (禮安鄕約) after the original implementation area (施行地域), had 28 articles (個條) composed, but its content (內容) not only had a strong will to purify (淨化) the social (社會) atmosphere (氣風) but also sought (追求) a type (類型) of creation (創造) from imitation (模倣).

In particular, Yi I (李珥) took a step further and in 1560 (年) created and implemented the Paju Hyangyak (坡州鄕約), in 1571 (年) the Seowon Hyangyak (西原鄕約), and in 1579 (Year) the Haiju Hyangyak (海州鄕約), each implemented in their respective regional societies (地域社會).

In the Paju Hyangyak (坡州鄕約), Yi I (李珥) clearly stated that Hyangyak (鄕約), regardless of the era (古今), is based on the principles (原理) of ① human common emotions (常情), ② obedience to heavenly principles (天理), ③ purification of customs (風俗), ④ national education (國民敎化) as its content (內容), and ⑤ not violating propriety (禮義).

However, Yi I (李珥) summarized the purpose (目的) of the Paju Hyangyak (坡州鄕約) into two aspects. One is to correctly teach propriety (禮儀) to the villagers (鄕民) so that all may return to what is benevolent and righteous (敎禮儀而歸于正), and the other is to have the leader (指導者) discuss (議論) with the residents (住民) all common concerns (公通關心事) of the village (鄕村) and handle them fairly (公明正大) to maintain (健在) the public principles (公理) of village life (生活) (讅于衆而復于公).

Furthermore, Yi I (李珥) stated that Hyangyak (鄕約) is not only a movement (運動) for the self-governance (自治) of regional society (地域社會) residents (住民) but also aims to eliminate mutual distrust (不信) among residents (住民) to establish (確立) social (社會的) discipline (紀綱), thereby ensuring (圖謀) the stability (安定) of the people's livelihood (民生), which is the foundation (根本) of the state (國家).

In other words, he clarified that if trust (信賴) is lacking (缺如) between officials and the public (官民間), the state (國家) cannot exist (存立) healthily (健全), and thus implementing (施行) Hyangyak (鄕約) means strengthening (圖謀) the foundation (根本) of the people's livelihood (民生), the root (根本) of the country (國家) (民無信不立, 立約所以立民地).

Based on such fundamental (基本) ideology (理念), the Seowon Hyangyak (西原鄕約) (能川) established a system (體制) for resident education (住民敎化) and


--- (p. 55) ---

## Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The method of organizing citizens (民組織方法) was concretized (具體化) in the case of the Haiju Hyangyak (海州鄕約), which, in addition to its ethical and cultural elements (遒義文化的要素), incorporated significant economic content (經濟的內容要素) to promote moral development (德風의 진작) based on a stable economic life (經濟生活의 안정기반).

Beyond this, Yi I (李珥) created various models of social movements (社會運動模型) to induce cooperative activities (協同的活動) among residents (住民), such as the Haiju Ilhyangyak (海州一鄕約), Sagye (社契), and Pungsugye (風樹契).

This tradition of social movements (社會運動의 전통) was inherited by Silhak (實學) scholars such as Yu Gye (柳磎) and Jeong Sul (鄭述), and by the time of An Jung-bok (安鼎福) (1712–1791), it had evolved into the Hyangsapbeop (鄕社法), which truly embodied the spirit of self-reliance (自活精神).

An Jung-bok's Hyangsapbeop (鄕社法) can be analyzed in four aspects:

1. **Organizational Structure (組織面)**: The leadership and responsibility were divided into four levels: Tongsu (統首), Gabjang (甲長), Sajaeong (社正), and Hyangsa (鄕師), with the organizational criteria for residents (住民組織基準) set as follows: five households per Tong (五家爲統), two Tongs per Gab (二統爲甲), ten Gabs per Sa (十甲爲師), and gathered Sa as Hyang (聚社爲鄕).

2. **Governance (治道面)**: The content included mutual vigilance (火燭相戒), mutual defense against thieves (盜賊相禦), mutual relief in times of distress (憂患相恤), mutual support in times of prosperity (搭殷相扶), mutual respect for laws and ordinances (法令相畏), and mutual support and caution (相扶相謹).

3. **Educational Content (敎育內容面)**: The content aimed to promote good customs (美風良俗) and included filial piety towards parents (孝順父母), respect for superiors (恭敬尊上), harmonious neighborhood relations (和睦隣里), education of descendants (敎訓子孫), securing livelihood (資安生利), and honesty in actions (無作弗僞).

4. **Promotion of Rituals and Customs (禮俗獎勵面)**: Particular emphasis was placed on the importance of martial arts (武藝) for all residents. On the 1st and 15th of each month, residents practiced archery (射圃) at designated locations as part of a national training plan (國民訓練計劃) to prepare for emergencies (有事時). The principle of "practicing archery during farming off-seasons" (農閑習射) was the foundation, where residents engaged in their own occupations (自己生業) during peacetime (平常時) and were mobilized for defense duties (防衛任務) during emergencies. Additionally, each household or village was required to keep a certain amount of weapon-like tools (武器性用具) to enhance the self-defense capabilities (自衛防衛能力) of the Hyangsa (鄕社). Residents were also required to participate in a local ritual (鄕禮) involving martial arts (武術) and etiquette (禮節) to prepare for emergencies, such as invasions by external enemies (外敵) or bandits (盜賊).

5. **Guidance on Economic Life (經濟生活指導面)**: Efforts were made to enlighten and guide residents' productive activities (生産活動) and to select and disseminate suitable crops for the region (適地作目).

Furthermore, all forms of harmful customs (廢風) such as social withdrawal (社會離脫), gambling (賭博), usury (高利債), debauchery (放蕩), and extravagance (奢侈浪費) were to be eradicated.


--- (p. 56) ---

The content aimed at rectifying society (社會淨化內容) was significantly included.
The village covenants (鄕約) had gone through a similar developmental path (發展經路) to emphasize that villagers (鄕村住民) must be self-aware (自覺) for village development (鄕村發展). Additionally, it stressed the need for collective effort (集團努力誘發) to find self-help measures (自活策) and cultivate the spirit (精神) and capability (能力) of self-defense (自主防衛) to repel external invasions (外敵의 침략) primarily through the united strength of the residents (住民). Particularly, the essence (本質) of village resident activities (鄕村住民活動) led by practical scholars (實學者) prominently displayed a self-defensive (自衛的) nature (性格), which might be seen as a manifestation of the determination (決意) not to repeat the humiliation (恥辱) experienced during the Japanese invasions of 1592 (壬辰倭亂) and the Manchu invasions of 1636 (丙子胡亂). Such village covenants (鄕約), originating from civilian (民間) initiatives, were regional (地域的) resident movements (住民運動) at the village level (鄕村單位). Despite interruptions, they persisted during the Joseon Dynasty (李朝時代) and even under Japanese colonial rule (日帝治下), where they were known as village fellowships (鄕徒鄕約) and continued in some regions (一部地方).

### 4. Social Movements Before Liberation (光復前)

During the Japanese colonial period (日帝治下), Korean social movements (社會運動) can be categorized into three types.

Firstly, there were popular movements (民衆運動) with anti-Japanese (抗日約) significance aimed at finding our homeland (祖國). Secondly, there were resident movements (住民運動) with assimilative educational (同化敎育的) implications by the Japanese (日帝). Thirdly, there were self-help movements (自活運動) that aimed to preserve the spirit (精神) of national revival (民族更生) without provoking the Japanese (日帝), maintaining traditional values (傳統維持的) in content (內容的).

The first type of movement lacked social nature (社會性) as an organized (組織化) popular movement (民衆運動) and struggled to establish a clear system (展開體系) for autonomous (自主的) and national (民族的) development. However, the third type, despite outwardly accepting the Japanese assimilative education (同化敎育) content (內容), maintained the possibility (可能性) of preserving and developing the values (價値) of national tradition (民族傳統) and regional society (地域社會) characteristics (特性) through self-reliance (自力更生) initiatives.

From this perspective, this section will focus on the third type of social movement (社會運動) to examine the pre-liberation (光復前) social movement landscape (社會運動樣相). As is widely known, the Japanese (日帝) assimilation policy (同化政策) under their rule (日帝治下) significantly influenced the social movement sphere (社會運動面).


--- (p. 57) ---

# Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

From this perspective, it can be seen that it was based on the principle of educating (敎化) residential communities (住民集團) without provoking nationalist sentiments (民族感情) to the maximum extent possible.

For example, according to a survey conducted in 1930 by requesting all provincial governors (道知事) nationwide, the number of model villages (模範部落) that had developed due to government directives (指示) and residents' self-motivation (自勵勉勵) is shown by province in Table 2, totaling 257 villages nationwide.

Even looking only at the main activities carried out in these 257 villages, as shown in Table 3, there were 381 cases of promoting production activities (生産活動), 465 cases of promoting cooperative work (協同作業), 213 cases of promoting custom improvement (風習改良), 56 cases of promoting living facilities (生活施設), and 425 cases of promoting activity organizations (活動組織), totaling 1,540 cases.

However, when examining the detailed contents of each promotional activity, there is a commonality that in almost every case, night schools (夜學), law dissemination (法令傳達), moral education lectures (敎化講習會), flag-raising ceremonies (國旗揭揚), and other daily activities with intentional political purposes (政治的目的) were included, albeit to varying degrees.

Furthermore, in terms of activity organizations (活動組織), it is notable that specific production activities (生産活動) were guided towards a cooperative system (組合體制), and at the same time, collective organizations (集團化) such as Donggye (洞契) and labor contracts (勞動契) were formed. Additionally, youth groups (幼年團), youth houses (青年舍), and women's associations (婦人會) were used to promote resident activities (住民活動) based on age or gender. Moreover, it can be seen that business activities (事業活動) were carried out based on the organizational power (組織力) of these collective groups (集團).

While these resident self-governance activities (住民自治活動) may appear to be autonomous activities (自治活動) on the surface, it would not be an incorrect expression to say that they were resident movements (住民運動) with an assimilative educational (同化敎育的) meaning (意味).

However, resident movements (住民運動) such as the "Village Compact" (鄕徒鄕約) had elements of national traditional consciousness (民族的傳統意識), historical succession consciousness (歷史承繼意識), and the spirit of self-preservation (自己保全) in their activities.


--- (p. 58) ---

There is.

Among the "Hyangsa Hyangyak (鄕徒鄕約)," the movement carried out in places such as Seomyeon (西面), Myeongnam-dong (明南洞) in Myeongcheon County (明川郡), Hamgyeongbuk-do (咸鏡北道) holds significant meaning as a resident movement. Introducing its main content, the first basic purpose is for residents to unite and cooperate to:
1. Encourage each other in virtue and business (德業相勸),
2. Regulate each other's faults (過失相規),
3. Interact with each other in rituals and customs (禮俗相交), and
4. Support each other in times of trouble (患難相恤).

Secondly, the basic organization targets Dongmin (洞民) as members (鄕眞)(約員), with several conditions attached.

Those wishing to join must present proof of membership in the Donggye (洞契) and pay the prescribed admission fee (30 jeon (錢) at the time) on the day of the general assembly. The general assembly decides on admission, and those not members of Donggye can be expelled (黜鄕)(loss of member status). However, forced expulsion is not allowed unless it is due to moving to another Dong (他洞).

The leadership organization of the Hyangyak (鄕約) consists of one Do Gam (都監) and several Do Yusas (都有司) and Jipsas (執事), elected for a one-year term.

Thirdly, the detailed rules include:
1. Practicing the Five Relationships (五倫) such as filial piety (孝敬), love (愛), and trust (信) to promote virtue and customs,
2. Dismounting (下馬) to greet elders,
3. Prohibiting violence (毆打), drunkenness (主正), and discord among residents,
4. Absolutely prohibiting alcohol consumption (飮酒) for those under 15 (歳).

To encourage mutual aid and good customs:
1. Joint burial (埋葬) is mandatory for members and their families aged 10 (歲) and above upon death,
2. Burials due to infectious diseases (傳染病) are exempt,
3. Relief (救恤) is provided to disaster victims (被災者),
4. Assistance (救濟) is given to those without livelihood (生計) measures.


--- (p. 59) ---

# Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Fourthly, to maintain village regulations (향규유지, 鄕規維持), penalties (벌칙, 罰則) were established. The main content of these regulations involved sanctions (제재, 制裁) for those who violated duties (작위의무, 作爲義務) or prohibitions (부작위의무, 不作爲義務).

It seems that movements such as the "Village Compact" (향도향약, 鄕徒鄕約) were wise examples of resident movements (주민운동, 住民運動) that reflected the contemporary situation (시대적 상황, 時代的 狀況).

In addition, enlightenment movements (민족계몽운동, 民族啓蒙運動) led by local residents (지방거주지사, 地方居住志士), religious figures (종교인, 宗敎人), teachers (교사, 敎師), and students (학생, 學生), as well as various types of social movements (사회운동, 社會運動) aimed at self-reliance (자력갱생, 自力更生), existed. However, it seems that organizing residents (주민, 住民) in a specific region (일정지역, 一定地域) and carrying out a purpose-driven movement (목적지향적 운동, 目的指向的運動) was not easy.

## 5. Regional Community Movements After the Korean War (한국동란, 韓國動亂)

From the founding of the nation (건국, 建國) until the Korean War (6.25 동란, 6.25動亂) ended in an armistice (휴전형태, 休戰形態), South Korean society (우리나라 사회, 我國社會) was in a state of flux (유동상태, 流動狀態). During this period, it is fair to say that there was an absence of regional community movements (지역사회운동, 地域社會運動).

During the war, our nation suffered over 1 million casualties (인명피해, 人命被害) and property damage (재산피해, 財産被害) amounting to 300 million dollars. Given these circumstances, finding a path to national self-sufficiency (국민자활, 國民自活) was one of the most urgent tasks. From this perspective, resident self-sufficiency movements (주민자활운동, 住民自活運動) for regional community development (지역사회개발사업, 地域社會開發事業) were required.

Thus, the initial impetus (시동, 始動) for regional community development projects (지역사회개발사업, 地域社會開發事業) began with the establishment of a two-year plan (2개년계획, 2個年計劃) in 1953 by the Korean government (한국정부, 韓國政府) and the United Nations Korean Reconstruction Committee (국제연합 한국재건위원단, 國際聯合 韓國再建委員團). Although 400 projects (개사업, 個事業) were completed under this plan, they were merely small-scale endeavors (소규모사업, 小規模事業).

However, the establishment of the "Korea-U.S. Joint Practical Committee for Regional Community Development" (지역사회개발한미합동실무반, 地域社會開發韓美合同實務班) on June 21, 1957, by the Korea-U.S. Joint Economic Committee (한미합동경제위원회, 韓美合同經濟委員會) to examine the feasibility of regional community development projects in Korea holds significant meaning. In this sense, it can be seen as the beginning (태동, 胎動) of regional community movements (지역사회운동, 地域社會運動) in our country.

At that time, the Korean side (한국측, 韓國側) was represented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (농림부, 農林部), the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs (보건사회부, 保健社會部), the Ministry of Education (문교부, 文敎部), the Ministry of Home Affairs (내무부, 內務部), and the Reconstruction Bureau (부흥부, 復興部). The U.S. Economic Cooperation Administration in Korea (주한미국경제협조처, 駐韓美國經濟協助處) (O.E.C) appointed representatives (대표, 代表) from the Regional Community Development Bureau (지역사회개발국, 地域社會開發局) and related fields (관계분야, 關係分野). Both sides formed an investigation team (조사반, 調査班) and selected the Gwangju Gun region (광주군지역, 廣州郡地域) in Gyeonggi Province (경기도, 京畿道) as one of the four areas for investigation.


--- (p. 60) ---

# Division by Unit Regions

To determine the feasibility, direction, and timing of community development projects in each unit region, a broad social survey was conducted across industries, education, telecommunications, medical facilities, and religion. The results were promising, leading to two main conclusions:

1. Korean farmers have the capability to improve their villages independently.
2. Some material support and guidance from external sources are necessary to modernize and develop rural Korean society.

Based on these conclusions, it was proposed to the Joint U.S.-Korea Economic Committee that community development projects in Korea should be carried out with O.E.C aid, including some subsidized and non-subsidized projects. The Joint U.S.-Korea Economic Committee's working group was subsequently disbanded.

In its place, a new body was established within the Joint U.S.-Korea Economic Committee: the Community Development Subcommittee. This committee was responsible for:

1. Selecting demonstration villages for community development.
2. Preparing for the Joint U.S.-Korea Community Development Conference.
3. Appointing staff for the Central Community Development Committee.
4. Preparing staff training at the New Life Education Institute.
5. Contracting technical support services from the U.S. East Asia Foundation.

Meanwhile, the Korean government decided on the outline of community development projects at the National Council meeting on January 24, 1958. The key points were:

1. Definition: "Community development refers to the process where residents of a certain region discover and solve their collective or individual challenges to improve their lives, through collective or individual planning and action, using their own resources or support from external sources (government or other agencies)."
2. Funding: To be covered by foreign aid materials and equivalent funds.
3. Pilot projects: To be implemented in Jeju Province and three other regions.
4. Consultative bodies: To be established under the Department of Reconstruction by presidential decree, with the Minister of Reconstruction as the chair and vice ministers of Home Affairs, Education, Agriculture and Forestry, Social Affairs, and Reconstruction as members. Each province and county was to establish its own committee, with the governor and county magistrate as chairs, and members appointed by the committee to discuss the projects.


--- (p. 61) ---

## Chapter 1: Historical Background of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Fifth, under the supervision of practical agencies, specialized guidance officers (專門指導員) and representative guidance officers (代表指導員) were appointed for specialized fields such as ① agricultural and forestry guidance (農林指導), ② social welfare (社會福祉), ③ health and sanitation (保健衛生), and ④ women's guidance (婦女指導). In addition, general guidance officers (一般指導員) were appointed for each village (部落).

On September 2, 1958, Presidential Decree No. 1384 was enacted and promulgated to carry out such business (事業). This marked the beginning of the first regional community development project (地域社會開發事業) in Korea.

However, the regional community development project (地域社會開發事業) faced difficulties in becoming established due to changes in the responsible agencies (所管機關) before achieving any significant results (事業成果).

Specifically, from September 2, 1958, to May 30, 1961, the Central Committee (中央委員會) oversaw the project, focusing on training objectives (訓練目標) such as ① cultivating leadership (指導力), ② fostering a spirit of cooperation (協同精神), ③ promoting a spirit of service (奉仕精神), ④ acquiring knowledge and practical methods for interpersonal relationships (對人關係知識 및 그 實踐方法), and ⑤ enhancing understanding of rural issues in Korea (韓國農村問題). The committee conducted education and training (敎育訓練) across various fields (分野) and held related official meetings (關係官會議) and international conferences (國際會議). However, on June 7, 1961, the Regional Community Development Central Committee (地域社會開發中央委員會) was abolished by Cabinet Decree No. 9 and reorganized into the Regional Community Bureau (地域社會局) within the Construction Ministry (建設部).

Subsequently, on July 22, 1961, the Regional Community Bureau (地域社會局) was transferred to the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (農林部) due to an amendment to the Government Organization Law (政府組織法) (Law No. 660). Then, on March 21, 1962, the Rural Development Law (農村振興法) (Law No. 1039) was enacted, leading to the integration of the former Agricultural Affairs Bureau (農事院) and the Regional Community Development Agricultural and Forestry Civil Servant Training Institute (農林公務員訓練院) under the unified guidance system (指導體系) policy.

The Rural Development Agency (農村振興廳) set three major priority objectives (重點目標) for the regional community development project (地域社會開發事業):

First, cultivate leadership (指導力) through the democratic organization (民主的組織化) of rural society (農村社會).
Second, increase farm income (農家所得) and improve the production base (生産基盤整備) by utilizing rural labor (農村勞動力) and idle resources (遊休資源).
Third, foster self-help capabilities (自助力) among local residents (地域民), maximize government support effects (支援效果), and strive for the stabilization (安定化) of the regional community (地域社會).

To achieve these priority objectives (重點目標), an extensive six-year plan (6個年計劃) for regional community development (地域社會開發) was developed. This plan, titled "Six-Year Plan (6個年計劃) for Self-Help Development (自助開發) of Village Residents (部落民)," was scheduled to be implemented from 1966 to 1971.

The concept (槪念) of regional development projects (地域開發事業) outlined in this plan was discussed at the National Council of State (國務會議) on January 24, 1958.


--- (p. 62) ---

The defined content (內容) was expressed somewhat differently.
That is, it was expressed as "The regional development projects (地域開發事業) of our country are projects (事業) planned and implemented by the villagers (部落民) themselves, based on the common desires (共通欲求) of the villagers (部落民), their creativity (創意), and their efforts (努力)."
Furthermore, the same plan (同計劃) pointed out that, in terms of its significance (意義面),
1. rural policies (對農村施策) often fail to promote the self-help capabilities (自助能力啓發) of villagers (部落民) and instead foster dependency (依他心),
2. there is almost no cooperation (協同化) in productive activities (生產活動) to overcome the small-scale nature (英世性) of agriculture,
3. rural resources (農村資源) are not effectively mobilized (動員), and
4. government agencies (政府機關) and organizations (團體) fail to comprehensively coordinate (綜合的調整) and penetrate (浸透) their rural policies (對農村施策) in local communities (地域社會).

However, it was stated that for the efficient promotion (效率的推進) of rural development activities (農村開發活動), three things are necessary: first, the democratization (民主化) of rural areas (農村), second, the scientification (科學化) of rural areas (農村), and third, the formation of capital (資本形成) in rural areas (農村).
To pursue these goals (目標推進), as shown in Table 4 (表 4), out of a total of 640,556 projects (件) targeting 33,100 villages (個) nationwide (全國), 233,553 projects (件) are to be implemented as support projects (支援事業) and 407,003 projects (件) as self-help projects (自助事業).
