Critiques (批判論) of our democracy (民主主義) can be broadly divided into two categories. The first approach idealizes (理想化) an abstract standard (基準), particularly that of Western-style (西歐式) liberal democracy (自由民主主義), as the essence (本質) of democracy (民主主義). It then criticizes (批判) the inadequacies (不充分性) of Korean democracy (韓國에서의 민주主義) based on this ideal. This argument is put forth by Korean intellectuals (知識人) who share political (政治的) affinities (性向) with certain countries and those who have direct (直接的) experience (經驗) with Western (西歐的) life (生活).


--- (p. 93) ---

One has a strong appeal (呼訴力) to some radical (急進的) segments (一部) of the general public (一般大衆), as well as to those who emphasize the traditional (傳統的) political-cultural (政治文化的) and socio-economic (經濟社會的) perspectives of Korea (韓國). This view questions the suitability of democracy (民主主義) in Korea (韓國) based on its past experiences (過去經驗) and argues that, since it is an imported (外來的) concept, we cannot expect it to function in Korea (韓國) as it does in its place of origin (發祥地). This claim suggests that we should replace it with some indigenous (土着) justification (名分). This argument is mainly advocated by those with politically (政治的) or culturally (文化的) conservative (保守的) stances (立場) and also has considerable appeal (呼訴力) to the general public (一般大衆).

First, let's examine the first criticism (批判). It emphasizes only the normative (規範的) goals (目標) of democracy (民主主義) in Korea (韓國) without giving due consideration (應分의 고려) to the reality (現實) surrounding it. As a result, this criticism (批判) fails to penetrate (貫通) the logic (論理) of reality (現實) as a concrete (具體的) means to realize (實現) the ideal (理想) it advocates. Therefore, when reality (現實) falls short of the ideal (理想), it either leads to indiscriminate (無分別) extremism (過激主義) or plunges into total (全面的) pessimism (悲觀主義). Moreover, this criticism (批判) denies all creative (創造的) elements (要素) in Korea (韓國) that could operate (作動) for the settlement (定着) and development (發展) of democracy (民主主義) in Korea (韓國) by penetrating (貫通) the historical (歷史的) nature (性格) of the objective (客觀的) conditions (條件) that have caused the insufficiency (不充分性) of liberal democracy (自由民主主義) it points out. In this criticism (批判), reality (現實) is merely an object (對象) of logical (論理的) and ethical (倫理的) assertion (斷定), and it cannot present (提示) any practical (現實的) alternative (代案) for action (實踐).

The second criticism (批判), which argues that liberal democracy (自由民主主義) is not suitable for Korea (韓國) based on historical (歷史的) experiences (經驗) and should be replaced with some indigenous (土着的) ideology (意識形態), commits a cognitive (思考上) error (誤謬) of perceiving (把握) tradition (傳統) as an unchanging (無變化), static (靜態的) entity (實體). The demand for some pure (純粹한) indigenous (土着) justification (名分) is mythical (神話的). What is called indigenous (土着的) refers to a complex (複合體) of values (價値) that have adapted (適應) to a specific (特定) society (社會) through the creative (創造的) acceptance (受容) of foreign (外來) values (價値). In this sense, democracy (民主主義) has already become an indigenous (土着的) ideology (意識形態) in Korea (韓國) as it has been a part (一部) of Korean history (韓國史) for the past 35 years (年間).

To discuss the Korean (韓國的) coordinates (座標) of democracy (民主主義) through these two criticisms (批判論), we need to examine what the basic (基本) principles (原則) of democracy (民主主義) are that are inherent (內在) in the first criticism (批判), and how they relate (關係) to the traditional (傳統的) factors (要因) and experiences (經驗) of Korea (韓國) that the second criticism (批判) contains.


--- (p. 94) ---

It is necessary to mention this.

Generally, the basic principles of democracy (民主主義) are discussed as national sovereignty (國民主權), separation of powers (3權分立), deliberation (審議) and the majority principle (多數決原則), representative government (國民代表制) and representative democracy (代議制). Of course, these principles of Western (西歐) democracy (民主主義) were based on long historical and ideological experiences that led to their creation and establishment. Democracy (民主主義) originated from the writings of the Greek historian Herodotus and grew within the ideological lineage that prioritized the individual (個人) over the state (國家), through the accumulated ideas of countless visionaries (先覺者) such as Locke, Rousseau, Montesquieu, Lincoln, Jefferson, and Mill.

Historically, democracy (民主主義) became a practical basis for governance and a political institution when the productive middle class (中産層) in the West (西歐) resisted the oppression (抑壓) and privileges (特權) of absolute monarchs (絶對君主) and feudal lords (封建領主) to secure their freedom (自由) in commercial activities (商業活動) and participation in policy decision-making (政策決定過程). Therefore, it was based on the formation of an industrial society (産業社會) mediated by the formation of the middle class (中産層), the establishment of a capitalist (資本主義) society (社會), the overall improvement (全般的向上) of national wealth (國富), high levels of urbanization (高度都市化), and the formation of harmonious interest groups (調和利益集團).

Culturally, it presupposed the maturity (成熟) of a culture (文化) of discussion (討論) and compromise (妥協), as well as a sense of community (共同體意識) among the people (國民), mutual respect (相互尊重) in lifestyle (生活樣式), self-governance (自治) ability (能力) and consciousness (意識), all set against the backdrop of a long-standing (長久) grassroots (基層) religious (宗敎) culture (文化).

These conditions and backgrounds are considerably distant from Korea's (韓國) historical (歷史的) traditions (傳統) and experiences (經驗) since the introduction (導入) of democracy (民主主義). Of course, it cannot be said that there were no democratic (民主的) factors (要因) in our traditional (傳統的) history (歷史). Although their practical significance (現實的意味) has faded and they have almost disappeared, traditions (傳統) of cooperative small-group living (小集團協同生活) such as "Dure," "Gye (契)," "Hyangyak (鄕約)," "Hyangsi (香徙)," and "Pobusang (褓負商)" are often cited as democratic (民主的) factors (要因). Moreover, the consciousness (意識) of "Aemin (愛民)" or "Minwigwi (民爲貴) Sajikchaji (社稷次之) Junwigeong (君爲輕)" derived from Confucian (儒敎的) tradition (傳統) well represents our traditional (傳統的) minben (民本) consciousness (意識). However, these cannot be easily described as democratic (民主主義) elements (要素). The concepts of "Aemin (愛民)" and "Minwigwi (民爲貴)" emphasize the ethicality (倫理性) of rulers (治者), so to speak, as a "wiminjeok (爲民的)(for the people (國民))" concept (槪念), which can be understood as an expression (表現) of ethical (倫理的) authoritarianism (權威主義). The more essential (本質的) characteristic (特徵) of democracy (民主主義), the concept (槪念) of "Uimin (依民)(by the people (國民))", gradually emerged through the Donghak (東學) Movement (運動) and the Enlightenment Period (開化期), and it was not until the March 1st Movement (運動) that it somewhat acquired a popular (民衆的) meaning (意味), according to the general (一般的) view (見解). In short, our traditional (傳統的) democratic (民主) consciousness (意識) can be traced back to minbenism (民本主義) represented by ethical (倫理的) authoritarianism (權威主義), or in other words, "wiminjeok (爲民的)"


--- (p. 95) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

It would be highly accurate to say that "Leadership from above" was emphasized and "Participation from below" was merely the exclusive domain of a small number of intellectuals after the Enlightenment Period.

Here, it is particularly necessary to discuss in detail the influence that the 36 years of Japanese colonial rule had on the introduction and development of democracy in Korea. This is because the "soil" of Korea when it introduced democratic systems after liberation was considerably different from the traditional factors mentioned above.

First, the 36 years of Japanese rule gave us not only a political vacuum but also a tendency towards resistance and subservience. During this period, the political arena was the exclusive domain of Japanese imperialism, and governing institutions were merely objects of unconditional resistance and forced subservience. Therefore, we were unable to cultivate self-governing capabilities, and unconditional resistance or a resigned tendency are now obstacles to the establishment of democracy.

Second, Japanese colonial rule distorted the nature of our political culture. As mentioned earlier, our traditional political culture, which can be defined as authoritarian and patriarchal, was not entirely incompatible with democracy, which has a strong ethical character. However, Japanese colonial rule stripped the ethical nature from our authoritarian tradition, leaving only exploitation, and thus distorted the character of "authority" to be purely negative. This point became a major cause of the distortion of power relations in Korean domestic politics after liberation.

Third, due to the highly undemocratic nature of Japanese rule, the Korean people were deprived of opportunities to receive democratic training and were made to universalize thorough undemocratic practices.

Fourth, the 36 years of Japanese rule created a large crack in the traditional communal consciousness, manipulating our national character to appear partisan and factional. A representative example of this is the colonial view of history, where the Japanese emphasized the factional strife of the Joseon Dynasty.

Fifth, the 36 years of Japanese rule distorted our modernization process. Due to colonial necessities, Japan planted extremely minimal and distorted forms of colonial industries in this land, forcing modernization to undergo a heteronomous and distorted process. For modernization to settle autonomously, it would have to go through natural conflicts and self-correction through dialectics.


--- (p. 96) ---

Legal development is a normal process. The conflict between traditional and innovative classes, the innovative and gradual transformation of social structures, and the collapse and modification of traditional value systems are all natural and timely processes. In this sense, the process of democratization in South Korea after the liberation was, in part, akin to a delayed childhood illness in a deformed child who had outgrown infancy.

Most critically, the Japanese colonial rule left behind a legacy of national division and confrontation with hostile forces as a product of international power politics, which posed a fundamental obstacle to the introduction and consolidation of democracy in South Korea. The introduction of liberal democracy in South Korea, unlike in other newly independent nations, was strictly controlled due to the absolute hostile environment created by the Cold War conflict between imperial powers. The fate of democracy in South Korea was tied to the nature of its strong political forces. In other words, liberal democracy, which should have been domestically oriented, played a special role as a "political weapon" in the international struggle against communism. Therefore, many countries in the free world that shared political orientations with South Korea often criticized its domestic politics because the political ideology and institutions of South Korea served as a "political weapon" for attacking communism.

The smooth institutional operation of liberal democracy is greatly influenced by the degree of international political autonomy a nation possesses. However, the pressure of the Cold War constrained South Korea's international political autonomy by framing its politics as a political weapon for the free world, aligning it with international missions. Furthermore, the structure of strong politics in South Korea caused national division, pushing the country into an extremely hostile confrontation, making "security" a more important governing rationale than "democracy." Awareness of the communist threat led to an obsession with stability over change, sometimes making restrictions on basic human rights inevitable, and hindering or delaying the social and economic structural reforms necessary for the consolidation and development of democracy.

Additionally, institutional transplantation defects arising from the process of introducing democracy should also be noted. A representative example is the ordinary election system. Democratic elections presuppose the autonomy, sound judgment, and conscience of individual citizens. Moreover, in today's


--- (p. 97) ---

## Chapter 2 (第2章) The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

Governance (國政) is becoming increasingly specialized and complex, making the need for such capabilities more urgent than ever before in history. In Korea (韓國), the introduction of universal suffrage (普通選擧制) without considering the public's (民衆) judgment (判斷能力) and political participation (政治參與樣式) has strengthened primary groups (1次集團) based on regional (地緣) and blood ties (血緣), undermined national cohesion (國民統合力), fostered large-scale political corruption (政治腐敗), and failed to elect true representatives (代辯者). The existing political climate (政治風土) was characterized more by extremism (極限) than compromise (妥協), more by emotional realism (情實主義) or authoritarianism (權威主義) than rationalism (合理主義), and more by corruption (腐敗) than representation (代議).

Related to this issue, we must also discuss the question of the nation's (國民) individual qualities (資質問題) in light of the periods following April 19 (4.19) and October 26 (10.26). During these times, from the perspective of "basic rights (基本權的) and freedoms (自由權), freedom from the state (國家)," the role of the state (國家權力) was minimized, reminiscent of the night-watchman state (夜警國家) era in Western Europe (西歐), while individual freedoms (個人自由) were greatly expanded. However, the political sphere (政界) was marked by extreme factionalism (派閥性), with some politicians (政治人) exercising power (權力意志) without regard for their political responsibilities (責任). Socially (社會的), there was no mature social stratum (社會層) capable of sustaining freedom (自由), and hasty actions to overcome the reality of a divided homeland (分斷祖國) or hasten political development (政治發展) overlooked the locus of responsibility (責任的所在) for freedom (自由). This indicates that mass public consciousness (大衆的公共意識) is still insufficient, underscoring the urgency (時急性) and necessity (切實性) of democratic (民主的) training (訓練).

We must also consider our economic circumstances (經濟的與件問題). Democracy (民主主義) is predicated on the existence of private economic power (私經濟力) and its fair distribution (公正配分). These two factors must develop in tandem; the absence of either distorts democracy (民主主義). Our economic circumstances (經濟的與件) are still in the early stages of industrialization (產業化). To resolve democratic issues (民主問題), improve overall wealth (全般的富), and foster a civil society (市民社會) led by a healthy middle class (健全中產層), we cannot avoid focusing on industrialization (產業化). This path can sometimes be contradictory to the process of democratization (民主化), and it has also widened the gap between rich and poor (貧富格差). It is for these reasons that the issue of democracy (民主) cannot be separated from the issue of welfare (福祉) at this point in time.

All the points mentioned thus far are inextricably linked to the Korean (韓國的) establishment (定着) of democracy (民主主義).


--- (p. 98) ---

# Korean Obstacles to Democracy and the Saemaul Undong

What may seem to conclude as a Korean theory of obstacles to democracy (대한 장애론), in fact, provides a reference point for the Korean coordinates of democracy (민주주의). When viewed in relation to the Saemaul Undong, this can be summarized in the following points.

First and foremost, it is essential to conduct artificial and organized political socialization (Political Socialization) under a firm belief in the superiority of democracy (민주주의). The process of mass training and internalization for the establishment of democracy is a substantial factor in embedding democracy in this land. The formation of healthy leadership, the establishment of a horizontal cooperative culture that enables discussion and compromise, the universalization of democratic citizens who can exercise freedom and participation as a duty and rights and participation as a responsibility, and the establishment of a social atmosphere that values virtue, common sense, honesty, and diligence—all of these cannot be realized without artificial and organized political socialization. As will be mentioned later, the greatest significance of the phrase "Saemaul Undong as a training ground for the practice of democracy (民主主義의 실천도장)" should be discussed from the perspective of political socialization.

Secondly, democratization (민주화) and industrialization (산업화), or basic rights-oriented freedoms (기본권적 자유권) and survival-oriented freedoms (생존권적 자유권), must be harmoniously realized. Industrialization and democratization are on the same wavelength. For industrialization to be efficiently promoted, it must be driven in a direction that encourages voluntary national participation in economic construction, effectively mobilizing the internal energy of the people. Conversely, for the maturation of democracy, industrialization is indispensable. The maturation of social and economic conditions for the establishment of democracy is impossible without industrialization, and industrialization is also impossible without the voluntary participation of the people.

Here, the 35-year process of democratic transplantation in Korea has significantly contributed to forming Korea's democratic soil. The remark by Walter Lippman that "the government that supplies the most is the best government" is also instructive. In this sense, the Saemaul Undong, as a modernization movement, is understood as a movement for "income increase (소득증대운동)" and a movement for "consciousness revolution (의식혁명운동)" as its main content, contributing to the process of maturing social and economic conditions for the establishment of democracy.

Thirdly, for democracy to take root in Korea, it must be combined with nationalism (민족주의) and...


--- (p. 99) ---

# Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It is not acceptable. Domestically, rather than a break from tradition, we must form a national value system based on cultural pride and the realistic reconstruction of tradition, and establish this as the foundation of democracy. Externally, we must possess political autonomy corresponding to a sovereign state and the flexibility to set our own domestic orientation. Having experienced the initial stage of dialectical self-development, South Korea's liberal democracy has functioned as the most effective counter-element to cosmopolitanism in the short term, and in the long term, it has paved the way for nationalism, which will be the greatest force in South Korea's future. Ultimately, South Korea's democracy signifies the concretization of universality and implies a fusion with nationalism. This proposition directly indicates the nationalization of South Korean democracy, which is rooted in confidence in cultural superiority. It is essential to emphasize that the Saemaul Undong is rooted in the traditional communal consciousness of our society and the revival of regional communities, and that it originated from rural areas.

### B. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and the Indigenization of Democracy

The democratic orientation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has already surpassed the stage of awareness since it began to take root in 1973.

Firstly, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) possesses the basic elements of indigenization of democratic institutions by being carried out through participation and discussion under a leader with "pure leadership," that is, a leader who is highly respected, creative, and dedicated, and is chosen according to the will of the whole community.

Secondly, the benefits gained through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) are fairly distributed and reinvested in common interest projects according to the will of the whole community. This process brings about welfare that manifests overall wealth increase and equality, and holds the promise of the growth of a harmonious interest society. This contributes to the maturation of the socio-economic conditions of democracy, which is directly related to the Saemaul Undong's top-level guiding value orientation of modernization.

Thirdly, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is the product of deliberate organizational efforts to accelerate the establishment of democracy. As previously mentioned, it is a process of political socialization in a broad sense. It is a well-known fact that the establishment of democracy cannot be achieved solely through the promotion of ideology or the transplantation of institutions. For democracy to take root, a process of political socialization for democracy must follow.


--- (p. 100) ---

Fourthly, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) serves as a foundation for fostering regional autonomy. For instance, the Saemaul Undong in rural areas emphasizes the development of the local community, which is a typical example. This is because the concept of "self-reliant village" has been introduced, ensuring not only economic self-sufficiency but also autonomous decision-making within the region. From an institutional perspective, this can serve as a precursor to a local autonomy system, and from a principled perspective, it holds significance as a training ground for "democracy through participation from below."

Fifthly, the Saemaul Undong is also aligned with democracy in its spiritual aspects. "Diligence, self-help, and cooperation" are the basic ideals of our democracy. Diligence provides substantial autonomy based on economic self-sufficiency and is one of the fundamental ethics of capitalism, which has given birth to democracy. Diligence (love and sense of mission for work) is the starting point of Protestant ethics. Moreover, self-help and cooperation without diligence as a premise are meaningless and do not exist. Self-help forms the basis of democracy, which presupposes equality. Those who lack the consciousness of self-help cannot cultivate autonomy, and this applies to both the national and individual realms. Self-help is ultimately the free expression of subjective will towards the realization of "the best" and simultaneously embodies the principle of self-responsibility. The autonomy of individuals, presupposing equality, and the recognition of freedom and responsibility that support it are fundamental requirements of democracy.

Cooperation is a core spiritual element of democracy. Voluntary participation, respect for diversity, an attitude of tolerance, belief in consensus, and community consciousness... All of these are spiritual and cultural requirements of democracy, and their formation is impossible without true cooperation.

Thus, the basic spirit of the Saemaul Undong, namely "diligence, self-help, and cooperation," is intrinsically linked to democracy.


--- (p. 101) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It is the content of spiritual development (精神啓發) and consciousness revolution (意識革命) for settlement (定着). This also becomes another phase (局面) as a political and socialization process (政治社會化過程) in another sense.
As seen so far, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is a path to mature the economic (經濟) and social (社會的) prerequisites (要件) for the settlement (定着) of democracy (民主主義) through industrialization (産業化), and also a path to form a democratic (民主的) political culture (政治文化) through a democratic (民主的) political and socialization process (政治社會化過程).
However, in the process (行程) of localizing (土着化) democracy (民主主義), the highest value (價値) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) lies in the fact that it opens the way for nationalistic (民族主義的) integration (接合) with our democracy (民主主義) of today and the future (將來). The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) itself is a modernization movement (近代化運動) for national revival (民族中興), and ultimately a nationalistic (民族主義) movement (運動) that completes the political (政治的), economic (經濟的), and military (軍事的) autonomy (自主性) of our nation (民族). Therefore, modernization (近代化), which is both a means (手段) and a goal (目標), is not found in a way (方途) that is disconnected (斷絶) from our tradition (傳統), but is found through modern (現代的) recreation (再創造) via connection (連結).

The most important aspect of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is that it aims (指向) to cultivate (涵養) a strong sense of community (共同體意識) and the spirit of cooperation (協同精神) that makes it possible. Its significance lies in the fact that it is not a contractual (契約的) cooperative relationship (協同關係) as in the West (西歐), but a virtue (美德) and custom (慣習) of mutual aid (扶相助) that has been localized (土着化), and a traditional (傳統的) sense of community (共同體意識) based on it.

In the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the will to "live well" does not merely mean having food to eat and clothes to wear, but living a life that is more cultured (文化的), with more leisure (餘裕) and dignity (品位), and not just living well alone, but creating a community where neighbors love and help each other, overflowing with human emotions (人情) and good customs (美風) that have been passed down from olden times in our country.

The reappearance (再現) of such traditional (傳統的) sense of community (共同體意識) is more urgent (切實) not only in the past settled (定住的) agricultural society (農耕社會) but also in today's world where individualism (個人主義) is extreme and identity (正體性) is confused. Some scholars (論者) define our traditional (傳統的) cooperative living structure (協同生活構造) as immature personality (人格的未成熟性) born of emotionalism (情誼主義) and other-consciousness tendency (他人意識性向), and see it as an obstacle (障碍要因) to the settlement (定着) of democracy (民主主義). However, we must recognize (認識) and practice (實踐) emotionalism (情誼主義) as a function (機能) of tolerance (寬容) and strong internal (內的) cohesion (結束力), and other-consciousness (他人意識) as a function (機能) of community consciousness (共同體意識) and respect (尊重) for honor (名譽) with high character (品格). The sense of community (共同體意識), which is the foundation (根幹) of our democracy (民主主義), is like this, our tradition (傳)


--- (p. 102) ---

The task of reinterpreting and shaping our unity (統) according to today's demands and our current situation requires both a powerful internal cohesion and external autonomy. In this sense, the localization of democracy (民主主義) implies a fusion with nationalism (民族主義). Thus, the meaning of democracy (民主主義) as a guiding principle of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) can be described as "national democratic (民族的) democracy (民主主義)."

### 4. Peaceful Unification (統一) of the Fatherland (祖國)

Our history over the past 35 years, marked by national division (分斷), can be explained by the fact that this division has dominated all aspects of our entire society. Internally, all our efforts towards modernization (近代化), industrialization (産業化), and democratization (民主化) have not been able to overcome the fixed limitations imposed by this division. Externally, the fact of division has made the Korean Peninsula a product of power politics among forces with vested interests, placing Korea far from the autonomy enjoyed by normal sovereign states and under the strong influence of international politics. The Korean Peninsula, divided in both territory and legitimacy, has existed as a forward base for the two poles of power politics. Here, the tragedy of fratricide, which may be the greatest shame in our national history, has further intensified the serious threat posed by the confrontational standoff between the two poles.

Unification (統一) is an urgent and fixed goal. However, the issue of unification (統一) is no longer a matter of aspiration but a complex and intricate problem requiring a long and arduous journey of theoretical and practical approaches. Essentially, national revival (民族中興) is impossible without overcoming division (分斷). As a national revival movement (民族中興運動), the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) is also a unification movement (統一運動) in this sense.

#### a. Coordinates (座標) of National Unification (祖國統一)

To examine the issue of unification (統一) as a guiding ideology (指導理念) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), we must first consider several fundamental issues regarding unification (統一), such as its meaning (意味), necessity (當爲性), methods (方法), and the future vision (未來像) of a unified fatherland (統一祖國).

First, the unification (統一) we must achieve is not merely formal unification (形式), i.e., territorial unification (國土), but substantive unification (內容), i.e., national unification (民族統一) that makes our national society (民族社會) substantially one. This problem has become particularly significant due to the past 35 years of North Korea's (北韓) alienation (異質化).


--- (p. 103) ---

# Chapter 2 (第2章) The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

Even if North and South become one, their unity (和合) will not be smooth, which is a serious issue (問題) to consider. North's face is vastly different from our ethnic history's orthodoxy (正統) not only in politics (政治) and economy (經濟), but also in cultural (文化的) aspects. In short, unification (統一) must be a unification (統一) that restores and substantively unites our ethnic orthodoxy (正統).

Next, if we examine why we desperately desire unification (統一), it is because, beyond experiencing various misfortunes (不幸) and pains (苦痛) due to division (分斷), division (分斷) has been a significant constraint (制約) on the promotion (推進) of modernization (近代化), narrowly industrialization (產業化) and democratization (民主化), as indicators (指標) of national revival (民族中興) and national goals (國家目標). Due to division (分斷), there are pains (苦痛) of separated families (離散家族) and defectors to the South, and we have to endure restrictions (制限) on freedom (自由) due to hostile confrontation (敵對的 対峙), making it difficult to form a normal ethnic nation (民族國家形成), forcing our democracy (民主主義) to accept an unavoidable situational logic (狀況論理). For industrialization (產業化), we must maximize (最大限) the use (活用) of the given territory (領土), manpower (人力), and existing resources (賦存資源), but the land (國土) is divided in two, and a large part (部分) of national power (國力) must be spent on preventing ethnic fratricide (民族相殘). In short, division (分斷) is the fundamental obstacle (障碍) to national revival (民族中興), modernization of the motherland (祖國近代化), and as parts (部分) of it, democratization (民主化) and industrialization (產業化).

Furthermore, considering that each surrounding country (周邊國) around the Korean Peninsula (韓半島) is a powerful political force (政治勢力), unification (統一) and stability (安定) of the Korean Peninsula (韓半島) also contribute to peace in Northeast Asia (東北아시아) and the world (世界平和).

Next, considering the methods (方法) of unification (統一), the approach (接近方法) to unification (統一) to overcome the pains (苦痛) and constraints (制約) of division (分斷) must, above all, be achieved through peaceful (平和的) methods (方法). The issue (問題) of unification (統一) is an inter-ethnic (民族間) issue (問題). Having already experienced the bitter fate (悲運) of fratricide (同族相殘), conflicts (紛爭) on the Korean Peninsula (韓半島) will inevitably invite the intervention (介入) of external forces (外部勢力), the surrounding major powers (周邊强大國), and if we experience another fratricide (同族相殘), our ethnic history (民族史) will likely regress by 50 years (年) or 100 years (年). In this sense, unification (統一) must be realized (實現) through peaceful (平和的) methods (方法), and the peaceful (平和的) settlement (定着) of the Korean Peninsula (韓半島) will be the first step. In relation to this, peaceful settlement (平和定着) will also somewhat alleviate the mutual hostility (敵對感) and mistrust (不信) formed by the 35 years (年) of hostile confrontation (敵對的 対峙), thereby addressing the issue (問題) of unification (統一).


--- (p. 104) ---

Creating an atmosphere conducive to peaceful resolution. For this, unification cannot avoid relying on gradual methods, and this gradual approach can help overcome the inter-Korean ethnic divergence that has occurred and contribute to the restoration of ethnic homogeneity. For this, prior exchange and contact between the South and the North are essential. Lastly, unification must depend on a method that opens the way to national prosperity and development, that is, a method aimed at national revival.

Finally, let us examine what the future of a unified homeland should look like.

The unification we desire is a national unification based on historical legitimacy and aimed at the prosperity and development of the entire nation. Therefore, the image of the unified homeland that results from this will, first, guarantee the participation of each individual member of the nation, second, ensure that welfare is evenly distributed to all members of the nation, and third, be a system that secures autonomy externally. Therefore, it will not be a unification with a retrogressive meaning of returning to the state before division, but a highly developed democratic welfare society where autonomy and equality are harmonized.

## II. The Path to Unification and the Saemaul Undong

The issue of unification is not one-sided but bilateral, not static but a delicate and arduous process with a difficult journey ahead. Therefore, it must be based on a clear perspective and foundation. Since the issue of unification is a national issue, the establishment of national consciousness becomes a basic premise for solving the issue of unification. However, in a situation where "I" and "we" are strictly distinguished and have been in chaos, the establishment of national consciousness is not an easy task. North Korea, as part of "us," is the target of integration, but at the same time, it is becoming the most dangerous "other" threatening "our" survival. How should we perceive North Korea? As an object of anti-communism, as an object of unification, it is both "us" and "the other" with two faces. However, ultimately, North Korea cannot be definitively placed outside the category of "us."

The Saemaul Undong has meaning as a process and method of unification. If the establishment of peace is the first step towards unification, then such establishment of peace presupposes the construction of a material and spiritual foundation that can establish peace. The construction of a foundation that can realistically control North Korea's erroneous delusion of communist unification is precisely


--- (p. 105) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It signifies the completion of security awareness (安保意識) and a self-reliant national defense posture (自主國防態勢). The path to this can only be found in the enhancement of national power (國力).

The Saemaul Undong (運動) as a modernization movement (近代化運動) must be viewed in terms of both systemic competition (體制競爭) with the North and the perspective of historical legitimacy (民族史的 正統性). It is no coincidence that our economic power (經濟力) began to show a remarkable superiority over the North starting in the 1970s, the decade when the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) was ignited, established, and spread. The competition between their "socialist (社會主義的) transformation (改造)" and our Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) has already been decided in terms of both the efficiency (效率性) of modernization (近代化) and the perspective of national historical legitimacy (民族正統性). Their method of collectivization (集團化) and nationalization (國有化) has not only completely annihilated our national cultural (民族文化的) heritage (遺産) across the northern land but has also fundamentally changed the character (性格) of both individuals (人間) and families (家庭), making them into "us" who are not like "us," thus darkening the future of national unification (民族統合). In contrast, the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), which views the present as an extension of the past and future and vice versa, embodies deep-rooted national consciousness (民族意識) and national identity (民族正體性). It is a nationalist (民族主義) movement (運動) based on historical legitimacy (民族史的 正統性) that holds promise for national unification (民族統一) and national development (民族發展).

## Section 2: The Concept of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

### 1. The Meaning of a Village (마을의 의미)

For a country or society (社會), it is essential to establish healthy common sense (健康) about life (生活常識) that supports the society (社會). Without this, the society (社會) is doomed to the fate of a house built on sand (砂上樓閣). Therefore, common sense (常識), as the English word suggests, is a common sense of life (生活感覺). We believe that the fundamental spirit (基本精神) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) should not be implemented either in a highbrow (高踏的) academic (學術的) dimension (次元) or at the level of simple, fragmented (斷片的) physical (物理的) actions (行動). Instead, it should be established and deepened (深化) at a moderate (中道) level (位相).

From this point (點), the German (獨逸) nationalist (民族主義) economist (經濟思想家) List (List) also argued that for economic development (經濟發展), the economic consciousness (經濟意識) of the nation (國民) must support it. Not only economic development (經濟發展) but also the development (發展) of a country requires the support of national consciousness (國民意識). This point was emphasized by "List" in his national (國)


--- (p. 106) ---

In the theory of productive forces (Theorie der Produktiven Kräfte), it was strongly argued that "No matter how diligent, thrifty, inventive, entrepreneurial, moral, and intelligent an individual may be, if there is no national unity and no national division of labor and combination of various productive forces, that nation can never achieve a high degree of happiness and power, nor can it secure the perpetual possession of its spiritual, social, and material wealth."

Moreover, he emphasized that for a country to rise as a first-class nation, the integration of national consciousness based on sound common sense is important. He also argued that to develop the nation normally, measures should be taken so that several generations pursue the same goal and their work and efforts are continuously inherited. In other words, he claimed that generations that are to be inherited should combine their strength towards the same purpose and share the necessary efforts among them.

The basic spirit of the Saemaul Undong is based on national common sense and is taken as the basic model for national integration. Moreover, it should not be limited to a model of the contemporary era but should be pursued by several generations with the same goal regarding the basic spirit of the Saemaul Undong, so that this movement can be continuously inherited.

The concept of "maul" (village) formed in the traditional consciousness structure of Koreans is different from the concept of "village" derived from the settlement phenomenon in the case of Westerners. In the dimension of a place where people live, the concept of "maul" does not differ between the East and the West. However, at least the concept of "maul" engraved in the hearts of Koreans has a unique and peculiar character that cannot be found in the Western cultural sphere.

Firstly, to Koreans, "maul" is not merely a settlement phenomenon where people live together for residence, but rather, it more fundamentally implies the character of being the eternal root of life. The concept of "hometown" is a native place of emotional life commonly possessed in the East and the West. However, in the case of Koreans, the concept of "maul" contains the ancestor worship consciousness that cannot be seen in Westerners. Therefore, "maul" is not only a place of material existence but is also represented as a source of spiritual heritage and blood ties. Therefore, at least to Koreans, the village is always represented as the origin of spiritual and blood ties.

Secondly, in the case of Koreans, the village is cozy


--- (p. 107) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

A village as a home approaches each individual. Our village structure (聚落構造) is not separated from nature (自然) as in the case of the West (西洋). Looking at the village structure (聚落構造) of the medieval (中世期) West (西洋), we see that it is separated from the nearby natural environment, with nature and farmland existing outside the castle (城), and the village (聚落) formed artificially (人爲的) around the church village (敎村) within the castle (城). Such a geographical (地理的) living (生活) atmosphere has been continuously passed down (傳承) through the early modern period (近世). However, in the case of Korea (韓國), villages have always created a living environment nestled in the cozy embrace of nature (自然). Therefore, unlike the "village" (village) of the West (西洋), Korean (韓國) villages are not separated from mountains (山頂) or nature (自然), but are generally nestled comfortably at the foot of the mountains (山麓). This is why Koreans have always felt that the village is like a hometown (故鄕) to them. In real life (現實生活), when Koreans are tired or experience unexpected failures (失敗), they almost without exception have an unconscious (無意識的) impulse (衝動) to return to their hometown village and rest (安住).

Analyzing such psychological (心理的) experiences, we can see that the concept (概念) of "village" itself is a spiritual (精神的) and blood-related (血緣的) root for Koreans, and at the same time, a place of rest (休息處) for the mind. It is more appropriate to interpret and explain that this concept (概念) exists for Westerners as well, but with a difference in degree (程度) rather than saying that it does not exist at all (全然). When we attempt to establish the concept (概念定立) of Saemaul Undong (運動) here, there is a deep reason to organize the traditional (傳統的) "village" concept (概念) of Koreans (韓國人). This is because the attitude (態度) towards the village (마을) ultimately explains the essence (本質) of the Saemaul Undong (運動). The organization (整理) of the concept (概念) of the village (마을) is a task (作業) that diagnoses (診斷) the consciousness structure (意識構造) of the people living in that village (마을). Therefore, understanding (理解) the concept (概念) of the "village" (마을) is very important.

### 2. The Spiritual (精神的) Treasure (寶在) of "Li-ren" (里仁)

The poet-saint (詩聖) of India (印度), "Tagore," analyzed the difference between Indian civilization (印度文明) and ancient Greek civilization (希臘文明) through the concept (概念) of the "village" (마을). Indian villages were formed in the jungle, while Greek villages were formed in the city (城) area. The jungle, with its unclear boundaries, is called a "sea of trees" (樹海) because it is like the sea. In an living environment (生活環境) with unclear boundaries (境界), it is inevitable (自然) to regard delusions (妄想) caused by attachment (執着) as taboos (禁忌). The foundation (基礎) of the Buddhist (佛敎的) view of life (人生觀) and worldview (世界觀) comes from villages that have grown (英글) in the atmosphere (氣氛) of the jungle (密林). On the other hand, as a city-state (都市國家), the castle (城) clearly distinguishes (分明) between "my" castle (城) and "your" castle (城). Therefore, the distinction (區別) between you and me becomes


--- (p. 108) ---

An accurate worldview that naturally emphasizes the difference between subjectivity and objectivity, is rationalistic and scientific, begins to emerge. On the other hand, in a village atmosphere akin to a dense forest, the significance of the individual is not particularly great. After all, what meaning can an individual hold in the vast expanse of the sea! Therefore, in a village atmosphere born out of such a dense forest, rather than emphasizing the consciousness of nature as the subject, it nurtures a mentality that is selfless and forgetful of the self. However, it is only natural that in a settlement born out of a bright sun, a bright atmosphere, and a geometric atmosphere of a fortress, people's hearts become geometric and possess the impulse of self-display.

Understanding the Korean perception and sentiment towards the concept of "village" is extremely important in establishing the basic concept of the Saemaul Undong. This is because, as analyzed by Tagore, we can clearly grasp how a village dominates a person's heart. As explained earlier, the Korean concept of a village includes the concept of a spiritual and bloodline root, and at the same time, the concept of a hometown as a resting place for the individual heart. Such a concept of a village is clearly inseparable from the Confucian worldview and philosophy of life. The relationship between the hometown village and the ancestral grave, and between the hometown village and ancestor worship, is inseparable for Koreans, and it cannot be said that this is unrelated to the formation of Confucian sensibilities.

From this perspective, if we summarize our topic, we can say that Confucian worldview always provides an ideal spiritual pattern for the village. This worldview is the "Li-ren (里仁)" worldview.

There is a passage in the "Analects (論語)" "Li-ren Pyeon (里仁篇)" as follows: "A virtuous village is beautiful; if one does not choose to live in a virtuous village, how can one be called wise?" (Li-ren wi-mi (里仁爲美), taek-bul-cheo-in (擇不處仁) eondeukji (焉得知)). Here, we need to analyze the concept of "Li-ren (里仁)" as a concept of a virtuous village or a virtuous village. The concept of "Li-ren (里仁)" or "virtuous village" presupposes that the villagers unite their hearts for a common good of the village. That is, it means that the villagers are spiritually united for the spiritual reality of "Ren (仁)" as a common good of the village.


--- (p. 109) ---

## Chapter 2 (第2章) The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

For a village to be possible, the mental attitude of the people living in the village must become a virtuous village (里仁) from within. Here, a question may arise as to how a person's heart can become a virtuous village (里仁).

### 3. The Context of Village Construction Movement (建設運動)

In general, a person's heart is also a community (共同體) like a village in terms of the relationship of inner spirit (內面的 精神). If a village is interpreted as a relational concept (關係槪念) formed among people, then a person's heart can also be interpreted as a relational concept (關係槪念) with oneself (自己) and one's own self (自身). For example, if the relationship (關係) between oneself (自己) and one's own self (自身) maintains a very intimate (親密) relationship like a close friend, then I naturally express a friendly relationship with others in matters. However, in stark contrast (正反對), if the relationship (關係) between me and myself (自身) is filled with hatred (憎惡) and dislike, then naturally the relationship (關係) between me and others also becomes filled with hatred (憎惡心) and aggression (攻擊心). In this sense, as Aristotle pointed out in his "Nicomachean Ethics (倫理學)," if the relationship (關係) between me and myself (自身) becomes that of a close friend (親友), then the relationship (關係) between me and others also becomes so, and conversely (正反對), if the relationship (關係) between me and myself (自身) becomes that of an enemy (敵), then the relationship (關係) between me and others also becomes so. Therefore, the nature (性質) that grows in the relationship (關係) between me and myself (自身) becomes the original (原本) of the human relationships (人間關係) formed in the relationship (關係) between me and others.

If a village is to be interpreted as a relational concept (關係槪念) between me and others, then such a relationship (關係) is not different from the externalization (外形化) of the relational concept (關係槪念) between me and myself (自身). Therefore, the order (秩序) of my heart colors the order (秩序) of the outer village as a basic (基本) foundation. Thus, if my heart is a spiritual (精神的) and inner (內的) village, then the neighborhood where people reside is an outer village. In this regard, unlike the Indian (印度的) village concept (마을槪念) and the Greek (希臘的) village concept (마을槪念), the traditional (傳統的) village concept (마을槪念) of Koreans (韓國人) has been idealized (象化) as a concept (槪念) of "里仁 (Iin)." For the village of "里仁 (Iin)" to be realized, the "heart" of the village people must first be "里仁 (Iin)-ized" as an inner (內的) and spiritual (精神的) village. This is because the "里仁 (Iin)-ization" of the heart as an inner (內的) village can never establish the "里仁 (Iin)-ization" of the neighborhood as an outer (外的) village without it.

Therefore, the traditional (傳統的) concept (槪念) of the Korean (韓國人) village has been formed based on the Confucian (儒敎的) value (價値) criterion (基準) of "里仁 (Iin)." If we reflect (省察) on this value (價値) criterion (基準), the village must first


--- (p. 110) ---

The Saemaul Undong's fundamental aspiration is to cultivate a community where people's hearts are transformed into "Liin (里仁)" (a virtuous and benevolent community). It begins with cultivating one's own heart into an "virtuous village," then extending this to the household, and ultimately to the nation and the world, harboring the grand ideal of transforming the world into a "Liin (里仁)" community.

Then, what relationship does the concept of the Saemaul Undong have with our traditional ideal concept of "Liin (里仁)"? Such ideal concepts were strongly highlighted in the Silla society through "Dure," in the Goryeo society through "Do (徒)" or "Sa (社)," and in the Joseon society through "Hyangyak (鄕約)," among others. "Dure," "Do (徒)," "Sa (社)," and "Hyangyak (鄕約)" all shared a common strategy of establishing healthy social values through the establishment of sound human life values.

Thus, socio-economic mutual aid was traditionally emphasized as not being a matter to be discussed separately from human ethical and spiritual order. Since this is not the place to elaborate on "Dure," the "Sa (社)" of the Goryeo period, or the "Hyangyak (鄕約)" of the Joseon period, we will refrain from further discussion on this matter. However, even taking one representative example, the "Hyangyak (鄕約)" of the Joseon period, we see that economic mutual aid and the formation of a communal prosperity zone in life order are manifested through social norms, but all such movements ultimately do not transcend the dimension of the "virtuous village" spirit order, which we have already discussed above as "Liin (里仁)ic (的)".

The concept of the Saemaul Undong is not different from our historical traditional examples of "Dure," "Do (徒)," "Sa (社)," or "Hyangyak (鄕約)." Therefore, if we explain the concept of the Saemaul Undong in terms of spiritual order, it should be understood within the context of the ideal of "Liin (里仁)ization," which is the traditional Korean concept of the village.

## 4. Modern Definition of a Village

However, this alone does not fully explain the concept of the Saemaul Undong. We must not forget that the Saemaul Undong has added unique elements distinct from the past "Dure," "Do (徒)," "Sa (社)," or "Hyangyak (鄕約)."

The practical learning ideology has added new elements of realism and pragmatism (實事求是) and the idea of enriching people's lives (利用厚生) to the concept of "Liin (里仁)" in "Hyangyak (鄕約)."


--- (p. 111) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) strongly imposed a progressive meaning. Thus, it aimed at a concrete, welfare-oriented, and scientific approach to the rehumanization of villages, targeting the rural areas that had fallen into the malady of idealization, which had begun to lose their creativity during the Joseon Dynasty (朝鮮朝). However, the Silhak Movement (實學運動), which was a precursor, remained merely an exercise and failed to revitalize the stagnant rural areas that had been in decline for a long time since the Joseon Dynasty (朝鮮朝) society. As a result, our rural areas, mired in the poverty of self-reliance from the Joseon Dynasty (朝鮮朝) society, could not improve their constitution even after the Silhak period (實學時代), and, as expressed by the late President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), our rural areas had been soaked in traditional bad habits for several centuries, for several hundred years. Thus, the term that had become synonymous with rural areas in a traditional sense was stagnation. (Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) Presidential Speeches (演說文集), "Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)," p.372)

Before the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) began, our rural areas were characterized by long-standing poverty, ignorance, and social indifference, showing no signs of proactiveness or ambition, and were in a state of stagnation. (Same Presidential Speeches (演說文集)) Furthermore, farmers had resigned themselves to the fact that no matter how hard they worked, they could not become wealthy, and reliance on others, laziness, and idleness were rampant in every corner of the rural areas. As a result, the healthy and productive concept of "ri-in" (里仁) disappeared, and the idea of "ri-in" (里仁) villages as a hometown concept (故鄕槪念) remained only in dreams or in the romanticism of the East, while reality became a mere poor, powerless, and despairing village.

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was launched to socialize the concept of "ri-in" (里仁), aiming to activate spiritual and social orders, similar to the past "dure" (두레) and "hyangyak" (鄕約). Thus, the late President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙) emphasized that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was not merely an economic movement to eliminate poverty but rather a national spiritual movement that targeted the roots of the problem. Therefore, the purpose of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is to drive out stagnant, lazy, dependent, and defeated minds and renew them first with progressive, diligent, independent, and willful minds, ultimately aiming to rehumanize the outer village in a new dimension.

However, even if the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) targets the newly renewed "ri-in" (里仁) movement, this alone is not sufficient to fully explain the concept of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). This is because


--- (p. 112) ---

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) is a movement aimed at modernizing our countryside, which is the spiritual homeland of our nation. Although the Saemaul Undong may evoke a traditional spiritual revolution, the spiritual "Li-in (里仁)" transformation does not necessarily promise industrialization, scientification, and modernization based on practicality and the betterment of people's lives. This is because traditional spiritual exemplars like the "Dure" and "Hyangyak (鄕約)" (village compacts), while historically significant, cannot alone serve as the foundation for modernization, industrialization, and scientification.

In this regard, the concept of the Saemaul Undong can be summarized in two points. First, it is a spiritual revolution aimed at igniting the creative spirit of villagers who have been in a state of exhaustion due to the decline of national power. Second, it is a movement to revitalize the ideals of practical learning, such as the betterment of people's lives and practicality, and to transform them into modern scientific and industrial actions. Therefore, without fostering a new order of the mind, the creation of new villages (spiritual revolution and modernization) cannot succeed. Renewing the order of the mind is not merely a matter of theoretical injection but is achieved through actions and practices that evoke experiential empathy and universal resonance. In this sense, the numerous Saemaul leaders in the countryside and cities of this land are proud actors and excellent practitioners who have evoked such empathy and resonance.

### 第3節 勤勉• 自助 • 協同의 精神

#### 1. Traditional Sublimation: The Spiritual Pillar

We have already examined how the concept of the Saemaul Undong encompasses both the character of "Li-in (里仁)" transformation as a spiritual revolution and the content of modernization (industrialization + scientification). When we consider these two essential aspects together, the guiding ideology of the Saemaul Undong emerges. When the late President Park Chung-hee proposed diligence, self-help, and cooperation as the guiding ideology of the Saemaul Undong, these ideals simultaneously encompassed the ideology of "Li-in (里仁)" transformation as a spiritual revolution and modernization as an industrial revolution.


--- (p. 113) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

To succeed in modernization (近代化), a nation needs not only scientific (科學化) and industrial (產業化) advancements but also a spiritual revolution (精神革命). Thus, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) can be seen as a grand creative movement that aims to integrate the spiritual virtues of our traditionalism (傳統主義) with the strengths of Western (西洋的) modern states (近代國家). It seeks to establish Korean democracy (韓國民主主義) and create a unique form of Korean capitalism (韓國的資本主義). Without delving into a lengthy explanation of the fusion of traditional (傳統的) village concepts and democracy (民主主義), we must reflect on how the spirit of traditional (傳統的) ethical concepts like "Dure" and "Hyangyak" (鄕約) meets the spirit of modern (近代) capitalism (資本主義) within the guiding ideology of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

The spirit of modern (近代) capitalism (資本主義精神) (industrialization (產業化) + scientific advancement (科學化)) has several characteristics that contributed to the success of Western (西歐) modernization (近代化).

Firstly, the spirit of capitalism (資本主義) signifies a shift in attitude towards profit-seeking compared to the feudal era (封建主義). While the modernizing spirit (近代化) rejects the view that profit-seeking is inherently immoral (惡), it does not condone unrestrained impulses. Instead, it transforms the spirit of profit-seeking into an ethos (ethos), or professional ethics. As symbolized by Franklin, modernizing spirit (近代化) and capitalistic spirit (資本主義化) are embodied in economic ethics (倫理) such as diligence, simplicity, frugality, and prudent living, encapsulated in the phrase "Close Up."

Secondly, the symbol of modern spirit (近代精神), capitalism (資本主義), and industrialization (產業化) justifies profit-seeking through the continuous performance of rational (合理的) economic activities (經濟行爲), which requires strict discipline and training. This distinction clarifies the difference between adventurous profit-seeking (冒險的營利主義) and rational capitalism (合理的資本主義).

Thirdly, to engage in rational (合理的) economic activities (經濟行爲) under strict discipline, there must be universally applicable (普遍) living standards (生活). Economic activities (經濟行爲) should not vary based on social status (身分的差別), blood ties (血緣), or regional ties (地緣). In other words, if economic activities (經濟行爲) and ethics (倫理) differ based on blood ties (血緣), regional ties (地緣), and academic ties (學緣), rational (合理的) living ethics (生活倫理) cannot be established, and modernization (近代化) cannot succeed. As Max Weber pointed out, the so-called "inner morality" (對內道德) (Binnen


--- (p. 114) ---

Internal morality (內道德) and external morality (對外道德) (Aubenmoral) are well separated, so within the scope of blood ties (血緣) and geographical ties (地緣), affection (溫情) overflows beyond self-interest (利害關係). However, outside this scope, deceit (詐欺) and theft (竊盜) are committed against other groups (集團), preventing the formation of universal economic ethics (經濟倫理). This makes it difficult to achieve the spirit (精神) of modernization (近代化). Therefore, the ideal type (理想型) of modernization (近代化) is a person who is diligent in their own duties (己職務) regardless of social status (身分), a life person (生活人) who achieves success (成功).

While we have briefly examined the spirit (精神) of capitalism (資本主義) as a symbol (象徵) of modernization (近代化), we do not advocate for early capitalism (資本主義) that disregards welfare (福祉) and well-being (厚生) in daily life (生活上). Instead, through the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), we aim to implement socialization (社會化) in hygiene (衛生) and welfare (福祉), learning the motivational factors (原因動機) or achievement motivation (成就動機) of modernization (近代化) from the spirit (精神) of capitalism (資本主義). Therefore, the capitalist achievement motivation (資本主義的成就動機) resulting from the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) as a fruit of modernization (近代化) does not contradict the demands of socialization (社會化) and welfare (福祉化).

Rather, the basic spirit (基本精神) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)—diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同)—promotes the activation (活性化) of the traditional (傳統的) spirit of "ri-in" (里仁) and accelerates the formation (形成) of a modern nation-state (近代國家). It also helps build a spiritual foundation (精神基盤) for socialization (社會化) and welfare (福祉化) based on the spirit of ri-in (里仁精神), while fostering capitalist achievement motivation (資本主義的成就動機).

The ideal (理想) of our traditional (傳統的) village concept (마을槪念), "ri-in" (里仁), is deeply rooted in Confucian (儒敎的) patterns (性向). As Max Weber warned, this can lead to the risk (危險性) of distinguishing between "internal morality" (對內道德) among kin (親族), blood ties (血緣), and geographical ties (地緣), and "external morality" (對外道德) applied to those outside this category (範疇). This results in vastly different qualities (質) of human relationships (人間關係) between those we know and those we do not. Such tendencies (性向) pose a significant obstacle (障礙要因) to the formation (形成) of a modern civil state (近代市民國家) that must objectively regulate (規律化) society (社會).

However, the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), interpreted as a new extension (延長線上) of dure (두레) and hyangyak (鄕約), can positively contribute to the socialization (社會化) and welfare (福祉化) of life (生活) through the spirit (精神) of cooperative ideals (協同理念) derived from the co-existence ideals (共存理念) of dure (두레) and the mutual aid ideals (相扶相助) of hyangyak (鄕約).

Therefore, the basic spirit (基本精神) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)—diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同)—triggers a capitalist achievement motivation (資本主義的成就動機) not found in the traditional (傳統的) ri-in (里仁的) communal view (共同體觀) and also stimulates traditional (傳統的) communal (共同)


--- (p. 115) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

This chapter also sheds light on the ideology of cultivating a culture of mutual prosperity (公榮), coexistence (共存), and empathic peace (共感的和平) based on a great-unity (大同的) cooperation (協同) that is faithful to the ideal (理想) of the body (體). Therefore, it can be said that while diligence (勤勉) and self-help (自助) emphasize modernizing (近代化) and industrializing (産業化) motivations and life ethics (生活倫理) from a capitalist (資本主義的) perspective relatively strongly, cooperation (協同) places more emphasis on the welfare (福祉) and primalization (原生化) of life (生活) for the maturation of a village-ren (里仁的) community (共同體).

### 2. The Logic of Spreading the Desire for Achievement (成就意欲)

There is a saying, "Heaven helps those who help themselves." To escape poverty, defeat, dependence, regression, and ignorance and to possess the substance (實質) of a modern state (近代國家), one cannot remove long-standing outdated customs (因襲) without the capitalist (資本主義的) motivations for achievement (成就動機) of diligence (勤勉) and self-help (自助).

In other words, this is a kind of social movement (社會化運動) that seeks to revive the traditional (傳統的) values (價値觀) of "village-ren" (里仁), such as mutual prosperity (共榮), coexistence (共存), and a shared destiny (共同運命), to overcome the selfish greed (利己的) that modernization (近代化) can bring. Such a social movement (社會化運動) has manifested as the spirit (精神) of labor-management mutual prosperity (勞使共榮) and the policy (政策) of labor-management parallel advancement (勞使併進) in the factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動). Although the ideology (理念) of such a Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) has not fully and perfectly blossomed in a mature manner, it is a fact that a conscientious (良心的) consensus (合意) on such a spirit (精神) has matured (成熟) over the past 10 years.

However, no matter how much the guiding ideology (指導理念) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) sheds light on both traditional (傳統的) "village-ren" (里仁) society (社會) and modernizing society (近代化社會) in a dualistic (兩價的) manner, this movement cannot succeed without leaders of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) who have strong action power (行動力) as their axis to realize such a guiding ideology (指導理念). That is, without a devoted (獻身的) actor (行動人) who can overcome social discrimination (克服) against farmers (農民) and working-class people (勤勞階層) caused by long-term stagnation, ignorance (無知) through education (敎育), increased income (所得增大), and life anxiety (不安) brought by social instability (不安定), the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) of the past 10 years could not have achieved success under difficult conditions.

In this regard, even if the fundamental spirit (基本精神) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) based on diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) is a combination (妙合) of traditional (傳統的) values (價値觀) such as the creation (創造) of a "village-ren society" (里仁社會) overflowing with reason (順理) and human nature (人情) and the values (價値觀) needed for the modernization movement (近代化運動), it is undeniable that the patriotic (救國的) devotion (獻身) of Saemaul Undong leaders (새마을指導者) is necessary for such a guiding ideology (指導理念) to take root in the spiritual soil (土壤) of this land.


--- (p. 116) ---

However, we must more fundamentally examine the popular foundation that allows the acceptance of the guiding ideology of the Saemaul leaders. This foundation can be interpreted from two perspectives. One is the active foundation of the populace, and the other is the passive foundation of popular psychology. The passive foundation of popular psychology is the unconscious hope for the creation of a society overflowing with "humanity and righteousness," an ideal that has grown within our nation's long cultural tradition, often referred to as the "virtuous village."

The reason why the guiding ideology of the Saemaul Undong has been actively accepted by popular psychology is directly connected to the issue of liberating the deep-seated "han" (a Korean term for a collective feeling of unresolved resentment and sorrow) that our this-worldly nation has profoundly experienced. Without elaborating on why our nation possesses a stronger this-worldly nature than an other-worldly one, if we premise that our nation is this-worldly, then the populace of this land has lived experiencing this-worldly dissatisfaction, or "han," stemming from poverty, ignorance due to lack of education, social discrimination arising from ignorance and poverty, and social instability and chaos.

The Saemaul guiding ideology, expressed through diligence, self-help, and cooperation, has placed great emphasis on transcending the absolute sense of defeat stemming from the populace's deeply rooted "han" and elevating the proactive spirit of forging one's destiny. The Saemaul leaders, embodiments of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, launched the Saemaul Undong based on a devoted philosophy of action. The underlying psychology behind their actions is that they, like the populace of this land, are possessors of absolute "han." Therefore, this guiding ideology carries a historical mission to overcome the absolute poverty, ignorance, instability, and alienation that have been synonymous with stagnation, laziness, and despair for hundreds of years in this land, aiming to create a true "virtuous village," a society overflowing with "humanity and righteousness," and to achieve the success of modernization by overcoming existing absolute "han."

Over the past decade, the Saemaul Undong has embarked on its journey with this complex character, shaped by history and society. Now, it should serve as a mirror for reflection, polishing the actions and footsteps of the past ten years to become the foundation of a national philosophy of life.


--- (p. 117) ---

## Section 4: Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Consciousness Revolution (意識革命)

### 1. Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Political Consciousness (政治意識)

#### a. Democratic Training (民主訓練) for Cultivating Leadership (主導力培養)

Is the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) a political movement (政治運動) or a social movement (社會運動) completely unrelated to politics (政治)? Those who actively support (支持) and participate (參與) in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) emphasize that it is a movement for the well-being of the people (國民), focusing on improving rural (農村) environments, increasing income (所得增大), promoting a spiritual revolution (精神革命), social reform (社會改造), and national revival (民族中興). On the other hand, those who criticize (批判) and underestimate (過少評價) the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) argue that it was initiated for the political (政治的) motive (動機) of strengthening the regime (政權强化) and served the political (政治) purpose (目的) of long-term rule (長期執權), making it a government-sponsored (官製) national movement (國民運動) that lacks the inherent (自體) strength (力) to sustain (持續) itself.

To discuss the political nature (政治性) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), it is essential first to clarify the concept (槪念) of politics (政治). In a narrow sense (狹意), politics (政治) refers to the actions (行爲) of individuals or groups related to acquiring (獲得) and maintaining (維持) political power (政治權力). Here, the formation (形成) and concretization (具體化) of national will (國民的意思), as well as conflicts (葛藤) and antagonisms (對立) among individuals or groups, are prominent features (樣相) of politics (政治). In a broader sense (廣意), politics (政治) is understood as collective actions (集團行爲) aimed at securing (圖謀) the survival (生存) and prosperity (繁榮) of the nation (民族), as well as the security (安全) and development (發展) of the state (國家). In this context, politics (政治) is understood as actions (行爲) that foster (圖謀) national consensus (國民的合意基盤) for the stability (安定) of people's livelihoods (民生) and national development (國家發展), promoting (促進) national integration (民族的統合) and collective cooperation (集團的協同). This seems to be the subjective (主體的) concept (槪念) of politics (政治) that should be highlighted (浮刻) in the reality (現實) of Korea (韓國). The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is unrelated to the narrow (狹意) political concept (政治槪念) of acquiring (獲得) and maintaining (維持) political power (政權). Therefore, participants in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) would not be concerned as long as any regime (政權) does not intentionally (故意的) suppress (抑壓) or obstruct (妨害) it. However, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) cannot be indifferent to the dignity (自尊) and prosperity (繁榮) of the nation (民族) or the security (安全) and development (發展) of the state (國家). In reality, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is a national movement (國民運動) targeting ( 겨냥하는) the modernization (近代化) of the fatherland (祖國) and the cultivation (培養) of national strength (國力), ultimately aiming to open (열자) the historical (歷史) chapter (歷史) of national revival (民族中興).

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) today is engaged in fulfilling various national (國家的) tasks (課題) and historical (歷史的) missions (使命).


--- (p. 118) ---

As a national movement (國民運動), its goals (目標), roles (役割), and functions (機能) hold significant meaning for many people. Given its comprehensive (全包括的) and multipurpose (多目的的) nature, the concept (槪念) of this national movement (國民運動) is prone to confusion (混同). Therefore, it is essential to clarify the objectives (目標), purposes (趣旨), and functions (機能) embedded in this term.

*   **Politics (政治)**
    *   Catalyst for political breakthroughs (政局打開) - Movement to accelerate national strength cultivation (國力培養) - Peaceful unification movement (平和統一運動) - Comprehensive national movement (國民總和運動) -
    *   Local autonomy movement (住民自治運動) - Intra-civil rights democratic movement (民權內民主主義運動) - New nation-building movement (國家建設運動)
*   **Economy (經濟)**
    *   National movement to eradicate poverty (國民皆勞運動) - Movement to improve living standards (運動) - Income augmentation movement (所得增大運動) - Productivity enhancement (生産性向上)
    *   Production increase movement (增產運動) - Cost reduction movement (原價節約運動) - Frugality and savings movement (勤儉貯蓄運動) - Welfare movement (厚生福祉運動)
*   **Society (社會)**
    *   Environmental improvement movement (環境改善運動) - Environmental beautification movement (環境美化運動) - Regional community development movement (地域社會開發運動) - Movement to establish three major orders (3大秩序確立運動) - Social purification movement (社會淨化運動)
    *   Neighborhood mutual aid movement (隣保相助運動)
*   **Culture (文化)**
    *   Spiritual revolution movement (精神革命運動) - National character reform movement (國民性格改造運動) - Rationalization and modernization movement (合理化·近代化運動) - Movement to establish national self-reliance (民族的自主性確立運動)
*   **History (歷史)**
    *   Movement to establish national self-reliance (民族的自主性確立) and national revival (民族中興運動) - National great leap forward movement (國民的一大躍進運動) for historical abbreviation (歷史短縮)
    *   Movement to pursue national reconciliation (國民的和解) and integration (統合), opening a new era (時代) through historical creation (歷史創造運動)

Here, we must examine the interrelationships (相關關係) between politics (政治), economy (經濟), society (社會), culture (文化), and history (歷史). History (歷史) is a process (過程) of self-expression (自己示顯) of the people's (民衆的) vital force (生命力). Politics (政治) is a product (産物) of history (歷史) and also a driving force (原動力) for new historical creation (歷史創造).
Economy (經濟) and society (社會) exist (存在) and change (變化) under the protection (保護), command (指揮), and control (統制) of politics (政治). Culture (文化) grows (成長) and blossoms (開花) on the foundation (土臺) of economy (經濟) and society (社會), but it cannot be free from the regulation (規制) and guidance (指導) of politics (政治). Conversely (逆로), it determines the direction (方向) of political change (政治變化) and historical creation (歷史創造), exerting a significant influence (影響) on political change (政治變化) and development (發展). In short, politics (政治) influences the development direction (發展方向) and character formation (性格形成) of economy (經濟), society (社會), culture (文化), and education (教育), leading (主導) historical creation (歷史創造). Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) must be seen as a political movement (政治運動) that exists (存續) under the protection (保護) and guidance (指導) of politics (政治) and exerts a decisive (決定的) influence (影響) on it.

**B. Practical Movement (實踐運動) of Political (政治的) Subject Concept (主體槪念)**

The Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) initially began as a rural environmental improvement movement (農村環境改善運動) called "New Village Beautification Movement (運動)" and expanded into a income augmentation movement (所得增大運動) called "Rural Prosperity Movement (農村 잘 살기 운동)" and a spiritual development movement (精神啓發運動). Due to this evolution, it was sometimes mistakenly perceived as a movement (運動) unrelated to politics (政治). However, this is not the case. If we consider the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) as a patriotic (愛國愛族) political movement (運動), it becomes a rich (豊富) and multi-dimensional (次元) endeavor.


--- (p. 119) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

This should be seen as a practical expression of political consciousness. In other words, the Saemaul Undong is a philosophy of life and a philosophy of practice. Therefore, we have referred to the Saemaul Undong as a practical dojang (training ground) for the localization of Korean democracy. In the past, when people thought of democracy, they associated it with presidential and National Assembly elections, and the opposition between ruling and opposition parties within the National Assembly and factional struggles within political parties. After holding elections, which involved all sorts of waste, mutual defamation, and absurdity, the general public would leave everything to the government and merely observe the opposition and factional struggles within the National Assembly as if they were someone else's business.

However, the Saemaul Undong is not a nominal, formal democracy that elects a president and National Assembly members every four or six years and then remains indifferent. It aims at a democracy where all members of society participate directly and cooperate in deciding all issues. The reason why this can be a practical dojang for the localization of Korean democracy is as follows:

The Saemaul Undong is not something done by a supreme leader or a small number of people, but is carried out with the participation of all villagers. The villagers first gather to elect village leaders. The elected leaders synthesize the opinions of all people to select projects that will benefit the entire village. Then, all villagers work together, cooperate, and promote joint projects. The results obtained here are fairly distributed among the villagers, and part of them is saved as a village common fund with the consent of the villagers. Then, what to do with this is put to the deliberation of the villagers again. In this way, villagers jointly participate in, discuss, decide on, and execute productive and constructive matters.

As the Saemaul Undong began to take shape, the following five-stage process was formalized:

[Diagram: Saemaul Undong 5-Stage Process]

**Saemaul Undong 5-Stage Process:**

| Stage | Upper Content            | Lower Content            |
| :-- | :------------------- | :------------------- |
| 1   | Ignition Stimulus (點火刺戟)   | Support of Materials (資材的支援) |
| 2   | Village General Assembly (總會)      | Selection of Projects (事業的選擇) |
| 3   | Planning Establishment (計畫樹立)   | Exploration of Methods (方法的摸索) |
| 4   | Cooperative Work (協同作業)   | Efforts of Cooperation (協同的努力) |
| 5   | Completion of Projects (事業完工) | (N/A)        |


--- (p. 120) ---

Vitalism cannot be distinguished from ideology. What Korea (韓國) requires today is not national security (安保) and urgent livelihood issues, but rather the power struggles and jockeying for position among professional politicians (職業政治人) and social leaders (社會有志), their baseless confrontations (對立), divisions (分裂), waste (浪費), and incitement (煽動). What is far more necessary is the revitalization (振作) of national morality (國民道義) and national spirit (民族正氣), the organization (組織化) of national life (國民生活) for national construction (國家建設) and social reconstruction (社會再建), and a spiritual revolution (精神革命). Therefore, when we accept this as the subjective (主體的) concept (槪念) of politics (政治), the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) is a political movement (政治運動) demanded by our current situation (現實狀況) and is supported by a high-level (高次元) political consciousness (政治意識).

### Da. Political Environment Purification (政治風土醇化) and Base Expansion Movement (基盤擴大運動)

Following the 10.26 incident (事態) and the passing of President (大統領) Park Chung-hee (朴正熙), the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) fell into a state of stagnation (沈滯狀態). With the inauguration (就任) of President (大統領) Chun Doo-hwan (全斗煥) as the 11th (第11代) president, the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) began to revitalize (活性化) once more. The Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) of the new era (時代) and new society (社會) has obtained an opportunity (契機) to expand (擴大) and develop (發展) by inheriting (繼承) the good points of the past (過去), rectifying (是正) and supplementing (補完) its shortcomings (未洽). To do so, it must transcend (超越) the limited forms (形態) of past (過去) village democracy (部落民主主義) and the kindergarten (幼稚園) stage of urban (都市) Saemaul, proving (證明) its usefulness (有用性) as a national movement (國民運動) for achieving (達成) the national goals (國家目標) of a new era (時代) and new country (國家). The ambitions (抱負) and statesmanship (經綸) of the president (大統領) leading the new era (年代) of the 1980s (年代) in his administration (國政) can be diagrammed (圖式化) as follows.

<Table 1>
[Diagram: National Administration Indicators for a New Era and New Country]
