**Diagram Explanation:**
<Table 1> National Administration Indicators (國政指標) for a New Era (時代) and New Country (國家)

*   **Ultimate Goal:** Construction (建設) of a democratic welfare state (民主福利國家)
*   **Three Major Indicators:**
    *   Indigenization (土着化) of democracy (民主主義)
    *   Construction (建設) of a welfare society (福祉社會)
    *   Realization (具顯) of a just society (正義社會)
*   **Common Sub-indicator:** Educational innovation (敎育革新) and reform (改造) of national spirit (國民精神) and national character (國民性格)

Whether the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) can continue to expand (擴大) and develop (發展) depends on how much its goals (目標) and functions (機能) are further advanced (高度化) compared to those of the past (過去). Will it be able to penetrate (浸透) all levels of society (各界各層)?


--- (p. 121) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The success of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) depends on how much enthusiastic (熱誠的) response (呼應) and active (積極的) support (支持) it can garner. The past (過去) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) had remained at the level of environmental improvement (環境改善), income increase (所得增大), labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), and establishment of order (秩序確立) in urban life (都市生活), which seems to have been problematic.

Environmental improvement (環境改善) had been carried out to the extent possible given the economic conditions (經濟與件) at the time. Income increase (所得增大) is related to the domestic and international (國內外) economic situation (經濟實情) and the government's (政府) budget scale (豫算規模), so it is something that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) alone cannot address. Labor-management cooperation (勞使協調) cannot expect improvement in workers' treatment (待遇改善) unless productivity (生產性) improves and corporate (企業) profits (利潤) increase. The establishment of order (秩序確立) in urban life (都市生活) had the limitation (制限點) of only applying to a minority (少數) of those who were inconsiderate (沒知覺) and lacked education (敎養).

Unless these limitations (制限) are overcome, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) will struggle to gain broad support (支持) and response (呼應) from all sectors of society (各界各層), and it will also fail to contribute to mobilizing (動員), organizing (組織化), and enlightening (啓蒙) the public (國民大衆) to achieve new national (國家) goals (目標). Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) of the 1980s (年代) implies that it cannot grow and develop (發展) without being backed by high-level (高次元) political awareness (政治意識) and strong (强力) government (政府) support (支援).

This means that, moving forward, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) must make a decisive (決定的) contribution to achieving sub-goals (下位)(手段的) such as the localization (土着化) of democracy (民主主義), the construction (建設) of a welfare society (福祉社會), the realization (具現) of a just (正義) society (社會), educational reform (敎育革新), and cultural development (文化暢達) to realize the national (國家) ideology (國家理念) of building a democratic welfare state (民主福祉國家) proposed by President Kim (金大統領). Thus, it can grow and develop (成長發展).

To achieve the localization (土着化) of democracy (民主主義), the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) must prove (證明) its value (價値) as a national (國民) movement (運動) that can supplement (補完) the institutional (制度的) mechanisms (裝置) of Western-style (西歐的) constitutional democracy (立憲民主主義). It should be a grassroots (最下單位) movement (運動) that builds up from the bottom of politics (政治) and society (社會) to the top, a national self-governance (國民自治) movement (運動).

Furthermore, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) should be a national (國民) movement (運動) that supplements (補完) the shortcomings (未備點) of social welfare policies (社會福祉政策) implemented by the government (政府) with enormous (莫大) budgets (豫算). It must contribute (寄與) to forming (形成) a national (國民) character (國民性格) that blesses (祝福) all citizens (國民) with a spiritual (精神) attitude (姿勢) to receive (福) blessings (福), and it should accumulate (積) achievements (實績) as a social welfare (社會福祉) movement (運動).

Moreover, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) of the new era (時代) must grow and expand (擴大) as a national (國民) movement (運動) for the realization (具現) of social justice (社會正義) by eliminating (除去) all kinds of (各種) injustice (不正), corruption (腐敗), irregularities (非理), and social (社會的) irrationalities (不條理) through social purification (社會淨化). All citizens (國民) must take the lead in building (建設) a just (正義) society (社會) where each individual (各己) fulfills (達) their social (社會的) duties (責務) and roles (役割), and each person (各者) receives a fair (正當) and just (公正) reward (報償).


--- (p. 122) ---

In the 1970s, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was known as the "Well-Living Movement" and the "Spiritual Revolution Movement." However, in the 1980s, the Saemaul Undong should be emphasized and highlighted as a movement for national self-governance (localization of democracy), a welfare society movement, a movement to realize social justice, and a movement to strengthen national spirit. While the previous Saemaul Undong merely put forth various slogans, from now on, it should be established as an ideology of a higher dimension and be concretized in the daily lives of the citizens. This is a problem that can only be possible if driven by a solid political consciousness of the citizens.

## 2. Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Economic Consciousness

### a. Expression of Active Economic Consciousness

The Saemaul Undong was not merely a movement that emerged and served the economic motives of national economic growth, improvement of corporate productivity, or enhancement of national welfare. However, it cannot be denied that it was stimulated by the economic situation of our country and started, growing and developing through the economic consciousness. To correctly understand the causes and background of the emergence and growth of the Saemaul Undong, let's review its process of occurrence, growth, and development.

After the May 16 Military Revolution in the 1960s, under the leadership of President Park Chung-hee, South Korea achieved remarkably rapid economic growth. However, during this period, the gap between the rich and the poor widened, and the gap between urban and rural areas deepened, resulting in a serious disconnect between the government leadership and the general public. Among these issues, the poverty and desolation of the countryside remained a serious problem for our national development for the following reasons.

First, as long as South Korea's rural areas continue to be poor and backward, they will continue to be excluded from the domestic consumption market, hindering the development of South Korea's industry. Even if the overseas market continues to expand, it will not be a big problem. However, from our perspective, we cannot pursue industrialization by relying solely on the overseas consumption market without expanding the domestic consumption market. If there is a market to be developed in the domestic consumption market, it is only the local areas and rural areas where a considerable number of the population still live. Therefore, the government should prioritize rural revitalization.


--- (p. 123) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Given the circumstances, it became impossible not to devise some interim measures. Considering the government's budget scale, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was conceived as a way to promote rural development without spending a large amount of money.

Secondly, political instability and social chaos that persisted in the shadow of rapid economic growth would undoubtedly expose social vulnerabilities in the context of inter-Korean confrontation.

Thirdly, the impoverishment and poverty of rural areas had been promoting the overpopulation of urban areas by pushing the rural population into major cities. As long as rural areas remained regions of relative deprivation, government efforts to prevent population concentration in Seoul were bound to fail. Moreover, due to the low productivity of rural areas, the government had to import about $100 million worth of food annually, exacerbating the shortage of foreign exchange.

Given these realities, the government could not avoid making a major decision to address the backwardness and poverty of rural areas. The government first focused on rural environmental improvement projects, which began as the Saemaul beautification project, focusing on village environmental improvement during the farming off-season from October 1970 to June 1971. To promote this project nationwide, the government supported each village unit with 335 units of cement, which was surplus due to overproduction and export stagnation. The government instructed each village to consult and work together to improve the rural environment. Later, the government promised additional support benefits if outstanding results were achieved in the Saemaul projects decided and promoted by each village. This is how the Saemaul beautification competition spread nationwide.

By 1972, based on the lessons learned from the 1971 Saemaul beautification project, the direction and methods of promotion were systematized. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) evolved to promote spiritual development of residents through environmental improvement and to achieve income growth on this new spiritual foundation. Why did the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) subsequently spread and grow rapidly nationwide?

The first reason is that it was initiated by President Park Chung-hee, who was born the son of a poor farmer, with the national policy of rural revitalization and poverty eradication.


--- (p. 124) ---

As the primary task, we must examine Park Chung-hee's (朴正熙大統領) determination to achieve national revival (民族中興) through a national movement (國民運動). We must also acknowledge the efforts of central and local government officials who worked diligently to maximize their administrative capabilities (行政能力) in accordance with the President's (大統領) intentions.

Secondly, we must consider the village leaders (指導者) who took an interest in overcoming rural poverty (貧困) and backwardness (落後性), dedicating themselves to improving their village's (自己) prestige (名譽) and welfare (福祉) through the "well-living" movement.

Thirdly, we must recognize the residents (住民) who enthusiastically participated in response to the government's (政府) active enlightenment (啓蒙) and support (支援).

It was the synergy of these three elements—President (大統領), village leaders (指導者), and residents (住民)—that led to the success of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).

The Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) can be broadly divided into rural (農漁村) and urban (都市) movements. The urban Saemaul Undong (運動) consists of three sub-movements: the Three Orders Establishment Movement (大秩序確立運動), regional Saemaul Undong (地域), and occupational Saemaul Undong (職能). The Three Orders Establishment Movement (大秩序確立運動) aims to make urban life (都市生活) brighter and cleaner through initiatives such as "standing in line," "not littering," and "speaking politely," although it is not directly related to improving economic conditions (經濟條件). However, both rural (農漁村) and urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動), including regional (地域) and workplace (職場) movements, were initiated to address the country's chronic poverty (貧困) and underdevelopment (退嬰).

## B. Popularization of Economic Self-Reliance Awareness (自立意識)

When examining the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) from an economic perspective (經濟的), it can be divided into three main areas (分野):

First is environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業), which include:
1. Expansion (擴張) and establishment (開設) of farm roads (農路)
2. Roof improvement (地붕개량)
3. Bridge construction (橋梁架設)
4. Breakwater construction (防波堤建設)
5. Water facilities (水利施設)
6. Public facilities (公共利用施設)
7. Village beautification (部落環境美化)
8. Other livelihood environment projects (生活環境事業)

Second is income increase (所得增大) and productivity enhancement (生産性向上) projects (事業), which include:
1. Village afforestation seedlings (苗木)
2. Production cooperative projects (生産協同事業) (group cultivation (集團栽培), compost production (堆肥增産), farming time (營農時) restrictions (制限), pest control (病虫害防除))
3. Increased land use (土地利用度增加)
4. Land reclamation (開墾) and tidal flat reclamation (干拓)
5. Aquaculture facility installation (水産養殖場設置)
6. Joint purchasing (共同購買) and joint sales (共同販賣), off-farm income (農外所得) projects, and factory production (工場生産) improvement (提高) and cost reduction (原價節減)

Third is the expansion (擴大) of welfare projects (厚生福祉事業), which include:
- Human relations improvement (人間關係改善), labor-management cooperation (勞使協助), neighborhood mutual aid movement (隣保救濟運動), and cultural welfare projects (文化福祉事業) (rural cultural projects (農漁村文化事業), standard rural housing (農村標準住宅), simple water supply facilities (簡易給水施設), mobile medical services (移動診療), village communication facilities (通信施設), and methane gas facilities (施設))
- Joint welfare facilities (共同福祉施設) (village community centers (會館), barbershops (理髮所), children's playgrounds)


--- (p. 125) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Bathhouses (목욕탕), daycare centers (탁아소), Saemaul savings banks (새마을금고), and other regional community development projects (지역사회개발사업) fall under this category.

Urban Saemaul Undong (運動) is divided into suburban (근교권), commercial business district (상업업무지구), and residential area (주거지역) Saemaul. However, the common goals (目標) they pursue (追求) primarily (主로) include environmental improvement (環境改善) projects (事業), production base establishment (生產基盤造成事業), and income increase (所得增大事業) projects. On the other hand, the focus (重點) of occupational (職能) Saemaul is on establishing transaction order (去來秩序確立), material saving movement (物質節約運動), production increase movement (增產運動), guiding (指導) participation plans (參與方) for member organizations (會員團體), and promoting (弘報) Saemaul education (敎育).

The main projects (主要事業) of workplace (職場) Saemaul include material saving movement (物質節約運動), expansion (擴大) of employee welfare (職員福祉) and benefits (厚生), workplace (職場) Saemaul savings bank (金庫), and environmental purification (環境淨化).

Factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (運動) focuses on cost reduction movement (原價節減運動), welfare and benefits (福祉厚生) for employees (從業員), labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), and fostering (育成) factory (工場) Saemaul savings bank (金庫).

Business establishment (業所) Saemaul emphasizes the use of receipts (正札制) and giving and receiving receipts (領收證), maintaining a clean and hygienic (淸潔衛生的) environment (環境) and attire (服裝), eliminating decadent behavior (頹廢行爲), and prioritizing (力點) courteous service (親切奉仕).

School (學校) Saemaul Undong (運動) has focused on moral (道義) and order education (秩序敎育) based on the Saemaul spirit (精神), regional community education (地域社會敎育), school environment improvement (學校環境整備), and industry-academia cooperation (産學協同) as its main objectives (主目標).

Among these, the most important aspect (側面) from an economic (經濟的) perspective (側面) is the factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (運動).

Factory (工場) Saemaul takes the concept (觀念) of "my company (企業) = my family (家族) = my country (祖國)" as its basic direction (基本方向) and foundation (土臺) to establish a Korean-style (韓國的) labor-management relationship (勞使關係). Concretely (具體的), it advocates (表榜) improving productivity (生產性向上) and reducing costs (原價節減), improving working conditions (勤勞條件), and training (養成) guidance personnel (指導要員). As practical items (實踐項目), it promotes (內示) the improvement (向上) of productivity (生產性) through the leadership (率先垂範) of the management (經營層), wage increases (賃金引上) linked to productivity improvement (生產性增大), and democratic (民主的) consultation (協議) on all business (事業). To eliminate (撤廢) the consciousness (意識) of discrimination (差別) among workers (勤勞者), it abolishes (撤廢) status-based (身分上) discrimination (差別) and educational restrictions (學歷制限), and advocates (優待) the preferential treatment (優待) of technical positions (技術職).

In addition, it aimed to create (造成) an atmosphere (雰圍氣) where workers (工員), employees (社員), and management (經營陣) eat (食事) together at the same table (食卓), enjoy (享) sports (運動) together, and openly discuss (相議) all difficulties (隘路事項).

To improve the working environment (勤勞環境), it recommended (權장) the establishment (設立) of night schools (夜間學校), the expansion (擴充) of welfare and benefits facilities (福祉厚生施設), the regulation (團束) of morals (風紀) around the factory (工場), and landscaping (造景) centered on employees (從業員).

The following table (表) is presented (提示) as the promotion method (推進方法) of factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (運動).

The following is the activity of the village savings bank (마을金庫). The village savings bank (마을金庫) began in 1963 (年) as one of the hometown development projects (鄕土開發事業) of the national reconstruction movement (再建國民運動). In 1972 (年), the government (政府) recommended it as one of the standard projects (標準事業) of the Saemaul Undong, and on March 22, 1973 (年月日), a federation (聯合會) was established as a corporation (法人) under the Credit Cooperatives Act (信用協同組合法). The ideology (理念) of the village savings bank (마을金庫) is defined as follows:

"The village savings bank (마을金庫) aims to achieve the prosperity (繁榮) and unification (統一) of the fatherland (祖國) based on the legitimacy (正統性) of the nation (民族) through a civilian movement (民間運動). By organizing the national living sphere (國民生活圏) into cooperatives (協同組合), it seeks to promote sound spiritual development (精神開發), realize social justice (社會正義), and build an economic cooperation system (經濟的協力體系)."

Its basic principle (基本原理) is to "develop the invisible (非可視的) achievements (成果) of the spiritual revolution (精神革命) into visible (可視的) achievements (成果), using their effects (效果) as a driving force (推進力) for further spiritual transformation (精神變革). This principle emphasizes that the achievements (成果) should lead to material (物質) progress (發展) while spiritual (精神) and economic (經濟) development (發展) complement and sustain each other (相互補完的且持續的發展)."

The operating principle (運營原理) is that "since all members (會員) are shareholders (株主), managers (經營者), and customers (顧客), a strong sense of belonging (所屬感) fosters a system of autonomous participation (自律參與) and self-governance (自治運營體制). Through continuous education (敎育) and management guidance (指導管理), the cycle of life improvement (生活化) → income (所得) → new heart (새마음) → new fulfillment (새보람) → new life improvement (새生活化)… is promoted indefinitely (無限循環), thereby advancing the development (發展) of both spirit (精神) and material (物質)."

The village savings bank (마을金庫) aims to achieve economic growth (經濟成長) through frugality (勤儉), thrift (節約), savings (貯蓄), and income (所得). It also seeks to foster a spiritual revolution (精神革命) through harmony (和合), neighborhood watch (隣保), cooperation (協同), and bonding (紐帶), creating a community where people trust and support each other. This, in turn, contributes to


--- (p. 127) ---

# Chapter 2 (第2章) The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

From the perspective of stimulating savings (貯蓄) and production (生産), the practical expression of the Saemaul spirit (精神) can be seen. Although its activities (活動) focus on savings (貯蓄) and loans (貸付) to increase income (所得增大), it is a remarkable movement (運動) in that it aims to develop a high-level cooperative ethics (協同倫理) of "one for many, many for one" and to foster human relationships (人間關係) of mutual understanding, trust, help, and love, thereby recovering humanity (人間性) and promoting common welfare (共同福祉).

The village savings bank (金庫) views its business (事業) as a first stage (一段階) of self-development (自己發展), engaging in credit loan businesses (信用貸付事業) for purposes such as clearing high-interest debts (高利債), production capital (生産資金), and medical expenses (醫療費). The second stage (第二段階) involves joint businesses (共同事業) such as purchasing and selling (購販事業), production income (生産所得事業), and cultural welfare (文化福祉事業) to contribute to regional development (地域開發). The third stage business (第三段階事業) includes corporate joint investments (企業合作投資), purchasing securities (有價證券), financial deposits (金融預託), and insurance enrollment (保險加入) to invest surplus funds (餘裕資金) and contribute to national development (國家發展).

## D. Establishing a National Economic Perspective (國民經濟觀)

Living well encompasses both the meaning of living well materially and economically (物質的, 經濟的) and the meaning of living well spiritually and morally (精神的, 道德的). Therefore, two methods are emphasized to achieve the goal of living well: the eradication of poverty (追放) and the spiritual reform movement (精神改造運動). The spiritual reform movement aims to cultivate the spirit of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) among the people (國民) to enable them to live well. Thus, the Saemaul Undong should be seen as a national movement (國民運動) that primarily aims for the improvement of material, economic, and environmental conditions (物質的, 經濟的, 環境的) for all citizens (國民).

The Saemaul Undong is a product of economic consciousness (經濟意識) that seeks economic improvement (經濟的) and development (發展). What is economic consciousness (經濟意識)? How does it differ from the economic consciousness (經濟意識) of Western societies (西歐社會) or communist states (共產國家)? Often, when people say "living well," they misinterpret it as "living well just for myself," "living well materially," or "living well competitively." However, the Saemaul Undong is characterized by the idea of "living well together," "living well not just materially but also spiritually," and "living well cooperatively rather than competitively."

The spirit of the Saemaul Undong is to create a prosperous and pleasant country (富强한) where not only I and my region (高場) can live well, but also our nation (國家), our generation (世代), and our descendants (後孫) can live well. Moreover, it aims to build a country where our surroundings (周邊) are free from hardship (不).


--- (p. 128) ---

Ignoring a neighbor you have encountered is not the spirit of Saemaul. When there is a neighbor in difficulty, do not regard it as someone else's affair but think of it as your own and gather strength among neighbors to help and care for each other. This spirit of Imbo (隣保) is the spirit of Saemaul.

In this regard, the economic consciousness of the Saemaul Undong (運動) inherits and reflects the traditional (傳統的) national view (國家觀), which sees the nation (國家) as an expanded form (形態) of family (家族) life (生活). This is a familialistic (家族主義的) national view (國家觀) based on mutual support (相扶相助) and symbiotic (共生), co-prosperous (共榮) principles. Furthermore, Korean society (韓國社會) has long maintained the tradition (傳統) of small cooperative (小協同體) communal (共同) life (體). Concrete (具體的) expressions (表現) of this include the village covenants (鄕約) advocating "mutual encouragement of virtue and business (德業相勸)," "mutual correction of faults (過失相規)," "mutual exchange of rites and customs (禮俗相交)," and "mutual relief in times of distress (患難相恤)." There are also various forms of associations (契) for mutual aid (共濟救助), such as Donglyang associations (同梁組合), Dongho kinship (同好親睦), and communal work (共同作業) organizations (組織) like Dure and Pumati in village communities (村落共同體).

In conclusion, the economic consciousness (經濟意識) supporting the Saemaul Undong (運動) differs in its origins from the Western (西歐) individualistic (個人主義的), materialistic (物質主義的), and competitive (競爭主義的) economic consciousness (經濟意識) based on the economic (經濟) interests (利益) of individuals (個人) or groups (集團). It also differs from the revolutionary (革命主義的) and expansionist (膨脹主義的) economic consciousness (經濟意識) of a totalitarian (全體主義) system (體制) advocating class interests (階級利益) and ethnic supremacy (民族至上). In a word, it should be seen as a modern (現代的) expression (表現) of a political (政治), economic (經濟), social (社會), and spiritual-cultural (精神文化) movement (運動) supported by a unique (獨自的) economic philosophy (經濟哲學) that has been passed down (連綿) through 4000 years (年) of history (歷史), rooted in the national founding ideals (建國理念) of Dan-gun (檀君), who hoped to build (建設) an ideal (理想的) welfare state (福祉國家) on earth (地上), and the traditional (傳統) thoughts (思想) of consolation (解寃), symbiosis (相生), co-prosperity (共榮), and harmony (造化).

### 3. Saemaul Undong (運動) and New Security Consciousness (安保意識)

#### Ga. Developmental (發展) Capabilities (力量) Forged by the Saemaul Undong (運動)

If the 1970s (年) were a decade when our country solidified its status as a modern nation (近代國家), the driving force (原動力) behind it was undoubtedly the achievements of the Saemaul Undong (運動). Indeed, it accomplished feats unseen in our modern history (近代史), such as achieving miraculous (驚異的) economic (經濟) growth (成長) and laying the foundations for an independent (自主的) national defense (國防力). The 1970s (年) began amidst difficult domestic and international (國內外的) circumstances. Externally, the United States (美國) pursued a policy (政策) of rapprochement with China (中共), and the Middle East (中東) region (地域) emerged as another conflict zone (紛爭地域).


--- (p. 129) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Middle East region had long been a strategic area possessing oil resources that were monopolized by Western imperial powers. When instability arose in this region, Western military forces had to be dispersed, which inevitably made the situation around the Korean Peninsula even more unstable. Although the Soviet Union's influence was somewhat checked by the Sino-Soviet split, this only made the situation more complicated for us.

Since the 1950s, the international politics of the Korean Peninsula have been shaped by the relationship between the United States and China. It is paradoxical that the United States and China, who fought as adversaries in the Korean War, have left the hostile relationship between North and South Korea unattended while pursuing reconciliation. This has further complicated the political situation on the Korean Peninsula.

In such a context, we had no choice but to cultivate a spirit of self-reliance and self-defense to protect ourselves. The Saemaul Undong was a national movement aimed at achieving national self-reliance, autonomy, and self-defense through the practice of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. It was a large-scale movement for the spiritual reform and unity of the nation.

This movement did not merely respond to the challenges we faced at the time but also sought to establish our position in the flow of world history and to equip ourselves as the main actors in national unification. It was an expression of the national will to build a system for these purposes.

### B. The Self-Reliant National Defense System and Security Consciousness

Until the 1960s, we had resigned ourselves to the belief that economic self-reliance and self-defense were impossible. We were trapped in a dependent mental state, relying on U.S. financial and economic aid to get by day by day.

The belief that economic self-reliance was impossible due to the lack of natural resources, a divided territory, and technological capabilities was deeply ingrained in our defeatist mindset.

This was especially true regarding national security. We believed that dealing with the North Korean invasion was impossible without the help of the United States and the United Nations. However, by the 1970s, our military had taken full responsibility for the entire demilitarized zone and had developed a strong consciousness that any provocation by North Korea could and should be countered by our own strength.

Examining this content, we realize that with effort, nothing is impossible. There is a great


--- (p. 130) ---

The national self-strengthening (自彊) was brought about by the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), a national movement (國民運動) centered around it. Under this premise, it is necessary to recall our security situation (安保狀況) in the 1970s (1970年代).

The most important institutional support for our national security (安保) was the security cooperation (安保協力) with the United States and our independent national defense force (自主國防力) related to it. However, in the 1970s, a problem was discovered in the institutional aspects of our security guarantee (安全保障) cooperation (協力) with the United States. This issue arose surrounding the withdrawal of the U.S. 7th Division from Korea in 1971.

At that time, U.S. Vice President Agnew informed the Korean government (政府) that out of the U.S. 2nd Division and 7th Division stationed (駐屯) in Korea, the 7th Division would be withdrawn. Then, President Park Chung-hee requested that the withdrawal of the 7th Division was unavoidable, but asked for a promise to keep the remaining 2nd Division stationed (駐屯) indefinitely. However, Agnew did not make such a promise.

Vice President Agnew's attitude was based on Article 4 of the Korea-U.S. Mutual Defense Treaty (防衛條約). Article 4 states, "By mutual agreement, the United States is granted the authority (權限) by the Republic of Korea to station (駐屯) its land, sea, and air forces, and the United States accepts this."

When this article was approved (批准同意), the U.S. Senate clarified that this article did not impose an obligation (義務) on the United States to station (駐屯) troops in Korea.

Due to this article, the United States did not consult with Korea in advance regarding the withdrawal of the 7th Division, nor did it make a promise to maintain the sole remaining 2nd Division indefinitely. This is because making a promise would constitute assuming an obligation (義務), and promising to assume an obligation would mean amending Article 4, something Vice President Agnew was not authorized to do.

In this way, when this treaty (條約) was concluded (締結) in 1954, it was sufficient for U.S. forces to be stationed (駐屯) in Korea, and there was no concern about whether they were stationed (駐屯) as a right or an obligation (義務) of the United States. However, since the U.S. forces were stationed (駐屯) as a right, there was no need for prior consultation with Korea or to obtain Korea's consent (同意) in the event of a withdrawal.


--- (p. 131) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Because of this, Korea had to go through a trial at one point.
On March 9, 1977, President Jimmy Carter of the United States announced the withdrawal of U.S. troops from Korea (USFK), the first time a U.S. President had done so without prior consultation with our side.
However, we were able to overcome this trial based on the spirit of the Saemaul Undong, with the belief that we must protect our own land. Starting from 1971, with the withdrawal of the U.S. 7th Division, we began the modernization of our military equipment, successfully completing this by 1974-75. Following this, from 1975 onwards, we implemented a five-year plan for strengthening Korea's military capabilities using the defense tax borne by all citizens.
This military strengthening plan, being funded entirely by our citizens' taxes, was inherently self-reliant from the outset.
Along with the progress of this plan, the foundation of self-reliant defense, the defense industry, was put on track, and this became a decisive opportunity for the formation of military strength based on the foundation of the national economy.
The most important aspect of this was the new evaluation of the North Korean (North Korea) military strength. The U.S. government had previously claimed that our evaluation of North Korean military strength was exaggerated. However, starting in the spring of 1978, coinciding with the emergence of pro-Soviet communist governments in "South Yemen," "Ethiopia," and "Afghanistan" with Soviet support, the U.S. began to reevaluate North Korean military strength. They confirmed that the North Korean military, previously thought to be 400,000 strong, was actually 700,000.

Secondly, we can point to the rise in oil prices and the resulting global economic recession, as well as the slowing of Korea's economic growth.
The military strengthening plan requires Korea's GNP to achieve an annual real growth rate of 9% to proceed smoothly. However, it is a well-known fact that this has not been the case recently.
Lastly, we can point to the political turmoil that followed October 26, 1979.
Due to these various factors, the first military strengthening plan was insufficient to deal with the arbitrary withdrawal policy of the U.S. military and to possess the capability to overwhelm North Korean military strength. Therefore, we had no choice but to continue with a second military strengthening plan.
As mentioned above, the characteristics of the 1970s were self-reliance and self-sufficiency in other fields, and


--- (p. 132) ---

Self-confidence has taken root, and in the realm of security, there is significant importance in establishing an independent security consciousness and solidifying it, along with acquiring fundamental military power as a realistic material force.

### Da. Independent Security System in the 1980s (年代)
The independent security system and military power established in the 1970s must be re-evaluated and developed in a new dimension as we enter the 1980s. We need to consider the reasons for this from the perspective of changes in the situation surrounding the Korean Peninsula. First, we must consider the historical fact that since 1950, the primary influential forces in the international politics of the Korean Peninsula have been the United States and China. The United States and China have resolved their 20-year hostile relationship and reconciled in the 1970s. As a result, a tripartite cooperative system of the U.S., Japan, and China has emerged in Northeast Asia, pushing the Soviet Union into a corner.

Therefore, to make up for this, the Soviet Union is attempting to establish communist governments in other parts of the world and, at the same time, is increasing its military power in the Northeast Asian region. This is evident in the strengthening relationship between the Soviet Union and North Korea.

Although it is true that Kim Il-sung has not met with the Soviet leadership in Moscow since Brezhnev came to power, it is also true that the Soviet leadership is dissatisfied with Kim Il-sung. However, it is not that the Soviet Union does not recognize the importance of the North Korean region. On the contrary, because they dislike Kim Il-sung, the importance of the North Korean region may even be increasing.

From these facts, it seems that the Soviet Union sees an opportunity to regain its influence on the Korean Peninsula, which it lost to China in 1950, and it appears to be aiming for the 1980s. Considering the prediction that the generation after Brezhnev will not tolerate Kim Il-sung's current ambiguous attitude, it is expected that a new situation will emerge in the Korean Peninsula, centered around competition between China and the Soviet Union for control over North Korea. This will be related to the fate of the Kim Il-sung regime.

Next, the deterioration of relations between Japan and the Soviet Union. Japan has traditionally been politically sidelined.


--- (p. 133) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The situation was such that Japan, having signed a peace treaty with China in August 1978, revealed an antagonistic attitude toward the Soviet Union, which had not only refrained from returning the so-called Northern Territories to Japan but also strengthened its dominance there. From this perspective, it appears that the international politics of the Korean Peninsula in the 1980s would unfold in a situation where the Soviet Union and Japan, which had been relatively passive and had left the primary role to the United States and China in Korean Peninsula issues until the 1970s, would newly emerge.

This situation manifested in Japan's full-scale military buildup and China's military strengthening with U.S. support. When combined with the already formidable power of the Soviet Union, it is clear that the security situation in Northeast Asia in the 1980s would be highly fluid. Consequently, inter-Korean relations were expected to become increasingly tense, and the conditions for security would require both military buildup and a high degree of political judgment.

Given this background, the security situation in the 1980s would likely be far more complex than in the 1970s, when it was shaped by U.S.-China relations. Therefore, it seems that our country is entering a new era in its international environment. Accordingly, just as domestic politics is entering a new phase, the external situation also requires a new posture and new capabilities for response.

The Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation must be further elevated in the 1980s, a decade that demands a higher level of national participation and cooperation to foster a new consciousness of security. We can no longer remain on the sidelines of history. We must develop our cooperative relationship with our ally, the United States, within a more independent framework. Furthermore, we must establish a new Korea-U.S. security cooperation system suited to the new era of mutual dependence and cooperation, thereby laying a solid foundation for the peace order of the Northeast Asia region. Through this, we will not only contribute to the maintenance of peace in this region but also become the principal agent of independent and peaceful unification.


--- (p. 134) ---

We must solidify our position and achieve the great task of national unification.

### 4. Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and New Social Consciousness

#### a. Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Reform of Social Constitution (社會體質)

Starting from 1970, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was fundamentally a movement to innovate the consciousness structure of the people. The innovation of consciousness structure and new behavioral patterns bring about new developments for society and the nation. Looking back, the 1970s were the "Decade of Leap" that could lay the foundation for national revival, and it was the Saemaul Undong that served as its basis. When we say that society is developing, the material (物質的) growth (成長) is important, but without the prior advancement of consciousness (意識), material (物質的) growth (成長) cannot take root. Looking at the developmental history of advanced societies (先進社會), there has always been a movement to reform the consciousness structure of social members for national unity (國民的 단합), and it is on this basis that the conditions for development were formed. From the late Joseon Dynasty, we missed the opportunity for the normal development of social consciousness (社會意識) due to the chaos of the surrounding situation (周邊情勢). The 36-year history (36年間) under Japanese colonial rule (日帝) made it impossible for a healthy consciousness (意識) to form as a nation (民族). And since 1945, the tragic history (歷史) of the division (分斷) of South (南) and North Korea (北韓) is beyond words, but even after the establishment (樹立) of the Republic of Korea, the overwhelming influx (流入) of foreign (外國) culture (文化) caused great confusion (混亂) in social consciousness (社會意識). The introduction (導入) of foreign (外國) culture (文化) and educational systems (敎育制度) was inevitable to build a new nation (國家), and the introduction (導入) of new culture (文化) from advanced (先進) Western countries (歐美) was also inevitable to eliminate the remnants of Japanese imperialism (日本帝國主義). However, the uncritical introduction (導入) of various systems (各種制度) and customs (風習) from Western countries (歐美), especially the United States (美國), caused great confusion (混亂) in the social consciousness (社會意識) of the people (國民). In Western empires (歐美帝國), individualism (個人主義) and liberalism (自由主義) have developed within a powerful social solidarity consciousness (社會連帶意識) based on long-standing Christian civilization (基督敎文明). However, without recognizing these facts (事實), superficial and ideological (觀念的) biases were formed.


--- (p. 135) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Due to the acceptance of foreign trends based on self-interest, the general consciousness of the people had come to be directed towards the pursuit of individual benefits and personal advancement.

On the other hand, the atrocities of the Korean War, which began with the North's invasion on June 25, had instilled a defeatist consciousness structure derived from the fear of war.

The Saemaul Undong of the 1970s was predicated on the aforementioned situation.

In this context, where the United States and China had been adversaries on this land and were now moving towards reconciliation, South and North Korea began to engage in dialogue. However, under the situation where the people showed no change in consciousness, it was difficult even to maintain the existence of the nation, let alone its development. From this perspective, it would not be an exaggeration to say that the Saemaul Undong of the 1970s was a kind of national salvation movement.

### B. The Saemaul Undong of the 1970s and Social Consciousness

In the 1970s, internally, the progress of economic development brought about a great movement of the population by occupation, that is, a significant decrease in the agricultural population, and along with the development of industry, brought great changes to the entire social structure of our country.

Externally, we witnessed the process of the end of the Vietnam War, and the issue of national unification became a pressing matter for all citizens.

These internal and external events, it can be said, demanded a new consciousness revolution.

The successful progress of economic development proved that we could also become self-reliant. Even economic experts and high-ranking officials in charge of the economy had been critical of a self-reliant economy. However, the foundation of economic self-reliance, started with the belief that "it can be done," certainly proved the validity of this belief.

This signifies the success of the Saemaul Undong. It can be said that the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation infused new vitality into our nation throughout the 1970s. It eradicated the dependence on others and the subservient consciousness that had led us to rely on others and look up to heaven, and brought about a consciousness revolution that instilled a spirit of independence and a belief in self-reliance in all citizens. This was the achievement of the Saemaul Undong.


--- (p. 136) ---

Based on the spirit of self-reliance (自立) and autonomy (自主), the negative and cynical social consciousness that had been prevalent, which was critical of everything, was transformed into a positive and rational way of thinking. This shift fostered an active, compromising, and cooperative attitude, which was firmly established.

It was here that the history of development and progress began within the framework of stability and order.

Meanwhile, as the national social consciousness was being established in this way, our educational ideology also had to be newly established based on new consciousness and ideology. Here, the "National Charter of Education (國民敎育憲章)" was enacted, presenting new guidelines for education and greatly contributing to the national consciousness revolution.

Since the establishment of the government in 1948, educational policies had been initiated more as an emergency response rather than being based on an accurate judgment of our reality. Moreover, there was a tendency to unconditionally reject or despise our beautiful traditional culture, which we should protect and develop, without even recognizing it.

The spirit of the "National Charter of Education (國民敎育憲章)" was to revive and restore the essence of our excellent traditions and establish the foundation of an autonomous consciousness.

Autonomous consciousness is fundamental to maintaining and developing the independence of the country above all other issues.

Throughout the 1970s, we implemented education with national identity and established a subjective historical consciousness, striving to make it a spiritual pillar for national development.

The establishment of such a subjective consciousness and the subsequent practice of self-help and autonomy greatly contributed to making the 1970s a period of revival in our national history.

Looking back, until the 1950s, our people had not developed or demonstrated autonomous consciousness, always living with a sense of dependence and poverty as if it were their destiny. In the 1960s, there was a new awareness of what political instability and social chaos meant.

Against this backdrop, on the one hand, there was a will to establish our own position and create history anew, and on the other hand, the implementation of economic development plans led to the realization of "We can do it too."


--- (p. 137) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

This gave them the confidence (自信感) that they could achieve anything.

With this as a backdrop, the Saemaul Undong (Movement) unfolded in the 1970s, allowing the nation to develop confident self-reliance (自立) and self-determination (自主) plans. The spirit of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) took root in the lives of all citizens, becoming the driving force for the country's development. Based on this self-reliance (自立) confidence (自信感), the national consciousness (自主意識) of self-determination (自主) was greatly enhanced. The consciousness (意識) of self-defense (自衛) in national defense (國防) became recognized as something that citizens of an independent country (獨立國家) naturally possess. Looking back, the 1970s was a time when we could firmly establish self-determination (自主) consciousness (意識) spiritually, self-reliance (自立) confidence (自信感) economically, and a resolve (決意) for self-defense (自衛) in national defense (國防). We can proudly say that these changes made the 1970s the "Era of Self-Determination (自主)" and the "Era of Growth (成長)."

This is based on the belief (信念) in social (社會) stability (安定) and development (發展). The belief (信念) in stability (安定) and development (發展) was first demonstrated in the 1970s. Historically, our nation had been in a continuous state of instability (不安), making it difficult to find a social (社會) atmosphere (風潮) of mutual trust (信賴). There was also no belief (信念) in development (發展). Despite the natural progression (當然) of social (社會) and national (國家) development (發展), citizens lacked this belief (信念).

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) succeeded in instilling the consciousness (意識) that social (社會) stability (安定) and national (國家) development (發展) are natural historical (歷史) progressions.

The inevitability (必然性) of stability (安定) and the necessity (當然) of development (發展) have shaped the progressive (前進的) attitude (姿勢) of the citizens.

### B. The Saemaul Undong (Movement) and Social (社會) Consciousness (意識) in the 1980s

At the threshold of the 1980s, we faced a significant national (國家的) trial (試鍊). This was the "October 26 Incident." As mentioned earlier, we defined the 1970s as the "Era of Self-Determination (自主)" and the "Era of Growth (成長)," made possible by the leadership of the late President Park and the national (國民) awareness (自覺). This event (事件) indicates that there were inherent issues (問題性) in the development (發展) and leap (飛躍) of the 1970s. Reflecting (反省) on these issues (問題性), the 1980s were a time of


--- (p. 138) ---

We must learn from past experiences, continuing to develop positive aspects while boldly removing problematic ones to elevate the 1980s into a new era.

The elimination of irrationalities in various fields carried out by the National Security Emergency Measures Committee in 1980 was an effort to remove various irrationalities that had been hidden under the shadow of the prosperous era of the 1970s.

This was a task to welcome the 1980s as a new era. It was a historical task to remove elements of political and social instability and to reform political institutions to localize democracy.

Political confusion and corruption had been carried out under the guise of democracy, and actions that paralyzed national and social consciousness under the pretext of freedom had been rampant.

During the 1970s, while we grew our economic strength and capacity for self-reliance, we failed to recognize or act upon the false notions about democracy and freedom. We realized that without breaking free from these false consciousness, we could not embark on new development.

It is a fact that we are indeed living in an era of democracy. However, while every country on this planet uses democracy as a slogan, some use the name of democracy to practice communism, others have dictatorial regimes, and still others have monarchical political systems.

This shows that the term "democracy" itself has no inherent meaning. What matters is the concrete content of the politics in question. What is important is not an abstract or sloganistic democracy, but a concrete democracy that stabilizes the lives of the people and sustains and develops the nation. We realized that it is not universal democracy that guarantees the lives of the people and the development of the nation, but the specific circumstances and conditions of each country that determine these outcomes. Meanwhile, externally, the North Korean regime held a Communist Party conference in October 1980 and reorganized its ruling class with Kim Il-sung's son at its center.


--- (p. 139) ---

And the Soviet Union seems to have started taking gradual action to regain its dominance over North Korea (北韓), which it had lost to China (中共) since 1950(年). In other words, for approximately 30 years since 1950(年), the international politics of the Korean Peninsula (半島) have been unfolding along the continuum of war and reconciliation between the United States (美國) and China (中共).

However, the 1980s(年代) are expected to bring significant changes to the surrounding situation of the Korean Peninsula (半島) with the new emergence of the Soviet Union and the reinforcement of Japan's military power, as well as the escalating tensions between Japan (日本) and the Soviet Union (蘇聯). In this context, we must establish a new social consciousness to respond autonomously (自主的) to the changing dynamics and foster a belief (信念) and will (意志) as the driving force (主體) behind national unification (民族統一). As we solidify the foundation laid in the 1970s(年代), we must embody a democratic welfare society (民主福祉社會) through the spirit of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) and significantly enhance our capabilities for autonomy (自主) and self-defense (自衛) to welcome the 1980s(年代) as an era of national unification (民族統一). To achieve this, we must first cultivate a strong will (意欲) and belief (信念) to build a just society (社會), fostering a social consciousness (社會意識) of solidarity (連帶) and cooperation (協同).

### 5. Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) and Traditional Cultural Consciousness (傳統文化意識)

Firstly, the strength that sustains a nation or an ethnicity (民族) is not merely a physical (物理的) force but refers to the power (底力) of the foundational culture (基層文化) upon which that ethnicity (民族) stands. If physical (物理的) force were the only concern, ancient (古代) global (世界) powers like the Scythians or the Mongol Empire (蒙古帝國) would not have vanished without a trace. Numerous ethnicities (民族) have boasted temporary prowess (强盛) only to disappear from the stage of history (歷史) due to the lack of foundational cultural (基層文化) power (底力). Conversely, ethnicities (民族) that have reached a cultural (文化的) zenith have shown resilience, maintaining their homogeneity (同質性) and unity (統一性) even under foreign (外族) rule, ultimately overcoming adversity (試鍊). Therefore, reviving and establishing our own excellent cultural (文化的) traditions (傳統) today is the path to cultural creation (文化創造). As Hegel (Hegel) also noted, creation (創造) for an ethnicity (民族) can never be an absolute creation (絶對創造) ex nihilo (無에서 유). This is why tradition (傳統) is discussed here.


--- (p. 140) ---

In history, all creation and construction must be premised on the inheritance of cultural and historical legacies that have been cultivated and nurtured. This is evident in the fact that the Renaissance movement in the West was made possible by reviving the cultures of Greece and Rome. It is said that in Japan, the spiritual foundation of modernization was the tradition of Bushido that they upheld. Therefore, the creation of new history or culture is never achieved without the foundation of tradition.

In 20th century India, Gandhi reinterpreted Hindu teachings to suit modern situations, and Nehru rediscovered India through the study of its history, thus recreating history. This recreation provided the driving force for India's national revolution.

In the case of plants, even if a tree from the tropics, where growth is vigorous, is planted in a cold region, it will not grow and will soon lose its life. Therefore, a culture divorced from history and tradition is no different from a tropical plant planted on ice.

Thus, the task of connecting long-standing traditions with creation is what should be considered the wisest human aspiration and ability. In other words, when accepting new creative elements, it should always be promoted in the process of revitalizing one's traditional constitution.

Therefore, a new understanding of Korean culture is one of the national tasks required of us. And this new understanding cannot be achieved without a warm interest in Korean culture. A few years ago, an exhibition of 5,000 years of Korean art was held in Japan, receiving much praise and admiration. When this exhibition was held in our country, countless people visited it.

At that time, the cultural properties on display were not something that had been hidden away, but when foreigners said they were good, people took them to be truly excellent and marveled at them. This makes one think that we have been living without knowing the true value of our traditional culture.

Yanagi Soetsu, a famous admirer of Korean art from Japan, collected items such as door handles, stone mortars, and straw shoes, which we often see in the countryside, in the Folk Art Museum he managed, and praised them highly. It is in such affection that Korean culture begins to shine with new light.


--- (p. 141) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

If one does not know the true value of what one possesses, it is as good as not having it at all.

We have been captivated by foreign cultures without truly understanding our own Korean cultural traditions. We must consider the immense invisible losses we have incurred as a result. Cultural traditions are not something we can create at will. Therefore, they are not a dead past but a living past, a shining past, and a past that serves as the driving force for creating the future.

Secondly, in our nation's ethical life, the principles of 〈Sincerity (誠)〉 and 〈Respect (敬)〉 are the core of the ethnic ethics we must inherit. If sincerity refers to an attitude of honesty in one's inner feelings, then love and respect mean putting into practice the act of mutual respect and affection. Our ethnic group has long held the philosophy of "respecting heaven and loving people," which is a philosophy of respecting those above and loving those below.

From ancient times, our ethnic group has deeply rooted the philosophy of valuing people, which is why the traditional spirit of our ethnic group consistently embodies the spirit of human respect and the spirit of love and respect. Among these, the most practical aspect is the philosophy of respecting the elderly, and when this philosophy is applied within the family, it becomes filial piety. When this philosophy of respecting the elderly expands beyond the family to the social level, it becomes the philosophy of respecting the elderly, even if they are strangers.

In truth, filial piety is the first duty one must practice to live a human life. Therefore, our filial piety connects with the philosophy of respecting the elderly, teaching us to respectfully treat not only our elderly parents but also elderly neighbors, and to put this into practice. Because we have had this spirit of human respect and love and respect, our family and social order have been properly maintained not by objective laws but by subjective self-restraint and moral laws.

Values and ethical consciousness can be seen as the basic framework of human behavior that integrates the unique spiritual culture of an era, with the ideal it pursues being the essence of being human. We must recognize that the philosophy of human respect and the spirit of love and respect inherent in our traditional society carry this meaning of humanization. Therefore, this is one of the long-standing virtues of our ethnic group, and today we must particularly


--- (p. 142) ---

Thirdly, the virtues of cooperation (協同) and solidarity (固結), which are indicators of the Saemaul Undong (運動), are also deeply rooted in our long history. As a single ethnic group (民族) sharing language (言語), culture (文化), and blood ties, our people have shared both hardships (苦難) and joys, fostering a uniquely strong ethnic consciousness (民族意識). This has cultivated a spirit of mutual aid and support (相扶相助) that has taken deep roots.

Such mutual aid (相扶相助), cooperation (協同), and solidarity (固結) have manifested in numerous customs, too many to recount. Notably, the "gye" (契) has been a traditional form of cooperation (協同體) in our society (社會). While historical records (記錄) suggest that the "gabae gye" (嘉俳契) of early Silla was the first, it is believed to have existed even earlier. The functions (技能) of the "gye" (契) have diversified as society (社會) has evolved (變化), particularly flourishing during the Joseon era (時代). This was because the "gye" (契) served as a driving force (原動力) for solving immediate issues (當面問題) in local self-governance (自治).

The "hyangyak" (鄕約), or village covenants, also emphasized moral guidance (勸善懲惡) and mutual aid (相扶相助), serving as self-governance regulations (自治規約) for rural communities (鄕村). These covenants integrated the Yu Clan's Covenant (呂氏鄕約) with our traditional cooperative spirit (協同精神), contributing to the cultivation of good customs (美風) and the establishment of a social moral code (社會道德). Among the provisions (強目) of the "hyangyak" (鄕約), "hwan-nan sang-hul" (患難相恤) particularly exemplifies the beautiful spirit of mutual aid (相扶相助).

Thus, the "hyangyak" (鄕約) and "gye" (契) stand as clear evidence of our people's long-standing tradition of unity and mutual support. In everyday life (實際生活), we have upheld a beautiful way of life (生活), supporting each other in both big and small matters.

Various forms of "gye" (各種契) were gradually eradicated by the Japanese imperialists (日帝) as part of their efforts to suppress our ethnic consciousness (民族意識). However, even under Japanese rule (日帝下), the Governor-General of Korea (朝鮮總督府) documented 481 types of "gye" (種類) in 1936. Moreover, J.S. Gale, in his "Korean Sketches" (韓國의 인상기), noted that while Westerners dig alone, Koreans (韓國人) cooperate, with one person holding a hoe (삽) and two to four others pulling the attached ropes in unison. This observation led Gale to highly commend the Korean cooperative spirit (協同精神).

Every ethnic group (民族) possesses its own traditional spirit (傳統精神) and ethical code (倫理). Ethics (倫理) are shaped by social (社會的), cultural (文化的), and historical (歷史的) contexts, and thus each ethnic group (各民族) has its own unique ethical framework.


--- (p. 143) ---

Ethics (倫理) vary among different groups. Therefore, the ethics of our nation (民族) must be recognized as valuable in and of themselves (自體).

Fourth, from ancient times, the Korean people's character (心性) has been full of humor (諧謔) and laughter. This healthy character (心性) was overshadowed by despair and tears due to the influence of Japan's colonial policies (政策). Rather than the will (意志) to overcome reality (現實) head-on (正面), there has been a tendency to escape from reality (現實) and indulge in sentimentality, which has infiltrated our popular culture (大衆文化). Even though several generations have passed since liberation (解放), the regressive (退嬰的) remnants of Japanese culture (日本文化) have not been thoroughly cleansed from our popular culture (大衆文化) and remain deeply ingrained.

From the popular songs that the masses (大衆) enjoy singing to the content of movies and plays (演劇), traces of Japanese influence can still be found, which corrupt our emotions (情緒) and hinder cultural development (文化發展). As a result, urban dwellers (都市人) are easily placed in a helpless state (狀態) where they laugh and cry according to the influence of mass media (大衆 매체), and sensitive teenagers (靑少年) are easily captivated by temporary pleasures (享樂) in mass society (大衆社會).

At this point in time, when the influence of popular culture (大衆文化) is stronger than ever, the negative impact of Japanese culture (日本文化) must be swiftly removed. Moreover, from a social and cultural perspective, so-called Yankee culture (洋基文化) has created a sense of alienation (異質感) with traditional Korean culture (韓國文化), which is also a problem. The cultural style (文化樣式) that pursues materialistic (物質的) pleasures (享樂) has eroded not only the traditionality (傳統性) of Korean society (韓國社會) but also traditional values (價値觀) and ethical consciousness (倫理意識). Thus, it has ultimately led to the uncritical acceptance (受容) of Yankee culture (洋基文化) in Korean society (韓國社會), marking the beginning of a cultural structural drift (漂流).

If we deeply scrutinize (洞察) our history (歷史), we will discover the lofty spirit (精神) that has continuously (綿綿히) flowed through our history of hardship (歷史), and we will feel endless gratitude toward our ancestors (祖上) who have left us our language, our writing, our customs (風俗), and our homeland.

It is rare for a nation or people with such a strong sense of self (主體性) to have preserved their unique cultural traditions (傳統) over thousands of years (數千年間) while being adjacent (隣接) to China (中國), which has been the center of Asia (中心). Therefore, viewing our history (歷史) with a negative (否定的) eye is a grave mistake. Such a self-denying (自己否定的) bad habit inevitably fosters a chronic (慢性的) sense of self-deprecation (自侮自嘲) toward one's own reality (自己現實).

The continuous (連續的) denial (否定) of the situation (狀況) that has barely been conscious (意識) since liberation (解放)


--- (p. 144) ---

Such self-denial inevitably implies abstract justifications and futile longing and admiration for others' realities. Many people are still trapped in the lingering effects of Japanese colonial education, suffering from a nationalistic form of self-loathing akin to the "leaf consciousness." This national inferiority complex, on one hand, allows decadent consumer culture to infiltrate our land, numbing our national agency, and on the other, it fuels antisocial individualism, deepening our social dual structure.

Whether it's an individual's personal affairs or national issues, achievement is impossible without personal pride or national pride. Even when admitting and reflecting on one's flaws, one must possess self-respect and confidence to avoid self-deprecation and self-destruction.

If the Saemaul Undong is a movement aimed at spiritual development, then what our nation needs is not a defeatist self-loathing, but rather the cultivation of positive self-confidence. In this regard, dismissing the traditions of our national culture would be nothing more than a prejudice stemming from excessive self-inflicted harm.

Our national cultural traditions were not created by us. They were created by our ancestors. They were born after being refined in the crucible of their time. Therefore, they are not a dead past, but a living past, a shining past, and a past that serves as the driving force for creating the future. Thus, tradition is both a historical and a value concept. Consequently, tradition serves both the function of social preservation and social creation, making the succession of tradition one of the most important cultural tasks for a nation.

Therefore, advocating for the succession of national cultural traditions does not equate to nationalism or exclusivity. Rather, a vibrant creative cultural spirit would not be stingy in absorbing advanced cultures. When discussing tradition, there is sometimes a tendency to lean towards a revivalist stance. However, we should not seek tradition for tradition's sake, but rather seek tradition for the development of the future.

Development can be seen as improving one's ability to solve the problems at hand. If the true meaning of development is such, then the culture needed in our country today is...


--- (p. 145) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Development that enhances the cultural conditions necessary to solve the pressing issues facing our culture will be the kind of cultural development we need. Therefore, the traditional culture we must inherit includes not only tangible artifacts but also the creative spirit itself. History is governed by the principles of continuity and creation. Thus, the cultural traditions we have discovered must be linked to new creations. Only such creations, rooted in tradition, can be the source of our courage and pride, and the driving force behind the creation of a new history.

This is precisely the spiritual awakening that the Saemaul Undong is promoting. Now, we must exert our utmost efforts to create a new history and culture. We must harbor a grand dream of forming a significant core of East-West cultural creation within world history. To achieve this, we must free ourselves from the false consciousness of cultural peripheralism and cultural dependency.

To do this, we must cultivate cultural self-confidence. We must sincerely accept the unique characteristics of all the historical and realistic foundations and materials at our disposal, absorb them through intellectual experience, and elevate them to universal logic. Dvořák composed his Fifth Symphony, "From the New World," based on the folk music of his homeland. However, he did not let the symphony be confined to the particularity of folk music; instead, he elevated it to musical universality. Therefore, when we project our future hopes onto the past and seek to discover in the days gone by what we aim to create anew, we call this the re-creation of history.

Thus, when we engage in a deeper and more ambitious exploration of traditional culture from a broader perspective, even Korean culture, which is criticized today as being ideologically neutral, will be able to conceive of a higher-dimensional logic of creation.

Only then can we depict the future vision that our culture should strive for. Perhaps the very essence of ushering in a new era lies in establishing a new cultural spirit and a new historical consciousness.

### 6. The Saemaul Undong and Educational Consciousness

First, there can be various perspectives on defining the phenomenon and concept of education.


--- (p. 146) ---

There is also the functional perspective that defines education as a means of inheriting and developing social culture. If education is a planned change in human behavior, then it can shape, enhance, and correct aspects of human behavior such as thinking skills, creativity, values, attitudes, knowledge, and techniques according to intended plans.

In particular, if education is about changing human behavior, then setting educational goals involves consciously and descriptively identifying the behavioral characteristics that need to be cultivated. This is why we emphasize the importance of consciousness structure in education: without the restoration of a correct consciousness structure, it is impossible to establish autonomy in any field.

Long ago, Hayashi Shihei of Japan's Tokugawa era said, "To become rich in a hundred years, promote learning; to become rich in fifty years, respect martial arts; to become rich in ten years, plant trees on the mountains; to become rich in one year, farm well; to become rich immediately, practice thrift." This emphasizes that education is paramount for long-term plans, whether for individuals or nations.

However, we have been conducting education in a haphazard manner, lacking a long-term vision. Particularly after liberation, the trend of relying solely on objective tests has simplified the consciousness structure of the younger generation. Additionally, the proliferation of various learning methods that have never been properly established has led to a situation where only superficial educational techniques are hastily transplanted. While Koreans should humbly learn from foreign countries with different histories and conditions, there is no need to vainly admire, blindly imitate, or belittle ourselves in comparison. We should not be overly concerned with frivolous and irresponsible evaluations from others, nor should we engage in self-flagellation. This is because we are different from them.

In this regard, our education system has introduced various educational methods alongside the names of famous foreign educationalists such as Dewey, Bruner, Piaget, and Skinner. Along with these introductions, a rich body of educational theory has emerged. However, there has been no establishment of human development that fosters independent thinking and action. Instead, issues such as the "sprout classroom," cram schools, the craze for private tutoring, and the dehumanization of classrooms—both inside and outside—are exacerbating serious social problems.

From this perspective, it seems that Korean education is revealing a state of philosophical poverty.


--- (p. 147) ---

# Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Even if asked to present clear objectives (目標) or plans (方案), there is no response. This stems from the poverty (貧困) of educational philosophy (敎育哲學). Therefore, to have clear objectives (目標), we must first start with a searchlight (探照) that indicates the direction (方向).

Secondly, the objectives (目標) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which is being established as the spiritual (精神的) foundation (基盤) of our country's modernization (近代化), are more concretely (具體的) presented. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is a movement aimed at spiritual development (精神啓發), a movement to rationally improve our living environment (生活環境), and an economic (經濟) movement (運動) aimed at increasing the income (所得增大) of the people (國民大衆).

We cannot help but greatly expect that the formation (形成) of such values (價値觀) will be achieved as soon as possible through education (敎育). Education (敎育) is the most essential path to cultivate (陶冶) the next generation (來日), who will bear the responsibility for tomorrow's history (歷史), with true values (價値觀). We are convinced (確信) that the success or failure of national revival (民族中興) depends on this.

The indicators of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) are diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). These three indicators are the source of power to create a new history (歷史), whether viewed from an individual (個人的) perspective or from the standpoint of society (社會) or the nation (國家). They are the spiritual (精神的) foundation (基盤) for modernization (近代化). The meaning of these indicators is also evident in the National Education Charter (國民敎育憲章), and they are necessary for our national (國民的) recognition (認識) to survive strongly before our history (歷史).

Diligence (勤勉), the indicator of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) supported by voluntary effort (自發的努力), is the foundation (根本) of all progress and creation (創造). Creativity (創造性) inevitably follows voluntary effort (自發的努力). Therefore, diligence (勤勉) can be said to be the very force that creates new values (價値) and creates new history (歷史). We can see the diligence (勤勉性) of the German (獨逸) people (國民). Even an 80-year-old (80老翁) finds something to do and works all day. It is not because life (生活) is impoverished (窮乏) that they must do so. They do this out of a keen sense that a life without work is a dead life, and a day without work is a dead day.

Diligence (勤勉) in life (生活) is not only expected to have an effect (效果) in the trivial (枝葉的) aspect of forming national capital (國民資本), but it may also be more important (重要) to consider it from the point (點) of view of the spiritual (精神的) vitality (生命力) of the national (國民) character (性格). Even if an advanced society (先進社會) claims to have entered the era of so-called high (高度) mass consumption (大衆消費), the trend of luxury and extravagance (豪華奢侈) in such an advanced society (先進社會) is like foam floating on water.


--- (p. 148) ---

Indeed, the majority of citizens still hold onto the philosophy of diligence (勤勉), simplicity (質素), and frugality (儉朴).

The national character of diligence (勤勉) and thrift (節約) is the most important educational indicator that displays and maintains the health of a nation and its people, whether in its revival period (中興期) or its mature period (圓熟期). To create new norms (慣値) or new history in any era is synonymous with development (發展). Therefore, development cannot exist without diligence.

Diligence also cultivates honest people. A society (社會) composed of such individuals is governed by trust and justice (正義), rejecting corruption and injustice, and becomes a bright society. For this reason, we must establish an appropriate level (水準) of consumption production (消費財生產) and consumption lifestyle (消費生活) today. The generalization (一般化) of the optimal level (最適水準) must be led by the guiding class, setting an example from the top. When this optimal (最適) pattern of consumption lifestyle is not generalized (一般化), most citizens below the middle class (中間層以下) will fall into deep alienation (疎外感), and there is a risk that the social homogeneity (同質性) serving as the spiritual bulwark (堡壘) of democracy (民主主義) and security (安保) will crack.

Diligent life (勤勉生活) must also embody future orientation (未來指向性). If diligent life lacks future orientation (未來指向性), it becomes an unbearable life instead. There is a difference between enduring (忍苦) like a slave, saving (節約), and being diligent (勤勉), and voluntarily doing so. The difference lies in whether one sees the future (未來) or not, and whether one believes in it or not.

In this way, diligent life (勤勉生活) becomes the foundation of a positive (肯定的) national character (民族性格), and various progressive (發展) spirits (氣風) can be deduced (演繹) from it. Therefore, through education, we must first cultivate a philosophy of life (生活哲學) that pours out one's body and mind into one's work with passion and sincerity.

Thirdly, the Saemaul Undong's (새마을運動) indicator of self-help spirit (自助精神) refers to the subjective (主體的) will to carve out one's destiny with one's own hands. Subjectivity (主體性) is a mental (心的) state, that is, the act of being conscious (意識) of oneself rather than others. Therefore, from an individual perspective, it can be said to originate from self-awareness (自我意識). Hence, subjectivity (主體性) is a concept that holds meaning as the self-awareness of the subject (主體) who is the will (意志) and decision-maker (決定). Therefore, recognizing oneself correctly is the act of establishing subjectivity (主體) as an individual, and recognizing us correctly is the act of establishing subjectivity (主體) as a people and as a nation.


--- (p. 149) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

These two subjects of consciousness are interrelated as closely as the relationship between teeth and lips. When they are not and are perceived as separate entities, both "I" and "we" lose our existential value and even the meaning of survival. Therefore, it is also a spirit of self-discipline. The spirit of self-discipline that protects oneself and one's country is the spirit of self-help and the spirit of total security, and it is also the subjectivity. Therefore, Korean education should possess this educational consciousness and cultivate the spirit of self-help that does not depend on others or shift one's responsibility to others, but rather tackles one's own tasks with one's own strength, regardless of the difficulties. Only on the foundation where the power of self-help is accumulated can subjective survival be possible in all fields such as politics, economy, society, and culture. In the end, it can be said that only the survival as a process of conscious subject practice can guarantee the life of an individual or a group in the true sense of meaning.

Therefore, we need to consider educational security. This is about cultivating a society where all citizens can trust and feel a sense of belonging and stability. The people of Vietnam and the people of Cambodia failed in this effort, which is why they became communist. And through education, we must also achieve economic security and psychological security.

Next, the indicator of Saemaul Undong, the spirit of cooperation, is the most needed in today's educational consciousness and is also the spiritual foundation of modernization. Cooperation and unity mean that humans do not dominate humans, but rather humans help each other.

Humans cannot live alone. Therefore, we cannot disagree with the views of ancient philosophers who defined humans as social animals or social beings. In this regard, a free person, in the sense of being free from any social constraints, does not exist. Therefore, the social relationships formed between people, that is, the relationship between individual and individual, between group and group, or between group and individual, can be summarized in one word as cooperation. Therefore, cooperation is also a minimum requirement for maintaining human relationships or society itself. That is why a village can develop only when all the people in the village unite, and national power can be cultivated and the modernization of the country can be achieved only when all the people can unite. Therefore,


--- (p. 150) ---

Our modernization cannot even be contemplated without the foundation of a spirit of cooperation.

However, in our current society, those who consider their own interests to be the highest ideal are willing to sacrifice even their lives for the sake of those interests. As a result, our society is characterized by three tendencies: first, the pursuit of sensual pleasures; second, a trend of money worship; and third, selfish behavior.

Yet, it would be incorrect to say that we have always lacked a spirit of cooperation as a nation. The consistent guiding ideology of our people has been the spirit of cooperation. Therefore, it is historically proven that our people have long incorporated the principles of cooperation and mutual assistance into their daily lives. This can be understood by examining the local agreements (향약) and contracts (계) of our country's communal societies. Among these, the most uniquely developed form in our country, aimed at perpetually realizing the spirit of mutual aid, is the contract (계). Contracts range from those formed for the sole purpose of fostering friendship to those established for savings, with numerous types distinguished by their specific objectives. However, their original purpose—the spirit of mutual aid—remains consistent.

Local agreements (향약) also played a significant role in establishing the tradition of mutual aid.
