They initiated public welfare projects to improve the lives of citizens, aided the weak through charitable endeavors, and contributed to the betterment of people's livelihoods. As local agreements initially focused more on the spiritual rather than the material aspect, they greatly contributed to fostering a sense of community bound by trust. If such a spirit, which respects trust, were to be revived in modern civic life, it would lead to a lifestyle that prioritizes public welfare and order, potentially eradicating the prevalent issues of distrust and corruption we lament today. Therefore, during the 19th century, when some Western societies were at an advanced stage of capitalism and centered around individualistic egoism, the spirit of cooperation observed among Koreans by Westerners like Father Dallet and Reverend J.S. Gale was one of mutual cooperation and generous treatment of others.

Thus, we are by no means a nation lacking in the spirit of cooperation. The perception that we do is a misinterpretation stemming from Western egoism. In any society, an individual consciousness that is not properly understood inevitably leads to a sickening egoism.

Therefore, Korean education must now foster a healthy sense of community, guiding the entire society forward.


--- (p. 151) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

We must strive to build a welfare society (福祉社會) based on the ideology (理念) that the individual exists for the community (社會) and the community exists for the individual. Fourth, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is clearly a movement for better living. Today, ten years after its inception, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has evolved into a movement aimed at creating a new nation and a new history, with ideals such as the localization of democracy (土着化), the realization of a welfare society (福祉社會), and the manifestation of a just society (正義社會). However, it is crucial to remember that in the process of pursuing these goals, individuals must never forget their sincerity (誠實性), honesty (正直性), and integrity (信義). Society, too, must establish systems (制度) for production (生産) and distribution (分配) that can guarantee the basic needs (衣食住) of all people, while striving towards the ideal of building a just society (公正). Confucius once said, "It is not the lack of material goods (物質) that is concerning, but the unequal distribution (分配) of them. Poverty (貧困) is not the issue, but insecurity (不安) is." This statement serves as a valuable lesson for us on the importance of distribution (分配) and justice (公正). Therefore, society must provide various conditions (與件) to foster a sense of cooperation (協同心) among individuals. As the saying goes, "The self (自我) is a social self (社會的)," these two must coexist (共存) hand in hand. Thus, both individuals and society must prioritize cultivating the ability (能力) and habit (習慣) of cooperation (協同). As mentioned above, we have discussed the development of the spirit (精神開發) centered around diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). However, these three spirits (精神) are not independent entities (獨立) but must be cultivated and practiced together through education (敎育) for the sake of modernization (近代化). Lastly, we must establish an educational theory (敎育理論) suitable for Korea (韓國) alongside this spiritual development (精神開發) movement. The most pressing concern for Koreans (韓國人) today is our own country, Korea (韓國), which is inseparably connected to our own lives (人生). Therefore, to draw a map (地圖) for the development of Korea (發展韓國), we must prioritize designing excellent education (敎育) that guides (指導) young people (靑少年) to act (行動) with a correct sense of values (價値意識). This is also the educational consciousness (敎育意識) possessed by the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). However, Korean education (韓國敎育) has thus far failed to correctly assess its own social (社會的) appropriateness (適切性), leading it to pursue only foreign (外來) educational theories (敎育理論). Currently, almost all (全部) of Korea's educational theories (敎育理論) are


--- (p. 152) ---

When Westerners create things for themselves, we often adopt them wholesale for our own country, using them to explain and guide our educational reality. Of course, we must learn much from the West, and we cannot deny that the educational theories we have accepted from them contain many invaluable elements that we must follow. However, on the other hand, there are things that we must inevitably discard because they do not suit our actual conditions, and there are times when our own ways are recognized as better.

Since Western ideas were created for their own societies, we must find methods to view our society through them. It is clear that if we forcibly try to be the same when we are manifestly different, this cannot happen. The more we try to resemble each other, the more we will lose our essence and even our very being. Therefore, we must delve into the Korean ideal of education and develop educational theories that align with our cultural, economic, and social conditions. Analyzing today's educational processes, views on students, teaching methods, views on textbooks, views on teachers, and the social appropriateness of education, investigating the values of adolescents, and preparing basic data for drafting future educational plans will also be responsive educational theories. Now, Korean education must emerge from the unique environment and conditions of our people. Truly, establishing educational theories that suit us will not only be a bond between theory and practice but will also, based on a keen sense of reality, improve and develop educational practices. The spiritual development and modernization that the Saemaul Undong aspires to also lie in the revival of the spirit of education. To achieve this, education based on borrowed realities, as in the past, will not suffice. A cultivated style of education, merely transplanted and manipulated, may temporarily dazzle others, but it will inherently have its limits. Therefore, to develop educational theories suitable for Korea, they must be closely related to our historicity of "now," the individuality of "here," and our national subjectivity of "we."


--- (p. 153) ---

# Section 5: Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and the New Human Image

In the 1970s, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which was being carried out on a national scale, was indeed a concrete program for modernization. This movement is a Saemaul Undong aimed at spiritual development, a movement to rationally improve our living environment, and an economic movement aimed at increasing the income of the people. The indicators of the Saemaul Undong are diligence, self-help, and cooperation.

Here, we have established a system centered around the goals of the Saemaul Undong, with the main human image, creative human image, and cooperative human image. This system is described with the intention of finding and establishing our main body, achieving creation and development based on the awareness of the main body, and finding a way of life based on the spirit of cooperation.

This system is also a value system that opens up a new era. Opening a new era means creating a new spirit, a new consciousness structure, and a new historical consciousness to cultivate the foundation of the mind of a new human being.

### 1. Main Human Image

Although the Korean Peninsula has faced 981 invasions by foreign tribes due to its geopolitical conditions until 1910, it has skillfully overcome these trials each time. However, recently, whenever we hear an earnest call to establish subjectivity amidst Westernization and modernization, we are reminded of the parable of the Prodigal Son from the Bible.

This is because subjectivity should have been a prerequisite before Westernization and modernization, but its emergence in the middle of the process implies that we have been led by others without our own spirit. Now is the time for us to become like the Prodigal Son who has returned and to open our eyes to the subjectivity of our nation once again.

Subjectivity is about being aware of oneself, not others. Therefore, when we say that we do something subjectively, it does not mean simply imitating or blindly following others, but rather performing something based on one's own free will. A person


--- (p. 154) ---

At the moment of decision, it is a fact that one should act upon what one believes to be right.

Therefore, a desirable subjectivity (主體性) requires an integrity (integrity) that is personal (人格的). For instance, it is established based on firm life philosophy (人生觀), unshakable beliefs (信念) and principles (志操), the legitimate possession of human spirit (人間精神), and intellect (知性) grounded in conscience (良心) as essential conditions.

In this way, subjectivity (主體性) is a function (函數) of the vitality (生命力) emanating from the self-consciousness (自我意識) of the self. It is the vital force (精氣) of individuals and the nation, a philosophy (哲學) of life (生) that affirms existence, and a code of conduct (行動規範) for autonomy (自律) and self-respect (自尊). In other words, it is the vital force (生命力) of the self, and the principle of survival (生存) for the nation to continue living.

Thus, the self-help (自助) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), as an indicator, refers to the subjective (主體的) will to carve out the destiny (運命) of our country with our own hands and the courage (自衛) to defend ourselves. For this, vitality (生命力) is extremely important for both individuals and the nation. We are the Korean people (韓民族). The Korean people have lived through 4,000 years of history (歷史) and continue to live today as the main actors.

Subjectivity (主體), it is the life (生命) given to us before choice (選擇), and no matter how difficult the reality is, it is the normative (規範的) subjectivity that we alone must take responsibility for and uphold.

Therefore, the central issue to be addressed in the image of subjectivity (主體人像) is to bring the subject to life within human consciousness (意識). However, to bring the subject to life within consciousness, a process of positively (肯定的) affirming and disciplining (自律) oneself is necessary. At this stage, the process of vocation (召命) unfolds. Therefore, the establishment of the image of subjectivity (主體人像) must be imbued with values (價値) and meaning (意味) that encompass vocation (召命), self-respect (自矜), self-esteem (自重), self-discipline (克己), reverence (敬虔), prudence (愼重), sincerity (誠實), belief (信念), principles (志操), righteousness (義氣), freedom (自由), and intellect (知性).

Based on this, what we must clearly resolve at this point (時點) is the belief (信念) that we too can stand proudly at the forefront (先頭) of the world. We must discard the fixed idea that only the great powers (强大國) can run at the very front and that we, as a small nation (弱小民族), can only follow behind. Ultimately, it is through the conscious process of subjectivity as a means of existence (生存) that individuals or groups can truly secure the meaning of life (生命).


--- (p. 155) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### 2. The Image of a Creative Person

To be creative, we must first have eyes that directly observe reality and a will to overcome it. Just as human affairs are created with humans as the main actors, creative thoughts and actions only gain clear meaning and value when they are imbued with human creativity. It is only when this creative will is accumulated that creative passion and drive can emerge.

Here, the philosophy of creation is inevitably linked to a person's view of life and worldview. When connected to a view of life and worldview, creation becomes the embodiment of an ideology. However, after such creative will and the passion for creation that arises from it, there must inevitably be a spirit of rational or scientific inquiry.

We have tended to take pride in our emotional warmth and rich sentiment, but we have not been without the tendency to be dominated by emotion even in cases where a rational, scientific, and objective attitude is required. The spirit of scientific inquiry manifests in rationally thinking about things, objectively analyzing them, empirically verifying them, and applying them efficiently.

It is here that the ability to drive creation emerges, and the development of wise efficiency becomes possible. We must not forget that the Saemaul Undong is ultimately a movement that takes the lead in realizing the task of modernizing the nation, demonstrating courage and wisdom. Therefore, we must continue to internalize rational thinking and the spirit of scientific inquiry.

Modernity began with this spirit, and modernization is the work of making this spirit a part of life. Therefore, modernization can be achieved through the application of science. Hence, the recent Saemaul Undong must become a scientific Saemaul Undong and a rational Saemaul Undong. In other words, the formula of diligence, self-help, cooperation + science emerges. Therefore, we must add science to the indicators of the Saemaul Undong—diligence, self-help, cooperation—to become people of the new era.

In this regard, ultimately, a scientific spirit of inquiry is what vitalizes a creative will.


--- (p. 156) ---

Creative passion, I believe, has found its proper direction. This is also a pressing task that we must address today to ensure our nation's survival in the grand march of human creation.

Next, as Hegel also mentioned, cultural creation by a nation can never be an absolute creation from nothingness, as there is no such thing. Therefore, all creation and construction must be based on the accumulated cultural assets, that is, the traditional cultural heritage that has been cultivated and nurtured up to now. Thus, the work of connecting long-standing traditions with creation is, above all, a wise human aspiration and ability.

From this perspective, the values and meanings to be addressed in cultural creation and the image of scientific creation include growth, ability, efficiency, meticulousness, inquiry, foresight, originality, analysis, meaning, wit, and rationality.

### 3. Pioneer Image

The following passage is an excerpt from a Korean history textbook:
"Our people... had no dissatisfaction with their own land, so they did not covet others' possessions or feel the need for aggressive invasion. And they helped each other and united their strength to protect the path of freedom and independence amidst turbulent times."

While I agree with the emphasis on cooperation as a guiding ideology of our people in the passage above, I wonder if the statement that 'we did not covet others' possessions' and 'we did not feel the need for aggressive invasion' implies that our people lacked a drive for achievement and retreated from competition and pioneering in world history.

Moreover, even in our country's legends, folktales, and fairy tales—our old stories passed down classically—emphasized virtues such as harmony and obedience rather than pioneering. That is why even today, children highly praise "Heungbu," who has not pioneered his own life.

Generally speaking, while the West has long held a mental attitude of conquering nature, the Eastern view of life has been to comply with nature rather than resist it. Thus, as our history approached modernity, our competitive spirit with world history, as well as our external pioneering spirit, became weakened, and this history of


--- (p. 157) ---

# Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

A dog finally became a rain barrier in our modern historical development.
Therefore, "Jeong(丁) Dasan(茶山)" once said in a tone of frustration that the land of this peninsula was too narrow and stifling: "Alas, people of our country! The east, west, and south are all surrounded by the sea, and the north is a high mountainous area with folds, making it seem as if we are trapped in a pocket. With our hands and feet always curled up, how can we ever stretch our energy and will?" "Park Jaegga(朴齊家)" also lamented that "During the 400 years of the Joseon(朝鮮) Dynasty(王朝), not a single foreign ship was allowed to pass, and children would cry in shame and embarrassment whenever they saw a foreign guest."

This statement reflects that the development of our history lacked an outward attitude or pioneering spirit to overcome natural and historical conditions. In reality, we admired nature and respected natural laws to the extent that we had no room for war or pioneering endeavors.

From this historical background, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has achieved excellent results in various fields through its development. We built new factories, paved highways, constructed ports and harbors, and created reservoirs. Just as the German(獨逸) people achieved the miracle of the Rhine(라인江) after World War II, we dedicated our pioneering and united efforts to creating the miracle of the Han(漢江) on this land.

Furthermore, while others achieved heavy chemical industrialization in 10 or 20 years, we accomplished it in just 5 to 10 years. With our will and effort, we must awaken a pioneering mission consciousness through the pioneering of values at this point, and with the passion inspired by this mission consciousness, we must exhibit a adventurous pioneering spirit. We cannot help but raise high the banner of pioneering and advance with the spirit of one for a hundred.

Only through this process can we cultivate the national strength to not only catch up with others but also surpass them. Now, Korea(韓國) is Korea(韓國) in the world. Although geographically located on the small Korean Peninsula(韓半島), our living space must encompass the world.

For this purpose, we must advance daily in transforming our national character as a long-term strategy. We must move forward with an active, pioneering spirit that knows no impossibilities to create the future. Therefore, the image of a pioneer should establish mission, spirit, passion, adventure, diligence, self-reliance, production, progress, reform, and development, and then


--- (p. 158) ---

We must assign value and meaning to it.
Thus, we must become a nation that develops the world, nature, and the country, and historicizes nature.

### 4. Cooperative Human Image

Humans cannot live alone. This is true both materially and spiritually. Even if the insights of Jesus, Buddha, or Confucius were extraordinary, if no one understood or accepted them, we could not call them ideologies. Humans are social animals even in the realm of spirit.
Therefore, humans are thrown into various social relationships from the moment they are born into this world. In other words, the fundamental fact of human existence is that humans are together. Thus, the relationship between the individual and society is akin to that between a fish and water. If humans are crops, then society or the nation is like the soil that nurtures those crops.
Therefore, each individual must be sincere to themselves while also objectifying and transcending themselves to have a shared consciousness with society and the group. Society must also develop into a society of trust and justice, which goes without saying. As the saying goes, "The self is a social self," these two must coexist as friends who hold hands affectionately.
The cooperative spirit, a hallmark of the Saemaul Undong, refers to this. Therefore, the ideal of creating a new history is not something that can be achieved by the efforts of a single individual. It is a result of cooperation achieved through mutual aid and effort. When each individual acts with a clear sense of purpose and that purpose aligns with the overall goal, only then can individuals cooperate for the whole, and the whole for the individual.
Moreover, an individual is not just an individual. As a member of society, they must uphold social responsibility, duty, and a sense of law. Human life and happiness depend on the nation and society. Therefore, especially those who are educated must engage in criticism that offers alternatives. This is what it means to have a sense of community.


--- (p. 159) ---

The ethics of criticism.

Of course, without candid criticism, progress tends to stagnate. Progress means social improvement. Therefore, a society that dislikes criticism cannot develop. However, when there is no alternative, practice should be prioritized over criticism. And resistance without an alternative is less important than creation.

Therefore, individuals should consider that their actions influence society and always act in a way that is socially appropriate. For example, they should prioritize reason over emotion and public interest over self-interest.

When individuals truly care for society and society exists for the sake of individuals, this is the ideal society. A society that balances freedom and equality, with justice and cooperation, is a just and welfare society. Therefore, both individuals and society must strive to develop democracy and realize the ideals of freedom and equality to build a welfare society.

To achieve this, the establishment of a cooperative mindset should be based on respect, integrity, honesty, tolerance, harmony, public interest, service, justice, and mutual support. The establishment of a social image should value and emphasize justice, participation, citizenship, democracy, duty, order, law-abiding, criticism, and welfare.

### 5. Ideal Lifestyle

Our people can achieve individual subjectivity and, through its expansion, national subjectivity by leading healthy lives. Similarly, the spirit of pioneering and creation, as well as the spirit of cooperation, can only be realized and truly valuable when based on a healthy lifestyle.

We often say "suit yourself" but fail to act on it. To live a suitable life, one must first know oneself. Keeping to one's limits is also a path of self-cultivation. Knowing oneself, understanding one's abilities, handling tasks commensurate with those abilities, and declining tasks beyond one's capacity is the way to keep to one's limits and a path of self-reflection and cultivation.


--- (p. 160) ---

However, it seems that our society today is increasingly embracing a culture of extravagance. People are more preoccupied with others' lives than their own, constantly mimicking others rather than focusing on their personal growth. Trends and consumer spending are prime examples of this phenomenon.

The essence of a proper lifestyle lies in the wisdom of living. By harnessing this wisdom, we can better elevate human values. This wisdom can be found in our pursuit of truth, goodness, and beauty in life. It is through this journey that we discover the meaning of life and find happiness.

To establish a proper lifestyle, we must approach life with humility. This means aligning our thoughts with our actions, our forms with our content, and our appearances with our substance. We must uphold family and social ethics, adopt a humanistic approach to life, embrace diligence, and cultivate values such as integrity, contentment, and frugality.

Currently, what we lack is the wisdom to live today by promoting diligence, thrift, and prudent consumption among all citizens, and by seeking a new order of life that suits our means. Only by understanding our place, knowing ourselves, and acting accordingly can we build a healthy society.

The Saemaul Undong aims to improve our living environment rationally and encourages individuals to take initiative in their own lives. To achieve this, each person must cultivate the attitude of a true "life person." In doing so, we can establish our families and society, and secure a foundation for our present and future lives.

Only then can we truly embrace the humility of life and become genuine "life persons" who align their thoughts with actions, forms with content, and appearances with substance. Moreover, the modernization we must pursue today will be directly proportional to our ability to improve the consciousness and attitudes of all citizens towards life.

To establish the ideal of a "life person," we must cultivate education, humility, cheerfulness, health, and leisure.


--- (p. 161) ---

## Chapter 2: The Fundamental Spirit of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Value and meaning must be attributed to leisure (暇), sentiment (情緖), family (家庭), thrift (勤儉), integrity (淸白), and contentment with poverty (安貧).

Ultimately, the ultimate purpose of life is a future vision (未來像) that humans determine for themselves in a subject-oriented (主體的) manner. Therefore, change (變化) is inevitably approaching in modern society. To cope wisely with such change, we must initiate the necessary transformation (變革) ourselves. In other words, we must become humans who are proactive (能動的), autonomous (自主的), and constructive (建設的) in adapting to change (變化). Otherwise, we risk becoming slaves to change (變化) rather than its masters (主人).

Today's world focuses more on the future (未來) than on the present. No one can deny that the future (未來) is the most powerful driving force behind the present. Therefore, we must cultivate intellectual (知的), emotional (情意的), functional (技能的), and value-oriented (價値觀的) characteristics that can foresee (豫見) and overcome (洞察) problems after development (發展). Our goal should be to develop humans (人間) for development (發展) and humans who transcend development (發展).

Thus, by making the new future (未來) our own, we can illuminate the past and present through creative individuals (創造人). This is precisely the human ideal (人間像) we aspire to.

## Chapter 3: The Implementation System of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)
### Section 1: Characteristics of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Implementation System

The factors that contributed to the success of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) are numerous. These include the capabilities and support of leaders, the efforts and encouragement of frontline administrative agencies without interference, appropriate support of materials and technical guidance, and the response and cooperation of residents. When reflecting on the 10 years of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the common denominator among the various factors that made the movement possible and successful can be attributed to "organization" and "organized power." Given that the content of the movement was highly complex and comprehensive, the driving force behind its advancement was primarily organization. This organization, which includes human and material elements, structure, and technical information, effectively manages these components to realize the movement's ideology and achieve its intended results when appropriately managed.

Therefore, the consistent implementation system discussed here should be understood in the broad sense of the organizational concept, encompassing goals, ideology, structure, human and material resources, technology, and information planning and management.

Among the various aspects of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) that have been studied and presented, the most prominent is the issue of leadership. From a management perspective, this corresponds to human factors. The materials invested in the business for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) would be the largest element in its implementation system. The efforts that amplified its effects are another important factor within the system, characterized by human aspects while also yielding material results. Additionally, the infusion of knowledge and wisdom has invigorated the system with technology and information. Cooperation, which smoothly integrates all components of the system and enables centrifugal force, is also a crucial factor within the implementation system. Thus, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) implementation system is composed of these elements, serving as the foundation for planning, management, execution, coordination, and evaluation.


--- (p. 164) ---

Despite this, over the past 10 years, materials and research on the above elements have been limited and insufficiently organized, seemingly failing to meet the necessary requirements commensurate with their importance. As previously noted, while the success or failure of the Saemaul Undong (運動) may indeed hinge on the capabilities of its leaders (指導者), leadership (指導力) without organizational (組織) support can be futile.

The Saemaul Undong (運動) made significant contributions to forming a communal consciousness (共同體意識形成) by organizing individuals (個個人) into a collective force. This force, in turn, became the driving force (原動力) for advancing the movement. The organization (組織) and its organized force—they are undoubtedly the source (源泉) of the great power that drove the Saemaul Undong (運動).

While this has been repeatedly explained and discussed, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is distinct from other movements (運動) or projects (事業) that have been or are currently being pursued. In other words, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is a purely original and creative Korean rural movement (農村運動) based on the unique national character (民族個性) of our historical (歷史) situation (狀況), and a nationwide modernization movement (近代化運動) (Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部), "Saemaul Undong (運動): From Its Beginning to the Present Day," 1973). Therefore, it differs in meaning (意味), ideology (理念), and nature (性格) from other regional community projects (地域社會事業), rural leadership projects (農村指導事業), national reconstruction movements (國民再建運動), agricultural cooperative movements (農協運動), and credit union movements (信用組合運動).

The Saemaul Undong (運動) is discussed in terms of its project structure (事業構造) and operational system (運營體系). The operational system (運營體系) can be further divided into a motivation system (動機賦與體系) and a project promotion system (事業推進體系) (Kang Shin-taek (姜信澤), "Planning (計劃) and Execution (執行) of Saemaul Projects (事業)," Administrative Review (行政論叢) 11:2, 1973).

First, examining the project structure (事業構造), the Saemaul project structure (事業構造) can be explained by dividing it into types and levels of projects (事業). This is particularly true because the Saemaul project (事業) is related to multiple agencies (部處).

Therefore, the Saemaul project (事業), characterized by a multi-faceted (多元的) organization (組織), is not connected to the mission (任務) or goals (目標) of a single agency (機關) but rather combines various projects from different ministries (各部處) that align with the ideology sought to be realized by the Saemaul Undong (運動). In this way, the structure (構造) of the Saemaul project (事業) can also have an integrative (統合的) character.

While it is well-known that the structure of the Saemaul project is primarily executed by the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部) and the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農水產部), even looking at the project structure of 1973 alone, it involves various other


--- (p. 165) ---

## Chapter 3: The Implementation System of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

The Ministry of Construction (工部), Ministry of Construction (建設部), Ministry of Home Affairs (保社部), Ministry of Communications (遞信部), Ministry of Education (文敎部), Ministry of Culture and Information (文公部), Ministry of Science and Technology (科學技術處), Rural Development Administration (農振廳), and Korea Forest Service (山林廳) each oversaw related projects. As the scale of the projects expanded, other government agencies such as the Ministry of Labor (勞動廳) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (動資部) became involved to such an extent that the movement took on a 「全政府的」 (全政府的) character.

The projects were also continuous. That is, not all Saemaul projects began in 1970; some projects that had existed before were renamed as Saemaul projects. For example, student volunteer activities (學生奉仕活動), rural electrification projects (農漁村電化事業), mobile medical services (移動診療), and family planning projects (家族計劃事業) fall into this category.

Due to the unique character of the Saemaul projects, their multi-purpose (多目的) and multi-agency (多部處的) nature, or 「全政府的」 (全政府的) character, as previously noted, almost all administrative agencies were involved, making inter-agency coordination complex. As a result, coordination and cooperation became the most prominent tasks in the planning and execution of the projects. To address this issue, the Central Consultative Council of the Saemaul Undong (中央協議會) was later established to effectively perform the role of coordination. However, it is also appropriate to recognize that the art of division of labor was being carried out even before its establishment. In other words, while the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部) primarily focused on basic and support projects, the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農水產部) took the lead in income-generating projects. Other agencies were also involved in related projects and villages.

Next, it is necessary to explain the project promotion system (事業推進體系) within the operational system (運營體系). Before introducing empirical cases (事例) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) promotion system (推進體制), it is necessary to familiarize oneself with a theoretical framework (理論的) that can explain the Saemaul Undong (運動) promotion system (推進體制). A macro theory (巨視理論) is convenient for theoretically describing a complex project system (事業體系). (능신택 (菱信澤), 前揭論文, 1973, 1974) The explanation of the project promotion system (事業推進體制) that can be interpreted using the so-called project promotion system (事業推進體制) model (模型) consists of the following components (構成要素). The first is the project planning and development system (事業計劃發展體系).

This refers to the case where the function (機能) of establishing (樹立) and adjusting (調整) the project plan (事業計劃) is performed in the traditional management system (管理體制), and the result (結果) of this function (機能) is sent to the operational system (運營體系).

Next is the project operation system (事業運營體系). This operates (運營) and manages (管理) the projects established (樹立) by the planning and development system (計劃發展體系), receives support (支援) from the support system (支援體系), and the result (結果) is fed back (還流) to the planning system (計劃體系).


--- (p. 166) ---

Contributing to better planning, the following elements can be identified as support systems, which include technical support and administrative support. The technical support system provides the technical knowledge required by other systems, including information on specialized fields, evaluation criteria for operations, and the roles of staff.

On the other hand, the administrative support system refers to a system that provides administrative support, such as personnel, budget, and organizational management, which are necessary for business execution.

The last element is the "public relations system," which performs the function of connecting the external environment to the promotion system. Each subsystem is connected by the flow of information, performing the functions of input and output necessary for the maintenance, development, and vitality of the system, ultimately influencing related systems.

When the above promotion system is projected onto the Saemaul Undong, it is not possible to fully explain the project itself with these descriptions. However, this will be of great help in understanding the project structure and promotion system.

In other words, in the Saemaul Undong, the development system of the project plan is the "Central Council of the Saemaul Undong," which forms the pinnacle of the promotion coordination system.

The promotion system of the Saemaul Undong mainly refers to the executive organization centered on the Ministry of Home Affairs. This is an inevitable conclusion stemming from the integration of frontline administration, and various projects, apart from technical guidance being carried out by the relevant ministries, must be operated in a unified manner through the local administrative organization of the Ministry of Home Affairs. Therefore, not only in the planning stage but also in the execution stage, although it may appear that various agencies are involved, the execution process of the project should be considered to align with the local administrative process.

If the Ministry of Home Affairs is the backbone of the operating system, other ministries become a kind of support system. At this time, the content of the support may include technical, information, resource support, and sometimes even human support. In addition, the cooperation of private organizations can also be seen as having the nature of a support system, and it can also be said that a separate promotion and operation system is formed at the same time.

Finally, regarding the public relations system, there is an opinion that the promotion coordination system of the Saemaul Undong performs such functional operations, but since the public relations system is formed by the cooperation and adjustment system of each agency as necessary, it is not necessary to interpret it restrictively.


--- (p. 167) ---

## Chapter 3: The Implementation System of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

As discussed, when reviewing the Saemaul Undong (Movement)'s implementation system according to the aforementioned classified basic frameworks, one can acknowledge that there are appropriate interpretations. Therefore, while keeping such classifications in mind, the actual system can be analyzed.

Before discussing the actual implementation organizations or structures in the next section, it should be noted that the classifications of the implementation system, such as execution and support, central and local, frontline, business-specific, and content-specific classifications, all function. Additionally, classifications under the central guidance system, such as the Central Deliberation Council and its affiliated agencies, or regional command and division of responsibilities, are indispensable classifications for understanding the actual implementation situation. It is important to minimize redundancy and describe all these aspects in advance.

### Section 2: The Operational System of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

An ideal Saemaul Undong (Movement) refers to residents voluntarily identifying their own issues, planning, and promoting regional community development and regional development.

However, the regional communities in our country are not yet equipped with conditions that allow residents to promote the movement on their own, necessitating a leading role from the government. Given the vast scope of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in terms of its targets and participation, it forms a large organizational system and is promoted as a multipurpose business. In reality, a single ministry cannot fully perform its functions, requiring comprehensive and integrated policies or support from each government ministry.

Given the nature of the Saemaul Undong (Movement), as mentioned earlier, its implementation system will be explained in two parts: the system for the development of Saemaul business plans (the coordination system for promoting the Saemaul Undong (Movement)) and the system for business operations (the administrative guidance system for the Saemaul Undong (Movement)).

#### 1. The System for the Development of Saemaul Business Plans

The Saemaul beautification movement was initiated in 1971 as an experimental project aimed at increasing residents' income and spiritual development. The Ministry of Home Affairs took the lead in this project, primarily focusing on environmental improvement initiatives.


--- (p. 168) ---

Initially, the government focused on ten key projects (事業) and provided administrative guidance (行政指導) and support (支援). However, starting in 1972, the approach shifted to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), a comprehensive development movement (開發運動). The scope of promotional projects (推進事業) was expanded to include spiritual development (精神啓發) and income-generating (生産所得) projects. To carry out these projects, the government established a promotional coordination body (推進協議體) consisting of vice-ministerial-level (次官級) officials or higher from each ministry (部處) on March 7, 1972, under Presidential Decree No. 6104. Specifically, a Central Coordination Council (中央協議會) was established at the central level to integrate, coordinate, and systematize various policies (施策) at the central government (中央政府) level. At the city (市) and provincial (道) levels, city-province coordination councils (市道協議會) were established, and at the city (市) and county (郡) levels, city-county coordination councils (市郡協議會) were established. In townships (邑) and townships (面), township promotion committees (邑面推進委員會) were established to enable regional (地域) planning adjustment (調整) and comprehensive promotion (綜合推進) functions. Additionally, village-level (單位) development committees (開發委員會) were formed for villages (里) and neighborhoods (洞) to ensure the full-scale promotion (總力推進) of Saemaul projects (事業). The administrative guidance system (行政指導體系) was strengthened, and a regional responsibility (地域別責任) guidance system (指導制) was established.

## Composition and Functions of the Central Coordination Council (中央協議會)

### (1) Composition (構成)
The Central Coordination Council (中央協議會) was established to discuss (協議) and coordinate (調整) the government's policies (施策) and plans (計劃) related to the Saemaul Undong (運動) to promote it in a comprehensive (綜合的) and unified (統一性) manner. The Central Coordination Council (中央協議會), referred to as the foundational ignition period (基礎點火時期) of the Saemaul Undong (運動), was launched as an organization (組織體) composed of vice-ministerial-level (次官級) officials from related ministries (關係部處) on March 7, 1972, under Presidential Decree No. 6104. Initially, it consisted of one chairperson (委員長) and 15 members (委員) and operated as a coordination council (協議會).

However, by 1975, designated as the year of the "Leap of the Saemaul Undong (運動)," the composition (構成) and functions (機能) of the Central Coordination Council (中央協議會) were strengthened to establish a comprehensive (包括的) and powerful (强力) promotional system (推進體系). On May 30, 1975, the number of ministries (部處) represented on the council increased from 15 to 22, and the council's functions were enhanced to comprehensively coordinate (包括調整) Saemaul policies (施策) and evaluate (評價分析) the outcomes (成果) of projects (事業).

Furthermore, in accordance with the directive (指針) to strengthen (補强) the composition (構成) of the Central Coordination Council (中央協議會) by adding ministries (部處) related to the Saemaul Undong (運動) that were not previously included, the council's regulations (規定) were amended under Presidential Decree No. 7639 on May 30, 1975. The composition (構成) as outlined in these regulations (規定) is as follows. According to these regulations (規定):

In relation to the composition of such a system (體系), it is necessary to examine the cases of other countries. That is, various


--- (p. 170) ---

There are scholars who classify the organizational types of central agencies (中央機構) for regional community development (地域社會開發) into three categories: so-called integrated type (統合型), adaptive type (適應型), and special business type (特殊事業型). The integrated type (統合型) is a form that places comprehensive (綜合的) guidance (指導) and support agencies (支援機關) directly under the administrative leader (行政首班), while the adaptive type (適應型) is a form where existing departments (部處) perform guidance (指導) and support functions (支援機能). The special business type (特殊事業型) is a form that establishes a special business dedicated agency (特殊事業專擔機關) to implement (實施) businesses (事業) for special (特殊) regions (地域) or groups (集團). Examining this by country (國家別), India (印度) and Pakistan's regional (地域) community development movements (社會開發運動) can generally be said to belong to the 'integrated type (統合型)', while some countries (國家) like Ghana adopt the 'adaptive type (適應型)'. The 'special business type (特殊事業型)', which establishes a special business dedicated agency (特殊事業專擔機構), is an organizational type (組織類型) adopted in countries (國家) like the United States (美國) and Mexico (墨西哥).

When viewing South Korea's Saemaul Undong (運動) as part of regional community development (地域社會開發) and examining it from the perspective of the organizational types (組織類型) of central agencies (中央機구) for regional (地域) community development (社會開發), it can be said that it is based on the 'adaptive type (適應型)' mentioned second, with 'integrated (統合的)' elements added to it. For example, in the central agency (中央機構) for the promotion system (推進體系) that promotes the Saemaul Undong (運動), the fact that there is a council (協議會) composed of representatives (代表) from each government department (各部處) can be seen as having an 'integrated (統合的)' element (要素). However, considering that this council (協議會) is not directly affiliated with the administrative leader (行政首班) such as the President (大統領) or the Prime Minister (國務總理) but is under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Home Affairs (內務部長官), and that the council (協議會) only performs the functions (機能) of consultation (協議) and coordination (調整) while the executive power (執行權) is managed by each department (各部處), it can be said that it is essentially an adaptive type (適應型).

## (2) Function (機能)
In accordance with the policy (方針) to comprehensively systematize (綜合體系化) all Saemaul policies (施策) of each government department (各部處) and related agencies (有關機關), and to establish a comprehensive (包括的) and powerful (强力) promotion system (推進體系) for the Saemaul Undong (運動) so that these policies (施策) can be implemented (實踐) seamlessly (一絲不亂) from the central (中央) level to the provincial (市道) level and down to the city/county (市郡) and village levels, the functions (機能) of the Central Saemaul Council (中央協議會) have been strengthened, as previously mentioned.

As is well known, the Central Council (中央協議會) performs the functions (機能) of consultation (協議) and coordination (調整) regarding the Saemaul Undong (運動). That is, it consults (協議) and coordinates (調整) the government's (政府) guidance (指導), support (支援) (including administrative (行政) and financial support (財政支援), technical support (技術支援)), and plans (計劃) to create integrated (統合) guidelines (指針). In performing its role (役割遂行), the Central Saemaul Council (中央協議會)


--- (p. 171) ---

# Chapter 3: The Promotion System of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

First, it comprehensively coordinates the long-term, medium-term, and annual plans of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement),
Second, it systematically and efficiently coordinates the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement),
Thirdly, it comprehensively coordinates the enlightenment and publicity activities related to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).
The fourth function is to comprehensively and systematically adjust the Saemaul education (敎育) and the publication of its teaching materials.
Finally, it regulates other necessary matters concerning the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), with guidelines to examine and analyze the progress of Saemaul projects (事業) on a quarterly basis and to comprehensively coordinate policies. Additionally, it has guidelines to have governors (市•道知事) attend the Central Deliberation Council (中央協議會) on a rotational basis to discuss and resolve difficulties.

Meanwhile, the Central Practical Deliberation Council (中央實務協議會) of the Central Deliberation Council (中央協議會) for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) can be seen to perform its functions by deliberating on the following matters:
First, pre-deliberation on matters requiring deliberation by the Central Deliberation Council (中央協議會) for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement),
Second, inter-agency (各部處間) practical deliberation matters related to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement),
Third, deliberation and examination of difficulties and solutions in the promotion of Saemaul projects (事業),
Fourth, matters related to quarterly achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), etc.

### B. Composition and Functions of the Provincial Deliberation Council (市•道協議會)

#### (1) Composition

The Provincial Deliberation Council (市•道協議會) is an organization that deliberates and coordinates the guidance and support for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) within the province (市•道). It is composed of the mayor (市長) or governor (道知事) as the chairperson (委員長), with vice mayors (副市長), vice governors (副知事), superintendents of education (敎育監), directors of the Rural Development Administration (農村振興院長), directors of the provincial land and construction offices (地方國土建設廳長), directors of the provincial postal offices (地方遞信廳長), directors of the provincial broadcasting stations (地方放送局長), university professors (大學敎授), principals of agricultural high schools (農業高校長), heads of agricultural cooperative branches (農協支部長), heads of fisheries cooperative branches (水協支部長), heads of forestry cooperative branches (山林聯合支部長), heads of local military branches (鄕軍支部長), and managers of local branches of the Korea Electric Power Corporation (韓電支店長) as members (委員).

The characteristics of the composition of the Provincial Deliberation Council (市•道協議會) can be pointed out in various ways, but first, it can be pointed out that it has strengthened the organic cooperation system among related agencies (諸關聯機關間) following the promotion of Saemaul projects (事業). For example, the Provincial Deliberation Council (市•道協議會) operates on the principle of functional responsibility sharing, so the director of the Rural Development Administration (農村振興院長) is in charge of Saemaul production projects (生産事業), the director of the provincial broadcasting station (地方放送局長) is in charge of publicity activities related to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the director of the provincial land and construction office (地方國土建設廳長) is in charge of land management (國土管理), and the provincial superintendent of education (市•道敎育監) is in charge of educational matters related to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). This can be seen from the above points.


--- (p. 172) ---

Next, let's examine the characteristics of the composition of the City/Province Consultative Councils (市·도(道)協議會) at the city and provincial levels. While the Central Consultative Council was composed of all relevant ministries and agencies related to the Saemaul Undong to discuss and coordinate, and to draft unified guidelines for the movement, the City/Province Consultative Councils were composed of heads of various local agencies to establish comprehensive plans necessary for the practical implementation of the Saemaul Undong.

## (2) Functions

The functions of the City/Province Consultative Councils, which were established to discuss guidance and support for the Saemaul Undong, can be summarized as follows:

First, they concretize the decisions made by the Central Consultative Council. In other words, when a draft unified guideline, which has been discussed and coordinated by the Central Consultative Council, is sent to each city and province, the City/Province Consultative Council drafts a concrete plan suitable for that city or province, considering the regional characteristics.

Second, the City/Province Consultative Councils draft comprehensive long-term plans for the Saemaul Undong. As mentioned earlier, the Interior Bureau establishes various plans. For example, they draft concrete and comprehensive long-term plans for various projects and tasks related to the Saemaul Undong, such as basic Saemaul projects, Saemaul lifestyle movement, Saemaul production projects, development of manufactured goods by farmers, national land management, removal of factors hindering the Saemaul Undong, Saemaul publicity activities, and Saemaul education.

Third, as is widely known, the City/Province Consultative Councils expand Saemaul education and publicity to induce the continuous development of the Saemaul Undong.

Fourth, it can be pointed out that the City/Province Consultative Councils have the function of comprehensively analyzing and removing factors that hinder the promotion of the Saemaul Undong and the results following those factors, thereby preparing the concrete foundation for the promotion of the Saemaul Undong.

Lastly, they can conduct surveys on regional characteristics and research development plans. The City/Province Consultative Councils sufficiently grasp various conditions (or characteristics) of each city and province, such as natural conditions, geographical conditions, and conditions for mobilizing resources, and establish development projects suitable for the region.


--- (p. 173) ---

### Chapter 3: The Implementation System of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Decisions are made, and the direction and specific guidelines for the implementation of related projects are researched. When drawing up the comprehensive plan for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), if the city(市) and provincial(道) councils (協議會) have already grasped the characteristics of the region (地域), it becomes possible to achieve efficiency and effectiveness in the implementation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) through the efficient allocation of resources (資源) and the efficient operation of funds (經費).

As mentioned repeatedly, among the functions of the city (市) and provincial (道) councils (協議會) in the implementation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the function (機能) (role (役割)) of investigating regional (地域別) characteristics (特性) and researching development plans (開發方案) based on them is considered a crucial issue that determines the success or failure of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) projects (事業).

### D. Composition and Functions of City (市) and County (郡) Councils (協議會)

#### (1) Composition (構成)

This council (協議會) is organized as a comprehensive guidance (綜合指導) system (體系) that connects the central (中央) government directly to the cities (市) and provinces (道) for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Looking at the composition of the city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會), the mayor (市長) or county magistrate (郡守) serves as the chairperson (委員長). The members (委員) include the city (市) and county (郡) education superintendent (敎育長), police chief (警察署長), rural guidance center director (農村指導所長), agricultural cooperative (農協) union president (協同組合長), agricultural high school (農業高等學校) principal (校長), postmaster (郵遞局長), and other necessary personnel (人士).

Here, we point out the characteristics (特徵) seen in the composition of the city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會).

Firstly, it can be pointed out that about 50% of the regular (正規) members (委員) of the city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會) are related to agriculture (農業). From the perspective of the composition ratio (比率), this indicates that as the implementation system (推進體系) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) transitions from the central (中央) organization (組織) to the local (地方) organization (組織), it is evolving into a system (系) of organizational bodies (組織體) that can better command (指揮), supervise (監督), and manage (管理) the more concrete (具體的) projects (事業) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Starting with the 1971 (年) Saemaul experimental project (實驗事業), the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which has spread (擴散) through ignition (點火), has been pursuing projects (事業) aimed at ultimately (窮極的) increasing the income (所得) of farmers and fishermen (農漁民). Therefore, in the composition of the city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會), regular (正規) members (委員) are those who can solve agricultural (農林) problems (問題) in the key (要) fields (分野) of rural (農村) projects (事業) and provide technical (技術) guidance (指導) to farmers (農民) as well as convey information (情報) related to farming (營農).

Secondly, another point that can be pointed out is that even in the process of moving to a lower-level (下位) organizational system (組織體系), the scope (範圍) of the organization's (組織體) composition (構成) remains expanded (擴大) and maintained (維持) in the same state (狀態).


--- (p. 174) ---

### (2) Function

As mentioned in the functions of the provincial council (시•도협의회), the county council (시군협의회) also primarily serves to provide comprehensive guidance for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) by investigating regional characteristics (지역특성) and studying development plans (개발방안). Due to the varying issues and conditions faced by each county (各己市•郡), the council addresses not only the content and strategies for promoting the Saemaul Undong but also management issues related to the projects. Therefore, the county council must first investigate and analyze the characteristics of the region to establish concrete plans for promoting the projects.

Secondly, the function of the county council is to guide and coordinate the Saemaul Undong. While the movement is primarily driven by local residents, government guidance and support are necessary until it reaches a certain level. Various aspects of guidance and support can be considered, including administrative and educational guidance, as well as financial, material, and technical support.

Moreover, when the guidance and support roles of the county council are appropriately distributed, the results of promoting the Saemaul Undong can exceed expectations and also enhance the residents' active participation.

Thirdly, the county council engages in enlightenment and promotional activities related to the Saemaul Undong. The methods and processes for promoting the Saemaul Undong projects are not fundamentally different from those of general regional community development. However, in the case of the Saemaul Undong, the government's policies and


--- (p. 175) ---

## Chapter 3 (第3章) The Promotion System of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

Support (支援) has been said to be further strengthened. However, the role (役割) of the government (政府) in the case of Saemaul projects (事業) is, as always, to stimulate and support the voluntary (自發的) participation (參與) and efforts (努力) of the residents (住民들) of the local community (地域社會). It is important to make residents (住民들) aware of and interested in the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) through basic projects (基本事業), and to stimulate their willingness (參與意慾) to participate in selected projects (事業). In fact (事實上), the purpose of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is to improve the economic (經濟的), social (社會的), and cultural (文化的) status (地位) of the entire community (住民全體) based on the cooperative (協同的) efforts (努力) of the residents (住民). Therefore, developing a sense of community (共同體意識) for promoting the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is undoubtedly important (重要).

Fourth, there are educational activities (敎育活動) for Saemaul leaders (指導者) and residents (住民). The purpose (目的) of education (敎育) for leaders (指導者) and residents (住民) is to cooperate (協同) and unite (團結) in continuously (持續的) carrying out and successfully (成功的) completing selected projects (事業). The educational content (敎育內容) for leaders (指導者) and residents (住民) of city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會) mainly includes spiritual education (精神敎育), technical (技術) and information education (情報敎育) on farming (營農), and leadership education (敎育) for leaders (指導者). Emphasis (強調) on security (安保) and economy (經濟) is also added.

Fifth, city (市) and county (郡) councils (協議會) evaluate (評價) the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) and devise comprehensive countermeasures (綜合對策) based on the evaluation results (評價結果). The Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) regards self-evaluation (自體的) of projects (事業) as an important (重要) task (課題) for the continuous (持續的) development (發展) of its projects (事業). In general (一般的), evaluating (評價) projects (事業) is important (重要) for reflecting (反映) or feeding back (還流) the results (成果) of implemented projects (事業) into new tasks (作業). Moreover, the effectiveness (效果) of project plans (事業計劃) is reviewed (檢討) and reflected upon (反省), and corrective measures (是正措置) are taken based on the points of improvement (改善點) discovered. Meanwhile, some scholars emphasize the following points regarding project evaluation (事業評價) in the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動):

1. Evaluation (評價) should be conducted using scientific (科學的) methods (方法) to judge (判斷) reality (實際) fairly (公正).
2. Evaluation (評價) must be conducted from an objective (客觀的) perspective (入場), and should not be influenced (作用) by preconceived notions (先入感) or biases (偏見).
3. Evaluation (評價) should be examined (檢討) in a direction (方向) that can concretely (具體的) present (提出) development materials (發展資料) for new tasks (作業). In particular, scientific (科學的) analysis (分析) should be conducted to present (提出) evidence (證據) of the necessary (必要) materials (資料) and possibilities (可能性) for the continuous (持續的) development (發展) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).


--- (p. 176) ---

It must be done.
Additionally, when conducting evaluations (評價), examining the procedures (節次) reveals:
First, clearly define the main purpose (目的) of the evaluation (評價) to set the content (內容) and direction (方向) of the evaluation plan (評價計劃).
Second, concretely determine the content (內容) and methods (方法) of the evaluation (評價).
Third, establish various means and systems (體系) for the evaluation work (評價作業).
Fourth, systematically organize (整理) the evaluation results (評價結果).
Fifth, analyze (分析) the evaluation results (評價結果) and seek methods for their utilization (活用方法).
After the city (市)·county (郡) council (協議會) has conducted the above evaluations (評價), it formulates comprehensive countermeasures (綜合對策) as corrective measures (是正措置).

Finally, the function (機能) of the city (市)·county (郡) council (協議會) is to establish plans (計劃) for the funds (資金) and material support (資材支援) required to promote (推進) the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). Support (支援) varies in content (內容) depending on the development stage of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動). Generally, the principles (原則) of support (支援) are:
1. Consider the self-help capabilities (自助能力) and efficiency (効率性) of the target regional community (對象地域社會).
2. Conduct it in a direction (方向) that connects production (生產) and income (所得).
3. It should respond to the needs (慾求) of the residents (住民) of the target regional community (對象地域社會).
Guidance (指導) and support (支援) for the Saemaul Undong (新村事業) were carried out in various ways, and this played a significant role in promoting the Saemaul Undong (新村運動).

## La. Composition (構成) and Functions (機能) of the Township (邑)·Township Promotion Committee (面推進委員會)

### (1) Composition (構成)

The Township (邑)·Township Promotion Committee (面推進委員會) was organized to promote (推進) the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) within the township (邑)·township (面) through comprehensive guidance (指導)·support (支援).
Examining the composition (構成) of this committee (本 委員會), it is chaired (委員長) by the township (邑)·township head (面長), with vice township (副邑)·township heads (面長), police station chiefs (支署長), local school principals (鄕土學校長), rural guidance sub-branch managers (農村指導所支所長), unit agricultural cooperative managers (單位農業協同組合長), fisheries cooperative managers (水産業協同組合長), postmasters (郵遞局長), Saemaul Undong (新村運動) leaders (指導者), and other necessary personnel (人士) serving as committee members (委員).
Meanwhile, examining some characteristics (特徵) of the composition (構成) of the Township (邑)·Township Promotion Committee (面推進委員會):
First, it can be pointed out that the Township (邑)·Township Promotion Committee (面推進委員會) is composed of people who can represent the will (意思) and interests (利益) of the local residents (地域住民).
Second, it was composed of representatives (代表) of guidance (指導) and support agencies (支援機關) for post-management (事後管理) of the Saemaul Undong (新村事業).


--- (p. 177) ---

### Chapter 3 (第3章) The Implementation System of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

One can point out that the Saemaul Undong (事業) is not only important for its implementation (推進) and achievements (成就), but also for how its results (成果) can be sustained (持續化) afterwards. In other words, post-management (事後管理) refers to the process (過程) of maintaining and protecting the results (成果) that have been achieved (達成) to ensure that their effects (效果) continue to manifest (顯現) afterwards. If post-management (事後管理) is not thorough (徹底), the existing results (成果) may become futile (徒勞), or in some cases, even hinder (阻害) the implementation (推進) of new projects (事業).

#### (2) Functions (機能)

The functions (機能) of the town (邑) and county (面) promotion committees (推進委員會) include:

1. **Surveying Residents' Aspirations (住民의 여망調査):** The primary (一義的) role (役割) is to survey (調査) the aspirations (與望) of the residents (住民). The Saemaul Undong (運動) is ultimately (結局) a movement to enhance (增進) the welfare (福祉) of the local residents (地域住民). Therefore, it is crucial (重要) to understand (把握) and comprehensively analyze (綜合分析) the hopes (希望) of the residents (住民) before promoting (推進) the Saemaul Undong (事業), as it requires (要求) integrated (統合的) efforts (努力) from all residents (住民) to take root (根付) and bear fruit (結實).

2. **Investigating and Studying Local Community Characteristics (地域社會의 특性調査 및 硏究):** Unlike agricultural guidance projects (農事敎導事業), the Saemaul Undong (事業) aims to enhance (增進) not only the individual (個個人) interests (利益) of farmers (農民) but also the overall (全體的) interests (利益) of the entire local community (地域社會全住民). Therefore, it is necessary (必要) to investigate (調査) and study (硏究) the various characteristics (諸特性) of the local community (地域社會) to explore (模索) new directions (方向) for projects (事業).

3. **Establishing Detailed Plans for Project Implementation (事業遂行에 소요되는 요소의 세부計劃樹立):** Detailed plans (計劃) are established for the necessary elements (要素) required for project implementation (事業遂行), such as funds (資金), materials (資材), and labor (勞力). Efficient allocation (配分) of resources (資源) during the project implementation (事業推進) process not only improves (提高) the efficiency (能率性) of the project (事業) but also contributes (貢獻) to maximizing (極大化) its effects (效果).

4. **Guidance and Pioneering Activities for the Saemaul Undong (運動) (新村運動에 대한指導 및 先驅的活動):** The town (邑) and county (面) promotion committees (推進委員會) also play a role (役割) in guiding (指導) and pioneering (先驅) activities (活動) for the Saemaul Undong (運動). Various institutional (制度的) supports (支持) are crucial (重要) for actively (積極的) promoting (推進) the Saemaul Undong (運動). For example, improving (改善) financial (金融) or fiscal (財政制度) systems (制度) to solve (解決) funding (資金問題) issues, improving (改善) ownership (所有制度) systems (制度) for collective production (共同生產), and other administrative (行政) guidances (指導) are necessary (必要). Additionally, educational (敎育) guidance (指導) is provided to expand (擴大) the Saemaul Undong (事業).

The education (敎育) for the Saemaul Undong (運動) includes:

1. Not only "education (敎育)" but also "training (訓練)."
2. Not only residential (合宿) education (敎育) but also club (クラブ) learning activities (學習活動).
3. Programmatic (式)


--- (p. 178) ---

In addition to education (敎育), on-site training (現場實習) is included, and fourthly, in addition to educational formats (敎育形式), "promotion" (弘報) is also included. Various forms of Saemaul education (敎育) can be summarized as follows (Table 1).

[Diagram: Forms of Saemaul Education]
The forms of Saemaul education (새마을敎育) are divided into three major categories: education (敎育), promotion (弘報), and training (訓練).
* The first category of education (敎育) includes program-style education (式敎育), admission-style education (入所式敎육), club learning activities (學習活動), and on-site learning-style education (現場習式敎育).
* The second category is promotion (弘報).
* The third category of education (敎육) includes training (訓練).

Source: Jang Won-sang (張源相), "Regional Community Development Administration (地域社會開發行政論)," Samyeongsa (三英社), 1979, p. 376

Fifthly, the functions of the township (邑) and myeon (面) Promotion Committee (推進委員會) include coordination (協調) with administrative agencies (行政機關) and related agencies (有關機關). As a large and multipurpose (多目的) project (事業) being promoted (推進), the Saemaul Undong cannot be handled by a single organization (組織體) or administrative agency (行政機關) alone, thus requiring the cooperation (協調) of various guiding (指導) agencies (機關) and related agencies (機關). The administrative functions (行政機能) of the government (政府) aim to promote (促進) voluntary (自發的) participation (參與) of the residents (住民) and provide guidance (指導) and support (支援). Schools (學校) contribute significantly to the Saemaul Undong through industrial cooperation (產業協同), training of leaders (指導者), and students' (學生) volunteer (奉仕) activities (活動). Religious organizations (宗敎團體), media outlets (言論機關), cooperatives (協同組合), and other social organizations (社會團體) also provide substantial support (支援活動).

### Ma. Composition (構成) and Functions (機能) of the Ri (里) and Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員會)

#### (1) Composition (構成)

Since the late 1960s (年代), comprehensive coordinating bodies (綜合協議體) have been organized in each ri (里) and dong (洞) to adjust (調整) the businesses (事業) and interests (利益) of various functional (機能別) resident organizations (住民組織). The Daedonggye (大同契) also falls under this category. The so-called "Ri (里) and Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員會)" is a coordinating body (協議體) with all residents (住民) of the ri (里) and dong (洞) as members, overseeing (統轄) each functional (機能別) organization (組織) within the ri (里) and dong (洞), and serving as a comprehensive group (統括集團) that deliberates (討議) and decides (議決) on development projects (開發事業) within the ri (里) and dong (洞). A comprehensive group (統括集團) refers to a comprehensive coordinating body (綜合協議體) that adjusts (調整) the businesses (事業) and interests (利益) of various functional groups (機能集團) to integrate (綜合) and unify (統一化) collective activities (集團活動) in the relevant region (地域).

On the other hand, before mentioning the composition (構成) of the Ri (里) and Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員會), we would like to briefly outline (略述) the objectives (目標) of this committee (委員會) for the sake of logical development (論理的展開).
The Ri (里) and Dong (洞) Development Committee (開發委員會) aims to ① adjust (調整) the activities (活動) of various functional (機能別) resident organizations (住民組織).


--- (p. 179) ---

## Chapter 3: The Implementation Structure of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) aims to promote the discussion and decision-making of Saemaul projects, as well as the efficient enlightenment of administrative policies. To achieve these goals, the composition of the Ri (里)•Dong (洞) Development Committees is as follows:

First, the committee includes substantial representatives from various village-level organizations and self-generated organizations, totaling around 15 members.

Second, the committee chairperson is either a Saemaul leader or a Ri (里) head. If the chairperson is a Ri (里) head, they must cooperate with the Saemaul leader to operate the Ri (里)•Dong (洞) Development Committee.

Third, under the chairperson, there are committees for agricultural associations, women's associations, youth associations, village savings banks, and village libraries, as well as auditors for these organizations.

The above organizational structure is summarized in Table 2.

Meanwhile, the organization of the Saemaul Youth Association (青少年會) "4-H" in our country is primarily a purposeful group targeting natural villages (部落), with membership open to males and females aged 13 to 26.
