# Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

## Section 1 (第1節) Rural Saemaul Undong (農村 새마을운동)

### 1. Objectives of Rural Saemaul Undong (農村 새마을운동의 목표)

The rural areas of our country were originally impoverished, and during the industrialization process through industrialization (工業化) in the 1960s (年代), while industry (工業) advanced, agriculture (農業) relatively stagnated. The gap in economic (經濟的), social (社會的), and cultural (文化的) conditions between urban (都市) and rural (農村) areas widened.

If this situation (事態) was left unchecked, rural (農村) areas would become even more backward and impoverished, leading to increased social (社會的) instability due to the dual structure (二重構造). Meanwhile, as this situation (事態) progressed, opinions (意見) that backward rural (農村) areas needed development (開發) and that a self-sustaining economic system (自立經濟體制) could not be established without agricultural (農業) growth (成長) gradually became public opinion (輿論化) in the late 1960s (年代).

President Park Chung-hee (大統領) at the time (當時) condensed (集約) these aspirations (捻望) and ignited (點火) the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), which spread (擴散) to become the nationwide (汎國民的) movement it is today (今日).

Although the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) initially started as the "New Village Beautification Project" (새마을가꾸기사업), it was a trial (試驗的) endeavor launched amidst much skepticism (懷疑). However, its achievements (成果) exceeded expectations (期待), setting a solid foundation (基盤) for the further development (發展) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) by 1972 (年).

In other words, the development process (發展過程) of the rural Saemaul Undong (農村 새마을운동) progressed from the initial stage (最初段階) of foundation-building (基盤造成), through the stage (段階) of self-help development (自助發展), to the stage (段階) of self-sufficiency completion (自立完成).

To reiterate, from 1971 (年) to 1973 (年), the living environment (生活環境) and production conditions (生産條件) of 34,665 (個) villages were established (造成). From 1974 (年) onwards, the movement moved beyond the stage (段階) of being initiated (點火) and stimulated (刺戟) by the government (官), expanding (擴大) the scope (範圍) of voluntary (自律的) participation (參與). This marked the beginning of the self-help development stage (自助發展段階), which continued (繼續) until 1976 (年) when villages entered the self-sufficiency stage (自立段階).


--- (p. 220) ---

And in 1977, the Saemaul Undong in rural areas entered the stage of self-reliance and completion, and the government planned to complete the first phase of the Saemaul project by 1981, pushing the Saemaul Undong as a single village. In the 1970s, the rural Saemaul Undong developed through three stages: base establishment, self-help development, and self-reliance completion, based on the growth stage.

However, if the setting of the promotion goals of the Saemaul project is based, the order is different, starting from the stage of ignition stimulation, expanding the stage of participation range, and going through the stage of establishing the base of the Saemaul Undong, and by the end of the 1970s, it had entered the stage of deepening and expansion. Through this development process, it brought about a great change in the consciousness structure of farmers, and with the confidence of "I can do it" and the will to "I must do it," the Saemaul Undong of that time spread from the city to the factory.

The ideology of the Saemaul Undong can be summarized in one word as a movement to live well. This living well means that neighbors help each other, live frugally, and create a beautiful and pleasant village, while increasing farm income, making the village prosperous, and being able to lead a more leisurely, dignified, and cultural life.

However, the philosophical significance of the Saemaul Undong is not only important that we live well today, but also that we create a well-lived hometown for a better tomorrow. In particular, the characteristics of the rural Saemaul Undong lay in the importance of action and practice, and the "Saemaul Beautification Movement," which was initiated in the early days of the Saemaul Undong, was a project that started with the conviction that if we work hard with the spirit of self-help and self-reliance, all villages will soon become well-lived and cozy villages.

However, just thinking that we can live well does not mean that we can live well, and only when action and practice follow can the Saemaul Undong succeed, and this philosophy of practice forms the basis. In terms of the method of promoting the rural Saemaul Undong, the first is to be diligent, and the second is


--- (p. 221) ---

# Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Self-help spirit (自助精神) must be strong, and thirdly, cooperation (協同) among all villagers was emphasized.

A. Motivation for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

(1) Ignition of the Spark (刺戟點火)

Over the past 10 years, we have elevated and promoted the potential (底力) of our nation, which has built a once-glorious culture (文化) and overcome national crises (國難), through the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Diligence without a foundation is merely laziness (懶怠), and self-help without a foundation is just dependence (依存). Moreover, a society (社會) without a spirit of cooperation (協同心) can only invite conflict and cannot expect even a hint of productivity.

The spirit of the Saemaul Undong was conceived on the basis of such principles (基調) and not only that, but the Saemaul spirit was manifested through the decisive will (決斷毅志) to induce practical action (誘發). In particular, the rural Saemaul Undong (農村새마을運動) began to ignite (點火) in 1971 when 335 units of cement were provided to each of the 33,267 administrative villages (行政里洞) across the nation, prompting each village to launch the Saemaul Undong.

Each village started various improvement projects, including the expansion and maintenance of village access roads (進入路), small streams (小河川), lowlands (小溜地), communal wells, communal laundries, composting sites (堆肥場), and village tree planting (植樹), among the 10 major (大) beautification projects. The rural Saemaul Undong (農村새마을運動) thus began to unfold experimentally (試驗的).

A total of 7.2 million residents participated in these Saemaul beautification projects (事業), with an average of 12 projects per village, totaling 385,000 projects nationwide. Although the rural Saemaul projects (農村새마을事業) were initially experimental (試驗的), their results exceeded expectations, instilling confidence (自信感) in both the relevant administrative agencies (有關行政機關) and farmers (農民) that "it can be done." This genuine desire (眞慾) to live better further fueled the spread of the Saemaul Undong, establishing both its qualitative and spiritual foundations (精神的).

In other words, the cement provided to each village (里洞) as 335 units was the material (物質的) element (要素) that enabled the beautification projects (事業). Meanwhile, the farmers' (農民) firm will and cooperative (協同) unity (團結力), expressed through these material (物質的) elements (要素) as a medium (媒體), became the farmers' (農民) new spiritual (精神的) asset (資産).


--- (p. 222) ---

Moreover, farmers abandoned their stagnant and passive conservative mindset, which had been steeped in resignation, and found a great opportunity to renew their traditional way of life based on self-reliance, recognizing that poverty was their own fault rather than someone else's. In other words, the spark that ignited the Saemaul Undong was the burning desire to hate poverty and the fear of stagnating in an inferior state.

By the end of that year (1971), an analysis of the Saemaul Undong's achievements revealed that out of 33,267 villages (ri) and neighborhoods (dong) nationwide, 16,600 had excellently accomplished many projects beyond expectations. The reason for this was that those villages had excellent leaders, while others lacked competent leadership.

Thus, in 1972, the principle of prioritizing support for outstanding villages was established, and 16,600 villages were uniformly provided with 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement each to accelerate the Saemaul beautification projects. Additionally, efforts were made to focus on promoting the spiritual development of farmers.

### (2) Saemaul Education and Leader Training

For the Saemaul Undong to succeed, it was deemed crucial to prioritize the cultivation of village leaders. Consequently, leader training was initiated. The Agricultural Cooperative College's attached educational institution in Iseo-myeon, Yeoju-gun, Gyeonggi-do, was established as the Diligent Farmer Training Institute on January 14, 1972, and provided education to diligent farmers nationwide. From July 2, 1972, the target was changed to Saemaul leaders.

Meanwhile, the Diligent Farmer Training Institute was relocated to the Farmers' Hall in Suwon on April 8, 1973, and its name was changed to the "Saemaul Leader Training Institute" on May 31 of the same year. This institute truly became the birthplace of Saemaul leaders, strengthening its substance and conducting Saemaul spirit education, which laid the foundation for the further spread and deepening of the Saemaul Undong.

### B. Setting Indicators

The Saemaul Undong takes on various meanings depending on the perspective from which it is viewed. In other words, the rural Saemaul Undong is, based on its practicing subjects, a movement for farmers to live well. Based on its projects, it is a movement for improving living environments, establishing production bases, improving circulation structures, and promoting efficient farming. From the perspective of participation, it


--- (p. 223) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

At that time, the movement included aspects of transforming the consciousness structure of farmers and regional development activities.

Therefore, the goals of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) can be divided into four main categories. Firstly, it aimed to cultivate the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation among farmers. Secondly, it sought to increase the income of farming households. Thirdly, it aimed to improve the living environment conditions in rural areas. Lastly, it aimed to achieve a technological revolution in agriculture.

To achieve these goals, the period from 1971 to 1981 was divided into three stages. The first stage, from 1971 to 1973, was set as the foundation-building stage. The second stage, from 1974 to 1976, was designated as the self-help development stage. The final stage, from 1977 to 1981, was set as the self-reliance completion stage.

(1) Short-term Development Goals

(a) Spiritual Development Aspect

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in rural areas was a movement aimed at transforming the consciousness structure of farmers. It intended to shift from a typical stagnant society characterized by backwardness, stagnation, resignation, and laziness to one with a spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Specifically, it aimed to establish a new value order of "we" on top of the existing value system that had been based on "me" until now.

Through this transformation of the farmers' consciousness structure, the movement also aimed to promote increased production and income, which is self-evident.

Another important intention in the spiritual development aspect of farmers was to encourage the participation of women, who had previously been closed off, in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) by having them actively engage in Saemaul projects.

(b) Production and Income Aspect

To increase production and income for farming households, the movement initially planned to start with easy projects. These included expanding roads, straightening embankments, organizing farmland, and improving irrigation facilities to promote agricultural mechanization.

Additionally, village access road construction and expansion, village road expansion, telephone installation, communal warehouses, and village markets contributed significantly to improving the circulation of agricultural products. Furthermore, these improvements facilitated the purchase of agricultural materials and daily necessities, providing convenience to the farmers.


--- (p. 224) ---

The contributions are undeniable.

On the other hand, as another measure to improve productivity and increase income, efforts were made to establish village nurseries and village farms (ginseng, medicinal herbs, high-quality vegetables, specialty crops, etc.), village afforestation, livestock farming, aquaculture, and joint pest control. Additionally, attempts were made to transition from individual farming to a cooperative farming system through the joint use of agricultural machinery.

**(D) Environmental Improvement Aspect**

To ensure the sustainability of the Saemaul Undong and to foster a sense of self-reliance, efforts began with the most visible and tangible projects that could be felt immediately.

First, plans were made to improve the rural environment, focusing on the village as the center of basic living areas, including roofs, walls, toilets, and livestock sheds.

Second, plans were made to increase the telephone penetration rate in rural areas, which are essential cultural facilities for modern life, to promote telecommunications facilities, and to improve rural water supply through simple water supply facilities and shared wells. Additionally, efforts were made to improve rural road networks.

Third, plans were made to establish village-level shared facilities such as village warehouses, village markets, and village community centers with shared bathhouses.

Fourth, efforts were made to improve the scenic beauty of the country through projects such as beautifying national highways, small towns, and tourist attractions.

## Chapter 4 Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

In addition, the movement aimed to utilize the idle labor force (遊休勞動力) in rural areas (農村) and activate potential resources (潛在資源). It sought to use materials like sand, stones, and gravel, which had previously been discarded, to build various community facilities (共同利用建物) such as village roads, small bridges (小橋樑), and sewers (下水溝).

While the Saemaul Undong was being initiated and its foundation was being established between 1971 and 1973, the major objectives and specific plans for achieving these objectives were as follows. The major projects set during this period aimed to achieve the following goals by 1981, as shown in <Table 1>.

### (2) Long-term Development Goals (長期發展目標)

#### (a) Basic Direction (基本方向)

The government (政府) planned to complete the foundation-building projects (基盤造成事業) by 1973. From 1974 to 1976, it aimed to focus on production base projects (生産基盤事業) and welfare income projects (福祉所得事業) to finalize the standard rural environment (農村標準環境) through self-help development (自助發展). From 1977 to 1981, the government aimed to strengthen the income base (所得基盤) and expand non-agricultural income sources (農外所得) to achieve income growth (所得增大) through a self-reliance completion stage (自立完成段階). By 1981, the government aimed to develop all 34,871 villages (個) nationwide into model rural communities (標本農村) of the 1980s, ensuring that farm income growth (農家所得增大) was achieved through the self-help efforts (自助努力) of farmers (農民). This was the basic direction (基本方向) set by the government (政府).

Furthermore, to achieve these goals (目標), the government (政府) planned to:
1. Pursue large-scale agricultural increases (農業增産) and short-term agricultural income growth (農業所得增大).
2. Actively create basic cultural and welfare environments (文化福祉環境) in villages (部落).
3. Develop new income sources (所得源) through afforestation (治山綠化).
4. Elevate the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神) into a national practical philosophy (國民的 實踐哲學) to establish a self-disciplined national discipline (自律的國民紀綱) by concentrating all guidance (指導力) on these efforts.

#### (b) Key Objectives (重點目標)

The Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) cannot be achieved solely through enthusiasm. There are limitations to the abilities of the villagers (部落民) and the government's (政府) support. Therefore, the government (政府) set concrete goals (具體的目標) for the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) by 1981, considering the constraints (制約性) and conducting thorough examinations (檢討) with long-term economic prospects (長期經濟展望) and comprehensive national development plans (國土綜合開發) for the 1980s and related plans (關聯計劃).


--- (p. 226) ---

It set long-term development goals in four areas. Specifically, it aimed to establish production bases (including income increase), promote land reclamation and greening, and create a welfare environment (standard) (see Table).

In terms of establishing production bases, notable long-term goals included achieving an irrigation rate of 93% or higher by developing agricultural water facilities, actively promoting land consolidation, and widely distributing agricultural machinery to promote mechanized and scientific farming.

To achieve the key goal of increasing income, several important projects were planned, including production increase projects and the construction of Saemaul factories. A notable project within the production increase efforts involved labor projects to create village community funds. These funds were used to establish and expand various community facilities such as community seedling farms and community livestock farms through a revolving investment approach. This not only had a significant impact on creating community funds but also aimed to utilize these funds for community facilities or projects that benefit all residents.

In constructing Saemaul factories, the goal was to modernize factories to promote industrialization in rural areas and expand sources of non-agricultural income.

To achieve the long-term development goals, one of the key targets set was the land reclamation and greening plan. This included promoting income-generating afforestation (economic forests) to increase income and preserve national land, as well as vigorously promoting greening for erosion control and fuel forests.

In welfare environment creation projects, efforts were made to improve living environments, upgrade rural sanitation facilities, and install and utilize community facilities (such as community warehouses, community markets, and village halls) to enhance community consciousness among residents and improve their quality of life.

Regarding key spiritual goals, the movement aimed to promote the spirit of Saemaul through the following six practices:

First, eliminate unproductive and irrational customs, organize residents into cooperative groups, and establish a new national discipline.


--- (p. 227) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Second, through a large-scale ritual simplification movement, funeral and wedding expenses (관혼상제비) were reduced from 5% of per capita income in 1971 to 2%.

Third, by continuing the family planning movement, the population growth rate was reduced from 1.5% in 1972 to 1.3%.

Fourth, through the farmers' savings movement, a spirit of thrift was fostered in rural areas, and the expansion of income was reinvested to pursue higher income.

Fifth, a village fund, serving as the core of cooperation, was established with a minimum of 1 million won per village, and this was utilized in a 'sequential method' (회전확대재투자방식) to promote economic self-reliance through the autonomous efforts of the village.

Sixth, the Saemaul education, which had focused on spiritual education, was developed into elite education and technical education to aim for the elitization and technicization of all farmers.

## 2. Characteristics and Tasks of the Initial Stage

### a. Classification of Village Types

In 1973, all villages across the nation were stratified into basic villages (기초마을), self-help villages (자조마을), and self-reliant villages (자립마을) based on their development levels. The Saemaul Undong was then initiated according to the capabilities of these villages. Along with this classification, Saemaul projects were divided into basic projects (기본사업), support projects (지원사업), and income projects (소득사업) based on their functions and impacts. Support was then provided according to the conditions and acceptance capabilities of the villages.

Villages were divided into three stages: basic villages, self-help villages, and self-reliant villages, because different support and guidance methods were required depending on the development stage of the villages.

According to the government's classification in 1972, there were 18,415 basic villages, 13,943 self-help villages, and 2,370 self-reliant villages.

Next, standard projects (표준사업) were set for each stage that villages should gradually transition to.

The standard projects for each village level were desirable from the village's perspective, and all villages were to develop from basic villages to self-help villages and then to self-reliant villages. The requirements for each level were clearly stated in advance, guiding the villagers to


--- (p. 228) ---

The purpose was to enable people to judge for themselves what needed to be done.

A basic village, as the name suggests, was a village where the Saemaul Undong had just begun, primarily focusing on Saemaul beautification projects. These villages mainly undertook projects such as expanding farm roads, improving roofs, repairing small streams, and building communal laundry areas. They received basic government support in the form of 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement.

Basic villages placed particular emphasis on environmental improvement and spiritual development to ignite the spirit of self-help.

The next stage, self-help villages, received basic government support and were villages where Saemaul beautification projects were nearing completion. In addition to beautification projects, they undertook projects such as beautifying small streams and creating multipurpose ponds. They also established communal nurseries, communal livestock farms, and communal farms, aiming to raise a village fund of 500,000 won.

For self-help villages, the government decided to provide sufficient support based on their achievements, unlike the basic support provided to basic villages.

Upon reaching the final stage of self-reliant villages, they undertook various projects such as communal income projects, production base projects, cultural welfare projects, income-central projects, and production cooperative projects that were not completed in the self-help village stage. They also strove to raise a village fund of over 1 million won to qualify as a self-reliant village and to promote projects.

On the other hand, the government established priority support policies and actively fostered self-reliant villages to play a leading role in the Saemaul Undong. When a village reached the self-reliant stage, the government mainly guided them to focus on income projects and cultural welfare projects.

Therefore, the standard projects set by the government for each village level were largely exemplary, and only the most common and essential ones were selected as mandatory standard projects for each village level. The mandatory standard projects required for promotion, or the mandatory standard projects for each village level, are as shown in Table 2. To advance from a basic village to a self-help village stage, in addition to Saemaul beautification projects, the irrigation rate had to reach 80%, and in cooperative farming, a preliminary level of cooperation


--- (p. 229) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The formation of action work teams and the establishment of a village fund of 300,000 won per village were among the necessary conditions.

When a basic village became a self-help village, the following mandatory criteria were required for promotion to a self-reliance village:

In addition to the Saemaul beautification projects, achieving a 70% irrigation rate, owning a power weeder, promoting cooperative production businesses, and establishing a village fund of 500,000 won were necessary. Achieving an income of 800,000 won per household was also a mandatory requirement.

After a self-help village matured, it would be promoted to the self-reliance village stage. The businesses that a self-reliance village had to undertake included improving village external small and medium streams, achieving an 85% irrigation rate, owning power tillers and power threshers, promoting cooperative production businesses, establishing a village fund of over 1,000,000 won, and achieving an income of 1,400,000 won per household. These were regulated as mandatory businesses.

## B. Functional Stage Division of Businesses (事業)

In rural Saemaul businesses, the nature of the businesses was divided into basic businesses (基本事業), support businesses (支援事業), and income businesses (所得事業). Accordingly, the relevant ministries (有關部處) that provide support were regulated.

Therefore, Saemaul businesses were planned and operated through functional stage division, where relevant government ministries mutually cooperated to support their respective businesses. Here, basic businesses included farm road construction, roof improvement, and other living environment businesses (生活環境事業), which were continuously supported by the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部).

Support businesses were divided into labor businesses (勞役事業) and cultural welfare businesses (文化福祉事業).


--- (p. 230) ---

Improvement projects such as village beautification, small road improvement, and small stream improvement were supported by the Ministry of Interior (內務部), while another support project (支援事業), the cultural welfare project (文化福祉事業), was spread across multiple ministries. The fishery village reclamation project (漁村干拓事業) was handled by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部), standard rural housing (農村標準住宅) by the Ministry of Construction (建設部), simple water supply facilities (簡易給水施設) and mobile medical services (移動診療) by the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs (保健社會部), village communication facilities (通信施設) by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (遞信部), and methane gas facility guidance (施設指導) by the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳).

Meanwhile, the income project (所得事業) was divided into two main categories: the income-centralization project (所得求心事業) and the Saemaul production project (生産事業). In the income-centralization project (所得求心事業), village afforestation and seedling cultivation (養苗) were guided by the Korea Forest Service (山林廳), and rural handicrafts (工藝品事業) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部).

The Saemaul production project (生産事業) aimed at increasing farm income (農家所得) focused on collective farming (集團栽培) of crops (作目), compost production (堆肥增産), agricultural time management (營農時期制限), pest control (病蟲害防除), and doubling land use (土地利用倍加), among other production cooperative projects (生産協同事業) and production structure improvement projects (生産構造改善事業). The Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農水産部) was responsible for guiding and supporting these projects.

### Da. Business Promotion Plan (事業推進計劃)

#### (1) Step-by-step village development plan (段階別育成計劃)
In the initial stage of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), the goals set to be achieved by 1981 through the movement were as follows: in terms of income (所得), an average of 1.4 million won per household for all farming households (農家), and in terms of village standards (水準), the development of all 34,871 villages nationwide into self-sufficient villages (自立마을).

To achieve these goals, the plan was to proceed in stages and annually: from 1973 as the infrastructure establishment stage (基盤造成段階), from 1976 as the self-help development stage (自助發展段階), and from 1981 as the self-sufficiency completion stage (自立完成段階). This was also the step-by-step village development plan (段階別育成計劃). Summarizing the content of this development plan (育成計劃), it was estimated that by 1973, all 34,665 villages nationwide, starting from basic villages (基礎마을) in 1971, would be able to develop as follows:

First, with a focus on igniting and heating up the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神) and establishing a self-help atmosphere (自助氣風), 30% would be basic villages (基礎마을), 60% self-help villages (自助마을), and 10% self-sufficient villages (自立마을).

Second, in the second stage (第2段階), from 1974 to 1976, the self-help development stage (自助發展段階), it was planned to further develop and advance the self-help cooperative power (自助協同力) that had been established so far.


--- (p. 231) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The plan was to elevate all villages from the basic village stage (基礎마을段階) to a level where 60% are semi-self-help villages (準自助마을) and 40% are self-sufficient villages (自立마을).

The third stage, which can be considered the self-sufficiency completion stage (自立完成段階), aimed to complete the income base (所得基盤) and dramatically increase non-agricultural income (農外所得). By the target year of 1981 (年), the plan was to develop all villages into self-sufficient villages (自立마을) by setting stage-by-stage (段階別) goals. Accordingly, annual (年次別) business goals (事業目標) were set to cultivate the villages.

## (2) Village Development Plans by Type (類型別 育成計劃)

Excluding cities (都市), all villages nationwide (全國마을) can be broadly categorized into flatland villages (平野마을), intermediate villages (中間마을), mountain villages (山村마을), fishing villages (漁村마을), and suburban villages (近郊마을). Just as the locational conditions (立地的 與件) of all villages nationwide (全國) differ, each has its own unique character (個性) in terms of living traditions (生活傳統) and ways of thinking (思考方式).

Taking this into account, the plan was to develop all villages based on their unique characteristics (個性). The government (政府) decided to categorize villages by region (地域別), village type, and special characteristics (特性別 類型化) to provide guidance (指導) tailored to each village's characteristics (特性). The government (政府) paid special attention to this aspect.

Following this plan, the government set the main guidance directions (方向) for villages based on their locational types (立地類型別 特性).

First, 8,104 flatland villages (平野마을) were selected to take a leading role in agricultural mechanization (農業機械化). The plan was to focus on guiding the reorganization of farmland (農耕地 整理), the establishment of agricultural machinery centers (農機械 設置), and the establishment of agricultural product processing facilities (農産物加工施設 設立).

For 18,995 intermediate villages (中間마을), the plan was to focus on guiding suitable crop farming (適性田作), including semi-enterprise livestock farming (準企業畜産) (Hanwoo (韓牛), pork (肉豚)), development of suitable crops (適性作物開發) (perilla, chili peppers, medicinal herbs, etc.), and fuel forest creation.

For 4,330 suburban villages (近郊마을), the plan was to focus on guiding advanced horticulture (高等園藝), fruit trees, vegetables, and home-based handicrafts (家內手工業). For 1,583 fishing villages (漁村마을), the plan was to focus on guiding the modernization (近代化) of fishing port facilities (漁港施設) to improve fishing gear (改善), construct breakwaters (防波堤), renovate piers, and develop aquaculture businesses (養殖事業).

For 1,953 mountain villages (山村마을), the plan was to focus on developing forestry income sources (林產所得源).


--- (p. 232) ---

### (3) Expansion Plan for the Movement by Region

If we consider a village to be the most basic unit of life, as well as a traditional community, we can refer to it as a 1st-order living sphere. Then, a few adjacent villages that are closely interconnected can form a 2nd-order living sphere. At the township level, we can consider a 3rd-order living sphere, and at the city/county level, we can refer to it as a regional urban sphere.

Of course, based on this classification method, we can also refer to our living spheres as follows. That is, from the village level, we can call the 2nd-order living sphere a cooperative sphere, the 3rd-order living sphere a small regional sphere, and the city/county level a medium regional sphere. In any case, the Saemaul Undong should be ignited at the village level, which is the 1st-order living sphere, and after achieving success, it should gradually expand its scope to the 2nd-order and 3rd-order living spheres.

According to this promotion plan, the Saemaul Undong also decided to expand its scale and scope from village-level projects to inter-village projects, and then to regional joint-use projects at the township level. Furthermore, in the process of promoting the movement, it began to organically link local projects and promote the Saemaul Undong in a developmental direction, adhering to the principles of functional and systematic connections.

At this time, inter-village joint projects and joint-use facilities included the establishment of agricultural product collection centers, the establishment of agricultural machinery centers, the establishment of agricultural product processing facilities, and the improvement of roads within the region.

### (4) Support and Promotion Strategies for the Movement

In supporting the Saemaul Undong in rural areas, support should be provided based on the village's long-term plan, with a long-term vision and in a planned manner. This will further foster the village's autonomous development aspirations and complete village projects one by one. At the same time, special efforts should be made to organically connect the village projects with each other and promote functional systematization.


--- (p. 233) ---

To enhance the effectiveness of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) projects, the principle of focusing support on outstanding villages was consistently upheld. In terms of supporting these projects, all Saemaul projects were categorized into three types and promoted accordingly: resident self-reliance projects, basic support projects, and special support projects.

Resident self-reliance projects referred to initiatives that should be carried out solely through the residents' own efforts, without support from the government or local autonomous bodies. These included projects such as compost production, time-limited farming, and village fund establishment. Basic support projects involved partially supporting basic materials like cement and rebar to facilitate projects such as village road improvement, sewer systems, and small-scale water facilities. Special support projects were those promoted according to the criteria set by the competent authorities for each project, based on their nature. These included projects like land consolidation, rural telephone services, and most village communal income-generating projects.

To elevate the achievements of the rural Saemaul Undong, all local administrative policies were shifted to a village-centered system. Particularly, efforts were made to improve the administration of local towns and districts, strengthen guidance for villages, and gradually expand village management projects like afforestation and seedling cultivation. Furthermore, local administrative policies were operated as welfare administration to make projects more income-oriented for residents. The promotion of these projects followed a multi-stage approach (rotational expansion and reinvestment method) to enable villagers to expand their welfare funds.

Additionally, as a long-term plan, the living areas of farmers were divided into small, medium, and large regional zones. Under the policy to gradually expand and develop the scope of Saemaul projects, plans were made to promote and implement communal projects and facilities for each regional zone. However, these project promotion plans could not be completed in the 1970s and were carried over into the 1980s.

### 3. Enhancing Farmhouse Income and Promoting Agricultural Production

#### a. Expansion of Income-Centered Projects and Afforestation
The implementation of income-centered projects to increase farmhouse income began in the mid-1960s.


--- (p. 234) ---

In accordance with the legislative spirit of the Agricultural and Fisheries Basic Act (업기본법), the basic direction of agricultural and forestry policies (농림시책) shifted from focusing on increasing food crop production (식량작물증산) to implementing projects to create main production areas (주산지) for economic crops (경제작물), including maintaining agricultural product prices (농산물가격유지). This shift gradually transformed into strategies to increase the income of farming and fishing households (농어가소득 증대시책).

Consequently, a bold initiative was undertaken to promote special projects for increasing the income of farmers and fishermen (농어민 소득증대 특별사업) across the nation's rural and fishing villages (농어촌) to enhance their income (소득). The push for these projects was driven by the need to overcome the lagging agricultural sector (농업부문 낙후성) in the rapid modernization process of the Korean economy (한국경제 근대화), making it an important task to achieve a harmonious and balanced development among industrial sectors (산업부문간 발전문제).

To narrow the gaps between industries (산업간) and regions (지역간) and create a balanced and stable rural and fishing community (농어촌), efforts were made to increase the income of participating farmers and fishermen (참여농어가 소득증대) and develop the regional community (지역사회 개발). The following selection criteria for projects were established to achieve these goals:

1. Projects that can achieve increased income for farmers and fishermen (농어민소득 증대) through the concurrent development of agriculture, industry, and fisheries (농공병진시책), with good prospects for economic profitability (경제적 수익성) and marketability (시장성).
2. Projects that enable complex production (복합생산) and can supply raw materials (원료) to adjacent processing facilities (인접 처리 가공시설).
3. Projects that can be successfully implemented (성공적 수행) with the active participation (적극적 참여) and support (호응) of local residents (지역주민).
4. Projects where the selection of crops (당해작물) or businesses (사업) must have sufficient technical feasibility (기술적 가능성) considering factors such as soil quality (토질), water resources (수자원), temperature (기온), and transportation (교통).
5. Project beneficiaries (사업대상자) must have sufficient experience (경험), track record (실적), and motivation (의욕) to manage or operate (경영 또는 관리) the project (당해사업).
6. Government support funds (정부 지원자금) should be allocated (계상) from funds secured (확보) by relevant government agencies (관계부처) that can be reliably used (확실하게 사용할 수 있는).
7. Resident self-funding (주민자담자금) should be set (책정) within the range that project managers or operators (당해사업 경영 또는 관리자) can sufficiently bear (부담) in terms of property (재산) and effort (노력).

Under these project selection criteria (사업선정기준) and support measures, the promotion and development of special projects for increasing the income of farmers and fishermen (농어민 소득증대 특별사업) were carried out. From the mid-1970s, these projects were included within the scope of the New Village Income Increase Special Projects (새마을소득증대 특별사업), and the promotion methods also shifted from being centered around specific individuals (특정인) or regions (지역) to a broader approach.


--- (p. 235) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

As the movement shifted to focus on villages and Saemaul leaders took the helm, the name of the initiative was changed to the Saemaul Income Augmentation Project. This led to vigorous efforts to boost farm household incomes through income-centered projects.

The Saemaul Income Augmentation Special Project aimed to specialize in production items at the village level and create main production areas to significantly increase the income of farmers and fishermen. The project prioritized support for outstanding villages to enhance investment effects and foster community cooperation. Simultaneously, it strengthened support for stable production items centered on exports. Efforts were made to promote continuous production and distribution systems in each regional production area. The main target items for the Saemaul Income Augmentation Project included:

1. Sericulture (蠶業) income
2. Shiitake mushroom (洋松茸) income
3. Specialty crop (特用作物) income
4. Medicinal herb (藥用作物) income

While establishing regional specialization systems for farm household income augmentation, the Saemaul Village Beautification Project was promoted, focusing on the expansion and construction of farm roads, the installation of large and small bridges, and the repair of village access roads to improve distribution and increase farm household income. Additionally, Saemaul warehouses were actively constructed to efficiently store and manage agricultural products.

Production cooperation projects included guiding the establishment of general farming complexes, horticultural complexes, and livestock farming complexes. Production teams were organized and operated by crop type to create a foundation for cooperative production and maximize production, distribution, and income.

During this period, large-scale afforestation projects were promoted to increase village income through community afforestation projects. Efforts were also made to develop forestry-specialized crops and guide residents to utilize them as income sources. Thus, afforestation projects implemented from the mid-1970s were highly contributory to village income.


--- (p. 236) ---

Fast-growing trees (速成樹) suitable for landscaping (造景) and early greening (早期綠化) of the countryside were prioritized in the forest greening projects (山林綠化事業) as part of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in rural areas.

On the other hand, villages centered around persimmon trees (주목) as the main species (主木) and engaged in collective (集團) afforestation (造林) of fruit-bearing trees (有實樹) to create a sustainable (恒久的) source of income (所得源) for farmers (農家). Particularly (特히) in villages highly dependent (依存度) on forest products (林產燃料) for fuel, community-level (마을單位) fuel forests (燃料林) were established, and the yield (收穫) per unit (單位當) was increased through a village-wide (마을共同) forest management system (育林管理體制) to aggressively (過敢) promote forest greening projects (山林綠化事業) as a source of income (所得源) for farmers (農家).

Additionally, villagers cooperated (協同) to produce seedlings (苗木) for afforestation (造林), linking (連繫) seedling collection (採苗) and afforestation (造林) to enhance (高) the success of village afforestation (마을造林), contributing (寄與) to increased (增加) income (所得) for residents (住民) while also improving (向上) the level (水準) of forestry technology (林業技術). Priority (優先) was given to villages with technical (技術) expertise (熱意) for village seedling production (育苗事業), and 1-2 tree species (樹種) that were easy (容易) to cultivate (施業) were selected to promote (促進) specialization (專門化) while aggressively (大大的) advancing (推進) forest greening projects (山林綠化事業).

Another objective (目的) of the forest greening projects (山林綠化事業) was the active (積極) protection (保護) and development (開發) of natural grass resources (自然草資源) to utilize (利用) them as a means (手段) of increasing (所得源) livestock income (畜產所得源) (家畜飼料).

The promotion (推進) of forest greening projects (山林綠化事業) aimed to manage (管理) and develop (育成) national and public forests (國公有林野) and absentee-owned forests (不在山主林野) through village-wide (마을共同管理) efforts (通), not only to achieve (期) forest greening (山林綠化) but also to qualitatively (質的) improve (向上) natural protection (自然保護) and secure (確保) water resources (水資源).

Furthermore, the forest greening projects (山林綠化事業) extended (及) to rural village (農村村) soil conservation projects (砂防事業), where villagers greened (綠化) bare land (裸地) around the village (周邊) and engaged in wild stream (野溪) soil conservation projects (砂防事業) to restore (直) eroded (倒) mountains (山) and valleys (溪谷). These projects were broadly implemented (推進) in the latter half of the 1970s (年代) as part of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in rural areas. The main contents (主要事業內容) of these projects were as follows:

1. Bare land greening projects (裸地綠化事業)
2. Wild stream soil conservation projects (野溪砂防事業)
3. Seed collection projects (種子採取事業)

Such forest greening (山林綠化) and increased forest income (山林所得增隊) aimed to maximize (最大限) the utilization (活用) of forest resources (山林資源) to develop (開發) and secure (確保) forest income sources (山林所得源). The main directions (主軸) of these efforts included the cultivation (栽培) of persimmon trees (主目), shiitake mushrooms (表고버섯), fruit-bearing trees (有實樹), and the afforestation (造林) of fast-growing trees (速成樹).

## B. Establishment of a Plan to Improve Rural Self-Sufficiency (農村自立度向上計劃)


--- (p. 237) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The development of rural society cannot be achieved in a discontinuous state. If development is to occur through a process of change, it is important to continuously propose new development indicators while building upon the foundation laid by the Saemaul Undong. Thus, as the rural Saemaul Undong entered the self-reliance completion stage in the latter half of the 1970s, the establishment of a self-reliance completion system became an important task for the further deepening and expansion of the rural Saemaul Undong. Consequently, the formulation and implementation of plans to improve the degree of rural self-reliance became an important task for the rural Saemaul Undong.

The demand for the self-reliance completion of rural areas emerged in the latter half of the 1970s. This is because, from this time onwards, efforts were focused on cultivating the self-help development capabilities of farmers and establishing a self-reliant development system centered around the village community. Moreover, in terms of project content, it became an important task to strengthen both the quantitative and qualitative aspects of various projects that had been promoted thus far, in order to lay a solid foundation for the realization of a welfare-oriented rural society.

From this point onwards, various educational projects were significantly expanded to enhance the self-help development capabilities of farmers. These projects targeted Saemaul leaders, including female Saemaul leaders and Saemaul youth, and included vocational training, agricultural guidance training, winter agricultural technology education, and other forms of specialized education. Through these efforts, specialized knowledge and skills necessary for daily life and agriculture were disseminated. Additionally, continuous efforts were made to promote the development of villages based on their respective development levels, aiming to raise the degree of village self-reliance to a higher level. This was done to promote balanced development in rural areas while simultaneously establishing an autonomous development base centered around the village community through the implementation of self-reliance improvement plans.

In particular, the direction of the plan's promotion placed emphasis on the cultural and welfare aspects. To improve the living conditions in rural areas from a health and hygiene perspective, communication facilities were significantly expanded nationwide, ensuring that every administrative village had telephone facilities. Additionally, simple water supply systems and mobile medical services were implemented.

Through these efforts, the aim was to reduce the development gap between rural and urban areas nationwide and to contribute to the establishment of a balanced national economy. Furthermore, the plan to improve the degree of rural self-reliance shifted from small-scale projects at the village community level to a more gradual and comprehensive approach.


--- (p. 238) ---

The plan aimed to expand the movement to large-scale regional projects by encouraging mutual cooperation among several villages with similar geographic, social, and economic conditions. The rural self-reliance improvement plan, as part of the Saemaul Undong, was designed to diversify and enhance rural income sources, shifting the focus from staple crops to high-value crops (various high-quality vegetables and fruits), fruit trees, special crops (ginseng, tobacco), livestock, and other specialty crops. This was done by considering each region's climate and local conditions, selecting appropriate crops, and promoting collective farming (cluster farming—main production area) while facilitating the purchase of necessary agricultural production materials and the sale of products in more advantageous ways.

The rural self-reliance improvement plan, as part of the Saemaul Undong, aimed to enhance farm income, diversify village income sources, and expand off-farm employment opportunities. Additionally, it sought to promote agricultural mechanization, improve farm management, and transform agricultural production structures. On another front, it aimed to foster social development in rural villages.

To measure the level of such social development, social indicators were used alongside economic indicators centered on material aspects. These social indicators measure various conditions across different social sectors to evaluate welfare levels and track social change processes. They encompass three areas: objective conditions, subjective welfare, and value trends. Often, objective conditions are used to understand the organic relationships among the components of the social system.

Thus, the rural self-reliance improvement plan was designed to set rural social development welfare indicators and implement them, considering aspects such as improved education levels and enhanced cultural living standards.

Additionally, the implementation of the rural self-reliance improvement plan was based on the comprehensive and integrated development of rural areas. First, it aimed to expand rural development. That is, through this, it sought to improve rural


--- (p. 239) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

The Saemaul Undong was promoted to create new aspects of the living environment, re-establish the spirit of cooperation, and firmly establish the will for self-reliance to improve the degree of self-reliance in rural areas.

Secondly, it aimed to pursue comprehensive rural development centered around economic zones. In other words, it sought to establish primary cooperative economic zones at the town and township levels, secondary cooperative economic zones at the city and county levels, and promote the formation of tertiary cooperative agricultural zones centered around major cities. This was done with the consciousness of purpose to further solidify the improvement of rural self-reliance.

Thirdly, it aimed to comprehensively promote strategic rural development projects. This included production base projects, increased production projects, rural industries, farm sideline businesses, environmental improvement, welfare enhancement, and educational projects, all in a comprehensive and inclusive manner.

Fourthly, it was promoted based on a consistent foundation of self-reliance, self-help, and cooperation throughout the entire process of production and distribution. Specifically, it promoted strategic product development projects for increased production centered around village units based on self-help and cooperation. It also promoted strategic processing and distribution development projects at the town, township, city, and county levels, as well as wide-area units, based on self-help and cooperation. This was done to solidify the foundation for improving rural self-reliance.

Fifthly, it was promoted to enable farmer self-help and cooperative organizations to play a leading role. In other words, it used cooperative associations as a medium to promote village-level improvement and joint development of idle resources. Simultaneously, it expanded and developed production support and distribution processing projects at the town, township, city, and county levels centered around special associations. This was done with the consciousness of purpose to firmly establish the improvement of rural self-reliance. The establishment of plans for improving rural self-reliance began in the latter half of the 1970s when the rural Saemaul Undong entered the stage of completing self-reliance. However, this was promoted with the consciousness of purpose to firmly establish a solid foundation for improving rural self-reliance, thereby realizing a welfare-oriented rural society. At the same time, it aimed to firmly prepare a foundation comparable to the self-reliance of urban areas.

### D. Variety Improvement (品種改良) and Renewal of Farming Techniques (營農技術)

Although Korea has traditionally positioned itself as an agrarian country, it has not achieved self-sufficiency in food and has not been able to wash away the disgrace of importing foreign rice. In terms of variety promotion, it has not been able to break away from the framework of cultivation using traditional varieties.


--- (p. 240) ---

It seemed to be the case.

Thus, in the agricultural technology aspect (營農技術面), stagnation (沈滯), poor performance (不振), and failure to break away from tradition (傳統性) were persistent. As part of the objectives of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in rural areas, achieving the ultimate goal of food self-sufficiency (食糧自給) and self-reliance (自足) required the promotion of the movement to develop and disseminate new varieties (新品種) and to renew agricultural technology (營農技術). This became an important task.

The expansion of the dissemination (普及擴大) of new varieties (新品種) was promoted by establishing demonstration sites (示範團地). At these sites, all farmers (農民) could constantly observe (觀察), and simultaneously, the sites recorded (記錄) the growth situation (生育狀況) and all work-related matters (作業關係). Evaluations (評價) were conducted at the site (團地現場) during the late seedling stage (苗板末期), heading stage (出穗期), and harvest stage (收穫期). Farmers actively participated (參與) in this process, acquiring (習得) and embodying (體得) the technology (技術) themselves, thereby achieving standardization (平準化) of technical levels (技術水準) and renewal (刷新) of agricultural technology (營農技술).

Through the promotion and development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in rural areas, the dissemination (普及) and expanded cultivation (擴大栽培) of unified (統一系統) and Yushin (維新系統) new varieties (新品種) were pursued to create a turning point (轉機) in food production (食糧增産) and to aim for increased farm income (農家所得增大). This effort began in the first half of the 1970s (1970년대).

By unifying (統一) varieties (品種) and cultivation techniques (栽培技術), equal yields (多收穫) could be achieved without gaps (隔差) between fields (圃地間). Simultaneous (同時) execution (施行) of the same work (作業) aimed to renew (刷新) agricultural technology (營農技術) through technical standardization (技術平準化). To this end, rice (米穀) collective (集團) cultivation (栽培) sites (團地) were operated (運營).

Furthermore, based on the diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperative spirit (協同精神) learned through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), collective work (共同作業) was practiced (實踐) from preparing seedbeds (못자리) to transplanting (모내기), fertilizing (施肥), and pest control (病蟲害 방제) to renew (刷新) agricultural technology (營農技術).

In particular, to actively introduce and disseminate (導入普及) improved varieties (品種改良), collective cultivation sites (團地營農) for rice (米穀), cereals (麥類), horticulture (園藝), and livestock (畜産) were actively promoted (推進).

Collective production work (生産協同作業) aimed to disseminate (普及) and expand (擴大) excellent varieties (優秀한) to achieve a turning point (劃期的) in rice production (米穀增産). Simultaneously, through the rice production process (米穀生產過程), collective (集團) time-limited farming (時限營農) addressed issues such as collective pest control (共同防除). Thorough cooperative work (協同作業) aimed to renew (刷新) agricultural technology (營農技術).

In particular, in the case of collective rice cultivation (米穀團地營農), farmers (農民) cultivating (耕作) fields (論) with similar natural conditions (自然條件) such as soil (土壤) and water (水利) set up (設定) a single site (團地), unified (統一) the variety (品種), and conducted (施) seedling raising (育苗) and transplanting (移秧).


--- (p. 241) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) practiced a cultivation method that unified and collectively implemented all processes and techniques of rice farming (水稻作), such as fertilization (肥), pest control (病蟲害防除), and water management (管理), in a metrological (計測的) manner, while aiming for variety improvement (品種改良) and simultaneously achieving a renewal (刷新) of agricultural techniques (營農技術). To this end, rice farming clusters (米穀團地營農) were established and operated.

Of course, the rice farming clusters (米穀團地營農) of the mid-1970s avoided the operation of large-scale production clusters (大單位增産團地) from the past and expanded village-based collective farming clusters (集團栽培團地). They adopted a cooperative farming cluster operation method (合同團地運營方式) that primarily cultivated new varieties (新品種) with a unified (統一) system (系統) within the clusters (團地).

To promote agricultural work (營農作業) cooperatively (共同) and collaboratively (協業), reduce costs (經費), and improve unit productivity (單位生產性), intensive cultivation methods (集約的栽培方法) were introduced. Regional (地域別) standard cultivation (標準耕種) criteria (基準) were set, agricultural machinery and materials (營農機資材) were prioritized for support (支援), and collective work (共同作業) was implemented. Demonstration farming (示範營農) was promoted as planned to renew (刷新) agricultural techniques (營農技術) for cereal cultivation (麥類栽培). To this end, agricultural operations (營農運營) centered around cereal clusters (麥類團地) were promoted.

In cases where individual farms (個別農家) raised livestock (家畜) using labor (勞動力) and agricultural by-products (農産副産物), not only was it difficult to improve the economic efficiency (經濟性) of raising (飼育) them, but due to insufficient technical (技術的) management (管理), productivity (生產性) was low, and small-scale raising (零細飼育) was disadvantageous (不利) for selling (販賣) as commodities (商品). To overcome this, livestock clusters (畜産團地) were operated by collectively (集團的) clustering (團地化) the same livestock breeds (畜種) to increase the number of livestock raised (飼育頭數) and create a foundation for economically efficient (經濟性) management (管理).

Despite the inevitable need for agricultural mechanization (農業機械化) in rural areas (農村) due to increased agricultural productivity (農業生産性), a decrease in the rural population (農村人口) leading to a shortage of agricultural labor (農業勞動力), and rising rural wages (農村賃金), purchasing agricultural machinery (農機械) was still a significant burden (負擔) for individual small-scale farms (零細規模農家別) to secure. Additionally, farmers (農民) not yet proficient (熟練) in machine management (機械管理) could not fully (完全) operate (運轉利用) or manage (管理) agricultural machinery (農機械). Therefore, small-scale farms (零細經營規模農家) could not economically (經濟性) afford to own (保有) high-priced (高價) agricultural machinery (農機械) for temporary (一時) use (使用), delaying agricultural mechanization (農業機械化) and hindering the improvement of farm productivity (農家生産性向上). To address this issue, village-level (單位) agricultural machinery (農機械) cooperative management bodies (共同運營體) were established as a means (手段) to contribute to the promotion of agricultural modernization (農業近代化).


--- (p. 242) ---

To promote the shared use of agricultural machinery, farmers were provided with agricultural machinery operation skill training, and repair centers were established centered around local agricultural cooperatives. This encouraged many farming households to participate in the demonstration of shared agricultural machinery management, fostering cooperation in farming and improving labor productivity.

By the late 1970s, to enhance productivity and rationalize management, the government expanded and strengthened the collective farming land development project. This involved the concentrated introduction of new high-yield crop varieties, fertilization, pest control, and other new cultivation techniques, as well as the efficient promotion of yield-increasing technologies.

In rice farming, to achieve short-term grain production increases, large-scale collective farming lands were established and operated, focusing on unified new varieties. These included contract yield-increase lands, self-reported yield-increase village lands, and collective farming lands. Additionally, demonstration lands for high-quality, high-yield new varieties such as Suwon 264, Milyang 23, and Naegyeong were established and operated to promote the expansion of new varieties and the renewal of farming techniques. The Saemaul Undong was vigorously promoted to achieve these goals.

Demonstration lands for new wheat varieties and collective soybean farming were also established and utilized as farmer education centers. These efforts aimed to expand the use of new varieties and renew farming techniques.

Furthermore, during the summer season, radishes and cabbages were produced using netting cover cultivation technology in highland and plain areas to increase farm income. Other crops such as garlic, onions, potatoes, strawberries, and peas were cultivated as pre-paddy crops to improve land use efficiency. Chili peppers were promoted through the dissemination of seedling cultivation and mulching transplantation techniques to ensure safe and high yields. Specialty crops like sesame, peanuts, rapeseed, and cotton were expanded in demonstration fields using high-quality seeds, which were then exchanged among neighboring farms to establish a system for the expansion and dissemination of high-quality seeds.

In regions where double-cropping of wheat and barley was not practiced, early-maturing barley varieties were introduced, and the cropping system was improved to enhance land use efficiency, increase food production, and raise farm income. Demonstration lands were established and operated in the central and northern regions for this purpose.

Additionally, to promote the dissemination of science and technology in rural areas and advance scientific farming, the Science and Technology Division organized the Saemaul Technology Guidance Team. Academics and technical experts actively participated in this initiative to achieve the renewal of farming techniques.


--- (p. 243) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

To support the essential specialized technologies (專門技術) for the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) and to guide various construction methods (工事), technical guidance teams (技術奉仕團) were organized and formed at the central and regional levels, with subdivisions (分科) for each sector (部門). Branches (支部) were established in each province (市道) to carry out systematic and flexible on-site guidance (現地指導).

Furthermore, the renewal of agricultural techniques (營農技術) was strongly promoted from an educational perspective (敎育的) on scientific farming (科學營農) for farmers (農民). This was done through various mass media (媒體) to disseminate (普及) necessary techniques (技術) for farmers and fishermen (農漁民) through expert explanations and guidance (解說指導) on secondary occupations (副業) and agricultural techniques (營農技術). This effort aimed to promote income growth (所得增進) and the scientification (科學化) of agriculture (營農), while also boosting enthusiasm (意慾) for the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동).

To foster an environment (與件) for scientific and technological advancement (科學技術), outstanding foreign (外國) and domestic (國內) scientific films (科學映畵) were secured (確保) and screened on a touring basis (巡廻上映). This provided opportunities (與件) to learn about advanced foreign science (先進科學), technology (技術), and information (情報), while also establishing (構築) the renewal of agricultural techniques (營農技術).

## 4. Stages Aimed at Regional Development (地域開發)

### a. Regional Dispersion of Saemaul Factories (工場)

As a leading policy (先導的) to increase non-agricultural income (農外所得) in rural areas (農村地域), the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) initiated the regional dispersion (地域分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) starting in 1973 (年). By 1973 (年), 111 Saemaul factories (工場) were designated and established (設立). From 1974 (年) to 1978 (年), 441 factories (工場) were established, and in 1979 (年), an additional 137 factories (工場) were set up, totaling 689 factories (工場) over the period (그간).

This initiative was crucial due to the high-speed and advanced economic growth (經濟成長) of the time, which made regional economic growth (地域經濟成長) through the dispersion of Saemaul factories (工場) an important task (課題) for the balanced development (均衡發展) of the national economy (國民經濟).

Regional economic growth (地域經濟成長) is often used interchangeably with terms like regional economic development (地域經濟發展) or regional economic expansion (地域經濟擴大). While there are various indicators (指標) to represent regional economic growth (地域經濟成長), some representative ones include improvements in regional welfare (福祉向上), increases in regional output (産出增加), and the growth of final goods (最終商品) produced in the region (地域). However, increases in output (産出) and final goods (最終商品) can be easily quantified (數量的).


--- (p. 244) ---

However, it has the flaw of physically perceiving economic growth (經濟成長) and measuring regional economic growth (地域經濟成長) through welfare (福祉) improvement is desirable as it uses the indicator of welfare (福祉), which is composed of complex (複合的) elements. However, it is very difficult to correctly grasp both physical (物理的) and social (社會的) welfare (福祉).

Therefore, regional economic growth (地域經濟成長) is not the same for all regions in a country, just as individual incomes (所得) vary from person to person. While differences in individual income (個人所得) arise from differences in occupation (職業) and personal skills (個人功能), regional economic growth (地域經濟成長) disparities stem from unequal distribution of regional (地域的) natural resources (自然資源) and time resources (時間資源), as well as differences in agglomeration economies (集積經濟性) and economies of scale (规模經濟性) due to localized (地方的) concentration (集中) of resources (資源).

Thus, it was a significant task to establish a cognitive system (認識體系) for the purposeful (合目的的) utilization (利用) of spatial laws (空間法則) across all economic policies (經濟政策) and to induce appropriate (適正) industrial dispersion (分散) location policies (立地政策) consciously (目的意識的) based on this cognitive system (認識體系).

The dispersion (分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) to local (地方) areas for the appropriate (適正) dispersion (分散) of industries (產業) would lead to the development (發達) of cities (都市) and the progress (進行) of industrialization (工業化), ultimately centering around hub cities (據點都市) with a population (人口) and employment (雇用) oriented (指向的) location (立地). With the confidence (確信) that this would become an absolute (絶對的) employment (雇用) attractive (誘引的) location (立地) for surrounding (周邊) rural (農村) residents (住民), the dispersion (分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) to local (地方) areas was promoted as part (一環) of the Saemaul Undong (運動).

Furthermore, the dispersion (分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) centered on rural (農村) areas aimed to absorb seasonal (季節的) idle (遊休) rural (農村) labor (勞動力), establish a new regional (地域) industrial (產業) structure (構造) through the investment (投入) of social overhead capital (社會間接资本) around (周邊) the factories (工場), and form small-scale (小規模) related (關聯) service industries (業種) centered around (聯關) raw materials (原料) production (生產) connected (連結) to the factories (工場). This aimed to link (連結) agriculture (農業) and industry (工業), establishing a new system (體制) for increased (增大) production (生產).

Additionally, the dispersion (分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) to rural (農村) regions (地域) contributed significantly to improving (改善) the production (生產) structure (構造) of rural (農村) areas by expanding (擴大) the production (生產) of new specialty crops (特用作物) and developing (開發) new sources (源) of income (所得) through processing (加工) locally (現地) produced (生產) raw materials (原料).

Moreover, the dispersion (分散) of Saemaul factories (工場) to rural (農村) regions (地域) introduced new non-agricultural (非農業) economic (經濟) sectors (部門) into rural (農村) economies (經濟), which had traditionally (傳統的) been organized (組織) and operated (運用) based on agricultural (農業) production (生產).


--- (p. 245) ---

## Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

There was also an attempt to reorganize rural economic organizations (農村經濟組織) through formation (形成), aiming to address the issue of resource (資源) movement and allocation between agricultural (農業) and non-agricultural (非農業) sectors within rural economic organizations (組織). Ultimately, this led to new changes and influences on the existing agricultural (農業) structure (構造面).

### B. Development of Rural (農村) Settlement (聚落) Structure (構造) Improvement (改善) Projects

Over a long period (期間), our rural (農村) settlements (聚落) had been formed (形成) haphazardly without planning (無計劃). To improve (改善) the structure (構造) of these settlements (聚落) was a primary (次的) and important (重要) task (課題) of the rural (農村) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). This involved creating (造成) a foundation (基盤) for the modernization (近代化) of rural (農村) agriculture (營農), including its scientific (科學化), mechanized (機械化), and cooperative (協業化) aspects. Additionally, it aimed to improve (改善) the residential (住居環境) environment (環境) of rural (農村) areas, ultimately realizing (具現) a bright and cheerful (明朗) rural (農村) landscape (相).

From the inception (點火) of the rural (農村) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) in 1970, environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) became a key (力點) initiative (事業) during the early (初期) stages of the rural (農村) Saemaul (새마을) projects (事業). This was intended to foster (鼓吹) a spiritual revolution (精神革命) by demonstrating (實感) the effects (效果) of cooperation (協同), self-help (自助), and diligence (勤勉).

Thus, rural (農村) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) were established (設定) as the primary (次的) common (共通) concern (關心事) of local residents (地域住民), addressing (選定) the most suitable (最適) projects (事業) based on the actual conditions (實情) of each village's surroundings (周邊). These projects (事業) were then implemented (施行).

As the rural (農村) Saemaul (새마을) beautification (事業) projects (事業) progressed (推進), the rural (農村) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) were categorized (區分) and advanced (推進) in stages (段階的) as follows:

1. Village-wide (全體) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) centered on roof (地붕) enhancement (改良).
2. Individual (個個) resident (住民) housing (住宅) improvement (改善) projects (事業) focused on enhancing (改良) living (住居環境) conditions (環境).
3. Village-wide (全體) welfare (福祉) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) centered on improving (改善) the structure (構造) of rural (農村) settlements (聚落).

In this way, rural (農村) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業) served as a crucial (重要) catalyst (點火劑) for the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) from its early (草創期) stages, being implemented (推進) as the first-phase (段階) projects (事業). Before the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), rural (農村) environments (環境) were characterized by narrow, winding paths (入口) overgrown with dense vegetation (草木), dilapidated walls (담장) left untended (手), and poorly arranged (配置) spaces (空間) between living quarters (居室), livestock sheds (畜舍), and outhouses (便所), lacking harmony (調和). At night, these rural (農村) areas were shrouded in darkness (暗黑).

Therefore, through the implementation (推進) of rural (農村) peripheral (周邊) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) projects (事業), the fundamental (基礎的) environment (環境) of the village was enhanced (改善).


--- (p. 246) ---

To improve living conditions and establish a foundation for production and income-generating activities, as well as to create an environment for healthy mental well-being and efficient, comfortable family life, it was essential to implement rural environmental improvement projects. These projects aimed to foster a spirit of cooperation among residents and stimulate their enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong by allowing them to experience the changes in their environment firsthand.

Thus, the improvement of rural housing environments primarily focused on upgrading roofs as the first key project. This initiative involved replacing thatched roofs with tiles, shingles, or corrugated iron to enhance the living environment in rural areas. Additionally, the straw previously used for thatched roofs was repurposed to produce handicrafts, contributing to increased income. The straw was also used as fuel to protect forests and as compost to boost food production and prevent soil acidification. Furthermore, this project aimed to save labor previously spent on annual roof repairs and redirect it towards more productive activities.

As the roof upgrading project neared completion in 1976, following its nationwide expansion starting in 1971, the focus shifted to rural housing improvement and rural settlement structure improvement projects, which began in earnest in 1977.

This shift occurred because, by 1977, the direction of rural environmental improvement had concretized into external improvements through rural housing upgrades. As farmers' incomes improved and their living standards rose, their preferences for housing also increased, making rural housing improvement a necessity. Additionally, the rapid modernization and urbanization of non-agricultural sectors necessitated a shift from merely upgrading roofs to a more comprehensive approach that included rural housing improvement and rural settlement structure improvement projects as part of the modernization efforts.

The rural housing improvement project encompassed not only the construction and upgrading of houses but also the development of village roads, the relocation of settlements, the provision of community facilities, and the improvement of ancillary buildings, all aimed at modernizing rural settlements.


--- (p. 247) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

This was done with the aim of constructing (建設) it. In this way, the Saemaul Undong (Movement) sought to improve the rural (農村) environment (環境) by reorganizing (整備) the disorderly (無質서하게) scattered (亂立) outbuildings such as compost sheds (堆肥舍), barns (畜舍), and toilets (便所) alongside (並行) houses in rural (農村) settlements (聚落).

The rural (農村) housing (住宅) improvement (改良) project (事業) was promoted (推進) with the aim of exploring (摸索) the direction (方向) for improving (改善) and reorganizing (整備) the scattered (散慢) and irrational (非合理) structure (構造) of rural (農村) settlements (聚落) by promoting (推進) it as much as possible (可及的) on a village (마을) unit (單位).

The promotion (推進) of the rural (農村) housing (住宅) improvement (改良) project (事業) considered (考慮) the conditions (與件) of farmhouses (農家) and set (設定) the site (垈地) scale (規模) to 100 pyeong (坪) as a principle (原則). The buildings (建物) were divided (區分) and set (設定) into 15 pyeong (坪型), 18 pyeong (坪型), and 20 pyeong (坪型) types (型) considering (勘案) the needs (需要) and income (所得水準) levels (水準) of farmhouses (農家).

The rural (農村) housing (住宅) improvement (改良) project (事業) was promoted (推進) based (立脚) on two methods (方法) and techniques (要領): improving (改良) individual (單獨) farmhouses (農家) and demonstrating (示範) the construction (建設) of new (新) villages (村). Standard (標準) designs (設計圖) and materials (資材) were standardized (規格化) to create (作成) designs (設計圖) such as "一" shape (字型) and "ㄱ" shape (字型) that suited (適宜) the actual (實情) conditions (實情) of rural (農村) areas (地域), and they were selected (選定) accordingly (相應).

In addition, the rural (農村) housing (住宅) improvement (改良) project (事業) was promoted (推進) as part (一環) of improving (改善) the environment (環境) along (並行) roads (道路邊) by consolidating (合村) or improving (改良) poor-quality (不良) detached (獨立) houses (住宅) scattered (散在) along (邊) roads (道路), preventing (豫防) traffic (交通) accidents (事故) caused (遮斷) by obstructed (遮斷) views (視界), and improving (改善) rural (農村) settlements (聚落) and housing (住居).

In particular, the rural (農村) settlement (聚落) structure (構造) improvement (改善) project (事業) was promoted (推進) by classifying (分類) villages (마을) into three types (類型): A, B, and C. Type A (型) aimed (對象) to relocate (移轉) all farmhouses (全體農家) to suitable (適正) locations (位置) such as hilly (丘陵地) areas (地) to improve (高度化) land (土地) use (利用) and create (具備) a new (新) and modern (近代的) village (村) appearance (面貌) in cases (境遇) where villages (村) and farmland (農土) were cut off (斷絶) by the construction (貫通) of expressways (高速道路) or in areas (地) prone (常習地) to water (水害) disasters (災). Type B (型) aimed (方向) to reorganize (整備) the village (村) structure (構造) in its current (現在) location (位置) in a more productive (生産的) and convenient (便益爲主) way (方) while relocating (移築) or rebuilding (改築) poor-quality (不良) houses (住宅). Type C (型) aimed (程度) to relocate (移築) or rebuild (改築) about 5-6 buildings (棟) in villages (村) that did not require (必要) improvement (改善) of the village (村) structure (構造).

Following the roof (地붕) improvement (改良) project (事業) promoted (推進) in the first half (前半期) of the 1970s, the latter half (後半) of the 1970s saw (推進)


--- (p. 248) ---

Starting from the period (期), the rural housing improvement project (農村住宅改良事業) and the parallel rural settlement structure improvement project (農村聚落構造改善事業) were actively promoted with the goal of enhancing the welfare and living standards of rural residents. These projects aimed to realize an ideal modernized rural society in the 1980s by building upon the experiences, techniques, and cooperative spirit cultivated through the rural Saemaul Undong (運動) up to that point. The projects were initiated with the purpose of advancing the roof improvement project (地붕改良事業), which was one of the core projects of the first phase of the Saemaul Undong (運動) focused on rural environmental improvement, into a more fundamental development of housing and settlement structure improvement projects. These projects were then inherited as the leading projects of the second phase of the Saemaul Undong (運動).

Additionally, the rural housing improvement project and the rural settlement structure improvement project were driven by the consciousness of rationalizing the rural consumption structure, promoting large-scale development, and realizing the construction of a welfare-oriented rural society by developing the infinite potential of rural areas. These projects also aimed to achieve balanced development between urban and rural areas based on the successful implementation of economic development plans and the short-term achievements of the rural Saemaul Undong (運動). Thus, they came to possess the core characteristics of the Saemaul Undong (運動) as key projects.

## 5. Saemaul Undong (運動) and the Path to Rural Prosperity (富强)

The Saemaul Undong (運動), which was experimentally launched in 1970 to address the urban-rural gap that emerged during the industrialization process of the 1960s and to develop the lagging rural areas, has achieved results beyond expectations. This has allowed the Saemaul Undong (運動) to take root in rural communities and significantly contribute to laying the foundation for agricultural, cultural, and spiritual revolutions in the Korean countryside over the past decade. This is a well-known fact.

Here, we have examined the process through which the rural Saemaul Undong (運動) has evolved. The development and progress of the Saemaul Undong (運動) are undoubtedly the fruits of the passion and relentless efforts of rural Saemaul leaders, relevant agency officials, and public servants, day and night.
