Today, we can see significant changes in the appearance of rural areas. Thatched houses have been replaced with cultural houses, village roads have been widened, and community centers and village warehouses have been established.

However, the achievements are not limited to these tangible outcomes. There are also intangible changes that we can observe with our own eyes, such as


--- (p. 249) ---

# Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It also brought about a significant transformation in the spiritual aspect, and now farmers have gained confidence through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), believing that "if we do it, we can do it." Their motivation to live well under their own responsibility has also increased.

Moreover, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in rural areas has discovered and nurtured numerous excellent rural leaders, which is an important achievement not inferior to material growth.

Of course, not all plans made and implemented by the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) were successful.

In the development process of the rural Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), there were instances of overly uniform planning, and there were also plans that were overly ambitious, among other less desirable aspects.

However, in the process of promoting new movements, some friction and side effects were inevitable in carrying out creative projects.

But one issue that must be emphasized is that in promoting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) going forward, it is important to consider the capabilities of farmers and the potential of rural areas and proceed gradually.

In the 1980s, it goes without saying that we must complete the tasks that were left unfinished in the past based on the foundation established over the past 10 years, further deepen them, and carry out new projects towards new directions.

The 1980s will be a period for laying the groundwork for our country to leap from the middle-income stage to the advanced stage, and it is expected that in the agricultural sector, the mechanization of agriculture, including the scientific management of farming, will be actively pursued to modernize agriculture.

In this new era of challenge, the rural Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) cannot be interrupted or weakened, otherwise it will not be able to respond to the new demands of the times.

The future Saemaul projects should raise the dimension and practical goals, expand the development base to a wider area, and focus on improving the cultural welfare and environment of farmers, developing non-agricultural income sources, and avoiding relying solely on the government in promoting the projects.


--- (p. 250) ---

It should evolve into a higher-dimensional Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) that goes beyond the scope of the village and is driven by farmers themselves. The goals of the rural Saemaul Undong to be pursued in the future can be broadly divided into social development (社會開發) and economic development (經濟開發) of the countryside.

In the "Social Development Movement (社會開發運動)," we should summarize the environmental improvement (環境改善) projects that have been pursued so far and, based on this foundation, carry out necessary projects to make the countryside a cultural rural area (文化農村). On the other hand, the "Economic Development Movement (經濟開發運動)" should focus on developing and cultivating suitable crops (適性作目) that match the conditions and characteristics of each region, promoting specialization (特化) by village and region, actively developing off-farm income sources (農外所得源), and drastically improving the distribution system (流通體系) to increase farm income (農家所得) and further solidify the foundation for regional economic (地域經濟) development.

Next, the rural Saemaul Undong should become a movement that expands its development hubs (開發據點) to a broader area.

The rural Saemaul Undong of the 1970s was carried out as a practical movement (實踐運動) at the village unit (마을單位), where people lived together in harmony (同居同樂), helping each other (相扶相助), and sharing a sense of community (共同體意識). It is true that this village-unit (마을單位) Saemaul Undong, relying on traditional cooperative consciousness (協同意識), achieved more than expected results.

However, for future social development (社會開發) and economic development (經濟開發), cooperation (協動) among farmers within the village alone may not be sufficient, and there will be no shortage of facilities (施設物) and projects that only village-unit (마을單位) residents can utilize.

Therefore, it is necessary to gradually expand the development hubs (開發據點) of the Saemaul Undong to a broader area.

The Saemaul projects to be unfolded in the future should be systematically organized (綜合體系化) into village-area development projects (마을圏開發事業) and cooperative-area development projects (協同圏開發事業), while interconnecting the projects of the village area and other regional areas (地域圏) in an organic (有機的) and complementary (補完的) manner to achieve synergistic (相乘的) development effects (開發效果).

Moreover, since the proportion of off-farm income (農外所得) in our country's farming households (農家) is still relatively low, we must actively develop off-farm income sources (農外所得源) to increase farm income (農家所得). We should also continue the attraction (誘致) and cultivation (育成事業) of rural Saemaul factories, which were initiated in the mid-1970s. If such industrial (工業) decentralization (地方分散) is linked to the development of home-based industries (家內工業) or farming side businesses (農家副業) at the village unit (마을單位), the scope of benefits (受惠) will be greatly expanded.


--- (p. 251) ---

## Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

It will be possible.
In any case, the development of external income sources (域外所得源) should be promoted as an important economic development project (經濟開發事業) for the 1980s (年代). Moreover, the economic development (經濟開發) and social development (社會開發) of rural areas (農漁村) cannot be led by the government (政府) forever. Therefore, the rural Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) in the 1980s (年代) will enter a transitional period (轉換期) where it gradually shifts to a system (體制) led by farmers' autonomy (農民自律). However, in the future, the promotion of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) will require not only the cultivation of rural leaders (農村指導者) but also the provision of necessary administrative (行政的) conditions (條件) to ensure that the projects (事業) planned by the leaders (指導者) are smoothly achieved (成就). Moreover, based on the material (物質的) conditions (條件) and experiences (經驗) accumulated over the past 10 years (年間), the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) must continue to develop (發展) and deepen (深化) without interruption (中斷).

### Section 2 (第2節) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) in Cities (都市), Factories (工場), and Schools (學校)

1. Overview (槪觀)

The discussion on what the essence (本質) of national development (國家發展) or modernization (近代化) is, depends on individual understanding (理解). However, most (大部分) scholars (學者) argue that national development (國家發展) should be achieved through balanced development (均衡發展), which involves economic development (經濟發展) as its core (中心), along with political development (政治發展) and socio-cultural (社會文化的) development (發展). They believe that the factors (要因) driving such development (發展) originate from the modernization (近代化) of human factors (人的要因). In other words, they emphasize that the modernization (近代화) process (作業) can only be further promoted (推進) based on the reform (改革) of the national consciousness structure (國民意識構造).

In particular, economic development (經濟發展), which plays a pivotal (中樞的) role (機能) in the process of national development (國家發展), can be measured (把握) in terms of quantitative (物量的) growth (成長). However, to maintain and expand (擴散) this development-oriented (發展指向的) trend (樣相), strong spiritual (精神的) support from the entire nation (國民全體) is necessary. Nevertheless, the results (成果) are not immediately (卽時) visible.

This fact (事實) can be compared (比喩) to the case (事例) of perfectly completing (完璧) the foundation work (基礎工事) and then constructing (構築) a high-rise building (高層建物) on top of it. We do not envy (部러워하지 않는) the Japanese-style (日本方式) modernization (近代化).


--- (p. 252) ---

The reason lies right here, and when foreigners visit Korea, they are often more impressed by the fact that every citizen is filled with a spirit of construction, rather than Korea's economic development. It is necessary to pay attention to the discovery of the Saemaul spirit, where everyone is filled with enthusiasm for construction.

Ten years after the Saemaul Undong was ignited in this land, our national territory and national spirit have been transformed and developed at a dazzling speed. In this way, the achievements of future-oriented projects are now continuously spreading and developing in cities, as well as in companies and academic institutions.

The first urban Saemaul Undong was promoted in four fields: workplaces, regions, households, and schools, each focusing on frugality, thrift, neighborhood watch, and cooperation. As a result, remarkable achievements were made in urban environmental improvement, Saemaul cooperative projects, and comprehensive citizen education.

Subsequently, based on the morality and public benefit of urban citizens, a healthy value system was established, and a philosophy of life based on norms and public virtue was solidified. This led to the improvement of the order in clean and dignified urban spaces. Moreover, through citizen guidance such as pedestrian order, picking up trash, using polite language, and observing etiquette, which are among the easiest tasks to implement in our daily lives, the atmosphere has been further matured.

Furthermore, with the establishment of the Saemaul Citizen Model as a goal, the autonomous participation spirit of professional organizations and self-generated organizations has been greatly heightened. As an example, the operation of neighborhood associations has been practiced in each region, taking the lead in social purification.

Thus, through the Three Major Order Establishment Movements—creating a comfortable and clean city in terms of environment, an orderly city in terms of action, and a dignified city in terms of spirit—the urban Saemaul Undong has been fully on track.

It seems too coincidental to be mere chance that the Factory Saemaul Undong began right after the first oil shock, which dealt the greatest blow to companies during their period of expansion and growth.

The Factory Saemaul Undong, which was launched under such adverse conditions, aimed to rearm the minds of employees, who had become disorganized, with the Saemaul spirit. It set the slogan of resource conservation, energy saving, quality improvement, and productivity enhancement, and almost uniformly focused on effectively and appropriately overcoming the recession or strengthening the management structure.


--- (p. 253) ---

## Chapter 4 Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The government (政府) established the Factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Promotion Headquarters (推進本部) in 1977 and designated the Factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) as a key project (重點事業) for guiding member companies of four economic (經濟) organizations including the Federation of Korean Industries (大韓商工會議所). It focused on planning (企劃), investigation (調査), guidance (指導), publicity (弘報), and educational (敎育事業) activities, thereby faithfully performing its role as a stage of self-help development (自助發展段階).

Notable projects at the time included the "Second Home (家庭化) Movement (運動)" in the workplace (職場), which aimed to treat employees (從業員) like family (家族) and factory (工場) work like tomorrow's work. Through joint birthday (生日) celebrations (祝賀會) and evening (夜間) special classes (特別學級), it greatly contributed to stabilizing labor-management relations (勞使關係) in companies (企業) and further promoted the voluntary development of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) activities (活動) to accelerate productivity (生産性) improvements (向上).

The second (第2) oil shock (石油波動), which emerged as the biggest domestic (國內) issue in 1979, and the Y.H. Trading Company (貿易會社) incident (事件) put the government (政府) in a position where it could not help but emphasize the necessity (必要性) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) once again.

In the early stages of capitalism (資本主義), labor-management relations (勞使關係) were sometimes accepted as having antagonistic (對立的) aspects, but in the mature stage (成熟段階), it has become a common sense (常識) in today's industrial society (產業社會) to lead to a cooperative relationship (協同關係) by improving mutual understanding (相互理解) and dialogue (對話) methods (方法).

In particular, the Factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is fostering a cooperative foundation (協同基盤) through the rise (浮上) of Korean-style (韓國的) corporate ethics (企業倫理觀) in a spiritual (精神的) sense, improving dialogue (對話) and consultation (協議) methods (方法) by establishing and operating labor-management councils (勞使協議會) in an institutional (制度的) sense, and introducing various Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) incentive systems (誘引制度) such as Saemaul Savings Banks (새마을金庫), daily necessities (生必品) purchasing (購販) businesses (事業) to focus on increasing employee (從業員) income (所得).

The School Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is being intensively operated as Saemaul Education (敎育) under the premise (前提) that the overall (全體) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) cannot be sustained (永續化) at a national (汎國民的) level (次元) without educational (敎育活動) activities for the development (啓發) of national spirit (國民精神) and spiritual revolution (精神革命).

Therefore, the Ministry of Education (文敎部) is steadily promoting (推進) Saemaul Education (敎育) to strongly support (支援) and improve the efficiency (効率化) of the overall (全體) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) through educational (敎育活動) activities, and to ensure that the educational (敎育) effects (効果) extend to families (家庭), local residents (地域住民), and the entire nation (全體國民).

Saemaul Education (敎育) has also grown (成長) and been organized (整理) steadily, escaping the chaotic state (混沌狀態) at the time of its inception (出發) in terms of students' (學生) school (學校) education (敎育) and establishing (確立) attitudes (姿勢) for income increase (所得增大) and spiritual (精神) development (發展).


--- (p. 254) ---

Residents are now entering a stage of consolidation where they are strengthening the substance of their education. The inception of Saemaul Education dates back to the 1970s, when various forms of education promotion, cultivation of cooperative and united spirits, construction of local schools, and socialization of education were reflected in scholarship policies and implemented. Since 1973, Saemaul Education has been established as one of the five major policies of the Ministry of Education and has been continuously realized as an important area of educational activities.

The Saemaul Undong began with the rural Saemaul Undong and expanded its base to urban Saemaul Undong, factory Saemaul Undong, and school Saemaul Undong. In other words, it has been proven that the Saemaul Undong can be ignited wherever the wisdom and ingenuity of our people reach, and this has taught us that it is the basic principle of national development.

At the present stage of attempting national development, the tasks that we should particularly focus on are:
1. Building an economy that drives out poverty and allows both rural and urban areas to prosper equally.
2. Eliminating distrust and injustice and rectifying the national discipline.
3. Strengthening the roots of freedom and democratic ideals to peacefully unify our divided nation.
We are confident that the Saemaul Undong we are currently promoting will shorten the time and effort required for these tasks.

## 2. Indicators of Urban Saemaul Undong

### a. Structural Characteristics of Urban Society

From a sociological perspective, until World War II, our regional societies were typically divided into two categories: rural and urban societies. Generally, the distinction between rural and urban societies can be made based on six factors: occupation, environment, scale of the regional society, population density, heterogeneity of the population, and human relationships. Therefore, if a specific regional society's indicators are simple, homogeneous, undifferentiated, and traditional, it is considered a rural society. Conversely, if it is complex, heterogeneous, differentiated, and dynamic, it is referred to as an urban society.

Thus, the characteristics of rural societies are traditionally based on blood ties, regional ties, and school ties to form society.


--- (p. 255) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Due to possessing characteristics such as similarity (類似性), communal (共同) social (社會的) concepts (觀念), communal (共同) customs (慣習), communal (共同) traditions (傳統), and communal (共同) sense of belonging (所屬感情), it is easy to form regional (地域的) integration (統合) or social (社會的) interest (關心) as a centripetal force (求心力).

In contrast, the characteristics of urban society (都市社會) are as follows:

First, secondary (次) and tertiary (次) industries (產業) dominate, residences (住居) and workplaces (職場) are separated, and there is high mobility (流動性) among residents (住民), making natural regional (地域的) integration (統合) weak.

Second, urban (都市) strata (階層) are complex (複雜) and differentiated (分化), and interpersonal relationships (對人關係) are secondary (次) group-based (集團的), leading to strong utilitarianism (功利性), individualism (個人主義的), and temporariness (一時的) among members (構成員), resulting in high anonymity (匿名性) in urban life (市民生活). Consequently, the control function (統制機能) over urban life (市民生活) is weak, and there are many violations of order (秩序) and criminal acts (犯罪行爲).

Third, the composition (構成) of urban (都市) residents (住民) is heterogeneous (異質的) and dynamic (流動的), human relationships (人間關係) are formal (形式的) and superficial (皮相的), and functional (機能的), causing members (構成員) to feel alienation (疏外感). As a result, citizens (市民) do not take an interest (關心) in social issues (社會問題).

Fourth, human relationships (人間關係) are mechanical (機械的), formal (形式的), partial (部分的), and temporary (一時的), leading to stereotypical (stereotype式) distinctions among individuals (個個人) based on their status (地位), occupation (職業), attire (衣裳), and language (言語). This gives rise to urbanites' (都市人) pretentiousness (虛勢), affectation (虛飾), trends (流行), and extravagance (奢侈).

Fifth, urbanization (都市化) implies industrialization (產業化), and industrialization (產業化) leads to population (人口) concentration (集中), resulting in severe income disparities (所得格差) and the existence of unemployed individuals (失業者). Consequently, urban (都市) slumization (slum化) occurs, and conflicts (葛藤) arise between and within strata (階層).

Due to these structural (構造的) peculiarities (特殊性) of urban society (都市社會), regional (地域的) integration (統合) is difficult, and the control function (統制機能) over urban life (市民生活) is weak, making it challenging to form a communal (共同體的) sense of unity (一體感) in regional society (地域社會). However, after World War II (2차(次) 대전(大戰)), with the advancement (高度化) of industries (產業) and rapid developments (開發) in information (情報) and technology (技術), the process of urbanization (都市化) should not be viewed solely as a revolutionary (變革的) law (法則) of rural (農村) areas, i.e., the collapse (崩壞) of traditional (傳統的) communal (共同體的) attributes (屬性). Instead, it should be approached (接近) from the managerial (管理的) perspective (側面) of the entire society (全體社會). In other words, as the entire society (全體社會) is increasingly integrated (統合) through urbanization (都市化), urban social issues (都市社會問題) must be understood (把握) from a comprehensive (全體的) managerial societal (管理社會的) standpoint (立場). To achieve this, the entire regional society (地域社會) must be formed (形成) in a way that fosters psychological (心理的) belonging (歸屬感), unity (一體感), or a sense of permanent residence (定住意識).


--- (p. 256) ---

Therefore, the most important issues arising here are the establishment of new values for an industrial society (産業社會), the balanced development (均衡的發展) of industries (產業) for regionalization (廣域化), the rationality (合理性) of social systems (社會制度), the issue of economic efficiency (經濟効率), the problem of conflicts among social strata (社會階層相互間), and the issues of social justice (社會正義) and welfare (福祉化). To address these, new values (價値觀) and order formation (秩序形成) must be established through civic education (市民敎育), and active civic participation (市民參與) must be institutionalized (制度化) as a prerequisite (先行).

As described above, urban societies (都市社會) and their members differ from rural (農村) ones in various aspects. In other words, while rural (農村) residents' consciousness (意識), concerns (關心), desires (慾求), and living standards (生活水準) are relatively homogeneous (同質的), those in cities (都市) are fluid (流動的), heterogeneous (異質的), complex (複合的), and pluralistic (多元的). Thus, it is almost impossible to form a cohesive force around a specific issue (特定問題) in cities (都市). This is not only the difference in approach between rural (農村) and urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動) but also the specificity (特殊性) of urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動) development (展開).

## II. Characteristics (特性) and Functions (機能) of Urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動)

In South Korea, the emergence of Saemaul Undong (運動) was an ideology (理念) that consciously adopted experiential (經驗的) value premises (價値前提) to create new history (歷史) from various heterogeneous (異質的) and contradictory value judgments (價値判斷) in the historical process (歷史過程) of long trials (試鍊). Therefore, this ideology (理念) has become a public creed (公共信條) deeply engraved (銘刻) in the hearts of all citizens (全國民) and has even become almost a national (國民的) faith (信仰化). Moreover, it has become a powerful fetus (胎兒) of a new national (民族的) subject consciousness (主體意識).

Thus, Saemaul Undong (運動) can be defined as an indigenous, creative (獨創的), and comprehensive (綜合的) model of social development (社會開發模型) that we have developed and advanced (開發發展) ourselves in our country.

Then, the logical (論理的) question (疑問點) that arises is what the essence (本質), ideology (理念), and goals (目標) of Saemaul Undong (運動) are. First, based on the experience (經驗) of the past decade (10年間), the essence (本質) of Saemaul Undong (運動) can be concluded (結論的) as follows: first, spiritual development (精神啓發); second, a practical (實踐的) philosophy of action (行動哲學) for modernization (近代化); third, national unity (國民總和團結) to overcome national crises (國難); and fourth, a great leap forward movement (大躍進運動) of the entire nation (全國民) to shorten history (歷史短縮).

If we acknowledge (認定) the essence (本質) of Saemaul Undong (運動) as such, its ideology (理念) can be defined (規定) as follows. That is, the first ideology (理念) of Saemaul Undong (運動) is the ideology (理念) of modernization (近代化); second, the ideology (理念) of welfare equality (福祉平等); third, the ideology (理念) of security (安保); and fourth, the inheritance (繼承) of the spirit (얼) of the Korean people (韓民族).


--- (p. 257) ---

# Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) can be considered an autonomous (主體的) ideology (理念). Even looking at the progress (展開內容) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) over the past 10 years (年間), its core (核心的) content strongly reveals a will (意志) to achieve (成就) self-reliance (自主), a self-sufficient (自立) economy (經濟), self-reliant (自主) defense (國防), and peaceful (平和的) unification (統一).

Therefore, reflecting on the past 10 years (年間) when the entire nation (國民) made strenuous efforts (努力) for the Saemaul Undong (Movement), we can summarize its characteristics (特性) as follows. First, the Saemaul Undong (Movement) has a characteristic (特性) of being a community (共同) of shared destiny (運命體的). Second, it is autonomous (主體的) and historical (歷史的). Third, it encompasses political (政治), economic (經濟), social (社會), educational (敎育), and cultural (文化的) characteristics (特性). Fourth, it possesses strong composite (複合的), comprehensive (綜合的), and national (擧國的) characteristics (特性).

Given the above (以上), the significance (意義) and function (機能) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in the cities (都市) during the 1980s (年代) are as important as they were in the past (過去). This is because, in the 1980s (年代), the proportion (比重) of the urban (都市) population (人口) will exceed 80% of the total (全) population (人口), and the contribution (寄與率) of the secondary (次) and tertiary (次) industries (産業) to the G.N.P. will also exceed 80%. Moreover, the formation (形成) of the centripetal force (求心力) and the guiding (指導的) function (機能) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) must be undertaken by urbanites (都市人). Thus, it is not an exaggeration (過言) to say that the success (成敗) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in the 1980s (年代) will depend on the urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (Movement).

In reality, the core (核心) function (機能) of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in rural (農村) areas is largely (多分히) to enhance (增大) individual (個個) members' economic (經濟) and cultural (文化的) status (地位) through increased (增大) income (所得). In contrast, the urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (Movement) aims to establish (確立) a new social (社會) ethic (倫理觀), corporate (企業) ethics (倫理), and national (國家) consciousness (觀) to achieve (具現) social (社會的) integration (統合) and a welfare (福祉) society (社會). Based on the past (間) 10 years (年間) of experience (經驗), the core (核心) of the rural (農村) Saemaul Undong (Movement) involves residents (住民) jointly (共同) improving (改善) the environment (環境), creating (造成) a production (生産) base (基盤), increasing (增大) shared (共同) facilities (施設), expanding (擴張) joint (共同) purchasing (購買) and work (作業), and enhancing (增大) income (所得) through the scientific (科學化) and mechanized (機械化) advancement (向上) of farming (營農). Additionally, through joint (共同) efforts (努力), the structure (構造) of the village (聚落) is improved (改善) to establish (確立) a modern (近代的) image (像) of rural (農村) life (上). This is also the case for the factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (Movement). The focus (力點) of the factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (Movement) is on spiritual (精神) development (啓發) to establish (確立) a new corporate (企業) image (人像), employee (從業員) image (像), and corporate (企業) consciousness (觀). Simultaneously, it aims to improve (改善) human (人間) relationships (關係) and foster (形成) a sense of unity (一體感) between management (使) and labor (勞) through cooperation (協同). This establishes (定立) a Korean-style (韓國的) system (體制) of labor-management (勞使) cooperation (協調) based on the Saemaul ideology (理念). Subsequently, through assigned (分任) activities (活動), it aims to reduce (節減) costs (原價) to enhance (增大) productivity (生産性). Furthermore, it seeks to increase (增大) welfare (厚生福祉) for employees (從業員), provide (實施) education (敎育) for working (勤勞) youth (青少年), and fulfill (遂行) the social (社會的) responsibilities (責任) of the corporation (企業) through external (對外) development (開發) support (支援) and volunteer (奉仕) activities (活動).


--- (p. 258) ---

Thus, the core of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in rural areas and factories lies in increasing income (所得增大), and its results are directly attributed to individual members. In contrast, the urban Saemaul Undong focuses on justice and the construction of a welfare society, or in other words, the establishment of a new national ideology. Its results are attributed to the entire society, not directly to individual members. Therefore, the former can be considered the primary function of the Saemaul Undong, while the latter can be seen as its secondary function.

As is widely known, the results of the rural Saemaul Undong are highly visible and measurable, and its achievements are directly attributed to individual members. This is why the rural Saemaul Undong has strong centripetal and driving forces, and active participation. However, the urban Saemaul Undong, which is centered around occupational groups, schools, culture, politics, religion, and other voluntary groups, has a more secondary function. Its results are not visible or measurable, and its achievements are not directly attributed to individuals. Due to these characteristics and functions, the content and methods of the urban Saemaul Undong differ from those of the rural and factory Saemaul Undong.

### Da. Content of Urban Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

In the case of South Korea, the types of Saemaul Undong can be theoretically divided into two main criteria: scale and structural characteristics. The former can be further divided into local and national Saemaul Undong. For instance, local Saemaul Undong refers to the Saemaul Undong in rural and urban areas at the level of villages and neighborhoods, or individual factories, occupational groups, and schools, and other basic units and institutions. On the other hand, national Saemaul Undong refers to cooperative and wide-ranging Saemaul Undong across multiple regions. For example, in rural areas, it may refer to cooperative and wide-ranging projects such as the expansion of roads, dikes, and irrigation facilities across multiple regions, or nationwide campaigns for nature conservation, spirit, action, and the establishment of environmental order. The latter, based on structural characteristics, can be divided into three main types: rural, urban, and military Saemaul Undong. And the rural Saemaul Undong can be further divided into rural, mountain village, and fishing village Saemaul Undong.


--- (p. 259) ---

## Chapter 4 Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong can be subdivided, and the urban Saemaul Undong can be further divided into school, factory, professional organizations, other voluntary groups, and residential areas and apartment complexes in urban areas. However, based on the past 10 years of experience and considering their structural characteristics and functions, it seems that the most appropriate way to categorize the types of Saemaul Undong in our country is into five types: rural, factory, school, professional organizations, and military Saemaul Undong. Therefore, in this context, the concept of urban Saemaul Undong refers primarily to the Saemaul Undong in urban areas and apartment complexes, as well as professional organizations such as media, broadcasting, finance, publishing, culture, transportation, commercial, construction, tourism, and various service industries, and other types of associations and self-generated groups. Thus, the annual directions, key projects, and implementation methods of the Saemaul Undong in these regions and groups can be broadly described as follows.

The momentum and urgency of modernization in rural areas, along with the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation of the Saemaul Undong, had an impact on individualistic, selfish, and utilitarian urban dwellers, leading some urban society's wealthy individuals, businesspeople, economists, and leaders to spontaneously initiate Saemaul Undong in their homes, factories, workplaces, schools, and urban areas. In 1973, the government designated street, sewer, and housing environment improvement as key projects for urban Saemaul Undong, promoting community clean-up campaigns such as cleaning, greening of vacant lots, and installation of trash cans. Additionally, sisterhood connection projects and savings campaigns were launched to foster a new civic spirit.

Starting in 1974, prominent figures from various sectors, including businesspeople, economists, religious leaders, journalists, and public officials, formed the Saemaul Undong Promotion Council and held the Saemaul Undong Promotion Conference after being educated at the Saemaul Training Institute, where they shared their empathy and awakening. They pledged to ignite the Saemaul Undong in their homes, workplaces, factories, schools, and communities. Therefore, the government, based on the experimental experience of 1973, set the basic goals of urban Saemaul Undong in 1974 for professional organizations, schools, communities, and families as the creation of an atmosphere for autonomous Saemaul Undong, the establishment of a civic image based on the spirit of Saemaul Undong, the revitalization of a lively and pleasant urban social atmosphere, and the enhancement of national unity and solidarity.


--- (p. 260) ---

# Localizing the Saemaul Undong

1975 was designated as the year of the urban Saemaul Undong's leap forward, with its basic direction set as the practical application of the Saemaul spirit (自助, 協同, 勸勉) in daily life, including frugal living through thrift, promoting national unity, and encouraging regular cleaning activities among all citizens. Key projects included the "Ten Major Thrift Campaigns" (청소, 능률향상, 부업 갖기, 심신수련, 사치 제거, 식생활 개선, 생활간소화, 저축운동, 물자절약 및 구두쇠운동) and the Neighborhood Watch (隣保) movement, as well as urban environmental improvement projects.

In 1976, the urban Saemaul Undong entered its full-scale phase, with basic goals focused on ethics (道義) and order (秩序). The first priority was to establish a sense of order based on ethics in the spiritual realm, the second was to foster a lifestyle that prioritizes public interest and order in behavior, and the third was to create safe, efficient, and comfortable urban spaces in the environmental realm.

However, achieving these goals was not something that could be easily accomplished in a short period. Therefore, the movement started with simple tasks that could be easily implemented, such as the "Orderly Pedestrian Movement," "No Littering or Spitting Campaign," and "Polite Language and Etiquette Campaign." The focus was on promoting these three major order campaigns (精神, 行動, 環境) to encourage widespread citizen participation.

1977 was designated as the year of deepening the urban Saemaul Undong, with a focus on promoting the "New Heart" campaign, establishing a healthy social order based on justice and ethics, making cleaning a daily habit, and fostering a culture of widespread citizen participation.

In 1978, the year was designated for the deepening and expansion of the urban Saemaul Undong. The basic policy involved autonomously and organically implementing the "Three Major Orders," "Nine Action Guidelines," and "Twenty-Seven Practical Goals." Large-scale Saemaul education and publicity, as well as enlightened enforcement, were to be carried out. Key projects included promoting order, enforcing order, expanding order-guiding facilities, and linking the ideology of the Saemaul Undong with the unique goals of individual regional and occupational groups to autonomously and organically deepen and expand the urban Saemaul Undong.

1978 was designated as the year of deepening and developing the urban Saemaul Undong, with the basic guideline being the practical application of thrift and savings in daily life to eliminate wasteful and decadent trends.


--- (p. 261) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

By strengthening Saemaul education (新村敎育) by function (機能), inducing the proactive participation of social leaders (社會指導層), actively utilizing the village council (反上會) as a forum for resident (住民) participation (參與) and dialogue (對話), reinforcing and fostering the Saemaul credit union (新村金庫) to expand the base (據點) of economic cooperation (經濟協同), and continuing the 3 major (大) order (秩序) movements (運動) of spirit (精神), action (行動), and environment (環境), social order (社會秩序) was established. Additionally, by creating a city (都市) environment (環境), a dignified (品位) and comfortable (快適) city (都市) was formed, and the functions (機能) of the autonomous (自生的) city (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) council (協議會) were strengthened.

Considering the series of motives (動機), goals (目標), functions (機能), characteristics (特性), and development (展開) contents (內容) of the city (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動) as mentioned above (以上), the main (主要) indicators (指標) of the city (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動) can be said to be spiritual (精神) development (啓發), environmental (環境) improvement (整備), social (社會) order (秩序) and purification (淨化), neighborhood watch (隣保運動) and welfare (厚生福祉) improvement (向上). This is because the city (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) first develops (啓發) the consciousness (意識) of all citizens (市民) through self-reflection (自省) and self-awareness (自覺) via Saemaul education (新村敎育), and at the same time, it establishes (定立) new images (像) of citizens (市民), office workers (職場人), and leaders (指導者) by improving (整備) and beautifying (美化) the urban (都市) space (空間) to create (造成) a safe (安全), comfortable (快適), and efficient (能率的) living (生活) environment (環境), known as environmental (環境) improvement (整備). Then, through the life (生活) application (化) of the Saemaul spirit (新村精神) such as frugal (勤儉) consumption (消費), saving (節約), and savings (貯蓄), it revitalizes (振作) the healthy (健全) urban (都市) social (社會) atmosphere (氣風). Furthermore, it fosters (暢達) civic (市民) ethics (倫理) where all citizens (市民) prioritize (前) public interest (公益) and order (秩序), abide by (遵守) laws (法) and public (公衆) morals (道徳), and eliminate (除去) irrationality (不條理) and non-rationality (非合理性) to establish (確立) a social (社會) discipline (紀綱) that matches (合) justice (正義) and ethics (倫理). Through the neighborhood watch (隣保運動), it forms (形成) a sense of belonging (歸屬感), oneness (一體感), and settlement (定住意識) for the entire (全體) regional (地域) society (社會), thereby aiming to build (建設) an advanced (先進) democratic (民主) welfare (福祉) society (社會).

**La. Process of Promoting the City (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動)**

The first stage (段階) of the process (推進過程) of promoting the city (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) can be considered the foundation (基礎) stage (段階), spanning from 1972 to 1974. During this period (期間), individual (個個) professional (職能) organizations (團體) and regional (地域) units (單位) independently (獨自的), sporadically (散發的), and non-systematically (非體系的) carried out partial (部分的) initiatives (展開) such as urban (都市) environmental (環境) improvement (改善) and improvement (整備) projects (事業) centered around savings (貯蓄運動) and neighborhood assistance (運動). For example (例), each (各) workplace (職場) organization (團體) and regional (地域) unit (單位) designated (定) the 1st of every month (每月) as Saemaul Day (新村의 날), spending 1 hour (時間) cleaning (清掃) the surroundings (周圍) while actively (積極) promoting (展開) projects (事業) such as street (街路) and alley (裏巷) cleaning (清掃), urban (都市) river (河川) improvement (整備), and urban (都市) greening (綠化). Furthermore, they carried out (展開) basic (基礎) improvement (整備) projects (事業) such as energy (能源) and material (物資) conservation (節約), simplification (簡素化) of life (生活), and social (社會) life (生活) improvement (改善), serving as the ignition (點火) and experimental (實驗) stages (段階) that birthed (胚胎) the momentum (氣運) of the city (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動).


--- (p. 262) ---

## Second Stage (段階): Self-Help Stage (1975~1977)

The second stage, known as the self-help stage, spanned from 1975 to 1977. During this period, the Saemaul Undong emphasized the promotion of the Saemaul spirit through Saemaul education. It established comprehensive systems through various Saemaul Undong comprehensive conferences and set up dedicated organizations such as the Saemaul Council and the Saemaul promotion agencies. Leveraging the organizational power of these bodies, the movement focused on improving personal lives, workplace standardization, and orderliness. It also formulated and implemented plans for various Saemaul projects. Thus, this period can be seen as a stage for the creation and establishment of urban Saemaul Undong. The key projects during this stage included the establishment of new values through spiritual development, the expansion of urban environmental beautification and improvement, the spread of urban Saemaul Undong fervor through a sense of unity among members, the promotion of frugal living and neighborhood watch activities, and the establishment of a civic ideal based on norms and public morality to create a clean, dignified, and orderly urban society.

## Third Stage (段階): Self-Reliance Stage of Urban Saemaul Undong (1978~1980)

The third stage was the self-reliance stage of urban Saemaul Undong, which lasted from 1978 to 1980. This period focused on the autonomous growth of urban Saemaul Undong. The key projects during this stage aimed to establish a civic ideal based on the Saemaul ideology, with the fundamental goal of promoting voluntary civic participation. The movement encouraged autonomous participation through self-generated organizations in regional apartment complexes, professional groups, and voluntary groups. In particular, neighborhood associations in regional units and apartment complexes carried out joint development projects. Professional groups practiced movements for street order, commercial order, and public morality, taking the lead in social purification. In terms of the environment, the movement actively promoted street improvement and natural conservation to create comfortable and clean cities. In terms of action, it aimed to create orderly and lively cities, and in terms of spirit, it sought to cultivate advanced cities with dignity in a high-industrial society. Through the three major movements of spirit, action, and environmental order, urban Saemaul Undong entered a stage of substantial deepening and expansion.

## Fourth and Fifth Stages (段階): Cooperation and Welfare Stages (1981 and Beyond)

The fourth and fifth development stages of urban Saemaul Undong are the cooperation and welfare stages, beginning in 1981. The core fundamental goals for these stages should focus on justice, ethics, and purification of society for the creation of a new era and history, aiming for a democratic welfare society.


--- (p. 263) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

As briefly reviewed above, when we look at the process of promoting the urban Saemaul Undong (Movement), we can conclude as follows. That is, although the history and experience of the urban Saemaul Undong (Movement) are short, many regional units, functional organizations, and voluntary groups have already progressed beyond the basic and self-help stages to the self-reliance stage, and in some units, they have even reached the self-managed level, similar to the rural and factory Saemaul Undong (Movement).

### 3. Indicators of the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement)

#### a. Basic Concept of the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The gross national product of Korea has grown to the level of 700 billion dollars and continues to expand through the development of modern industries, which are based on advancing science and technology. Accordingly, the functions of the government are also expanding. The government's diplomatic activities, education, technical administration, and other functions are being operated in close connection with economic policies, and recently, even national defense policies are being operated in close cooperation with economic policies.

Government-level economic policies have been re-recognized as the management of large-scale national projects, and such management, from the planning stage to the process of organization, coordination, and control, aims to achieve the efficiency of economic policies through the rationalization of management capabilities.

The factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) is an important task for the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to systematically plan, coordinate, and control areas related to strengthening the competitiveness of individual economies that have a significant impact on the national economy, stabilizing labor-management relations, improving productivity, and distributing results.

The Ministry of Commerce and Industry began working on the basic concept after holding the first factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) meeting presided over by the Minister in June 1973. Here, we will briefly introduce the outline of the basic concept, which was the most appropriate guiding method at that time, based on the content announced by the government at that time.

##### (1) Basic Ideology

The Saemaul Undong (Movement) is a movement to live well based on the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation.


--- (p. 264) ---

# The Action Philosophy of Modernizing the Fatherland and a Nationwide Movement for National Unification

(2) Justification
(가) Our Unique Traditions

[Diagram: Relationship Between Our Unique Traditions and the Revival Movement]

Our unique traditions are divided into village compacts (향약), mutual aid groups (두레), and cooperative associations (계). This diagram shows how these traditions manifest in the revival movement through moral guidance and punishment (권선징악), mutual aid (상호부조), joint cooperation (공동 협업), and rural development (향촌 발전).

(나) Participation of All Enterprises—Leadership Role in Agricultural-Industrial Advancement (농공병진) and National Strength Organization

### Factory Saemaul Movement (工場새마을運動)

[Diagram: Flowchart depicting the development process of the Factory Saemaul Movement (工場새마을運動)]

* **Upper Elements:**
  * Saemaul Spirit (勤勉) (Diligence • Self-help • Cooperation)
  * Basic Policies (環境) (Environmental Improvement (改善) Income Increase (增大))
* **Intermediate Activities:**
  * Implementation of productive activities (生産活動)
* **Direct Results:**
  * Improved productivity (生産性) and enhanced welfare (福祉) of employees (從業員)
* **Final Goals:**
  * Creativity (創意化) for all businesspeople (企業人)
  * Efficiency (能率化) for all employees (從業員)
  * Innovation (革新化) for all factories (工場)

In the basic conceptualization process, one key point to summarize is that the goal is to establish a Korean (韓國的) corporate (企業) ethics (倫理觀) based on the logic of efficiency (能率), and to contribute significantly to national power (國力) organization (組織化) through the process of increasing productivity (生産性), enhancing employee (從業員) income (所得), regional (地域) Saemaul Movement (運動), and social (社會的) integration (統合).

### Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) and the Establishment of Corporate Ethics (倫理觀)

The necessity of the Factory Saemaul Movement (工場새마을運動) has been emphasized since the government (政府) announced its basic conceptualization (基本構想), focusing on the establishment (確立) of the ideology (理念) of a management (經營) community (共同體).

The historical (歷史的) background (背景) of the management (經營) community (共同體) ideology (理念) can be traced to the unique (固有) customs (美風) of our society (社會), such as the Du-re (두레), Hyang-yak (鄕約), and Gyey (契), which emphasize the promotion of virtue and punishment of vice (勸善懲惡), mutual (相互) cooperation (協助), joint (共同) cooperation (協業), and the development (發展) of rural villages (鄕村). These have been highlighted as exemplary (將顯) movements (運動) for guiding the practical (實踐) direction (方向) of the Factory Saemaul Movement (工場새마을運動).


--- (p. 266) ---

This is said to be the essence of Korean corporate ethics. Therefore, the enterprise owner is expected to embody the spirit of a family head and implement it, while employees, as members of a family, are expected to find and practice what they should do for the enterprise owner and for the development of the enterprise. This process is seen as the establishment of Korean corporate ethics (Table 3).

Originally, the concept of Betriebsgemeinschaft (operating community) starts from a sociological approach. This is because modern management studies have tried to grasp the object of management as a human group, leading to the development of enterprise institutional theory. Today, Betriebsgemeinschaft is studied from the perspective of the organizational cooperative body of management. This approach indicates a shift from a static to a dynamic method, emphasizing the spiritual attitude of humans.

## Chapter 4 (第4章) Development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

German (獨逸) management scholar (經營學) H. Nicklisch is known for viewing management (經營) communities (共同體) as organic (有機的) entities (活動體) of human (人間) activity. An organism (有機體) can be seen as a relationship (關係) of totality (全體性), and an organization (組織), as a human (人間) organic (有機的) entity (活動體), signifies a management community (經營共同體) that exists as a unified (統一) whole (合一體). Therefore, a community (共同體) possesses a community will (共同體意志) and engages in community actions (共同體行爲) to form a unified whole (合一體).

In this context, the community will (共同體意志) refers to the establishment (確立) of ethical (倫理的) corporate (企業) ethics (倫理觀) in the case of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動), while community actions (共同體行爲) signify that both labor (勞) and management (使) faithfully (忠實) perform (履行) their respective roles (役割). The unified whole (合一體) refers to individual (單位別) companies (企業) and factories (工場).

Most (大部分) of South Korea's (我國) companies (企業), as management communities (經營共同體), have not strayed far from the traditional (傳統的) form (形態) of family businesses (家族企業). Consequently, the community (共同體) consciousness (意識) among family members (家族成員) is quite strong. When management goals (經營目標) are deemed excellent (優秀) and valuable (價値的), it becomes relatively easy (容易) to carry out (遂行) tasks, highlighting a characteristic (特徵) of the corporate (企業) climate (風土). The consciousness (意識) of unification (統合) through familial (家族的) integration (統合) sometimes exerts a latent (潛在的) influence (影響力) on corporate (企業) employees (從事員).

For instance (例), employees (從業員) tend (傾向) to view (思考) the company owner (企業主) as a parental figure (父母). However, the question (問題) arises as to whether the company owner (企業主), as a parental figure (父母), genuinely shows (表示) concern (關心) and sincerity (誠意) towards employees (從業員) who share (共有) a similar (同) stance (立場). It is regrettable (遺憾) that employees' (從業員) tendency (傾向) to follow (追從) may be somewhat blind (盲目的) and habitual (慣習的), lacking (缺如) critical (批判的) faculties (能力).

In the future (今後), setting (設定) the direction (方向) for establishing (定立) a Korean (韓國的) corporate (企業) ethics (倫理觀) through the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) should consider (考察) the differences (差異) between foreign (外國) and South Korean (我國) management (經營) styles (方式) as one important (重要) method (方法).

Western nations (歐美諸國) had initiated (推進) modernization (近代化) and industrialization (工業化) much earlier (以前) than South Korea (我國), accumulating (蓄積) considerable (相當) wealth (富). This can largely (多分) be attributed (基礎) to the development (發展) of science and technology (科學技術) and the spirit (精神) of rationalism (合理主義) underlying (基礎) corporate (企業) activities (活動), leading (結果) to high (高度) growth (成長). Thus, it is not an exaggeration (過言) to say that high (高) wages (賃金) and high (高) efficiency (能率) management (管理) styles (方式) have been established (實現) based (基礎) on the traditional (傳統的) foundation (基盤) of individual (個人的) efficiency (能率) principles (主義). The "mechanism" of scientism (科學主義) and pragmatism (實用主義), rooted (基礎) in the historical (歷史的) and traditional (傳統的) foundation (基盤) of Western nations (歐美諸國), is being promoted (推進).


--- (p. 268) ---

Law (法) may foster positive feelings (好感) regarding economic development (經濟發展), but it also brings about a crisis (危機) of new civilization (文明) due to the deepening (深化) of human alienation (人間的疎外現象).

Japan (日本), too, is introducing and operating (導入運營) traditional (傳統的) factors (要因) of succession and development (繼承發展) in its management (經營管理) methods (方式). Since the Edo period (幕府時代), it has developed unique (獨特) human relationship (人間關係) techniques (技法) based on the hierarchical (位階) order (秩序) that has been passed down (傳來) between superiors (上) and subordinates (下), advancing (發展) towards collective (集團的) efficiency (能率主義). Economists (經濟學者) argue that the ideology (理念) of collectivism (集團主義) has greatly contributed to creating new miracles (奇蹟) on the postwar (戰後) ruins (廢墟).

We cannot ignore the common (共通) task (課題) of efficiency (能率主義) seen in advanced industrial nations (先進工業國家). Given our position of rapidly maturing industrialization (工業化) in a short period (短期間), it is no exaggeration to say that management (經營管理) methods (方式) aimed at maximizing efficiency (能率極大化) are our immediate tasks (當面課題). However, where should we derive (緣由) the basic (基本的) ideology (思想) for adopting such efficiency (能率主義) methods (方式)? This should be organized (整理) in the process (過程) of re-presenting (再顯) the purification (醇化) of our unique (固有) good customs (美風良俗), as emphasized in its inevitability (當爲性). Therefore, for convenience (便宜), we will denote (表記) this as community-based (經營共同體的) efficiency (能率主義).

Then, what are the methods (方式) to implement (具現) community-based (經營共同體的) efficiency (能率主義)? This can be approached (接近) in various ways depending on the views (見解) of scholars (識者).

The ultimate goal (目的) of community-based (經營共同體的) efficiency (能率主義) through the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) can be summarized as the development (發展) of my workplace (職場) → the development (發展) of the nation (國家). While the larger goal (目標) is seen as the development (發展) of the nation (國家), these three goals (目標) should be pursued (追求) in the same dimension (次元), and the practical (實踐) methods (方式) should start from each's own position (位相), with labor (勞) and management (使) being particularly important. Here, I would like to present the role (役割) from the perspective (入場) of employees (從業員).

First, it is very important to evaluate (評價) one's position (位置) and role (役割) in the process (過程) of self-assessment (自我點檢).

Second, in the process (過程) of self-renewal (自我革新), one should strive (盡) to the best (最善) to fully (充實) perform (充實) the role (役割) given to oneself (自己) through self-capacity development (自己能力啓發).

Third, in the process (過程) of self-fulfillment (自我充實), it is emphasized to complete (完遂) the role (役割) of developing (開發) one's job content (職場內容) more meaningfully (알차게) and expanding (寬) one's range of action (行動半徑) infinitely (無限大).

Fourth, in the process (過程) of self-realization (自我實現), one should fulfill (完遂) the responsibility (責任) given to oneself (自己) to achieve (實現) self-realization (自我實現).


--- (p. 269) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

This is a process that satisfies the desires of the people.

Fifth, in the stage of self-development (自我發展段階), one must recognize their role (役割) and contribute to the development of the company (企業). In the process of the organization (組織) developing, one must find a way to develop oneself.

Such practice starts from oneself, leading to the development of the individual, the company, and the nation. This is the direction of the efficiency-oriented management community (經營共同體的能率主義) emphasized in the factory Saemaul Undong (工場新村運動), and I believe it is a shortcut to establishing a Korean corporate ethics (企業倫理觀).

### D. Characteristics of Factory Saemaul Undong (工場新村運動)

#### (1) Spiritual Development Movement (精神啓發運動)

The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is based on the fundamental ideology (基本理念) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同) with the new village spirit (粘神). Therefore, the factory Saemaul Undong (工場新村運動), like the rural (農村) and urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (新村運動), has the characteristic of being a spiritual development movement (精神啓發運動) that fosters a diligent (勤勉) workplace atmosphere (職場風土) with honest (誠實) and upright (正直) work attitudes (勤務姿勢).

The spiritual development movement (精神啓發運動) being promoted in companies (企業) and factories (工場) aims first to establish a diligent (勤勉) workplace atmosphere (職場風土) with honest (誠實) and upright (正直) work attitudes (勤務姿勢). Second, it involves the establishment and operation of a suggestion system (提案制度) through creativity (創意) and effort (努力), continuous promotion of organizational development (組織開發) and material development (素材開發) as self-help activities (自助活動). Third, it aims to promote harmony (調和) and unity (團結), strengthen teamwork (team work) within business departments (現業部署內), and improve productivity (生産性) through cooperative living (協同生活).

#### (2) Economic Development Movement (經濟開發運動)

The Korean economy (經濟) has undergone rapid growth (高度成長) in the 1960s (年代) and established the foundation for a self-sufficient economy (自立經濟基盤) by the late 1970s (年代). By 1986 (年), the end of the Fifth Five-Year Economic Development Plan (第5次經濟開發5個年計劃), the country achieved $500 billion in exports (輸出) and a per capita income (人當所得) of $4,100, thus knocking on the door of a welfare society (福祉社會).

In line with the pace of economic (經濟) development (發展), the growth process (成長過程) of companies (企業) has progressed from the startup (創業) and dawn stage (黎明段階) of the 1960s (年代) to the expansion (擴張) and preparation stage (整備段階) in the 1970s (年代). Looking ahead to the 1980s (年代), companies (企業) are expected to enter a mature stage (成熟段階), focusing on human resource development (人力開發), technological innovation (技術革新), and market expansion strategies (市場擴大戰略).


--- (p. 270) ---

Although the Factory Saemaul Undong has been in existence for a relatively short period of time, it has proven its worth through energy conservation, resource saving, and quality improvement movements, overcoming economic downturns and leading to profitable management. The Factory Saemaul Undong will continue to play a significant role in promoting corporate development and, ultimately, national economic growth through cost reduction and improved productivity.

### (3) Social Integration Movement

In the process of modernization, the recurring tasks are social integration and reunification. Therefore, modernized leadership that can correctly understand the nature of social change and integrate the various elements accompanying such change becomes a decisive issue.

The Factory Saemaul Undong has emerged as a significant modernized leadership influencing the modernization process. The social integration movement, which connects the Saemaul Undong hubs among workers at various demonstration factories and between demonstration factories, holds important implications.

In other words, company employees influence each other vertically and horizontally through the Human Tree Movement, while demonstration factories extend their influence to surrounding and affiliated factories, and ultimately to the rural Saemaul Undong, urban Saemaul Undong, and school Saemaul Undong. Through this cyclical process of reunification, the Factory Saemaul Undong creates opportunities to organize national power.

### (4) Practical Life Movement

The Factory Saemaul Undong is not a project driven by theory or any particular model, but rather a movement characterized by practical action based on the Saemaul spirit.

This movement can be seen as a humanism that pursues truth and satisfies romance within the moral code of practical action aimed at setting an example for working people. It is viewed as a great leap forward movement that fundamentally changes the expression of our people, who have long lost their individuality amidst ignorance and poverty.


--- (p. 271) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Starting with the spirit of smiling while conversing, singing while producing, picking up even a single piece of discarded paper, and cherishing even a single tree by the roadside, it expanded the opportunities for active management participation and took on the role of gathering collective wisdom for the development of enterprises.

### B. The Promotion Process of the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement)

#### (1) Foundation Stage (1974~1976)

The year 1970 was a significant turning point for the development of our nation. The Saemaul Undong (Movement), which began to echo nationwide, became a decisive turning point that awakened the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation in our rural areas, which had been stagnant in poverty and ignorance for a long time.

The Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) was also ignited by the rural Saemaul Undong (Movement). In 1974, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry organized the Central Promotion Committee for the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement), composed of executives from four economic organizations and academics. They expanded the selection of model companies and provided guidelines and operational directives for the establishment of Saemaul Undong (Movement) promotion organizations and the selection of projects by factory.

The Central Promotion Committee set the basic direction of the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) to align with the basic policies of environmental improvement and income increase based on the Saemaul spirit. It aimed to enhance productivity and welfare through the creativity of all businesspeople, the efficiency of all employees, and the innovation of all enterprises, ultimately characterized by the development of substantial production activities.

Looking back, the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) began at the end of 1973, coinciding with the first oil shock, when the economy was rapidly declining. Although the government was concerned, the unyielding will and efforts of all businesspeople and employees led to material savings, energy conservation, and quality improvement, overcoming the recession and creating a turning point to strengthen management capabilities.

Most companies set the company's philosophy or basic management policies as a spiritual benchmark for all employees. Of course, many companies had already promoted similar ideologies to the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in their company philosophy or basic management policies and had cultivated a Saemaul spirit atmosphere. However, most companies introduced the Factory Saemaul Undong (Movement) as a means to efficiently carry out their business.


--- (p. 272) ---
