Basic goals and action guidelines are adopted and implemented as shown in Table 4. Such business operation methods aim to make employees aware of the clear goals of the Saemaul Movement in advance and to find a focal point to strongly promote the movement by autonomously selecting the company. Then, how have the practical goals of promoting the Factory Saemaul Movement been set? In a word, they are not given any special meaning. They are simply a method of concentrating the efforts for management rationalization that the company has been implementing as usual on the Saemaul spirit atmosphere. The management activities of the company essentially aim to maximize profits through profitability and profitability. Therefore, management rationalization will be an essential element in management that the company is most concerned about and promotes as a task.


--- (p. 273) ---

# Chapter 4 Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

However, if such rationalization (合理化) efforts are pursued without limit and misguided (誤導), there is a risk of various social (社會的) ills (病弊) and the loss of public (公共) nature (性) of enterprises (企業). Therefore, it is considered most desirable for management (經營) attitudes (態度) to directly link the results (結果) of management (經營) rationalization (合理化) to increased (增大) income (所得) for employees (從業員).

Thus, profit (利潤) maximization (極大化) and income (所得) increase (增大) have been set together as the practical (實踐) goals (目標) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動). Therefore, management (經營) activities (活動) aimed at internal (內在) potential (潛在力) have been promoted in conjunction with value-added productivity (附加價値生產性) through management (經營) rationalization (合理化) activities (活動) that companies have been conducting traditionally. As a result (結果), employees' (從業員) income (所得) is increasing (增大) through the rational (合理) distribution (配分) of the outcomes (結果). It is only when these two objectives (目的) are operated in parallel (並行) that the interest (關心) and response (呼應) of all employees (全體從業員) can be expected.

Then, how have the practical (實踐) goals (目標) set in the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) been achieved through what management (管理) methods (方式)? This can be sufficiently explained by the following Table 5.

The characteristics (特徵) of this management (管理) method (方式) are that the Management by Objectives (目標管理制度) system (制度) is slightly modified (變形) and operated (運營) to suit the characteristics (特性) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動). That is, from the process (過程) of selecting (選定) a business (事業), improvements (改善) in human (人間) relationships (關係) and labor-management (勞使) cooperation (協調) are pursued as the foundation (基礎), and through thorough (充實) exchange (交換) of opinions (意見) among employees (從業員), their management (經營) intentions (意思) are sincerely (成實) reflected. In the process (過程) of executing (執行) this, management (管理) activities (活動) such as planning (企劃), execution (執行), evaluation (評價), and measures (措置) of the business (事業) are smoothly promoted (推進) through self-control management (自己統制管理) methods (方式) based on the reported (申告) goals (目標), delegated (委任) responsibilities (責任), and authorities (權限). Of course, such business (事業) promotion (推進) methods (方式) have been pursued while maintaining (維持) a cooperative (協同) nature (性格) throughout the company (全社的), considering (考慮) appropriate (適切) maintenance (維持) factors (要因) and motivation (動機) aspects (面) as necessary (必要).

The characteristics (特徵) of the foundation (基盤) establishment (造成) stage (段階) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) include strengthening (强化) Saemaul (새마을) education (敎育) to foster (造成) the atmosphere (風土) of Saemaul (새마을) spirit (精神), rational (合理) selection (選定) of Saemaul (새마을) businesses (事業), and efficient (能率) management (管理) methods (方式).

The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) designated (指定) 200 model factories (示範工場) in the first phase in March 1974, and additionally selected (選定) 300 factories (工場) in the second phase. In June of the same year, it collected (發掘) and distributed (配布) advanced (先進) cases (事例) from 11 factories (工場), widely promoting (弘報) the systematized (整理) types (類型) of Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) promotion (推進) methods (方式). Through guidance (指導) and encouragement (督勵) activities (活動) for the aforementioned 500 model factories (示範工場), the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) has promoted (推進) the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動).


--- (p. 274) ---

### <Table 5> Factory Saemaul Management Method

[Diagram: Factory Saemaul Management Method]

*Diagram Description:*

This diagram illustrates the management method of the Factory Saemaul Movement as a flowchart, centered around 'Objective Management', 'Maintenance', and 'Saemaul Division of Labor Activities'.

**1. Objective Management**
*   **Self-Control:** Achieved through the processes of planning, execution, evaluation, and measures.
*   **Motivation:** Encourages member participation through achievement, growth, responsibility, and recognition.
*   **Proposal Adoption:** Incorporates member proposals into the self-control process.

**2. Maintenance**
*   Based on 'cooperative' relationships, the following elements are continuously managed:
    *   Encouraging the improvement of active motivation
    *   Gatherings
    *   Cultivation
    *   Local support
    *   Living compensation
    *   Economic factors

**3. Saemaul Division of Labor Activities**
*   At the core of the 'comprehensive' management method, interacting with the following elements.
*   **Communication:** Pursues smooth communication through labor-management cooperation and improved human relationships.
*   **Group Activities:** Informal and formal groups operate within the framework of the 'nation', interconnected with each other.

Source: Korea Trade Association (韓國貿易協會) Publication, Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) Promotion (推進) Technique (技法) Explanation Book (解說書), 1978.

The movement was put on the right track.

### (2) Self-Help Development Stage (1977~1979)

If the 1960s are seen as a transitional period for Korea's economic and social development, characterized by a one-sided pursuit of economic growth and modernization, then the post-1970s period should be viewed as an era of transformation into a diversified industrial society and the search for corresponding measures.

In the 1960s, the Korean economy pursued economic growth—quantitative increase in wealth—through government-led economic development plans, a kind of state capitalism. On the social front, there was an expansion of materialistic values, the emergence of efforts for an industrial society driven by the growth of modern enterprises, and the deepening of the diversified and stratified social structure.

Therefore, the transitional phenomena of Korea's economic and social structure in the 1960s would, upon entering the 1970s,


--- (p. 275) ---

# Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

This period can be characterized by the exploration of settlement types (類型) aimed at the 1980s (年代). In other words, as Korea (韓國) moved towards the 1980s (年代), its economy (經濟) and society (社會) began to emphasize the corporate (企業) management philosophy (經營 理念) and status (位相) that would lead the country into a high-tech industrial society (高度 産業 社會). Additionally, private enterprises (民間 企業) in Korea (韓國) started to emphasize their social responsibilities (社會的 責任) more than ever before in order to form and develop a modern industrial society (近代的 産業 社會).

If a corporation (企業) is operated solely for the benefit of a particular capitalist (資本家) without considering the interests (利益) of workers (勤勞者) and the general consuming public (一般 消費 大衆), the capitalist society (資本主義 社會) that serves as the background for its existence (存在) will become the target of their criticism (批判) and attacks (攻擊). This will make it impossible to maintain the corporation (企業) in the long term (長期的) and sustain the capitalist system (資本主義 體制).

Therefore, it is necessary to consider the interests (利益) of the general consuming public (一般 消費 大衆) and workers (勤勞者), as well as other stakeholders (利害 關係者), and adjust their relationships (關係) while establishing the corporation (企業) as a social institution (社會的 公器) and maintaining and developing the capitalist system (資本主義 體制). This management responsibility (經營 責任) is what is referred to as the social responsibility (社會的 責任) of corporations (企業). It was during this period that the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場 新村運動) was ignited with the recognition of the need to determine the direction (方向) of such corporate management responsibility (經營 責任).

In February 1977, the government (政府) established the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場 新村運動) Promotion Headquarters (推進 本部) within the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry (大韓 商工會議所) to perform guiding functions (指導 機能) as the number of model factories (示範 業體) increased.

During this period, the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場 新村運動) was promoted in the following ways, with a focus on the sincere fulfillment of corporate social responsibility (社會的 責任):

First, responsibility for the maintenance and development of the enterprise (企業 維持 發展 責任) was promoted through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) assignment activities (分任 活動) to maximize productivity (生産性) and fulfill social responsibility (社會的 責任) by rationally distributing the results (合理的 配分 結果).

Second, responsibility towards workers (勤勞者 責任) was promoted through improvements in wages (給與 改善) based on performance distribution (成果 配分), and the expansion of welfare and welfare facilities (福祉 厚生 施設 擴充).

Third, responsibility towards shareholders (株主 責任) was promoted by recognizing the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場 新村運動) as a driving force (原動力) for the sustained development of the enterprise (企業 發展).

Fourth, responsibility towards consumers (消費者 責任) was promoted through improvements in product planning (製品 企劃), quality improvement (品質 改善), and after-sales service (事後 管理) as a result of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) assignment activities (分任 活動).


--- (p. 276) ---

Fifthly, the most significant achievement is the contribution to regional community development. Through rural service activities mobilizing labor, technology, and equipment, sisterhood partnership projects, and industrial cooperation, both spiritual and material support has been actively provided. This has been linked with the Saemaul Undong in local communities, greatly contributing to self-organization.

Sixthly, government policies such as resource conservation, corporate disclosure, and fair trade have been faithfully reflected and yielded many results through the factory Saemaul Undong.

In addition, notable achievements include the "Second Home Movement" in the workplace, which has greatly contributed to stabilizing labor-management relations. The Factory Saemaul Undong Promotion Headquarters, under the slogan "Treat employees like family and factory work like your own," has promoted various love-in-action movements, including:

1. Helping underprivileged colleagues
2. Sending family newsletters
3. Promoting family Saemaul Undong
4. Joint birthday celebrations
5. Joint wedding ceremonies
6. Shared use of in-house welfare facilities
7. Factory visits by employees' families
8. Family Day events including employees' families
9. Operation of night special classes
10. Awards for filial children, daughters, and wives

These ideas stem from the notion that while workplaces and homes are separate living spaces, they cannot be considered in isolation, as work provides the means for family life. Therefore, the aim is to revitalize the workplace atmosphere to provide the same sense of happiness, stability, and joy as one experiences at home. Ideally, business owners should care for their employees' difficulties and hardships warmly, as a family head would, and employees should, in turn, treat the company owner like a parent and manage company affairs diligently, as they would household matters. With this mindset, the factory Saemaul Undong has blossomed into the "Second Home Movement" in the workplace during this period, which I would particularly like to emphasize.

I am confident that these aspects will have a significant spiritual influence on the establishment of Korean labor-management relations in the future.

Initially, labor-management relations in capitalist societies were sometimes seen as antagonistic. However, in the mature stage, improving mutual understanding and communication methods to foster a cooperative relationship has become an unchanging common sense in today's industrial society.


--- (p. 277) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong

At the present time, Korea's labor-management relations are based on a productive cooperative relationship, and workers' labor protection is guaranteed by the Constitution and labor laws. However, several issues remain.

First, considering economic trends and the rate of price increases, labor unions demand a certain rate of wage increases as an annual event, and while settlements are reached, neither labor nor management is fully satisfied. In some companies, wage increases are demanded through power struggles regardless of the company's survival.

Second, in the case of companies that grew rapidly in the 1960s and 1970s, some business owners or managers who have relatively high confidence still cannot let go of the idea that employees are merely paid to work. Therefore, even if they attempt to have a dialogue with employees, they fail to develop the methods or media for such dialogue.

Third, company employees lack a fundamental attitude of contributing to national development by fostering the company with a sense of community and creating opportunities for self-development. If this is attributed to a lack of employee qualifications, the company also bears some responsibility. Specifically, companies have not been thorough in investing in education or providing adequate job guidance.

Fourth, although labor-management councils are established and operated to improve productivity, some companies either ignore them from the start or operate them merely as a formality. In particular, attempts to intentionally manipulate labor unions are fundamentally misguided. As a result, labor-management relations have sometimes been considered and addressed only in terms of extreme confrontational situations. Considering these factors, the Factory Saemaul Undong Promotion Headquarters has promoted labor-management cooperation through various publicity activities to overcome the conflicting interests between labor and management and the lack of understanding among some businesspeople.

First, from a spiritual perspective, this involves emphasizing the realization of the ideology of a management community, which can emerge from the unique workplace norms of a company, the management philosophy of the business owner, or the nature of cooperative work methods.

Second, in terms of institutional mechanisms, there are various examples, but the most representative is the sincere operation of labor-management councils or labor-management consultation meetings.


--- (p. 278) ---

Currently, under the Labor Union Act (勞動組合法), companies that have labor unions (勞動組合) are required to establish labor-management councils (勞使協議會) to discuss matters such as collective agreements (團體協約), employment rules (就業規則), production (生産), education and training (敎育訓鍊), work environment (作業環境), grievance handling (不滿處理), and labor-management dispute prevention (勞使紛糾豫防). However, I would like to point out that there are many cases where companies operate these councils merely as a formality.

Thirdly, we have recommended improving labor-management relations (勞使關係) in a future-oriented (指向的) manner, including welfare projects (福祉事業) such as performance distribution (成果配分), expanded opportunities for management participation (經營參加), special recruitment for employees (從業员特採制), operation of workplace savings (職場金庫), consumer cooperatives (消費組合), and retirement insurance systems (退職保險制度) that match the company's (企業) capability level (能力水準). Such business plans (事業計划) should be reviewed (檢討) and drafted (立案) by the labor-management council (勞使協議會) as much as possible, starting with feasible projects (可能事業), and widely promoting (弘報) and making them known (周知) to employees to build a solid foundation of agreement (同意基盤).

### (3) Maturity Entry Stage (1980~)
In the process of developing capitalism (資本主義) over 200 years in Western Europe (西歐), we have been searching for our development direction (發展方向) in a compressed history (歷史) of about 30 years, facing countless challenging factors (挑戰的要因). However, through the united strength (力) of the government (政府), companies (企業), and workers (勤勞者), we have established the foundations (基礎) of capitalism (資本主義), passed the stabilization stage (定着段階), and are now beginning to enter the maturity stage (成熟段階).

Now, the Korean economy (韓國經濟) urgently needs active countermeasures (能動的對應策) against the vicious cycle (惡循環) brought by changes in the growth environment (成長環境). Specifically, internationally, we must address:
1. Resource nationalism (資源民族主義) and new protectionism (新保護主義) in advanced countries (先進諸國) triggered by the oil shock (石油波動),
2. Weakened international competitiveness (對外競爭力) due to the rapid rise in wages (勞賃), and
3. Resistance (抵抗的要素) from increased market share (占有率) of Korean products (韓國商品) in the global market (世界市場).

Domestically, we are facing issues such as:
1. The persistence (慣性) of stagflation (stagflation現狀),
2. The need to respond (副應) to domestic desires (國內的與望) for economic (經濟) and price (物價) stability (安定), and
3. The worsening (惡化) of corporate finances (企業收支) and the occurrence (發生) of unemployment (失業).

As we enter the 1980s (年代), Korean corporate management (企業經營) is undergoing a major turning point (轉換期). From a corporate perspective (企業立場), we must simultaneously fulfill our role (役割) as the main driver (主體) of sustained national economic growth (國民經濟持續成長) domestically (對內的) and strengthen our international competitiveness (國際競爭力) in the era of globalization (國際化時代) externally (對外的).

To address these two tasks (課題) simultaneously, we must pursue management rationalization (經營合理化) along with management (經營).


--- (p. 279) ---

## Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### Mechanism for Stabilizing Labor-Management Relations

[Diagram: Mechanism for Stabilizing Labor-Management Relations]

The above diagram illustrates the mechanism for stabilizing labor-management relations.
The main elements and flows are as follows:

**Center:** Stabilization of labor-management relations

**Elements Influencing the Stabilization of Labor-Management Relations:**

*   **Tradition of labor-management relations**: Contributes to the stabilization of labor-management relations by promoting a cooperative relationship between labor and management.
*   **② Direct institutions for adjusting labor-management relations**: Direct institutional approaches from wages (labor unions) and workers influence the stabilization of labor-management relations.
*   **③ Technical maturity in collective bargaining**: The conclusion of collective bargaining influences the stabilization of labor-management relations.
*   **① Daily business management** (labor policy • manager's personality): Affects the stability of the company, management capabilities, and industrial environment.

**Labor-management entities and interactions:**

*   **Wage laborers (labor unions)** → Workers → Employees
*   **Employers** → Users → Managers
*   **Cooperative relationship in production**: Occurs between employees and managers.
*   **Increase in added value** and **creation of economic trust** affect workers.
*   **Resolution of individual grievances** affects employers.
*   **Collective bargaining → Conflict in distribution** process and **conclusion of collective bargaining** directly influence the stabilization of labor-management relations.

Source: Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Promotion Headquarters, Factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Future Vision (1978)

The modernization of the quality is further promoted, but it has a complementary relationship with each other, and in the latter case, high-condition, high-efficiency, and high-welfare management methods ultimately strengthen the management quality and promote management rationalization.

Here, high-condition refers to the improvement of the working environment and working conditions, and high-efficiency refers to high productivity. High-welfare means that the fruits accumulated by maximizing the efficiency of employees are directly linked to income increase, considering the sociality of the company, through a kind of management cycle (management cycle).


--- (p. 280) ---

In an undeniable law-abiding state (法治國家), where the forces of public order (治安力) and administrative power (行政力) were paralyzed, collective riots (集團亂動) occurred, causing both the government (政府) and businesspeople (企業人), as well as workers (勤勞者), to be simultaneously humiliated. The recent Dongwon Coal Mine (東原炭座) Sabuk Incident (舍北事件) did not so much provide us with a lesson (敎訓) as it exposed the shameful (恥部) fact that our economy (經濟) and social structure (社會構造) are far too vulnerable.

Without a nation (國家), businesses (企業) cannot exist, and without businesses (企業), there can be no workplace for employees (從業員). Conversely, for all citizens (全體國民) to live well, business activities (企業活動) must be conducted, and efforts must be made for national development (國家發展). However, the sad reality (現實) today is that the close bond (紐帶意識) and social responsibility (社會的責任) among these three parties (3者間) are severely lacking.

When we commonly discuss labor-management relations (勞使關係), we tend to think only of institutional mechanisms (制度的裝置).

While it is undeniably one of the most important things, the operation (運營) of these institutions (制度) also depends on the bilateral (雙務的) relationship between businesspeople (企業人) and worker collectives (勤勞者集團). From this perspective, the spiritual (精神的) aspect should be emphasized even before the institution (制度) itself. Only then can we expect efficient (能率的) operation (運營) of the institution (制度), followed by a future-oriented (指向的) aspect that nurtures a bright tomorrow (來日) for workers (勤勞者). It is only when these three elements are well balanced that productive (生産的) and cooperative (協同的) labor-management relations (勞使關係) can be established.

The most representative (代表的) labor-management disputes (勞使紛糾) that have recently caused significant social controversy (社會的物議) were the YH Trade (貿易) Incident (事件) in 1979 and the Dongwon Coal Mine (東原炭座) Incident (事件) in 1980.

These two incidents (事件) occurred just before and after the October 26 Incident (10.26사건), each delivering a significant shock (衝擊) and a sense of emptiness (虛脫感).

The former case (前者) was an example of businesspeople (企業人) abusing the government's economic policy (經濟政策) focused on growth (成長) and export (輸出). The latter case (後者) stemmed from the employer (企業主) taking labor-management relations (勞使關係) too lightly and the lack of dialogue (對話) to address the fervor (雰圍氣) of union activities (勞組活動) in a climate of liberalization (自由化).

Such cases (事例) were merely surface manifestations (表面化) of social problems (社會的問題). Beyond these, countless complex (複雜한) and difficult-to-understand (理解) labor-management conflicts (勞使紛爭) have been raised. In particular, after the October 26 Incident (10・26事態), there is no denying the fact (事實) that division (分裂), jealousy (猜忌), antagonism (反目), mistrust (不信), and confusion (混亂) continued to escalate during a period when democratic development (民主發展) should have been steadily promoted (推進).


--- (p. 281) ---

## Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

These problems are expected to manifest in various forms depending on the development of production technology, labor market trends, the nature of labor union activities, the consciousness of workers, the values of management, and the relative importance of government policies towards these factors. To prevent these problems in advance, it is necessary to strengthen the foundation of dialogue and negotiation between labor and management.

Our country's economy is now entering a major trial period. Based on the experience of advanced countries, it is expected that it will be difficult to continue high growth beyond the $100 billion export era. It is seen that a radical measure needs to be prepared to adapt to and coexist with the fierce international competition and achieve victory. According to the analysis of the Bank of Korea, while our country's enterprises have expanded significantly in terms of external appearance along with economic growth, they are found to be lacking in substance. In particular, in terms of the profitability of enterprises, the return on total investment is 4.8% for manufacturing companies and 3.6% for export companies, and in terms of productivity, it is still below 50% of the level of advanced countries and 70% of the level of Japan. The Saemaul Undong task activities being promoted by Korean enterprises are evaluated as a driving force to overcome these obstacles and rise up.

The government authorities, considering these points, have announced measures to revitalize the Saemaul Undong in factories, emphasizing two policies in particular.

One is to emphasize the establishment of a Korean-style labor-management relationship where labor and management, before asserting their respective interests, unite their efforts towards the common goal of the survival of the enterprise and the livelihood of employees. The other is to recommend the promotion of Saemaul Undong task activities on the basis of a stable labor-management relationship. In other words, it is intended to actively reflect the wisdom and ingenuity of employees in management policies through Saemaul Undong task activities and to improve productivity and management level in a short period of time. In response, for companies with good results, financial support is being considered, and tax support is also being considered.

The characteristics of the Saemaul Undong in factories in the 1980s are to achieve the realistic task of management rationalization that enterprises are currently facing through more efficient Saemaul Undong task activities.


--- (p. 282) ---

## 4. Indicators of School Saemaul Undong (Movement)

### a. Basic Concept of School Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The recognition that education and training are important factors in national development is relatively recent. This recognition can be simply explained as the fact that human capabilities such as creativity, judgment, organizational skills, and observational skills nurtured through education and training contribute more distinctly to economic growth than material resources. We refer to these factors as human capabilities or human resources.

Factors necessary for development include entrepreneurial spirit, achievement motivation, rational thinking, innovative attitudes, creative spirit, and progressive views. However, most of these factors belong to the deep structure rather than knowledge or technology. Today, there is a strong tendency to interpret education and training in relation to economic development from the perspective of human resource development and to confuse human resource development mainly with technological development. However, such views are somewhat shortsighted. Human factors necessary for economic development include knowledge and technology, but productive attitudes and progressive values that enhance such knowledge and technology must precede them.

Therefore, educational or training plans for human resource development should not focus solely on knowledge or technology but should be built on scientific thinking, creative progressive views, the spirit of innovation, universality, and civic-mindedness. Otherwise, it may lead to a waste of human resource development investment and may leave behind factors that are dysfunctional for national development.

In this sense, school Saemaul education, which forms the core of the School Saemaul Undong (Movement), is guided in a direction that develops and practicalizes the deep structure of human factors, thereby gaining sympathy from all sectors of society. So far, school Saemaul education has contributed significantly not only in the spiritual education aspect that has supported the Saemaul Undong (Movement) from its ignition stage to the present but also in the aspects of environmental improvement and income increase.

The education community has long been promoting regional community school movements, hometown school movements, and whole-village education movements under the spirit of the socialization of education. On December 5, 1969, the National Education Charter was proclaimed.


--- (p. 283) ---

## Chapter 4 (第4章) Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

During the first anniversary ceremony, the late President Park Chung-hee expressed deep concern for the socialization of education, which led to the further activation of the Saemaul education movement.

On March 7, 1972, a special presidential address was issued in the presence of all cabinet members, local governors, and superintendents of education, actively promoting the Saemaul beautification movement. This address, which emphasized practical education directly linked to production and the national spirit of overcoming national difficulties, became a historic opportunity for the systematic improvement and dissemination of school Saemaul education. Furthermore, from March 24 to 25 of the same year, the National Conference of Educators was held in Daegu, where it was resolved to actively participate in national security and the Saemaul Undong. The conference also pledged to prioritize production education as the immediate task of education and to contribute actively to the establishment of self-reliant national defense and the Saemaul Undong.

Consequently, in January 1973, a dedicated department for Saemaul education was established within the Ministry of Education, and the scholarship policy was formulated to include the deepening of Saemaul education as one of the general policies. Educational efforts were concentrated on the localization of the curriculum, the expansion of adult education, and the development of volunteer activities. Thus, the school Saemaul Undong is characterized by setting educational tasks to resolve issues through Saemaul education and promoting achievable areas in the overall operation of school education. This maximization of educational functions is evaluated as a task to promote the spiritual revolution and economic development of the entire nation, thereby accelerating the modernization of the motherland and the revival of the nation.

The basic objectives of Saemaul education, under the ideology of the National Education Charter, are set to cultivate the Saemaul spirit among students and local residents through school education. This aims to contribute to regional development and national progress by nurturing practical individuals. To achieve these objectives, the following eight items are set as policies for Saemaul education and are being implemented in educational settings.

First, the curriculum is localized based on survey contents related to regional community development, and is operated centering on solving fundamental problems of the regional community (Curriculum).

Second, learning guidance is recommended to be diversified by utilizing human, material, and cultural resources of the regional community (Learning Guidance).

Third, to cultivate the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, and to foster a rational, efficient, and productive lifestyle, the school is guided to plan and manage both internal and external school life systematically.


--- (p. 284) ---

## Life Guidance (生活指導)

Fourth, schools should provide various opportunities for education for the entire community, including children, non-school-going youth, and adults (adult education).

Fifth, schools should actively participate in community development by conducting educational volunteer activities (volunteer activities).

Sixth, schools should implement model education for income increase to promote the advancement of science and production technology in the community (production education).

Seventh, schools should serve as the center of the community, fostering educational, cultural, and sports activities and taking on the main role in promoting them (cultural activities).

Eighth, schools should sufficiently promote the community through the publication of success stories of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) and other publications (cultural activities).

To implement the above policies, ① general education activities are modeled into 8 areas and 28 sub-projects to carry out educational activities, while ② supportive educational activities and ③ other Saemaul Education research, evaluation, teacher training, university Saemaul Undong, and workplace Saemaul Undong are being strongly promoted.

During the base-setting stage of the Saemaul Undong from 1972 to 1973, general education activities were divided into 10 areas, with 19 common sub-projects and additional projects chosen by provincial and city plans. However, from 1974, during the self-help development stage, based on two years of field application experience and the policies of Saemaul Education, these were revised and modeled as follows, and it was recommended that provincial and city education committees implement them according to the realities of the corresponding regions.

#### (b) Learning Guidance (學習指導)

### (2) Research and Evaluation of Saemaul Education
#### (a) Research on Saemaul Education
To systematically research Saemaul Education, seek solutions to immediate issues in educational settings, deepen and establish Saemaul Education, and incorporate the Saemaul Spirit into daily life, research schools were designated and operated. The results of these studies were published to promote generalization.

Additionally, the progress of Saemaul Education was summarized, future directions were explored, and outstanding cases were collected and published in booklets. These booklets were distributed and promoted to schools at all levels and relevant agencies.

#### (b) Evaluation and Policies of Saemaul Education
Outstanding cases of successful Saemaul Education were identified nationwide and reported to the President in the Monthly Economic Trends Report to boost the morale of the main actors and widely utilize them as reference materials for Saemaul Education. From the case of Jinbyeong Han, principal of Chugok National School in Chunseong County, Gangwon Province, in March 1973, to the end of 1979, there were 20 such cases. For the commendation of outstanding organizations and individuals in Saemaul Education, an achievement evaluation was conducted to promote the continuous development and deepening of Saemaul Education. Awards were given to outstanding organizations and contributing educators.

### (3) Support Activities for the Saemaul Undong
#### (a) Adult Education
The Ministry of Education and the Central Council of the Saemaul Undong started operating 158 permanent Saemaul Schools from 1975, one per city/county education office. These schools were attached to agricultural high schools (including agricultural colleges) and vocational high schools. The permanent Saemaul School education was conducted for local residents in four terms (one term for 50 people) from July to August, with each term lasting three days. The education was divided into common and elective types, tailored to the region.


--- (p. 287) ---

## Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The curriculum, designed to suit the emotional context, operates with a focus on spiritual development (精神啓撥) at 15%, income increase at 70%, and other areas at 15%. In 1979, to enhance the outcomes of this education, residential education was implemented in all schools except for 18 schools in the metropolitan area, and active participation from the target individuals was encouraged.

### (B) Student Volunteer Activities

While student volunteer activities were primarily centered around rural enlightenment activities (農漁村啓蒙活動) until the 1960s, the 1970s marked a shift towards more organized and systematic union structures, establishing a clear trajectory. Notably, through the student patriotic corps (學徒護國團) system, the spirit of "learning while fighting" and "working while realizing" was embodied, showcasing the intellectual capacity of university students and their self-governing abilities. This led to a resolute commitment to playing a leading role in regional development and national construction.

When categorized by time, student volunteer activities are divided into summer volunteer work (夏季奉仕) and winter volunteer work (冬季奉仕). Functionally, they are classified into comprehensive volunteer work (綜合奉仕) encompassing education, technology, and labor activities, and medical and dental student-led volunteer medical services (診療奉仕) in medically underserved villages (無醫村). By target region, they are distinguished into rural area volunteer work (農漁村地域奉仕) and urban area volunteer work (都市地域奉仕).

The volunteer activities of intellectuals can be traced back to the period before the March 1st Movement (運動), even reaching the era of King Yeongjo (英祖代) of the Joseon Dynasty (李氏朝鮮), known for producing many scholars. Examining the development process of student volunteer activities since the establishment of the union system (聯合會 體制), we find the following:

In the first year of 1970, when the volunteer union (奉仕聯合會) was established encompassing all universities nationwide, 10,202 students from 119 schools participated in volunteer activities across 668 regions under the auspices of Kyung Hee University (慶國大學校).

In the second year of 1971, 11,064 students from 113 schools participated in volunteer activities across 762 regions under the auspices of Korea University (慶國大學校).

In the third year of 1972, 14,192 students from 120 universities participated in volunteer activities across 708 regions under the auspices of Korea University (高麗大學校).


--- (p. 288) ---

Starting in 1973, when Chung-Ang University hosted the 4th session, not only did 70 vocational schools nationwide newly participate in this plan, but a plan was also added for medical and dental colleges nationwide to conduct medical service activities in villages without doctors. As a result, in 1973, an unprecedented 37,776 students from 254 colleges participated in activities in 1,241 regions.

In 1974, during the 5th session hosted by Sungkyunkwan University, 43,576 college students from 265 colleges nationwide conducted service activities in 1,590 regions, marking significant development in scale.

In 1975, during the 6th session hosted by Hongik University, 60,221 service team members from 282 schools participated in activities across 1,168 regions nationwide, achieving many results.

In 1976, under the auspices of Dankook University, university service activities were conducted. This was the first service activity held after the establishment of the Student National Defense Corps. The participation situation saw 44,147 people from 289 schools conducting activities in 1,111 regions, bringing about several developmental changes.

First, it was decided to organize service activity teams in units of 30 to 40 people as a principle. Second, the service activity period was set to 10 days or more to allow for more substantial service. Third, service activity regions were selected based on the voluntary will of the service team members, and whenever possible, specific regions were set as concentrated service regions by university units. It was encouraged that universities play a leading role in deeply implanting their ideals in these regions and comprehensively developing the local society. Fourth, as part of the efforts to expand the scope of the Saemaul Undong to urban areas, university students took the lead in initiating urban Saemaul service activities.

The university student service activities, in which almost all universities nationwide participated, saw 50,781 people from 288 schools participate under the auspices of Hanyang University in 1977, conducting service activities in 1,128 regions. In 1978, under the auspices of Kyung Hee University, 51,295 people from 279 schools conducted service activities in 1,051 regions.


--- (p. 289) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

In 1979, Sungjeon University (崇田大學校) organized 292 schools (個校) with 54,790 students (學生) participating in service activities (奉仕活動) as on-site training (現場實習) in 1,170 regions (地域) nationwide (全國). In 1980, Sungjeon University (崇田大學校) continued to organize these activities.
Starting in 1979, there has been a push to combine service activities (奉仕活動) with on-site education (現場敎育), encouraging students to apply (體驗) the theories (理論) they learn in school (學校) in the field (現場) and practice (實習) them. Additionally, regional development (地域開發) joint service activities (聯合奉仕活動) are being carried out to cultivate (功養) the Saemaul spirit (精神) among middle school (中等學校) students (學生), foster (견지) their love for their hometown (鄕土愛) and country (祖國愛), and encourage them to actively participate (自進參與) in the development of society (社會) and the nation (國家).

(d) University Saemaul Undong (運動)

At this point, where the initial Saemaul Undong (運動), centered around rural areas (農村), is now expanding to cities (都市) and the participation (參與) of intellectuals (知識人) is being requested (要請), the University Saemaul Undong (運動) holds significant meaning.
University Saemaul Undong (運動) is operated (運營) under the supervision (主管) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) division (部) of the Student National Defense Corps (學徒護國團), divided into Saemaul Undong (運動) and education (敎育) suited to its characteristics (特性). Universities (大學) have been continuously (持續) making efforts (努力) to deepen (深化) the spirit (精神) and functions (機能) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) through education (敎育) and research activities (硏究活動). The expansion (展開) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) is primarily carried out (展開) within universities (大學單位) to mature (成熟) it and then gradually expand (擴大) it to a cooperative system (協同體制) that connects (聯合) universities (大學) and extends (擴大) to the regional community (地域社會).
To ensure the efficient operation (運營) of the University Saemaul Undong (運動), the University Saemaul Undong (運動) Council (協議會) was established in August 1974, with universities (大學) nationwide (全國) joining (加入) it.

① University Student (大學生) Saemaul Undong (運動) Research Presentation Meeting (硏究發表會)
To invigorate (活力) the University Saemaul Undong (運動) and enhance (高起) student (大學生) participation awareness (參與意識), research presentation meetings (硏究發表會) are held to present (發表) research papers (硏究論文) and outstanding cases (優秀事例) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) that students (大學生) have researched (硏究) and practiced (實踐).

② University Professor (大學敎授) Saemaul Undong (運動) Research Presentation Meeting (硏究發表會)
The University Professor (大學敎授) Saemaul Undong (運動) Research Presentation Meeting (硏究發表會) has been held annually (年例) since 1975. Each year, 10 to 20 tasks (課題) are assigned (賦與) for research (硏究), and the presentation meeting (發表會) is held under the supervision (主管) of the Saemaul Research Society (硏究會) with the support (後援) of the Ministry of Education (文敎部) as an annual event (年例行事). Such research (硏究) not only contributes (貢獻) to the establishment (定立) of the direction (方向) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) but also greatly contributes (貢獻) to promoting (促進) the research activities (硏究活動) of university professors (大學敎授).


--- (p. 290) ---

### ③ Establishment and Operation of University (大學) Saemaul (新村) Research Institutes (硏究所)

To promote the development, deepening, and expansion of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) in universities, various research institutes within the universities are utilized, or separate Saemaul Research Institutes (新村硏究所) are established to deepen academic research on the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) and to develop and implement plans for promoting the movement within the university. In particular, to accelerate and strengthen the increasingly deepening and developing university Saemaul Undong (新村運動), and to induce the academic and functional participation of university (大學) people for the development of a nationwide Saemaul Undong (新村運動), the establishment of Saemaul Research Institutes (新村硏究所) in each university (大) was recommended.

In January 1977, through a meeting of student affairs directors (學生處 過長) from each university, and in February through a meeting of university presidents (總長), university Saemaul promotion councils (推進協議會) were formed centered around professors (敎授) and students (學生) who had completed Saemaul education (敎育). Using these councils as a foundation, the spread of the university Saemaul Undong (新村運動) was promoted, and the establishment and operation of dedicated Saemaul research institutes (硏究所) were encouraged. As a result, by the end of October 1980, 44 universities had established permanent research institutes (常設硏究所) and were conducting research.

### Da. Characteristics of School (學校) Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

The characteristics of the School (學校) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) lie in Saemaul education (敎育). This is because the ultimate goal of Saemaul education (敎育) aligns with the development of the Saemaul spirit (精神), contributing to regional community (地域社會) development and national development (國家發展). Saemaul education (敎育) involves connecting issues related to students (學生) and regional residents (地域住民) with the school's (學校) educational problem-solving capabilities, selecting specific tasks, and resolving them. Therefore, these characteristics can be further concretized as follows.

#### (1) Establishment of New Value Systems (價値觀)

Saemaul education (敎育) for students (學生) and regional residents (地域住民) aims to cultivate the Saemaul spirit (精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同), intentionally changing their value systems (價値觀), attitudes (態度), and behavior patterns (行動樣式). This role is increasingly important.

In a country like ours, transitioning from a traditional agricultural society (農業社會) to a modern industrial society (産業社會), it is common to encounter the evils of selfishness (利己心) and dual-structural value systems (二重構造的 價値觀). As a preventive measure, while considering national development (國家發展) and social development (社會發展), one must also think about the development (發展) of the individual (個人). Therefore, the satisfaction of the individual's (個人) growth (成長) and development (發展) should ultimately be extended to the development (發展) of one's hometown, workplace (職場), and country. It is hoped that this way of thinking will be fostered in a healthy manner. This is what truly contributes to the enhancement of national power (國力伸張).


--- (p. 291) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

It is an important opportunity to foster a sense of unity (團結心) and cooperation (協同心) that broadens the base (底邊) of the movement.

The necessity of cultivating the Saemaul spirit (精神) and Saemaul education (敎育) can be traced back to the national (國定) education system established by the National Education Charter (國民敎育憲章) promulgated in 1968. Furthermore, on March 24, 1972, at the National Educators' Conference (全國敎育者大會) held in Daegu (大邱), the late President Park Chung-hee emphasized in his address (致辭) the following characteristics of Saemaul education (敎育):
1. Education (敎育) that fosters a national (民族的) self (自我) and understands it
2. Education (敎育) that emphasizes a correct understanding (認識) of the group (集團) and the nation (國家)
3. Productive education (生産敎育) that contributes to national development (國家發展)
4. Security education (安保敎育) for victory and unification (勝共統一)

Looking back, in the past (過去), our country had unclear educational ideals (敎育理念) and was overwhelmed by the influx of foreign goods (外來文物), leaving no time to digest them, and was only preoccupied with imitation (模倣), losing its self (自我) and floundering. Education (敎育) in the name of democracy (民主) was merely a mechanism (mechanism) for transmitting (傳達) knowledge (知識) and skills (技術), and countless students were unable to establish a firm belief (信念) and philosophical (哲學的) foundation (基礎) for the future of the nation (國家發展) or their own future (自己將來問題).

Now, the Saemaul education (敎育) led by the Ministry of Education (文敎部) is greatly contributing to correcting the bright expression (表情) of the nation (民族) by developing (開發) and rediscovering (再發見) its historical (歷史的) and cultural (文化的) traditions (傳統) as a brilliant national heritage (民族遺産), and nurturing (育成) patriotic (愛國) humans (人間), diligent (勤勞) humans (人間), smiling (微笑) humans (人間), and humans (人間) who practice (實踐) love (愛).

### (2) Participation in Regional Community (地域社會) Development (開發)

The Saemaul Undong (運動) must ultimately stimulate behavioral changes (行動變化) among local residents (地域住民) to achieve immediate goals (當面目標). Such behavioral changes (行動變化) bring quick and effective results when schools (學校) faithfully perform their given functions (機能) and missions (使命).

Therefore, the primary concern (主要關心) of schools (學校) is to enhance the knowledge (知識), functions (機能), and attitudes (態度) of local residents (地域住民) for improving their living standards (生活改善) and increasing their income (所得增大), and to accelerate the construction (建設) of a welfare society (福祉社會) by cooperating (協助) with other administrative agencies (行政機關) related to community education (住民敎育).

Major initiatives through which schools (學校) contribute to regional community (地域社會) development (開發) via the Saemaul Undong (運動) include sisterhood ties (姉妹結緣), regional community (地域社會) enlightenment (啓蒙), industry-academia cooperation (産學協同), neighborhood assistance, and nature conservation (自然保護) movements (運動).


--- (p. 292) ---

### La. The Process of Promoting School Saemaul Undong (Movement)
#### (1) The Stage of Establishing the Foundation (1960〜1972)
School Saemaul education, which began during the ignition stage of the Saemaul Undong (Movement), has strongly supported the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in terms of spiritual education, environmental improvement, and income increase. With a long ideological origin ranging from regional community school movements under the spirit of socializing education to hometown school movements and the Onmaeul education movement, School Saemaul education emerged as a central function of the School Saemaul Undong (Movement) from the beginning.

Schools have not only provided Saemaul spirit education but also carried out various training sessions, skill development, life improvement, educational environment creation, and self-reliant school operations to perform exemplary and central roles in the regional community. They have also created a decisive opportunity for improving the academic atmosphere.

Education and economic growth are inseparable. In this sense, it is necessary to relatively appreciate the level of Korea's economy during this period. Coincidentally, while the School Saemaul Undong (Movement) was establishing its foundation, the government implemented the first and second five-year economic development plans.

During the first five-year plan period, to satisfy the prerequisite conditions for industrialization, the government attempted to develop power sources necessary for various industrial production activities, such as cement, oil, and fertilizer plants, as well as viscose rayon and various chemical fiber plants. Simultaneously, it actively developed railways, roads, and ports, and significantly expanded social overhead capital. Moreover, it promoted the construction of import-substituting industries following the construction of key industries.

The second five-year plan reinforced the competitive foundation of the export-oriented industrial structure established during the first period and promoted the targeted development of strategic industries, such as petrochemical, steel, and machinery and metal (including electronics) plants, which were becoming the core of industrial structure sophistication. Consequently, strengthening the foundation for the growth of intermediate capital goods industries became a characteristic of this period.

These characteristics of economic development rapidly accelerated the pace of industrialization in urban areas. The growth shock from this led to the ignition of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in rural areas. During this period, the large-scale production and supply of cement, in particular, was significantly utilized as an important material for the rural Saemaul Undong (Movement).


--- (p. 293) ---

## Chapter 4 (第4章) Development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

It became possible. Moreover, the fact that the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) started in rural areas (農村) and could be established without encountering significant obstacles is attributed to the effectiveness of the Saemaul education (새마을敎育) that had been promoted in schools (學校).

### (2) Deepening and Expansion Stage (深化擴散段階) (1973~1975)

Starting from 1973, efforts were made to deepen (深化) Saemaul education (새마을敎育) through the rational (合理的) operation (運營) of the curriculum (敎育課程), strengthening of learning guidance (學習指導), school opening (學校開放), adult education (成人敎育), volunteer activities (奉仕活動), local community education (鄕土社會敎育), and cultural activities (文化活動). Adjustments (調整) were made to emphasize creativity (創意性) and innovative (劃期的) practices (實踐), aiming to make schools (學校) the center of local development (鄕土開發) and to promote education (敎育) that reflects national pride (國格), renews (革新) the country's educational climate (敎育風土), and contributes to national development (國家發展) and peaceful unification (平和統一).

Thus, the main scholarship policies (獎學方針) focused on the rationalization (合理化) of curriculum (敎育課程) operation (運營), expansion (拡充) of adult education (成人敎育), and the promotion of volunteer activities (奉仕活動). The activities included:
1. Revising (改正) the curriculum (敎育課程) of elementary schools (國民學校) and middle schools (中學校) to strengthen (强化) Saemaul education (새마을敎育)
2. Establishing (設置) and operating (運營) summer and winter Saemaul schools (새마을學校)
3. Setting up (設置) departments (部署) responsible for Saemaul education (새마을敎育)
4. Holding (實施) Saemaul education (새마을敎육) achievement presentation meetings (實績發表會)

In 1974, schools (學校) were required to gain the trust (信賴) of the local community (地域社會) by providing substantial content (內容). School educational activities (學校敎育活動) were guided to evoke gratitude (感謝) and influence (影響) among local residents (地域住民).

During this period (時期), the characteristics of the economic development plan (經濟開發計劃) included a rapid increase (急增) in industrial production (工業生產) and export growth rates (輸出成長率), rapid development (開發) of key industries (基幹工業), and a gradual shift (脫皮) from primitive (原始的) agricultural production methods (農業生産方法). The growth (成長) in content (內容) and speed (速度) was notable, and the construction of key industries (基幹產業) and the transformation of the industrial structure (産業構造) enhanced inter-industry (相互間) linkage effects (聯關效果), leading to the reorganization (再編成) of the industrial system (產業體制) and the efficient operation (運營) of industrial production facilities (工業生産施設).

However, the first oil shock (第1次石油波動) in November 1973 caused a slight contraction (位縮) in corporate management (企業經營), and in 1975, there was a temporary (一時的) downturn (下降) in the economy (景氣). During this period (時期), the school (學校) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) placed particular emphasis (意義) on resource conservation education (資源節約敎育) and dietary improvement education (食生活改善敎育), which is highly significant (評價).

### (3) Daily Life Stage (生活化段階) [1976~]

Since 1976, the fundamental goal (基本目標) of the school (學校) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) has been to incorporate (生活化) the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神) into daily life (生活). The promotion policy (推進方針) was proposed as follows:


--- (p. 294) ---

First, through the operation of self-reliance schools (自活學校) and the utilization of idle land (空閑地), the spirit of Saemaul was incorporated into daily life, and education on material savings (物質節約), improved diet (食生活改善), and the neighbor-help movement was actively promoted to strive for the practice of thrift (勤儉), savings (節約), and totality (總和).

Second, schools were to act as the brain (頭腦) of the local community (地域社會), guiding the practice and establishment of morality (道德性) through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) driven by units such as families (家庭) and workplaces (職場), and particularly leading urban Saemaul Undong (都市新村運動) to cultivate the spirit of thrift (勤儉), neighborhood watch (隣保), and self-defense (自衛).

To achieve these objectives, the following measures were taken: ① revising part of the textbooks (敎科書) for the 1977 academic year (學年度), ② continuing the operation of permanent Saemaul schools (常設新村學校)(敎室) from 1976, ③ evaluating the performance (實績) of the 3rd Saemaul education (新村敎育) and policies (施策), ④ designating and operating model urban Saemaul education schools (都市新村敎育示範學校) (22 schools (個校)), ⑤ publishing Saemaul Undong (新村運動) booklets (册子), and ⑥ holding a conference (發表會) to present research (硏究) on Saemaul education (新村敎育).

The year 1977 focused on cultivating the spirit of Saemaul through production technology education (生産技術敎育) and volunteer activities (奉仕活動), actively promoting material savings (物質節約), increased savings (貯蓄增大), improved diet (食生活改善), and the neighbor-help movement (鄰保運動), with schools serving as the center (中心) of the community (地域社會) to fulfill the socialization (社會化) function of education (敎育) and leading the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) by units (單位), particularly strengthening the promotion of urban Saemaul education (都市新村敎育) to cultivate the spirit of security (安保) and self-defense (自衛).

In 1978, efforts were made to deepen Saemaul education (新村敎育) and lead regional Saemaul Undong (地域新村運動) to cultivate the spirit of Saemaul (新村精神), with a focus on recognizing that the nation's territory (國土) is a treasure trove (寶庫) of nature (自然) and that nature conservation (自然保護) is fundamental (根本) to preserving the territory (國土). To this end, the following actions were taken: ① continuing the operation of permanent Saemaul schools (常設新村學校)(敎室) from 1978, ② evaluating the performance (實績) of the 5th Saemaul education (新村敎育) and policies (施策), ③ interim reporting (中間報告) on the operation of model urban Saemaul education schools (都市新村敎育示範學校), and ④ strengthening nature conservation activities (自然保護活動).

In 1979, business goals (事業目標) and policies (方針) similar to previous years were pursued diligently.

In 1980, in accordance with the government's basic policies (基本施策) for the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), the direction of Saemaul education (新村敎育) was focused on education regarding thrift (勤儉), savings (節約), nature conservation (自然保護), cultivating a healthy citizen consciousness (健全市民意識), and regional community development education (地域社會開發敎育).

The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) in schools was carried out as a movement (運動) to improve education (敎育), and Saemaul education (新村敎育) was promoted as a means to cultivate the spirit (精神) and abilities (能力) for all citizens (國民全體) to live well together.

Thus, Saemaul education (新村敎育) was pursued through the rational operation (合理的運營) of the curriculum (敎科課程), learning guidance (學習指導), and life guidance (生活指導).


--- (p. 295) ---

# Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong was implemented according to the actual conditions of local communities and has consistently fulfilled the socialization function of education by carrying out adult education (成人敎育), volunteer activities (奉仕活動), production (生産) and consumption saving (消費節約) education (敎育), nature conservation activities (自然保護活動), and cultural (文化) and publicity activities (弘報活動). It has greatly contributed to creating a new academic atmosphere (學園風土造成).

### Section 3: Saemaul Education (새마을敎育)

#### 1. Concept (槪念) and Essence (本質) of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育)

##### a. General Significance (一般的意義) of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育)

Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) refers to the education aimed at cultivating all citizens into individuals well-versed in the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神) and technology (技術) to effectively promote the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). There are three important factors here: first, all citizens (全國民), second, the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神), and third, technology (技術).

Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) is not education (敎育) targeted at a part (一部) of the citizens (國民) but is national education (國民敎育) targeted at all citizens (全國民). It is education (敎育) that is implemented without discrimination based on occupation (職業別), gender (性別), age (年齢別), class (階層別), region (地域別), or religion (信仰別). It is not just education (敎育) for farmers and fishermen (農漁民) but also for factory workers (工場勤勞者), businesspeople (商業人), soldiers (軍人), officials (官吏), and educators (敎育者). In other words, it is education (敎育) received by all citizens (全國民) regardless of their background—agriculture (農), industry (工), commerce (商), military (軍), government (官), and private sector (士). In this regard, it differs from any previous education (敎育). Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) is implemented everywhere, regardless of whether one is male (男子) or female (女子), young or old, high-ranking or low-ranking, in the countryside or in the city (都市).

Religious differences (信仰差) are not an issue for Saemaul Education (새마을敎育). Moreover, this education (敎育) is not temporary (一時的) but perpetual (永續的). The characteristics of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) are its universality across society (汎社會性), regions (汎地域性), classes (汎階層性), and time (汎時間性).

Given the above significance (意義), the historical (歷史的) trajectory of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) can be broadly summarized as being divided into Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) in school education (學校敎育) and Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) in society (社會).

Next, Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) is education (敎育) for a human consciousness revolution (人間意識革命) armed with the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神). The Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is a national aspiration project (民族宿願事業) known as the "well-being movement (運動)," and becoming a "new person" from a pre-modern (近代的) human (人間) of the "era of hardship (時代)" to a modern (近代的) human (人間) is a prerequisite (必須條件).


--- (p. 296) ---

It is a clear and logical conclusion. The term "three people" is necessary to define based on the historical and social conditions of our reality. Only human existence established at the intersection of temporality and spatiality can be a concrete human being.

A thorough understanding of national identity and security, the localization of democracy, a subjective historical consciousness, the establishment of national ethical consciousness, and the creation of a Korean version of the general modern citizen are urgent historical tasks in the current situation of Korea. These are all issues related to spiritual education, which need no further explanation.

The Saemaul spirit, which is a concentrated expression of such educational tasks, is expressed as the philosophy of practice of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Our impoverished past stemmed from the weakness of the spiritual attitude of being diligent, trying to help oneself, and trying to combine forces. It is impossible to solve the problems facing Korean society with a spirit of laziness, seeking only the virtue of others, and wanting to live well alone. When all citizens are armed with the Saemaul spirit, any difficulty can be overcome.

Lastly, Saemaul education should focus on technical education. It is a well-known fact that modern society is an era of technological innovation, and it is said that the social changes in one year today are comparable to those of the past 1,000 years. Therefore, it is too obvious that poverty cannot be overcome and income increased to build a prosperous society with the existing agricultural and construction techniques. While the ideal of traditional education has been to pursue the harmonious development of knowledge, virtue, and physical fitness, the ideal of Saemaul education can be said to lie in the harmonious development of knowledge, virtue, physical fitness, and technology.

Of course, industrial development, environmental improvement, health and hygiene, and self-defense are all demanding modern scientific learning backed by the latest technology from all citizens. Therefore, it is only natural that Saemaul education has focused on technical education and will continue to do so in the future, becoming an even more important educational project.

Above, several factors related to the general significance of Saemaul education were discussed, but it should be remembered that there are more essential issues above them. That is, the Saemaul Undong itself is not an issue at the level of political power, but an eternal mission of the Korean people derived from a deeper spiritual historical, cultural historical, and ideological historical significance. This point should not be overlooked in the exploration of the meaning of Saemaul education.


--- (p. 297) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The term "Saemaul" carries a unique connotation that cannot be found in any other foreign language. It encompasses not only the countryside but also "Seoul," and it includes not just general fishing villages but also "government offices" and "companies" (Saemaul Research Institute, Saemaul Research Papers, Volume 1, pp. 46~50, 1976, reference).

While it was stated that Saemaul education targeted the entire nation, it is only when we interpret its spiritual foundation in this context that we can establish a foothold for it as an educational endeavor that is de-politicized, non-partisan, and perpetual. If we were to seek the fundamental spirit of Saemaul education in foreign concepts such as "Community" or "Dorf," it would be difficult to resonate with and internalize the hearts of the Korean people.

What is needed is a mindset that values our "spirit (魂)" as the foundation and accepts others' ideas as "tactics (術)," which we refer to as the "spirit-first, tactics-second ideology (思想)." We believe that "subjectivity (主體性)" refers to nothing other than this attitude. Examining the decade-long transformation of Saemaul education, which carries such significance, in concrete terms is expected to greatly contribute to regional community development and education in Korea in the future.

### B. The Educational Historical Significance of Saemaul Education

Saemaul education possesses unique characteristics that set it apart from any traditional or recent educational endeavors, making its educational historical significance substantial.

Firstly, it has distinctive features from a social educational historical perspective. In both Eastern and Western traditional societies, education was characterized by strong natural laissez-faire, lacking intent, purpose, or organization.

In the West, as modernity approached, some elite groups engaged in voluntary charitable phases or claimed educational rights based on one-sided public demands, with some universities responding to these claims. However, the state's interest in social education remained very passive, merely expressing concern. Thus, it took a considerable amount of time for the subjects of social education to become all-encompassing.

In Korea, traditional social education was left in a state of natural laissez-faire due to the barrenness of industrialization or the stagnation of rural areas. From the late 19th century, as national awareness began to emerge, social education in Korea was more characterized by relief efforts rather than charitable endeavors. However, it did not progress beyond the stage of unplanned, unorganized, and small-scale industrial social education led by a few groups. Therefore, in terms of educational policy and financial investment,


--- (p. 298) ---

## The 10-Year History of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It had consistently shown vulnerability due to the near absence of models.

However, today's Saemaul education is a social education that is policy-oriented, organized, and planned at the highest national policy level, targeting the entire nation. This can be seen as a creative form of Korean lifelong education linked to the lifelong education advocated by UNESCO since 1965, and it can also be considered a new form of social education that can be showcased to the world.

Secondly, the broad scope of the education targets can be noted. Students participate in the localization or socialization of the curriculum, while vice-ministers and other public officials, university presidents, professors, members of the National Assembly, judges and prosecutors, top executives and all employees of corporations, journalists, farmers, and housewives are also educated. The total number of participants reaches 70 million (as of the end of October 1980), making this a social education effort of unprecedented scale in our history, which can be described as a national and ethnic educational scale.

Thirdly, the educational content has distinct characteristics. Common spiritual education is provided across all social strata. For example, cooperative leaders, university professors, and female village leaders receive the same educational content at the same time and place from the same instructor. This is not an education that is merely intellectual or elitist, but rather a philosophy of life and a philosophy of practice based on life experiences. The core of its general content is the "success stories," whose protagonists are humble members of the public, not people of high learning or high rank. Their life journeys are extraordinary, and their stories of overcoming fate to achieve today's glorious success move all who hear them, evoking great gratitude and self-reflection. This unique educational method transcends differences in status, knowledge, and occupation and focuses on human education.

Fourthly, while independent Saemaul education had significant effects and characteristics, the process of the Saemaul Undong itself became an educational curriculum that should also be highly valued. That is, villagers, regardless of the size of the matter, centered around young and capable village leaders, solved village issues through the process of self-consultation, achieving great results. In doing so, they cultivated democratic training and a sense of responsibility. Apart from this, the process of the Saemaul Undong


--- (p. 299) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The proactive life philosophy of "If you do it, it can be done," which was formed through the Saemaul Undong, as well as scientific methods of handling things, the ability to distinguish between public and private matters, the spirit of self-help, the spirit of cooperation, and the spirit of sacrifice are, from the perspective of value education, quite noble educational effects that cannot be denied.

Fifthly, Saemaul education was not merely a simple ideological spiritual education but an education that accompanied tangible material evidence such as increased income and environmental improvement. From this point of view, the educational effect was stronger than any other social education.

The educational function of the hyanggyo (鄕校) during the Joseon (李朝) period was playing a fundamental role in establishing Confucian (儒敎) morality in our country through voluntary participation and inbo (隣保) activities of the people. The educational value of the persistent night schools (夜學) and enlightenment movements (啓蒙 運動) during the Japanese colonial period (日帝 時代) was also significantly evaluated and should not be denied. However, those educations were for the "mind" or "heart" but did not provide "hands." The fact that Saemaul education did not forget technical education was very wise from this perspective, and the idea of organizing technical service teams (奉仕團) was a unique feature that had never been seen before in the past.

Sixthly, Saemaul education was a nationwide and societal education that particularly emphasized "leader education (指導者 敎育)" and sought integration with occupational or positional job training. Efforts to avoid the drawback of neglecting specificity while emphasizing universality should be highly appreciated.

The development process of Saemaul education, which carries various meanings, will be concretely reviewed over the past 10 years across various fields, and future prospects will be explored.

## 2. Content and Methods of Saemaul Education

### a. Basic Structure of Saemaul Education Content

The content of Saemaul education is centered around the general theory and practical methods of the Saemaul Undong, and plans that can be participated in according to the characteristics of the educational targets. Unlike subject-based (主知主義的) curricula or the transmission of knowledge, it adopts experiential mutual education methods.

Therefore, the methods of Saemaul education are derived from the ideology and goals of the Saemaul Undong.

The basic structure of the Saemaul education curriculum emphasizes the following content.

First, the principle of subjectivity (主體性)


--- (p. 300) ---

# Emphasizes National Revival and Establishment of Subjectivity

The Saemaul Undong is a spiritual reform movement based on the new village spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, and also signifies a human reform movement.

The human image to be formed through Saemaul education is not a vague and universal democratic citizen, but a self-reliant citizen with a clear national consciousness established in our historical reality, possessing a firm subjectivity and consciousness of self-reliance. Therefore, the autonomy of education and the autonomy of the educational curriculum have the same meaning.

To further internalize, expand, and develop the Saemaul Undong as a centripetal movement of the nation, the focus should be on fostering self-reliant human images through human reform via Saemaul education, relying on social education.

## Second, the Principle of Productivity

The Saemaul Undong is a movement for living well. However, it is a movement for everyone to live well together.

The most pressing task facing our nation and our people was the rapid development of the national economy. The practical philosophy of modernization through economic development to overcome poverty and live well also resonates with the spirit of Saemaul.

Productivity means producing capable individuals who can fulfill the roles required by society as it develops industrially.

## Third, the Principle of Utility

Emphasizes the improvement of qualities to be on par with advanced citizens in a high-industrial society.

In other words, it aims to cultivate useful individuals who can perform their duties perfectly through the refinement of creative job techniques. It is based on the ideology of modernization where practical learning is applied, not empty theories.

## Fourth, the Principle of Regionality

In a developing country like ours, in addition to school education, social education also has a heavy responsibility for improving and enhancing the cultural and living standards of regional societies. This is because the expansion and development of Saemaul education is closely related to social education.

Through the awareness and voluntary participation of all citizens, the opening of my family, my workplace, and my regional society


--- (p. 301) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

Development (發展) refers to a national movement (國民運動) that advances toward national development (國家發展).

Fifth, the Principle of Rationality (合理性)

In designing the training curriculum (硏修敎育過程) for Saemaul Education (새마을敎育), the ideological (理念) and goal-oriented (目標) sociophilosophical (社會哲學的) stance (立場) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), sociological (社會學的) investigations (調査) of contemporary society (現實社會), and other factors are considered in selecting educational content (敎育內容). The selected content is organized (組織하는) by taking into account its systematicity (系統性), relevance (關聯性), the educational level (敎育水準), interests (興味), and efforts (努力) of the participants (參加하는), and other factors (等).

The Saemaul Education Curriculum (새마을敎育過程) is thus divided into three categories (分類된다) based on the aforementioned principles (原理): the Spiritual Education Curriculum (精神敎育過程), the Vocational Education Curriculum (職務敎育過程), and the Technical and Functional Education Curriculum (技能敎育過程).

The Spiritual Education Curriculum (精神敎育過程) is based on the Saemaul Spirit (새마을精神) of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). It aims to cultivate individuals (人間意識) who can bring about planned (計劃的인) changes (變化) in society (協同) and become healthy (健全한) members (構成員) of the new mind (새마음), new person (새사람), new workplace (새직장), new society (새社會), and new nation (새나라). Through strengthening spiritual education (精神敎育), it establishes a national perspective (國家觀) and fosters leaders (先導者) for the implementation (實踐) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) and total force security (總力安保).

The Vocational Education Curriculum (職務敎育過程) provides vocational training (職務訓練) to lay the foundation for self-realization (自己實現) and the development of qualities (資質開發) necessary for citizens (國民) in an advanced industrial society (高度産業社會).

The Technical and Functional Education Curriculum (技能敎育過程) aims to cultivate professional competencies (職務能力) in response to the basic policy direction (施政基本方向). It targets not only public officials (公職者) but also the general public (一般社會人) to maximize human capabilities (人間能力) and become capable producers (生産人) for building a modern society (近代社會).

The basic structure (基本構造) of the Saemaul Education Curriculum (새마을敎育過程) can be illustrated (圖示) as follows in <Table 7>.

In the following table (圖表), Type I (類型) involves the Saemaul Education Curriculum (새마을敎育過程) and a residential training program (合宿課程) lasting 70 hours (時間), with a focus on spiritual education (精神敎育).
