This educational process can be seen as a form of spiritual development or human education aimed at cultivating the ideal human form as a Korean citizen and a modern national citizen. It is a training process for Saemaul leaders with the following goals: ① the advancement of the Saemaul Undong and the elite training of its leading personnel, ② the promotion of self-help movements by elite leaders, and ③ contributing to modernization through diligence, self-help, and cooperation.

Type II is conducted in parallel with the Saemaul education process (I) and implements on-the-job training. Therefore, it can be seen as a special educational process where the 70-hour residential Saemaul education and separate on-the-job training are combined.

Type III, on the other hand, is a simple form of on-the-job training aimed at cultivating the personality of a capable professional and providing practical education for the development of various techniques. Additionally, Type IV (76 hours) and Type V (152 hours or more) also have their own characteristics as on-the-job training.

This training education includes various forms such as public administration Saemaul training, factory Saemaul training, urban professional organization Saemaul training, rural Saemaul leader training, fishing village Saemaul leader training, and military Saemaul training. However, while Type I residential training is the representative form of spiritual education, on-the-job training education can be found in Types IV to V.

In this training education, more time is allocated to on-the-job training than to spiritual development education, maximizing the educational effect.

Type VI can be thought of as having the same form as Type III. However, it is a special form of Saemaul education as a technical and skill education process.

The total education time is 43 hours or more, focusing more on technical and functional aspects to refine various techniques, resulting in a practical and useful education.

In terms of the scale of Saemaul education, there is the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute at the national level, and at the local level, there is rural and fishing village Saemaul education, urban Saemaul education (workplace units, school units, factories, regional social Saemaul, etc.), and military Saemaul education, which can be further divided.

## II. The Curriculum of Saemaul Education

The content of Saemaul education being implemented in our country is diverse. Indigenous


--- (p. 303) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

The more diverse the training forms, the harder it is to write a standardized curriculum. Therefore, the training forms of various training institutions (제연수기관) being implemented based on the Suwon (水原) Saemaul Leader Training Institute (새마을지도자연수원) as a standard will be divided into I to VI and explained.

## (1) Saemaul Education (Type I) Curriculum

This curriculum focuses on spiritual development (정신계발) for training. The institution that developed the Type I curriculum is the Suwon (水原) Saemaul Leader Training Institute (새마을지도자연수원), which has been a pioneering (元祖的) institution for Saemaul Education (새마을교육).

This training institute initially focused on rural Saemaul leaders (새마을지도자) and self-sufficient farmers (자립농가) in 1972. In 1973, it expanded to include rural women leaders (부녀지도자), frontline administrative officials (시장, 군수 etc.), and farmers. In 1974, it targeted urban Saemaul leaders (새마을지도자), corporate personnel (기업체 인사), social leaders (사회지도급 인사), and high-ranking officials (고급공무원). In 1975, it aimed to broaden the base of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) by including officials (공무원), university professors, and students from various urban strata (都市社會各階層). From 1976 onwards, it expanded to include factory workers (공장근로자) and the general urban population (都市一般).

The content of the education (敎育內容) initially focused on spiritual education (정신敎育), agricultural technology education (農業技術敎育), family planning (家族計畫), economic security (經濟安保), and case studies (成功事例) for the rural population (農村). In the mid-term, it emphasized improving human relations (人間關係改善), cost reduction (原價節減), increasing productivity (生産性向上), and division of tasks (分任討議) for factory Saemaul (工場새마을). In the later stages, it focused on deepening the urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을운동) by establishing new national views (國家觀) and ethical views (倫理觀), promoting loyalty and filial piety (忠孝思想), family rituals (家庭儀禮準則), and general cultural lectures (一般敎養講座), thereby gradually deepening and systematizing Saemaul Education (새마을敎育).

Analyzing the regular curriculum (正規硏修課程) of the Suwon (水原) Saemaul Leader Training Institute (새마을지도자연수원):

- Spiritual Development (精神啓發) (16 hours, 27%)
- Security (安保) and Economy (經濟) (6 hours, 10%)
- Case Studies (成功事例) (10 hours, 17%)
- Division of Tasks (分任討議) (13 hours, 22%)
- Field Trips (現場見學) (8 hours, 14%)
- Other Subjects (其他敎科目)

Within the Spiritual Development (精神啓發) subjects, Saemaul subjects (새마을敎科目) account for 17% (10 hours). Including Saemaul subjects within other subjects, the total reaches 69%.

The adjustment of the standardized textbook (標準敎科書) to correct the tendency of being too focused on the Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) field began in 1977.

A notable trend is the strengthening of national spiritual education (國民精神敎育), indicating that the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) is not only a material movement (物量運動) but also increasingly emphasizes spiritual education (精神敎育).


--- (p. 304) ---

As mentioned earlier, the self-generated (自生的) Saemaul education curriculum (敎育課程) was fragmented and lacked standardization (標準化), leading to the establishment of a basic structure (基本構造) suitable for its organization. Under the auspices of the Office of the Prime Minister (總務處), the Saemaul education standard curriculum (敎育標準敎科) was formulated. This led to the establishment of the National Spirit Education Research Committee under the Prime Minister's Office (國務總理) in 1977, and the active role of the National Spirit Education Coordination Committee as a policy advisory body has brought us to the present day. The contents (內容) are as follows.

### First, the Field of National Spirit Education (國民精神敎育 分野)

① National Subjectivity Historiography (民族主體史觀): This subject (敎科) aims to change the ideology of modernization (近代化理念) and establish self-determination (自主性確立), with 2 hours allocated as a principle.
② Lessons from Overcoming National Crisis (國難克服敎訓事例): Centered around the historiography of overcoming national crisis (國難克服史觀), 2 hours are allocated to explore wise leadership ideologies (指導思想) and the superiority (優越性) of our nation in history, and to seek ways to overcome crises.
③ Economic Growth (經濟成長) and Our Attitude (姿勢): Allocated 2 hours. This subject was previously included in the fields of Saemaul spirit education, security (安保), and economy (經濟), but in 1977, the National Spirit Investigation Committee emphasized the structural change of national consciousness (民族意識) following economic growth (經濟成長) and included it in the field of national spirit education (國民精神敎育 分野). Opinions converged (集約) on emphasizing the German (獨逸) national character (國民性) and focusing on the practical application of frugal living.
④ National Ethics (國民倫理): The previous guiding ideology (指導理念) has been changed to national ethics (國民倫理), with 2 hours (時間) allocated.

The field of national spirit education (國民精神敎育 分野) consists of 4 subjects (敎科目) totaling 8 hours (時間), accounting for 13% of the total time allocation.

### Second, the Field of Unification and Security Education (統一安保敎育 分野)

Reduced from the previous 4 subjects (敎科目) to 2 subjects (敎科目), the subjects on the North Korean regime's (北傀) strategy against the South (對南戰略) and the reality of North Korea (北韓의 實情) have been discontinued, focusing only on international situations (國際情勢), our security situation (安保狀況), and our unification policy (統一政策) as educational content (敎育內容).

The field of unification and security education (統一安保敎育) is allocated 4 hours (時間), accounting for 6.5% of the total.

### Third, the Field of Saemaul Spirit (精神 分野)

Comprising 4 subjects and 16 hours (時間), this field accounts for 23%.

Saemaul Movement (運動) and National Development (國家發展): A 2-hour (時間) subject that has replaced the previous Saemaul Movement (運動) and guiding ideology (指導理念). For example, the Suwon (水原) Saemaul Leadership Training Institute (指導者 硏修院) offers various subjects such as the Saemaul Movement (運動) and spiritual revolution (精神革命), the Saemaul Movement (運動) and our attitude, and the footsteps of the Saemaul Movement, all integrated into this single subject.


--- (p. 305) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The subject matter was narrowed down.
1. **Saemaul Success Cases (成功事例)**: This subject is allocated 8 hours (時間) to cover cases of rural (農村) Saemaul, urban (都市) Saemaul, workplace (職場) Saemaul, and school (學校) Saemaul.
2. **Saemaul Field Education (現場敎育)**: This subject is allocated 4 hours (時間) for field learning. This subject emphasizes the learning (學習) form of comparative education (比較敎育) in the field (現場) of Saemaul education (新村敎育).
3. **Saemaul Volunteer Service (努力奉仕)**: With a rational (合理的) operation of the subject (敎科運營) in life science (生活科學), 2 hours (時間) are allocated.

Fourthly, other affiliated subjects are diversely composed and focus on learning (實習), case studies (事例硏究), etc. Breaking it down, subjects that highlight the government's (政府) policy (施策) priorities include natural conservation (自然保護) (2), consumer savings (消費節約) (2), reform of popular affairs (庶政刷新) and our posture (姿) and situation (勢) (2), etc. In 1980 (年), three additional subjects were implemented as special spiritual education: economic reality (經濟現實) and policy direction (施策方向) (1), today's reality and our resolve (覺悟) (1), international situation (國際情勢) and security situation (安保狀況) (1). Additionally, there are Saemaul films (映畫), savings campaigns (金모으기), wholesome entertainment (健全娛樂), wholesome songs, sports, and basic security training (安保基礎訓練). Division of tasks (分任討議) (10) and my resolution (決意) (1) are also included in the miscellaneous category, forming part of the Saemaul training (硏修) subjects (敎科科目).

With the Saemaul spiritual education curriculum (精神敎育課程) at its core, the curriculum for national security unification (統一安保分野) and the curriculum for national spiritual education (國民精神敎育) are operated effectively (效果的) as a trinity (三位一體) to cultivate the historical (歷) forces (史) for creating a new era (創造). These can be considered subjects (敎科科目) for establishing theories (理論定立). Furthermore, the fourth category of other related curricula (關聯敎育課程) emphasizes experience (經驗) and participation (體驗), making it a desirable form of core education (中核敎育課程).

Such a well-polished and systematic curriculum (敎育課程) could not have been achieved by chance. It originates from the philosophy (哲學) of national revival (民族中興) derived from the decisive leadership (英斷) of the late President Park Chung-hee (朴正熙).

The development history (發展史) of the Saemaul education curriculum (新村敎育課程) began in 1972 (年) and, taking 1977 (年) as a turning point (起點), entered a stage of in-depth development (深化發展段階) without deviating (離脫) from its orbit (軌道), becoming the driving force (原動力) for establishing today's new society (社會). To facilitate understanding, the historical (歷史的) development content (發展內容) of the Saemaul education curriculum (新村敎育課程) is compared below, which is expected to aid in researching and developing future tasks (發展課題).

## Chapter 4 (第4章) Development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

First, the time allocated for national spirit education decreased from 14% to 13%, reducing the total time by 1 hour.

Second, the field of unification and security education (統一安保敎育分野)

Similar to the national spirit field (國民精神分野), before 1976, the standard curriculum was insufficient, leading to the establishment of 108 subjects covering international affairs, South Korea's security, North Korea's (北傀) strategies against the South (對南戰略), the fundamental philosophy of communism (共産主義), the situation in North Korea (北韓), the Korean War (韓國動亂), and the weaknesses of communism (共産主義). In 1977, the curriculum focused on international affairs, South Korea's coordinates (座標), the situation in North Korea (北韓), and South Korea's unification policy (統一政策), comprising 9% of the total time over 6 hours. However, in 1978, due to strong advocacy from the National Unification Board (國土統一院), the curriculum was reduced to 4 subjects covering 8 hours and 11% of the total time, focusing on North Korea's strategies against the South (對南戰略), international affairs, and our security (安保). Essentially, the 1977 curriculum on international affairs and South Korea's coordinates (座標) was split into two. By 1980, the curriculum was further reduced to 2 subjects, covering 4 hours and 6% of the total time. Our unification policy (統一政策) has seen some modifications in its educational content since before 1976, but the number of subjects remains unchanged. In contrast, the situation in North Korea (北韓實情) was consistently taught but was discontinued in 1980.

(2) Job Training Courses

This training course is designed to enable more efficient and scientific job performance. The types are diverse, ranging from II to V. Therefore, the training content is centered on research and learning tasks based on actual cases, with a focus on participatory education. In other words, it aims to cultivate job capabilities for problem-solving.

Type II is a job training course conducted in parallel with Saemaul Education. The training content includes the Saemaul Education course Type I (70 hours), with an extended training period for job training, which is its distinctive feature. In some cases, continuous residential training for job training and Saemaul Education residential training, as well as job training, may be conducted separately.

This type is compiled with diverse job contents according to the training goals of the training institute. For example, public administration training institutions, factory Saemaul training institutions, urban professional organization Saemaul training institutions, and agricultural and fishing village Saemaul training and education institutions can be mentioned.

A brief introduction to the special training institutions for Saemaul Education courses according to their types is as follows.

First, the educational goal of the training institution for public administration is to strengthen spiritual education and foster a national perspective.


--- (p. 310) ---

The establishment of a welfare state (福祉國家) by strengthening total security (總力安保) and national subjectivity (民族主體性), cultivating leaders (先導者) for this purpose, ② establishing a sound attitude among public officials (公務員) with a deep commitment to public ethics (公職倫理), and ③ fostering professional administrators (專門行政家) who adapt to developmental administration (發展行政). This includes the Central Public Service Training Institute (中央公務員敎育院), public service training institutes (公務員敎育院) under each ministry, state-owned enterprises (國營企業體), and the Saemaul Training Institute (새마을敎育硏修院), primarily adopting vocational training courses (職務敎育課程) in conjunction with Saemaul education. For instance, local (地方) public service training institutes (公務員敎育院) implement Saemaul education (새마을敎育) and vocational training (職務敶育) separately, with vocational training courses (職務敎育課程) including New Recruit Class (新規採用者班), General Administration Class (一般行政班), Accounting Vocational Class (會計職務班), and Tax Administration Class (稅務行政班), among others. Additionally, recent initiatives include a unique one-day citizen (市民) Saemaul education (1日敎育) program.

Secondly, the Factory Saemaul Training Institute (工場새마을硏修院) aims to ① elite (精銳化) the leaders (先導要員) of the Factory Saemaul Movement (工場새마을運動), ② fulfill corporate innovation (企業革新) and social responsibility (社會的責任) to play a pivotal role in national revival (民族中興), and ③ enhance productivity (生產性) through improved labor-management cooperation (勞使協調增進) to build a welfare industrial society (福祉産業社會). To achieve these educational objectives (敎育目的), the institute offers three main courses (課程): General Senior Management Class (一般高級經營者班), Leader Class (指導者班) for factory (工場) Saemaul leaders (指導者) and middle management (中間管理層), and Women Leaders Class (婦女指導者班) for female employees (女子從業員).

Thirdly, the Urban Saemaul Training Institute (都市새마을硏修院), representing urban vocational group education (都市職能團體새마을敎育), aims to ① elite (精銳化) the leaders (先導者) of the Urban Saemaul Movement (都市새마을運動), ② create a bright (明朗) and orderly (秩序) society through the practical application (生活化) of Saemaul spirit (精神), and ③ establish a sound national ethic (國民倫理) and value system (價値觀確立) to build a welfare state (福祉國家).

Fourthly, rural Saemaul education (農村새마을敎育) focuses on ① establishing national subjectivity (民族主體性) through the practical application (生活化) of Saemaul spirit (精神), ② increasing income (所得) through the scientific advancement (科學化) of production (生產), and ③ building a welfare rural community (福祉農村) through modernization (近代化) and a strong national consciousness (國家觀). The main components of rural Saemaul education include Saemaul rural leader (農村指導者) education (敎育), agricultural education (營農敎育), agricultural machinery education (農機械敎育), and special education courses (特殊敎育課程).

The most standard (標準) and widely implemented type (類型) of vocational training course (職務敶育課程) is IV.

As shown in <Table 12>, the fields of national spirit education (國民精神敎育分野), unification and security education (統一安保敶育分野), and Saemaul spirit education (새마을精神敶育分野) have been significantly reduced, while vocational training (職務敶育) content has been greatly strengthened. Specifically, vocational subjects (職務敶科目) account for about 8 subjects, or 60% of the curriculum. This education

(3) Technical · Skill Education Curriculum
As indicated in the above table, Type VI is similar to Type II. The difference here is that the focus is on technical training rather than job training, targeting skilled workers or employees in skill-based occupations.


--- (p. 312) ---

The approaches can be seen as different.
As seen above, although there may be some differences depending on the type of Saemaul Training Institute (硏修院), the three pillars of national spirit education (國民精神敎育), unification and security education (統一安保敎育), and Saemaul spirit education (새마을精神敎育) are combined to maximize spiritual development (精神啓發). Alongside these, with equal or greater emphasis, there is job training (職務敎育) aimed at cultivating capable professionals and well-rounded individuals. Additionally, there is a broad and diverse range of social education (社會敎育), including general education (素養敎育) and various social issues (餘他社會問題), as well as vocational training (職能分野) and technical education (技術敎育), and leisure education (餘暇善用). Furthermore, it is guiding towards a lifelong education system (平生敎育體制) that allows individuals to enjoy life. Therefore, the ultimate goal of training education (硏修敎育) should be focused on building a cheerful and orderly welfare state (福祉國家), and it is undergoing a major shift towards education (敎育) that cultivates patriotic citizens (愛國하는 국민(國民)).

Examining the time allocation for Saemaul education (새마을敎育), the characteristics are as follows.

First, when looking at Type I Saemaul education (새마을敎育) as a benchmark, it is primarily lecture-based, accounting for 50.7%. In contrast, Type IV job training (職務敎育) courses emphasize case studies (事例), real objects (實物), and participatory education (參與式敎育).

Second, when the total (總) education time (敎育時間) is categorized into spiritual education (精神敎育) time, job training (職務敎育) time, and technical and vocational education (技術 • 技能敎育) time, job training accounts for 55.4% and technical and vocational education for 30.9%, while spiritual education time is only 13.7%. The low proportion of spiritual education time is because this data is from a 1977 survey. As mentioned earlier, since 1978, the field of spiritual education has been on an increasing trend.

In particular, with the arrival of 1980, the direction of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) was re-established as a national spirit reform movement (國民精神改革運動), so it is expected that national spirit education (國民精神敎育) will change significantly.

### Da. Methods of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育)
Saemaul education (새마을敎육) is shifting from theoretical education focused on lectures to practical life education (生活敎育) that addresses immediate real-world problems and meets the needs of the participants, taking into account their diversity. Specifically, it combines practical case-based education (實技事例) and audiovisual education (視聽覺敎育), with a focus on experiential lectures (體驗式) and participatory education methods (參與式敎育) being widely adopted.


--- (p. 313) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong

In this way, by arousing the interest and concern of trainees and solving their needs, voluntary learning motivation was stimulated, not only developing intelligence but also fostering creative human will, thus laying the foundation for the development of Saemaul history. It made a significant contribution to the development of human resources capable of adapting to and pioneering rapidly changing social and economic environments.

### ① The lecture method is being developed into a new form.
Depending on the nature and teaching objectives of the Saemaul education curriculum, the lecture method can be effective. In addition to oral lectures, utilizing various teaching methods and learning materials can enhance effectiveness.
To maximize the effects of Saemaul education,
*   First, it is conducted in a direction that transmits new knowledge, technology, and information and induces learning motivation, sufficiently achieving the intended purpose;
*   Second, general education focuses on spiritual development and fostering a sense of mission relevant to the times;
*   Third, specialized learning in each field is deepened through applied lectures, experiential, and participatory education methods, and efforts are being made to maximize effects through the development of audiovisual equipment.

### ② The workshop method has enhanced the effectiveness of Saemaul education.
The workshop is one of the educational methods widely used in adult education. Through the autonomous discussion and work of trainees, this method solves problems or tasks, achieving remarkably high results.
Adult education achieves good effects when participants' problem awareness and voluntary participation consciousness are heightened.
A representative subject applying this method is the division of tasks for discussion, which
*   First, cultivates the ability to solve problems that arise during the promotion of Saemaul projects and income-increasing projects;
*   Second, fosters a spirit of cooperation through the search for and discussion of common problems;
*   Third, emphasizes the formation of techniques to guide residents; and
*   Fourth, the division of research tasks is conducted autonomously, providing an opportunity to cooperate and enhance common productivity through the process of reporting results, thus fostering democratic citizens.

# Contributions to Quality Improvement

It also greatly contributes to improving the qualities required as a leader. In addition, educational methods such as case presentations (事例發表) and dialogue (對話) are applied here. This can also be explained as participatory education (參與式敎育).

### ③ Methods for Forming Learning Diagnoses (學習診斷) in Training Education (硏修敎育)

Methods for forming learning diagnoses in training education vary depending on the educational content (敎育內容) and methods (方法). In the Saemaul training curriculum (敎育課程), lectures centered around theory for adults (成人) can be effective even for large-scale groups (大單位集團), while discussions (討議) and consultations (協議) combined with joint work (共同作業) are more effective in small groups of 10 people or fewer (以內).

### ④ Recent Trends in Training Education Methods (硏修敎育方法)

Recent trends in training education methods utilize a systemic approach (體制接近)(System approach) by expanding manipulative games (操作的)(game) to analyze problem situations (問題), develop possible solutions, and train decision-making skills (意思決定技術) required in the problem-solving process (問題解決過程) through simulation methods (模擬式方法)(Simulation Method).

Such educational methods (敎育方法) are more effectively applied to training (硏修) in job training courses and technical and skill education courses (技術• 技能敎育課程), achieving high educational effects (敎育効果).

### ⑤ Variety in Training Education Methods (硏修敎育方法)

As mentioned above, the educational methods (敎育方法) applied to training education (硏修敎育) are diverse. The most important factor supporting this is the method of strengthening learning motivation (學習動機).

To elaborate on a few points from the previous lectures (講義):

First, Saemaul training education (硏修敎育) strengthens learning motivation (學習動機) through experiential education (體驗式敎育), yielding significant results. Specifically, practical case studies (實技事例), practical training (實習), field trips (現場見學), and life experiences (生活體驗)(including overnight stays (合宿)) greatly contribute to the substantive improvement (內實化) of education (敎育).

Second, the appropriate use of audiovisual education (視聽覺敎育). That is, maximizing the use of audiovisual equipment such as V.T.R., projectors (映寫機), recorders (錄音器), and slides to enhance learning effects (學習効果).

Third, self-reflection (反省) within experiences, such as personal resolutions (決意) and daily self-reflection diaries (日日自省錄), provides opportunities to solidify the foundation for self-realization (自我實現).

Fourth, lifelong education (平生敎育) is facilitated through follow-up guidance (追隨指導). By developing forms such as on-site visits (現地訪問) and correspondence guidance (通信指導), re-education (再敎育) is provided to Saemaul trainees (硏修生) to revive what may have been forgotten after graduation. A representative example is the one-day re-training (再硏修) for graduates implemented at the Suwon Saemaul Leadership Training Institute (水原새마을指導者 硏修院). The curriculum (敎育課程) is diverse, allowing re-trainees (再硏修生) to recall past training (硏修) and achieve significant results in training education (硏修敎育) in terms of future life and human transformation (人間改造).

Additionally, there are self-generated gatherings centered around trainees. For example, we can mention the "Parksimhoe (朴心會)." Other examples include on-site guidance for agricultural machinery and mobile guidance.

## ⑥ Methods for Evaluating Saemaul Education (敎育)

To measure the effects of education and the shift in technology acceptance, pre-evaluation, mid-term evaluation, and comprehensive evaluation are conducted. Through analysis and reflection, surveys using questionnaire methods are carried out to seek measures for improving education, yielding good results.

Furthermore, self-evaluation methods such as daily self-reflection journals (自省錄) and personal resolutions are employed according to the unique characteristics of the training institutes, yielding significant results. However, there is an urgent research task to use practical evaluation methods. While there are methods like the "guess who test," they pose challenges in measurement.

In addition to these institutional elements, to strengthen the motivation for Saemaul education (敎育), pre-notification formation evaluation before learning, and reward systems are methods that can easily strengthen learning motivation. Formative evaluation for correction points out learning deficiencies and corrects them. Such corrective processes not only enhance corrective responses but also help develop stimulating self-concepts, proactive attitude changes, and competitive spirit, which are widely recognized as mature motivations.

## ⑦ Lectures on Saemaul Education (敎育)

Lectures on Saemaul education (敎育) are characterized by the participation of experts from various fields and all strata of society.

First, looking at the composition of lecturers in the spiritual education (精神) field, out of a total of 727 individuals, external experts account for 65%, which is 32% more than the total number of experts. Among these external experts, civil servants make up the largest group with 181 individuals (39%), followed by university professors with 110 individuals (3%), successful case presenters with 19%, and famous individuals with 10%. The remaining 140 individuals include about 3% members of the National Assembly.

The content handled by lecturers for each subject is primarily dependent on civil servants and university professors because the training institutes themselves cannot cover subjects like national subjectivity historiography and national ethics. The field of unification and security education is dominated by professors, while the ideology of the Saemaul Undong is mainly handled by training institute instructors and public officials.


--- (p. 316) ---

It is composed of the ranks of Muwon (務員) and Professor (敎授).

Lastly, among Saemaul Education (새마을敎育), the most impressive subject (敎科) is Success Cases (成功事例), followed by the fields of Saemaul Spirit Education (새마을精神敎育分野) and National Security and Unification Education (統一安保敎育分野) in that order. Conversely, the lowest response (反應) is seen in Divided Debate (分任討論). In the future, the response to the subjects (敎科目) that should be emphasized is the research and development of Success Cases (成功事例) at a nationwide (汎國民的) level, the exploration of interesting teaching methods (講義法) for the field of Saemaul Spirit Education (새마을精神敎育分野), and the clear selection of educational objectives (敎育目標) for the field of Civic Spirit Education (民精神敎育分野). Therefore, the subject names (敎科目名稱) of the Saemaul Education Curriculum (새마을敎育課程) should be reviewed and adjusted appropriately to be realistic and interesting. Additionally, the methods (方法) of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) should be implemented in large groups gathered in one place, as well as through visiting or itinerant education (巡廻敎育), and should be researched and developed as a lifelong education system (平生敎育體制) as an immediate task.

### 3. The Reality of Saemaul Education (새마을敎育의 실제)

To successfully carry out the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動) and achieve sustainable (永續的) development (發展), the most important factor is the cultivation of human resources (人間育成) as the main actors (主人公) leading the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動). This human resource development (人間育成) must be based on education (敎育). In particular, the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動) is based on human elements (人間的要素) such as diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同), requires scientific and technological means (科學技術的手段) such as income increase (所得增大), and necessitates an active spirit of public service (人間的 봉사정신). Therefore, it is impossible to cultivate such human qualities (人間的素養) without education (敎育).

Thus, the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動) is an expression of the national (民族的) will (意志) for all citizens (國民) to live well, and it is based on the practical principles (實踐原理) of full participation (全民參與), nationwide implementation (全域展開), and sustained effort (全力持續). Consequently, Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) must be disseminated (擴散) and implemented (實施) nationwide, regardless of age or gender (男女老少), from growing children to adults (成人).

Since the inception (點火) of the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動) in 1970 until today, over a decade, Saemaul Education (새마을敎育) has been steadily carried out through school education (學校敎育) from elementary (初) to university (大學) levels. It has also been widely disseminated (擴散) and implemented (實施) through various channels, including government-affiliated agencies, private organizations (民間團體), Saemaul Education Training Institutes (새마을敎育硏修院), industries (産業體), and factories (工場), thereby laying the foundation (基盤) for the sustainable (永續的) development of the Saemaul Movement (새마을運動).


--- (p. 317) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

has made enormous contributions to building this foundation. From this perspective, this section will examine the actual implementation and dissemination processes of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) from three aspects: ① school-based Saemaul education (學校새마을敎育), ② social Saemaul education (社會새마을敎育), and ③ Saemaul technical education (技術敎育).

## A. School-based Saemaul Education (學校새마을敎育)

### (1) The Significance and Necessity of School-based Saemaul Education (學校새마을敎育)

Education plays the most pivotal role in successfully leading the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동). In particular, to pass down the Saemaul spirit to future generations as a historical legacy, it is crucial to cultivate the abilities and attitudes necessary for the next generation to inherit and carry forward this spirit. Therefore, Saemaul education within the school system holds significant educational importance.

Firstly, from a historical perspective, schools in Korea have been serving an educational role in the development of villages and local communities since the 10th century. For instance, hyanggyo (鄕校) had characteristics similar to today's local schools (鄕土學校) or community schools (地域社會學校). Myeongnyundang (明倫堂) also provided education for Confucian scholars (儒生) and social education for general villagers (一般鄕民), playing a central role in local education (鄕土敎化). Furthermore, during the Japanese colonial period, as part of the policy to increase production in the colony, there was an emphasis on social service activities centered around middle schools, lending improved farming tools, holding product evaluation meetings, establishing home vegetable gardens, and providing guidance on pig farming and agricultural techniques.

In particular, the establishment of elementary schools in remote villages in 1933 was fundamentally a part of the colonial policy, aiming to provide elementary education even in the most isolated areas, ostensibly to achieve universal education. After liberation in 1945, the social functions of schools were emphasized, and during the Democratic Party administration in the 1950s, the construction of local schools was promoted as an educational policy to contribute to regional development. The 4H club movement in the 1950s, the National Reconstruction Movement in 1961, and the student enlightenment movement for local communities after the May 16 Revolution (革命) all expanded the opportunities for schools to serve in regional development.

In July 1972, the Ministry of Education emphasized that schools should play a role in improving or developing local communities in connection with the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), and announced the establishment and operation of Saemaul schools. The objectives of schools presented here were to cultivate the Saemaul spirit and to


--- (p. 318) ---

It aims to contribute to income growth through practical skills and establish sound national ethics and rational living attitudes, emphasizing these aspects to develop and sustain the Saemaul Undong as a nationwide movement.

School Saemaul education currently being implemented connects school and community movements directly with regional development projects. It is a unique form of Korean school education that participates in and cooperates with the nationwide Saemaul Undong led by the state.

While examining the process of school localization, it is evident that this responds to societal demands for practicality, shifting away from traditional schools that were isolated from society and focused on impractical knowledge-driven academism. This aligns somewhat with the spirit of today's Saemaul education. However, the ideological pursuit emphasized in today's Saemaul education—such as the passion for national modernization, the desire to escape prolonged poverty, and the drive to promote a spiritual revival movement to realize a welfare state and society—is historically unique in its voluntarism and creativity, making its significance profound.

Thus, the distinctive feature of Saemaul education is that it began as a nationwide, government-led initiative but is now evolving into a citizen-led movement. Another characteristic is that it has shifted from focusing on material, external transformations to emphasizing qualitative and spiritual value enhancement, and is now advancing towards expanding qualitative capabilities.

Secondly, considering its national relevance, today's world has entered an era of resource wars, with countries weaponizing their natural resources, causing economic imbalances. While advocating for peaceful coexistence, nations are primarily concerned with their own defense and national interests. Additionally, as a divided nation, Korea faces unpredictable threats from North Korea, necessitating a strong foundation for peace and efforts towards unification. This requires fundamental strength-building.

Given these national realities, today's school education must emphasize its role in contributing to the existence and development of the nation and society, not just individual personality completion and self-realization. Schools and students must be fully mobilized for this realistic task.


--- (p. 319) ---

## Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

School education (學校敎育) should embrace the ideology (理念) and content (內容) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to elevate the consciousness of the community (共同體意識) and actively promote the socialization (社會化) of education (敎育). At the same time, it should play a leading role (先導的役割) in regional community development (地域社會開發) and further expand its role (役割) beyond the school (學校). Therefore, this issue (問題) is also an important practical task (實踐課題) given to Korean education (韓國敎育) in reality (現實的).

From this perspective (觀點), schools (學校) must aim to cultivate and practice the spirit of Saemaul (新村精神) among students (學生) through education (敎育), thereby elevating the consciousness of being the main subject (主體意識) of the nation (國家) and ethnic group (民族), and establishing a practical image of a Korean (韓國人像) who loves the country (愛國) and the ethnic group (愛族). In other words, Saemaul education (新村敎育) is the manifestation (發顯) of the national ambition (民族雄志) to build a better country (國家) to live in. Therefore, it should instill the spirit of the nation (民族) in the younger generation (後世代) through education (敎育), develop the latent consciousness of being the main subject (主體意識) among the people (國民), and contribute to establishing a firm attitude towards life (生活姿勢) for the eternal prosperity (永遠繁榮) and security (安全) of our nation (民族) as Koreans (韓國人).

(2) Process of Practice (實踐) and Diffusion (擴散過程)
(a) Setting the Basic Direction (基本方向設定)

Saemaul education (新村敎育) is an educational movement (敎育運動) that arose with inevitability (必然性) due to national (國家的) and social (社會的) demands (要求). The question of how education (敎育) contributed to realizing the ideology (理念) of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is a prerequisite (前提), and in this context, Saemaul education (新村敎育) has been considered the most important aspect of school education (學校敎育).

Saemaul education (新村敎育) is a practical education (實踐敎育) that aims to strengthen the bonds (紐帶) between individuals (個人), regional communities (地域社會), and the nation (國家), and to move from a traditional stagnant society (沈滯社會) to a developmental functional society (機能社會). It is based on a firm spirit of Saemaul (新村精神) as its ideological foundation (理念的基底), maximizing the socialization function (社會化機能) of education (敎育) and the educational function (敎育的機能) of society (社會) to promote spiritual development (精神啓發). Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) can achieve its goals (目的) through such educational activities (敎育的活動), and the role (役割) of supporting this will be the basic goal (基本目標) of Saemaul education (新村敎育). Under this premise (趣旨), in 1972 (年), the Ministry of Education (文敎部) proposed that the goal (目標) of Saemaul education (新村敎育) is to cultivate the spirit of Saemaul (新村精神) among students (學生) and local residents (鄕土住民) through school education (學校敎育) under the ideology (理念) of the National Education Charter (國民敎育憲章), thereby contributing to local development (鄕土開發) and national development (國家發展) by fostering practical Koreans (實踐的韓國人).

From this goal (目標), it can be seen that the ideological basis (理念的根據) of Saemaul education (新村敎育) is the National Education Charter (國民敎育憲章), and the study (學)


--- (p. 320) ---

# School Education (學校教育)

Throughout the entire school education system, the core of the educational content was explicitly stated as cultivating the Saemaul spirit (精神) in both students (學生) and residents (住民). The goal was not to produce highly educated individuals who were selfish (利己的) and unproductive (非生產的), but rather to foster action-oriented (行動的) and constructive (建設的) individuals who could contribute to the development of their local communities (地域社會) and the nation (國家社會發展), thereby nurturing true Koreans (韓國人).

The specific goals and policies of School Saemaul Education (學校새마을教育) aimed to:
1. Enhance the effectiveness (效果) of education (教育) through its socialization (社會化), strengthening the cooperative system (協同體制) between schools (學校) and local communities (地域社會).
2. Establish a healthy mental attitude (精神姿勢) among citizens (國民), characterized by rational (合理的) living habits (生活態度), diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), self-reliance (自立), cooperation (協同), and a national perspective (國家觀) centered on security (安保爲主).
3. Contribute to the development of local communities (地域社會發展) while promoting modernization (近代化) for the construction of a unified and prosperous (統一繁榮) nation (祖國建設).

## (Na) Establishing the Foundation for Promoting Saemaul Education (教育) (教育推進의 기반조성)

To effectively achieve the goals of School Saemaul Education (學校새마을教育), the "Direction for Promoting Saemaul Education (教育推進方向)" was organized in 1972, and school education plans (教育計劃) were unified as shown in the following example (圖示) <Table 13>.

To effectively operate and implement the basic policies of Saemaul Education (教育), the following directions were organized:

In light of the scope (領域) of promoting Saemaul Education (教育), the local community (鄕土社會) should be organized and operated to collect and utilize relevant materials (資料). For example, adult education (成人教育), social surveys (社會調査), and investigations into the consciousness structure (意識構造) of residents (住民) for embodying the Saemaul spirit (精神) should be conducted. Policies (施策) should be carefully selected (精選) considering each school (學校別) and region (地域別). Emphasis should be placed on practical measures (實踐事項) and methods (方法) tailored to different types of schools, such as elementary schools (國民學校), high schools (高等學校), vocational high schools (實業高校), liberal arts high schools (人文高校), rural schools (農村奧地), urban schools (都市學校), island schools (落島), medium-sized city schools (中都市學校), peripheral island schools (島嶼周邊), and central city schools (都心學校).

Therefore, the policies of the Ministry of Education (文敎部方針) and the provincial (市道) policies (施策) should be carefully selected (精選) and adjusted (調整) to fit the reality (實態) of regional community schools (地域社會學校) in line with the Saemaul spirit (精神). The most central tasks (中核的課題) should be addressed first, with gradual expansion (漸進的波及).

Furthermore, the Ministry of Education (文敎部) took the first step in promoting Saemaul Education (教育) by establishing an administrative responsibility and command system (指揮體制) through the appointment of education officers (教育擔當官), provincial education committees (市道教育委員會), and city/county education offices (市郡教育廳). The nationwide conference was held, and the determination for total security (總力安保) and Saemaul education (敎育) was made. That is (即), they were classified into ① common items (共通事項), ② urban type (都市型), ③ rural and fishing village type (農漁村型), and ④ remote island type (島嶼僻地型), fully considering the specificity of local communities to maximize their achievements (成果).

### (라) Practice (實踐) and Diffusion (擴散) of Education (敎育)

Following the basic direction (基本方向) and goal setting (目標設定) of school (學校) Saemaul education (敎育), the establishment of a promotion base (推進基盤) and the establishment of an administrative (行政的) support system (支援體制), Saemaul education (敎育) gradually spread (擴散) and was implemented (實施) from elementary schools (國民學校) to universities (大學).

In 1973 (年) and 1974 (年), the school (學校) Saemaul movement (運動) was practiced in school districts (學區) and school units (學校單位). Elementary schools (國民學校) directly connected (直結) homes and schools, strengthened the operation (運營) of mother's classrooms (敎室) and housewife's classrooms (敎室) so that the school (學校) Saemaul movement (運動) could directly extend (連結) and be practiced as a home (家庭) Saemaul movement (運動). In middle (中) and high schools (高等 學校), students' (學生) skills (技術) were connected (連結) to regional (地域) Saemaul movements (運動) through learning activities (學習活動), and in universities (大學), participation was promoted through research activities (硏究活動), volunteer activities (奉仕活動), and alumni association activities (鄕友會活動). In particular (特히), school (學校) Saemaul movements (運動) were promoted to ensure that factories (工場), farms (農場), and villages became students' learning grounds (學習場) through industrial-academic cooperation (產學協同), and the connection (結緣) of rural (農村) Saemaul movements (運動) with technology (技術) was promoted so that the technology (技術) learned at school (學校) could contribute to the development (發展) of the local community (地域社會).

In this way, school (學校) Saemaul education (敎育) had to be directly connected (直結) to the scope (領域) and methods (方法) of the school (學校) Saemaul movement (運動), so school (學校) Saemaul education (敎育) also took charge (擔當) of Saemaul education (敎育) in the field (分野) of social education (社會敎育) outside the school (學校), in addition to learning activities (學習活動) and school life (校內生活) within the school (學校).

First, in terms of the practice (實踐) of in-school (校內) Saemaul education (敎育), in the case of elementary and secondary schools (初中等 學校), organizations (組織) such as the faculty and staff association (敎職員會) or the Saemaul education (敎育) promotion (推進) committee (委員會) were established for effective (效果的) promotion (推進), and each (各) school (學校) had a Saemaul education (敎育) officer (擔當 敎師) in charge of the actual work (實務).

In particular (特히), in 1976 (年), the operation of model schools (示範學校) for urban (都市) Saemaul education (敎育) was made public as a measure (方案) to promote (促進) and deepen (深化) the urban (都市) Saemaul movement (運動), inviting national education superintendents (敎育長) and principals (校長) for observation (觀察) and understanding (理解).


--- (p. 323) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

Urged.

In December 1976, the winter vacation (冬季休暇) was utilized to actively promote environmental purification (環境淨化) and nature conservation (自然保護運動) at suburban areas (郊外地), tourist spots (觀光地), amusement parks (遊園地), and mountain climbing sites (登山地) as part of the urban Saemaul education activities (都市新村敎育活動). This led to the establishment of practical plans (實踐計劃) tailored to the realities of each region (地域社會) for every school level (各級學校). Nature conservation (自然保護) content (內容) was also incorporated into the educational curriculum (敎育過程) of elementary schools (國民學校), middle schools (中學校), and high schools (高等學校).

In 1977, the focus was on actively promoting production technology (生産技術), educational volunteer activities (敎育奉仕活動) to cultivate the Saemaul spirit (精神), resource conservation (物資節約), savings increase (貯蓄增大), improved diet (食生活改善), and neighborhood mutual aid (運動). Schools (學校) were encouraged to maximize their regional socialization functions (地域社會化機能) to lead the Saemaul Undong (運動). Along with this, the policy for scholarships (獎學方針) aimed to further deepen (深化) general educational activities (一般敎育活動) to solidify (內實化) Saemaul education (敎育). Educational activities (敎育活動) were planned (計劃) and implemented (實施) according to the realities (實情) of each city/province education committee (市•道敎育委員會) or each school level (各級學校), with careful consideration (配慮) to ensure educational achievements (敎育的成就).

For universities (大學), the Saemaul Undong (運動) was carried out through school units (學校單位) or circle centers (中心) based on the guidelines for promoting university Saemaul Undong (大學新村運動推進指針) and self-planning (計劃樹立) of each school (學校自體). This was done through academic research (學問硏究) and practice (實踐). Particularly (特히) after the establishment (創團) of the Student National Defense Corps (學徒護國團), a Saemaul department (部) was created to organize (組織的) and plan (計劃的) the movement more effectively (展開). The main areas of focus included:

1. Creating a healthy campus life atmosphere (學校的健全生活氣風造成)
2. Renewing the academic atmosphere (勉學風土的刷新)
3. Environmental purification (環境淨化)
4. Resource conservation (物資節約)
5. Expanding volunteer activities (奉仕活動展開) and developing research demonstration regions (硏究示範地域設定開發)
6. Joint projects (合同事業) with relevant regional social organizations (地域社會有關機關)

These areas were creatively (創造的) selected (選擇) and developed (開發) according to the unique characteristics (特殊性) of each university (大學).

Starting from 1977, universities (大學) were encouraged (勸獎) to establish (設置) Saemaul Undong promotion committees (運動推進委員會) and affiliated Saemaul research institutes (硏究所) to serve as the foundational bodies (母體的役割) for researching and practicing (硏究實踐) university Saemaul Undong (大學新村運動) and education (敎育). Excellent case presentations (優秀事例發表會) of university student Saemaul Undong (大學生新村運動) were held to enhance (鼓吹) students' (學生) participation awareness (參與意識) and promote (促進) their understanding (理解) and proactive (積極的) attitudes (態度) towards the Saemaul Undong (運動). In terms of the curriculum (敎育課程面), subjects (科目) such as sociology (社會學), schools (學校) and regional societies (地域社會), and regional society development theory (地域社會開發論) were used to approach (接近) and understand (理解) the Saemaul Undong (運動) theoretically (理論的), and to analyze (分析的) and review (檢討) it for theoretical establishment (理論的定立). Some universities (大學) conducted (實施) Saemaul research education (硏究敎育) through Saemaul academic lectures (學術講演會) and one-day Saemaul school operations (1日新村學校開設運營).

Secondly, for extracurricular (校外) Saemaul education (敎育), in the case of elementary schools (國民學校) and middle/high schools (中•高等學校), generally


--- (p. 324) ---

Through school(學校) surroundings(周邊) environmental improvement(環境整備), beautification work, cleaning, neighborly assistance, traffic organization(交通整理), social purification(社會淨化) campaigns, volunteer activities(奉仕活動), and other means, the acquisition of the Saemaul spirit(精神) and the cultivation of proactive and practical competencies(素養) are being promoted. University students(大學生) in particular have organized volunteer activities(奉仕活動) in rural(農村) and urban(都市) areas under a united(聯合) system(體制), categorizing them into labor service(勤勞奉仕), educational service(敎育奉仕), and medical service(醫療奉仕). In urban(都市) areas, efforts have been focused on fostering the spirit of neighborhood mutual aid(隣保精神) and patriotism(愛鄕心) among residents(住民), as well as guiding housewives(主婦) in side businesses(副業), thrift(勤儉節約), and improving living attitudes(生活態度改善). In 1979(年), under the guidance of professors(敎授), volunteer activities(奉仕活動) were organized by specialized(專攻) fields(分野) and skill groups(技能 集團), allowing students to directly apply the specialized knowledge(知識) and skills(技術) they have learned at school(學校) through on-site(現場) learning, greatly contributing to the development(發展) of the local(地域) community(社會).

### Social(社會) Saemaul Education(敎育)

#### (1) The Significance(意義) and Necessity(必然性) of Social(社會) Saemaul Education(敎育)

There is no doubt that the sustainable(永續的) development(發展) of the Saemaul Movement(運動) must be based on education(敎育). One of the functions(機能) of this education(敎育) is the aspect of Saemaul education(敎育) imparted to the younger generation(後世代) through school(學校) education(敎育), while the other is the education(敎育) conducted for people(社會人) from all walks of life(各界各層) in society(社會). One of the greatest achievements(成果) of the Saemaul Movement(運動) is its function(機能) as social(社會) education(敎育) for the entire nation(國民).

Social(社會) education(敎育) refers to organized(組織的) educational activities(敎育活動) primarily targeting(主로) youth(靑少年) and adults(成人), excluding those conducted as part of the school(學校) education(敎育) process(過程). Such adult(成人) education(敎育) is widely promoted alongside the ideals(思想) of the right to education(敎育權) and the right to learning(學習權) for the general public(一般國民), and today, it is further accelerated alongside the concept of lifelong education(平生敎育)(Life-long education). Saemaul education(敎育) also possesses the characteristics(性格) of lifelong education(平生敎育), necessary for living one's entire life(一生).

Thus far, Saemaul education(敎육) has sufficiently fulfilled the role of social(社會) education(敎育). Its scope(領域) has expanded to include civil servants(公務員), military personnel(軍人), businesspeople(企業人), professors(敎授) and teachers(敎員), journalists(言論人), workers(勤勞者), farmers(農民), housewives(家庭主婦), and students(學生). In many respects, it has excellently contributed to the development of the spirit(精神開發) through fostering the spirit of self-reliance(自主精神), promoting healthy thinking(健全思考) and behavioral norms(行爲規範), awakening national consciousness(國民的覺醒), upholding public interest(公益崇尙), and promoting efficiency(能率化), among other aspects of ideological education(思想敎育). Ultimately, the Saemaul Movement(運動) has striven to create a better society(社會), a welfare society(福祉社會).


--- (p. 325) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

If we consider the Saemaul Undong to be the collective will of society (社會人) in action, then it is impossible without a spiritual revolution (精神革命) of society (社會人) to build a welfare society (福祉社會). Cultivating human elements of society (社會人) such as diligence (勤勉性), self-help (自助性), and cooperation (協同性), and developing and investing in the knowledge and technology necessary to build a better new society (社會) are all areas that education (敎育) must undertake. Therefore, to elevate the Saemaul Undong into an integrated national movement (民族運動) across various fields such as politics (政治), economy (經濟), society (社會), culture (文化), and education (敎育) for the unification (統一) of the fatherland (祖國) and the eternal prosperity (繁榮) of the nation (民族), comprehensive social education (社會敎育) across a wide range of areas (領域) is extremely necessary and holds great significance (意義). In fact, the Saemaul Undong has been practiced with a focus on developing villages through various development projects (開發事業) and cultivating the spirit of the people (國民) through education (敎育).

As a result, the Saemaul Undong (새마을事業) itself has been a process of national education (國民敎育), playing the role of a training ground (訓練場) for residents to learn and practice how to live well. Therefore, Saemaul education (새마을敎育) has been the driving force behind the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). Based on Saemaul spiritual education (새마을精神敎育), it has contributed to nurturing the leadership abilities (指導能力) of individual citizens (國民) and acquiring technologies for increasing income (所得增大), thereby promoting the internalization (內面化) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).

From this perspective, Saemaul education (새마을敎育) as social education (社會敎育) must continue for the sustained development (發展) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) or for the continued existence and development (存續發展) of society (社會). It is a task that must be continuously practiced to elevate the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) into a movement (運動) to enhance the integrated national capabilities (統合的民族力量).

## (2) Process of Practice (實踐) and Diffusion (擴散)

### (가) Education (敎育) by Training Institutions (訓練機關)

Starting with the establishment of the Suwon (水原) Saemaul Leader (指導者) Training Institute (硏修院) on July 2, 1972 (年), various government agencies, organizations, schools (學校), factories (工場), and industrial bodies (產業體) have been implementing appropriate Saemaul education (새마을敎育). Currently (現在), there are approximately 80 educational institutions (敎育機關) nationwide, including:

1. Saemaul Leader (指導者) Training Institute (硏修院) (Suwon (水原))
2. Central (中央) Government Agency (部處) Civil Servant (公務員) Training Institutes (敎育院)
3. Metropolitan (市) and Provincial (道) Civil Servant (公務員) Training Institutes (敎育院)
4. Training Institutes (訓練院) of State-owned (國營) Enterprises (企業體) and Private (民間) Organizations (團體)
5. Provincial (道) Farmers' (農民) Training Institutes (敎育院)
6. Metropolitan (市) and Provincial (道) Agricultural Machinery (農機械) Training Institutes (訓練院)
7. Private (民間) Training Institutions (訓練機關) (Example: GaNaAn Agricultural Army (農軍) School (學校))

Looking at the practice process (實踐過程) of Saemaul education (새마을敎育), in '72 (年度), the focus was on the education (敎育) of Saemaul leaders (指導者).


--- (p. 326) ---

In 1973, the year aimed to achieve the perpetuation, scientific advancement, and technical enhancement of the Saemaul Undong (Movement). It provided spiritual education to village residents, elite education to village leaders, and technical education to field-specific guidance officers. Through extensive enlightenment and promotional activities, it widely publicized the achievements of the movement, laying the groundwork for its long-term development. Special emphasis was placed on educating women leaders, mayors, and county governors.

In 1974, Saemaul education focused on substantiating the Saemaul Undong (Movement) and scientifically and technically advancing its implementation. It aimed to support these efforts spiritually, particularly expanding and deepening the urban Saemaul Undong (Movement). This included educating urban Saemaul leaders, social leaders, high-ranking officials (central government department heads, vice ministers, university presidents, etc.), and corporate executives. The goal was to spread the mature enthusiasm of Saemaul from rural areas to cities and workplaces, encouraging voluntary and autonomous implementation of the movement in all aspects of society and work. Notably, the achievements in the field of Saemaul education in 1974 included integrating and systematizing previously scattered efforts.

In 1975, education targeted Saemaul leaders and social leaders, with various administrative agencies and organizations taking the lead. They categorized trainees by process, focusing on elite specialist education at the central level and basic course education at the local level, while guiding and implementing life education at the village level.

In 1976, the initiatives continued from 1975, with central government and provincial authorities providing elite and income-centered business education to 13,400 male and female Saemaul leaders nationwide. The content emphasized education based on the Saemaul spirit, focusing on Yu Shin (Revolution), anti-communism, production, and income increase. The approach of having all instructors and trainees live together was significantly expanded. Success case presentation meetings were held to discover and replace new figures, and post-education guidance for graduates and morale-boosting measures for Saemaul leaders were continuously developed to enhance educational effectiveness.

Furthermore, in 1976, Saemaul education and training, along with Saemaul promotion, were pursued on a nationwide scale. Efforts were made to vividly preserve and publicize the daily progress of Saemaul projects. Meanwhile, sisterhood ties among rural and fishing village Saemaul groups and volunteer activities led by university students and various organizations reinforced national unity. The 4H Club, life improvement projects, family planning, village libraries, and village banks were operated rationally, achieving the desired outcomes.


--- (p. 327) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

By the end of October 1980, the cumulative number of people who had completed Saemaul education (敎育) by target group (對象別) was as follows (Table 14): Saemaul leaders (指導者) totaled 267,000 people, while leaders (長) and vice-ministers (次官), National Assembly members (國會議員), university professors (大學敎授) (including presidents (總長)), judges and prosecutors (判檢事), lawyers, businesspeople, and leaders (長) of social (社會) organizations (團體) totaled 274,000 people. Public officials (公務員) numbered 27,000 people. Additionally, the number of people who had participated in resident (住民) education (敎育) programs, such as tree-planting teams (作目班), agricultural machinery (農機械), and farming techniques (營農技術), exceeded 68 million people.

This indicates that many individuals received multiple rounds of education (敎育) tailored to their needs (必要). Furthermore, the number of villages that conducted village-level (單位) education (敎育) for all residents (住民) in special (特殊) villages reached 1,618.
