Examining the education (敎育) situation (狀況) by regional (地域) unit (單位), central (中央) education (敎育) focused on spiritual (精神) education (敎育) for self-reliance (自立) and basic (基礎) village leaders (指導者). City (市) and provincial (道) education (敎育) centered on income-increasing (所得增大) business (事業) education (敎育) for self-help (自助) village leaders (指導者) and spiritual (精神) education (敎育) for regional (地域) social (社會) leadership (指導層) personnel (人士). City (市) and county (郡) education (敎育) involved traveling to mountainous (山間) remote areas (奧地), islands (島嶼), and backward (落後) villages (마을) to provide spiritual (精神) education (敎育) and education (敎育) related to policies (施策).

In terms of occupational (職能) education (敎育), the central (中央) government (部處) oversaw programs aimed at developing the Saemaul spirit (精神) and improving job performance (職務 能率), as well as promoting productivity (生産性) enhancement (增大) and resource (資源) conservation (節約). Starting in 1974, annual education (敎育) was provided to leaders (長) and managerial staff (幹部級) of various organizations (團體), as well as departmental (部署別) responsible parties (責任者). Notably, in 1976, the program was expanded to include working women (勤勞 女性), vocational training institute (訓練院) students (學生) and teachers (敎師), adults (成人), workers (勤勞者), women's leaders (婦女 指導者), and employees (任職員) of various organizations (各級 團體).


--- (p. 328) ---

## Attitudes Gained Through Saemaul Education by Field

Through Saemaul education, all members have acquired spiritual attitudes that can be considered as lessons. Not only in households and workplaces, but also in the development of local communities, they are making tireless efforts with dedication, which can be seen as the embodiment of the Saemaul spirit.

### (B) Promotion and Education by Social Groups

The Saemaul Undong is now developing into a nationwide movement involving all citizens, reaching every sector and stratum of society, including rural areas, cities, households, workplaces, and institutions.

However, to indicate the correct direction of the Saemaul Undong and to introduce and spread the new trends of the movement that are emerging across the country, it is necessary to awaken those who are unaware and encourage those who are aware to make further efforts. This role of promotional activities is becoming increasingly important and necessary.

Promotional activities, involving both public and private promotional agencies, have been actively engaged in evaluating and introducing the ideology and spirit of the Saemaul Undong, as well as the achievements that the rural Saemaul Undong has brought to us. This has not only contributed to the continuation of the Saemaul spirit but also stimulated awareness and efforts in the spiritual aspect of urban citizens and contributed to increasing the income of rural residents. By thoroughly disseminating technical information and successful cases of income-generating businesses, these activities have actively contributed to establishing the foundation for increasing residents' income and recognizing the necessity of national participation.

So far, Saemaul education through promotional activities has been widely implemented through TV films, radio broadcasts, newspapers, magazines, photo exhibitions, posters, Saemaul literary creation, publication of comprehensive monthly magazines, academic lectures, research paper presentation competitions, publication of research paper booklets, and other printed materials. For example, to enhance the acceptance and participation awareness of residents in rural and urban areas regarding the Saemaul Undong, Saemaul promotional materials are being distributed to places such as neighborhood associations, women's classes, Saemaul community centers, citizens' universities, senior citizens' schools, and senior citizens' community centers. Through methods such as lectures by community leaders, village leaders, Saemaul leaders, related personnel, social leaders, and other influential figures, efforts are being made to promote the cultivation of the Saemaul spirit among residents and the establishment of a healthy lifestyle.

Meanwhile, Saemaul education is no longer just education for leaders or a specific stratum of society, but it has reached a stage where it needs to develop into a nationwide education. From this perspective, the systematized Saemaul national education system has been established. According to this educational system, for the youth generation of the 10s, follow-up education after school education includes activities of the Saemaul Youth Association for learning.


--- (p. 329) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Through collective education (集團敎育), the spiritual training (精神訓練) that the new generation (世代) should possess was fostered. The 20s generation (代) received specialized agricultural technical education (營農技術敎育) as follow-up education (後縱敎育) after military education (軍敎育) to lead scientific farming (科學 營農) in the village. For the 30s generation (代), the focus was on cultivating and discovering leaders (指導者) through Saemaul elite (精銳) personnel education (敎育). For all citizens (國民) aged 40 and above, agricultural education (營農敎育) was lifeized (生活化) with village-level education (敎育) as the mainstay. This can be considered a characteristic (特徵) of the movement.

### D. Saemaul Technical Education (技術敎育)

#### (1) Significance (意義) and Necessity (必要性) of Saemaul Technical Education (技術敎育)

In the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), income-generating businesses (所得事業) are the most important aspect. If the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is a movement (運動) to live well, what does "living well" mean? It would mean having a beautiful and pleasant environment, and leading a clean and abundant life (生活). Such a rich and comfortable blessed life (福) is not just about material wealth (物質的 富) but also requires spiritual abundance (精神的 豊饒) to be achieved simultaneously. However, material wealth (物質的 富) is the source (源泉) that brings spiritual stability (精神的 安定). In the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), production (生産) and income-generating businesses (所得事業) are the very endeavors (事業) to build a rich and blessed village (福). Therefore, increasing production (生産) and income (所得) is an important prerequisite (要件) and goal (目標) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). Emphasizing the spiritual development (精神啓發) aspect and focusing on environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業) had been, in the end, a basic effort (努力) to increase production (生産) and income (所得).

No matter how much one wants to enjoy the conveniences (利器) of modern civilization (現代文明) and cultural life (文化生活), such desires (慾望) cannot be fulfilled without the necessary economic conditions (經濟的 與件). However, increasing productivity (生産性) and income (所得) cannot be achieved without introducing and applying scientific (科學的) technology (技術). In particular, in a country like Korea, where farmland (農耕地) is limited, farming scale (營農規模) is small, production infrastructure (生産基盤施設) is weak, and the distribution structure (流通構造) is not rationalized (合理化), increasing income (所得) is by no means an easy task.

Since 1974, various technical education (技術敎育) programs for increasing production and income (生產所得增大) have been urgently implemented through Saemaul education (敎育) under the banner of the income-increasing movement (所得增大運動). The reason (理由) for this is that, to sustain the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), it is extremely important not only to educate (敎育化), scientize (科學化), but also to technologize (技術化).


--- (p. 330) ---

In modern industrial society, technology is an essential requirement for comprehensive education. From this perspective, Saemaul technology education must be applied in various places, from rural and urban areas to industrial sites, factories, workplaces, and homes, ranging from simple to specialized technologies. This is an important task that cannot be overlooked. Moreover, the Saemaul income business cannot achieve its intended goals without the support of science and technology. Given our reality of promoting the mechanization of agriculture and the scientification of farming, education for the dissemination of new science and technology is an urgent matter.

## (2) Process of Practice and Dissemination

Although education for the dissemination of science and technology related to income increase is generally in a very insufficient state, the contents of practice can be roughly divided into ① agricultural technology education, ② construction technology education, ③ family planning education, ④ winter farmer education, and ⑤ other education.

### (a) Agricultural Technology Education

In the winter of 1973, utilizing the agricultural off-season, Saemaul schools were established and operated in 2,208 regions nationwide, providing education to a total of 470,000 residents on increased production techniques, sound national ethics, and rational living attitudes. In particular, during the winter off-season, the time was used for learning to improve agricultural knowledge and techniques, and idle labor was productivized to contribute to the increase of Saemaul income. Education was provided to a total of 224,000 general farmers and village guidance committee members.

In 1974, following the establishment of the Saemaul national education system, specialized agricultural technology education was provided to the 20-something age group as follow-up education to military education, to lead the scientific farming of the village. At this time, the technology education was practiced by dividing it into agricultural basic education, agricultural technology education, and specialized technology education. Agricultural basic education was carried out as short-term education for all farmers, utilizing the agricultural off-season of the village, and general agricultural techniques such as economic crop cultivation methods and special crop management methods were provided. Agricultural technology education was carried out as mid-term education at farmer education institutes, targeting diligent farmers and rural guidance personnel, and was provided according to the type of crop. Next, specialized technology education was handled by provincial farmer education institutes, targeting the core young generation of rural areas, and was provided according to the field of technology.


--- (p. 331) ---

## Chapter 4: Development of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Professional education lasting one month or more was implemented, systematizing technical education at the village→county→provincial (道) levels.

In 1976, as part of the Fishery Village Technical Guidance (漁村技術指導), Fishery Village Guidance Officers (漁村指導員) were stationed in key production areas (生產團地) focusing on aquaculture villages (養殖漁村家) under the Fishery Village Association (漁村契). Expert guidance officers were assigned to oversee specific products (品目別), promoting the scientific advancement of technical guidance. Simultaneously, efforts were strengthened to prevent disasters (災害豫防) and implement disaster management measures (防災對策). Regular technical guidance and consultations were conducted, technical journals (技術誌) were published and disseminated for research and development (硏究開發) breeds, and advancements in fishery technology (水產技術) were pursued.

The Saemaul Technical Service Corps (技術奉仕團), established in 1975 under the auspices of the Ministry of Science and Technology, aimed to disseminate scientific technology to agricultural (農) and fishery villages (漁村) and promote scientific farming (科學營農). Academics (學界) and experts (專門家) from various fields actively participated, providing essential specialized technologies (專門技術) for the Saemaul Undong (運動) and guiding construction methods (工法) for various projects (各種工事). This empowered farmers and fishermen (農漁民) with technical skills (技術能力). Notably, in 1976, the corps provided technical support (技術支援) for the comprehensive development (綜合開發) of Jeju Province (濟州道), achieving significant results. The Saemaul Technical Service Corps (技術奉仕團) was organized into central and regional units (中央及地域團), with subdivisions (分科) for different sectors (部門別) and branches (支部) in cities and provinces (市•道). They conducted systematic and flexible on-site guidance (現地指導), technical consultations (技術相談), and technical enlightenment activities (技術啓蒙活動), including lectures on home science for housewives (主婦生活科學講座). They also published technical newsletters (技術回報), disseminated information, and engaged in various volunteer activities (奉仕活動) through sisterhood ties (姉妹結緣), significantly contributing to the advancement of the Saemaul Undong (運動).

In 1974, under the auspices of the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳), 282 dedicated farmers (篤農家) received advanced agricultural technical education (營農技術敎育) to increase their income (所得增大) and promote scientific farming (科學營農), aiming to boost unit production (單位生產量). This education disseminated and expanded new, evolving technologies, enabling these farmers to act as autonomous experimental institutions (試驗機關). Additionally, 27,115 farmers (農民) received technical education (技術敎育) on agricultural machinery (農機械). The Science and Technology Service Corps (科學技術奉仕團) visited factories (工場) and businesses (企業體) nationwide, providing guidance (指導) and technical education (技術敎育) to 31,580 technicians (技術者), contributing to the enhancement of their technical skills (技術能力). Notably, from 1974 to 1976, agricultural textbooks (營農敎本) were published to increase income (所得增大) for the Saemaul Undong (運動), covering 35 types of crops, including food crops (食糧作物), horticulture (園藝), specialty crops (特用作物), and livestock (畜産), which were used for technical dissemination (技術普及).

### (b) Construction Technical Education (建設技術敎育)
To disseminate the construction technologies (建設技術) necessary for the Saemaul Undong (運動), foster autonomous construction capabilities (自主的建設能力), and ensure the solidity of construction projects (工事) for the substantive advancement of the Saemaul Undong (運動), educational measures (敎育方案) focused on technical guidance (技術指導) were implemented.


--- (p. 332) ---

Civil servants (公務員) were targeted for education (敎育) by the central government (中央), with 1,869 individuals receiving training. At the local level, a total of 28,000 villagers (住民) were educated, which contributed to the substantial progress of various Saemaul construction (建設) projects.

### (Da) Family Planning (家族計劃) Education (敎育)

Through enlightenment (啓蒙) and education (敎育) by the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs (保社部) and family planning (家族計劃) research institutes (硏究院) under each city (市), province (道), and county (郡) health center (保健所), the population growth rate (人口增加率) of our country has significantly slowed from 2.7% in the 1960s (年代) to 1.6% in the 1970s (年代). This has been reported as a substantial effect. However, Korea's (韓國) population growth rate (人口增加率) still ranks among the highest in the world. In 1978 (年), it is estimated that the population increases by approximately 579,000 people each year (每年). It is projected that by the 2000s (年代), the total population (全體人口) of our country will reach approximately 55 million to 60 million people (萬名). Consequently, food security (食糧) measures (對策) are becoming a significant issue, and the Population Policy Committee (人口政策委員會) is planning, promoting, and implementing agricultural land (農耕地) expansion (擴張) projects (事業).

In light of these national (國家的) realities (現實), the necessity (必要性) of family planning (家族計劃) projects (事業) has been reaffirmed (再認識). By disseminating (普及) knowledge (知識) about population growth (人口增加) characteristics (屬性), understanding (理解) and a sense of crisis (危機意識) have been fostered (鼓吹). Therefore, appropriate (適正) scale (規模) family planning (家族計劃) concepts (構想) are being encouraged (勸獎) and enlightened (啓蒙) for practical implementation (實踐).

### (Ra) Other (其他) Education (敎育)

Guidance (指導) on rural (農村) and urban (都市) women's (婦女子) side businesses (副業) and the dissemination (普及) of knowledge (知識) related to home economics (生活科學) have been promoted (勸獎) for direct (直接) application (應用) to daily life (生活). This has significantly influenced (影響) improvements (改善) in mental hygiene (精神衛生) management (管理), child-rearing (育兒) education (敎育), and lifestyle attitudes (生活態度).

Through various (多樣) methods (方法) such as these, Saemaul education (敎育) has been practically implemented (實踐), leading residents (住民) in rural (農村) and urban (都市) areas (地域) to recognize (認識) the legitimacy (當爲性) of the Saemaul Movement (運動). This has resulted in more proactive (積極的) participation (參與) and practical implementation (實踐), deepening (深化) the movement within daily life (生活).

Nationwide (全國的), Saemaul education (敎育) has been expanded (擴大) and implemented (實施) among various sectors (各界各層), including government (政府) agency (機關) civil servants (公務員), university professors (大學敎授), industrial bodies (產業體), journalists (言論人), businesspeople (商工人), financial professionals (金融人), social leaders (社會指導者), and students (學生). This has enabled these professionals (職場人) to identify (自身) their roles (一) within their workplaces (職場) and to take the initiative (自身) in practical implementation (實踐).

In particular, each factory (工場) has achieved improvements (提高) in quality management (品質管理), cost reduction (原價節減), labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), and employee welfare (從業員福祉). Industrial bodies (産業體) have greatly contributed (提高) to increased productivity (生産性) through unity (人和團結).


--- (p. 333) ---

# Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is also making progress in school (學校) Saemaul education (敎育). Its achievements include fostering frugality (勤儉節約) and neighborhood spirit (隣保精神), cultivating public morality (公德心), the Korean language purification movement (國語醇化運動), and patriotic activities (愛國活動) to inspire patriotism (愛國心). Through service activities (奉仕活動) and Saemaul creative works (作品) activities (活動), it has provided opportunities to contribute to urban social development (都市社會發展). In general workplaces (一般職), efforts have been made to promote resource conservation (物資節約), workplace ethics (職場倫理), and neighborhood assistance movements (運動) as central themes, fostering a trend (氣風) of voluntary (自律的) practice (實踐). In particular, in 1976, the government strongly guided the establishment of a comprehensive national participation system (總和參與體制) and distinguished between regional (地域) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) and occupational (職能) Saemaul Undong (新村運動), providing directions for practice (實踐) in each field (分野別). Additionally, model (示範) Saemaul villages (洞) and model (示範) Saemaul workplaces (職場) were actively fostered at the regional (地域) unit (單位) and various levels (各級) of occupational (職能) units (單位). At the same time, through the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Council of Private Organizations (民間團體) and regular meetings (常會), a voluntary (自律的) practice (實踐) foundation (基盤) was solidified, expanding and spreading the enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) comprehensively (全面的). This led to its development in a new dimension (次元) and hastened its institutionalization (本格化). As a result of these efforts, urban social order (都市社會秩序) is gradually improving, and the urban environment (都市環境) is becoming cleaner. Therefore, the voluntary (自律的) practice (實踐) foundation (基盤) of urban Saemaul Undong (都市新村動) is being solidified.

## 4. Saemaul Leader (指導者) Education (敎育)

### A. Saemaul Education (敎育) and Cultivation of Leadership (指導力) (培養)

For group (集團) activities (活動) to proceed in a more desirable direction (方向) and be effective (効果的), excellent qualities (資質) and leadership (指導力) of the leader (指導者) are the most important factors (要因) required, which is a well-known fact.

The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is also a group (集團) activity (活動), so for it to proceed in a desirable direction (方向) and be effectively (効果的) carried out (遂行), excellent qualities (資質) and leadership (指導力) (Leadership quality) of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) are inevitably (必然的) required.

The appropriate qualities (資質) of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) include, first, desirable values (價値觀), second, desirable social (社會) and psychological (心理的) needs (慾求), third, a firm national security perspective (國家安保觀), and fourth, moral character (道德的品性).

Desirable values (價値觀) of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) include:
① Not believing in fatalism (運命論), which holds that human lifespan (人間的壽命) or wealth and poverty (貧富) are determined by fate (運命).


--- (p. 334) ---

① A will orientation is required, which is the belief that one can carve out one's own destiny through willpower.
② A science orientation is required, which means making decisions based on rational methods rather than superstitious ones when faced with choices or making decisions.
③ A secondary group orientation is required, which means prioritizing individuals based on their abilities rather than personal relationships, even if they are strangers, to involve them in regional community development.
④ An achievement orientation is required, which means abandoning the pursuit of mere comfort and striving to complete even the most difficult tasks.
⑤ A self-assertion orientation is required, which is the belief that expressing one's own opinions openly is more appropriate than suppressing them.
⑥ A future-time orientation is required, which means pursuing future happiness rather than being satisfied with the past or present.
⑦ An equality orientation is required, which means adopting egalitarian and resident-centered thoughts and attitudes when guiding residents, rather than authoritarian ones.

Therefore, values that are unsuitable for a Saemaul leader include superstition orientation, primary-group orientation, enjoyment orientation, self-restriction orientation, and authority orientation.

The desirable socio-psychological needs of a Saemaul leader can be enumerated in various ways, but considering the essential needs required, they are roughly as follows:

① An acquisition need is required. This is the desire to accumulate property and expand business. The more a Saemaul leader has this acquisition need, the more likely it is that the Saemaul business pursued in the region will continue to expand.


--- (p. 335) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

② A recognition need is required. Recognition need is the desire to receive praise from others and the desire to become a leader. The greater the recognition need of a Saemaul leader, the more it is expected that their volunteer activities for the residents will increase.

③ An affiliation need is required. Affiliation need is the desire to cooperate with others to participate in joint projects for the local community.

④ A cognizance need is required. Cognizance need is the desire to learn and discover new facts or technologies. The greater the cognizance need of a Saemaul leader, the more likely it is that new farming methods will be introduced or created in rural areas, or new regional development plans, environmental beautification, or methods of maintaining order will emerge in urban areas.

⑤ An achievement need is required. Achievement need is the desire to overcome even the most difficult tasks and achieve them quickly. The greater this achievement need, the more diligence appears. A leader with a strong achievement need will complete one community task and immediately start another. Therefore, they must always be diligent and active.

⑥ A nurturance need is required. Nurturance need is the desire to directly or indirectly help residents in difficult situations or impoverished neighbors. The greater the nurturance need of a Saemaul leader, the more likely it is that the poverty issues in that community will be resolved.

In addition, a conservation need, the desire to protect nature and preserve cultural heritage left by ancestors, is also required of a Saemaul leader. Additionally, a construction need, the desire to build new houses, roads, bridges, public buildings, etc., is also required.

Several desires that are unsuitable for a Saemaul leader include:

① An abasement need. Abasement need is the desire to accept one's own inferiority complex, endure others' blame or scolding, and live passively in subjugation to others without actively improving the environment. In other words, it is the desire to live without agency, catering to the whims of those who are currently better off or hold higher positions than oneself.


--- (p. 336) ---

### Needs of Saemaul Leaders

1. **Achievement Need (achievement need)**. The achievement need is the desire to excel and accomplish goals. It is the drive to succeed and be recognized for one's accomplishments. A Saemaul leader with a strong achievement need can inspire and motivate the local residents to work together and achieve common goals.

2. **Aggression Need (aggression need)**. The aggression need is the desire to oppose others' wills and sometimes challenge them, aiming to harm others. If a Saemaul leader has a high aggression need, it becomes difficult for local residents to cooperate and unite.

3. **Dominance Need (dominance need)**. The dominance need is the desire to ignore others' wills and reflect only one's own will unconditionally. It is the drive to influence others' actions and sometimes control them. The more dominant a Saemaul leader is, the more the unity and cooperation among residents are disrupted.

4. **Rejection Need (rejection need)**. The rejection need is the desire to distance oneself from people or things that are opposed to or disliked by oneself. It includes the desire to withdraw from neighboring residents or the village's joint ventures that one dislikes.

Furthermore, in terms of national reality, Saemaul leaders must have a firm sense of security (安保觀) established with a sense of self-reliant national defense (自主國防觀) and a peaceful sense of unification (統一觀). Whether Saemaul leaders are rural leaders (農漁村指導者) or urban leaders (都市地域의 지도자), they must all consider connecting the activities of local residents to the national security perspective (國家安保觀). If Saemaul leaders do not have a established national security perspective (國家安保觀), it is highly likely that income-increasing projects (所得增大事業) and environmental beautification projects (環境美化事業) through the Saemaul Movement (새마을운동) will become meaningless. The establishment of a national security perspective (國家安保觀) generally correlates with the number of security education (安保敎育) credits completed, so there is a great need for Saemaul leaders to complete security education (安保敎育). Additionally, the higher the level of education (敎育水準), the more likely one is to have a strong national security awareness (國家安保意識), so this point should be considered when selecting Saemaul leaders (選擇時).

The national security perspective (國家安보觀) of Saemaul leaders is expected to influence the establishment of the national security perspective (國家安보觀) of local residents to some extent. However, the establishment of residents' national security perspective (國家安보觀) is influenced by many factors beyond the influence of Saemaul leaders' security perspective (安保觀).

Saemaul leaders are required to have moral and ethical qualities (가치관). To promote desirable changes in the moral and ethical values (價値觀) of Saemaul leaders, previous Saemaul education has emphasized honesty orientation (正直指向性). Honesty orientation is the belief that one must never deceive others or other groups to pursue the interests of oneself or one's own group. Honesty orientation is essential for small-scale communities.


--- (p. 337) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong

It is an ethical consciousness (倫理意識) required of everyone, from shop owners (主人) to high-ranking civil servants (高級公務員) responsible for major national (國家) duties (職責). Moreover, it is a value system (價値觀) particularly required of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者), who are the actual leaders (指導者) of local residents (地域住民). Generally, integrity (正直指向性) is particularly required when pursuing benefits (利益追求時). There are roughly two reasons why integrity (正直指向性) is particularly required of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者):

1. If a leader (指導者) of residents (住民) pursues personal interests (個人利益) through improper methods (不正한方法), they will immediately lose the trust (信望) they have built up from the residents (住民) and will no longer be able to fulfill their role (役割) as a leader (指導者).
2. It is due to the negative influence (惡影響) on the residents' (住民) consciousness structure (意識構造). Generally, residents (住民) consciously (意識的) or unconsciously (無意識的) imitate (模倣) the region's leader (指導者). If the leader (指導者) pursues personal interests (個人利益) through improper methods (不正한方法), a considerable number of residents (住民) will soon follow the leader's (指導者) actions (行動). For these reasons (理由), the most pressing ethical aspect (倫理面) required of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者), along with sexual morality (性道德), is perhaps integrity (正直性).

Another ethical aspect (倫理的面) strongly required of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) is the orientation towards justice (正義指向性)(justice orientation). The orientation towards justice (正義指向性) is the belief (信念) that it is more desirable to restrain (抑制) or even struggle (鬪爭) against the will (意思) of an individual (個人), leader (指導者), or group member (集團構成員) when it heads in the wrong direction (方向), rather than passively (消極的) endure (甘受) it by considering one's own interests (利害得失).

Often, when the will (意思) and actions (作動) of an individual (個人) or group (集團) do not proceed correctly, it is because they do not comply (遵守) with social norms (社會規範), or they violate (違反) sound common sense (常識) or universally accepted truths (眞理).

Therefore, Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) should not only persuade (說得) and understand (理解) residents (住民) to prevent them from committing injustices (不義), but they themselves should not compromise (妥協) with injustice (不義).

Other desirable qualities (資質) of Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) include a positive (肯定的) orientation (指向性) towards change (變化), inclusivity (包容能力), a spirit of sacrifice (犧牲精神), and smooth vertical (縱的) and horizontal (橫的) human relationships (人間關係).

The value systems (價値觀), social (社會) and psychological (心理的) needs (欲求), national security views (國家安保觀), and ethical views (倫理觀) pointed out above as necessary (必要) for Saemaul leaders (新村指導者) are mainly related to the Saemaul leaders' (新村指導者) life (人生), attitude (態度), and way of thinking (思考方式).


--- (p. 338) ---

The qualities related to education (敎育) can be established and increased through education (敎育). Therefore, when compiling an educational curriculum (敎育課程) for Saemaul leaders (指導者), the educational content (敎育內容) must be strengthened to ensure that such qualities are cultivated.

The leadership qualities (指導力)(leadership quality) of Saemaul leaders (指導者) are mainly related to their knowledge (知識) and abilities (能力). When leadership qualities (指導力) are strong, they can generally perform the following functions (機能):

1. Consulting with residents (住民) to set goals (目標) for Saemaul projects (事業) that residents (住民) can achieve on their own.
2. Encouraging residents (住民) to achieve the set goals (目標) of Saemaul projects (事業) and providing various means (手段) to do so.
3. Acting as a focal point (求心點) for residents (住民) to unite (團結) firmly.
4. Enhancing mutual interaction (相互作用) among residents (住民), such as close communication (意思疏通) and mutual support (相扶相助).

The leadership qualities (指導力) of Saemaul leaders (指導者) can also be cultivated to some extent through education (敎育). Therefore, when compiling an educational curriculum (敎育課程) for Saemaul leaders (指導者), content (內容) aimed at cultivating leadership qualities (指導力) should be included more than at present.

## II. Education (敎育) for Rural (農漁村) Saemaul Leaders (指導者)

### (1) Necessity (必要性) of Cultivating Rural (農漁村) Saemaul Leaders (指導者)

Since the Saemaul Undong (運動) in rural areas (農漁村) began in 1970, Saemaul projects (事業) have been carried out with village-level (單位) Saemaul leaders (指導者) and women leaders (婦女指導者) at the center. Therefore, the success (成功) of rural (農漁村) Saemaul projects (事業) has largely depended on the character (人格) and leadership qualities (指導力) of the village's Saemaul leaders (指導者).

As the role (役割) of Saemaul leaders (指導者) in rural areas (農漁村) has a decisive (決定的) influence on the Saemaul Undong (運動), the re-education (再敎育) of current rural (農漁村) Saemaul leaders (指導者) and the cultivation (育成敎育) of successors (後繼者) are absolutely necessary for the continued development (展開) of Saemaul projects (事業) in the present (現在) and the future (將來).

Before the Saemaul Undong (運動) began in rural areas (農漁村), diligent farmers (篤農家) played the actual (實際的) role (役割) of leaders (指導者) in their villages. In other words, they performed the role (役割) of today's Saemaul leaders (指導者). Therefore, villages with diligent farmers (篤農家) saw an increase (增大) in the overall (全體) income (所得) of the village.


--- (p. 339) ---

The village environment had also improved in a more desirable direction. However, villages without prominent farmers were always stuck in a state of stagnation. However, at the present time, every rural village has a Saemaul leader selected, and how these leaders are re-educated and how education is conducted to cultivate future successors will determine the key to the continued success of today's Saemaul Undong in rural areas.

### (2) Enhancing the Qualities of Rural Saemaul Leaders and Saemaul Education

Education to enhance the qualities and leadership of Saemaul leaders began with the "Saemaul Leader Course" at the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute, which started in July 1972. The Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute has established the following goals for Saemaul education:
1. Elite training of Saemaul Undong vanguard personnel
2. Development of self-help core movements and promotion by elite leaders

To achieve these goals, the institute has been conducting education on the following contents:
- Saemaul Leader Course (11 days; 103 hours)
  1. Cultivating Saemaul Spirit: 20 hours (20%)
  2. Saemaul Projects: 27 hours (26%)
  3. Division of Tasks and Discussion: 18 hours (17%)
  4. Field Trips and Others: 18 hours (17%)
  5. Success Cases: 14 hours (14%)
  6. National Security and Economy: 7 hours (6%)

Examining the process of delivering and acquiring such educational content, all trainees live together and engage in division of tasks and discussions in the evening to discover problems and new tasks of the Saemaul Undong, cultivate problem-solving skills, and learn communication methods. Additionally, they hear directly from Saemaul leaders with outstanding achievements about their success stories and visit villages where the Saemaul Undong is being implemented in an exemplary manner to listen to the opinions of the Saemaul leaders in those villages.

Through these educational methods, all trainees experience a heartfelt emotion and gain a firm belief in the Saemaul Undong. In other words, the education at the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute can be confidently stated as education aimed at practice.


--- (p. 340) ---

The Saemaul Undong (運動) in rural areas (農漁村) was not solely dependent on the leadership (指導力) of individual Saemaul leaders (指導者). Rather, it was the Saemaul women leaders (婦女指導者) in each village who played a crucial role in encouraging women to actively participate in the movement. Over the 10 years since the inception of the Saemaul Undong (運動), the role of these women leaders has been immense. They transformed household savings into livelihoods, scientifically advanced the rural (農漁村) way of life (衣食住), and played a decisive role in turning some idle villagers into diligent ones.

Thus, just as education (敎育) is essential for rural (農漁村) Saemaul leaders (指導者), it is equally important for Saemaul women leaders (婦女指導者). Considering this, the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute (硏修院) established a "Saemaul Women Leaders (婦女指導者) Course" and provided education (敎育) similar to that of the Saemaul Leader (指導者) Course. The main difference was that the curriculum placed less emphasis on national security (安保) and economic (經濟) issues, and instead focused more on family (家庭) matters and savings (貯蓄).

The "Saemaul Leader (指導者) Course" and "Saemaul Women Leaders (婦女指導者) Course" at the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute (硏修院) have served as models for Saemaul education (敎育) at various levels, and their teaching methods have also been emulated. Consequently, various Saemaul training institutions (硏修機關) have adjusted the curriculum of the Suwon Institute slightly to suit their needs.

Evaluating the education (敎育) of Saemaul leaders (指導者) and Saemaul women leaders (婦女指導者) to date, it is undeniable that the results have been highly successful. However, from an ethical (倫理的) perspective, the curriculum has emphasized "integrity orientation (正直指向性)" but has barely touched upon "justice orientation (正義指向性)." To foster a just (正義) and welfare-oriented (福祉) society in the future, the curriculum must incorporate content aimed at cultivating "justice orientation (正義指向性)."

### (3) Cultivating Successor Leaders (承繼指導者) in Rural Areas (農漁村)

To ensure the perpetual (永久的) continuation (存續) of the Saemaul Undong (運動), it is essential to cultivate successor Saemaul leaders (承繼指導者). This is particularly pressing in rural areas (農漁村), where the question of how to nurture future Saemaul leaders (指導者) has become a serious issue. The reason for this is that over the past 10 years, industrial (工業) cities (都市) have


--- (p. 341) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Due to the trend of rural population (農村人口) concentration in cities following rapid economic growth (高度成長), a significant number of rural youth (農村靑少年), particularly those who have received secondary education (中等敎育) or higher (以上), are leaving farming (離農). In other words, the number of potential candidates (候補者) who could become Saemaul leaders (새마을지도자) in rural and fishing villages (農漁村) is gradually decreasing.

However, from the current perspective (現 時點), if the state (國家) provides special support (特別支援) to policies (政策) such as the Saemaul Youth Association (새마을靑少年會), agricultural high schools (農業高校), and regional community development departments (地域社會開發學科) at universities (大學), the issue of cultivating future Saemaul leaders (指導者) in rural and fishing villages (農漁村) can be easily resolved (解決).

### (a) Cultivating Rural and Fishing Village (農漁村) Saemaul Leaders (指導者) through the Saemaul Youth Association (새마을靑少年會)

Despite the noticeable trend (現象) of rural youth (農村靑少年) and young adults (靑壯年) of productive age (生産齡) migrating to cities (離農), one notable fact (事實) is that approximately 38% of rural youth aged 19-24 are participating (參與) in Saemaul Youth Association (새마을靑少年會) activities (活動). An even more encouraging fact (事實) is that the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳) has been providing comprehensive elite (綜合精銳) training (訓練), including Saemaul spirit education (새마을精神敎育), scientific farming techniques (科學營農技術), and business management skills (經營技術) for agriculture (農業人), with the goal (目標) of cultivating (育成) core successors (基幹的 後繼者) who will lead (主導) the future development (農業發展) of rural agriculture (農村農業) and possess the qualities (資質) of true democratic citizens (民主國民).

Spiritual education (精神敎育) focuses on cultivating (培養) the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神), establishing a national perspective (國家觀), and physical and mental training (心身鍛鍊) and cooperative living training (協同生活訓練) to nurture (培養) the capabilities (力量) of future Saemaul leaders (後繼 新村指導者). Meanwhile, farm machinery training (農機械訓練) centers on practical training (實技實習訓練) for operating (運轉), manipulating (操作), and maintaining (整備) large agricultural machinery (大型農機械) to cultivate (育成) a workforce (役軍) for agricultural mechanization (農業機械化). Additionally, various income-generating crop (所得作目) centered scientific farming techniques (科學營農技術) and business management education (經營技術敎育) are being emphasized (注力) to cultivate (育成) new agriculturalists (새農業人) who can lead (先導) regional agricultural development (地域農業開發) as responsible agricultural entrepreneurs (擔當 企業農).


--- (p. 342) ---

Saemaul Youth (靑少年) members are undoubtedly the successors to future rural (農漁村) Saemaul leaders (指導者). While it is true that organizations such as the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農業振興廳) have been responsible for their education (敎育) and support (支援), they have not received as much attention from the government (政府) as urban youth organizations (예를 들면 한국소년소녀단(韓國少年少女團)). Just as high-ranking government officials serve as honorary presidents for the Korea Youth Association (韓國少年少女團), boosting morale (士氣振作) to the utmost, the Saemaul Youth Association (靑少年會) also deserves significant government attention and active support for its members.

Specific measures to strengthen the Saemaul Youth Association (靑少年會) include the following:

First: Expand and establish the Saemaul Youth Association (靑少年會) as the main entity (主體) for rural development (農漁村開發), and reinforce its organization (組織) and membership (會員).

Second: Significantly strengthen the active administrative (行政的) and financial (財政的) support measures from related agencies such as the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農水産部), the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部), and the Ministry of Education (文敎部).

Third: Institutional support measures (制度的) should be devised (講究) for members with outstanding abilities (能力) and a strong desire to settle in agriculture (營農定着意慾).

Fourth: Establish a comprehensive societal cooperation support system (汎社會的協力支援體制) centered around guiding agencies (指導機關), particularly strengthening private sponsorship activities (民間後援活動).

Fifth: Devise various morale-boosting measures (士氣振作對策) as spiritual rewards (精神的補償策) that instill a sense of purpose and pride (矜持) in members and respond to their activity achievements (活動業績).

### (나) Cultivating Rural Saemaul Leaders (指導者) through Agricultural High Schools (農業高校)

While the number of industrial high schools (工業高校) has increased due to heavy industrialization policies (重工業政策), the number of pure agricultural high schools (純粹農業高校) has decreased. Recently, there is even a trend of pure agricultural high schools being reorganized into comprehensive high schools (綜合高校), and this trend is growing. Examining the student increase (學生增加) from 1965 to 1978, industrial high schools (工業高校) increased by 4.5 times, humanities high schools (人文高校) by 3.3 times, while agricultural high schools (農業高校) only increased by 1.1 times. Moreover, national treasury support (國庫支援) for demonstration agricultural high schools (示範農業高校) (13 schools, based on Presidential Decree (大統領令))—established to cultivate core rural leaders (核心的農村指導者)—is too insufficient. This point requires government reconsideration (政府的再考).

However, examining the Ministry of Education's (文敎部) cultivation plan (育成方案) for 60 pure agricultural high schools (純粹農業高校) until 1981, there are very encouraging aspects.

First: Fully provide experimental and practical facilities (實驗實習施設) at 100%, with the required amount (所要額) fully covered by national treasury expenses (國庫負擔).


--- (p. 343) ---

# Chapter 4 (第4章) Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

Firstly, revise the curriculum for agricultural education (農業敎育) to focus on practical training (實習);
Secondly, expand scholarship (獎學金) provisions to attract outstanding students (優秀學生);
Thirdly, plan to increase practical training fees (實習費) and raise allowances for practical education teachers (實科敎員);
Fourthly, provide special support funds (特別支援金) to graduates (卒業) who return to farming (歸農定着者) after graduation (卒業);
Fifthly, plan to increase practical training fees (實習費) and raise allowances for practical education teachers (實科敎員).

The aspect related to cultivating future rural (農村) Saemaul Undong (運動) leaders (指導者) is the provision of special support funds (特別支援金) to graduates (卒業) who return to farming (歸農定着者) after graduation (卒業).

It seems reasonable to view students (學生) planning to settle in agriculture (營農定着) among agricultural high school (農業高校) graduates (卒業豫定者) as future successors (承繼者) of rural (農村) Saemaul Undong (運動) leaders (指導者) and provide various supports (支援) to them. To strengthen their willingness to engage in agriculture (營農意欲) and their determination to become future Saemaul Undong (運動) leaders (指導者), it would be a good measure to have them undergo practical training (實習) as candidate leaders (候補生) from the second semester of their third year (學年).

(d) Cultivating Rural (農漁村) Saemaul Undong (運動) Leaders (指導者) through University (大學) Regional Community Development (地域社會開發學科) Majors

Currently (現在), our country has departments of community development (Department of community development) and regional development (Department of regional development) in several universities (大學) and graduate schools (大學院). The department of community development (地域社會開發學科) is established in 5 universities (個校), and the regional development (地域開發學科) is established in 2 universities (個校). The purpose of their establishment (設置目的) is to cultivate core (核心的) leaders (指導者) for regional community development (地域社會開發). In other words, the purpose of their establishment (設置目的) is to cultivate capable (能力) mid-level (中堅幹部) leaders (指導者) with both theoretical (理論) and practical (經驗) knowledge in regional community development (地域社會開發). Therefore, graduates (卒業者) from university (大學) and graduate school (大學院) departments of community development (地域社會開發學科) should be selected (選定) not as local (現地) village leaders (指導者) in rural areas (農漁村), but as mid-level (中堅幹部) officials in regional community development (地域社會開發) tasks (業務) at the county (郡), provincial (道), or central government (中央部處) level. To cultivate competent (有能) professionals (專門人) who can oversee (主管) regional community development (地域社會開發) tasks (業務), the educational direction (敎育方向) of the department of community development (地域社會開發學科) should be set (設定) as follows.

Firstly, focus on cultivating leaders (指導者養成) for multifaceted (多面的) regional community development (地域社會開發);
Secondly, cultivate not only theoretical (理論習得) knowledge but also practical (實踐能力) skills in regional community development (地域社會開發);
Thirdly, establish (定立) the theory (理論) of regional community development (地域社會開發) on a multidisciplinary (多學問的) foundation (基礎) to integrate (統合) aspects such as spiritual development (精神啓發), economic development (經濟開發), and social development (社會開發).

d. Education (敎育) of Saemaul Undong (運動) Leaders (指導者) in Urban (都市) Areas (地域單位)


--- (p. 344) ---

## (1) Necessity of Cultivating Urban Unit Saemaul Leaders

The Saemaul Undong in rural areas began in 1970, while the urban Saemaul Undong started later in 1973. Like the rural Saemaul Undong, the urban movement emphasized the spiritual reform of residents. The results included Saemaul cleaning, the enhancement of merchants' business ethics, urban greening, the establishment of Saemaul savings banks, the improvement of alleys, the citizen order movement, the operation of neighborhood associations, the frugal consumption movement, and the civil service reform movement. It cannot be denied that a significant portion of urban residents have acquired desirable consciousness structures as a major achievement of the urban Saemaul Undong.

Currently, urban unit Saemaul leaders are selected per neighborhood (tong) as Saemaul leaders and women Saemaul leaders. However, it seems that neighborhood unit Saemaul leaders have not actively led residents and developed the Saemaul Undong like village unit Saemaul leaders in rural areas. In fact, administrative agencies above the neighborhood level have mainly led the urban Saemaul Undong.

This phenomenon is partly due to the characteristics of cities, but there are also issues with the qualifications and leadership of urban Saemaul leaders. Generally, the educational level of urban Saemaul leaders is lower than or equal to the average educational level of residents. To develop the urban Saemaul Undong, centered around urban Saemaul leaders like in rural areas, there should be a reconsideration of the educational qualifications of urban Saemaul leaders during their selection. Given the current qualifications and leadership of urban Saemaul leaders, they should be required to complete more Saemaul education courses.

## (2) Contents of Urban Saemaul Leader Education

Various private organizations and civil servant training institutes have created "Urban Saemaul Leader Courses" based on the "Saemaul Leader Course" model from the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute, with slight modifications for each institution.

Taking the example of the Seoul Metropolitan Government Civil Servant Training Institute, the "Urban Saemaul Leader Course" is composed of the following contents:

* Urban Saemaul Leader Course (Seoul Metropolitan Government Civil Servant Training Institute)
  * Total: 58 hours (100%)
  * ① Saemaul Spirit: 16 hours (28%)


--- (p. 345) ---

## Chapter 4: Development Process of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

② National Spirit (國民精神): 11 hours (時間) (19%)
③ National Security and Unification (統一安保): 4 hours (時間) (7%)
④ Reform of Public Affairs (庶政刷新): 2 hours (時間) (3%)
⑤ Nature Conservation (自然保護): 2 hours (時間) (3%)
⑥ Task Discussion (分任討議): 10 hours (時間) (17%)
⑦ Village Treasury (金庫): 1 hour (時間) (2%)
⑧ Others (其他): 12 hours (時間) (21%)

It can be seen that the education content emphasizes the Saemaul spirit (精神) and National Spirit (國民精神) as the main focus. As such, the emphasis on education content for spiritual reform (精神改革) has led to a positive change in the consciousness structure (意識構造) of many urban (都市) Saemaul leaders (指導者) in a desirable direction.

However, even though the urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動) should also be a practice-oriented (實踐爲主) movement, it is less practical compared to rural (農村) areas, which must have its reasons. A detailed analysis of the Seoul Metropolitan City (서울特別市) Saemaul Leader Training Course (指導者課程) reveals a significant difference in the number of hours spent on theoretical lectures (理論講義時間數) versus practical training (實習時間數). The ratio of theoretical lecture hours (理論講義時間數) to practical training hours (實習時間數) is approximately 67% to 33%. From the perspective of educational effectiveness (教育效果面), practical training (實習) and on-site education (現場教育) such as Saemaul on-site observation (現場見學), Saemaul volunteer work (勞力奉仕), and basic security training (安保基礎訓練) should be expanded. Additionally, more time should be allocated for task discussion (分任討議). Conversely, the number of hours spent on theoretical lectures (理論講義時間數) should be reduced. By doing so, it is believed that the practical abilities (實踐力) of urban (都市) Saemaul leaders (指導者) can be enhanced.

### (3) Cultivating Successors (承繼) for Urban Units (都市地域單位)

Cultivating successors (後繼者) for urban (都市) Saemaul leaders (指導者) is a much more challenging task compared to rural (農村) areas. Even now, there are regions (地域) where the head of the neighborhood (통리) also serves as the Saemaul leader (指導者), indicating the inherent difficulties in cultivating urban (都市) Saemaul leaders (指導者). However, to cultivate future urban (都市) Saemaul leaders (指導者), residents (住民) with an education level (學力) equivalent to or higher than the average, preferably university graduates (大學卒業者) who live an independent life (自營生活) and have a keen interest in regional development (地域開發), should be selected, ideally two per region. These individuals should be arranged to receive education (教育) at various levels of Saemaul educational institutions (教育機關). Of course, they should be awarded a certificate of completion (履修證) for the Saemaul Leader Training Course (指導者課程), and currently,


--- (p. 346) ---

All benefits (恵澤) given to the Saemaul leaders (指導者) in the village should be provided to them as well. On the other hand, they should often be informed of the municipal (市政) situation (狀況) to stimulate their willingness (意欲) to participate in municipal (市政) affairs (參與). Through such a process (過程), it is expected that those elected as Saemaul leaders (指導者) will excellently perform their duties (業務).

### 라. Factory (工場) Saemaul Leader (指導者) Education (敎育)

#### (1) Necessity (必要性) of Cultivating (育成) Factory (工場) Saemaul Leaders (指導者)

The Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) began after the oil shock in 1973. The direction (方向) of the Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) is to improve labor-management (勞使) relations (關係) so that business owners (企業主) make their utmost efforts (努力) to enhance the welfare (福祉) of workers (勤勞者), and workers (勤勞者) make their utmost efforts (努力) to reduce costs (原價) and improve productivity (生產性). After the Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) was launched, welfare facilities (福祉厚生施設) for workers (勤勞者) have been significantly expanded. Dormitories (寄宿舍), company housing (舍宅), medical facilities (醫療施設), cafeterias (食堂), bathhouses (沐浴湯), and rest rooms (休憇室) have continued to be expanded despite recent difficult economic conditions (經濟與件).

The reason why the Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) has achieved such remarkable results (成果) is believed to be due to the Saemaul education (敎育) for Factory Saemaul leaders (指導者) and group leaders (分任組長).

Factory Saemaul education (敎育) was primarily conducted by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) at the designated First Factory Saemaul Training Institute (硏修院) and Second Factory Saemaul Training Institute (硏修院) for representatives (代表者), executives (任員), and managers (幹部) of companies (企業). In addition, group leaders (分任組長) and general employees (一般 社員) completed Saemaul education (敎育) at one of the 10 private training institutes (民間 硏修院), including the Canaan Agricultural and Military School (農軍學校). Meanwhile, 21 factories (工場) have established their own training institutes (自體 附設 硏修院) and are providing the same Saemaul education (敎育) as regular training institutes (正規 硏修院) to workers (勤勞者) and general employees (一般 社員).

Currently (現在), Factory Saemaul leaders (指導者) are mostly selected from among executives (任員), managers (幹部), and employees (社員) of companies (企業體) as well as group leaders (分任組長). They carry out the Saemaul Movement (運動) in consultation (協議) with each group member (分任組員). It is a well-known fact (事實) that the success (成果) of the Factory Saemaul Movement (運動) is determined by the leadership (指導力) of the Saemaul leaders (指導者). Therefore, the necessity (必要性) of Saemaul education (敎育) to improve the qualifications (資質) and leadership (指導力) of Factory Saemaul leaders (指導者) is gradually increasing.

#### (2) Contents (內容) of Factory (工場) Saemaul Leader (指導者) Education (敎育)

Looking at the contents (內容) of Factory Saemaul education (敎育), they differ from those of rural (農漁村) Saemaul leader (指導者) education (敎育).


--- (p. 347) ---

A point (點) is discovered. In factory Saemaul education (工場 새마을敎育), the focus is on teaching the Saemaul Undong (運動) in factories, economic realities (經濟現實), and tasks (課題).

The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) has compiled a model (模型) for factory Saemaul education (工場 새마을敎育), which is roughly as follows:

## Factory Saemaul Education (工場 새마을敎育) Content (內容) (Leader Training Course (指導者班))

(Total) 50 hours (時間) (100%)
1. Cultivating the Saemaul Spirit (精神) : 5 hours (時間) (10%)
2. International Situation (國際情勢) and National Security (國家安保) : 5 hours (時間) (10%)
3. Economic Situation (經濟現況) and Tasks (課題) : 10 hours (時間) (20%)
4. Saemaul Undong (運動) in Factories : 9 hours (時間) (18%)
5. Success Stories (成功事例) : 8 hours (時間) (16%)
6. Division of Tasks and Discussion (分任討議) : 10 hours (時間) (20%)
7. Life Education (敎養) : 3 hours (時間) (6%)

The content (內容) of factory Saemaul education (工場 새마을敎育) proposed by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) aligns with the actual (實際) implementation (展開) of factory Saemaul projects (工場 새마을事業). It encompasses issues such as improving productivity (生産性), reducing costs (原價), savings (貯蓄), labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), environmental cleanup (環境淨化), and welfare (福祉) of workers (勤勞者).

In implementing (實施) Saemaul education (敎育) for factory Saemaul leaders (工場 새마을指導者), a policy consideration (政策的考慮) is necessary. Previously, the trainees (被敎育者) themselves bore the expenses (經費) for the education (敎育) of factory Saemaul leaders (工場 새마을指導者). However, since the second half of 1970 (年), the government (政府) has been covering half (半) of the costs (負擔). Nevertheless, as Saemaul education (敎育) instills a sense of mission (使命感) in the trainees (被敎育者) as Saemaul leaders (指導者), it is reasonable to think that the state (國家) should fully support (支援) the entire cost (全額). In such cases, it is expected (豫想) that the educational outcomes (成果) will be higher.

### (3) Cultivating Successor Leaders (後繼指導者) for Factory Saemaul (工場 새마을)

It is desirable (思慮) that factory Saemaul leaders (工場 새마을指導者) are appointed (選任) from both the management side (經營者側) and the labor side (勤勞者側). However, many companies (企業體) still only select Saemaul leaders (指導者) from the management side (經營者側). Such companies (企業體) should quickly select individuals with leadership skills (指導力) from among the division leaders (分任組長) as Saemaul leaders (指導者). In general (大槪), the general affairs manager (總務課長) or the general affairs director (總務部長) is appointed (選任) as the Saemaul leader (指導者) from the management side (經營者側), and this point (點) should also be considered.


--- (p. 348) ---

Reconsideration is necessary. Rather than limiting the selection to the General Affairs Section Chief (總務課長) or General Affairs Department Head (總務部長), it is more appropriate to appoint someone who understands the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), actively supports it, and has strong leadership skills from among the executives or senior employees.

The achievements of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) in factories also seem to depend significantly on the abilities and efforts of the Saemaul leaders (指導者) in those factories, which is not an overstatement. Therefore, the issue of cultivating both management-side and labor-side Saemaul leaders (指導者) is of great importance. To cultivate management-side Saemaul leaders (指導者), junior employees with leadership potential should be selected and given regular Saemaul education (新村敎育) training. Similarly, to cultivate labor-side Saemaul leaders (指導者), members of division teams with strong leadership skills should be selected to receive focused Saemaul education (新村敎育).

## 5. Prospects for Saemaul Education (新村敎育)

Through the above process, we have reviewed the development of Saemaul education (新村敎育) by examining its concept (槪念) and essence (本質), content (內容) and methods (方法), actual implementation (實際), and various aspects of leader cultivation education (養成敎育). Based on the issues identified through this work, we will now discuss the prospects for Saemaul education (新村敎育).

First, considering the positive aspects that should be continued:

Firstly, Saemaul education (新村敎육) has been attempted as a structural (構造的) change targeting the entire society (全社會), which was very effective. It is impossible to achieve the desired results by educating only specific occupations (職種), genders (性別), age groups (年齡別), classes (階層別), or regions (地域). Therefore, it should continue to be promoted in a comprehensive (汎) manner across society (社會), regions (地域), classes (階層), and time (時間).

Secondly, Saemaul education (新村敎육) has rightly focused on spiritual education (精神敎育) as its core, aiming for a revolution in human consciousness (意識革命). Politics (政治), economy (經濟), national defense (國防), and culture (文化) are all closely tied to human spiritual attitudes (精神的姿勢). It is essential to emphasize a firm sense of national identity (國家觀), security (安保觀), localization of democracy (民主主義), subjective historical consciousness (歷史意識), national ethical consciousness (國民倫理意識), and community consciousness (共同體意識). This is a top priority (至上命令) for our reality, and it is urgently necessary to continue and strengthen these efforts.

Thirdly, Saemaul education (新村敎육) has been developed based on the foundation of practical philosophy (實踐哲學), and this should not be interrupted.


--- (p. 349) ---

## Chapter 4: The Development of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It will not work. Strengthening national power (國力强化) must, of course, be considered from material (物質的), institutional (制度的), and facility (施設的) aspects. However, if the nation (國民) lacks a strong willpower (意志力) toward practice (實踐), it will be of no use. Historically (歷史的), empty theories (空理空論) have been a major reason why our Korean society (韓國社會) has not been able to overcome poverty for a long time. While intellectual power (知力) of the nation (國民) is necessary for strengthening national power (國力强化), if the will (意志) to practice (實踐) does not follow, it becomes useless. True national power (國力) can only be strengthened by the willpower (意志力) of the nation (國民) filled with passion (熱意).

Fourthly, the direction of conducting technical education (技術敎育) in parallel with spiritual education (精神敎育) should be maintained in the future. To improve the national economy (國民經濟) and strengthen national defense (國防力) in the rapidly changing era of technological innovation (技術革新), the introduction (導入) and dissemination (普及) of advanced global technologies (先進技術) from a scientific (科學的) perspective is an essential requirement (必須要件). Continuous promotion (推進) of technical education (技術敎育) along with spiritual education (精神敎育) is necessary (必要). Therefore, it is desirable to gradually integrate and promote Saemaul education (새마을敎育) with vocational education (職務敎育) in the future. In particular, education (敎育) for leaders (指導者) and future leaders (後繼指導者) is a crucial task (課題) that should not be overlooked (度外視).

The Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is unfolding as a nationwide ethical movement (全國民的倫理運動). Its ultimate goal (窮極目的) is to establish a well-off society (社會) by rectifying the ethical (倫理的) discipline (紀綱) of our society (社會). It is not just about living well, but about living well in a righteous (正當) and just manner (正義). Without this, we cannot achieve a welfare-oriented (福祉) and just (正義) new society (社會). While Korea (韓國) has achieved many learning effects (學習效果) during the grand implementation of Saemaul education (새마을敎育), there are still some aspects that require partial improvement (改善). Let us reflect (反省) on a few of these points.

Firstly, education (敎育) should not be merely formalistic (形式化) and demonstrative (展示的). As seen before, despite the immense investment (投資) made by almost the entire nation (全國民) in Saemaul education (새마을敎育), the recent revelation of enormous social corruption (社會腐敗相) is clear evidence that the education (敎育) has not truly been internalized (內實化). Of course, education (敎育) is not something that can yield results (成果) overnight (一朝一夕). It is a sustained endeavor (永續事業) that must be carried out persistently (遂行). Do not despair (落心); we need a stronger will (意志) for education (敎育).

Secondly, the most powerful method (方法) in education (敎育) is the demonstration (示範) by the educator (敎育者). When Saemaul education (새마을敎育) is considered a nationwide (全國家的) scale of social education (社會敎育) or lifelong education (平生敎育), the upper echelons (上層) and leadership strata (指導階層) of society (社會)


--- (p. 350) ---

People must never forget that the exemplary conduct of leaders is the most effective educational method. Mouthing slogans like anti-communism (승공), total security (총력안보), and national unity (국민총화) while actions lead to defeat of communism (패공), weakened security (안보약화), and national division is a direction that the upper echelons of society and leading figures cannot afford to take. Those who cannot expand the criteria for happiness from their own homes and families to the nation and its people should not be involved in national education. Social distrust stems from broken promises. A profound reflection from leaders at all levels is urgently needed.

Thirdly, Saemaul education must be carried out for the improvement of the welfare of all citizens and the eternal prosperity of the nation, and thus requires a commitment to sustainability. It must be emphasized that this is by no means education for a specific regime or political faction. In modern nations, the declaration that education is politically neutral is an eternal effort to establish the true face of education, which must always be for the people. The method for sustainability lies in democratization. While most policy-making originates from the government, for a project to become sustainable, it must be internalized through the democratization process to the life goals of all citizens.

The necessity of government-led initiatives in the ignition stage is inevitable in any newly developing country. However, once the project reaches a certain level and enters the development stage, it is desirable to shift to a private-sector-led approach. Therefore, authorities should focus more on providing direction, information, and financial support rather than command and control.

Fourthly, the curriculum and methods should move away from uniformity and towards diversification. The unique needs of different occupations and workplaces should be respected and reflected, and varying the content and methods of education according to the target audience will enhance effectiveness.

For example, diversifying the selection of success story protagonists can help them focus on their duties and raise awareness among the learners. Similarly, diversifying lecturers can expand the participation of intellectuals.

Fifthly, methods for education evaluation and follow-up guidance need further research. While the quantity may have been high, the qualitative internalization and sustained effects still require continuous post-education guidance and


--- (p. 351) ---

The development of appropriate educational evaluation methods is essential for this task, and the cooperation of experts in this field is urgently needed.

As seen above, Saemaul education has brought about tremendous spiritual changes over the past decade, has greatly contributed to fostering the will to live and national vitality, and has played a significant role in providing an important opportunity in Korean history. In the 1980s, as we enter a new era, we must continue to advance by supplementing and correcting what we have learned from past experiences. Our future will be full of hope if we do so.

Based on our efforts so far, further progress must be made.
