# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

## Section 1: Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Production Base Development Projects

### 1. Overview of Production Base Development Projects

The ultimate goal of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is to improve the quality of life through increased agricultural and fisheries productivity, higher incomes for farmers and fishermen, and enhanced cultural and welfare standards. Therefore, it is only natural that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) aims to establish, improve, and expand modern production methods and production base development projects to increase income.

Production base development projects vary in type and content depending on the target project and its specifics. They also differ in nature from individual environmental improvement projects or fragmented production projects in terms of scale and investment. In the initial stages of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the focus was on improving the living environment by prioritizing environmental improvements. However, since 1974, the emphasis has shifted to expanding production base development projects beyond the village level to the surrounding village area. As a result, the scope, content, and scale of these projects have gradually expanded, and they have evolved into Saemaul cooperative circle projects where villages cooperate with each other. Consequently, residents' awareness of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has shifted towards a more macroscopic, long-term, and future-oriented direction. The content and quality of promoting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) have also become more scientific, progressive, and bold, demonstrating a strong will and ambition.

### Ga. Agricultural Production Base Development Projects

One of the main reasons why our rural agricultural and fishing villages have not been able to overcome their backwardness is the lack of production bases, which has constrained production activities and kept productivity at a low level.

Therefore, the establishment of production bases for agriculture and fisheries is an important and urgent prerequisite for promoting the modernization of rural agricultural and fishing villages.


--- (p. 354) ---

Securing the necessary farmland (農耕地) and developing safe water sources (用水源) for it, as well as establishing a stable agricultural base (安定營農基盤) through land consolidation (耕地整理) and drainage improvement (排水改善), are prerequisites for ensuring a stable food supply (食糧).

Agricultural production infrastructure projects (農業生產基盤造成事業) aim to increase production per unit of farmland (農耕地), supplement insufficient labor (勞動力) through labor-saving measures (省力化作業), and improve agricultural productivity (農業生產性) by rationalizing management (經營合理化). These efforts and cost savings contribute to production and stimulate the motivation for expanded agricultural reproduction (擴大再生產).

However, such agricultural production infrastructure projects (農業生產基盤造成事業) cannot be achieved through the individual efforts (努力) or financial resources (財力) of farmers (農民) alone, requiring active government (政府) support and investment (投資).

Therefore, the government (政府) has consistently focused efforts (努力) on various sectors (分野別), considering the effects (效果) and nature (性格) of these projects. While the implementation of agricultural water development projects (農業用水開發事業) for water management (管理) has annually improved the water safety rate (水利安全率), efforts have also been made to promote agricultural mechanization (農業機械化) to address increased water usage per unit (單位用水量) due to rice variety improvement (品種改良) and time-limited farming (時限營農), as well as the decreasing trend (減少趨勢) in rural labor (農村勞動力) due to industrialization (工業化).

In particular, since the early 1970s, as part of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), the government (政府) and farmers (農民) have jointly expanded and promoted simple water development projects (用水開發事業) such as tube wells (管井), underground drainage ditches (集水暗渠), waterways (導水路), dikes, and pumping stations (揚水場). These efforts have significantly contributed to establishing the self-sufficiency base (自給基盤) for staple crops (主穀) like rice and barley since the mid-1970s.

The government's (政府) agricultural production infrastructure projects (農業生產基盤造成事業) have focused on:
1. Agricultural water development projects (農業用水開發事業) to overcome natural disasters (自然災害),
2. Large-scale comprehensive agricultural development projects (農業綜合開發事業) centered around the four major rivers (4大江),
3. Land consolidation projects (耕地整理事業) and drainage improvement projects (排水改善事業) to promote agricultural mechanization (農業機械化),
4. Preventing the conversion (轉用) of farmland (農耕地) to other purposes (他目的) due to urbanization (都市化) and industrialization (工業化), and expanding farmland (農地) through reclamation (開墾) and landfill (干拓).

As of the end of 1978, the nation's (全國) agricultural water facilities (農業用水施設) totaled 72,000 sites (個所) with a beneficiary area (蒙利面積) of 1,312,000 towns and steps (町步), covering 85% of the total. Among these facilities, reservoirs (貯水池) numbered 18,000 sites (個所) with a beneficiary area (蒙利面積) of 591,000 towns and steps (町步), accounting for 52.7%. Next were pumping stations (揚水場) with 3,068 sites (個所) and a beneficiary area (蒙利面積) of 131,000 towns and steps (町步), making up 11.7%, followed by dikes with 18,000 sites (個所) and a beneficiary area (蒙利面積) of 129,000 towns and steps (町步), comprising 11.5%.


--- (p. 355) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The large-scale agricultural integrated development project (農業綜合開發事業) had completed the first phase (1段階) of the Geumgang (錦江), Pyeongtaek (平澤), Gyeongju (慶州), Gyehwa Island (界火島), and Yeongsan River (榮山江) projects by the end of 1979. A total of 153.9 billion won was invested, developing 69,000 jeongbo (町步). As a result of this completion, 11,000 jeongbo of new farmland was expanded, and land consolidation (耕地整理) was carried out on 23,000 jeongbo. Consequently, 82,000 jeongbo of rice paddies received agricultural water supply, leading to a food production increase effect of 135,000 tons.

This also brought about improvements in the cropping system (作付體系) and changes in agricultural production technology structure (農業生產技術構造). Indirect effects included changes in farmers' consciousness structure (意識構造變化) and the establishment of proactive and scientific farming attitudes (營農姿勢). Furthermore, it served as an opportunity to develop and activate the region's human (人的) and material (物的) resources, promoting the advancement of rural urbanization (都市化) and achieving results in regional tourism development (地域觀光).

The land consolidation project (耕地整理事業) invested a total of 103.5 billion won over 8 years, from 1972 to 1979, developing 173,000 jeongbo anew. It completed land consolidation on 322,000 jeongbo, which corresponds to 54.8% of the target area of 588,000 jeongbo.

The direct results of such land consolidation projects include increased productivity due to improved land use efficiency (土地利用度) and reduced production costs due to decreased labor input (勞動力投下量). Indirect effects include increased non-farm income (農外所得) due to wage increases (賃金) during the construction period (工事期間), preservation of farmland (農耕地), and visual effects, among other ripple effects (波及效果).

## B. Fishery Production Base Construction (漁業生産基盤造成事業)

Our country's fishing villages (漁村) had been almost defenseless (無防備) against frequent natural disasters (自然的災難), accepting poverty as an inevitable fate (宿命) and spending years in resignation (體념). This was largely due to the lack of fishery production bases (漁業生産基盤) such as ports and fishing vessels.

However, the Saemaul Undong in fishing villages (漁村新村運動) has overcome resignation (體念) and inspired courage to challenge the sea, building on the traditional spirit of mutual aid (相扶相助) that has been passed down since ancient times (古來).

Fishery (漁業) projects in fishing villages (漁村) through the Saemaul Undong are conveniently divided into four categories: production base (生産基盤), income increase (所得增大), welfare environment (福祉環境), and spiritual development (精神啓發). Among these, the production base category (生産基盤部門) includes three projects: Saemaul fishing port construction (漁港修築), cooperative fishing vessel construction (協同漁船建造), and fishing village cooperative base facilities (漁村契基盤施設).


--- (p. 356) ---

Since the inception of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) for fishing villages in 1972 until 1979, a total of 25.9 billion won was invested in this project, including subsidies, loans, and self-funding. Of this amount, 16.2 billion won (63%) was allocated to the income enhancement sector, while 5 billion won (19%) was invested in the production infrastructure sector.

Fishing ports are essential elements for the safety and protection of fishing boats and for the handling of catches, playing a crucial role in fisheries production. In our country, there are 1,398 small-scale, non-designated fishing ports primarily used by coastal fishermen.

By linking these fishing ports in remote islands and coastal areas with the Saemaul Undong for fishing villages, efforts have been made to improve the basic facilities of fishing ports, albeit centered around piers.

The Saemaul Fishing Port Construction Project, which began in 1975 and continued until 1979, constructed a total of 9,368 meters of fishing port facilities.

The cooperative fishing boat construction project, aimed at enhancing fishermen's income, providing basic equipment, and fulfilling fishermen's long-standing desire for jointly constructing and operating fishing boats, has resulted in the construction of 869 cooperative fishing boats from 1973 to 1979. This has laid the foundation for increasing fishermen's income.

The production infrastructure projects for fishing villages, overseen by the Fisheries Cooperatives, include the repair and improvement of basic facilities such as piers and landing sites, as well as the construction of simple processing plants, simple fishing boat repair shops, and other production infrastructure for fishing villages.

From 1972 to 1979, a total of 1.6 billion won was invested in these projects, resulting in the construction of 418 piers, 114 breakwaters, 66 cargo handling sites, 75 simple processing plants, 43 breakwaters, 36 consignment sites, and 114 other facilities, totaling 868 projects.

Other projects that can be included in the category of fisheries production base construction include auxiliary facilities, joint fishing ground resource creation, remote island and coastal fishing village development projects, and pier construction projects as part of the Saemaul beautification projects overseen by the Ministry of Home Affairs, which are currently conveniently included in the income enhancement project sector.

Projects for auxiliary facilities such as fishing ground management boats, transport boats, and joint warehouses have seen a total investment of 2 billion won by 1979, resulting in the completion of 1,005 projects. Joint fishing ground resource creation projects, using methods such as seed shell broadcasting, stone casting, artificial fish reefs, and rock blasting, have resulted in a total of 11,778 townships by the end of 1979.


--- (p. 357) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

The Saemaul Undong (新村運動) has achieved remarkable results.
Development projects in remote islands and rural areas, as well as the Saemaul beautification projects, have yielded significant outcomes.

## B. Saemaul Beautification Projects

The Saemaul beautification projects are one of the fundamental initiatives of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動), divided into sub-projects aimed at creating a production base, increasing income, and improving the village environment.

Among these, the Saemaul beautification projects related to agricultural production base creation include the construction of communal composting sites (共同堆肥場), communal workspaces (共同作業場), communal livestock barns (共同畜舍), and warehouses (倉庫), as well as the improvement and maintenance of small streams (小河川), and the expansion of village bridges (橋梁) and roads.

The Saemaul beautification projects prioritize starting with small-scale, easy-to-implement tasks, focusing on communal interests of village residents that are difficult to achieve individually and directly tied to the communal benefits and long-standing aspirations of the village.

To prevent soil degradation (地力減退), organic fertilizers (有機肥料) must be abundantly applied, which necessitates continuous compost production (堆肥增產). However, as rural labor becomes scarce and household environments are organized through village structure improvement projects (聚落構造改善事業), compost production has declined. Therefore, communal composting sites (共同堆肥場) were established to encourage communal collection and boost residents' motivation for compost production.

Alongside the establishment of communal composting sites (共同堆肥場), communal workspaces (共同作業場) were set up at the village level to maximize economies of scale and achieve multifaceted effects.

In a small-scale farming system like that of Korea, communal work is actively encouraged to overcome the issue of excessive costs due to the small scale of operations.

Moreover, in an era when agriculture faces challenges both domestically and internationally, it is imperative to pursue economies of scale through communal work to avoid relying solely on increasing agricultural product prices under the small-scale farming management system.

To reduce the inefficiency of small-scale sideline livestock farming (畜産), which has a long history, and to facilitate labor savings, technology introduction, and disease prevention, the Saemaul beautification projects include the construction of communal livestock barns (共同畜舍).

Furthermore, as villages require storage and management of purchased production materials and government-purchased grains, residents are encouraged to collectively build warehouses (倉庫) as part of the Saemaul beautification projects.


--- (p. 358) ---

In rural (農村) living environments (生活環境) and production activities (生產活動), small streams (小河川) play a very important (重要한) role (役割) at times and can also cause damage (被害). For the cultivation (栽培) of crops (農作物), irrigation water (灌漑水) is essential, but if the management (管理) of small streams (小河川) is neglected, it can cause water damage (水害) to farmland (耕作地) and houses (家屋). Therefore, it is impossible for residents (住民) not to be sensitive to the interests (利害關係), and thus, the improvement (改補修) of small streams (小河川) also occupies a significant (比重) position and weight (位置) in the Saemaul beautification projects (事業).

Road expansion (道路擴張) is more important than anything else in helping economic activities (經濟活動) for production (生產) and distribution (流通) to be carried out efficiently (效率的).

Therefore, the government (政府) included bridge (橋梁) and village road expansion projects (擴張事業) as one of the key projects (重點事業) in the early (初期) stages of the Saemaul beautification projects (事業).

### La. Saemaul Cooperative Circle (協同圈) Projects (事業)

Cooperative circle (協同圈) development projects (開發事業) refer to projects (事業) where residents (住民) of different villages (部落) jointly (共同) develop (開發) the living environment (生活環境), production base (生產基盤), and specialized (特化) crops (作目) of villages (마을). Projects (事業) related (關聯) to the creation (造成) of production bases (生產基盤) include road construction (道路開設) and bridge construction (橋梁架設), stream (河川) management (管理), and the installation (設置) of joint (共同) warehouses (倉庫) and joint (共同) workplaces (作業場), etc.

In the early (初期) stages (段階) of the Saemaul Movement (運動), small projects (事業) were promoted (推進) one by one, taking a natural (自然) village (部落) as a unit (單位). As a result, most (大部分) of the basic environmental (基礎環境) improvement projects (改善事業) and production base (生產基盤) creation projects (造成事業) at the village (마을) level yielded (期待) effects (效果) beyond expectations (以上). Based on the experience (經驗) and motivation (意慾) gained from this, they began (始作) to tackle (着手) long-standing projects (宿願事業) between villages (마을간).

While Saemaul beautification projects (事業) target (對象) the 1st (次) living circle (生活圈), cooperative circle (協同圈) projects (事業) target (對象) the 2nd (次) living circle (生活圈), which is the area (地域) between villages (마을간). Therefore, when the interests (利害關係) of two or more (個) adjacent (以上) villages (마을간) align (一致), they cooperate (協同) to undertake (着手) large-scale (大單位) long-standing projects (宿願事業) such as inter-village (農路) roads or irrigation facilities (水利施設) that are relatively (比較的) large in scale (規模).

Among the cooperative circle (協同圈) projects (事業) related (關聯) to the creation (造成) of production bases (生產基盤), the most important (重要한) project (事業) is the construction (開設) and maintenance (整備) of inter-village (農路) roads, which are closely related (密接한) to labor productivity (勞動生產性).

The second most important (重要한) project (事業) is road construction (道路開設) and bridge construction (橋梁架設), which facilitated (包含) the smooth movement (移動) of production factors (生產要素) including labor (勞動力), materials (資材), and agricultural and livestock products (農畜産物) between villages (마을간).


--- (p. 359) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The following can be mentioned as river (河川) management (管理): improvement (整備) of dikes (둑) that block rivers (河川), improvement (整備) of irrigation canals (導水路) that lead water from rivers (河川) to farmland (田畓), repair (個보수) of small rivers (小河川), and improvement (整備) of embankments (堤防), etc. The installation of small reservoirs (小溜池) and pumping stations (揚水場) is also related to water management and irrigation (灌漑), so it can be included in river (河川) management (管理) projects (事業).

The final project (事業) of the cooperative circle (協同圈) is a shared warehouse (共同倉庫) and a shared workshop (共同作業場). Since the unit of the village (部落) differs in the number of households (戶數) and residents (住民), the prospect (展望) of this project (事業) will be bright only in cases where several villages located in the same living area (生活圏) jointly establish (建立) a large-scale (大規模) warehouse (倉庫) to gain advantages (有利性). However, a shared workshop (共同作業場) will only be necessary (必要性) in special (特殊) circumstances (境遇).

## 2. Projects (事業) for Establishing Agricultural (農業) Production (生産) Base (基盤)

### (a) Changes in Management (經營) Conditions (與件)

#### (1) The Third (第3次) Five-Year (5個年) Plan (計畫) and Innovative (革新的) Development (開發) of Rural (農漁村) Economy (經濟)

During the period (期間) of the first and second (次) five-year (5個年) economic (經濟) development (開發) plans (計畫), a policy (政策) centered on industry (工業) with high investment (投資) efficiency (效率) was pursued (追求) to achieve rapid (急速) economic (經濟) growth (成長). While this led to high (高度) growth (成長) in the mining and manufacturing (鑛工業) sector (部門), the agricultural (農業) sector (部門) experienced relatively slow (低速) growth (成長), resulting in a gap (格차) between agriculture (農) and industry (工). This was an undeniable fact (事實).

However, the third (第3次) five-year (5個年) economic (經濟) development (開發) plan (計畫) can be seen as providing a new turning point (轉機) for agricultural (農政) policy (政). Due to the successful (成功的) implementation (遂行) of the first and second (次) five-year (5個年) plans (計畫), the surplus (餘力) from the rapid (飛躍的) growth (成長) of the industrial (工業) sector (部門) could be invested (投入) into the development (開發) of the agricultural (農業) sector (部門).

Under these economic (經濟的) conditions (與件), the third (第3次) five-year (5個年) economic (經濟) development (開發) plan (計畫) presented three development (開發) goals (目標). One of them was the basic (基本) direction (方向) for production (生産) base (基盤) establishment (造成) projects (事業), which aimed to expand (擴大) investment (投資) for agricultural (農業) production (生産) base (基盤) establishment (造成). This included vigorously promoting (推進) projects (事業) such as agricultural (農業) water (用水) development (開發), large-scale (大單位) comprehensive (綜合) agricultural (農業) development (開發), farmland (耕地) improvement (整理) and drainage (排水) improvement (改善), and preservation (保全) and expansion (擴大) of farmland (農耕地) development (開發).

#### (2) Spread (擴散) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)


--- (p. 360) ---

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which began in the 1970s, not only revitalized the appearance of rural Korea in the short term by driving out long-standing stagnation and poverty, and infusing farmers—who had lived listlessly in a state of despair and failure—with new vitality and motivation, but also presented the possibility of developing rural areas into welfare-oriented communities in the long term.

In this way, the Saemaul Undong shifted the consciousness structure from a passive attitude that accepted poverty and ignorance as fate to an active attitude of accepting and overcoming development and change. This transformation led to vibrant rural communities filled with new courage and motivation, exemplified by the phrases "If you do it, it can be done" and "We can do it too." Additionally, basic living environments such as roofs, village paths, and walls were improved, and overall rural environments—including transportation, communication, hygiene, culture, and welfare—were enhanced.

The Saemaul projects started with relatively easy basic environmental improvement projects that residents could handle, gradually developing into production base projects. Through this training process, residents' belief and motivation that "If you do it, it can be done" led to the development of production and income-generating projects.

### (3) Achievements of the Green Revolution

In the first year of the Third Five-Year Economic Development Plan (1972), the total food production was 48,038 thousand stones, consisting of 27,481 thousand stones of cereals, 12,736 thousand stones of wheat, and other miscellaneous grains.

During the 1960s, agricultural policies focused on emergency measures such as developing water resources for agriculture and reorganizing farmland on a small scale. As a result, the country had to import food every year, consuming a massive amount of foreign currency.

However, in the 1970s, the policy direction changed to focus on long-term prospects, with the government exerting full effort into the comprehensive development of the four major river basins and increasing food production.

These government efforts finally succeeded, achieving an initial rice production of 30,867 thousand stones in 1974—exceeding 30 million stones for the first time. From 1975 onwards, the country reached the stage of self-sufficiency in staple grains.

In 1977, the successful cultivation of new varieties led to a production of 41,706 thousand stones, marking the first time in history that production surpassed 40 million stones.

#### B. Agricultural Water Development Projects

Korea has long been an irrigated agricultural country. As early as the Three Kingdoms period, our ancestors practiced rice farming,


--- (p. 361) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The business of initiating submerged cultivation began to expand farmland from riverbank plains to remote mountainous areas, developing water intake and reservoir facilities accordingly.

However, the history of fighting against natural disasters while farming, as evidenced by the many irrigation facility ruins such as the Pikgol Diike from the Three Han Period, is also a history of water resource development that has continued to this day.

Continuing this history, Korea's agricultural water business has seen significant development in recent years, and particularly since the 1970s, it has brought about even more accelerated development alongside the spread of the Saemaul Undong. The following are the circumstances and achievements of the business promotion that began in the latter half of the 1960s, as well as vivid cases of overcoming drought.

### (1) Circumstances and Achievements of Business Promotion

From 1967 to 1968, severe droughts continued in the southern regions of Korea. President Park declared, "We must rid ourselves of the shameful legacy of our ancestors who passively accepted the idea that 'natural disasters are unavoidable and farming is a gift from heaven,' and merely waited for favorable weather. Just as we have eliminated the barren winter season, we must also overcome drought." He emphasized the need for a drought countermeasure and presented the "Guidelines for Agricultural Water Development" to this end, stating, "Even if today's work is difficult and arduous, we must sacrifice for the future when we can pass on farmland free from drought and live well. It is our generation's mission to successfully implement an agricultural water development plan that allows us to look forward to a better tomorrow."

The main contents of these guidelines include dividing the regions into three categories: areas to be converted into irrigation-safe fields, areas suitable for direct seeding of dry fields, and areas to be converted to paddy fields. The funds required for development should be secured domestically, but foreign loans with favorable conditions should also be attracted. Thus, in December 1968, a three-year plan for agricultural water development, focusing on groundwater development, was established. By the end of the project in 1971, a total of 401 billion won was invested to develop 284,000 jeongbo of new farmland and 494,000 jeongbo of reinforced farmland, raising the irrigation-safe field rate from 58% in 1967 to 81% in 1971.

This groundwater development project is scheduled to continue until 1976, the final year of the Third Five-Year Economic Development Plan.


--- (p. 362) ---

The continuous development of agricultural water facilities has been carried out under the goal of improving the safety and irrigation of all farmlands (全農土). From 1972 to 1976, a total of 83.6 billion won was invested over five years, increasing the area of safely irrigated farmlands (水利安全畓) from 1,082,000 town steps (町步) out of the total farmland area of 1,255,000 town steps in 1972, thereby raising the ratio of safely irrigated farmlands to 84%.

Such agricultural water development projects have improved the productivity of farmlands (耕地) and, through appropriate water management, have created a stable foundation for farming, allowing farmers to focus on agriculture with peace of mind.

During the third five-year economic development plan (第3次 經濟開發 5個年 計劃), agricultural water development was given top priority in agricultural investment, and from 1974, AID loans and agricultural promotion loans from Japan were introduced to expand support. As a result, by the end of 1978, there were a total of 72,103 agricultural water facilities nationwide, benefiting an area of 1,121,000 hectares, which is 85% of the total farmland area of 1,312,000 hectares.

When these facilities are categorized by type, reservoirs (貯水池) account for 18,115 sites with a benefited area of 591,000 hectares, making up 52.7%. Next are water pumping stations (揚水場) with 3,068 sites and 131,000 hectares (11.7%), followed by underground canals (暗渠) with 18,252 sites and 129,000 hectares (11.5%).

Such simple agricultural water development projects, including reservoirs, water pumping stations, weirs (堰), waterways (導水路), and collection underground canals, have been promoted in conjunction with the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) since the early 1970s, conducting community-level joint work to prevent the loss of farmland due to water disasters and secure water sources.

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Increased agricultural productivity (農業生産性) and improved farming (營農) led to an increase in agricultural income (農業所得).

In areas that were uncultivated (未耕地) but had no water source (水源) and were thus used as leisure land (休閑地), the stable supply of agricultural water (農業用水) enabled efficient use of land (土地) for paddy fields, meadows, and orchards. This not only prevented drought damage (旱害) and increased land productivity (土地生産性), but also boosted per-unit yield (單位當收穫量) and improved the cropping system (作付體系) to enhance income (所得增大). Additionally, it reduced the time and labor (勞力) spent on irrigation and drainage (灌排水).

### (2) Drought (旱害) Mitigation and Progress

The severe drought of 1978 was unprecedented in its severity.

It was far worse than the most severe drought recorded in the past decade, in 1968, and was not limited to certain regions or rain-fed fields (天水畓) and fields with unstable irrigation (水利不安全畓), but was a nationwide phenomenon (全國的現象).

At the time, the drought situation was characterized by a lack of snowfall (降雪量) during the winter and continuous drought from the beginning of the year, resulting in only 163mm of rainfall (降雨量) by May 10, which was 91mm less than the average (平年) of 254mm. The water storage rate (貯水率) was 64%, which was 30% lower than the average of 94%.

The drought continued, and by June 10, the rainfall was 241mm, which was 113mm less than the average of 354mm. The water storage rate was only 21%, which was 59% lower than the average of 80%. Among the 1,522 reservoirs (貯水池) managed by agricultural land improvement associations (農地改良組合), 19.6%, or 289 reservoirs, were completely depleted (枯渴).

In particular, the lack of rainfall in the Jeollanam-do (全南) and Gyeongsangnam-do (慶南) regions caused rice seedlings to wither and spring crops such as barley and rapeseed to suffer serious damage. In the island regions (島嶼地方) of South Gyeongsang Province (南海), water shortages (食水難) were so severe that administrative ships (行政船) were mobilized (動員) for emergency water supply measures (給水對策).

In Chungcheongnam-do (忠南), rainfall in April was only a quarter of the average, leading to the depletion (枯渴) of not only paddy fields and small reservoirs (小溜池) but also larger reservoirs (貯水池) and wells (管井).

In Jeollabuk-do (全北), the prolonged lack of rainfall (無降雨) not only affected rapeseed and sweet potatoes but also stunted the growth of horticultural crops (園藝作物), with germination rates (活着率) declining and growth coming to a halt (停止).


--- (p. 364) ---

Due to the severity of the drought, the government issued the "Drought Overcoming Guidelines" on January 23, 1978. Nationwide, cities and provinces conducted self-inspections and maintenance of wells and pumps from March 1 to April 30. The central government, in a joint effort by the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, conducted a re-inspection of 25,686 wells and 41,153 pumps from May 1 to 10, mobilizing a total of 560 personnel to ensure full preparedness for water use. On April 25, the government instructed local offices nationwide to establish countermeasures against spring droughts. Subsequently, the government convened a national governors' conference on May 1, anticipating that the drought would be nationwide and long-term. It prioritized the inspection and maintenance of wells and pumps, the installation of paddy field reservoirs, standby reservoirs, and mobile reservoirs, and the establishment of emergency measures for drinking water in island and remote areas. On May 7, the government established the "Central Drought Countermeasures Headquarters" under the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, issued the "Drought Overcoming Emergency Order," and allocated a record-high budget of 330 million won, including reserve and local funds, for drought countermeasures. It set the deadline for transplanting rice seedlings to July 10 and launched a total war against the drought. For reservoir measures, it installed paddy field reservoirs and mobile reservoirs in areas where warm-water and water reservoirs could not be installed, fully mobilized pumps, and provided subsidies or financial support for pesticide costs related to drought-induced diseases, amounting to 300 million won, and for the installation of 1,200 deep wells in severely affected areas, costing 40 million won.

Starting from May 20, for the irrigation operation to begin transplanting, the government mobilized 25,066 newly installed and repaired wells and 29,335 pumps nationwide, along with 6,000 newly supplied pumps and 500 km of water supply hoses to prepare for transplanting. As a result, both warm-water and water reservoirs achieved 100% of the planned area by May 15, and 47% of the transplanting was completed by June 9, just before the rainfall on June 10. This timely promotion of seedling cultivation and transplanting, despite the severe drought, became a decisive factor in overcoming the 1978 drought.

First, examining the physical aspects of the achievements in drought overcoming, the drought overcoming efforts in 1978 included

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

## Achievements (成果)

As a result, 40,213 thousand seok of rice was produced, slightly falling short of the initial target of 42,000 thousand seok. However, compared to an average year, this was a significant achievement, comparable to a bumper harvest.

The amount of resources mobilized to overcome the drought included 2,524 thousand units of water pumps and 41,207 units of electric motor pumps. Additionally, 11,433 units of agricultural equipment were deployed to irrigate 768 thousand jeongbo of rice paddies.

A total of 39,100 thousand people participated in the drought response efforts. Among them, 18,573 thousand were farmers, while the remaining 20,527 thousand consisted of government officials, employees of public institutions and organizations, military personnel, and students.

The government's policy-driven will to overcome the drought, meticulous planning and countermeasures, the fervent determination of farmers inspired by the Saemaul spirit, and the united support of the public who did not treat the drought as someone else's problem—all these elements combined to create a force that left a lasting lesson on this land: "While droughts may come, drought damage can be prevented." This achievement also demonstrated the great potential of farmers, honed through the Saemaul Movement, in the field of agriculture.

## Large-Scale Agricultural Comprehensive Development Projects (大單位農業綜合開發事業)

### (1) Purpose and Background of the Project

As of the end of 1979, the total cultivated area of our country is 1,311 thousand jeongbo, with 87% (1,153 thousand jeongbo) being irrigated farmland. However, due to climatic characteristics, a significant area experiences temporary water shortages during the rice transplanting season, leading to drought damage. Additionally, the short length of major rivers and unfavorable conditions for water resource utilization result in flood damage during the rainy season.

Given these unfavorable natural conditions and a high population growth rate, achieving food self-sufficiency was challenging, necessitating the import of grain. Until the 1960s, the gap between rural and urban living standards was significant, leading to a mass exodus from farming. Even in irrigated farmland, the lack of drainage facilities made it difficult to engage in double cropping or mechanized farming.

To modernize these backward rural areas promptly, it was deemed necessary to focus on large-scale agricultural comprehensive development centered around the four major rivers. In June 1965, President Park (朴大統領) issued a special directive, and the government began planning without being constrained by topographical conditions.


--- (p. 366) ---

To bolster agriculture's long-term foundation and realize all-weather farming, large-scale integrated agricultural development projects were undertaken as part of the so-called Four Major Rivers (4대강) basin comprehensive development initiative. These included projects in the Geumgang (錦江) and Pyeongtaek (平澤) areas, the first phase of the Yeongsan River (榮山江) basin, the Changnyeong (昌寧) area, and the Imjin River (臨津江) area.

Basic surveys were conducted from 1966 onwards, focusing on the Four Major Rivers basins. The Geumgang-Pyeongtaek project began in 1970, the first phase of the Yeongsan River project in 1972, and the Gyeongju (慶州) and Gyehwa Island (界火島) areas in 1974. All projects were completed between 1975 and 1979, with a total investment of 153.9 billion won, developing 68,707 jeongbo of farmland.

Ongoing projects included the Changnyeong and Imjin areas, as well as the Sapgyocheon, Mihocheon (美湖川), Namgang (南江), Nakdonggang (洛東江), Geumgang, and the second phase of the Yeongsan River projects. A total of 560.2 billion won was invested, with plans to complete 96,217 jeongbo of farmland by 1986.

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

First, from 1970 to 1976, a total of 17.1 billion won (KRW) in domestic and foreign investment was injected into the Geumgang Region (錦江地區) across 2 provinces (個道) and 5 counties (個郡), including Buyeo County, Gongju County, and Nonsan County in Chungcheongnam-do, and Ik-san County and Okgu County in Jeollabuk-do. The project results show that the developed area (開發面積) was 12,148 jeongbo, the improved irrigation area (灌漑改善) was 3,838 jeongbo, the reorganized farmland area was 6,546 jeongbo, and the newly cultivated area (開畓) was 1,761 jeongbo. As a result, 1,477 jeongbo of farmland (農耕地) was expanded, and a food production increase (食糧增産) effect of 29,000 tons was achieved. At the same time, one reservoir (貯水池), eight pumping stations, 495 km of water supply channels (用水路), and 12 km of drainage channels (排水路) were completed as major facilities.

The Pyeongtaek Region (平澤地區) Comprehensive Agricultural Development Project was initiated in 1970 and completed in 7 years. A total of 38 billion won (KRW) was invested across Pyeongtaek County and Hwaseong County in Gyeonggi-do, and Asan County and Cheonwon County in Chungcheongnam-do, developing 18,419 jeongbo of farmland (農耕地). The improved irrigation area (灌漑改善) was 7,756 jeongbo, the reorganized farmland area was 6,173 jeongbo, and the reclaimed and cultivated area was 4,490 jeongbo. Additionally, two tidal embankments (防潮提), 18 pumping stations, one drainage station, 934 km of water supply channels (用水路), and 50 km of drainage channels (排水路) were completed as major facilities. As a result of these projects, 4,674 jeongbo of new farmland (農耕地) was expanded, achieving a food production increase (食糧增産) effect of 34,000 tons.

The Gyeongju Region Comprehensive Agricultural Development Project, as part of the Comprehensive Tourism Development Project (觀光綜合開發事業), was initiated in 1974 and completed in 4 years in 1977. This project, carried out in Gyeongju City and Moonseong County in Gyeongsangbuk-do, developed 1,140 jeongbo of farmland (農耕地), improved irrigation for 749 jeongbo, and reorganized farmland for 346 jeongbo. A total of 4.9 billion won (KRW) in domestic and foreign investment was injected.

Additionally, the newly cultivated (開畓) area is 2,500 jeongbo, the irrigation and drainage channels (用排水路) are 335 km, there are four water intake facilities (양수장), and the reinforcement (補强) of irrigation and drainage channels (用排水路) is 93 km.

As a result of this project, agricultural water can be supplied to 2,500 jeongbo of rice paddies, and there was an expansion (擴張) of 2,500 jeongbo of farmland (農耕地) and a food (食糧) increase (增産) effect (效果) of 11,000 tons.

### (3) Project (事業) Promotion (推進) Achievements (成果)

By 1979, the achievements (成果) of the completed large-scale agricultural comprehensive development projects included an expansion (擴張) of new farmland (農耕地) by 11,369 jeongbo and reorganization (整理) of farmland (耕地) by 23,365 jeongbo, increasing the utilization (利用) area (面積) to 81,777 jeongbo. The resulting increase (増産) in grain (米穀) production was 135,000 tons.

The achievements (成果) from the completion of large-scale agricultural comprehensive development projects can be divided into direct (直接) and indirect (間接) effects (效果) as follows.

First, among the direct (直接的) achievements (成果), the increase (増産) in food (食糧) production can be mentioned.

This shows an increase of 615 kg, demonstrating the food production increase effect of this project.

Secondly, there is the effect of improving the cropping system. By rationally improving the cropping system, agricultural income can be increased, and the diversification of the cropping system enables the rational and efficient use of farmland.

Thirdly, there is the external expansion of farmland. Previously, areas that were left undeveloped or idle have had their latent land resources developed and utilized. Suitable areas for reclamation have been developed into farmland, making them productive and efficient.

Fourthly, there is the change in the structure of agricultural production technology. The active introduction of agricultural mechanization has developed labor technology conditions and levels to a higher stage, greatly improving labor productivity through the enhancement of scientific farming technology. The introduction of superior varieties and improved fertilization methods have also greatly increased land productivity.

Moreover, as agricultural production technology is revolutionized, it cannot be overlooked that it is also having a considerable impact on agricultural management. In a small-scale farming system like ours, it has produced the effect of transitioning from traditional self-sufficient farming methods to business-oriented farming methods.

Finally, the increase in the income of farmers in the river basin, along with the improvement of their economic status, has steadily laid the foundation for the welfare of rural and fishing villages.

Next, the following five indirect achievements can be mentioned.

Firstly, there is the change in the consciousness structure of the residents. Farmers, who had been stuck in stagnation and backwardness for a long time, have been liberated through year-round agriculture.


--- (p. 370) ---

Once realized, people shifted from a fatalistic attitude to a proactive one.
Secondly, farming attitudes (營農姿勢) are being established.
With the advancement of agricultural mechanization, scientific farming (科學營農) attitudes are being established, turning farmers into those who continuously study and acquire techniques. Farmers, who were previously isolated (孤立) and scattered (散在), are transitioning towards a cooperative farming system (協同營農體制).
Thirdly, the activation (活性化) of regional resources (地域賦存資源).
It has become an opportunity to develop human (人的) and material (物的) resources (資源) that are inherent and potential (潛在) in the region, and it has also greatly contributed to regional development.
Fourthly, the advancement (進展) of urbanization (都市化) in rural areas.
During the process of promoting comprehensive development projects, not only were major transportation routes in rural areas established, but existing roads were also improved, leading to a closer connection (密着化) between cities and rural areas. The shortening of living spaces between urban (都) and rural (農) areas through the expansion of social overhead capital (社會間接資本) has promoted the homogenization (同質化) of living standards.
Furthermore, the expansion of rural electrification (農村電化) and communication networks has not only brought economic benefits but also accelerated the urbanization of rural areas.
Lastly, the development effect (開發効果) of regional tourism (地域觀光).
As a result of the ripple effects of the comprehensive development project, new tourist spots have been developed. In addition to natural conservation (自然保護) as part of the Saemaul Undong, it has also contributed to the development of local specialties (土產品) and the increase in income of local residents.

## 라. Land Consolidation Project (耕地整理事業)

### (1) Project Promotion (事業推進) Purpose (目的) and Background (經緯)
The Land Consolidation Project (耕地整理事業) has been sporadically implemented since liberation, led by local governments or farmers, using external loans, local funds, and farmers' contributions. However, it became a full-fledged government policy project in 1972 alongside the Saemaul Undong.
The Land Consolidation Project (耕地整理事業) is an essential prerequisite for improving farming efficiency, agricultural mechanization, and controlling water irrigation and drainage (灌排水).
As such, the total target area for the Land Consolidation Project, a necessary condition for rural modernization (農村近代化), is 588,000 jeongbo, which is 44.8% of the total cultivated area (總畓面積) of 1,312,000 jeongbo. As a result of consistently promoting it on an annual basis, by the end of 1979, 322,000 jeongbo, corresponding to 54.8% of the target area, had been completed.


--- (p. 371) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The project is scheduled to be completed by the end of the 1980s, with a total of 588,000 *jeongbo* of land readjustment planned to be finished by introducing foreign loans and maximizing the shortening of the project period.

## (2) Project Implementation Achievements

Since the land readjustment project was institutionally supplemented and prepared in 1971, it has gained attention as an important field of agricultural infrastructure development projects. During this period, there have been many improvements in development methods and land exchange methods. The contents are as follows:

First, the standard project cost per unit was made realistic by considering the price increase rate, thereby aiming to strengthen the substance of the construction work.

Second, in areas where water source facilities such as reservoirs, dams, and pumping stations were completed, if the possible area for land readjustment was the same as the beneficiary area, main and branch water supply facilities were implemented in parallel with the land readjustment project to save construction costs.

Third, the unit cost per project, which had been uniform nationwide, was implemented with differential unit prices by region, thereby eliminating the phenomenon of insufficient project costs in mountainous areas and focusing on drainage improvement in land readjustment target areas to make paddy field farming possible due to climatic conditions.

Fourth, in April 1975, the "Agricultural Modernization Promotion Act" was amended to lower the lower limit of land exchange from 500 *pyeong* to 300 *pyeong* during the land exchange process after land readjustment, thereby protecting the rights of small-scale farmers.

Finally, to improve the land exchange business, which had caused many complaints during the land readjustment project, the existing small-scale land exchange service agencies were merged to establish a dedicated land exchange agency with credibility, and the land exchange officer qualification examination system was implemented. The system was improved so that only those who passed the examination could be in charge of the land exchange business, and 117 land exchange officers were produced by 1978.

Such land readjustment projects had low achievements from 1968 to 1970. The reasons for this are as follows:

First, there was a policy consideration to implement land readjustment projects based on improving the safety of agricultural water development and paddy field farming based on this safety.

Second, farmers' active participation in the mobilization of labor, which beneficiaries had to bear, was not sufficient.


--- (p. 372) ---

The lack of voluntary participation by farmers due to the complexity of procedures and methods for land exchange and registration following land readjustment cannot be overlooked.

However, the Saemaul Undong, which spread nationwide in the early 1970s, was promoted in conjunction with land readjustment projects, with the government providing active support. Beneficiary farmers actively participated in labor mobilization, making land readjustment projects more vigorous. As a result, rural areas were transformed into well-organized, chessboard-like welfare villages, and the technical conditions for agricultural mechanization were met.

### (3) Project Promotion Achievements
The purpose of land readjustment projects is to collectivize fragmented farmland and rectify the irregular shapes of farm plots, thereby enhancing the productivity of land and labor. This facilitates agricultural mechanization and promotes agricultural modernization. The effects of these projects include increased production, reduced production costs, land conservation, and spillover effects.

The most significant direct achievement of land readjustment projects is the improvement of land utilization. Specifically, implementing land readjustment converts fields into rice paddies, expanding the area of rice paddies but reducing the total arable land area. However, the arable land area


--- (p. 373) ---

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

A decrease in area does not necessarily mean a decrease in production volume.
According to a sample survey of 32 completed project areas, in the case of cereals, the paddy field area expanded and the unit production increased, resulting in an increase of 76.7 kg per 1,000 square meters. The possible area for double cropping in paddy fields, which was 71.8% before the project, increased to 77% after the project.

The most significant aspect of production cost savings is the reduction in labor input. In rice farming, the number of people required per 1,000 square meters decreased from 17.9 to 16.3, a reduction of 1.6 people. The results are similar for double cropping in paddy fields.

Indirect effects of land consolidation include the preservation of farmland.
Land consolidation work is mostly earthwork, which mixes old topsoil with subsoil, thus having the effect of improving soil quality. It neutralizes acidic farmland, making it more suitable for rice farming and improving soil fertility. It also prevents the loss or collapse of ridges during heavy rain and blocks the loss of fertilizer components due to irrigation and drainage, thus contributing to farmland preservation.

Finally, the ripple effects of implementing land consolidation include the visual aspect where farmland is organized into certain zones, becoming a landscaping project. With the reduction in labor, it is possible to promote sideline businesses for farmers. The connection between farm roads and main roads is well established, making it convenient for the transportation of agricultural products to the market while also improving traffic between villages, strengthening bonds, and increasing farmers' productivity.

### Ma. Farm Road Construction

#### (1) Importance of Farm Roads

Farm roads refer to rural roads with a width of 5 meters or more that connect villages with national highways, local roads, neighboring villages, and farmland.

The concept of farm roads was first established and their importance recognized after the beginning of the Saemaul Undong in the early 1970s.

The improvement of agricultural productivity is ultimately connected to the income of farmers and fishermen through the effective improvement of transportation conditions, which allows for the smooth circulation of production materials and products. The qualitative improvement of rural life can also be expected when there is close contact with the outside world, allowing for the smooth circulation of living materials, information, and knowledge.


--- (p. 374) ---

Thus, in the economic development of rural areas, the construction of farm roads is an important prerequisite.

Among the various plans of the Saemaul Undong, the farm road construction project was prioritized and initiated for this very reason.

## (2) Achievements in Farm Road Construction

The farm road construction project, which has been promoted alongside the Saemaul Undong and recognized for its importance, resulted in the construction or expansion of a total of 61,797 km of roads by 1980. This distance is equivalent to 51 round trips between Seoul and Busan. During this period, 124.2 million won in government support and 124.1 million won in resident contributions were invested in farm road construction.

In particular, before 1976, the farm road construction project focused on connecting villages to each other or to national and provincial roads. However, from 1977 onwards, it evolved into large-scale cooperative circle projects connecting counties. To address the challenges of constructing roads in difficult terrain, a World Bank loan of 2.7 million dollars was introduced starting in 1976. This funding enabled the construction of 850 km of farm roads and the installation of 211 bridges, significantly improving the existing farm roads.

The constructed farm roads were enhanced in functionality to serve as rural industrial roads. Emphasis was also placed on improving and maintaining the structure of existing farm roads. Most of these projects were carried out by the villagers themselves. By the end of 1979, a total of 229 km of farm roads nationwide had been paved, covered with gravel, or straightened, enabling them to function effectively as farm roads. Additionally, bus routes were extended, allowing buses to reach the villages.

## (3) Outcomes of Farm Road Construction

Traditionally, the primary means of transportation in rural areas of Korea was the carrying pole. However, with the construction of village roads, farm roads, and bridges of various sizes, the rural road network expanded, making handcarts and agricultural machinery important modes of transport.

As such, farm road construction facilitated the smooth transportation of rural residents, reduced travel time, and enabled the swift circulation of various agricultural products and production materials. This led to a reduction in transportation costs and time, as well as an increase in the price and trading conditions of agricultural products.


--- (p. 375) ---

In addition, the construction of farm roads (農路開設) resulted in an improved cropping system (作付體系), making it possible to transition to more convenient farming. This also promoted agricultural mechanization and reduced labor hours. Furthermore, opportunities for employment outside the agricultural sector and educational opportunities for children expanded. Simultaneously, smooth communication with other villages or the outside world enhanced the social status (地位) of rural residents, alleviating their sense of isolation. This also greatly contributed to the economic development (經濟發展) of Korea's rural areas.

### 3. Fishery Production Base Construction Project (漁業生產基盤造成事業)

#### a. Production Base Facilities of Fishery Villages (漁村契의 生産基盤施設)

##### (1) New Community Movement in Fishery Villages (漁村새마을運動)

Marine organisms (바다生物) have the characteristic of mobility (移動性), which means that the sea, the production site (場) for fishery villages (漁村), is used as a common fishing ground (共同漁場). Therefore, fishery villages (漁村) should have a long-standing tradition of cooperative effort (協同努力) due to the collective nature (總有的) of fishing grounds (漁場). However, our fishery villages (漁村) have been unable to escape a life of poverty lacking in planning, influenced by a fatalistic (宿命論的) value system (價値觀) stemming from frequent disasters (災厄). This is because overcoming the natural conditions (自然條件) of the sea and establishing a fishery production base (漁業生產基盤) was a task too daunting for the strength of a single village unit. The efforts of impoverished fishermen (漁民) alone were insufficient to construct large and sturdy fishery port facilities (漁港施設修築) that could withstand typhoons. For small-scale fishermen (零細漁民) without capital (資本), owning a fishing boat (漁船) equipped with gear (裝備) in a port (漁港) lacking safe mooring (安全 繫留) facilities was a kind of gamble. The vulnerability of fishing boats (漁船) and other means of production (生産手段) kept fishermen mired in poverty. This vicious cycle of poverty led to the habituation of a resigned attitude (體質化) that accepted poverty as an inevitable part of being a fisherman (漁民). However, overcoming this resignation and gathering the courage to challenge the sea was encouraged by the New Community spirit of diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), and cooperation (協同). The New Community Movement in fishery villages began in 1972.

##### (2) Development of Fishery Villages (漁村契의 發展)

The fishery village New Community projects (漁村새마을事業) were, by their nature (性格上), cooperative endeavors (協同事業) above the village unit (以上單位), centered around the fishery village associations (漁村契), which are subordinate organizations (下部組織) of the fishery cooperatives (水產業協同組合) in the fishery industry (漁業). In other words, the principal (事業主) of all fishery village New Community projects (漁村새마을事業) was, in principle (原則的), the head of the fishery village association (漁村契長).


--- (p. 376) ---

The Fishery Village Association (어촌계(漁村契)) is a self-help and spontaneous cooperative body of local fishermen (지역어민(地域漁民)) that has inherited the traditional spirit of associations (계(契)) from ancient times (고래(古來)). It can trace its origins to various fishery-related associations (어업(漁業) 관계(關係) 계(契)), such as the Fishermen's Association (어부계(漁夫契)), Fishing Boat Association (어선계(漁船契)), and Fishing Net Association (어망계(漁網契)). The establishment of the Fishery Cooperative (수산업협동조합(水產業協同組合)) in 1962 marked the beginning of the Fishery Village Association as the foundation organization of the cooperative, which started to be established in coastal fishery villages (연안어촌(沿岸漁村)) across the country.

The operational areas (업무구역(業務區域)) of the Fishery Village Associations are primarily based on natural village units (자연부락(自然部落)). At the time of their establishment in 1962, there were 3,530 natural fishery villages nationwide (전국(全國) 어촌자연부락수(漁村自然部락數)). Consequently, the number of Fishery Village Associations, which was 1,786 at the end of 1962, increased annually. By the end of 1972, when the Fishery Village New Community Movement (어촌(漁村)새마을사업(事業)) began, the number of Fishery Village Associations reached a record high of 2,258. However, this increase also led to conflicts among the associations due to the difficulties in dividing maritime areas (해면구역(海面區역)) and the resulting disputes over fishing grounds (어장이해(漁場利害)). In other words, the increase in the number of Fishery Village Associations sometimes led to the division of fishery villages (어촌(漁村)).

To address this issue, the integration and reorganization (통합정비(統合整備)) of the Fishery Village Associations were initiated. Notably, the amendment of the Fishery Cooperative Act (수협법(水協法)) in 1977 enabled the establishment of corporate Fishery Village Associations (법인어촌계(法人漁村契)), leading to the creation of large-scale corporate Fishery Village Associations with legal personality (법인격(法人格)) granted to those with 50 or more members (계원수(契員數) 50인(人) 이상(以上)) and the ability to operate independently (독립채산(獨立採算)). Considering the trend of the New Community Movement (새마을사업(事業)) expanding to include several villages in a cooperative circle (협동권사업(協同圈事業)), this measure was timely and appropriate. As of the end of 1979, there are a total of 1,439 Fishery Village Associations, including 45 corporate ones. Given that the recent number of natural villages (연안(沿岸) 자연부락(自然部락)) (리단위(里單位)) is 3,174, it means that, on average, 2.2 natural villages form one Fishery Village Association.

As of the end of 1979, the total number of fishermen (총어민수(總漁民數)) is 783,000, and the total number of Fishery Village Association members (총어촌계원수(總漁村契員數)) is 117,000, which corresponds to 15% of the total number of fishermen. On average, each Fishery Village Association has 82 members. However, even now, their collective efforts are insufficient for unit projects (단위사업(單位事業)) to improve the sea, so the trend of large-scale Fishery Village Associations will continue to be promoted.

Since the inception of the Fishery Village New Community Movement (어촌(漁村) 새마을운동(運動)) in 1972, the fishery production base (어업생산기반(漁業生產基盤)) has been expanded, and income-increasing projects (소득증대사업(所得增大事業)) have borne fruit. Along with this, large-scale corporate Fishery Village Associations have emerged due to the consolidation (통폐합(統廢合)) of small Fishery Village Associations. Our fishery villages are rapidly strengthening their self-reliance base (자립기반(自立基盤)). In 1978, all basic-stage Fishery Village Associations were eliminated, and as of the end of 1979, out of a total of 1,439 Fishery Village Associations, 208 (14%) are self-help Fishery Village Associations (자조(自助) 어촌계(漁村契)), and the remaining 1,231 (86%) have reached the self-reliance stage (자립(自立) 어촌계(漁村契) 단계(段階)).

### (3) Investment Achievements in Production Base Facilities (생산기반시설(生產基盤施設)의 투자실적(投資實績))


--- (p. 377) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

The Ministry of Fisheries (水產廳) has conveniently categorized the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) projects in fishing villages (漁村) into four sectors: income increase (所得增大), production base (生産基盤), welfare environment (福祉環境), and spiritual development (精神啓發). The projects in the production base sector (生産基盤部門) for fishing villages (漁村) include three initiatives: Saemaul harbor maintenance (漁港修築), cooperative fishing boat construction (協業漁船 建造), and infrastructure (基盤施設) for fishing village associations (漁村契).

Examining the project funds (事業費) (including subsidies (補助), loans (融資), and self-funding (自擔)) invested in the production base sector (生産基盤部門) by year, as shown in <Table 5 (表 5)>, the fishing village (漁村) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) projects started with 25 million won (百萬원) in 1972 (年) and saw no significant change in project funds (事業費增加) until 1974 (年), which also stood at 32 million won (百萬원). However, from 1975 (年) with 192 million won (百萬원), the project funds (事業費) nearly doubled each year, reaching 1,583 million won (百萬원) in 1978 (年), and 2,006 million won (百萬원) in 1979 (年).

Looking at the proportion of project funds (事業費) for the production base sector (生産基盤部門) out of the total fishing village (漁村) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) projects by year, in the early stages of 1972 (年), almost all funds were invested in the income increase sector (所得增大部門), which could directly raise income (直接所得), resulting in the production base projects (生産基盤事業) accounting for only about 2.5% of the total. However, as the limitations of income increase projects (所得增大事業) due to the weak production base (生産基盤) became apparent, the investment ratio (投資比率) for the production base sector (生産基盤事業部門) began to relatively increase from 9.1% in 1975 (年), reaching 27.9% in 1979 (年), with 2,006 million won (百萬원) out of the total fishing village (總漁村) Saemaul Undong (新村運動) project funds of 7,183 million won (百萬원) invested in the production base sector (生産基盤部門).

However, the production base projects (生産基盤事業) still fall far short of what is needed.


--- (p. 378) ---

From 1972 to 1979, a total of 25,927 hundred million won was invested in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in fishing villages (漁村). Of this amount, 62.6%, or 16,233 hundred million won, was allocated to income increase (所得增大), 19.2%, or 4,969 hundred million won, to production base (生產基盤), 11.1%, or 2,871 hundred million won, to welfare environment (福祉環境), and 7.1%, or 1,854 hundred million won, to spiritual development (精神啓發). This indicates that the Saemaul Undong in fishing villages prioritized income increase, with relatively smaller investments in other areas such as production base, welfare environment, and spiritual development. Notably, the root cause of the precariousness (零細性) of fishing villages can be traced back to the inadequacy of fishing port facilities (漁港施設) and fishing vessels (漁船), which are essential for fishing production (漁業生產). Considering that the investment per unit project in fishing production base is significantly higher than in other areas of the Saemaul Undong, the relatively low investment ratio in this area is perplexing. However, given the extreme poverty of our fishing villages at the early stages of the Saemaul Undong, it was inevitable to focus on income increase projects that show immediate investment effects. Another point not to be overlooked is that the Saemaul Undong, being a movement for better living (well 살기 운동), focused on income increase, leading to a classification of projects that may have introduced some bias. This is evident in cases where a sub-project is ambiguously classified and included in the income increase category, such as the current inclusion of auxiliary facilities (附帶施設) and joint fishing ground resource creation (共同漁場資源造成) in the income increase category. Additionally, the fishing village development projects in remote islands and areas (落島僻地漁村開發) are now all included in the income increase category, despite containing various sub-projects related to production base and auxiliary facilities.

### 나. Fishing Port (漁港) Repair (修築) and Fishing Vessel (漁船) Construction (建造)
The Saemaul Undong projects can be divided into fishing port repair and cooperative fishing vessel construction as follows.

#### (1) Saemaul Fishing Port Repair (漁港修築)
A fishing port (漁港) is a crucial element for fishing production (漁業生產), serving as a base for the safekeeping of fishing vessels (漁船) and the handling of catches (漁獲物). It encompasses both water and land areas. To function effectively, a fishing port must be equipped with fishing port facilities (漁港施設). These facilities include, first, basic facilities (基本施設) such as breakwaters (防波堤), dikes (防潮堤), and quays (證岸) for the outer perimeter, as well as berthing areas (泊場) and landing stages (揚陸場) for mooring. Second, it must also have transportation facilities (輸送施設) like railways and roads, preservation facilities (保全施設) for fishing vessels and gear, communication facilities (通信施設), supply facilities (補給施設), processing facilities (加工處理施設) for marine products (水產物), and crew welfare facilities (船員厚生施設) for functionality.


--- (p. 379) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

In Korea, relatively large-scale fishing ports are classified and designated as 1~3rd class fishing ports (漁港) according to the Port Law (港灣法), based on the size of their usage and the administrative agencies responsible for their maintenance. In addition to these designated fishing ports (指定漁港), there are numerous small-scale, non-designated fishing ports (非指定漁港) along the coastlines that are primarily used by local fishermen. As of the end of 1979, Korea had a total of 1,814 fishing ports, including 416 designated ports and 1,398 non-designated small-scale ports.

Fishing port improvement projects (漁港改修事業) typically require substantial investment, making it challenging for the government to finance the basic facilities of designated ports. Consequently, the non-designated small-scale fishing ports along the coastlines and islands have been developed as part of the Saemaul Undong's production base projects (生産基盤事業), focusing on improving basic facilities such as piers (船着場).

By the end of 1979, a total of 9,389 meters of piers had been constructed or improved, with 3,275 meters completed by 1975, 785 meters in 1976, 2,609 meters in 1977, 1,489 meters in 1978, and 1,240 meters in 1979. The total project cost amounted to 944 million won.

The funding criteria for Saemaul fishing port improvement projects support 80% of the costs for pier (船着場) and wharf (物揚場) construction, with 50% coming from the national treasury (國庫) and 30% from local funds (地方費), while the remaining 20% is borne by the local community. The execution of these projects is overseen by the mayors (市知事) and governors (道知事).

Through consistent progress in fishing port Saemaul projects, the basic fishing facilities (漁業基本施設) within fishing village associations (漁村契) have significantly improved. As of the end of 1979, out of 1,439 fishing village associations, 1,183 (82.4%) have piers, 578 (40.3%) have breakwaters (防波堤), 543 (37.8%) have seawalls (護岸), 195 (13.6%) have wharves, and 227 (15.8%) have fishing ground access roads (漁場進入路).

In terms of the facility rate (施設率), which represents the ratio of current facilities to the total required facilities,


--- (p. 380) ---

The level of repair and construction work on fishing ports (漁港) can be inferred once again to be quite low.

Examining the current status of basic fishing (漁業) facilities in non-designated small-scale fishing ports (漁港), out of a total of 1,439 fishing villages (漁村), the total length of piers (船着場) required is 106.5 km. By the end of 1979, 62.8 km had been completed, resulting in a completion rate of 58.9%. For cargo handling facilities (物揚場), 2.5 km were installed out of the required 8.8 km, achieving a completion rate of 28.0%. Breakwaters (防波堤) saw 19.7 km constructed out of the required 57.0 km, with a completion rate of 34.6%. Seawalls (護岸) had 79.7 km built out of the required 129.2 km, reaching a completion rate of 61.7%. Other facilities had 3.0 km completed out of the required 6.3 km, with a completion rate of 48.0%. Therefore, out of the total required length of 307.8 km, 167.6 km had been completed by the end of 1979, resulting in an overall completion rate of 54.5%. On the other hand, dredging required 41.4 thousand m³, but only 2.0 thousand m³ had been completed, achieving just 4.8%. From this, it can be seen that construction of piers (船着場) and seawalls (護岸) in small-scale fishing ports (漁港) has barely exceeded half of the required amount, while other facilities are still in the initial stages, and dredging has only just begun. Furthermore, as the trend towards motorization and larger vessels in fishing boats (漁船) continues, the required amount of facilities will increase significantly. Therefore, continuous investment is required for fishing port (漁港) facility repair and construction as a production base business.

## (2) Cooperative Fishing Boat (漁船) Construction

Ownership of fishing boats (漁船), which is the basic equipment for increasing fishermen's (漁民) income, has been the greatest wish of fishing village (漁村) residents, yet it has not been resolved for generations, preventing fundamental improvement in fishermen's (漁民) lives.

While the root cause was the small-scale nature of fishermen's (漁民) operations, the lack of economic cooperative (協同) power to pool limited funds and the lack of self-help spirit to operate fishing boats (漁船) through aid and cooperation were even more significant factors.

These issues have been overcome through the experiences of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in the past.


--- (p. 381) ---

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) made it possible to construct and operate cooperative fishing vessels (協業漁船) and laid the foundation for increasing income in fishing villages (漁村). Reviewing past business achievements, in 1976, 70 million won was invested to construct 20 cooperative fishing vessels (共同運營漁船) for the first time, along with fishing village cooperatives (漁村契). This aimed to form the income base of self-reliant fishing villages (自立漁村) with the spirit of cooperation in the Saemaul Undong (新村精神), targeting the employment of 140 fishermen (漁民) annually and achieving a 300% increase in catch (漁獲高). By 1979, a total of 42 vessels were constructed with an investment of 1,614 million won.

The cooperative fishing vessel (協業漁船) construction project supported fishing village cooperatives (漁村契) that had the capacity for self-funding (自擔能力), eliminated illegal fishing (不正漁業), obtained fishing permits (漁業許可), and chose industries suitable for regional characteristics (地域特性). Specifically, it supported the construction of standardized large-scale cooperative fishing vessels (標準化協業大型化漁船) by members of the same fishing village cooperative (同一漁村契員), encouraging the participation of skilled cooperative members (職能契員) with experience in fishing vessel operations (漁船運營經驗) to promote rational operations (合理運營). The scale of fishing vessel construction (漁船建造規模) targeted strengthening the self-reliance (自立度) of fishing village cooperatives (漁村契) and laying the foundation for growth into corporate fishing (企業漁業), with a goal of 60~90-ton vessels.

### D. Fishing Village Cooperative (漁村契) Infrastructure (基盤施設)

#### (1) Types of Infrastructure (基盤施設種類)

All fishing village (漁村) Saemaul Undong (新村) production base projects (生產基盤事業) carried out by the Fisheries Cooperative (水產業協同組合) as the main entity (事業進行主體) are included here. These projects aim to ensure the safety of mooring fishing vessels (漁船安全繫留), increase the capacity to unload catches (漁獲物揚陸能力), and improve other production bases (生產基盤) to protect the property (財産) and lives (人命) of fishermen (漁民). For convenience, these projects are divided into infrastructure improvement projects (基盤施設改補修事業) and fishing village cooperative (漁村契) pier construction projects (遊盤構築事業).

Firstly, fishing infrastructure improvement projects (漁業基盤施設改補修事業) are the most basic and in-demand projects for the livelihood (生活手段) of fishing villages (漁村). These projects involve the production (生産) using fishing vessels (漁船) by fishing villages (漁村).


--- (p. 382) ---

It is essential to have means (手段) to overcome natural crises (自然的 危機) and protect property (財産) by improving necessary facilities (必要施設) when needed.

To this end, the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (水協) prioritizes the repair and maintenance of existing facilities (旣存施設) such as piers (船着場), breakwaters (防波堤), etc., when they show signs of aging (老朽) or damage (破損). In unavoidable cases (不得已), it supports small-scale (小規模) new or extended facilities (新規 또는 연장施設). Eligible projects (支援對象事業) include piers (船着場), cargo handling facilities (物揚場), breakwaters (防波堤), seawalls (護岸), and access roads (進入路).

Secondly, the Fisheries Cooperative Union (漁村契) infrastructure projects (基盤構築事業) are necessary (必要) for the organizational (組織的) development (育成) of the Fisheries Cooperative Union (漁村契). These projects target relatively large-scale (比較的 規模) facilities (施設) required for the comprehensive operations (綜合事業 遂行) of the Fisheries Cooperative Union (漁村契). Eligible projects (對象事業) include Fisheries Cooperative Union (漁村契) halls (方舍), collective shipping stations (共同出荷場), and simple fishing boat repair shops (簡易漁船修理所).

That year, 2 simple processing plants (簡易處理場) and 1 cargo handling facility (物揚場) were completed, totaling 3 production base projects (生產基盤事業) with an investment of 40 million won (百萬圓). ### La. Other Production Infrastructure Projects

Although classified under different project names, these are included here as they substantially fall under fishery production infrastructure projects. Income-increasing projects under the jurisdiction of the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (수협), such as ancillary facilities and joint fishing ground resource creation, are a type of production infrastructure project. Additionally, due to the unique characteristics of the remote island fishery village development projects also under the jurisdiction of the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives, these projects have their own names, but they encompass all fishery village Saemaul Undong projects, including income-increasing, production infrastructure, and welfare environment projects. We will examine the performance of the production infrastructure projects included in these special projects. Furthermore, there are pier projects under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Home Affairs as part of the Saemaul beautification projects. As these projects also fall under fishery village production infrastructure, we will examine their performance to date.

#### (1) Ancillary Facilities

Joint fishing grounds and aquaculture facilities, which were previously owned by fishery cooperatives and focused on harvesting naturally occurring attached organisms, had been unable to overcome their small-scale nature due to insufficient harvesting methods and techniques, lack of resource conservation and transportation management techniques, inadequate production activities, and excessive operating costs. To address this, ancillary facilities for joint fishing grounds have been established to facilitate the transition from extractive fisheries to more active aquaculture, enabling planned production, rationalizing resource management, improving work efficiency, and enhancing product quality to increase productivity. Supported projects include fishing ground management vessels, transport vessels, joint warehouses, joint workplaces, and spore cultivation facilities. The ancillary facilities project began in 1972 with an investment of 1 million won for one kelp cultivation facility. Since then, the types of ancillary facilities and the number of projects have continued to increase each year, reaching 262 projects with an investment of 670 million won in 1978. In 1979, the number of projects compared to the previous year was


--- (p. 384) ---

A total of 236 projects were executed, with a total investment of 799 million won.

From 1972 to 1979, the total achievements of the ancillary facilities business were as follows: 689 fishing ground management ships (漁場管理船) for 1,123 million won, 12 common transport ships (共同運搬船) for 163 million won, 174 common warehouses (共同倉庫) for 500 million won, 17 breeding farms (培養場) for 63 million won, and other businesses, totaling 1,007 projects with an investment of 1,984 million won.
