## (2) Common Fishing Grounds (共同漁場) Resource Development (資源造成)

This business involves undeveloped fishing grounds (未開發漁場) being jointly developed and expanded by fishing village residents (漁村住民) to increase unit productivity (生産性), with a focus on natural resource (自然産) harvesting. Through resource development (資源造成), this business aims to protect resources (資源) from disorderly capture and increase the primary income (所得) of fishermen. This main business (本事業) primarily supports those who have already obtained a license for the first kind (第1種) of common fishing grounds (共同漁場). New development projects can also be considered if they are feasible. Eligible support businesses (支援對象事業) include young shell broadcasting (稚貝撒布) (targeting clams, abalone, and other shellfish), throwing stones (投石) (targeting abalone, octopus, and other sea creatures), artificial fish reefs (人工魚礁), and rock blasting (岩盤爆破).

From 1972 to 1979, the achievements in common fishing grounds (共同漁場) development were as follows: young shell broadcasting (稚貝撒布) achieved 3,742 ha out of the target 5,626 ha, with a completion rate of 66.5%; throwing stones (投石) achieved 1,114 ha out of the target 1,500 ha, with a completion rate of 74.3%; and other businesses (其他事業) achieved 370 ha out of the target 450 ha, with a completion rate of 82.2%. These results demonstrate a consistent effort to meet the targets.

## (3) Remote Island (落島) and Rural (僻地) Fishing Village Development (漁村開發) Business (事業)

The remote island (落島) and rural (僻地) fishing village development (漁村開發) business aims to alleviate the sense of isolation experienced by fishermen (漁民) due to unfavorable geographic conditions.


--- (p. 385) ---

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Efforts were concentrated on supporting these fishing village associations (漁村契) to gradually improve and achieve balanced development among regions.

The executing bodies for the projects were the regional fisheries cooperatives (水協), which took all fishing village Saemaul projects (事業) as target projects (對象事業).

There are a total of 3,422 islands (島嶼) in Korea, including both North and South, of which 85%, or 2,904, are located south of the demarcation line (休戰線). Among the islands (島嶼) in South Korea, 2,238 are uninhabited, and the remaining 23%, or 666 islands, are inhabited. Excluding Jeju Island (濟州道) and 23 islands connected to the mainland, there are 642 islands targeted for development. Among these, development projects are being carried out as part of the Saemaul Undong (事業) for 453 islands with populations of 50 or more. As of 1979, there are 274 fishing village associations (漁村契) in remote island areas (落島僻地).

Since 1972, seven projects, including piers (船着場), roads (道路), power facilities (發電施設), government ships (行政船), waiting rooms (待合室), piers (棧橋), and emergency medical supplies (常備藥), have been carried out annually for island development (島嶼開發). From 1972 to 1979, a total of 2,751 million won was invested in island development (島嶼開發), achieving significant results.

# (4) Fishery Village Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Improvement Project

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project began as a leading core project of the initial Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and has since improved the living environment structure through this project. The reform of the environment structure ignited and inspired the Saemaul spirit and became a driving force for income growth.

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project has been promoted with a focus on expanding the production base since 1974. As a Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project through fisheries, there is the fishery village wharf facility project hosted by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The wharf project hosted by the Ministry of Home Affairs increased from 189 sites in 1972 to 337 sites in 1974 and 435 sites in 1975. After that, the amount of business showed a decreasing trend, with 379 sites in 1976, 316 sites in 1977, 273 sites in 1978, and 243 sites in 1979, achieving a total of 2,172 sites by 1979.

## 4. Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Improvement Project

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which started with the motivation to live well, aims to improve the welfare of residents through income growth by increasing production and improving the living environment. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project is one of the basic projects of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), starting with small tasks to improve the production base and income, and gradually expanding the environment of the village.

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project related to the formation of agricultural production bases consists of communal composting sites and work sites, communal livestock barns and warehouses, small stream improvement, and the expansion of village bridges and roads. As the sub-projects indicate, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) improvement project starts with small projects that are of common interest to the villagers and require collective effort.


--- (p. 387) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

The Saemaul Undong prioritized and promoted village projects that were difficult to accomplish alone but directly benefited the community. Through easy and cost-effective Saemaul village beautification projects, inefficient production conditions were improved, labor was saved, and the advantages of collective work were realized.

Now, let's examine how Saemaul village beautification projects connect to the establishment of a production base. If the foundation or base for production activities is referred to as the production base, then creating and cultivating this base is of utmost importance. Improving or enhancing the production base means improving production conditions that can either increase output with a given input of production factors or reduce the input of production factors for a certain output. In other words, it is about creating a foundation that can enhance the efficiency of production. Therefore, projects such as land consolidation (耕地整理), expansion of irrigation and drainage facilities (灌排水施設), new construction or renovation of farm and livestock buildings (農畜舍), expansion of roads and other infrastructure, and improvement and repair of various facilities and equipment can all be included in the establishment of a production base.

Basic production base establishment projects such as land consolidation and expansion of irrigation and drainage facilities are such significant tasks that they will be discussed in another section. Here, we focus on the achievements of Saemaul village beautification projects that residents can easily undertake at any time and the effects they have on production base establishment projects.

## A. Village Collective Production Base Establishment Projects (共同生産基盤造成事業)

### (1) Collective Composting Sites (共同堆肥場)

The central task of agricultural policy is to increase production, i.e., to increase yields per unit area. To achieve this increase in production, high-yielding new varieties have been developed and promoted, and the production of chemical fertilizers has been promoted. As a result, the production increase target has been achieved, but on the other hand, the adverse effect of degrading soil fertility is also significant. Continuous increase in the application of inorganic fertilizers not only reduces soil fertility and acidifies the soil but also degrades soil fertility, which is a crucial issue as it permanently reduces the productivity of land that should be used indefinitely.

As part of the Saemaul village beautification projects, the establishment of collective composting sites helps first, farms that find it difficult to set up their own composting sites, and second, prevents each household from owning individual composting sites.


--- (p. 388) ---

By eliminating foul odors and sanitary issues, thirdly, it can raise awareness about the importance of compost production, and fourthly, even if the importance of compost production is recognized, by participating in collective collection, practical compost production can be achieved. Fifthly, by collectively managing compost sites, labor can be conserved.

From the perspective of achievements, the establishment of communal compost sites during the early stages of the Saemaul Undong initially focused on environmental improvement projects, leading to a surplus of rural manpower and the relatively easy implementation of communal compost site installations, which were significant for both agricultural production and village sanitation. As shown in <<Table 12>>, the number of communal compost sites installed nationwide was 3,097 in 1972, decreased to 1,522 in 1973, and then surged to 5,812 in 1975. However, from 1976 onwards, the achievements were very low, dropping to just 308 in 1979. By including the communal compost sites existing before the start of the Saemaul Undong village beautification project, a total of 70,081 sites were installed by 1979, achieving a completion rate of 50.4% of the total target of 138,936.

The establishment of communal compost sites during the early stages of the Saemaul Undong achieved significant results. Starting with small projects, villagers gathered to discuss the selection of compost site locations, the scale and shape of the compost sites, and the importance of compost production. They then enhanced soil fertility with the produced compost, thereby improving agricultural productivity. This was one of the important achievements. Moreover, by accomplishing small tasks, villagers gained confidence to challenge larger projects with their own strength, laying the groundwork for a higher level of achievement. However, despite the remarkable achievements of the early Saemaul Undong, as time passed,


--- (p. 389) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

As a result, the business of creating communal composting sites (共同堆肥場) is declining. The most important reason is that, since the mid-1970s, the rural labor force (農村勞動力) has been decreasing at an astonishing rate. As a result of this labor shortage (勞動力減少), there were not enough workers to go out into the fields (山野) to gather grass.

The second reason is that, as labor became scarce, rural wages (農村品價) began to rise rapidly. Economically, it became more advantageous to use the wages earned from other work to purchase cheap chemical fertilizers (化學肥料) rather than spending time gathering grass from the mountains and fields. Soil degradation (地力減退) is a secondary issue, and the immediate priority is the annual input (投入) and output (產出), i.e., cost and revenue. The countryside has changed a lot. Therefore, in the future, there will be some limitations to increasing compost production (堆肥增產) and operating communal composting sites (共同堆肥場), and new directions will need to be explored. One good method for improving soil fertility (地力增進) is to expand the production (生産) of manure (厩肥), a byproduct (副產物) of livestock farming (家畜飼育). It is undoubtedly an important area for organic (有機質) fertilizer sources (肥料源) along with increased livestock production (畜產物增產). This is related to the communal barns (共同畜舍) mentioned later, so it will be explained there.

## (2) Communal Workspaces (共同作業場)

Among the Saemaul beautification projects, the establishment of communal workspaces (共同作業場) is a significant undertaking with considerable importance. In a country like Korea with a small-scale farming (小農) structure, it has the advantage of achieving economies of scale (規模經濟). Individual farms (個別農家) under small-scale farming have low efficiency (效率性) as a single work unit (作業單位). If a hamlet (部落) integrates and expands its work scale as a single economic unit (經濟單位), it can improve work efficiency (能率) and the quality of agricultural products (農產物), facilitate the introduction of new technologies (技術導入), and increase investment (投資) and utilization efficiency (利用效率) of agricultural machinery (農機械).

In hamlets that primarily cultivate staple crops (主穀), communal threshing yards (共同脫穀場) can be established, or agricultural machinery (農機械) can be used communally. Communal drying facilities (共同乾燥場) can be set up to dry not only staple crops (主穀) but also chili peppers and other crops. In villages that mainly cultivate fruit trees (果樹) and horticultural crops (園藝作物), establishing communal workspaces (共同作業場) for washing (洗滌), sorting, and packaging these agricultural products (農產物) can facilitate their circulation (流通) and increase their market value (市場價值). In villages primarily engaged in sericulture (養蠶), establishing communal silkworm rearing facilities (共同飼育場) for young silkworms (稚蠶) can save labor (勞動力) and prevent pests and diseases (病蟲害).


--- (p. 390) ---

Effectively control (防除) and facilitate the introduction of new technologies.
Looking at the performance of the joint work site (共同作業場) installation project (設置事業) in <Table 13>, the total number of installations (設置棟數) from 1972 to 1980 was 6,263 units (棟), which was only 18% of the initial target (當初目標) of 34,665 units (棟). Although it was not intended to complete all installations during this period, the lack of wide spaces suitable for installation or the excessive cost seems to have been a limiting factor (制約要因), so there is no need to be constrained by the performance (實績).

However, in terms of achievements (成果) and significance (意義面), it cannot be underrated (過小評價). Joint work was not an easy task before the installation of joint work sites (共同作業場). The decision by residents (住民) to create a joint work site (共同作業場) presupposes the importance (重要性) of joint work and participation (參與) in it. Although the performance (實績) is small, the significance (意義) is great. Ultimately, in a small-scale farming system (小農體制) like ours, we must find the advantages (有利性) of scale (規模) through joint work. At the current stage (現段階), vegetable farming households (菜蔬栽培農家) are joining forces in groups of about 10 households (餘戶) to practice joint fertilization (共同施肥), joint pest control (共同防除), joint use of farm machinery (農機械), joint harvesting (共同收穫), joint washing (共同洗滌), joint supply (共同供給) and packaging, and joint shipping (共同出荷), thereby overcoming all inefficiencies (非效率性) that can arise from small-scale operations (零細規模).

As the issue of joint work site (共同作業場) installation (設置問題) has economic (經濟的) significance (重要性) beyond just providing a joint work site, even if the performance (實績) and progress (進度) are sluggish (不振), we should not rush or give up, but rather persistently promote it (推進) along with the change in the consciousness structure (意識構造變化) of the village residents (部落住民). At a time when agricultural production (農業生產) is facing challenges from the international market (國際市場), it is not possible to easily raise agricultural product prices (農産物價格) under a small-scale farming management system (小農經營體制), so we are in a position where we cannot ignore the advantages (有利性) of large-scale (大規模) economy (經濟) through joint work.

(3) Joint Livestock Barn (共同畜舍)


--- (p. 391) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Most general farming households in our country have traditionally and currently engaged in small-scale livestock farming, raising 1-2 heads of Korean cattle (Hanwoo), several pigs, and dozens of chickens as a side business. Due to the small scale of this livestock farming, farmers have been insensitive to market price fluctuations and have struggled to adopt new technologies or implement efficient livestock management. To eliminate the inefficiency of having one person spend an entire day feeding cattle, residents took the lead in building communal livestock barns. Starting in 1972, these barns primarily targeted fattening cattle, with 757 barns built nationwide in the first year, 1,028 barns in 1979, and 124 barns in 1980, totaling 4,476 barns. This achieved 14% of the initial goal of 32,729 barns. As an ongoing project, communal livestock barns hold several economic significances.

Communal livestock barns hold several economic significances.
1. First, they allow farmers to raise livestock in large-scale facilities beyond the limited scope of individual farming households, preparing a system to meet increased demand for livestock products.
2. Second, they enable economies of scale through communal livestock farming, providing a foundation for reducing production costs.
3. Third, they facilitate the introduction of livestock management technologies and disease prevention, enhancing the productivity of livestock products.
4. Fourth, they maximize the utilization of idle resources within the village, contributing to increased income for village residents.
5. Fifth, they make it easier for villagers to agree on systematic sales or communal marketing, reducing excessive circulation costs and various drawbacks associated with individual sales.

However, despite the various advantages and benefits of communal livestock barns, there are also important issues that cannot be overlooked. Livestock production is driven by the motivation to increase production stemming from the notion of "mine" ownership. In other words, farmers work hard with the expectation that their efforts will be rewarded with corresponding profits. However, in communal livestock barns, the rewards for taking turns working are distributed among all participating villagers, not just the individual. This can lead to neglect in livestock management due to the less apparent personal benefits. Such phenomena


--- (p. 392) ---

Collaboration (協業) in the process often leads to concerns about reduced productivity (生產性). Ultimately, while establishing a common livestock barn (共同畜舍) is important, the success or failure of joint livestock management (共同飼筵管理) is even more crucial. In this regard, intensive research (硏究) and adjustments must follow.

### (4) Community Warehouse (共同倉庫)
The establishment of community warehouses (共同倉庫設置) is a very important part of the Saemaul beautification project. In villages with community warehouses (共同倉庫), not only can autumn (秋穀) and summer grains (夏穀) be stored, but government purchased grains (收買穀) can also be stored. This can help generate community funds through storage fees.

Community warehouses (共同倉庫) can also be used to store fertilizers (肥料) and production materials (生產資材), enabling timely supply (適期供給) according to the production season. They can also store communal machinery or individual farm equipment, and manage the storage of other agricultural products (農產物).

The construction of community warehouses began in 1972 with 1,699 units (棟), reached 6,367 units (棟) in 1974, and then decreased annually to 778 units (棟) in 1979. However, between 1972 and 1980, a total of 22,143 units (棟) were built, achieving 64% of the initial target of 34,665 units (棟).

If community warehouses are built to an appropriate scale for the village's economic unit (經濟單位) and effectively manage the storage of agricultural products (農產物) leaving the village and production materials (生產資材) entering the village, the storage fees that would otherwise go to middlemen can be converted into village residents' income. This can have a positive economic impact. Additionally, it can reduce distribution costs (流通費用) for production materials (生產資材), contributing to lower production costs.

However, if community warehouses are built too large or too small without considering the village's economic scale and unit, and without planning, it may not improve the efficiency (效率性) of actual use. This could burden residents with costs, undermining the community's sense of unity and cooperative spirit (協同精神), so caution is needed.

## B. Village Road Expansion Project (擴張)
### (1) Village Road Expansion


--- (p. 393) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The convenience of roads is one of the most important functions among the superstructure (上部構造) that supports all economic activities (經濟活動). Depending on whether one takes a direct route (直線上) or a detour (迂廻) to reach a destination, there will be a difference in the time (時間) required. Even if it is the same road, the time (時間) difference and the quantity and weight of goods transported will vary depending on whether one walks or uses a cart (牛馬車) or an automobile (自動車). Additionally, there can be significant differences in transportation costs (運送費用).

Convenient roads facilitate the transportation (交通) of rural residents (農村住民), shorten travel time (所要時間), and reduce the cost of transporting agricultural products (農產物) and production materials (生産資材). Reducing circulation costs (流通費用) makes the use of production materials (生産資材) cheaper and increases the quality price (品質受取價格) of agricultural products (農產物).

Wide and effective roads (效果的) will also facilitate the operation (動作) of agricultural machinery (農機械), save labor time (勞動時間), and improve labor productivity (勞動能率). As vehicles that could not previously enter now reach the doorsteps of villages due to the expansion (擴張) of village roads, not only passenger cars (乘用車) but also various freight vehicles (貨物車輛) can enter the village. This not only enhances convenience (便利性) and reduces transportation costs (運搬費用) but also brings about changes in the consciousness structure (意識構造).

Considering the importance (重要性) of these factors, the government (政府) prioritized bridge (橋梁) construction and village road expansion (擴張事業) in the early stages of the Saemaul beautification project (事業). Given that the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) itself is a movement that garners high resident (住民) interest (關心) and directly affects resident (住民) interests (利害), involves minimal direct resident (住民) burden (負擔), fosters easy cooperation (協同), and yields significant social (社會) and economic (經濟的) effects (效果), it is natural that bridge (橋梁) construction and village road expansion (擴張事業) should hold significant weight (比重).

In the first year of the Saemaul beautification project (事業) in 1972, village road expansion (擴張事業) accounted for 61% of the total project (事業).

However, the actual expansion (擴張) of village roads faces various challenges. This is because individual farmlands (個別農家의農土) have long existed around the narrow roads that have been in place since ancient times (古來). Moreover, the relocation (移動) or demolition (撤去) of some existing houses (家屋) is required, necessitating significant sacrifices (犧牲) from the village residents (住民). These sacrifices must be made not by force (強要) but through mutual consultation (相互協議) and voluntary consent (自發的意思).


--- (p. 394) ---

Recognizing the importance, people began to compromise and provide land. The government started to encourage the promotion of projects by providing cement and facility materials to villages that were prepared for village road expansion. Of course, the period for collective work was chosen to be as much as possible during the farming off-season.

The initial target for the village road expansion project was 26,666 km. However, including the 9,624 km completed sporadically before 1972, 21,624 km was achieved in 1972, recording an astonishing achievement rate of 89%. The following year, 1973, saw an expansion of 10,862 km, exceeding the initial target by 10%, and was evaluated as a peak project of the Saemaul Undong. From 1974 onwards, due to a shortage of target lengths, achievements decreased, but by 1980, a total of 43,385 km of village roads were expanded, achieving 165% of the initial target, a remarkable achievement.

The village road expansion project can be said to have achieved remarkable results not only for improving the village environment but also for establishing an agricultural production base. As such, as results became significantly apparent in the village road expansion project, residents increased their familiarity and efficiency with the Saemaul project itself, gaining confidence and self-assurance, and decided to use it as a catalyst for the Saemaul Undong.

(2) Village Bridge Construction Project

Following the village road expansion project, road expansion and development, as well as large and small bridge construction projects, were carried out. As the Saemaul beautification project became more substantial, not only did resident participation increase, but government support also increased, and the project continued to expand.


--- (p. 395) ---

## Chapter 5 Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Roads into villages, which had been passable only by horse-drawn carts, were expanded to accommodate large vehicles with ease. Modern concrete bridges were progressively constructed on paths that had previously been makeshift wooden bridges or ford crossings. The government provided cement, reinforcing bars, and other materials, while residents contributed land and labor, working cooperatively to build the bridges. Initially, bridge construction began with smaller projects due to a lack of experience and materials. However, as years passed, experience grew, and a spirit of cooperation flourished, enabling residents to undertake larger bridge projects independently, even without government support.

There were numerous locations requiring both large and small bridges, leading to a total target of 76,749 sites set for 1972. In that year, 12,800 bridges were constructed, achieving 16.7% of the goal. The following year, 1973, saw the completion of 9,963 bridges, reaching 42% of the target. By 1974, the third year, 54.5% of the bridges were built, surpassing half of the initial objective. This continuous effort resulted in the construction of 4,019 bridges in 1979 and 3,208 bridges in 1980, culminating in a total of 79,516 bridges, achieving 104% of the original target. Thus, the initial goal was accomplished over the past decade.

Unlike village road expansion projects, bridge construction required precise technology and meticulous management. The knowledge gained from the trial-and-error process of bridge construction also served as a catalyst for advancing into housing construction and other architectural endeavors.

However, some bridges were hastily constructed, and when considering long-term traffic volume, some were found to be too small or inconveniently placed. Once concrete bridges are constructed, they become permanent. Therefore, to avoid the enormous cost of potential removal, thorough measurement and review should be conducted beforehand to ensure their permanence.

### D. Small Stream Improvement Projects

Streams play a vital role in rural production activities and environmental improvement. Water is directly used for various crops and is closely related to evaporation. However, if stream management is neglected, cultivated land and houses may be


--- (p. 396) ---

Flooding often causes water damage.
To protect farmland and houses from water damage and connect these streams to food production for increased income, improve the village environment, preserve the country's land in a balanced way, and activate idle resources and labor to create external income sources, the Saemaul beautification project selected the small stream improvement project.

The government established a long-term plan for small stream improvement and conducted a nationwide survey of small streams in 1972. According to the survey results, streams that needed improvement were 8,451 km of small streams, 5,733 km of minor streams, and 3,053 km of medium streams, totaling 17,239 km. Based on these survey results, the government drew up a small stream improvement plan, deciding to start with the improvement of gullies, followed by small streams and medium streams. The small streams and ditches within the village with a stream width of 2m or less were set as part of the Saemaul beautification project to be carried out by the residents' own efforts. The minor and medium streams were to be carried out as government-supported projects, with the necessary funds divided among national treasury subsidies, local funds, and resident contributions. The implementation of the project itself was to be carried out by the residents in a joint direct management system.

To ensure that there were no technical defects, the government encouraged complete construction through design-based work and conducted technical education while simultaneously carrying out thorough completion inspections. In the initial stage of promoting the small stream improvement project, residents jointly participated and improved the small streams and ditches within the village through their own efforts, achieving good results. Using this as an opportunity, they expanded the improvement project to minor and medium streams. The government prioritized areas prone to water damage, providing concentrated financial support and encouraging stream improvement through village joint projects, achieving remarkable results. As previously mentioned, the total length of small streams requiring improvement was 17,239 km. As shown in <Table 15>, 19,665 km were completed between 1972 and 1980, achieving 114.1% of the target. However, looking at the details, the small stream improvement project at the village level was almost completed by the mid-1970s, and using this as a foundation, several villages cooperated to improve the small streams.


--- (p. 397) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong

The movement is advancing toward large-scale projects in each region.

Through the promotion of small stream improvement projects, not only were farmlands and houses protected from water damage, but new farm roads were also developed through the construction of embankments. Additionally, 550 hectares of new farmland were created, and increased production effects were achieved through improved irrigation conditions. The ripple effects were quite significant.

However, in the process of transforming small stream improvements into permanent projects using cement, many places were found to lack efforts to establish comprehensive village development plans (綜合開發計劃) to prevent the need for future improvements in other forms, or to carry out the work in a scientific and rational (合理的) manner. While it can be somewhat acknowledged that these trial-and-error (試行錯誤的) projects in the early stages were due to a lack of experience and ideas, in the future, efforts must be made to promote more scientific and economical small stream improvement projects (改補修事業) by learning from past trial-and-error (試行錯誤) experiences.

## La. Evaluation of Saemaul Beautification Projects

Saemaul beautification projects related to production base establishment (生產基盤造成事業) include the communal composting sites (共同堆肥場), work sites (作業場), communal livestock barns (共同畜舍), warehouses (倉庫), small stream improvements (小河川改補修), and village bridge (橋梁) and village road expansion (擴張) projects, as previously examined.

To sprout new growth in the 5,000-year-old traditional (傳統的) Korean countryside, the Saemaul Undong initially selected projects with high resident interest (關心度), directly related to resident benefits (利害), with minimal resident burden, easy cooperation, and significant social (社會) and economic (經濟的) effects (效果). From this perspective, Saemaul beautification projects became the central task (中心課題) of the Saemaul Undong.

The village road expansion project, which exceeded its initial (當初) target (目標) by 66% over the past 10 years, was at the center.


--- (p. 398) ---

Through these efforts, such as the bridge construction project (achieving 104% of the target), the communal warehouse construction project (64% completion), the small stream improvement project (114.1% completion), the communal composting facility project (over 50% completion), and the communal work facility installation project (18% completion), village residents experienced not only economic benefits but also a spiritual revolution characterized by diligence, self-help, and cooperation.

Communal composting facilities (共同堆肥場) were established to prevent soil degradation, with villagers collectively producing organic fertilizers (有機質肥料). Additionally, communal work facilities were created to achieve economic advantages from large-scale operations, which not only improved the environment but also promised long-term benefits such as increased productivity and income.

To improve the efficiency of secondary livestock farming (副業畜產), which had been stagnant, communal livestock barns were built. Furthermore, storage and management facilities for products and materials were established, strengthening not only the production base but also distribution functions.

River improvement projects, which can be either advantageous or disadvantageous depending on management, helped prevent water damage while enhancing irrigation facilities (水利施設), which are almost indispensable for crop cultivation, thus achieving dual benefits.

Expanding village roads and constructing bridges made all means of transportation more convenient, reducing the costs of purchasing and distributing production materials and also cutting the distribution costs of agricultural products, thereby contributing to increased income. These efforts not only expanded the production base but also significantly contributed to developing the residents' consciousness.

Among the benefits that village residents gained through these New Village beautification projects, the most important is the spiritual confidence and self-assurance rather than material gains. The mindset that residents develop after collectively accomplishing tasks—such as "We can do it," "We can also live well," and "It's good after fixing it"—is a precious spiritual asset (資產) that cannot be easily obtained.

However, the history of development warns against complacency at any point. Humans begin to move, strive, and work for something the moment they feel a sense of lack and necessity.


--- (p. 399) ---

# Chapter 5: The Trajectory and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

I would like to point out a few things to whip us all and reflect (反省) on in order to promise (期約) new development (發展). First, we should not rush the Saemaul village beautification project. Second, we must establish goals with feasibility (具現性) and plans with scientific (科學性) rigor to complete every single village beautification project with permanence (永久性). Third, all Saemaul village beautification projects must be designed and implemented to suit the conditions (與件) of each individual village and the personality (個性) of its residents. Fourth, political (政治的) neutrality (中立) and sustained (恒久的) implementation. If the Saemaul Undong is not a movement by the residents, for the residents, and of the residents, it will not last. We must all remember that when political (政治性) involvement leads to a lack of purity (純粹性), it is difficult to garner the support of many residents. And the Saemaul village beautification project must be continued, without interruption, until our rural areas can live as well as advanced countries (先進國).

## 5. Saemaul Cooperative (新村協同) District (圈) Projects (事業)

Saemaul Cooperative (新村協同) District (圈) Projects (事業) refer to projects jointly developed by residents of two or more villages (部落) to improve their living environment, production base (生産基盤), and specialized crops (特化作目).

In the early days of the Saemaul Undong, projects were initiated within the boundaries of a single natural village (自然部落), starting with small-scale endeavors. As residents worked together to improve their surroundings and develop their villages, they cultivated a spirit of cooperation (協同), self-help (自助), and diligence (勤勉). With the completion of most basic environmental improvement projects and production base (生産基盤) development projects at the village level, and having achieved more than expected results, residents began to undertake inter-village projects based on the momentum (鼓吹) and experience gained.

The purpose of Saemaul Cooperative (新村協同) District (圈) Projects (事業) is to promote balanced regional development (地域開發) on a broad scale (廣域的) by encouraging residents of two or more neighboring villages (隣接) to jointly undertake large-scale inter-village projects such as farm roads (農路) and extensive water facilities (水利施設). This aims to strengthen the self-sufficient production base (生産基盤) of the regional economy (地域經濟), establish a Saemaul cooperative (協同) system (體制) among regional residents (地域住民), and ultimately contribute to national development (國家發展).


--- (p. 400) ---

## Expansion of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Cooperation Circle (協同圈) Business

In 1974, a trial implementation of joint wish projects among neighboring villages yielded significant results, leading to the expansion of the scale and scope of Cooperation Circle (協同圈) businesses alongside village-level projects. In the initial stages of Cooperation Circle (協同圈) businesses, the primary characteristic was the collective mobilization of labor. As the businesses expanded, financial resources and technology increased, and the scope of cooperative management grew. Additionally, businesses began to diversify.

In selecting villages for cooperation and business projects, factors such as geographical features, social solidarity, living conditions, and economic and social conditions were considered to form Cooperation Circles (協同圈) among villages with high degrees of similarity. Sometimes, 3 to 6 natural villages would cooperate simultaneously to not only expand the production base but also to install cultural and welfare facilities, improve distribution infrastructure, and pursue other inter-village development projects.

### Implementation Policies for Saemaul Cooperation Circle (協同圈) Businesses

1. **Target Selection**: Prioritize regions where regional development directions align and inter-village cooperation is strong, selecting development project areas based on the concept of residents' living spheres.
2. **Project Initiation**: Begin with wish projects that are feasible for inter-village resident cooperation, considering the ease of business implementation, the degree of benefit to villages, and resident activity levels.
3. **Organizational Structure**: Establish a "Saemaul Cooperation Circle (協同圈) Business Promotion Committee" at the Cooperation Circle (協同圈) level to jointly promote projects using the Saemaul beautification business method.
4. **Fund Management**: Deposit business funds supported by cities, counties, and districts in financial institutions such as Saemaul savings banks or agricultural cooperatives under the joint names of all Saemaul leaders within the district, following the progress of Cooperation Circle (協同圈) development projects.
5. **Cost Sharing**: Adhere to the principle that residents jointly bear approximately 50% of the support business funds.

### Criteria for Setting Cooperation Circles (協同圈)

1. **Resident Motivation**: The business itself should be able to enhance residents' development motivation.
2. **Regional Similarity**: Set appropriate circles based on the concept of residents' living spheres, considering regions with similar or identical geographical features, traditions, and farming methods.
3. **Priority Support**: Set regions where the principle of prioritizing outstanding villages can be applied.
4. **Expansion Potential**: Set regions where inter-village related businesses can be continuously expanded as a result of business implementation and the spread of the Saemaul spirit.
5. **Resource Utilization**: Set regions where idle resources and potential unemployed labor can be mobilized.


--- (p. 401) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

First, regions are designated where production can be increased and where technical cooperation (技術協同) between villages is possible. Sixth, regions and projects are set up where new sources of income (所得源) can be developed, and where the benefits of the projects can be felt by the villagers, as well as increased.

To effectively select the targets for Saemaul cooperative (協同圈) projects (事業), a "Saemaul Cooperative (協同圈) Project (事業) Promotion Committee (推進委員會)" is first formed, elected by the consensus (總意) of the residents. The Promotion Committee (推進委員會) selects one project (事業) per district (圈域) as a principle (原則), prioritizing projects that can maximize effectiveness (效果) among the common (共同) aspirations (宿願) of the participating (參與) villages. Additionally, during the project selection process, consideration is given to large-scale (大規模) regional development (地域開發) projects (事業) that can enhance (擧揚) the employment effects (就勞效果) within the district (圈域), and small-scale (小規模) projects (事業) are arranged to be promoted in the Saemaul beautification projects.

Saemaul cooperative (協同圈) projects (事業) related to the establishment of production bases (生産基盤造成) include the improvement and construction of farm roads (農路), paving of farm roads (農路), road construction and bridge construction (橋梁架設), and the improvement or repair of facilities related to water management such as weirs (洑), waterways (水路), small rivers (小河川), dikes (堤防), small reservoirs (小溜池), and pumping stations (揚水場), as well as the installation (設置) of communal warehouses (共同倉庫) and workplaces (作業場).

### A. Expansion (擴充) of Inter-village (部落間) Substructure (下部構造)

#### (1) Improvement (整備) and Construction (開設) of Inter-village (間) Farm Roads (農路)

The expansion (擴張) and improvement (整備) of farm roads (農路), or the construction of new straight roads, have significant economic (經濟的) implications beyond just improving the rural environment. Traditional farm roads (農路) in Korea are narrow, circuitous, and linear, allowing only people and livestock to pass through, making it difficult for ox carts (牛馬車) or automobiles (自動車) to traverse. This results in increased travel time to destinations (目的地) and significant constraints on the transportation of large quantities of goods (物量), directly impacting labor productivity (勞動生産).

Furthermore, the expansion (擴張) and improvement (整備) of farm roads (農路) are closely related to the mechanization (機械化) of agriculture. Even if land consolidation (耕地整理) is well underway, the narrowness (狹小) of farm roads (農路) can prevent agricultural machinery (農機械) from reaching the fields, making agricultural mechanization (機械化) practically difficult. Therefore, the first condition (條件) that must be addressed for agricultural mechanization (農業的(農業)機械化(機械化)) is the expansion (擴張) of farm roads (農路).

Recognizing the importance (重要性) of farm roads (農路) as described above, the cooperative (協同圈) project (事業) under the Saemaul Undong (運動) promotes the improvement (整備) of farm roads (農路).


--- (p. 402) ---

Preparation and establishment began with 37 projects in 1976, completing 64.7 km. In 1977, 390 projects were initiated, completing 69.1 km, and in 1978, 33 projects were started, completing 47.9 km. It is important to note that individual farm households' preparation or establishment were excluded here, focusing instead on cooperative circle projects between villages for farm road improvement and establishment.

Paving of farm roads began with 22 projects in 1977, completing 5.1 km. However, considering the actual usage of farm roads, paving has little economic significance. If farm roads are used in conjunction with general roads, the economic feasibility of paving would be high. However, for purely agricultural roads, it would be more desirable to use the funds for the expansion and improvement of other farm roads.

As this is a cooperative circle project between villages, separate from village-level Saemaul beautification projects, the start and achievements are relatively late and low. However, considering its economic importance, such projects need to be continuously promoted.

## (2) Road Construction and Bridge Installation

Road construction and bridge installation have two main economic significances. Firstly, they facilitate the smooth movement of production factors between villages, and secondly, they make the movement and joint shipment of agricultural and livestock products easier. Apart from economic effects, they also promote mutual cooperation systems between villages and facilitate communication with residents of other villages.

However, the most important aspect is the smooth and convenient movement of production factors, including labor, between villages. Throughout history, there has been little economic exchange between villages. This is especially true in terms of the exchange of goods through division of labor and the distribution of production factors. In extreme cases, each village has different levels of currency and different prices for production materials, particularly those produced by farms, creating a kind of closed economic system.

For efficient distribution of resources and competitive production of agricultural and livestock products, leading to cost-saving movements, it is necessary to break down the economic closure between villages. In this sense, road construction and bridge installation between villages hold great significance.


--- (p. 403) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Bridge construction (橋梁架設) in 1977 saw an impressive start of 71 projects, completing 2,117 meters. In 1979, 41 projects (件) were initiated, completing 2,577 meters. Bridge construction (橋梁架設) and road development (道路開設) projects hold significant economic and social importance. Therefore, they should be prioritized in regional development (廣域圈) projects and pursued with bold initiatives.

### B. River Management (河川管理)

Every year, floods (洪水) and water disasters (水害) occur frequently across the country. Due to the lack of trees on the mountains and minimal soil erosion (腐蝕土), rainwater quickly flows into rivers, causing these phenomena. Floods (洪水) damage crops (農作物) and disrupt agricultural activities, while water disasters (水害) destroy residents' homes (家屋) and farmland (農土). Sometimes, they even claim precious lives (人命). However, rivers are not unnecessary. Water is essential for growing crops (農作物) and producing food (食糧) vital for human survival (生存). It is also indispensable in daily life. The question is how to secure the necessary water and manage the excess to prevent water disasters (水害) proactively.

#### (1) Weirs (洑)

River management (河川管理) involves various types (種類) and forms (形態). First, consider weirs (洑). Weirs (洑) are low embankments built to store water or raise the water level (水位) for irrigation (灌漑) of fields higher than the river level. While the importance of weirs (洑) diminishes when rivers are in full flow, their role becomes crucial during droughts (旱魃) or when water levels are low for other reasons.

As part of cooperative (協同圈) projects, weir (洑) construction initiated in 1976 completed 37 projects (件), constructing 1,910 meters. In 1978, 7 projects (件) were started, completing 617 meters. Since weirs (洑) have already been installed in most necessary locations, new constructions are not as numerous. Instead, the task of repairing and maintaining existing weirs (洑) is more pressing. As weirs (洑) are crucial for irrigation (灌漑), they have been consistently maintained even before the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). In some aspects, rural cooperation (農村의 協同) initiatives began with the construction and maintenance of weirs (洑). As previously mentioned, economic exchange (經濟的 交換行爲) between villages did not occur


--- (p. 404) ---

Even if there were existing structures, mutual cooperation was often required to install and maintain them.
### (2) Waterways

Waterways are necessary to guide water from reservoirs or ponds to fields. Waterways share some similarities with footpaths but also have distinct differences. Just like footpaths, waterways should ideally follow a straight line to their destination to avoid detours, which can lead to water wastage and increased time. However, waterways should not necessarily be too large or wide. If they are disproportionately large or wide compared to the required water volume, it can lead to excessive water consumption, posing significant problems during droughts. Additionally, the ground surface of waterways must be sturdy. If the ground is not robust, a substantial amount of water will seep into the soil, reducing the effectiveness of the collective effort.

Most areas with fields already have waterways in place. Through the Saemaul cooperative circle projects, 11 projects were initiated in 1976, constructing 5,604 meters of waterways, and in 1978, 9 projects were initiated, completing 5,110 meters. Similar to reservoirs, it is crucial to reinforce and rationally improve existing waterways, not just focus on constructing new ones.

### (3) Small Streams

The improvement of small streams involves constructing concrete retaining walls, straightening detours, widening where necessary, and narrowing where appropriate to suit the given conditions. In 1976, 37 projects were initiated, completing 10,669 meters of stream improvements. In 1977, 36 projects were initiated, completing 5,272 meters, and in 1978, only 5 projects were undertaken, improving 1,760 meters.

### (4) Small Ponds

Small pond improvements involve constructing temporary reservoirs to store water flowing down from mountains or falling from the sky, which can then be used for cultivating crops. These temporary reservoirs are particularly meaningful for production base formation when fields are collectively owned by residents from multiple villages.

The improvement or construction of small ponds is a recent initiative under the Saemaul cooperative circle projects.


--- (p. 405) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Before 1978, there were no such projects, which is a notable characteristic. In 1978, three projects were initiated, completing 6,600 pyeong (坪) of small reservoirs (小溜池). In our country, where cultivated land is relatively scarce compared to population growth, increasing the area of farmland, particularly irrigated land, is crucial for ensuring a stable food supply. Therefore, the construction and maintenance of small reservoirs should be considered a key project of the Saemaul Undong, requiring continuous cooperation and effort from village residents to share the benefits.

Similarly, projects such as irrigation channels and small stream improvements play a vital role in production infrastructure development as cooperative community projects. Thus, they should be planned and pursued in conjunction with government investment.

### D. Inter-village Joint Warehouses

A characteristic of traditional natural villages in our country is the wide variation in the number of households and residents. Some villages are very small, while others are large. Larger villages with extensive economic activities can independently manage and operate warehouses and workshops. However, many villages are small and have limited economic activities centered around production, making it difficult to construct or establish independent warehouses or workshops.

For small villages, it would be more efficient to build and operate joint warehouses with neighboring villages rather than constructing them on a per-village basis, which would incur significant financial burdens. Our country has many mountains and valleys, often leading to multiple villages within the same region using the same roads and engaging in similar economic activities. Therefore, determining the location for joint warehouses is not particularly challenging.

Agricultural products and production materials tend to have large volumes, making warehouse utility highly valuable in a market economy. Storing fertilizers, other production materials, or government-purchased grains can reduce purchase costs and lower storage expenses for agricultural products. Additionally, it prevents storage costs from being transferred to middlemen, allowing farmers to benefit from the savings.

As part of inter-village cooperative projects, 28 joint warehouses were initiated in 1976.


--- (p. 406) ---

In 1976, a total area of 1,640 pyeong was constructed. There were no achievements in 1977, but in 1978, construction began on 6 buildings, completing 470 pyeong.

## La. Evaluation and Prospects of Inter-Village Businesses (협동권사업)

As defined earlier, inter-village businesses (협동권사업) refer to projects where residents of different villages jointly develop the living environment, production base, and specialized crops between villages. Detailed implementation projects related to the creation of a production base include the improvement and establishment of farm roads, the establishment of roads and bridges, river management, and the installation of shared warehouses and workspaces.

Looking at the annual progress of inter-village businesses in <Table 16>, from 1975 to 1980, 2,972 million won was supported for 975 areas.

Based on the experience and cultivated diligence, self-help, cooperation spirit, and strong will and passion, the development of the second living circle, the inter-village cooperation circle, has begun. Through various inter-village businesses, significant achievements have been made in expanding economic exchange between villages, which had traditionally maintained a closed economic system, and strengthening the consensus system. However, it is difficult to expect economic exchange and cooperation between residents of different villages without a change in their consciousness structure. Just because roads have been expanded, bridges have been built, and shared warehouses and workspaces have been established does not mean that residents' consciousness and behavior have changed quickly. Changes in consciousness and behavior take time.

From a theoretical perspective, it was expected that various exchanges between villages would lead to the efficient distribution of production factors and resources, as well as the exchange of products. However, in reality, it is difficult to expect significant horizontal exchanges.

From the perspective of creating a production base, in the future, inter-village businesses should select and promote projects directly related to residents' production activities, such as improving and repairing irrigation channels, managing small rivers and dikes, and installing small reservoirs and water pumping stations through cooperation among residents of different villages with common interests in the region. Additionally, the establishment or improvement of farm roads and the construction of bridges should continue.


--- (p. 407) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

These are the tasks to be undertaken.
Cooperative businesses (事業) that have a direct or indirect relationship with agricultural production (農業生産) are expected to have a bright future and should continue to be pursued.
