Source: Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries

In 1972, trial plots for new rice varieties were established centering around main production areas. After achieving success here, collective farming sites began to be established nationwide. Starting in 1974, vegetable and livestock production teams organized by farmers themselves were set up in each village according to local conditions, promoting collective farming and cooperative agricultural practices that boosted production. The rural community shifted from relying solely on the government to taking the initiative to solve all problems on their own.

Despite the challenges of rural labor shortages, villagers worked together to increase fertilizer production and improve soil fertility. They jointly controlled pests and diseases and overcame severe flood damage. Additionally, they eagerly adopted improved new varieties and new farming techniques, and the joint use of agricultural machinery gradually increased. It was this change in spirit and shift to cooperative methods that made dramatic agricultural production increases possible.


--- (p. 439) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

### II. Soil Improvement and Fertility Enhancement

Increasing agricultural production (農業生産) can be achieved either by expanding the cultivated area (耕地面積) or by increasing the yield per unit area (單位面積當生産量). However, for our country, expanding the cultivated area (耕地面積) is almost impossible to expect.

In reality, the cultivated area (耕地面積) in our country, which was 2.3 million ha in 1970 (年), decreased to 2.21 million ha in 1979 (年), a reduction of 90,000 ha. This is well known to be due to industrialization (工業化) and urbanization (都市化) following the high-growth (高度成長) policy (政策), which has encroached upon farmland (農耕地). This trend is expected to continue in the future. Therefore, to increase agricultural production (農業增産), there is no choice but to increase productivity (生産性) per unit area (單位面積當).

For this, excellent new varieties (新品種) need to be developed (開發) and disseminated (普及), and farming techniques (營農技術) need to be improved. However, the "land," which is the basis of agricultural production (農業生産), must be vibrant (活氣) and alive. Land being vibrant (活氣) means that it can support the active habitation (棲息) of various microorganisms (各種微生物) and has the ability to supply sufficient nutrients (充分營養分) to crops (作物). Only then can crops (作物) grow vigorously and become resilient to various diseases, pests (病蟲害), and drought and water damage (旱水害), leading to high yields (多所出).

However, so far, the conditions for farming (營農與件) in our country have seen more factors (要因) that weaken soil fertility (地力) rather than enhance it. That is, with the expanded dissemination (擴大普及) of high-yield new varieties (多收穫新品種), the use of chemical fertilizers (化學肥料) has increased significantly, leading to soil acidification (酸性化) and easier aging (老化).

Additionally, as the agricultural labor force (農村勞動力) has become predominantly female (婦女子) and aged (老齡化), it has become difficult to increase the production of compost (堆肥增產), which requires a lot of labor (勞動力). In fact, even in the early 1970s (年代初), our farmers (農家) focused more on the short-term use of convenient chemical fertilizers (化學肥料) rather than long-term (長期的) efforts to enhance soil fertility (地力增進). Despite the government (政府) providing free soil improvement agents (土壤改良劑) such as agricultural lime (農用石灰), farmers often left them unused in their fields. Moreover, they did not put much effort into increasing compost production (堆肥增產).

However, with the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) as a catalyst (契機), farmers' awareness (農民認識) of soil fertility enhancement (地力增進) improved. Additionally, as farming machinery (耕耘機) and tractors began to be disseminated (普及), the entire village (全村住民) started to collaborate (共同) in producing compost (堆肥生産) collectively (共同), leading to a nationwide compost production movement (全國堆肥增產運動). Conversely, the use of soil improvement agents (土壤改良劑) such as silicate fertilizers and agricultural lime (農用石灰)


--- (p. 440) ---

The tendency to avoid (忌避) decreased. As a result, although the amount of compost produced (堆肥生産量) decreased from 42 million (百萬) tons in 1970 to 32 million (百萬) tons in 1974, it increased again to 37 million (百萬) tons by 1979. Considering that straw, previously used for thatched roofs (草家地붕), began to be used as compost due to the improvement of rural housing (農村住宅改良), the amount of compost produced has significantly increased.

The use of silicate fertilizer (規산質肥料), a soil conditioner (土壤改良劑), increased from 17,000 (千) tons in 1970 to 350,000 (千) tons in 1979 despite being supplied on a paid basis (有償供給). The use of agricultural lime (農用石灰) has also been consistent. Additionally, the areas of soil import (客土) and deep plowing (深耕作業面積) have recently increased again, indicating that farmers' (農民) motivation (意慾) and effort (努力) for soil improvement (地力增進) are on the rise.

When comparing the amount of fertilizer applied per unit area (單位面積當施肥量) with Southeast Asian (東南亞) countries, along with Japan (日本), Korea has already reached the highest level, and further increase in chemical fertilizer application (化學肥料增投) is expected with the development and popularization (開發及普及) of high-yield varieties (多收穫品種). Consequently, the necessity for soil improvement (地力增進必要性) is also expected to grow. (Fertilizer application per hectare in 1977: Korea (韓國) 457.7kg, Japan (日本) 428.1kg, Taiwan (臺灣) 329.9kg, Malaysia 49.6kg, Indonesia 35.0kg, Philippines 32.2kg, Thailand (泰國) 15.6kg). Government (政府) policies (施策) that actively support soil improvement (地力增進) as a catalyst (契機) for the Saemaul Undong (運動) must be established to ensure that the goal of increased food production (食糧增産課題) is achieved without hindrance (蹉跌).

### Da. Improvement of Varieties (品種改良) and Increase in Yield (收量提高)

There is no more distinct and reliable method of increasing production (增産方法) than developing new seeds (種子) with significantly higher yields (所出) than those previously cultivated (栽培). Since the establishment of the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳) in 1962, various crop (農作物) and livestock (家畜) improvement projects (品種改良事業) have been actively promoted to improve local varieties (在來種) and develop new varieties (新品種).

By introducing excellent foreign seeds (優秀種子) and crossbreeding them with local varieties (在來種), various new varieties (新品種) that are resistant to diseases and pests (病蟲害), grow well, and have high yields (所出) have been developed and popularized (普及). Among them, the most outstanding achievement is the development and popularization of high-yield new varieties (多收穫新品種) of law seed, known as the "Green Revolution" (綠色革命). The government (政府) began developing new varieties (新品種) in the late 1960s to achieve self-sufficiency (自給) in rice, the main grain (主穀).

After numerous trips to Japan (日本) and the Philippines for the development of new varieties (新品種), domestic adaptation tests (國內適應試驗) were conducted, and unified rice (統一벼) began to be distributed to farms (農家) for the first time in 1972. Since then, the area of cultivation (栽培面積) of new varieties (新品種) has rapidly expanded each year. Specifically, the area of cultivation (栽培面積) of new varieties (新品種) in 1974 was


--- (p. 441) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The area under cultivation, which was 1,814ha (15.2% of the total area) in 1971, increased to 533,000ha (44.6% of the total area) in 1976 and reached 929,000ha (close to 80% of the total area) in 1978. As a result, Korea's rice production, which had remained at around 2 million koku (石) per year during the 1960s, surpassed 3 million koku (石) in 1974 and, just three years later in 1977, achieved an unprecedented global record of over 4 million koku (石), enabling complete self-sufficiency in rice.

In terms of increased yield per 10a (當), the average annual increase was only 2.9kg during the 1960s. However, from 1972, when new varieties began to be disseminated, the annual yield increased by an average of 32.4kg. Consequently, by the early 1970s, when the yield per unit area was still significantly lower than in Japan, Korea surpassed Japan in 1974 and has continued to do so. Moreover, among the 16 countries in Southeast Asia, Korea ranks third, following Malaysia and Thailand, in terms of the rate of increase in agricultural production. (Calculation based on FAO production statistics for 1961-65 compared to 1975-79)

What made this Green Revolution possible? The primary factor was, of course, the active development and dissemination of new varieties.

However, the secondary contribution must be attributed to the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). The fact that the development and dissemination of new varieties coincided almost exactly with the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) cannot be dismissed as a mere coincidence.

If these new varieties had been disseminated during the 1960s, before the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the increase in production might have been much less, and the term "Green Revolution" might not have been applicable. This is because the rapid and successful dissemination of new varieties within such a short period can be attributed to the following factors.

Firstly, the adoption of collective farming methods, such as the installation of collective seedbeds and collective pest control, was made possible by the establishment of the cooperative management methods of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Secondly, new varieties require early planting and thus necessitate the early installation of seedbeds, early transplanting, increased fertilization, timely pest control, and other new farming techniques, as well as persuasive efforts. The cultivation of these new varieties was made possible due to the Saemaul Undong's (New Community Movement) emphasis on self-help and diligence.


--- (p. 442) ---

### La. Cooperation in Farming and Overcoming Disasters

Agriculture targets organic life forms, unlike factory production, and is thus exposed to weather conditions and pests, directly affected by them.

Natural disasters can suddenly appear and spread rapidly, requiring immediate action to prevent crop failure. However, individual efforts are insufficient, and even if one's own fields are treated, neighboring fields with pests can quickly spread the issue to one's own.

Thus, cooperative efforts and joint work are essential for disaster management. However, before the Saemaul Undong in the 1960s, there were almost no measures against various disasters, and farmers often blamed the heavens for their misfortunes. This was because tasks that required the collective effort of the entire village were instead handled individually by each farmer.

In the 1970s, disasters became more frequent and severe. As the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides increased, crops became more susceptible to diseases and pests. For instance, rice pests affected 76,000 ha in 1970, but this increased to 425,000 ha in 1976 and 911,000 ha in 1978.

However, unlike in the past, farmers did not passively endure these challenges. The entire village came together for joint pest control work using newly supplied powered pest control machines. They treated areas ten times larger than those affected by pests each year.

For example, while 3.8 million ha were treated in 1970, over 10 million ha were treated from 1978 onwards, successfully overcoming pest issues. Additionally, in 1978, an unprecedented severe drought struck, but farmers and the entire nation united to overcome this unprecedented drought, demonstrating that collective strength and effort could conquer any natural disaster.

Notably, a similar severe drought occurred in 1968, before the Saemaul Undong, resulting in a 30% reduction in rice harvests. However, the Saemaul spirit


--- (p. 443) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動)

In the latter half of the 1970s (年代), despite experiencing more severe droughts than in the 1960s (年代), rice production exceeded 40 million bags (萬石), demonstrating the immense power of diligence (勤勉), cooperation (協同), and cooperative methods (協同方式).

### Farm Machinery (農業機械) for Shared Use (共同利用)

The rapid industrialization (工業化) that took place throughout the 1960s (年代) and 1970s (年代) accelerated the outflow (流出) of the rural population (農村人口), particularly the young and middle-aged (靑壯年層), thereby contributing to the sharp rise in rural wages and exacerbating the shortage of agricultural labor.

As a result, the mechanization (機械化) of agricultural production (生産) emerged as a key priority (當面課題) for the government (政府) starting in the 1970s (年代).

The government had been focusing on the supply of small-scale (小型) farm equipment such as plows (耕耘機), sprayers (噴霧機), threshers (脫穀機), and water pumps (揚水機). From the latter half of the 1970s (年代), it began to prioritize the supply of small-scale (小型) farm machinery for the complete mechanization (一貫機械化) of rice farming (水稻作), including transplanting machines (移秧機) and binders, as well as large-scale (大型) farm machinery such as tractors, combines, and dryers.

However, given the reality of Korean agriculture (農村實情), where small-scale (零細) farmers (小農) with less than 1 hectare of cultivated land (耕地) account for more than two-thirds (2/3) of the total, it was impractical for individual farm households (農家) to afford high-priced (高價) agricultural machinery.

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Purchasing and utilizing machinery is not only difficult in terms of economic capability but also lacks economic feasibility. For instance, if we assume that the surplus of a farming household's economy is used to purchase a tractor, Japanese farming households can do so in 2 years, whereas it would take Korean farming households 16 years.

To address these issues of agricultural mechanization, the Saemaul Undong actively promoted the shared use of agricultural machinery as part of its initiatives. To promote the village-level shared use of agricultural machinery, work teams were organized at the village level, and guidelines for the shared operation of agricultural machinery were issued and actively fostered. However, despite the number of work team organizations reaching 15,000 by 1977, significant achievements were not made in the shared use of agricultural machinery.

After the supply of large agricultural machinery such as tractors, combines, and dryers, as well as agricultural machinery like transplanters and binders, the situation changed, and the shared use of agricultural machinery began to progress actively. According to a nationwide survey conducted by the Agricultural Cooperatives' Research Department as of August 30, 1980, the number of agricultural machinery shared use organizations totaled approximately 5,340. In terms of the year of organization, only 2% of the total were established before 1976, with over 80% organized after 1979. The forms of shared use are as follows: individual ownership lease-type shared use accounts for 50% of the total, followed by shared ownership shared use among several farming households, and village-level shared use accounts for about 10%.

As such, the fundamental reason for the recent active promotion of the shared use of agricultural machinery is that agricultural machinery with extremely high work capacity, such as transplanters, binders, and combines, have been supplied recently, despite the annual workable days being extremely limited. The annual workable days per machine are 18 days for transplanters, 30 days for binders, 26 days for combines, and 30 days for dryers, all within 1 month, which is an extremely short period. On the other hand, the annual work capacity is 12~21ha for transplanters, 15~27ha for binders, and 9~18ha for combines, revealing that one machine can handle farming work for 10~20 farming households.

### 4. Comprehensive Development of Regional Agriculture and Increase in Agricultural Income

#### a. Comprehensive Development and Model Cultivation by Village Type

(1) Setting the Direction of Comprehensive Development by Village Type
As the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) spread to almost every village, starting from 1973, all 34,655 villages across the nation were categorized into three levels—basic villages, self-help villages, and self-reliant villages—based on their development level. Support was then provided to promote Saemaul projects according to the capabilities of these villages.


--- (p. 447) ---

It began.

In 1973, an average of 494,000 won per village was provided by the government, but due to the principle of prioritizing outstanding villages, the scale of government support varied depending on the level of development. Specifically, basic villages received 414,000 won, self-help villages received 277,000 won, and self-reliant villages received 2,446,000 won. In the case of self-reliant villages, they received government support nearly five times the national average per village.

The level of voluntary participation by village residents, following the differences in the scale of government support, also showed significant variations depending on the level of village development. Nationwide, the average resident's share per village was 2,217,000 won, but basic villages contributed 2,488,000 won, self-help villages 1,696,000 won, and self-reliant villages 3,192,000 won, indicating a high level of voluntary participation by residents of self-reliant villages.

However, in the case of self-reliant villages, as the scale of government support increased, the voluntary participation of residents did not increase proportionally, resulting in a lower proportion of resident's share in the total investment per village compared to other villages. Specifically, while the average resident's share nationwide reached almost 82%, self-reliant villages fell short of even 60%. This relatively low level of voluntary participation by residents of self-reliant villages was not due to a lack of resident's willingness to participate but rather due to the lack of planned direction for income increase.

Therefore, in 1974, income-generating business development directions were proposed based on the village's location, special characteristics, and the type and scale of existing resources. The aim was to support residents in developing businesses suitable for their village's characteristics, creating and implementing plans autonomously.

To set the income-generating business development directions, the government first conducted an income survey targeting 500 sample villages with a total of 40,000 households.

The results showed significant differences in household income levels depending on the village's location type. Specifically, the income per household was highest in plain villages at 572,000 won, followed by mid-mountain villages at 535,000 won, mountain villages at 517,000 won, and suburban villages at 512,000 won. Fishing villages had the lowest household income at 465,000 won.

In addition, there were also significant differences in high-income sources depending on the village's location type.


--- (p. 448) ---

An analysis of the income sources of farm households that have already achieved a per-household income of over 1,400,000 won with less than 1 hectare of cultivated land revealed that:

* Plain villages derived 31% of their income from processed agricultural products,
* Mountain villages obtained 43% from livestock products,
* Fishing villages gained 29% from aquaculture,
* Suburban villages earned 75% from livestock and horticulture.

These findings suggest that farm households should focus on regional specialization of agricultural production suited to the village's location to increase their income.

Based on the survey results, five basic types of income-generating businesses were proposed, tailored to the characteristics of each region. While all villages should commonly pursue food production increase, the priority for income business development should be:

* For plain villages: Specialty crops, livestock, fruit trees, and vegetables in that order,
* For mid-mountain villages: Livestock, forestry, fruit trees, and specialty crops in that order,
* For mountain villages: Forestry, livestock, specialty crops, and fruit trees in that order,
* For fishing villages: Aquaculture, livestock, specialty crops, and vegetables in that order,
* For suburban villages: Vegetables, fruit trees, livestock, and specialty crops in that order.

## (2) Establishment of Long-term Income Increase Plans by Village

After setting development directions by village type, 4,000 villages were selected from the 7,000 self-sufficient villages in 1974. Residents of these villages were tasked with establishing 7-year income increase plans (1975-1981) with 1981 as the target year.

An analysis of the income increase plans completed in the first phase for 138 villages showed that the target year for achieving a per-household income of 1,400,000 won was 1978 for plain villages, 1980 for mid-mountain and mountain villages, and 1981 for fishing and suburban villages (see Table 35).

Regarding income structure, the proportion of agricultural income is expected to decrease from 84% in 1974 to 77% in 1981, while non-agricultural income is projected to increase from 16% to 23%.


--- (p. 449) ---

It was found that for small-scale farming households (零細農家) where food crops (食糧作物) are the center of agricultural management (農業經營), there was a tendency to specialize (專業化) in high-profit (收益性) special crops (特作) or livestock (畜産部門).

In terms of resource (資源) utilization (利用), the highest interest (關心) was shown in the development (開發) and utilization (利用) of mountainous areas (山地), with an expected (豫想) 24.8ha per village (當), followed by the creation (造成) of meadows (草地) at 8.2ha, and also a high interest (關關) in the utilization (利用) of public water (公有水) resources (資源), with a scale (規模) reaching 6ha per village (當).

In terms of land (土地) utilization (利用) measurements (計測), paddies (畓) were greatly utilized (利用) for increased food (食糧) production (增產) through double cropping (二毛作), while fields (田) showed a strong tendency (性向) to be used for the cultivation (栽培) of economic crops (經濟作物) such as fruit (果實), vegetables (野菜), and specialty crops (特用作物). For mountainous areas (山地), there was a strong tendency (傾向) to utilize (利用) them as timber forests (用材林), mulberry fields (桑田), and meadows (草地).

In terms of the characteristics (特性) of village types (類型別), fishing villages (漁村) showed a focus (關心) on expanding cultivated land (耕地) and improving irrigation facilities (水利施設), while plains (平野) and suburban (都市近郊) villages showed a focus on the modernization (近代化) of distribution facilities (流通施設). Mountainous (山間) and mid-mountain (中山間) villages showed a greater interest (關心) in the creation (造成) of meadows (草地) and the development (開發) of mountainous agriculture (山地農業).

In terms of investment plans (投資計劇), the average annual investment (投資額) per village (當) during the planning period (計劃期間) was 7,500 thousand (千) won (圓), with facility investment (施設投資) accounting for the largest share (比重) at 39%, followed by livestock (畜産) at 28%.

If the annual investment (投資額) per village (當) is expanded (擴大) and estimated (推定) on a national (全國) scale (單位), it amounts to a total (總) of 1,326 billion (億) won (圓).


--- (p. 450) ---

In 1975, the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries' total investment amounted to 269.2 billion won, nearly 50% of which was allocated to this business plan. Due to the enormous scale of financial investment required, this business plan, which was established in a short period of time by merely gathering the opinions of residents without undergoing necessary pre-investigation, data collection, and analysis of economic feasibility and rationality, had significant practical issues. Although it could not be implemented due to various factors such as problems inherent in the plan itself and constraints in fund-raising, it had great significance and achievements in terms of education.

Firstly, the establishment of long-term plans for the future by the residents at the village level not only enabled village residents to have a vision for the future but also particularly stimulated the development of mountainous agricultural development and water resources, which had been idle resources.

Secondly, as the direction of key business development varied depending on the characteristics of each village, it became possible to set efficient administrative guidance and support directions.

Thirdly, the establishment of long-term plans served as an opportunity for research and practical training for village residents, village leaders, and responsible officials, resulting in significant educational effects.

### (3) Achievements in Cultivating Excellent, Self-Sufficient, and Model Saemaul Villages

The Saemaul Undong began at the village level. As the Saemaul Undong progressed from the stage of basic life environment improvement and spiritual development to the stage of income increase, the government made various policy efforts and endeavors to further substantiate and sustain the Saemaul Undong at the village level. From 1973 to 1978, over six years, the government and related agricultural and forestry agencies competitively promoted various businesses, including the Excellent Saemaul Special Support Project, Income Increase Self-Sufficient Village Cultivation, Structural Improvement Model Village Cultivation, Cooperative Saemaul Cultivation, and Large-Scale Saemaul Income Increase Model Village Cultivation.

The contents of these excellent and model village cultivation projects were mutually similar, but there were significant differences in support methods depending on the supervising agencies.

#### (a) Excellent Saemaul Special Support Project


--- (p. 451) ---

# Chapter 5: Practice and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

One of the fundamental principles (根本原理) of promoting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is that residents (住民) themselves solve their own problems (問題) based on the residents' diligence (勤勉), self-help (自助), cooperative spirit (協同精神), and voluntary (自發的) participation, and that they are supported (支援) to do so autonomously (自律的). Therefore, external (外部) or government (政府) support (支援) for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is not essential (本質的), but rather aims to accelerate (加速化) the movement through minimal (最小) support (支援) and to maximize (最大) residents' self-help (自助) and cooperative (協同的) efforts (努力). Moreover, when providing support (支援), the principle of promoting goodwill competition (善意的競爭) among villages (相互間) was applied to maximize (極大化) the support effect (支援效果), and the priority support principle (優先支援原則) for excellent Saemaul villages (優秀새마을) was implemented.

According to these support principles (支援原則), the special support project (特別支援事業) for excellent Saemaul villages (優秀새마을) was carried out to enable villages that had consistently done well in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to pursue desired projects (宿願事業) with special support (特別支援). The aim was to instill a sense of accomplishment and pride (矜持) in the supported villages (支援受村), encouraging them to pursue Saemaul projects (새마을事業) with even greater enthusiasm (熱誠的), while stimulating neighboring villages (隣近마을) that did not receive support to develop a desire for business development (事業開發欲) and competitive spirit (競爭心), thereby promoting new advancements (促進). This project (事業) was conducted under the auspices (主管) of the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部) from 1973 to 1980, targeting an average of approximately 4,000 villages (個) per year, totaling 33,742 villages (個). Each village (當) received 100-150 million won (萬圓), amounting to a total of 44.1 billion won (億) in subsidies (補助金).

The contents (內容) of the special support project (特別支援事業) include more than ten types (餘種) of projects (事業), ranging from production infrastructure improvement (生産基盤整備事業) to production income (生産所得事業) and cultural welfare (文化福祉事業). The characteristic (特徵) of these projects (事業) is that the benefits of development (開發惠澤) are not monopolized (獨占) by specific farming households (特定農家) but are shared equally (均等) among all residents (住民) of the village (村).

However, all the aforementioned projects (事業) were not implemented as comprehensive (綜合的) package programs (package program) intensively (集中的) invested (投入) in the target villages (對象村), but rather, the villagers (住民) made a joint decision (共同意思決定) to select only 1-2 projects (事業) out of the more than ten types (餘種) available. Nevertheless, production income projects (生産所得事業) were generally prioritized (一般優先的), and villages were encouraged (勸獎) to develop and cultivate income-specific crops (所得特化作物) suitable for their regional (地域) characteristics (特性) and to establish main production clusters (主産團地) at the village level (單位). The limitations (制限) on the number of projects (事業件數) and scale (規模) were inevitable (不可避) due to the restriction (制限) of the support funds (支援資金規模) of 100-150 million won (萬圓) per village (當). In particular, the active promotion (積極勸獎) of production income projects (生産所得事業) was aimed at maximizing (極大化) the support effect (支援效果) while ensuring the continuous (持續的) implementation of Saemaul projects (새마을事業).


--- (p. 452) ---

The purpose was to expand it.
In addition, the Ministry of the Interior (內務部) supported 4,924 villages, including islands, coastal fishing villages, and villages along railways, with a total of 24.6 billion won (2.46 million dollars) from 1975 to 1976. The funds, amounting to 500,000 won (50,000 dollars) per village, were primarily used for production and income-generating businesses and national land improvement projects.

Furthermore, from 1976 to 1978, the government provided special education for village leaders in 1,494 backward villages. Following this, each village received 1 million won (100,000 dollars), totaling 1.494 billion won (149.4 million dollars), to support the residents' long-cherished projects. This aim was to enhance the residents' enthusiasm and confidence in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

### (b) Exploring the Development of Self-Sufficient Villages (自立마을) and Structural Improvement Villages (構造改善마을)

Three structural weaknesses of agricultural production in our country have been emphasized: the small scale of farming, the low rate of basic equipment, and the reliance on rice and wheat for subsistence farming. Due to these structural weaknesses, a vicious cycle of low agricultural productivity, low income, widening urban-rural income gaps, and the intensification of small-scale farming has repeated. Consequently, meeting the demand for agricultural products and increasing farmers' income have consistently been pressing issues in agricultural policy.

To address the urban-rural income gap, measures such as price maintenance for agricultural and livestock products and the low-cost supply of agricultural materials have been emphasized. However, these measures have been temporary and short-term due to the heavy fiscal burden and their impact on overall prices, making sustained implementation difficult. Therefore, fundamental and long-term measures for improving agricultural productivity and sustainably increasing farmers' income have been emphasized as major agricultural policy tasks. These include the rational improvement of agricultural structures.

Agricultural structure improvement projects have long been a focus of interest worldwide. Japan, for instance, began its structural improvement projects in 1961, completing its first and second ten-year plans and starting new agricultural structure improvement projects in 1978. In our country, attempts were made in the 1960s to foster self-sufficient and stable farming households, but these efforts failed due to inadequate conditions and misguided development directions. However, taking the spread of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) as an opportunity, efforts to improve agricultural structures began in earnest in 1973.


--- (p. 453) ---

# Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul business (事業) was carried out in parallel with the agricultural structure improvement business (農業構造改善事業). The Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (農水產部) decided to implement this business (事業) in two stages. In the first stage (段階), the focus was not on economic zones (經濟圈) but on villages, linking the business (事業) with outstanding Saemaul villages as model projects (示範事業). In the second stage (段階), a full-scale agricultural structure improvement business (農業構造事業) centered on economic zones (經濟圈) was to be promoted. This business (事業) was carried out over a four-year period from 1973 to 1976, through the following three stages:

First, in 1973, the Ministry of Home Affairs (內務部) selected 2,307 self-reliant villages (自立마을) out of which 1,832 villages with particularly strong voluntary development (自發的 개발) were chosen. These were nurtured as general self-reliant villages (一般自立마을). From these, one village per county (郡) was selected, totaling 138 villages, which were nurtured as income-increasing self-reliant villages (所得增大自立마을). Furthermore, one village per province (道) was selected from the income-increasing self-reliant villages (所得增大自立마을), totaling 8 villages, which were nurtured as model villages for structural improvement (構造改善示範마을).

For the nurturing of general self-reliant villages (一般自立마을), funds amounting to 870 million won per village, totaling 162 billion won, were provided over a three-year period from 1973 to 1975. Of the total funds, 53% was allocated to livestock (畜產), cash crops, sericulture (蠶業), and other income-generating agricultural businesses (生産所得事業). The next largest allocations were 24.7% and 13.4% for land infrastructure improvement (土地基盤整備事業) and agricultural mechanization (農業機械化事業) respectively, while only 4.4% of the total support funds were allocated to circulation facilities (流通施設). Therefore, it can be seen that the general self-reliant village nurturing business (一般自立마을育成事業) placed the greatest emphasis on increasing agricultural production (增產) and expanding development (開發擴大) to increase agricultural income (農業所得增大).

For the nurturing of income-increasing self-reliant villages (所得增大自立마을), outstanding agricultural extension workers (指導士) from the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳) were permanently stationed as resident agricultural extension workers (駐在指導士) to strengthen agricultural technical guidance (營農技術指導). Additionally, funds amounting to 106 million won per village, totaling 14.6 billion won, were provided over a three-year period from 1973 to 1975. In the case of income-increasing self-reliant villages (所得增大自立마을), almost all of the support funds were invested in expanding development (開發擴大) for growth agriculture (成長農業). The reason for this was that the production infrastructure improvement business (生産基盤整備事業) for income-increasing self-reliant villages (所得增大自立마을) was almost entirely completed.

The structural improvement model village nurturing business (構造改善示範마을育成事業) went one step further than the income-increasing self-reliant village nurturing business (所得增大自立마을育成事業), placing the greatest emphasis on achieving the self-sufficiency and stability of individual farm management (個別農家單位農業經營自立安定化). To this end, various businesses (種事業) such as agricultural mechanization (農業機械化), specialization of farm management (農業經營專門化), and expansion of the scale of management (經營規模擴大) were promoted in an integrated manner. This was carried out over a four-year period from 1973 to 1976.


--- (p. 454) ---

### (Da) Performance of the Saemaul Income Augmentation Demonstration Villages

As the Saemaul Undong shifted its focus to augmenting farm household income, the Rural Development Administration also began promoting the Saemaul Income Augmentation Demonstration Village Development Project as a 7-year plan from 1973 to 1979. Initially, one village per county was selected nationwide, totaling 138 villages. However, in 1974, one additional village was selected from each Self-Help Village and Basic Village, excluding Jeju Province, bringing the total to 154 villages for the demonstration project.

For the demonstration development villages, trained rural leaders were stationed in each village to investigate the management status of farm households and village resources. Based on these findings, they collaborated with village residents to establish farm household-specific agricultural improvement plans and comprehensive village development plans, guiding and supporting their implementation. Additionally, new crop varieties and technologies were prioritized for introduction and dissemination to elevate the villagers' agricultural technology level to that of individual farms. Furthermore, support was provided to utilize idle resources around the village and monetize them.

To improve individual farm management, the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries focused on expanding livestock and horticulture, key growth industries, as well as modernizing distribution facilities by enhancing agricultural mechanization and storage and processing facilities for agricultural and livestock products. To effectively promote these projects, a total of 196 million won (subsidies) was provided to each village from 1973 to 1978.

Starting in 1977, the Saemaul Income Augmentation Comprehensive Development Project was implemented under the auspices of the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (NACF), leading to the completion of the initial plan one year ahead of schedule by 1978. From 1979 onwards, the target villages were fully transitioned to the Saemaul Income Comprehensive Development Project areas.

### (Ra) Performance of the Cooperative Saemaul Villages

As the government's agricultural policies shifted to focus on Saemaul income augmentation, the NACF also began promoting the "Cooperative Saemaul" villages, selecting one village per county nationwide, totaling 138 villages from 1973 onwards. The development goals and methods of the Cooperative Saemaul villages were also attempted by the government and related agencies, focusing on outstanding...


--- (p. 455) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The cultivation of self-sufficient model villages is almost the same. That is, the cultivation project of cooperative Saemaul villages also aims to ① promote the development of high-income and high-efficiency agriculture, achieve the goal of increasing farmers' income by 1.4 million won in 1981, and cultivate model villages that can achieve this goal ahead of schedule, and ② through the demonstration effect of these model villages, lead all villages across the nation to the level of these model villages by 1981.

The cultivation method is also not a single-item or business development but a comprehensive development method, as in the case of the self-sufficient village and structural improvement model village cultivation projects for increasing income by the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, and the model village cultivation project for increasing income by the Agricultural Development Administration. In other words, various projects such as the improvement of the production base, the development of production and income businesses, the expansion of common-use and circulation facilities, the mechanization of agricultural production, the improvement of the living environment, and the expansion of cultural and welfare facilities are promoted as a package program, and the target village is comprehensively developed with a focus on this.

In terms of differences in development strategies from other model village cultivation projects, they can be found in aspects such as ① the maximum utilization of the internal organization of the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation, the production team organization, ② the setting of development priorities, and ③ the linkage between the village comprehensive development project and the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation business.

The National Agricultural Cooperative Federation aims to promote the cooperative and scientific nature of farming through the step-by-step strengthening of production team activities and to achieve high-income and high-efficiency agricultural production through this, and it has made this the basic strategy of village comprehensive development.

To strengthen the step-by-step cultivation of production team activities, in the case of food crops, the focus is on variety unification, joint pest control, and joint work in the initial stage, and then on the joint use of farm machinery, and further on joint packaging and joint shipment. In the case of livestock production teams, in the initial stage, the focus is on the joint purchase of feed and livestock, the joint use of farm machinery, the next stage is on the joint use of facilities such as barns, and the joint creation of pastures, and in a more advanced stage, joint breeding and joint shipment are attempted, and the step-by-step cultivation direction of the production team is set.

According to the priority of such development strategies, in the initial stage of cultivating cooperative Saemaul villages ('73~'74), the greatest emphasis was placed on improving the village environment, developing idle mountainous areas, introducing income crops such as Korean beef, dairy cows, and pigs, and mechanizing agricultural production. In the next stage ('75~'76), more emphasis was placed on the joint creation of pastures and the expansion of joint-use facilities such as barns, pigsties, workshops, and breeding facilities. In the completion stage of the project in '77


--- (p. 456) ---

By the year 1978, emphasis was placed on the expansion of circulation facilities such as storage warehouses (貯藏庫), sales outlets (販賣場), and village factories (도정공장). To promote the comprehensive development projects (開發事業) of cooperative Saemaul villages in a phased manner, the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協) provided medium-term (中期) and short-term (短期) funds of 82 million won per village annually, totaling 432 million won over the six years from 1973 to 1978.

(4) Achievements and Issues of Demonstration Saemaul Village Development Projects (事業)

(a) Achievements of Demonstration Saemaul Village Development (育成)

The achievements of the demonstration Saemaul village development projects, carried out by the government (政府), the Rural Development Administration (農村振興廳), the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (農協), and other related agencies (有關機關) with the same purpose (目的) in various forms (形態) and methods (方法), can be observed from multiple perspectives (側面). Not only did it develop the Saemaul movement (運動) in rural areas (農村) into a sustained movement (運動), but it also achieved significant results in the improvement (整備) and expansion (擴充) of the production base (生産基盤), the expansion (擴充) of production and circulation facilities (流通施設), the promotion (促進) of agricultural mechanization (農業機械化), the development (開發) and expansion (擴大) of growth agriculture (成長農業), and the increase (增大) of farm income (農家所得) through these efforts.

Looking at the achievements in the improvement of the production base (生産基盤), the cooperative Saemaul villages have accomplished the development of idle mountainous land (遊休山地), the creation of meadows (草地), and land consolidation (耕地整理), with the improvement (整備) and expansion (擴充) of the production base (生産基盤) reaching 8.7 hectares per village.


--- (p. 457) ---

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

There were various production and distribution facilities such as barns (畜舍), silos, communal workplaces (共同作業場), livestock facilities (畜産施設), warehouses (倉庫), storage houses (貯藏庫), and sales venues (販賣場). From 1973 to 1978, over a period of 6 years, an average of 13.3 buildings (棟) per village were constructed. Additionally, agricultural machinery such as tractors (耕耘機), sprayers, and threshers were supplied at an average of 32.2 units (臺) per village. Furthermore, livestock such as Hanwoo (韓牛), dairy cows, pigs, rabbits, and goats, which were key projects for income increase (所得增大), were newly introduced at an average of 176.2 heads (頭) per village.

As a result of these development achievements (開發成果) in various village-level projects (村單位各種事業), income increase (所得增大) was realized. In the case of model development villages (示範育成마을), the per-household income (戶當所得) of farming households (農家戶當所得) was significantly higher compared to other general villages (一般마을). Specifically, the nationwide average per-household income (全國平均戶當所得) in 1978 increased by 415% compared to 1972, reaching 1,884,000 won (千원). However, in the model villages (示範마을), the income increased by an additional 100 percentage points, reaching a 514% increase, surpassing the nationwide average level (平均水準) in 1979 at 2,348,000 won (千원) (see Table 37 for reference).

When examining the achievements in increasing farming household income (農家所得增大實績) by village type (마을類型別), in 1972, the income level (所得水準) was highest in fishing villages (漁村마을), followed by suburban (都農近郊), intermediate plains (平野中間), and mountainous villages (山間마을) in that order. Subsequently, the income growth rate (所得增加率) was highest in mountainous villages (山間마을) at 612.7%, followed by plains (平野), intermediate (中間), suburban (都農近郊) villages, with fishing villages (漁村마을) having the lowest growth rate. As a result, in 1978,

In terms of annual income levels by village type, the ranking was reversed, with the per-household income of farm households in plain villages reaching the highest at 2,502 thousand won, followed by suburban villages. The income level of fishing villages, which was the highest in 1972, dropped to the lowest rank (see Table 38).

The main reason why the farm household income in demonstration villages increased more than in general villages is that, based on continuous education for residents, demonstration villages focused on promoting agricultural innovation to increase food crop production, as well as the development of livestock, fruit, and horticulture. The high income growth rate in mountainous demonstration villages can be attributed to the rapid development of growth agriculture, which has unleashed its potential. The relatively high income level in suburban villages can be explained by the expansion of suburban agriculture and the increase in non-agricultural income through the establishment of non-agricultural employment (see Table 39).

The development projects in demonstration villages also had a significant impact on changing farmers' attitudes. In demonstration villages, 61.4% of farmers were satisfied with agriculture, 69.7% of farm households frequently participated in agricultural technology education, and 62.0% of farm households adopted new agricultural technologies earlier than others. However, in general villages, only 49.4% of farmers were satisfied with agriculture, 39.0% of farm households frequently participated in agricultural technology education, and only 36.3% of farm households adopted new agricultural technologies early.

Therefore, the development projects in demonstration villages can be evaluated as achieving not only increased agricultural production and income but also significant results in stimulating farmers' development aspirations and changing their attitudes.

**(b) Problems with Demonstration Village Development Projects**

The various forms of demonstration village development projects that have been promoted in a multifaceted manner have undoubtedly played a leading role in the continuous development and substantiation of the Saemaul Undong in rural areas. Demonstration villages have led the regional specialization of agricultural production and high efficiency, high income, and have successfully promoted comprehensive development projects by village type based on this.

However, on the other hand, the demonstration projects also had significant problems.


--- (p. 461) ---

## Chapter 5: Practice and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong

Accordingly, it is also undeniable that the project could not avoid exposing its own limitations. The fundamental reason why there were significant constraints on both the expansion of the ripple effects, which were one of the objectives of the model village development project, and the in-depth development of the project itself can be found in the following:

First, the small scale of the project.
At the village level, even the project for improving production infrastructure faced constraints due to the fragmented and dispersed nature of individual farmlands. Even if the production infrastructure was improved, the efficiency and economic feasibility of using large agricultural machinery such as tractors and combines at the village level were too low, making their introduction extremely limited. Moreover, the enhancement of the commercial and profitability of agricultural products through regional specialization, as well as the strengthening of competitiveness with other regions, would be practically difficult to expect unless the scale of regional specialization was expanded beyond the township level. Under such circumstances, introducing large-scale modern distribution facilities at the village level for the modernization of the circulation of agricultural and livestock products was a problem that was far from feasible.

Second, the low self-financing rate of village residents for the required funds and the consequent excessive scale of external support funds were another problem.

Third, as a problem, the dispersion of development administration functions and the resulting low efficiency can be pointed out. The fact that each specialized government agency and related organizations had competitively promoted the model village development project had significant meaning in terms of the fair distribution of support benefits. However, the fact that the government's administrative support functions, the Rural Development Administration's technical guidance functions, and the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation's business functions, including funds, materials, and product storage and processing, were not comprehensively coordinated and were instead dispersed, resulted in lower efficiency and achievements of the project, which cannot be denied.

Lastly, the weakness of the evaluation function for the project's achievements can be mentioned. Most organizations showed high interest in the support of project funds and the implementation of plans and results, but the evaluation of the specific achievements and problems of the project was extremely


--- (p. 462) ---

Neglected in the past, this led to almost all village projects being pursued in a uniform manner, relatively disregarding regional uniqueness and residents' will, which could not but lower the project effects.

Considering various trial-and-error problems, starting from 1977, the Saemaul income comprehensive development project was launched to improve these issues and enhance investment efficiency in rural development.

## II. Special Projects for Increasing Farmers and Fishermen's Income

### (1) Implementation Process of the Special Agricultural Project (農特事業)

In the 1960s, South Korea's economy, driven by industrialization-first policies in economic development plans, widened the income gap between urban and rural areas. To address this, the government began focusing on policies to increase farmers' and fishermen's income, starting with price stabilization measures for agricultural and marine products in 1966.

Consequently, in early 1968, the First Special Project for Increasing Farmers and Fishermen's Income (’68∼’71) was established, targeting 43 items in 90 main production clusters over four years, and implemented from May 11, 1968.

After completing the First Project, from 1972, the Second Special Project (’72∼’76) was pursued as part of the Third Five-Year Economic Development Plan, centering on one main production cluster per county. From 1974, various income-increasing projects, including farmers' and fishermen's side businesses and off-season production projects, were integrated and adjusted into the Saemaul Income-Increasing Project, with the Special Project for Increasing Farmers and Fishermen's Income as the core. Later, to pursue the farmers' and fishermen's income-increasing project more vigorously, it was separated from the Saemaul Income-Increasing Project and implemented as the Third Special Agricultural Project from 1979.

### (2) Achievements of the Special Agricultural Project (農特事業)

During the First Special Agricultural Project, a total of 47.1 billion won was invested in 43 items, including sericulture, cash crops, livestock, and fisheries, establishing 90 main production clusters. Participating farms accounted for 18% of all farms, totaling 450,000 households. During the Second Special Agricultural Project, 87.9 billion won was invested in 29 items, establishing 135 main production clusters, with 750,000 households participating.

Achievements of the Special Agricultural Project include:


--- (p. 463) ---

## Chapter 5 Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Firstly, it is notable that specialized production clusters (주산 단지) were formed for specific items such as Jeju's mandarins, Yesan's apples, and Pyeongchang's hops, leading to collective cultivation, and production, processing, and distribution were integrated, playing a pioneering role in regional development.

Secondly, it can be pointed out that the increased production of target items met domestic demand and significantly boosted the export of agricultural and marine products. Based on 1967, by 1971, the total export value of agricultural and marine products reached 328 million dollars, increasing by 255%. Notably, canned clams increased tenfold, and oysters increased by more than 18 times.

Thirdly, the agricultural special (농특) projects contributed to increasing the income of participating farms and fostering professional farms. During the first agricultural special project period from 1968 to 1971, the income of participating farms was more than 10% higher than that of general farms. By the end of the second agricultural special project in 1977, the average income per general farm was 1,433,000 won, while the income per participating farm was 1,574,000 won, which was 9.8% higher. Additionally, the number of professional farms, which was only 3,000 in 1967, increased to 12,000 by 1976, a fourfold increase.

The success factors for the creation of main production clusters (주산단지) in agricultural special projects, which yielded good results, can be attributed to the following facts:

* Firstly, the enthusiasm and self-help spirit of farmers and fishermen were vigorous;
* Secondly, there was sufficient prior review of the appropriate scale of the business and the selection of crops;
* Thirdly, the introduction and acquisition of new technologies, as well as continuous research and development, were carried out simultaneously;
* Fourthly, strong leadership and a spirit of cooperation were utilized to achieve the rationalization of management.

However, the promotion process of agricultural special projects was not without its issues. Specifically, the first agricultural special project focused on the creation of large-scale main production clusters (주산단지), whereas the second agricultural special project centered on administrative units, leading to the creation of many small clusters (소단지) for multiple items. As a result, the form and function of main production clusters (주산단지) were incomplete. Moreover, excessive emphasis on increased production led to insufficient appropriate production based on supply and demand estimates for each item, resulting in overproduction of items such as solanum nigrum and salted laver. Additionally, there was a lack of support for creating production bases to improve productivity, as the focus was solely on expanding the cultivation area. Furthermore, storage, processing, and transportation facilities were inadequate, and the collection, shipment, and sales system was irrational, leading to somewhat insufficient circulation measures for the products.

Therefore, the government thoroughly examined these issues to avoid future mistakes in implementation (시행착오).


--- (p. 464) ---

to avoid going through unnecessary detours and to focus on strengthening the internal substance, it has been guided in a direction that can achieve this.

### (3) Saemaul Income Augmentation Project

#### (a) Change of Direction

The Saemaul Undong is a movement for better living, so the income augmentation project and its pursued goals do not conflict with each other. However, as seen during the execution process of the agricultural special project, the linkage between the agricultural special project and the Saemaul Undong was insufficient. This was due to the lack of sufficient prior coordination in the planning and project promotion methods. President Park also emphasized this point in his speech at the Saemaul Income Augmentation Promotion Conference on May 18, 1972, stating, "I believe that the agricultural and fishery income augmentation special project is both a part of and the entirety of the Saemaul Undong. In other words, the ultimate goal of the Saemaul Undong is the augmentation of agricultural and fishery income, and we must pursue this movement with the goal of income augmentation."

As the pursued goals of the agricultural special project were of the same nature as those of the Saemaul Undong, the direction was changed to the Saemaul Income Augmentation Project starting from 1974, following President Park's instructions. Along with this change of direction, the project has been promoted as a comprehensive policy for income augmentation, including agricultural and fishery side businesses and off-season production projects.

#### (b) Basic Goals and Policy Directions

The Saemaul Income Augmentation Project has aimed to augment the income of agricultural and fishery populations and, through this, to expedite the construction of a high-income welfare agricultural village where all farmers can live well together. The following items have been emphasized and promoted as policy directions for this purpose.

First, the development and expansion of agricultural and fishery household income sources, excluding the food sector, and concentrated support for this purpose,
Second, the increased production of food substitute crops and the promotion of food self-sufficiency through this,
Third, the large-scale development and expansion of side business projects for the income augmentation of agricultural and fishery populations,
Fourth, the development and expansion of export strategy items for the augmentation of agricultural product exports,
Fifth, the active promotion of agricultural structure improvement projects through the Saemaul Income Augmentation Project,
Sixth, the promotion of village development projects and regional unit development projects, with a focus on the creation of main production clusters, etc., in conjunction with each other.


--- (p. 465) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

In order to promote the Saemaul Income Increase Project (所得增大事業) more efficiently in this direction, the Saemaul Income Increase Promotion Council (所得增大推進協議會) was established and operated.

**(Da) Business Promotion Methods (事業推進方式) and Business Contents (事業內容)**

The principle of prioritizing outstanding villages (優秀마을) for support was applied, and the target areas were primarily selected as self-reliant villages. In terms of business promotion methods, the focus shifted from individual or region-centered businesses to village-centered businesses, with Saemaul leaders (새마을指導者) taking the lead in promoting the Saemaul business methods. Additionally, efforts were made to link the traditional main production zone development projects (主産團地造成事業) with the Saemaul projects by forming production teams (作目班) for each product in the target villages to encourage cooperative businesses (協同事業). To ensure that farmers could focus solely on production, emphasis was placed on establishing a stable production base. The business items (事業種目) focused on strengthening support for stable production items centered around exports. Distribution facilities (流通施設) were expanded in each regional production area (産地) to reinforce a continuous production and distribution system (流通體系).

**(Ra) Business Achievements (事業實績) and Results (成果)**

The number of zones (團地數), which was only 135 in 1977, increased to 678 in 1978. Although it decreased to 587 in 1979 due to the exclusion of livestock zones (畜産團地) from the project targets, 605 zones are planned for 1980. The total project cost (總事業費) invested over the past three years amounts to 142.9 billion won (億圓).

Looking at the major item-wise business achievements (品目別事業實績), the following can be noted. For silkworms, the expansion of new mulberry fields (桑田) was avoided, and the management of existing fields was thoroughly implemented to establish a production base (生産基盤). Additionally, 9,190 silkworm houses (蠶室) were constructed to produce high-quality silkworm cocoons (優良蠶繭), which served as an opportunity to strengthen international competitiveness (國際競爭力). For mushroom cultivation, instead of constructing new cultivation sheds (栽培舍), efforts were made to maximize the use of existing facilities. 212,000 pyeong of cultivation sheds were repaired, and 31 processing plants (加工工場) were modernized. As a result, mushroom canned food exports reached $46 million in 1979, significantly contributing to the income increase (所得增大) of mushroom cultivating farmers (栽培農家).

### 4. Saemaul Comprehensive Income Development Project (새마을所得綜合開發事業)

**(1) Background of Promotion (推進背景)**

The Saemaul Comprehensive Income Development Project (새마을所得綜合開發事業) was initiated in 1977. Its background can be understood from the perspectives of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), agricultural policies (農政), and the agricultural cooperative movement (農協運動) at that time.


--- (p. 466) ---

First, from the perspective of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), to further substantiate and perpetuate this movement based on the achievements made so far in spiritual development (精神啓發) and environmental improvement (環境改善), income augmentation (所得增大) emerged as a major task. For income augmentation, it is desirable to simultaneously achieve increased production (增產) and improved farm gate prices (農家受取價格). Moreover, a comprehensive approach (綜合的) is necessary, encompassing not only production (生産) but also processing (加工) and distribution (流通). While agricultural production (農業生産) could achieve efficiency (能率) at the village level (單位), processing (加工) and distribution (流通) faced difficulties in pursuing economies of scale (規模의 경제성) at this level. This was a fundamental limitation of the village-level (單位) Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in promoting income augmentation projects (所得增大事業), necessitating a new approach (接近) beyond the village level (單位).

Second, from the perspective of agricultural policy (農政), in the 1970s (年代), self-sufficiency (自給) in grain (米穀) was achieved through the development (開發) and dissemination (普及) of new varieties (新品種), and agricultural income (農業所得) saw a dramatic increase (增大) due to the high rice price policy (高米價政策). However, this income policy (所得政策) dependent on high rice prices (高米價) hindered the development (開發) of new sources of agricultural income (農業所得源). Furthermore, policies (施策) aimed at increasing production (增產) by commodity (品目別) and raising average farm income (農家所得增大) nationwide (全國平均槪念) failed to adequately reflect the will of individual farmers (個別農民意思) or the comprehensive development (綜合的開發) of regional resources (地域賦存資源). At this juncture (時點), there was an urgent need (要請) to attempt a bottom-up development approach (上向的開發方式) based on the will of individual farmers (個別農民意思) and regional realities (地域實情).

Third, from the perspective of the agricultural cooperatives (農協), the various business functions (事業機能) of comprehensive agricultural cooperatives (綜合農協) had been performed individually, failing to be organically linked (有機的連繫) and promoted (推進) at the level of regional comprehensive agricultural development (地域農業綜合開發). However, after completing the basic management self-sufficiency plan (基礎經營自立化計劃) by 1977 (年), and with each local cooperative (全單協) securing a certain level (一定水準) of facilities (施設), funds (資金), and personnel (人員), our country's agricultural cooperatives (農協) could actively participate (參與) in regional agricultural development (地域農業開發), similar to those in advanced countries (先進國).

## (2) Significance (意義) and Characteristics (特性)

Against this backdrop (背景), the Saemaul Comprehensive Income Development Project (所得綜合開發事業) was launched. This project aims to maximize development effects (開發效果) by rationally combining (合理的結合) the cooperative production functions (協同生産機能) at the village level (單位) and the production and distribution support functions (流通支援機能) at the township level (邑面單位), based on the self-help (自助) and self-reliance capabilities (自立力量) of farmers (農民) and agricultural cooperatives (農協) cultivated through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) and agricultural cooperative movements (農協運動). Therefore, the comprehensive development project (綜合開發事業) targets townships (邑面單位) as the development subject (開發對象). Under the auspices (主管) of the local cooperative (單協), Saemaul leaders (새마을指導者) will lead village discussion meetings (座談會), gauge residents' opinions (住民意思), and formulate a five-year plan (5개년計劃) based on this input (把握).


--- (p. 467) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Comprehensive Agricultural Development Plan (農業綜合開發計劃) was being established and promoted.

This project (事業) was initially conceived as a comprehensive rural development project (農村綜合開發事業) aimed at achieving high-income (高所得) welfare (福祉) rural construction (農村建設), with project items (種目) including production base (生產基盤), production facilities (生產施設), circulation facilities (流通施設), agricultural mechanization (農業機械化), and crop introduction (作目 導入), as well as cultural (文化) and welfare facilities (福祉施設). However, due to financial support (資金支援) constraints, from 1978 (年) onwards, cultural (文化) and welfare facilities (福祉施設) were excluded, and the project was limited to regional comprehensive agricultural development projects (地域農業綜合開發事業). As a result, the project's goal (目標) shifted to increasing agricultural production (農業增產) and increasing income (所得增大). To this end, the direction of regional comprehensive agricultural development (地域農業綜合開發方向) was set to establish production circles (生產圈) based on the will of the residents (住民意思) and regional conditions (地域實情), and to induce regional specialization (地域別特化) of agricultural production (農業生產) through the introduction of combined main (主), secondary (副), and auxiliary (從) crops (作目), thereby emphasizing the stabilization of farm income (農家所得安定化) and the maximization of resource utilization (資源利用極大化). In addition, efforts were made to strengthen the integrated system (一貫體制) of production and sales (生產販賣) through the establishment of production bases (生產基盤造成), agricultural mechanization (營農機械化), and the expansion of production, processing, and circulation facilities (加工流通施設).

The basic strategy (基本戰略) for promoting this project (事業推進) involved having the village cooperation (單協) take charge (主管) from the planning stage (計劃樹立) to post-management (事後管理). That is, under the supervision (主管) of the village cooperation (單協), project plans (事業計劃) were established (樹立) based on the will of the residents (住民意思), and the project (事業) was promoted (推進) through comprehensive support (綜合支援) of funds (資金), materials (資材), and circulation (流通), as well as the development of direct management projects (直營事業), while the village cooperation (單協) also took responsibility for post-management (事後管理). Meanwhile, administrative agencies (行政機關) and other agricultural-related agencies (農業關聯機關) adjusted (調整) and concentrated (集中) their development administration functions (開發行政機能), such as administrative measures (行政措置) and agricultural technical guidance (營農技術指導), to invest (投入) in the project. To establish the comprehensive development plan (綜合開發計劃), a planning team (企劃團) was formed within the village cooperation (單協), and to support this, a support consultation council (支援協議會) was established at the face (面), county (郡), province (道), and central (中央) levels, consisting mainly of administrative agencies (行政機關), agricultural cooperatives (農協), and rural guidance agencies (農村指導機關). These support consultation councils (支援協議會) were tasked with discussing (協議), adjusting (調整), supplementing (補完), and confirming (確定) project plans (事業計劃), coordinating support (支援) among related agencies (關係機關), and resolving issues (問題點) and difficulties (隘路事項) encountered during project promotion (事業推進).

When comparing such comprehensive development projects (綜合開發事業) with previous agricultural policies (農政施策), particularly special agricultural projects (農特事業), it can be seen that while the goals of increasing agricultural production (農業增產) and increasing agricultural income (農業所得增大) are the same, there are differences in the methods employed. That is, while special agricultural projects (農特事業) primarily targeted regions (地域) above the county level (郡單位以上) and introduced single crops (單一作目), comprehensive development projects (綜合開發事業) targeted town and face units (邑面單位) as project areas (事業地區) and introduced combined main (主), secondary (副), and auxiliary (從) crops (作目). Moreover, throughout the introduction process (導入過程), the will of the farmers (農民意思) was given greater importance than the will of the government (政府意思). Additionally, while special agricultural projects (農特事業) were mainly government-led (政府主導) with support (支援) from funds (資金) and technology (技術), comprehensive development projects (綜合開發事業) involved not only such government support (政府支援) but also the agricultural sector (農).

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Comprehensive support from cooperatives, including the provision of materials and funds, as well as comprehensive support for the sale and processing of agricultural products, was carried out in parallel. For business promotion, even if the revenue and expenditure could not be balanced, non-profit businesses such as the mechanized rice transplanting center business, which is directly operated by the agricultural cooperatives, were promoted.

The promotion method of the Saemaul Income Comprehensive Development Project has already been newly introduced and promoted in foreign rural development projects. In particular, Japan has been pursuing comprehensive agricultural development combining farming and livestock since 1978, focusing on regional agriculture reorganization based on regional characteristics and residents' creativity, aligning with our comprehensive development project. Additionally, Japan's agricultural cooperatives have independently developed a comprehensive three-year plan followed by a regional agricultural promotion plan, which also aligns with our comprehensive development project in terms of method. Furthermore, Mexico's rural development project, supported by the World Bank and targeting 50 regions, also shares similar promotion methods and contents with our comprehensive development project.

### (3) Promotion Achievements

The comprehensive development project was promoted in a total of 250 regions from 1977 to 1980. The most important factor in promoting the comprehensive development project is the acceptance capacity of a single cooperative, so the most significantly considered element in the criteria for selecting business regions was the management self-sufficiency of a single cooperative (50 points), followed by the performance of the Saemaul project (30 points) and the potential for regional specialization in agriculture and the development of existing resources (20 points). The selection of business regions was evaluated, determined based on these selection criteria, and the selected regions' single cooperatives were to establish a five-year plan, with the initial three years relying on government and agricultural cooperative fund support to establish a plan with a scale of 500 million won, and the subsequent two years to be established as a self-promotion plan by the single cooperative. Thus, from 1977 to 1979, a total of 634.6 billion won was invested in 200 regions to carry out various businesses.

The composition of the total investment amount is 66.6% in loans, 24.0% in self-funding, and the remaining 9.4% in subsidies. The business items, including the 1980 plan, total 112 items in 6 categories. The investment details by business category from 1977 to 1979 show that the first priority was the farmer support business, such as

The Crop (作目) Introduction (入殖) sector accounted for 50.2% of the total investment (總投資額), with major crops (主要作目) including Fattening Cattle (肥育牛) (21.1% of total investment (總投資)), Breeding and Fattening Cattle (育成肥育牛) (10.5%), Breeding Cattle (育成牛) (9.6%), Piglets (仔豚) (4.1%), Dairy Cows (乳牛) (2.4%), etc. Additionally, production facilities (生産施設) were supported alongside crop (作目) introduction (入殖), with investments in greenhouses (7.9% of total investment (總投資額)), cattle barns (牛舍) (7.4%), pig barns (豚舍) (3.5%), poultry barns (鷄舍) (2.0%), etc. for farm facility support, and rice seedling facilities, breeding farms, and seedling farms etc. for the expansion of direct-operated production facilities, amounting to 23.4% of the total investment (總投資額).

Furthermore, land consolidation (耕地整理) (7.5% of total investment (總投資額)) and pumping stations (揚水場) (1.5%) etc. for production base establishment projects (生産基盤造成事業) accounted for 11.0% of the total investment (總投資額). The purchase of agricultural machinery such as power tillers, tractors, transplanters, combines, and binders by farmers was supported, and the establishment of agricultural machinery centers, agricultural machinery repair centers, and fuel (油類) handling facilities (取扱所) by single cooperatives (單協) was promoted with 9.3% of the total investment (總投資額) invested (投資) to promote agricultural mechanization.

To improve the distribution of produced agricultural products, emphasis was placed on the expansion of processing and distribution facilities by single cooperatives (單協), with investments in warehouses, vehicles, cold storage, processing plants, sales facilities, etc., amounting to 5.9% of the total investment (總投資額).
