## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The Saemaul Income (所得) Comprehensive Development Project (綜合開發事業) has various business items (種目), so its effects can be observed from multiple perspectives. However, based on on-site survey (現地調査) results, they can be summarized as follows.

First, there is the effect of increased agricultural production (農業增産) and increased agricultural income (農業所得). A simple survey was conducted targeting major crops (主要入殖作目) for farmers (農家), such as fattening cattle (肥育牛), breeding cattle (育成牛), pig farming (養豚), and facility horticulture. The results showed that in 1977, each household (戶當) raised 2.03 head of fattening cattle, 1.15 head of breeding cattle, 22.9 head of pigs, and established 251 pyeong of facility horticulture, generating additional income (追加所得) ranging from 42,100 won to 488,000 won. In 1978, the scale of farming (入殖規模) per household increased compared to 1977, and the income also increased. Households participating in 1977 earned additional income ranging from 120,700 won to 1,931,900 won, while those participating in 1978 earned additional income ranging from 94,700 won to 744,600 won. Furthermore, the structure of farming income (營農收入) for farming households changed in terms of crops (作目別). A survey conducted by the Rural Development Administration (農振廳) on the income share (收入比重) of crops introduced through the Comprehensive Development Project revealed that as of August 1979, the share of introduced crops (入殖作目) in farming households' income was the highest. The share was 16.9% in regions that started the project in 1977, 8.9% in regions that started in 1978, and 0.6% in regions that started in 1979. This indicates that the earlier a region started the project, the more likely introduced crops became the main source of income (所得源) for farming households.

Furthermore, the income increase effect (增大效果) of the Saemaul Income Comprehensive Development Project is even more evident from the farming household income survey conducted by the Rural Development Administration in 1978. While the income of farming households (農家) and agricultural income (農業所得) in demonstration villages (示範마을) were both higher than the national average (平均), the income of farming households in demonstration villages within the project regions was about 300,000 won higher than in other villages. Notably, while non-agricultural income (農外所得) was lower than in other regions, agricultural income was significantly higher at 1,861,000 won.

Second, there is the effect of comprehensive development (綜合開發) of regional agriculture (地域農業). One distinct feature of the Comprehensive Development Project compared to existing agricultural development projects is that it introduces crops in a complex manner tailored to regional settings. Therefore, the comprehensive development effects of this project include the regional specialization (地域的特化) of complex crops (複合作目) with significant interrelated effects on agricultural production, improved utilization (利用度) of local resources (賦存資源), and stable increase (安定的增大) in farming household income. Most regions where this project was implemented have induced the specialization of regional agriculture by considering the conditions of regional agriculture and either treating the entire region as a single production circle (生産圈) or dividing it into several production circles, and introducing suitable crops in a complex manner. This has enhanced the comprehensive development effects.


--- (p. 472) ---

The third effect is the development of farmers' consciousness structure. With the introduction of new farming technologies such as fattening cattle, raising fattening cattle, and facility horticulture through comprehensive development projects, farmers in the project areas became very proactive in adopting farming technologies. In particular, the National Agricultural Cooperative Federation (Nonghyup) successfully promoted demonstration projects for the mechanization of rice transplanting and harvesting, although these projects resulted in deficits of 874,000 won in 1977 and 1,199,000 won in 1978 on average per mechanization center from a management perspective. However, these projects instilled confidence in farmers regarding the possibility of complete mechanization of rice farming and the necessity of shared use of agricultural machinery. This is evident from surveys conducted among farmers in areas where the projects were implemented and those where they were not.

Furthermore, comprehensive development projects emphasized regional conditions and farmers' intentions (76.7% of participating farmers responded that they were able to cultivate the crops they initially wanted). Based on this, agricultural cooperative unions linked regional comprehensive agricultural development plans with single cooperative business plans and promoted cooperative business in an organic and interconnected manner, which was highly significant.

Ultimately, the promotion of comprehensive development projects led agricultural cooperative unions to expand facilities for production, processing, and distribution, which were either loss-making or low-profit businesses. While this put short-term pressure on the unions' management, the effects on agricultural production, farm income, regional agricultural development, and changes in farmers' consciousness were substantial. As a result, both farmers and Nonghyup employees evaluated these projects as more aligned with farmers' interests and the cooperative movement's objectives compared to existing projects, and deemed them worthy of priority promotion by all agricultural cooperative unions.

Meanwhile, the issues that arose from the project promotion between 1977 and 1979 are as follows:

Firstly, since no appropriate scale was suggested for crop cultivation, there was a tendency for small-scale cultivation to be dispersed among many farms, making it difficult to secure a certain level of income and cultivate independent and stable farmers.

Secondly, there was a tendency to select crops based on short-term profitability, leading to experiences like the price collapse of pork in 1979. To overcome these issues, it is necessary to first set appropriate farming scales for each region and farming type, similar to independent and stable farms in Japan, to ensure a certain level of income and promote the cultivation of independent and stable farms through appropriate-scale crop cultivation. Additionally, strategic crops should be selected and cultivated based on long-term supply and demand forecasts, guiding planned production to prevent overproduction and


--- (p. 473) ---

## Chapter 5 Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The pursuit of stable income for farming households requires improving business methods.

### A. Improving Agricultural Product Distribution

#### (1) Saemaul Undong (Movement) and Agricultural Product Distribution

Economic development promotes specialization among economic entities, which in turn increases the physical and economic distance between producers and consumers of specific products and services. The decrease in agricultural population due to economic development can be interpreted as increasing the proportion of the population that can consume agricultural products only after they go through the distribution stage. Therefore, the faster the pace of economic development, the greater the potential for widening the scope of agricultural product distribution issues.

In this context, agricultural product distribution issues should be understood as a result accompanying the process of economic development, and their resolution cannot be achieved solely by approaches aimed at solving distribution itself. Fundamental conditions that can narrow the economic and physical distance between producers and consumers, i.e., improvement of the distribution environment, must precede. The distribution environment includes two major aspects: physical environment such as road and communication network improvements, and human distribution environment including the basic attitudes and transaction customs of distribution entities towards distribution. Improving both requires enormous costs and time.

Until the mid-1960s, the necessity for improving agricultural product distribution was not so serious, but by the late 1960s, interest began to grow. However, due to the enormous costs and time required, efforts to improve it did not progress.

With the onset of the Saemaul Undong (Movement) in the 1970s, it became a turning point for improving the distribution environment. From the perspective of agricultural product distribution, its significance lies in the fact that it became a pivotal period for improving the distribution environment. The Saemaul Undong (Movement) not only improved the physical distribution environment within rural areas, such as roads and communication networks, but also brought about significant changes in farmers' basic attitudes towards agricultural product distribution, thus providing a major opportunity for improving the human distribution environment. However, it is clear that improving the physical distribution environment alone cannot achieve distribution improvement without the development and progress of farmers' self-help and self-reliant efforts, which are the main content of improving the human distribution environment.

With the progress of physical and human distribution environment improvements triggered by the Saemaul Undong (Movement),


--- (p. 474) ---

Improvements and maintenance of distribution facilities such as warehouses, vehicles, agricultural product collection, and sales facilities have been carried out, and based on this, farmers' participation in distribution has increased. Consequently, the role of merchant organizations in production areas has decreased, and significant changes in production area market organizations have become apparent.

(2) Improvement of Physical Distribution Environment and Distribution Facilities
The improvement of living environments in rural areas was a key project in the first stage of the Saemaul Undong. The significance of this project for improving the basic conditions of agricultural product distribution is immense. While expressways and other main roads, constructed as part of the national economic development plan, play important roles, their functions would be limited to connecting cities if rural road improvements and maintenance were not supported. To make national main roads such as expressways useful for farmers, improvements and maintenance of rural internal roads, such as farm roads and village roads, must accompany them.

After 1970, the Saemaul Undong, based on farmers' self-help efforts, led to a significant advancement in the improvement of rural internal roads. The combined efforts of the government in constructing expressways and other main roads, and farmers' self-help efforts, synergistically enhanced the overall effectiveness of national roads. This fact not only highlights the effects of the Saemaul Undong but also signifies the importance of concluding nationally-led development initiatives through farmers' self-help efforts.

Through the Saemaul Undong, the expansion and improvement of farm roads and village roads were completed, and telephone installation was achieved in all 18,600 legal village units nationwide. This laid the foundation for improving the basic conditions of agricultural product distribution, including the improvement of distribution information. Furthermore, changes in farmers' participation attitudes and improvements in project promotion methods through the Saemaul Undong led to the maintenance of irrigation facilities, land consolidation, and other improvements in agricultural production bases. Along with the advancement of scientific farming and the formation of main production areas by crop, the unification of farming techniques for improving the high quality of agricultural products was achieved, contributing to the improvement of the physical distribution environment for agricultural products.

Along with the preparation of the above physical environment improvements, distribution facilities such as warehouses, transport vehicles, agricultural product collection facilities, and sales facilities were quantitatively expanded, and qualitative improvements were also carried out simultaneously. The expansion and improvement of agricultural product distribution facilities, particularly by the cooperative system organizations,


--- (p. 475) ---

In addition to the facilities owned by the National Agricultural Cooperatives Federation (農協) shown in the table, there was also an expansion and improvement of distribution-related facilities at the village level or by farmers themselves. Most of these were established through the efforts of farmers, with some support from the government, taking the form of village warehouses (마을倉庫) owned jointly by village residents. By 1979, more than 184 such warehouses had been established and were in use. Additionally, 236,000 power tillers (耕耘機), supplied by the end of 1979 for individual or shared use by farmers, were being utilized as a means of transporting agricultural products (農産物).

The improvement in the physical distribution environment had various aspects, but in terms of changes in the means of transporting agricultural products (農産物) (specifically grains (米穀)), the proportion of transportation powered by engines increased significantly from 4.2% in 1968 to 65.2% in 1978 (National Agricultural Cooperatives Federation (農協中央會) Research Department, The Current Status and Tasks of Agricultural Product Distribution in Korea, December 1979, p. 110).

(3) Progress in Human Distribution Environment and Increased Farmer Interest in Distribution

As an economic activity (經濟行爲), distribution activities (流通行爲) require that the various actors involved in distribution change their attitudes and perceptions from passive to active. Without this shift, fundamental improvements in distribution are impossible. In particular, the role of farmers, who are the producers (生産者) and the starting point of agricultural product distribution (農産物流通), is significant as a distribution entity (流通主體) influencing the entire agricultural product distribution. If farmers focus only on their roles as producers (生産主體) and consumers (消費主體), neglecting their role as distribution entities (流通主體), it would be difficult to expect the overall rational development of agricultural product distribution (農産物流通). With the advent of the 1960s and the onset of rapid economic growth (高度經濟成長), the proportion of the population engaged in agriculture (農業人口比率) began to decrease.


--- (p. 476) ---

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) served as a catalyst to raise farmers' interest and self-help efforts regarding distribution, amidst conditions where the commodity ratio of agricultural products was increasing. It is a fact that the recognition that farm household income is realized through the distribution of agricultural products, and the need for farmers' own efforts to improve distribution, were greatly promoted by the Saemaul Undong, which emphasized "spiritual development of farmers for a better life."

As economic and environmental changes occurred alongside changes in spiritual attitudes brought about by the Saemaul Undong, the human distribution environment of farmers as distribution entities was enhanced. The increased interest of farmers in distribution is evident in the following data. In 1968, only 57.3% of farm households checked prices before selling grains (Nonghyup Central (農協中央會), Joint Market (合同市場) Survey Team (調査團), Grain (米穀) Marketing Survey (調査) Report (報告書), 1968.12. p. 122). However, by 1978, this figure had risen to over 90% (Nonghyup Central (農協中央會) Survey Department (調査部), Current Status (現況) and Tasks (課題) of Agricultural Product Markets (農産物市場) in Korea, 1979.12), indicating a change in farmers' attitudes towards a more proactive stance regarding the distribution of agricultural products.

Along with changes in farmers' attitudes, improvements and enhancements in physical distribution environments and facilities were carried out in parallel. As a result, changes began to appear in the distribution organizations of agricultural products at the production sites, with farmers participating as distribution entities. This is evident in the efforts of farmers to increase their bargaining power in agricultural product distribution through collective shipment.

### (4) Formation of Farmers' Shipment Organizations and Weakening of Production Site Merchant Organizations

As part of farmers' self-help efforts, recognition and concrete actions regarding collective shipment have increased, leading to significant changes in the market organizations of agricultural products at production sites. Previously, production site markets were dominated by merchant organizations, but now the proportion of direct shipments by farmers and organizational shipments led by farmers through voluntary shipment groups and Nonghyup organizations (unit associations and special associations) has increased significantly. While it is difficult to grasp the market share by distribution entity for all agricultural products due to the variety of products and significant price fluctuations by item, according to Nonghyup's estimates, the market share of Nonghyup at production sites was only at the 10% level in the early 1970s. However, by 19


--- (p. 477) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Evaluation (評價) and Achievements (成果) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

By the end of the 1970s, this had improved to the 20% level. Meanwhile, according to a survey conducted by the Federation of Korean Industries (大韓商工會議所), the market share by entity for green produce in the four regions of Wanju (完州), Seongju (星州), Jinju (晉州), and Namwon (南原) showed that Nonghyup (農協) (single cooperatives and horticultural associations) accounted for 39%, local collection and exporting farmers 34%, voluntary export organizations 7%, and individual farmer exports accounted for 20% (Federation of Korean Industries (大韓商工會議所), Directions for the Development of Modernization of Agricultural Product Distribution (農産物流通近代化展開方向), August 1979, p. 122, based on data from December 1978 to May 1979). While there may be questions about whether this survey result represents all agricultural products and the entire country, it is undeniable that by the end of the 1970s, compared to the late 1960s before the start of the Saemaul Undong, farmers began to make collective efforts to export together.

The enhancement of farmers' leadership in agricultural product production areas and the relative weakening of merchant organizations are not only evident in the market share by distribution entity but also in the changes in farmers' sources of price information (for grains). In 1968, the dependence on merchants and five-day markets as sources of price information for farmers was 60.2% (Nonghyup (農協) Central Union (中央會) Research Department (調査部), IMI Joint Market Research Team (合同市場調査團) Grain Marketing Survey Report (米穀マーケティング調査報告書), December 1968, p. 124). However, by 1978, this dependence had decreased to 38.9%, while the dependence on Nonghyup (農協) and newspapers and other mass media had increased from 18.5% to 42.5% during the same period (Nonghyup (農協) Research Department (調査部), Current Status (現況) and Tasks (課題) of Agricultural Product Distribution (農産物流通) in Korea, December 1979, p. 114).

Actual participation in agricultural product distribution requires considerable experience, technology, facilities, and funds, etc. Therefore, the participation in agricultural product distribution through organized collective efforts via Nonghyup (農協) and others is still in its early stages and has many immature aspects. In particular, without the necessary conditions for the grading and standardization of agricultural products and the collectivization of exports, and under the operational form of Nonghyup (農協) which has not yet established a completely independent and self-reliant system, most agricultural product exports are still limited to collective transportation. However, it is significant that the first step towards the collectivization of agricultural product exports has been opened. In the future, as time passes, actual distribution experience will accumulate, appropriate business targets will be selected, and farmers' financial capabilities will be supplemented. It is expected that, in parallel with the improvement of the distribution environment, farmers' collective exports will develop into a more advanced form.

### (5) Tasks for Improving Agricultural Product Distribution (農産物流通改善課題)


--- (p. 478) ---

In the 1960s, with the government-led overall economic development, the foundation for improving circulation conditions was established to some extent. However, this foundation alone could not directly contribute to improving the environment for agricultural product circulation. For this, changes from within the rural areas, such as the improvement and development of rural roads and the enlightenment of farmers as circulation entities, were necessary.

As the momentum for high economic development took root in the 1970s, the Saemaul Undong, which began at this time, provided a pivotal opportunity for a dramatic improvement in both material and human circulation environments. This opened a path for the effects of government-led economic development to directly contribute to the improvement of agricultural product circulation led by farmers. The significance of the Saemaul Undong can be found in this aspect, and as a result, significant changes in the agricultural product circulation organizations in producing areas have been observed, as previously examined. However, for these changes to bear fruit and for the improvement of agricultural product circulation in producing areas to take root, many tasks still need to be resolved.

Firstly, the organization of intermediary markets, specifically central wholesale markets, which connect producing area markets and consumer area markets, can be mentioned. Currently, agricultural product central wholesale market organizations can be divided into legally recognized wholesale markets (including National Agricultural Cooperative Federation auction sites) and illegal but practically operating wholesale markets. The market share of illegal wholesale markets, which are being driven underground primarily to avoid taxation, reaches 73.7% in the case of vegetables in Seoul (Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Directions for the Modernization of Agricultural Product Circulation, August 1979). In a state where most agricultural product transactions are underground, it is clear that improving circulation, which aims for fairness and efficiency in circulation, is impossible.

Factors that further promote the underground nature of agricultural product transactions include the inadequacy and insufficiency of facilities in legally recognized wholesale markets, the underdevelopment of grading, packaging, and standardization of agricultural products, and the lack of a market information system. Improving these factors is impossible through the efforts of farmers or agricultural organizations alone and requires more attention and investment from the government.

To further promote and develop the momentum for improving agricultural product circulation, initiated by the self-help efforts of farmers through the Saemaul Undong, the government should fulfill its role.


--- (p. 479) ---

# Chapter 5 Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It seems that the time has come when it is mature.

## 5. The Industrialization of the Off-Season and the Increase in Non-Agricultural Income

### A. Trends in Non-Agricultural Income

One symbolic change that can be pointed out within our rural society through the economic development of the 1960s is that the barren hills have disappeared. If there was another symbolic change achieved through the Saemaul Undong in the 1970s, it would be the disappearance of the off-season in agriculture.

The reasons why the off-season has disappeared from rural areas can be found from various perspectives.

First, it can be seen that our country's agriculture has changed into "non-leisure agriculture" due to the rapid development and expansion of livestock, fruit trees, horticulture, and so-called growth agriculture. However, a more important reason can be found in the fact that opportunities for employment in fields other than agriculture have rapidly increased within our rural society as a result of the Saemaul Undong.

New Village factories have been promoted nationwide at the township level, and on the other hand, New Village income projects and off-season industrialization projects have been continuously promoted since 1972. As a result, opportunities for non-agricultural employment have rapidly increased, and the foundation for the stabilization of non-agricultural employment has also been laid.

These facts are substantiated by various statistics. That is, since 1974, an average of 115,200 people have been employed in the New Village income projects annually, and an average of 122,300 households, more than half of the total farming households in our country, have participated in the off-season industrialization projects. Moreover, the number of employees stably employed in New Village factories has been increasing every year since 1973, reaching nearly 70,000 by the end of 1979.

This increase in non-agricultural employment has led to a sharp increase in non-agricultural income, and as a result, farm income has continued to increase. That is, the average income per farming household increased from 256,000 won in 1970 to 2,228,000 won in 1979, an 8.7-fold increase. However, while agricultural income increased by 7.9 times during the same period, non-agricultural income increased by 11.3 times, which is 3.4 times more, indicating that the increase in non-agricultural income has contributed significantly to the increase in farm income.


--- (p. 480) ---

The increase in non-agricultural income (農外所得) has contributed significantly to this growth. As a result, by the end of 1979, the proportion of non-agricultural income in farm household income, which had not exceeded 20% in the early 1970s, surpassed 30%.

The increase in non-agricultural employment (農外就業) has significantly contributed to the growth of non-agricultural income (農外所得), as seen in the structural changes in non-agricultural income.

While agricultural ancillary service industries (農業附帶 서비스業種) have shown rapid growth, the share of sideline income (兼業所得) in non-agricultural income decreased from 15.5% in 1970 to 6.4% in 1979. In contrast, wage income (賃金所得) increased from 43.4% to 45.4%, with the main driver being the increase in fixed income, i.e., salaries (給料). Additionally, other income (其他所得) increased from 41.1% in 1970 to 48.2% in 1979, driven by the increase in farm miscellaneous income (農家雜收入).

Thus, the increase in salaries (給料) and farm miscellaneous income (農家雜收入) has been the main driver of the growth in non-agricultural income (農外所得). This is evident in the construction of Saemaul factories (工場) and the decentralization policy of industrial complexes (工團), which have provided farm households (農家) with stable non-agricultural employment opportunities (農外就業機會) to increase their salary income (給料收入) and subcontracting opportunities (下請業) to increase their farm miscellaneous income (農家雜收入), thereby significantly contributing to the growth of non-agricultural income (農外所得).

## II. Off-season Production Business (農閑期 生産化事業)

### (1) Business Objectives (事業目的)

In South Korea, farmers and fishermen (農漁民) have traditionally had a seven-month working season for rice farming, followed by a near half-year (近半年) off-season (農閑期) with little to no work.

President Park Chung-hee (朴大統領) emphasized this fact and, along with the inception of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), directed in a speech to the National Mayors and County Chiefs Conference (全國市長 ㆍ 郡守大會) on March 12, 1970, that farm households (農家) should promote sideline businesses (副業) or home-based industries (家內工業) and maximize the utilization of the off-season (農閑期) to increase farm household income (農家所得).

Following President Park Chung-hee's (朴大統領) directive, the off-season production business (農閑期 生産化事業) was initiated in 1972 with the objective to "absorb (吸收) the idle labor force (遊休勞動力) in rural fishing villages (農漁村) during the off-season (農閑期) into productive income-generating activities (生産所得事業), achieve scientific farming (科學營農), and ultimately increase agricultural production (農業增産) and farm household income (農家所得)."


--- (p. 481) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

Such off-season agricultural production businesses have been promoted in the following three forms. That is, businesses such as income-increasing businesses (所得增大 事業) that do not require special technology (技術) and can be produced with small capital (小資本) in winter, such as sack, yarn, kkeochi, jukse products, and willow products, businesses to improve agricultural productivity (農業 生產性) by thoroughly preparing for farming work in winter, such as object (客土), deep plowing (深耕), barley treading, fertilizer increase, and well repair, and winter agricultural education (冬節期 營農敎育) businesses for the early realization of scientific farming (科學 營農) have been promoted as priority businesses (力點 事業).

### (2) Basic Policy (基本方針)

The off-season agricultural production business (農閑期 生產化 事業) has been promoted as a regional priority business (力點 事業) to avoid formal and demonstrative business promotion and to contribute to the actual increase in income (所得增大) and improvement in productivity (生產性) of farmers, with the promotion body (推進 主體) being the village-level Li-dong Development Committee (里洞開發 委員會) and promoted as a Saemaul cooperative business.

In addition, under the responsibility of mayors (市長), county magistrates (郡守), and governors (道知事) nationwide, the functions (機能) of local administrative agencies (地方行政機關), rural guidance agencies (農村 指導機關), and agricultural cooperative (農協) system agencies (系統 機關) at each level have been organically integrated and unified for promotion. At the same time, the active participation (參與) of all farming households (農家) has been strongly induced to aim for a new Saemaul village (新村) without an off-season (農閑期) in rural areas (農村), with the basic policy (基本方針) set as such.

### (3) Promotion Guidelines (推進要領)

First, to establish a guidance system (指導體制), a "Off-season Agricultural Production Business Promotion Council (農閑期 生產 事業 推進協議會)" was organized for each level, and the functions (機能) of each agency (機關別) were organically integrated and operated to improve business performance (事業 成果).

These councils held a council (協議會) at least once a month for each level to evaluate the promotion achievements (推進 實績) and quickly resolve problems that arise during the promotion process.

Second, relevant agencies (有關機關) set the period from December 1 to the end of March of the following year, a total of four months, as the period for emphasizing off-season agricultural production businesses (農閑期 生產 事業), and strengthened publicity (宣傳) for farmers and fishermen (農漁民) to enhance their participation awareness (參與 意識).

Third, mayors (市長) and county magistrates (郡守) selected one model village per township (邑) and township (面) with a large amount of business, diverse business items, and good cooperation through the city (市) and county (郡) council (協議會), but concentrated various supports such as funds (資金), materials (資材), sales channels (販路), technical guidance (技術指導), and education and training (敎育訓練) on the selected model village to prioritize other villages and enhance the ripple effect (波及 效果).


--- (p. 482) ---

### (4) Business Achievements

Before the inception of the Saemaul Undong in the 1960s, only a few farmers and fishermen utilized the off-agricultural season (farmers' idle period) as a traditional sideline activity on an individual household basis. The income level of farmers and fishermen was increasingly diverging from that of urban workers, and there were no employment opportunities outside of farming, leading to an increase in potential unemployment due to idle labor force throughout the year.

The social conditions of rural areas were transformed by the Saemaul Undong, fostering a new spirit of industriousness. The off-agricultural season production business, supported in the Saemaul Undong manner—from individual to village units with priority given to exemplary villages—resulted in the elimination of the off-agricultural season and contributed significantly to reducing the income gap between urban and rural areas.

From December 1972 to March 1980, the total funds allocated to the off-agricultural season production business amounted to 8,910 million won, including short-term operating funds and local funds. A total of 9,778 thousand households participated in this business, producing goods worth 2,946 billion won and generating an estimated income of 1,881 billion won. The following table details the annual achievements.

#### B. Construction of Saemaul Factories and Increase in Non-Agricultural Income

#### (1) Achievements in the Construction of Saemaul Factories

Alongside the inception of the Saemaul Undong, the government made various policy efforts and endeavors to increase non-agricultural income.


--- (p. 483) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Tasks of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

As part of such policy efforts, the government began constructing Saemaul factories in rural areas starting in 1973, with the goal of establishing one factory per village (1면 1공장), totaling 1,470 factories by 1981.

From 1973 to 1979, over a period of 7 years, the government designated a total of 689 Saemaul factories. To promote the construction and operation of these factories, the government provided a total of 319 billion won in facility funds and 86.4 billion won in operating funds, amounting to a total of 406 billion won.

As a result, by the end of 1979, out of the total designated factories of 689, 71.4% (492 factories) were completed and are currently in operation. The total production performance of these factories in 1979 was 4,263 billion won, and their overseas export performance reached 494 million dollars.

(2) Effects of Saemaul Factory Construction

The primary objective of initiating the Saemaul factory construction project was, as explained earlier, to absorb the idle labor force in rural areas, turn labor into productive work, and thereby increase non-agricultural income. The secondary objective was to revamp the regional industrial structure through the production of raw materials related to factory operations and the development of small-scale related service businesses, further accelerating the increase in non-agricultural income.

Therefore, the effects of Saemaul factory construction can be analyzed from two aspects: the increase in employment and wage income, and the production of raw materials and the development of related service industries, leading to an increase in agricultural and non-agricultural income.

First, looking at the effects of increased employment and wage income, in the first year (1973), the number of employees was 17,000, and the total wages paid, including subcontracted wages for farmers, was 121.2 million won. However, by the end of 1979, the number of employees had increased to 67,900, which is 3.9 times more than in 1973. The total wages paid, including subcontracted wages for farmers, had increased to 66,795 million won, a staggering 55.1 times more.


--- (p. 484) ---

Additionally, the amount spent by farming households (農家) on purchasing raw materials (原料) increased from 242 million won (百萬元) in 1973 to 4,243 million won (百萬元) in 1979, marking a 17.5-fold increase. However, data on the development of related service industries (業種) and the resulting effects on increasing non-farming income (農外所得) have not yet been collected, making it difficult to analyze the concrete effects (效果).

### (3) Construction of Saemaul Factories (工場) and Their Issues (問題點)

The construction of Saemaul factories (工場) not only provides jobs for those who wish to work by absorbing idle labor (遊休勞動力) in rural areas (農漁村地域) and increases non-farming income (農外所得) through wage payments (賃金支給), but also restructures the regional industrial (産業) structure (構造) to establish a foundation for the continuous increase of farming household (農家) income (所得). In this regard, its significance (意義) is immense.

However, reviewing the progress (推進) and achievements (成果) to date reveals that it encompasses numerous issues (問題點).

The first issue (問題點) is that the progress (實績) in factory (工場) construction (建設) is remarkably poor compared to the initial goals (目標). By 1981, the target for Saemaul factory (工場) construction (建設) was set at one factory (工場) per household (戶), totaling 1,471 factories (工場). However, as of the end of 1979, when the project was nearly completed, the number of designated factories (工場) was only 46.8%, and the number of operational factories (工場) was 33.4%, indicating a very poor achievement (實績) compared to the target (目標).

Secondly, although the Saemaul factory (工場) construction (建設) project (事業) in rural areas (農漁村地域) has not yet advanced beyond the basic (基礎的) stage (段階), its overall (全體的) economic (經濟) impact (效果) on rural areas (農漁村地域) has fallen significantly short of expectations (期待) in terms of both employment (雇用) and increasing non-farming income (農外所得增大).

When considering all farming households (農家), the employment effect (效果) is only one person (名) per 33 households (戶), and the income increase (所得增大) is merely 32,000 won (千元) per household (戶). Considering that a significant portion of the workforce (人力) employed in Saemaul factories (工場) consists of specialized technical personnel (專門技術人力) who have migrated from urban (都市) areas (地域), the employment and non-farming income increase (農外所得增大) effects (效果) must be further underestimated (低評價).

The third issue (問題點) is that among Saemaul factories (工場), a considerable proportion (比重) are industries (業種) that require specialized technical personnel (專門技術人力) such as metals (金屬), electricity (電氣), machinery (機械), and chemical products (化學製品).


--- (p. 485) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

There is a lack of institutional measures to provide such technical education to the idle workforce in rural areas.

Lastly, expecting significant development of related service industries with just one factory per village is difficult, and this could also hinder the establishment of new factories in rural areas.

Considering these issues, it appears that future construction of Saemaul factories should move beyond the one factory per village approach and expand to one factory per county or township. Additionally, various institutional support measures should be devised for this purpose.

**La. Increase in Wages and Forestry Income**

**(1) Saemaul Wage Income Business (勞賃所得事業)**

Since 1974, the government has been promoting the Saemaul Wage Income Business, which was designated as a basic Saemaul project in 1975. The business model was revised, and it has been implemented nationwide in both urban and rural areas.

Traditional wage businesses aimed primarily at stabilizing the lives of the underprivileged, and their business models were mostly either dispersing wages or providing relief while idle.

However, the Saemaul Wage Income Business has advanced beyond being a measure for stabilizing the lives of the underprivileged. It aims to produce idle labor force, increase residents' income, and develop the local community, making it a multi-purpose project. Specifically, during the agricultural off-season, the idle labor force in rural areas, particularly the underprivileged, is mobilized to carry out various resident-desired projects such as developing agricultural water resources, river improvement, land formation, and afforestation in urban fringes, remote islands, mountainous areas, disaster-stricken regions, and other underdeveloped areas. This aims to enhance the underprivileged's diligence and self-reliance, increase their income, and develop underdeveloped areas, achieving triple effects.

The Saemaul Wage Income Business has been promoted through the following three methods:

The Saemaul Wage Income "1호(號)" Business primarily aims to provide employment for the underprivileged, operated by mayors, county governors, or township mayors, or through a village contracting method.

The "2호(號)" Business is implemented as an economic measure under the auspices of the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries and the Ministry of Construction, prioritizing employment in food production and construction projects through a contracting method.

The "3호(號)" Business aims to provide employment for the underprivileged, low-income earners, employment seekers, or village residents.


--- (p. 486) ---

Local governments had been promoting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) using their own budgets as funding sources. However, the Saemaul Labor Income "2nd" project was discontinued starting in 1976 due to economic stagnation caused by the 1973 oil shock, and the "3rd" project was also discontinued starting in 1977 due to funding constraints. As a result, only the Saemaul Labor Income "1st" project has been continuously promoted.

To promote the "1st" Labor Income project, the government invested an average of approximately 200 billion won per year, totaling 1,200 billion won from the national treasury and local taxes over six years from 1974 to 1979. Regarding the participation status of residents, an average of 538,000 households per year, totaling 3,226,000 households, participated. The number of people employed per year averaged 11,520,000, totaling 69,121,000, which is approximately 1.8 times the total population of our country. In terms of employment days per household, the average was 28.3 days per year, totaling 133.9 days over the past six years.

The labor income per household obtained through these employment projects averages approximately 25,000 won per year, totaling 184,000 won. The main achievements of the projects carried out in an average of 8,825 locations per year, totaling 25,952 locations, are as follows (Table 45).

(2) Increasing Forest Income


--- (p. 487) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

A country with bare mountains is easily misunderstood as a nation of lazy people or a people who cannot escape poverty.

In our country, where about 70% of the national land area is forest, cultivating and protecting forest resources is a way to protect our and our neighbors' property, a shortcut to strengthening national power, and can also be a way to take care of our health.

As the Saemaul Undong (事業) settled into its regular course, village environments were improved and incomes increased. Residents began to seek stable sources of income rather than unstable ones, and as a result, they became highly interested in the long-term development of forest resources, which has a significant effect on increasing income. Taking this as an opportunity, the government established a 10-year (個年) plan for afforestation and greening (治山綠化) and has been promoting it as part of the nationwide Saemaul Undong (運動) since 1973, with the participation of the entire nation (國民).

The fundamental purpose of this endeavor (事業) has been to develop new long-term sources of income, preserve the nation's land (國土) through afforestation and greening (治山綠化), and pursue the benefits of cooperation by having all village residents plant and cultivate trees with a single mind.

In promoting nationwide afforestation and greening (治山綠化) endeavors (事業), during the initial (初期) stage, emphasis was placed primarily on afforestation (造林) endeavors (事業) such as creating economic forests (經濟林) with significant income-increasing effects and afforestation (造林) with fast-growing trees (速成樹) with rapid growth rates (成長). From 1977 onwards, the government designated the first Saturday of November each year as "Forest Cultivation (育林) Day" to encourage the nation (國民) to pay more attention not only to afforestation (造林) but also to forest cultivation (育林).

To promote afforestation (造林) endeavors (事業) for the development of forest (山林) income sources (所得源) more efficiently, the government has been promoting them from three aspects: village afforestation (마을造林), village livestock (마을畜産), and rural (農村) fuel (燃料) measures (對策).

The village afforestation (마을造林) endeavor (事業) has focused on prioritizing afforestation (造林) in jointly managed (共同) village forest land (林野) to establish a joint (共同) income (所得) base (基盤). Additionally, it has been promoted in three directions: afforestation (造林) of fast-growing trees (速成樹) to achieve early (早期) improvements in village scenery (景觀), soil conservation (土砂), and water resource (水資源) development; afforestation (造林) of fruit-bearing trees (有實樹) to create a base (基盤) for generating cash (現金) income (所得) from forests (山林) every year (每年); and the creation of fuel forests (燃料林) to achieve self-sufficiency (自給) in fuel (燃料) for rural and fishing villages (農漁村).

Fast-growing trees (速成樹) have been established at an average (平均) of 46,904 hectares per year (年), totaling 304,000 hectares (千), achieving


--- (p. 488) ---

Rural (農村) fuel (燃料) measures are crucial not only for smoothly supplying forest (林産) fuel (燃料) to fishing villages (漁村) but also for increasing (增殖) and protecting (保護) forest (山林) resources (資源). Therefore, the government (政府) has promoted rural (農村) fuel (燃料) measures alongside long-term (長期的) afforestation (造林) projects by encouraging individual (個別) farms (農家) to conserve (節約) fuel (燃料) at the village (單位) level, collectively (共同) developing (造成) fuel forests (燃料林) suitable for the village's (當) consumption (消費) level, and jointly (共同) managing (管理) them.

## Ma. Increasing (增大) Fishery (漁業) Income (所得)

### (1) Fishing Village (漁村) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and Increasing (增大) Income (所得)

Leveraging the national (國土) territory's (位置) characteristic of being bordered by the sea on three sides (3面), the fishing village (漁村) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was initiated to develop (開發) the potential (可能性) of a maritime (海洋) nation (國家) and transform (發展) traditional (前近代的) collection-centered (採集) fisheries (漁業) into modern (近代的) fixed (定置) fishery-centered (漁業) operations (中心), aiming to develop (開發) fishing villages (漁村) and increase (增大) fishermen's (漁家) income (所得). The "New Fishing Village (漁村) Construction (建設) Project (事業)" began in 1972.

The "New Fishing Village (漁村) Construction (建設) Project (事業)" was divided into several sectors (部門) for strategic (戰略) promotion (推進) based on regional (地域別) characteristics (特性) and the village's (當) development (發展) stage (段階). These included ① increasing (增大) income (所得), ② production (生産) base (基盤), ③ welfare (福祉) environment (環境), and ④ spiritual (精神) development (啓發).

Such new fishing village (漁村) construction (建設) projects (事業) have been systematically (體系) promoted (推進) across 1,583 villages (個) nationwide (全國), yielding significant (相當) results. During the period from 1972 to 1979, a total of 25.927 billion won was invested (投入) (see Table 49 for reference).


--- (p. 490) ---

The business funds (事業資金) for these projects were procured through the beneficiaries' (受惠者) own contributions (自擔), government (政府) subsidies (補助), and loans (融資) from organizations like the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (水協), with government subsidies (政府補助) accounting for the largest share at 39% (10,088 million won), followed by loans (融資) and own contributions (自擔) at 34% (8,688 million won) and 27% (7,151 million won) respectively.

The "New Fishing Village Construction Project" (新漁村建設事業) was designed and implemented with four core projects (基幹事業) that complemented and supplemented each other, ultimately aiming to raise the income of fishing households (漁家) to the level of farming households (農家) or urban families (都市家計). In particular, the income enhancement (所得增大) sector was divided into various sub-projects (細部事業) such as increased aquaculture (增養殖), fishing (漁撈) ancillary facilities (附帶施設), joint fishing ground resource development (共同漁場資源造成), and fishing village sideline businesses (漁村副業) for execution (執行).

Therefore, the next section will examine in more detail the implementation results of the income enhancement projects (所得增大事業) that have been the mainstay of the New Fishing Village Construction Project (新漁村建設事業).

### (2) Structure of Fishing Village Saemaul Income Enhancement Projects (漁村新村所得增大事業)

The Fishing Village Saemaul Income Enhancement Projects (漁村新村所得增大事業) were divided into six sectors (部門) that could directly contribute to increasing the income of fishing households (漁家): increased aquaculture (增養殖), fishing (漁撈) ancillary facilities (附帶施設), joint fishing ground resource development (共同漁場資源造成), fishing village sideline businesses (漁村副業), inland water surface development (內水面開發), and improvement of fishery product circulation (水産物流通改善). These projects were further selected as specific targets (對象) reflecting regional (地域的) site conditions (立地條件) and the will of fishermen (漁民), and were implemented while being adjusted to form an organic (有機的) connection (連繫) with each other.

These various projects (各種事業) were also designed to encourage active (積極的) participation (參與) and cooperation (協同) among residents (住民) by limiting the projects directly managed (主管) by the government (政府) to only two sectors (部門): increased aquaculture (增養殖) and inland water surface development (內水面開發). The remaining projects were promoted with the Fishing Village Association (漁村契) and the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives (水協) as the center (中心).


--- (p. 491) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

(3) Income (所得) Increase (增大) Business (事業) by Sector (部門別)

Examining the sector-specific achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) income (所得) increase (增大) business (事業) in fishing villages (漁村) by year reveals the following.

During the period from 1972 to 1979, the aquaculture (增養殖) business (事業) received a total investment (投入) of 6,048 hundred million (百萬) won, accounting for 37.2% of the total investment (投入額) of 16,233 hundred million (百萬) won in income (所得) increase (增大) businesses (事業), making it the largest sector. Resource (資源) development (造成) accounted for 15.2%, and ancillary facilities (附帶施設) accounted for 12.4%.

① Aquaculture (增養殖) Business (事業)
The business (事業) of increasing (增) and cultivating (殖) various shellfish (貝類), including abalone (石花) and razor clams (새꼬막), as well as the cultivation (養殖) of seaweed (海苔), was primarily carried out along the southern coast (南海岸). Over the past decade, a total of 6,048 hundred million (百萬) won was invested (投入), making it the sector with the highest share (比重) in income (所得) increase (增大) businesses (事業). The planning (計劃), guidance (指導), and post-management (事後管理) of the business (事業) were directly (直接) managed (管掌) by the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (水產廳).

Among these, the aquaculture (養殖) business (事業) is evaluated (評價) as having significant (相當) meaning (意義) as a more direct (直接) strategy (戰略) for increasing (增) the income (所得) of fishermen (漁家) through increased (增) production (產) of marine products (水產物). It is a fact (事實) that this business (事業) has significantly (相當) contributed (寄與) to shifting (轉換) fishermen's (漁家) production (生產) activities (活動) from traditional (從來) extraction (採取) to aquaculture (養殖) centered (中心).

② Ancillary Facilities (附帶施設) Expansion (擴充) Business (事業)
To expand (擴充) various facilities (施設) necessary (必要) for fishing (漁撈) or aquaculture (養殖) to increase (增) the income (所得) of fishermen (漁家), a total of 2,005 hundred million (百萬) won was invested (投入) during the period from 1972 to 1979. Primarily led (中心) by fishing village (漁村契) cooperatives (契) and fisheries cooperatives (水協), 1,007 joint facilities (共同施設) such as communal (共同) warehouses (倉庫), communal (共同) workplaces (作業場), simple (簡易) sales (販賣) sites (場) for fishing boats (漁船), and seedling (種苗) cultivation (培養) sites (場) were constructed (築造) and operated (運營).

In particular, this business (事業) promoted (促進) cooperative (協同) production (生産) activities (活動) among fishermen (漁家) by jointly (共同) processing (處理) after landing (揚陸), not only reducing (節減) costs (費用) but also contributing (寄與) to jointly (共同) guiding (指導) processing (處理) techniques (技術). It also helped (幫助) enhance (高) the commercial (商品) value (性) of marine products (水產物).

③ Joint Fishing Grounds (共同漁場) Resource (資源) Development (造成) Business (事業)
The joint fishing grounds (共同漁場) resource (資源) development (造成) business (事業) received a total investment (投入) of 2,471 hundred million (百萬) won during the period from 1972 to 1979, significantly (相當) contributing (寄與) to the transition (轉換) from catching (捕) fisheries (漁業) to cultivating (養) fisheries (漁業). The resource (資源) development (造成) business (事業) primarily (主要) targeted (對象) undeveloped (未開發) fishing grounds (漁場) for the release (撒) of fry (稚魚), cultivation (養殖) of kelp (再來麻) and laver (미역), and propagation (增殖) of rockweed (岩苔類). The business (事業) was mainly (爲主) conducted (推進) as a communal (共同) effort (事業) at the fishing village (漁村) level (單位), aligning (相應) with the UN/FAO development (開發) strategy (戰略) of conserving (保存) and developing (開發) marine (海洋) resources (資源).


--- (p. 492) ---

# ④ Fishery Village Sideline Businesses (漁村副業)

In our country, fishery villages (漁村) rely not only on fishing (漁業) for household (家計) self-sufficiency (自立), but also because near-shore (沿近海) fishing activities (漁撈活動) are seasonal (季節性) due to natural conditions (自然條件). Therefore, increasing the non-fishing income (漁業外所得) of fishermen (漁家) is of considerable strategic (戰略的) importance.

This initiative aimed to increase income (所得) from fishery village sideline businesses (漁村副業) by producing handicrafts (工藝品) using fishery by-products (漁撈副產物) such as shellfish (貝類), processing food (食品加工) like salted and fermented seafood (鹽藏物) such as jeotgal (젓갈류), and dried fish (乾魚物) such as anchovies (멸치). By utilizing the idle labor force (遊休勞動力) in fishery villages (漁村), this initiative significantly contributed to increasing the disposable income (可處分所得) of fishermen (漁家).

# ⑤ Inland Water Development (內水面開發)

The inland water development (內水面開發) project was primarily aimed at promoting inland fisheries (內陸漁業) through freshwater aquaculture (淡水養殖) and increasing the income (所得) of farmers and fishermen (農漁民). The Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries (水產廳) invested a total of 1,751 million won (百萬원) in this project from 1972 to 1979.

# ⑥ Improvement of Distribution Structure (流通構造改善)

Previously, the distribution structure (流通構造) of fishery products (水產物) in our country was overly complex in the middle stages (中間段階) and the distribution facilities (流通施設) were outdated (落後), resulting in very low prices (受取價格) received by fishermen (漁家). Particularly for small-scale fishermen (零細漁家), the exploitation by middlemen (中間商人) led to excessive price margins (價格 마진) and quantity margins (物量 마진).

To address these issues (問題) and increase the income (受取所得) of fishermen (漁家), the project aimed to strengthen the processing (加工處理) functions (機能) centered around fishery village cooperatives (漁村契) and ensure fair pricing (適正價格) and sales channels (販路保障) for water (水).

# Chapter 5 Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The association (協會) oversaw the establishment and operation of sales venues (販賣場). These sales venues, organized by fishing village units (漁村契), facilitated direct distribution to consumers in cities, significantly reducing traditional intermediary distribution margins and contributing substantially to increasing fishermen's (漁家) earnings. In addition to the aforementioned projects, sisterhood ties (姉妹結緣) with fishing villages (漁村) and tourism development (觀光開發) along coastal areas (海岸地帶) were also pursued as part of efforts to increase fishermen's (漁家) income. Recently, there has been growing interest in underdeveloped villages (低開發部落), including remote fishing villages (僻地漁村) and low-income fishing villages (低所得漁村), which have lagged in development.

### (3) Achievements and Issues

The fishing village Saemaul Undong (漁村新村運動) was consistently promoted from 1972 to 1979 with a total investment of 25,927 hundred million won (百萬圓) in income increase (所得增大), production base establishment (生産基盤造成), welfare environment (福祉環境), and spiritual development (精神啓發) to achieve the goal of self-sustaining growth (自立成長).

However, most fishing villages (漁村) centered around fishing village units (漁村契) faced challenges such as insufficient voluntary participation (自發的參與) of fishermen (漁民), a lack of capable leaders, and inadequate investment in Saemaul projects, which collectively hindered the achievement of expected outcomes. While the income of fishermen (漁家) increased significantly due to the promotion of Saemaul projects, it still lagged considerably behind urban households (都市家口) and farming households (農家), and income disparities within fishing villages (漁村) became pronounced, as shown in <Table 51>. The increase in fishermen's (漁家) income cannot be attributed solely to income-increasing projects (所得增大事業) but should be viewed in conjunction with related indirect support projects such as production base establishment (生産基盤造成) and welfare environment (福祉環境). Notably, production base establishment (生産基盤造成), excluding the reconstruction of fishing ports (漁港修築), showed almost no progress until 1975, which could be considered a factor that limited the potential for future income increase (所得增大). Furthermore, previous income-increasing projects (所得增大事業) in fishing villages (漁村) had relied on a single-project (單一事業) approach, failing to maximize complementary and supplementary effects (補完補充效果) tailored to regional characteristics (地域特性) in an integrated manner. In other words, while the content of the projects was systematically organized in stages, the implementation method was fragmented, preventing the limited investment resources from reaching economic units.

Additionally, the year-to-year fluctuations in fishery household income appear to be more severe compared to farm households or urban households, which is another issue. From the perspective of stabilizing fishery household income, new measures need to be explored.

### Section 3: Welfare and Social Services of the Saemaul Undong

#### I. The Significance of Welfare and Social Services

Throughout the development of the Saemaul Undong, welfare and social services have been actively promoted since the early stages of the movement and have achieved remarkable results. In the Saemaul Undong, welfare and environmental projects have played a strategic role in motivating residents to participate and in continuously fostering their motivation. While production base projects, income augmentation projects, and spiritual development projects expect relatively long-term and intangible results and qualities, projects in the welfare and environmental sector manifest their results or the outcomes of efforts in a tangible and visible form within the daily lives of residents. Therefore, these projects hold strategic importance among all the projects.


--- (p. 495) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

In the initial stage of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), there was a tendency to focus on tangible and visible welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業), leading to criticism that the movement was overly concerned with demonstrating immediate improvements in the residents' (住民) physical living environment (生活環境). However, the achievements and contributions of these welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業) were significant in several aspects for igniting and sustaining the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).

Firstly, for a nationwide movement like the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), it is crucial to motivate residents (住民) by providing immediate and tangible benefits that they can experience firsthand. In this regard, the initial welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) played an excellent role. Starting with improvements in the immediate living environment (生活環境), these projects fostered self-help (自助的) spirit and cooperative methods among residents (住民), serving as a good opportunity. The logic was that a national movement (國民運動) should start with nearby and easier tasks rather than distant and difficult ones.

Secondly, welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業) addressed the basic needs and demands of residents (住民). They provided an opportunity to establish a new development philosophy (開發哲學) that went beyond materialistic and monetary economic growth (經濟成長主義). The results of development (開發), from the perspective of the citizens (國民), manifested as improvements in their daily living environment (生活環境). Therefore, during the high-growth period from the 1960s (年代) to the 1970s (年代), welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業) were crucial in meeting the rising expectations of residents (住民) and visualizing these expectations. These projects were not merely about tangible and visible contributions but were also processes aimed at increasing income (所得增大) and spiritual development (精神啓發), making significant contributions.

Thirdly, the welfare and environmental projects (福祉環境事業) sector evolved and expanded in scope and depth alongside the development of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). Initially focused on roof improvement projects (改良事業), the movement progressed to housing improvement projects (改良事業) and, by the mid-1970s (年代), further intensified into village structure improvement projects (聚落構造改善事業), bringing about qualitative and quantitative transformations. The village structure improvement projects (聚落構造改善事業) deepened the spatial reorganization (空間的再編成) of roof improvement (改良), housing improvement (住宅改良), and agricultural management (農業經營), which was noteworthy.


--- (p. 496) ---

Furthermore, the improvement of village structures (취락구조개선) has served as a comprehensive development tool that enables the integrated promotion of related welfare and environmental projects, such as simple water supply (간이급수), public toilets (공동변소), sewer installation (하수구설치), and the enhancement of village communication facilities (마을통신시설향상).

Fourthly, the welfare and living projects (복지후생사업) carried out as part of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) possess an encompassing nature (포괄성). Rather than ending as individual projects (개별사업), they formed another elevated business system (사업체계) as a totality (총체). This is a characteristic (특색) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), demonstrating its inherent completeness (자체 완결성) and the logic of its promotion (추진논리). Welfare and environmental projects (복지환경사업) were implemented as pre-investments (선행투자) for production base formation projects (생산기반조성사업), and production base formation projects (생산기반조성사업) were promoted before income augmentation projects (소득증대사업). This can be likened to the logic (논리) that in economic development (경제개발), social overhead capital investment (사회간접자본투자) and direct production activities (직접생산 활동) must precede development (개발). Therefore, welfare and environmental projects (복지환경사업), income augmentation projects (소득증대사업), production base formation (생산기반조성), and spiritual development projects (정신계발사업) were inseparable development tools (개발수단). The contribution (공헌) and achievements (성과) of these various development tools (제(諸) 개발수단) had a synergistic (상승적) effect and were mutually complementary (상호보완적), which was another characteristic (특색) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동).

Fifthly, we can point to the content-specific characteristics (내용적 특성) of the welfare and living sector (복지후생부문) that the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in our country signifies. While welfare and living (복지후생) from a national development policy perspective (국가개발정책적 차원) implies social security (사회보장) or social policy measures (사회정책적 제수단), the welfare and living sector (복지후생부문) in the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) had a self-limited meaning (제한된 의미). The Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) did not replace the development philosophy (개발철학) pursued since the 1960s (1960년대), which was economic development (경제개발), but rather started from the modernization of rural areas (농촌근대화), which had been relatively neglected in the process of economic development (경제개발) or industrialization (공업화). Therefore, the welfare and living sector (복지후생부문) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) had a meaning (의미) that was not opposed to economic development (경제개발), but rather focused on the improvement of living environments (주거환경 개선), the enhancement of medical and health services (의료보건 향상), and the development of underdeveloped regions (낙후지역 개발), which are ordinary meanings (평범한 의미) for the improvement of the national living environment (국민생활환경 향상). The welfare and living projects (복지후생사업) embedded in the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) were not abstract and grandiose development strategies (개발전략) like social development (사회개발), but rather focused on the improvement and enhancement of the living environment (생활환경 향상과 개선) that citizens (국민) could feel most keenly in their daily lives (일상생활), which can be cited as a characteristic (특성).

Above, we have examined the general characteristics (일반적 특성) and significance (의의) of welfare and living projects (복지후생사업) related to the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in our country. Next, we will look at the following, carried out as part of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동).


--- (p. 497) ---

By reclassifying various welfare and living standards (福祉厚生) business sectors (事業部門), it seems possible to evaluate the achievements and results of the Saemaul Undong (運動) in a more systematic way. The welfare and living standards business sectors (福祉厚生事業部門) can be broadly reclassified into five areas (領域): living environment improvement projects (生活環境改善事業), medical (醫療) and health promotion projects (保健向上事業), small town (小都邑) improvement and development projects (整備及開發事業), island (島嶼) and port (港灣) development projects (開發事業), and other projects (其他事業). First, as living environment improvement projects (生活環境改善事業), we can include roof improvement (地改良), housing improvement (住宅改良), village structure improvement (聚落構造改善), village communication (通信) and telephone projects (電化事業), and daycare center operations (託兒所運營). These are all focused on improving the overall living environment (生活環境改善) of the village. Second, as medical (醫療) and health promotion projects (保健向上事業), there are medical activities (醫療活動) related to the medical (醫療) and health (保健) of the people (國民), nutrition management (營養管理), family planning (家族計劃), and water supply and sanitation management (給水衛生管理). Third, as small town (小都邑) development (開發) and improvement projects (整備事業), considering the special characteristics (特殊性) of small towns (小都邑) that possess both rural (農村的) and urban (都市的) characteristics (性格) in the context of the bifurcation (兩分化) of rural (農村) and urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (運動), we have classified small town (小都邑) beautification and small town (小都邑) functionalization projects (機能化事業) as one project (事業). Fourth, as island (島嶼) and port (港灣) development (開發) projects (事業), considering the locational (立地的) and strategic (開發戰略上) special characteristics (特殊性) of islands (島嶼), we have grouped island (島嶼) and off-island (落島) development and port (港灣) and other (其他) development together. Finally, we will examine the achievements and results of the Saemaul Undong (運動) over the past 10 years (年間) by project (事業別), separately classifying temple (寺刹) environment improvement projects (環境整備事業) that do not belong to any of the above (以上) but have their own special characteristics (特殊性).

## 2. Living Environment Improvement Projects (生活環境改善事業)

### 가. Housing Improvement Projects (住宅改良事業)

#### (1) Background of the Project (事業의 배경)

The rural (農漁村) housing improvement project (住宅改良事業) was a major national undertaking (大役事) aimed at inheriting (繼承) the rural (農漁村) residential living culture (住居生活文化) that has been passed down (傳來) through 5,000 years (年) of history (歷史), adapting (適應) to modern (近代的) lifestyles (生活樣式) while preserving (維持) traditional culture (傳統文化), and making the living environment (住居生活) convenient (便利) and beautiful (美麗).

Analyzing (分析) the state (實態) of rural housing (農村住宅), which had been a symbol (象徵) of stagnation (停滯) and backwardness (落後) for centuries (數世紀) in our country, in terms of its location (立地), it was generally situated (立地) in a backs-to-the-mountain-and-faces-to-the-water (背山臨水型) layout, where it was easy (容易) to secure (確保) farmland (農耕地), water (用水), and fuel (燃料), and oriented (指向) towards the south with the east gate (南向東門) to allow for wind protection (防風) and ample sunlight (日照).


--- (p. 498) ---

However, housing arrangements were scattered and inefficient, living spaces and workspaces were mixed, housing materials were not sturdy, sanitary facilities were poor, and housing sizes were too small. Additionally, farmers' mindsets were conservative and passive, making it impossible to introduce improved living styles.

After the 1960s, as the government's rural modernization policies and economic development plans were implemented, while issues of clothing and food were somewhat resolved, the living environment in rural and fishing villages remained unchanged and stuck in old ways.

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong, which began in the early 1970s, started with environmental improvement projects. Rural housing environment improvement projects were a key initiative of the Saemaul Undong from its early stages.

## (2) Project Development and Achievements

### (a) Roof Improvement Project
The roof improvement project was initiated as a spark project for the Saemaul Undong before embarking on a full-scale housing improvement project and village improvement project in rural areas.

By replacing thatched roofs in rural and fishing villages with tiles, slates, or corrugated iron, this project aimed to improve the living standards of farming households and the overall living environment in rural areas. Additionally, it sought to utilize the remaining straw to produce processed goods or industrial raw materials, increase non-farming income, use it as fuel and fertilizer, conserve forest resources, and contribute to increased production, among other multi-purpose effects.

Thus, the roof improvement project played a leading role in improving the living environment and transforming poor and backward rural areas into economically and modernized ones.

In 1972, the government invested 41 billion won, residents contributed 87 billion won, totaling 128 billion won, to start improving the roofs of 413,000 households. By 1978, an additional 38 billion won was invested to improve the roofs of 30,000 households.


--- (p. 499) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Improving (良) to achieve the goal of 2,456 thousand units (千棟), 107% of the target was accomplished with 2,618 thousand units (千棟) improved (改良), and the roof improvement project (事業) was completed in 1978.

### (B) Rural Housing Improvement Project (農漁村住宅改良事業)

The roof improvement project (改良事業) has been replacing thatched roofs (草家) with tiles, slates, or galvanized sheets. However, a significant number (相當數) of existing rural houses (農村住宅) have weak (弱) and dilapidated (老朽不良) lower structures (下部構造), requiring either complete reconstruction (改築) or replacement with new buildings (新築). Therefore, it became necessary to go beyond roof improvements and move towards repairing (補修) or constructing (建設) rural houses (農漁村住宅).

As the roof improvement project (事業) was successfully implemented and the basic (基礎的) improvement (改善) of rural housing (農村住宅) environment (環境) was achieved to some extent, on September 25, 1975, the late President (大統領) Park Chung-hee instructed to study (硏究) the standardization (規格化) plan (方案) for rural housing (農村住宅). Then, on November 4 of the same year, he instructed, "From now on, we should focus (力點) more on housing (住宅) improvement (改良) rather than roof improvement (改良). Let's consider 1976 as the trial period (試驗期間) for the promotion (普及) of rural housing (農村住宅) and launch a large-scale (大大的) promotion (推進) starting from 1977."

According to the housing (住宅) census results (結果) of the Economic Planning Board (經濟企劃院) in 1975, the total number (總) of rural houses (農村住宅) in our country was 2,925 thousand units (千棟). Among these, 500 thousand units (千棟), corresponding to 18%, were substandard houses (不良住宅). These are being improved (改良) annually (年次的) under the first five-year (第1段階 5個年) substandard housing improvement plan (不良住宅改良計劃) from 1977 to 1981.

The rural housing improvement project (農漁村住宅改良事業), which was one of the environmental improvement projects (環境改善事業) and the core (中心) of the first stage (第1段階) of the Saemaul Undong (運動), has been further developed (發展) in a more fundamental (根源的) way. As a leading project (先導事業) for the second stage (第2段階) of the Saemaul Undong (運動), it aims to enhance (向上) the welfare (福祉) level (水準) of rural residents (農漁村住民). Based on the experiences (經驗), technologies (技術), and cooperative spirit (協同精神) cultivated (圖謀) through the achievements (成果) of the Saemaul Undong (運動), it is a policy (施策) to expedite (實施) the ideal (理想) modernization (近代化) of rural areas (農村) in the 1980s (年代). This project (事業) is based on community cooperation (住民協同).


--- (p. 500) ---

Prior to the comprehensive improvement of rural housing (農村住宅), the government concurrently carried out the Jigong Improvement Project (事業) to partially improve substandard housing located near roads, highways, and railways, as well as houses in low-lying areas near rivers, mountainous valleys, and remote islands prone to flooding. In 1976, under government leadership, the feasibility of rural and fishing village housing improvement projects (農漁村住宅改良事業) was assessed, and resident preferences for housing types and sizes were analyzed. Based on the lessons learned from the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), a trial phase was implemented. In 1977, the project was expanded to other regions based on the results of the trial, and from 1978 onwards, the housing improvement project was fully implemented nationwide.

From 1976 to 1979, a total of 185,782 units were improved with an investment of 262,727 million won, achieving 34.4% of the total target of 540,000 units.

The improvement content shows that 56% was supported improvement and 44% was self-improvement. The funding composition was 72.2% loans, 4.8% subsidies, and 23.0% resident burden, indicating that most improvements were made through loans.
