## Chapter 5: The Nature and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

First, it strengthens enlightenment (啓蒙);

Second, it emphasizes fostering a respect for the law (遵法精神) through school education (學校敎育) and family education (家庭敎育).

Third, it promotes practical enlightenment (實踐啓蒙) to maintain law and order (遵法秩序) through law-abiding education (遵法敎育) for members of professional organizations (職能團體) and various levels of Saemaul organizations (새마을組織).

Fourth, to realize a life of law and order (遵法秩序 生活), efforts are being made to promote law-abiding life (遵法生活) through Saemaul spirit enlightenment (새마을精神啓蒙), flag-lowering ceremonies (國旗降下式), and the removal of decadent (頹廢的) factors (要因), as well as campaigns for traffic order (交通秩序), education for drivers (運轉者) and guides (案內員), and the expansion of facilities (施設) for order induction (秩序誘導). Additionally, efforts are being made to prevent littering, improve the environment of markets and shopping districts (市場商街 環境整備), and renew the street environment (街路環境). All possible measures are being taken in these areas.

Fifth, continuous efforts are being made to crack down on offenders (沮害事犯) who disrupt street order (距離 秩序), such as those who obstruct automobile (自動車) and pedestrian (步行者) traffic (交通沮害 行爲), as well as offenders who violate public morals (公衆道德 違反者), eliminate decadent trends (頹廢風潮 一掃), and disrupt recreational order (行樂秩序). Additionally, efforts are being made to crack down on offenders who disrupt environmental order (環境秩序), such as those who have the habit of littering (習性), illegal advertisements (不良廣告物), and unclean areas (不健全地帶).

### (Da) For the Institutionalization of Neighborhood Cooperation (隣保協同)

First, efforts are being made to make regular attendance at neighborhood meetings (班常會) a habit and to strengthen the operation of neighborhood meetings (班常會) for the efficient promotion of common interests (共同關心事).

Second, related organizations (有關組織) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) are emphasizing the autonomous (自律的) practice of urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을運動) and the effective (實效性) development of projects as neighborhood cooperation organizations (隣保協同組織), as well as the leading role (先導的 役割) of fostering an advanced citizen consciousness (先進市民 意識).

Third, sports clubs (體育클럽) such as soccer, basketball, tennis, and table tennis, as well as hobby clubs (趣味同好人會) such as metal crafts (金屬工藝), embroidery (刺繡), flower arrangement (꽃꽂이), choir (合唱), mountain climbing (登山), fishing, and early morning meetings (早起會) are being organized to deepen and expand projects such as:

1. Developing hobby activities (趣味活動) utilizing school facilities (學校施設)
2. Cultivating a spirit of cooperation (協同意識) among members (會員) through hobby activities (趣味活動)
3. Creating a harmonious atmosphere (和合雰圍氣) through mutual communication (意思疏通) among members (會員)
4. Promoting a climate of rewarding good and punishing evil (勸善懲惡 風土)

### (3) Workplace Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The government has been making all-out efforts to promote the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) in an autonomous (自律的) and systematic (體系化) manner under the cooperation (協助) of private organizations (民間團體), aiming to unite the will of the people (國民意志) and cultivate self-reliance (自主力) through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), thereby creating a new history (歷史) of independence (自主), self-reliance (自立), and prosperity (繁榮).

Since 1978, the government has been focusing on the Three Major Order Movements (大秩序運動) as the basis of the urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을運動) to establish citizen order (市民秩序), establish discipline for action order (行動秩序紀綱), and renew urban environmental order (都市環境 秩序).


--- (p. 550) ---

As the movement progressed, the private organization Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Council actively participated and shifted its business promotion direction to the Three Great Order Movements, dividing its overall business into movements for spiritual order, behavioral order, and environmental order. In particular, it has been carrying out key promotion businesses such as the Healthy Workplace Movement, Neighbor Helping Movement, Saemaul Education Business, Establishment of Traffic Order and Joint Use of Private Cars Movement, Nature Conservation Movement, Strengthening of Labor-Management Cooperation System Movement, and Order Establishment Promotion Business.

As the year 1979 approached, the aforementioned Council focused on promoting the workplace Saemaul Undong as the core of urban Saemaul Undong. Its characteristics are as follows:

First, by maximizing the educational function, it brought about a great transformation in the consciousness structure of citizens, removed the sparseness of citizens' interpersonal relationships, indifference to regional society, and lack of solidarity, and at the same time corrected them while practicing and mastering the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation.

Second, through the promotion of spiritual development movements, it fostered a harmonious atmosphere among workplace people and cultivated public morality to encourage voluntary practical will.

Third, by making thrift and savings a way of life, it established a healthy social atmosphere and greatly contributed to overcoming resource difficulties through the conservation of materials and "energy."

Fourth, through the Inbo (Neighborhood Watch) Movement, it encouraged workplace people and local residents to help each other, thus accelerating the formation of a communal consciousness.

Since 1980, the urban Saemaul Undong has been promoted while maintaining a common character, but to establish the image of Saemaul citizens, it is pursuing the promotion of private sector-led Saemaul Undong, the substantialization of Saemaul promotion and education, the cultivation and spread of excellent Saemaul, and the strong promotion of occupational Saemaul Undong.

### D. Reflection

Korean society is experiencing the collapse of traditional values due to rapid urbanization and overconcentration of population, and significant changes in the structure of consciousness due to the indiscriminate influx of Western culture. Meanwhile, the characteristics of urbanites are emerging as the rise of the omnipotence of wealth, the expansion of egoism, moral decline, extravagance and waste, and the desire for quick success. Therefore, the urban Saemaul Undong, which has been promoted since 1973, has greatly contributed to gradually improving and overcoming these pathological phenomena of urbanites.


--- (p. 551) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

In this way, as the urban Saemaul Undong (運動) progresses, significant achievements are being made across various fields. However, there are still inherent (內包的) issues within the project's implementation process and external (外延的) projects that need to be expanded.

First, let's examine the inherent (內包的) issues of the urban Saemaul Undong (運動). These include:

1. Urban residents' (都市人) perceptions of their occupations (職業), interests (關心), and living standards (生活水準) vary greatly, leading to a lack of interest in neighborhood and regional projects (地域事業). Consequently, there is a shortage of materials (素材) for common interests (共同關心事) and a lack of cooperative attitudes (協力姿勢).
2. Due to the unique living conditions (生活條件) of urban areas, it is difficult to find Saemaul leaders (指導者), and their leadership (リーダーシップ) is often hindered by surrounding circumstances (周邊與件). Moreover, they often lack a sense of mission (使命感).
3. The conditions for the participation of social leaders (社會指導層) and the wealthy (富裕層) are insufficient, and there are not enough incentives (誘引策) to encourage participation in the Saemaul Undong (運動). As a result, projects promoting frugality (消費節約) and neighborhood cooperation (隣保協同事業) are not being carried out effectively.

Next, let's list the external (外延的) issues that require special attention and improvement in the field of urban Saemaul Undong (運動):

1. Measures to prevent various crimes (各種犯罪). Recently, the increase in various crimes and the intellectualization (知能化), large-scale (大型化), and brutality (暴惡化) of criminal activities have become significant social issues (社會的 病因). Notably, the frequency of crimes (頻度) is higher in large cities (大都市) than in rural areas (農村) or towns (邑單位地域), highlighting the relatively strong tendency towards interest group (利益集團) behavior in urban areas.
2. Traffic problems (交通問題). Traditionally, our efforts to improve the supply (供給) and price stability (價格安定) of final consumer goods (最終消費財) centered around clothing, food, and housing (衣食住) have been a priority. However, with the progress of industrialization (產業化) and the growing interest in improving welfare (福祉向上), the demand (欲求) for solutions to transportation issues (行問題) is also increasing. Although the government's (政府) efforts are gradually improving traffic conditions (交通問題), the quantitative (量的) increase in transportation means (交通手段) is not keeping up with the expansion of transportation facilities (交通施設) and roads (道路), leading to traffic congestion (交通滯症) and other inconveniences and dangers in urban areas (都市).
3. Gradual measures to address tense human relationships (人間關係) should be pursued.


--- (p. 552) ---

The construction of high-rise "apartments" and the development of luxurious housing in development areas are blocking neighborly interactions and making people's hearts increasingly harsh. Along with this, research findings show that the stronger the urban nature, the higher the education level, the younger the age, the higher the income, and the more specialized knowledge or social prestige required in one's occupation, the worse human relationships become.

The initial Urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을運動) was promoted in four fields—workplace, region, family, and school—through thrift and neighborhood watch movements (근검절약 and 임보운동), resulting in remarkable achievements in urban environmental improvement, new village labor credit business (새마을노대사업), and comprehensive citizen education (汎市民敎育面).

Subsequently, the movement aimed to establish a sound value system (가치관) based on the morality (道義) and public benefit (公益) of urban citizens, and to foster a lifestyle philosophy (生活哲學) grounded in norms (規範) and public spirit (公德心). This effort sought to improve the order (秩序) of clean and dignified urban spaces (都市空間) and to promote citizen education (市民啓導) through tasks easily practicable in our daily lives, such as pedestrian order (步行秩序), picking up trash (休紙줍기), speaking politely (고운말쓰기), and observing etiquette (禮儀지키기), thereby further maturing the atmosphere.

Moreover, with the establishment of the Saemaul Citizen Model (새마울市民像) as its goal, the movement actively encouraged voluntary participation (參與) from professional organizations (職能團體) and self-organized groups (自生組織), fostering a vibrant spirit (氣風). Examples include regional (地域別) operations of neighborhood associations (반상회운영), workplace (職場別) initiatives such as street order (거리秩序), simple trade order (簡去來秩序), public morals (公衆道德), and the movement for moral living (生活道義運動). Through these efforts, the Urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을運動) was fully established on a solid foundation, leading to a comfortable and clean city (都市) in terms of environment (環境面), an orderly city in terms of behavior (行動面), and a dignified city in terms of spirit (精神面).

However, these improvement efforts should be seen as an ongoing process (過程), not a final stage (完結段階), and thus their continuity (繼紹性) must be maintained. Additionally, active measures (活性化面) are necessary to address inherent issues (內包的問題點) that are difficult to resolve during the promotion process (推進過程) and new challenges (課題) that arise concomitantly.

Regarding measures for inherent issues (內包的問題點):

First, to address apathy (無關心) stemming from differences in occupation (職業), interest (關心), and living standards (生活水準), it is essential to start with easy projects (事業) and common interests (共同關心事) through various voluntary organizations (自發的單體) or ad hoc groups (任意組織) as centers, gradually expanding from there.

Second, to tackle the difficulty in discovering Saemaul leaders (새마을指導者) and the lack of a sense of mission (使命感) due to urban (都市) living conditions, it is crucial to develop the unique characteristics (個性) and traits (特性) of each city (都市).


--- (p. 553) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

I believe that it is very important to discover and cultivate Saemaul leaders (指導者) from among those engaged in industries (業種) suited to the characteristics of each region (地域) (e.g., ancient capital (古都) cities, lakeside (湖畔) cities, resort (休養) cities, green cities), and to expand and develop their businesses (事業) by connecting them with their livelihoods (生業).

As a measure to induce the participation of the social (社會) leadership (指導層) and the wealthy (富裕層), it is necessary to strengthen their Saemaul education (敎育) and to expand the roles of women's associations (婦女會), centered around activities such as promoting thrift (勤儉節約), eliminating evil customs (弊習), and guiding home-based handicrafts (家內手工業).

Countermeasures for external (外延的) issues include:

First, regarding various (各種) crimes (犯罪), it is necessary to create an environment (風土) that emphasizes (重視) family (家庭) education (敎育), improve the quality (質的) of the mass media (매스컴), restore the authority (權威) of educational institutions (敎育機關), and strengthen the activities (活動) of religious (宗敎) organizations (團體). However, among these, activities (活動) and roles (役割) that are educational (啓導的) should be considered as part of the scope (範疇) of the urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).

Second, regarding traffic (交通) issues, it is possible to mention the early completion (早期完工) of additional (追加) subway (地下鐵) construction (工事), the establishment (新設) and expansion (擴充) of automobile (自動車) road networks (道路網), the expansion (擴充) of parking (駐車場) facilities (施設), and the observance (遵守) of traffic (交通) order (秩序). However, without a significant improvement in the national (國民) consciousness (意識) regarding the maintenance (維持) of order (秩序) through urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), it is believed that the intended (所期) purpose (目的) cannot be achieved (達成).

Third, regarding measures to alleviate strained human relationships (人間關係), it is necessary to purify (醇和) national (國民的) values (價値觀) through Saemaul education (敎育) for each social stratum (各階層別), have the intellectual (知識人) and other (各界) leadership (指導) strata (階層) take the lead (率先垂範), have media organizations (言論機關) actively (主導的) promote the formation (形成) of excellent (優秀) human relationships (人間關係), and have religious (宗敎) organizations (團體) and other (等) charitable (慈善) activities (活動) serve as exemplary (示範的) guides (啓導). Additionally, successful (成功) cases (事例) should continue to be accumulated (蓄積) and promoted (弘報) through the urban (都市) Saemaul Undong (새마을運動).

## 2. Factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

### Ga. Background (背景)

The Factory (工場) Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) was ignited (點火) during the period (時期) of the first (第1次) oil shock (oil shock) in 1973 (年), when the national economy (國民經濟) was suffering a major (大) blow (打擊). The oil shock (oil shock) caused a sharp (急) rise (騰) in energy (能源) prices (價格) and other (等) raw material (原資材) prices (價格), which greatly (大) stimulated (刺激) domestic (國內) prices (物價) and reduced (減少) real (實質) income (所得) and demand (需要), leading to a recession (不景氣), slowed (鈍) growth (成長), and increased (增加) unemployment (失業). At the same time (同時), the increased (增加) burden (負擔) of imports (輸入) and the slowed (鈍) exports (輸出) resulted in a current account (國際收支) deficit (赤字).


--- (p. 554) ---

# Expansion and Development of the Factory Saemaul Undong

To address the severe economic challenges both domestically and internationally, a new powerful strategy was urgently needed. In response, the Factory Saemaul Undong was born.

Under adverse economic conditions, the Factory Saemaul Undong aimed to rearm disheartened workers with the new Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. It encouraged efforts to improve productivity through energy conservation, material savings, and cost reduction. Meanwhile, business owners were urged to re-recognize their social responsibilities, improve workers' welfare, and rationalize management. This dual approach helped our economy grow and stabilize, gradually absorbing the impact of the oil shock, reducing the trade deficit, stabilizing prices, recovering economic growth trends, and ensuring employment stability.

The Factory Saemaul Undong, once ignited, set out to achieve its goal of maximizing productivity through the innovation of all enterprises, the efficiency of all workers, and the reform of all factories during its early stages.

By the mid-1970s, Korean corporate management entered a major turning point. Enterprises had to simultaneously fulfill their role as the driving force behind the continuous growth of the national economy domestically and strengthen international competitiveness externally. From this perspective, the movement focused on spreading and localizing the Saemaul spirit, emphasizing the improvement of workers' real income and enterprise productivity through corporate solidification. It also aimed to maximize workers' efficiency and link the accumulated passion directly to improving their real income, centering on the rationalization of management.

As a result, model enterprises were expanded, and methods for promoting productivity improvement and the Factory Saemaul Undong were disseminated. Simultaneously, a dedicated division was established in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, a promotion headquarters in the Federation of Korean Industries, and branches in local chambers of commerce to strengthen the promotion organizational system.

By the late 1970s, due to the recurrence of energy crises and resource nationalism, both domestic and international economic conditions worsened again. This necessitated the evolution of the Factory Saemaul Undong to better cope with the situation. Consequently, the movement encouraged creative efforts for overcoming difficulties through smooth labor-management cooperation and further promoted the growth of enterprises and the improvement of workers' welfare.


--- (p. 555) ---

With a focus on balance and harmony, the movement was promoted. To this end, incentives for outstanding factories were strengthened, while efforts were concentrated on stabilizing workers' lives and increasing their real income, stabilizing and strengthening the foundation for corporate management and growth, and protecting consumers. Various projects were carried out with these priorities in mind.

## II. Achievements and Results

### (1) Spiritual Development

Like the rural and urban Saemaul Undong, the factory Saemaul Undong is a movement aimed at fostering a culture of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. When viewing modernization in terms of spiritual and material aspects, the Saemaul Undong, which serves as the ideological foundation for the modernization of the nation, can be seen as a movement that seeks to embody the three major spirits in daily life and increase income based on these spirits. As Gunnar Myrdal argued in his book "Asian Drama," modernization cannot be achieved without prior spiritual rationalization, making spiritual development a crucial aspect of the factory Saemaul Undong.

Spiritual development efforts in companies and factories include:

1. Creating a workplace environment that values diligence, encouraging employees to think honestly, work sincerely, and improve their work attitudes.
2. Promoting self-help activities that enhance productivity and develop the company through creative and dedicated Saemaul Undong tasks.
3. Fostering cooperative production by strengthening teamwork, particularly in operational departments, to improve productivity.

The first step in creating this Saemaul spirit environment was the introduction of Saemaul training and education. This education covers the philosophy of the Saemaul Undong, the selection and promotion methods of practical projects, and the knowledge related to these aspects. Without a firm belief that the efforts of all employees will lead to improved welfare, regional social development support, and national development, the movement may lack depth and sustainability. Therefore, it is essential to maintain this belief throughout the process of initiating and sustaining the movement.


--- (p. 556) ---

Education in the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is absolutely necessary.

Generally, enterprises can be considered to consist of human and material elements, and the process of combining these two elements and efficiently performing their functions is essentially all enterprise management activities. Among these two elements, improving the quality of human resources is a matter related to education and training. Through education and training, the explicit and potential abilities of production subjects are developed in the direction and content required by the enterprise, thereby efficiently achieving management objectives. Behavioral scientist Cris Argyris argues that "humans generally only utilize about one-third of the abilities they possess. If the methods of use are excellent, the remaining two-thirds can also be well utilized to achieve high efficiency. However, if the methods of use are poor, even that one-third cannot be utilized, leading to a negative impact on enterprise activities." Education and training play a guiding role in developing the potential abilities of individuals.

Education and training, in addition to school education received by humans as they grow up in the world, are extended through social education in the workplace, continuously aiding human growth. Moreover, in the era of exploding knowledge and information, for efficient information management, lifelong education, and the establishment of value legitimacy in developing countries facing Durkheim's "anomic" situations, continuous education and training are even more urgent.

The factory Saemaul Undong, which began from such a perspective, saw its basic concept promoted and transmitted to companies, gradually developing educational courses. As the Factory Saemaul Leadership Training Institute's corporate class, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's first and second training institutes, and the Busan Training Institute were established in succession, many leaders were produced, becoming the driving force for the ignition and spread of the factory Saemaul Undong.

### (가) Factory Saemaul Training Institute Education (敎育)

The factory Saemaul training education, established through such processes, began with the ignition personnel training course in early 1973, where business owners, managers, and middle managers voluntarily enrolled. With the goal of practical life education and cultivating the leadership abilities of leaders, this education, which had initially been limited to model companies, gradually saw an increase in educational demand as the factory Saemaul Undong spread. Consequently, the Korea Electric Power Corporation Training Institute, on March 18, 1974, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry


--- (p. 557) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

Designated as the Saemaul Undong Factory Training Institute No. 1, it produced 7,593 leaders (名) until it was transferred to the Ministry of Energy and Resources on January 20, 1979. On July 7, 1975, the Saemaul Undong Factory Training Institute No. 2 was established in the Korea Export Industrial Complex by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and by the end of July 1980, it had produced 24,869 leaders (名).

Meanwhile, efforts were made to educate the increasing number of female workers. On April 25, 1978, the Ju-an Training Institute for Women was established, and by January 1979, when it was transferred to the Saemaul Undong Training Institute, it had trained 4,076 female leaders (名). To alleviate inconveniences caused by the transfer of the training institutes (Korea Electric Power Corporation Training Institute, Ju-an) and the concentration of educational facilities, workers in the Busan region voluntarily established and operated a rare training facility in the country on November 6, 1978, focusing on training leaders in the Yeongnam and Honam regions.

The educational achievements of the Saemaul Undong Factory Training over the past 7 years amount to a total of 47,936 individuals (名), with an increasing trend in participation rates each year.

When divided by position, representatives and executive-level individuals total 13,908 (名), accounting for 29.4%, while middle management totals 19,462 (名), accounting for 41.2%. The training institutes designated by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry have focused on individuals with significant influence and potential for educational impact within corporate entities.

When divided by gender, out of the total 47,198 individuals (名) who completed the education, 84.6% (39,952 individuals (名)) are male, while female leaders account for only 15.3% (7,246 individuals (名)). This disparity is due to the insufficient investment in female education by corporations and the lack of specialized educational facilities for women, which has hindered continuous female education. However, the government has focused on educating representatives of working women, such as dormitory supervisors and group leaders, to ensure that the educational effects are quickly disseminated.

In terms of the educational curriculum, the focus was primarily on the fundamental ideology of the Saemaul Undong (Movement), national security, and the economic situation.


--- (p. 558) ---

In addition to the basic subjects (基本科目) covering quality (質), the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) included unique subjects (科目) such as quality management (品質管理), productivity improvement (生産性向上), labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), and the technique of division of tasks and discussion (分任討議技法), thereby enhancing educational effects (敎育效杲). In particular, in 1980, the focus of education (敎育) was placed on establishing professional ethics (職業倫理) and corporate ethics (企業倫理) and strengthening the social responsibility (社會的責任) of corporations (企業).

In selecting instructors (講師選定), considering that the target audience (敎育對象者) were mid-level executives (幹部級) who were core personnel (核心要員) of the Korean economy (經濟界), authorities (權威者) in the relevant subjects (該當科目) were invited (招聘). In terms of educational methods (敎育方法), the approach moved away from being solely lecture-based (講義式一邊倒) to incorporating various educational materials (敎育器資材) such as audio-visual aids (視聽覺敎材), as well as encouraging discussion (討論) and participation (參與) to motivate (動機誘發) behavioral change (行動的變化) and self-reinforcement (自己强化).

Each training institute (各硏修院) also conducted follow-up guidance (追隨指導) for a certain period (一定期間) (6 days and 7 nights (泊日) to 4 days and 5 nights (泊日)) in addition to regular education (正規敎育). They collected self-reflection logs (自省錄) and personal resolutions (決議) written during the education period (敎育期間) and sent them back after a certain period (一定期間) had passed (經過) to revive (喚起) the Saemaul spirit (새마을精神). They also conducted regular surveys (設問) of the trainees (敎育研修者) to share the latest techniques (最新技法) and to listen to their suggestions (建議) and difficulties (隘路).

Such training education (硏修敎育) was not only conducted at the training institutions (硏修機關) designated by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部). As the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) became more privately led (民間主導), private training institutions (民間硏修院) targeting general employees (一般職員) were established in addition to the designated training institutes (指定硏修院) that had focused on executives (幹部敎育) and company presidents (企業體長).

This was due to the fact that the two training facilities (硏修施設) designated by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (商工部) could not meet the educational demand (敎育需要), and as the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) progressed under private leadership (民間主導), it was a result of the will (意志) of those who aimed to cultivate (養成) seeds for the modernization (近代化) of the motherland (祖國).

As of July 1980, there were a total of 8 private training institutions (民間硏修院) (Table 70), and the number of people they educated reached 164,454.

The achievements of such training education (硏修敎育) included not only providing a turning point (轉機) for self-renewal (自我革新) by bringing together people (企業人) from various industries (業種) across the nation (全國各處) to exchange opinions (意見) and learn problem-solving methods (問題解決的方法) regardless of their rank (職級), but also serving as a foundation (土臺) for the quantitative expansion (量的擴大) and qualitative deepening and development (質的深化發展) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) as they returned to their respective reference groups (準據集團) and carried out core movements (核運動).


--- (p. 559) ---

The movement, as shown in the next chapter, has shown concrete results in labor-management cooperation (勞使協調), productivity improvement (生産性向上), cost reduction (原價節減), and employee welfare improvement (從業員福祉向上). The foundation of these results can be said to have started from education (敎育).

Just as the great leap in modern science (近代科學) was the result of "thinking from a different angle (角度) and reaching a conclusion (結論) that had not been reached before," the self-rediscovery (自我再發見) and innovation (革新) through factory Saemaul education (新村敎育) is what the British (英國) historian (家) Butterfield called a "change in thinking (思考的轉換)." It can also be said that it has become an opportunity (契機) to change the conventional (從來) corporate view (企業觀), labor-management view (勞使觀), and occupational view (職業觀).

(b) On-site Training (巡廻敎育) by Economic Organizations (經濟團體)

Separate from the training (硏修) process (課程) that focused on self-change (自我變化) through theory (理論) and discussion (討議) by isolating a limited number of people (人員) in a certain place (場所), on-site training (巡廻敎育) methods that go directly to the field (現場) of the business (業體) to provide the latest (最新) information (情報) and techniques (技法) and to listen to opinions (意見) were developed from 1978 to provide more people (人員) with economical (經濟的) and direct (直接的) on-site (現場) education (敎育).

In line with this, the Factory Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Promotion Headquarters (推進本部) has developed a method to provide more people (人員) with economical (經濟的) and direct (直接的) on-site (現場) education (敎育) by going directly to the field (現場) of each (各) company (企業體) to provide the latest (最新) information (情報) and techniques (技法) and to listen to opinions (意見).


--- (p. 560) ---

### (2) Labor-Management Cooperation

In modern society, often referred to as the age of organizations, every individual is absorbed into an organization and realizes themselves as a member of it. Therefore, as humans have long been called social animals, the history of humanity can be seen as a complex and diverse process of social organization development. Society, as a group of humans living in the same place under some law or norm, can achieve healthy development when the people constituting it demonstrate sincerity, effort, progressive spirit, and correct consciousness, thereby fostering harmonious human relationships.

In this context, if the members of an organization established to achieve a certain goal do not feel a sense of responsibility for achieving the organization's objectives, lack motivation and morale, and are trapped in dissatisfaction, there will be frequent disagreements between management and labor. Consequently, the will to develop and the quality of products will continue to decline, and the development and prosperity of the enterprise will be at risk.

### (다) In-house Corporate Education

Meanwhile, each corporation also established in-house training institutes, with 21 companies going so far as to set up affiliated training institutes, to ensure the early establishment of the Factory Saemaul Undong. These companies operated separate Factory Saemaul education programs in addition to their regular industrial training courses. Most other companies implemented relay education through regular Saemaul education trainees.

Thus, Factory Saemaul education, over the past seven years, has seen an increase in the number of education targets, leading to specialization of content and diversification of methods. In terms of the education system, it has become organized, and its achievements have been maximized in various aspects as discussed in the next section.


--- (p. 561) ---

## Chapter 5: Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

There is no way to skip this.
The phrase "A company is human" can be seen as originating from this context, and the role and importance of human relationships within an organization called a company are directly linked to the prosperity and decline of that company. Based on this, we will summarize the significance and importance of labor-management relations, the content and achievements of labor-management unity created through the Saemaul Undong in factories, the problems and future directions in the process of promotion, and improvement measures in order.

### (A) The Meaning and Characteristics of Labor-Management Relations

The basic direction of labor-management relations is to recognize the point that it is a human relationship and to establish a paternalistic labor-management relationship based fundamentally on the improvement of mutual human relationships. Industrial self-governance should be promoted with the aim of achieving industrial peace and social stability, while fostering a sense of social responsibility and discipline, and further strengthening the management structure of the company.

Labor-management relations can be interpreted in two ways: one refers to the relationship between the employer and the worker, and the other refers to the relationship between the labor union and the employer. The former is called the employee relationship or cooperative relationship, and the latter is called the antagonistic relationship. Originally, capital aims at profit, but as a means to this end, it produces and distributes certain socially useful goods. From the perspective of production, capital, whether it is the capital itself or a manager acting as its agent, is responsible for the functions of planning, organizing, and directing production. The relationship between the two is a productive cooperative relationship. Therefore, labor-management relations, which are in an antagonistic relationship between capital and wage labor, are at the same time in a cooperative relationship as employees between managers and workers. This nature is similar to the dual nature of a commodity as a unity of use value and exchange value. Looking at the relationship between workers and employers, once workers agree to the employment conditions of the employer and start working, they perform certain tasks under the employer's orders. Both workers and employers cooperate with each other to achieve a unified management goal. At this time, the employee relationship, which is a human relationship between the employer and the worker through command and order, can be said to be in a functional cooperative relationship for the same goal. In such a situation, the functional relationship between the employer and the worker in the provision of labor is a cooperative relationship, but in economic relations, it is a relationship in which the employer tries to provide labor at a lower wage.


--- (p. 562) ---

Labor relations often involve a conflicting relationship due to the desire for high wages. As seen above, labor relations have both conflicting and cooperative aspects, which is inevitable. We should focus on how to alleviate conflicts and promote cooperative relationships. The issue of pursuing rationality and peace between labor and management is not only a political and social problem but also a task for our industrial society. We must continuously strive for the maturation and localization of this issue.

## (b) Implementation and Achievements
Through the Factory Saemaul Undong, efforts were made to foster a sense of unity between labor and management. The Factory Saemaul Undong is a movement where entrepreneurs and workers trust and support each other, working together with one heart and one mind to improve their lives. Entrepreneurs and workers should always have the consciousness and mental attitude of being a community of shared destiny. Regardless of the challenges faced by the company, they should consider the company's actual situation and start with small and easy tasks to promote harmony and foster a sense of unity. To this end, the movement was initially promoted by executives and employees who had received Saemaul education, and the implementation and achievements of the business can be examined by distinguishing the contents promoted by the management side, the contents promoted by the workers, and the contents promoted jointly by labor and management.

First, the contents promoted by the management side include explaining the management policy, goals, and company performance to the workers, treating them like their own children, and directly participating in their difficulties or during celebrations and condolences to encourage them. They also visit the work sites to comfort the workers who are working hard, and organize joint birthday celebrations for the employees to foster a sense of gratitude towards the company and a culture of mutual respect. They always engage in dialogue and consultation to quickly and actively resolve the workers' difficulties. Additionally, to enhance the welfare of the employees, they improve the working environment by implementing businesses such as lighting, heating and cooling, ventilation, dust collection, noise prevention, and wastewater treatment, and support the workers' learning path by implementing scholarship support programs, providing scholarships, and building dormitories and dining facilities.


--- (p. 563) ---

# Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The company has installed rest areas and other welfare facilities, and has made sincere efforts in various welfare businesses such as the Saemaul savings bank and purchasing and sales centers. This has fostered a sense of gratitude among employees towards the company and instilled in them the spirit of "our factory, our shared living space."

On the other hand, workers have voluntarily understood the company's situation and participated in it, creating an atmosphere where they take care of machines as if they were their own bodies and work hard, thinking of company work as their own. This has led to increased productivity, active quality control, process improvement, and other divisional activities. Examining the contents promoted jointly by labor and management, the company holds Saemaul morning assemblies and flag-lowering ceremonies to foster patriotic and company-loving spirits, practicing industrial patriotism. The company also organizes company picnics and invites employee families to the factory, creating a second home atmosphere. Furthermore, the Labor-Management Council, composed of representatives from both management and labor, is held monthly to exchange opinions freely, fostering a harmonious labor-management cooperation atmosphere and a sense of common destiny.

Through the joint efforts and dedication of company owners and workers, mutual trust and a sense of proper professional ethics have been established. This has not only ensured employment stability and reduced turnover rates but also strengthened the company's foundation.

(4) Problems and Improvement Measures

However, in the process of overcoming various problems and difficulties, it is important to recognize that dissatisfaction and friction are inevitable in human society, groups, and organizations. While managing to handle such friction and dissatisfaction rationally and harmoniously, it is also true that there is no perfect unity or mutual satisfaction in the subtle relationship between labor and management cooperation and conflict.

Analyzing a few factors related to this:

First, human desires are infinite,

Second, there is always a conflict of understanding between managers and those being managed,

Third, industrial society is dynamic, always requiring new distributions of income and power.


--- (p. 564) ---

Fourthly, management and labor unions are institutionally set up to disagree, and if they were always in a state of agreement, there would be no need or reason for labor unions to exist. Considering this, it is necessary to consider the inevitable cooperation and harmony of conflict between management and labor. However, to actively address these factors and foster a continuous sense of unity between management and labor, the following must be considered:

Firstly, businesspeople and workers must establish a sound mental attitude, ethical values, and a sense of national identity. To achieve this, continuous and thorough Saemaul education must be strengthened to eliminate irrational thinking, envy, waste, and selfishness, and to realize a moral and righteous society.

Secondly, the closed and familial nature of corporate management must be renewed, promoting corporate transparency and professional management systems. This will not only enhance the social responsibility of corporations but also address worker grievances through dialogue and understanding, strengthening labor-management solidarity.

Thirdly, labor unions should reform their structures and activities to foster a new mental attitude and culture, supporting the coexistence and symbiosis of corporations and workers. By contributing to national economic development, labor unions can become truly influential organizations, highly regarded by workers, businesspeople, and all citizens. This requires voluntary effort and active participation in the Saemaul Undong.

Fourthly, a master plan for welfare and fringe benefits must be implemented. Considering the scale and capacity of the corporation, a feasible and persuasive welfare master plan should be created and executed annually. This will continuously improve the quality of employees and motivate them. Especially during economic downturns, workers should voluntarily endure hardships and approach corporate survival with a humble and active mindset. This must be firmly established.

From the above, we have examined the significance of the Saemaul Undong in industrial society, its main promotional contents and achievements, issues and improvement measures in the promotional process. To foster a harmonious labor-management cooperation culture and continuously strengthen the sense of unity between labor and management, the following must be done:

Firstly, the Saemaul Undong must be firmly established within all enterprises, fostering a strong sense of shared destiny between labor and management, thereby localizing Korean labor-management relations.

Secondly, the movement to make factories a second home must be promoted in a substantial and continuous manner, involving employees.


--- (p. 565) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) The Merits and Demerits (功過) and Achievements (成果) of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

By establishing a value system (價値觀) that includes national views (國家觀), life philosophies (人生觀), and professional ethics (職業倫理觀), efforts were focused on creating an environment where employees could feel secure (安心) in their workplaces (職場), find joy and fulfillment in their work lives (職場生活), and

Thirdly, under the policy (方針) of returning the fruits of labor (結實), accumulated through the blood, sweat, and tears of employees (從業員), to the employees themselves, wages (賃金) were included in the enhancement of welfare and benefits (福祉厚生擴充). Furthermore, various Saemaul incentive systems were strengthened to induce voluntary participation (自發的參與), thereby creating a workplace environment (職場風土) where honest and diligent workers (正直하고 성실한 근로자) could thrive. This was emphasized as a powerful (强力) initiative to promote the well-being of the nation (國民總和) and economic development (經濟發展).

### (3) Improving Productivity (生産性向上)

#### (a) Saemaul Undong (運動) in Factories (工場) and Productivity (生産性) Improvement (向上)

The Saemaul Undong (運動) in factories (工場) aimed to maximize productivity (生産性向上) and economic results (經濟成果) through productive activities (生産活動) based on the Saemaul spirit (精神). This movement (運動) sought to return these achievements (成果) to the employees (從業員), ultimately leading to improved welfare (福祉向上) for each individual (個人) and the success of the enterprise (企業). When considering the Saemaul Undong (運動) as a movement (運動) for both factories (工場) and employees (從業員) to thrive, productivity (生産性向上) improvement (向上) becomes an indispensable (必須不可缺) key point (要點) in promoting the movement (運動).

For all employees (從業員), who are directly involved (直接的) in enterprise (企業) operations (運營), wages (賃金) are the most important means of livelihood (生計手段). If wage (賃金) issues (問題) do not keep pace with the times (時代發展), it will negatively affect (惡影響) not only each individual (個人) but also the enterprise (企業體) and even national development (國家發展). While unconditional wage increases (無條件賃金引上) can weaken corporate management (經營), strict suppression of wage increases (引上) can reduce employees' (從業員) work motivation (勤勞意慾), leading to social and economic problems (問題). The best solution (手段) to this dilemma (進退兩難) is productivity (生産性向上) improvement (向上). This is because productivity (生産性向上) improvement (向上) is the source (源泉) of wage increases (賃金引上) and the best means (手段) to enhance the ability to pay wages (支付能力) through increased added value (附加價値增大) from productivity (生産性向上) improvement (向上).

However, in the reality (現實) of our country (我國), where technological innovation (技術革新) and facility modernization (施設近代化) have not yet been fully achieved across industries (産業全般), and productivity (生産性) based on labor hours (勞動時間) has not significantly improved (改善), two aspects (側面) must be considered: the application (適用) of rational factory management methods (合理的工場運營技法) and the enhancement (昇揚) of work motivation (勤勞意慾).


--- (p. 566) ---

To bring labor and management closer together, it is essential to promote the Factory Saemaul Undong, which aims to improve productivity through cooperation between labor and management, thereby increasing employees' quality of income and welfare. In a nutshell, the ultimate goal of the Factory Saemaul Undong is to establish a labor-management cooperation system, improve labor-management relations, enhance productivity, achieve complete self-reliant growth of Korean enterprises, and increase employees' quality of income and welfare. By efficiently addressing productivity improvement, companies naturally focus on welfare measures for employees, which in turn strengthens the labor-management cooperation system. Therefore, the successful achievement of the Factory Saemaul Undong is closely related to productivity improvement.

To this end, the Factory Saemaul Undong has established various support systems, focusing on productivity improvement as one of its core business contents. These include the production and dissemination of manuals, films, slides, and VTRs on related techniques, the activation of support for division of labor activities and suggestion systems, etc. As a result, significant achievements have been made in various fields such as the reduction of various raw and auxiliary materials, energy conservation, quality improvement and management, and process improvement. These achievements not only form the basis for the development of enterprises and the enhancement of international competitiveness but also contribute greatly to the return of these achievements to employees, regional social development, the advancement of national development, and the improvement of employees' quality of income and welfare.

### (b) Factory Saemaul Division of Labor Activities

Just as an experienced driver can tell which part of a car's engine is malfunctioning just by listening to the engine sound, employees who have worked on-site for several years are the most knowledgeable about their assigned tasks and processes. However, under the existing vertical organizational structure of management, on-site employees have only moved as one organic body following instructions and orders from the vertical hierarchy. In modern enterprises where the scale of factories has expanded and processes have become more subdivided and complex, the impact of each on-site employee's assigned tasks on the entire process and factory has increased. In such a reality, the best way to instill a sense of participation and self-realization in on-site employees, who are well-versed in their tasks and processes, and to raise them as the main players in productivity improvement is


--- (p. 567) ---

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The division of labor activities (分任活動) is a system (制度) that organizes meetings (會議組織) by distinguishing each production unit (生產單位) and discussing issues (問題點) and improvement measures (改善策) related to their work (作業) to achieve specialization (專門化) and improved productivity (生產性向上). Additionally, it contributes significantly to improving human relations (人間關係改善) by holding periodic meetings (週期的) among employees (從業員) within the production unit (生產單位). When about 10 employees (從業員) working on a particular process (工程) gather to discuss issues (問題點) related to their tasks (業務), improvement measures (改善方案), human relations (人間關係改善), and opinions (意見) on factory operations (工場運營), and implement (實踐) these, it can become a means (手段) to improve productivity (生產性向上) and promote the development (發展) of the company (企業). Therefore, the division of labor activities (分任活動) has become the main driver (主役) for improving productivity (生產性向上) in companies (企業). Consequently, guidance (指導) was provided to establish division of labor teams (分任組) in all factories (工場), develop and disseminate (普及) division of labor discussion techniques (分任討議技法), and prioritize (比重) education (敎育) on division of labor activities (分任活動) in training institutes (硏修院) and mobile training sessions (移動巡廻敎育). Additionally, guidance was provided to hold division of labor competition conferences (分任組競進大會) in each factory (各工場) to discover (發掘), reward (褒賞), promote (昇給), and advance (昇進) outstanding cases (優秀事例), and standardize (標準化) these cases within the company (社內) to improve productivity (生產性向上). Starting in 1978 (78年), national division of labor activity competitions (全國分任活動競進大會) were held to reward (褒賞) and publicize (弘報) outstanding cases (優秀事例), making division of labor activities (分任活動) a means (手段) for employees (從業員) to directly contribute (直接寄與) to improving company management (企業經營改善). As a result, as of the end of 1979 (79年), 60% of the 5,209 factories (工場) evaluated for promotion performance (推進實績評價), totaling 3,136 factories (工場), have established division of labor teams (分任組) to serve as the main drivers (主役) for improving productivity (生產性向上).

Regarding the number of division of labor teams (分任組), there was a rapid increase (急伸張) to 38,000 (38千) in 1977 (77年), 60,000 (60千) in 1978 (78年), and 69,000 (69千) in 1979 (79年). Additionally, the number of participating employees (參與人員) increased significantly to 570,000 (57萬) in 1977 (77年), 990,000 (99萬) in 1978 (78年), and 1,130,000 (113萬) in 1979 (79年).

### (다) Suggestion System (提案制度)

The suggestion system (提案制度) is a system (制度) that deviates (脫皮) from the traditional vertical management (垂直的經營) mindset (思考方式) where employees (從業員) merely follow instructions (指示) and orders (命令) from managers (經營管理者) or middle management (中間管理層). It encourages employees (從業員) to take pride (愛着) in their work (作業), actively seek improvement measures (改善策), and make bottom-up suggestions (上向式建議) that are then adopted (採擇) and implemented (實施). This system (制度) greatly contributes (寄與) to improving productivity (生產性向上) by collecting (蒐集) opinions (意見) from employees (從業員) directly involved in production (生產) in a bottom-up manner (上向式), investigating (調査) their feasibility (妥當性), and then implementing (實施) them.


--- (p. 568) ---

Therefore, this system is more effective in practical terms. To further activate this system, a reward, promotion, and advancement system was established to provide appropriate treatment to employees who made practical suggestions. As a result, by 1979, 2,716 factories, accounting for 50% of evaluation factories, had implemented this system. Additionally, in terms of performance, the total number of suggestions increased from 62,000 in 1978 to 90,000 in 1979, and the amount of rewards also increased from 2.4 billion won in 1978 to 4.1 billion won in 1979, proving that this system is gradually gaining significant response from each factory.

**(b) Achievements**
Thanks to the activities of the Saemaul Undong task forces and the activation of the suggestion system, each factory achieved remarkable results in various fields such as saving raw and auxiliary materials, energy conservation, quality management improvement, and process improvement, which greatly contributed to the development of enterprises and the enhancement of international competitiveness. Moreover, not only did it achieve tangible monetary effects, but it also improved labor-management cooperation, inter-employee human relations, employee participation awareness, self-actualization needs, and work environment, contributing significantly to the establishment of Korean labor-management relations. At the same time, by dedicating themselves to regional community development, they played a major role in realizing the social responsibility of enterprises.

Looking at the specific tangible effects, the achievements made by employees through task force activities and the suggestion system amounted to 127.2 billion won in 1978 and 250.3 billion won in 1979. When these achievements are considered as a percentage of the total manufacturing cost, they accounted for 0.9% in 1978 and 1.36% in 1979, which is a remarkably high ratio compared to the enterprise's net profit rate on total manufacturing cost. The achievements resulting from this are as follows by category:

1. **Saving Raw and Auxiliary Materials**
Saving raw and auxiliary materials is an issue of reducing various raw and auxiliary materials invested in product production, thereby reducing input costs, increasing productivity, and ultimately increasing corporate profits. Therefore, many factories have actively promoted this through task force activities and the suggestion system. However, while saving raw and auxiliary materials increases profits and productivity, if the degree of savings becomes excessive and leads to a deterioration in product quality, it reaches a stage where the original


--- (p. 569) ---

## Chapter 5: Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The essential meaning (本質的意味) of this can disappear and instead become a cause (原因) of worsening management (經營惡化).
For successful (成功的) savings of raw and auxiliary materials (原•副資材), it is crucial how to rationally (合理的) allocate and input (配分投入) the many raw and auxiliary materials (原•副資材) into the product (製品), and how to reuse (再活用) the discarded raw and auxiliary materials (原•副資材) to produce better products (製品). The key lies in finding better allocation methods (配分方法) through division of labor activities (分任活動) and suggestion systems (提案制度) in each factory (各工場), and reusing discarded raw and auxiliary materials (原•副資材). As a result, 47.5 billion won was saved in 1978 and 91.3 billion won in 1979. This translates to an average of 9,117 million won per factory in 1978 and 17,533 million won in 1979, significantly contributing to the development (發展) of the company (企業).

## ② Energy Conservation (節約)

For a resource-poor (資源) country, especially (特히) with limited energy resources (資源), energy conservation (節約) is of utmost importance (重要). Moreover, with the recent (最近) sharp rise (急上昇) in energy prices (價格), energy costs (費用) as a percentage (比率) of total manufacturing costs (總製造原價) have been increasing, making energy conservation (節約) even more critical (重要性). Through division of labor activities (分任活動) and suggestion systems (提案制度), various practical examples (實踐事例) were created, such as reusing waste heat (廢熱) and reducing the use of passenger cars (勝用車) by replacing traditional fuels (燃料) with cheaper alternatives (代替). As a result, 4.31 billion won was saved in 1978 and 85.9 billion won in 1979. On average (平均) per factory (工場當), this amounts to 8,283 million won in 1978 and 16,485 million won in 1979, greatly contributing to the rationalization (合理化) of corporate management (經營).

## ③ Process Improvement (工程改善)

Many processes (工程) are involved in producing a product (製品). Although these processes (工程) are systematically (體系的) based on rational (合理的) and scientific (科學的) grounds, there is still room for improvement (改善) in many aspects (部分的).
Given the rapid development (發達) of science (科學) and technological improvements (技術改善) at this point in time (現時點), improving the output process (產出過程) following input (投入) is a matter of life and death (死活) for a company's (企業) competitiveness (競爭力).
While process improvements (工程改善) can be achieved through scientific (科學的) and technological (技術的) innovations (革新), employees (從業員) working on the shop floor (現場) are often the best (主役) at understanding the characteristics (特徵) and content (內容) of the processes (工程), making them key players in process improvement (工程改善).


--- (p. 570) ---

Therefore, the cooperation and creativity of employees form the core of process improvement. Through employee participation in task-based discussions and suggestion systems, we can examine the results of process improvement efforts, such as:

- In 1978, 1,745 factories participated in process improvement, enhancing 16,900 processes and achieving results worth 366 billion won.
- In 1979, 2,542 factories joined, improving 26,300 processes and achieving tangible results worth 731 billion won.

In addition to these tangible results, process improvement has also led to the elimination of pollution, improved working environments, and increased convenience for employees, among other intangible benefits.

## ④ Quality Improvement

As the factory Saemaul Undong spread nationwide and gained momentum, each factory began to develop various effective measures to improve productivity according to its own characteristics. Consequently, quality improvement management also began to be implemented in earnest in all factories.

Quality improvement management aims to set quality standards to exclude the possibility of quality degradation in the production process and further improve quality, ultimately reducing defect rates and enhancing overall quality.

As factory Saemaul task group activities and suggestion systems became more active, more effective practical measures for quality improvement management emerged. As a result, defect rates for various products significantly decreased, greatly contributing to the enhancement of our products' international competitiveness.

## (4) Welfare and Living Standards Improvement

The primary goal of a company is to generate profits through production activities. However, the profits that companies pursue should be within the socially acceptable and reasonable range. It is from this perspective that the issue of a company's social and ethical responsibilities arises.

In the past, companies could focus solely on private profits. However, in today's industrial society, it is impossible to pursue profits while ignoring social and ethical considerations. Therefore, companies must now return profits to society and engage in social and ethical services.

## (4) 복지(福祉)·후생향상(厚生向上)

The primary goal of a company is to generate profits through production activities. However, the profits that companies pursue should be within the socially acceptable and reasonable range. The phrase "socially acceptable and reasonable" implies that companies have social and ethical responsibilities.

In the past, companies could focus solely on private profits. However, in today's industrial society, it is impossible to pursue profits while ignoring social and ethical considerations. Therefore, companies must now return profits to society and engage in social and ethical services.


--- (p. 571) ---

## Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The view that the purpose of corporate existence (企業存立) is to generate profits has emerged. This profit (利潤) of the corporation (企業), along with its social (社會的) and ethical (倫理的) service purposes, has made it inevitable for corporations to invest in the welfare (厚生) and well-being (福祉問題) of their employees (從業員).

Welfare (厚生) and well-being (福祉問題) can be viewed from two perspectives (觀點):
1. Economic (經濟的) welfare (福祉)
2. Non-economic (非經濟的) welfare (福祉)

Economic (經濟的) welfare (福祉) refers to direct monetary (貨幣) benefits such as wages (賃金), bonuses (上料金), and allowances (手當). In contrast, non-economic (非經濟的) welfare (福祉) refers to benefits that cannot be directly measured in monetary (貨幣) terms, such as health and welfare (保健厚生), recreation (娛樂), housing (住宅), and cultural education (文化敎育等), which are related to human satisfaction (人間的滿足).

The most desirable direction for improving welfare (厚生福祉向上) is to balance and harmonize the progress (增進) of both economic (經濟的) and non-economic (非經濟的) welfare (厚生福祉).

Since the nationwide (全國的) spread (擴散) of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動), there has been a notable effort to improve the welfare (福祉向上) of employees (從業員). This includes division of labor activities (分任活動) and suggestion systems (提案制度等), which have led to increased productivity (生産性) and corporate profits (企業利潤). When productivity (生産性) improves, business owners (企業主) should reinvest the increased profits into improving employee welfare (厚生福祉向上), which is the goal of the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動).

In other words, business owners (企業主) should strive to improve employee welfare (福祉向上), while employees (從業員) should take initiative in their work (工場日), treating it as their own responsibility. This mutual effort leads to harmony between labor and management (勞使和合), ensuring that both the corporation (企業) and the employees (從業員) thrive.

As a result, various government support measures (政府支援施策), such as medical insurance systems, education systems for working youth (勤勞靑少年就學制度), and housing facilities in industrial complexes (集團工業地域住宅施設普及), have been implemented. Additionally, individual corporations (各企業體) have gradually shown interest in and taken action to improve employee welfare (厚生福祉增進).

Examining the current state (實態) of welfare (厚生福祉) within factories (工場), there are various types of benefits, including wages (賃金), employee stock ownership (勤勞者持株制), bonuses (上料金), pension systems (年金制度), living support systems (生活援護制度), mutual aid businesses (共濟會事業), medical insurance systems (醫療保險制度), recreation (娛樂), hobby facilities (趣味施設), housing (住宅), dormitory facilities (寄宿舍施設), and educational businesses (敎育事業). Here, we will highlight a few key areas (事項) and review their achievements (成果).

### (가) Welfare Benefits (福利厚生費)

Welfare benefits (福利厚生費) within corporations (企業) can be broadly categorized into statutory welfare benefits (法定厚生費) and non-statutory welfare benefits (法定外福利厚生費).


--- (p. 572) ---

There exists.

Statutory welfare benefits (法定 복리후생비) refer to benefits provided to employees as mandated by law, including workers' compensation insurance premiums (產災保險料), retirement allowances (退職金), and employer contributions to health insurance premiums (醫療保險料). On the other hand, non-statutory welfare benefits (法定外 복리후생비) are voluntarily provided by employers to enhance employee welfare, such as cultural, sports, and recreation expenses (文化 體育 娛樂費), and cooperative financial services (共濟金融). While statutory welfare benefits have gradually increased due to government policies such as the expansion of medical insurance (醫療保險擴大), there has been a significant rise in voluntary non-statutory welfare benefits as well. Recent data shows that in 1978, factories nationwide with 50 or more employees spent an average of 200 million won on welfare benefits, increasing to 240 million won in 1979. This gradual increase reflects the growing interest of employers in employee welfare, complementing various welfare systems and facilities to be discussed later.

**(b) Collective Purchasing (共同購販) Business (事業)**
Collective purchasing businesses, which supply necessary daily goods to employees at lower prices, have been actively conducted recently, significantly contributing to the increase in employees' real income (實質所得). By minimizing essential distribution margins (流通마진) in the distribution process (流通過程), this system provides employees with lower prices and improved convenience. In 1978, 635 factories participated, but this number surged to 1,079 in 1979. Additionally, transaction amounts (去來額) increased from 25.3 billion won in 1978 to 29.4 billion won in 1979, indicating a trend towards substantial growth.

**(c) Dormitories (寄宿舍)**
As industrial structures (產業構造) become more advanced, issues related to housing support (住宅支援), company housing (社宅), and dormitories (寄宿舍) for employees have gained importance due to urban population concentration (都市集中化) and housing shortages (住宅難). Securing accommodation (住居施設) for employees working away from home (客地) has become increasingly crucial.


--- (p. 573) ---

# Chapter 5: Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) Achievements and Results

Moreover, its importance (重要性) is increasing. Especially in densely populated industrial areas (工業地域) or newly developed industrial areas (新興工業地域), securing housing facilities (住居施設) is more than just about securing housing (住居); it significantly contributes to the real income (所得面) of employees (從業員).

As a result, companies (企業) have also started to pay attention to this matter. In 1977, 1,945 factories (工場) secured a total of 350,000 pyeong (坪) of dormitories (寄宿舍), benefiting 220,000 employees (從業員). In 1978, this increased to 2,413 factories (工場) securing 470,000 pyeong (坪) of dormitories (寄宿舍), benefiting 280,000 employees (從業員). By 1979, 2,782 factories (工場) had 550,000 pyeong (坪) of dormitories (寄宿舍), providing benefits to 330,000 employees (從業員). This gradual increase shows the growing concern for employee dormitory facilities (寄宿施設).

### (La) Cafeterias (食堂)

The effects of installing cafeterias (食堂) within factories (工場) to provide meals at low cost or for free can be broadly categorized into two main aspects.

First, providing meals at low cost or for free contributes to increasing the real income (所得) of employees (從業員). Secondly, when both laborers (勞) and management (使) gather in one place to eat, it helps to reduce the gap between them while also improving human relations (人間關係). Consequently, many factories (工場) have started to pay attention to installing cafeterias (食堂). In 1977, 2,894 factories (工場) had cafeterias (食堂), increasing to 3,548 factories (工場) in 1978, and 4,022 factories (工場) in 1979, providing convenience to employees (從業員).

### (Ma) Rest Rooms (休憩室)

Rest periods (休息) during employees' (從業員) daily routines (日課) serve as a foundation for improving productivity (生產性). Rest rooms (休憩室) are places where employees (從業員) can listen to music (音樂), read (讀書), or engage in conversation (對話) during their break times (休息時間) to relieve fatigue from their daily routines (日課).

In 1977, 2,682 factories (工場) had indoor rest rooms (屋內休憩室), increasing to 3,288 factories (工場) in 1978, and 3,737 factories (工場) in 1979, showing a gradual increase in the number of factories (工場) installing these facilities (施設).

### (Ba) Bathrooms (沐浴室)

Bathroom facilities (沐浴室) are important not only for the health and hygiene (衛生) of employees (從業員) but also for their mental well-being (精神). Comparing employees (從業員) who return home dirty from work with those who return home clean after taking a bath (沐浴) clearly shows the important role these facilities (施設) play in their mental well-being (精神).


--- (p. 574) ---

## Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) 10-year History

Accordingly, factories also paid attention to bathhouse facilities, achieving significant progress with 2,350 factories in 1977, 2,881 factories in 1978, and 3,356 factories in 1979.

### (Sa) In-house Medical Facilities

Although the gradual establishment of the medical insurance system (醫療保險制度) has significantly expanded medical benefits (醫療惠澤), in-house medical facilities (自體醫療施設) are still necessary for simple treatments, etc. Consequently, factories have established medical rooms (醫務室) or, in the case of larger factories, their own hospitals (自體病院) to provide medical benefits not only to employees but also to their families.

The number of factories with medical rooms increased from 732 in 1977 to 1,021 in 1979. Factories with their own hospitals increased from 64 in 1977 to 81 in 1979.

### (A) Sports Facilities

To enhance employees' physical fitness, 2,458 factories in 1977 and 3,346 factories in 1979 have equipped sports facilities. In 1979, factories had an average of 2.7 types of sports facilities per factory.

### (Ja) Scholarship System

The scholarship system (獎學金制度), which supports educational funds (學資金) for employees, their children, sisterhood-linked villages (姉妹結緣部落), groups, etc., not only fosters a strong desire for learning among the recipients but also holds significant meaning from the perspective of socially returning corporate profits (企業利潤). Factories that prioritize creating scholarship funds (優先獎學基金), aiming to provide scholarships continuously regardless of business performance, increased from 335 in 1978 to 371 in 1979. Factories providing scholarships increased from 919 in 1978 to 1,070 in 1979. Moreover, the total scholarship amount increased by 72% from 32 billion won in 1978 to 55 billion won in 1979, showing a significant increase in ratio compared to the increase in the number of factories. This demonstrates a substantial strengthening in the scholarship amount.

### (Cha) Commuter Buses

The number of factories operating commuter buses (通勤버스) to provide convenience for employees' commuting increased from 1,448 in 1978 to 1,800 in 1979.

### (Ka) Company-subsidized Lunch

Factories' subsidies for employees' lunches (中食) not only provide material support but also spiritual support.


--- (p. 575) ---
