This also has great significance at the face level. When a company provides lunch and labor and management sit together to share a meal, even if it's just one meal a day, it plays a significant role in improving human relationships. Looking at the progress, in 1978, 2,667 factories and in 1979, 3,567 factories bore all or part of the lunch costs. Among these, the number of factories that completely bore 100% of the lunch costs increased from 1,197 in 1978 to 1,734 in 1979, showing a gradual increase in the number of factories that fully bear the lunch costs.

(Other) Labor Youth Education System (Industry-affiliated Schools and Evening Special Classes)

### ① Significance

In various industries, including industrial complexes, the labor youth who are the main players in national economic construction are provided with the opportunity to receive education suitable for the industrial site, thereby:

Firstly, instilling pride and morale in the labor youth as industrial soldiers, while
Secondly, aiming to improve production technology and effectively cultivate the required manpower for each industry and function to achieve self-sufficiency, and
Thirdly, expanding the industrial linkage system.

This system, which has new significant implications from the perspective of the factory Saemaul Undong, is the strongest welfare business for labor youth who cannot advance to higher education due to their family circumstances and have entered the career frontline. It is also a direct motivation system with great significance. From the perspective of equal educational opportunities and raising the national level of education, it has considerable significance.

To this end, the government is easing school establishment requirements while devising various support measures. The factory Saemaul Undong promotion organization is also organizing support groups to preemptively resolve difficulties in their education and is actively promoting the complete settlement of this system through guidance projects and promotional activities.

Originally, this system was initiated by the special attention and consideration of the late President Park Chung-hee in 1966, and has developed in conjunction with the activation of the factory Saemaul Undong. While industry-affiliated schools and evening special classes are the same in their establishment purposes and content, industry-affiliated schools refer to a system in which an industry employing 1,000 or more workers establishes a school within the same industry to educate willing workers, whereas evening special classes


--- (p. 576) ---

The system differs in that it establishes evening classes (夜間制學級) with the same curriculum (同等課程) as existing schools (旣存學校) for companies (產業體) employing (雇傭) more than 100 workers (勤勞者 100人 以上), offering a separate form of education (別途)의 교육形態) during daytime (晝間) with equal status (同等) but different in that classes are held.

Examining the distinctive features of this system (制度) compared to general schools (一般學校), we find:

First, the uniqueness lies in the burden of educational costs (敎育費 負擔). Unlike general middle and high schools (中高等學校) that follow the principle of beneficiary burden (受益者負擔原則), where students bear the costs, this system operates on the principle that the affiliated companies (所屬企業體) of enrolled workers (就學勤勞者) bear the tuition fees (授業料) as a rule.

Second, the uniqueness in the curriculum (敎育課程). Unlike general schools (一般SCHOOL), the curriculum for special classes (特別學級) and attached schools (附設學校) is designed considering the working hours (勤務時間) of enrolled workers (就學勤勞者) to match industrial sites (產業現場). Therefore, while 2/3 of the total required educational units (總敎育履修 單位) must be completed, 1/3 can be replaced with on-site training (現場實習), providing flexibility (彈力性) in curriculum operation (敎育課程 運用).

Third, the admission method (入學方法) differs from the entrance examination system (入試制度) of general middle and high schools (中高等學校). It allows selection (選拔) on a school-by-school basis (學校單位別), regardless of joint entrance exams (聯合考査) or lottery assignments (配定).

Fourth, the uniqueness in admission qualifications (入學資格). Unlike general schools (一般學校), only those who have graduated from elementary school (國民學校) or middle school (中學校) and hold the status of a worker (勤勞者 身分) are allowed to enroll (入學).

As seen above, this system, which began in 1976, has achieved remarkable development as an important part of the factory Saemaul Undong (工場 새마을운동), thanks to the active support (支援) of the government (政府), the full cooperation (協助) of schools (學校) and companies (企業), and the enthusiasm (意慾) of enrolled workers (就學勤勞者) for their studies (學業).

## ② Achievements

Starting with 5 schools (學校) and 2,210 students (名) in 1976, including Chungnam Bangjuk (忠南紡織) attached vocational high school (附設實高) and Bangnim Bangjik (邦林紡績) attached girls' middle school (附設 女中), industrial attached schools (產業體 附設學校) saw an 8-fold increase in the number of schools and a 13-fold increase in the number of students to 42 schools and 29,070 students in just 4 years, with 5 schools and 5,632 students in 1977, 23 schools and 12,941 students in 1978, and 31 schools and 23,624 students in 1979.

Evening special classes (夜間特別學級), which began in 1977, also saw a rapid expansion from 25 schools and 3,278 students in 1977 to 59 schools and 9,879 students in 1978, 82 schools and 30,439 students in 1979, and 99 schools and 26,642 students in 1980 in just 3 years.


--- (p. 577) ---

# Chapter 5: History and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The number of students has grown more than eightfold. As of 1980, the total number of schools enrolling working youth is 141, with a total of 55,712 students, demonstrating significant achievements of this system.

As of 1980, the current status of enrolled students by course is as follows: 11,232 students in secondary education, 3,553 students in high school humanities courses, 19,818 students in industrial courses, and 21,109 students in commercial courses. Examining the educational effects, the proportion of enrolled students under this system among all working youth eligible for education in the country, i.e., those who cannot advance to higher education due to family circumstances, etc., is 0.8% in junior high school courses in 1977, 3.0% in 1978, and 5.4% in 1979. In high school courses, it is 2.7% in 1977, 4.9% in 1978, and 9.5% in 1979, showing a high proportion. As of the end of 1979, 8% of all working youth are benefiting from this system, and it is expected that the proportion will increase significantly in the short term due to the rapid increase in the number of enrolled students each year. This system, in harmony with broadcasting correspondence schools, plays an important role in providing learning opportunities for our working youth who cannot pursue their passion for learning due to family circumstances, etc.

### D. Appreciation

The establishment of Korean corporate views and corporate images, the promotion of labor-management cooperation for the establishment of joint management bodies, and the construction of a welfare society through management rationalization are all aimed at the development of movements for the well-being of both labor and management. With the construction of a national comprehensive security system and the cultivation of international competitiveness as basic goals, the factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has been promoted for seven years. During this period, it has not only contributed to the improvement of employees' welfare but also to energy conservation, material conservation, and technological development, thereby contributing to the success of our ambitious industrialization policy and export expansion. Its merits are considerable. While celebrating the unprecedented growth of our economy through the success of the first and second five-year economic development plans, we unexpectedly faced the first oil shock. However, we overcame it smoothly and maintained the growth trajectory, which should be attributed to the development of the factory Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

However, it is undeniable that there were errors in the process of promotion that were not intended.


--- (p. 578) ---

Now we are facing the imminent challenge of the second oil crisis and must determine how to overcome this trial. At the same time, we must reflect on the merits and demerits of the Saemaul Undong to date and use this as an opportunity to develop a future-oriented direction for the factory Saemaul Undong, promoting its continuous expansion.

Firstly, despite being a spiritual movement, the factory Saemaul Undong, like its rural counterpart, has inevitably taken on an external character focused on visible phenomena rather than internal purification. There have been many cases where people lived in beautifully arranged environments but did not embody beautiful lifestyles. For instance, while advocating for corporate ethics, labor-management issues were often handled using pre-modern, hierarchical methods. Moreover, within societies that have prospered through the Saemaul Undong, there have been many instances where the desired honest and diligent social order has been fundamentally undermined. This can be attributed to an overindulgence in rapid, materialistic development, which has led to an insufficient system for establishing human and mental order to manage material order effectively. In other words, there has been a lack of bold pursuit of internal purification and its transformative patterns.

After the October 26, 1979 incident, there were over 1,500 labor-management disputes, with many occurring in leading companies. The concentration of leading companies in larger enterprises, and the increase in labor disputes due to the activation of labor unions as political development progressed, all indicate errors in past labor policies and the deepening process of the factory Saemaul Undong that must be acknowledged.

As the labor market shifted from surplus to scarcity, sustained high wage increases accompanied material production growth, yielding policy efforts to address relatively low wages. However, gradual price hikes continued to widen the relative wage gap. Furthermore, after 1979, enterprises focused solely on one-sided requests for employees to endure worsening management conditions without clear guarantees. Additionally, as the system changed, perceptions of Saemaul deteriorated uncontrollably, leading to the removal of factory Saemaul signs and the abolition of Saemaul divisions in large enterprises, which are the root causes of the current situation.


--- (p. 579) ---

# Chapter 5: Background and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The conscious avoidance by the media, a public opinion medium, of promoting or enlightening the public about the Saemaul Undong (Movement) has led to a decrease in the interest of the general public and workers. This can be attributed to the lack of Saemaul education, the absence of educational effects, and the lack of long-term vision. Consequently, the perception of Saemaul among businesspeople deteriorated first, and due to reasons such as capital shortages caused by economic stagnation, they avoided sending their employees to Saemaul training institutes. As a result, only 94% of the planned education was conducted in the first half of 1980, marking a 13% decrease compared to the same period last year.

In response to the wave of social purification sweeping the nation, along with the dawn of a new era where honest and diligent people thrive, the business community held the "Businesspeople's Convention for Corporate Culture Renewal" on July 16 and proclaimed a six-item "Corporate Ethics Code," establishing it as workplace norms. They also adopted 52 specific action items for implementation and pledged to put them into practice.

Now, businesses are no longer what they used to be, and businesspeople must deeply understand the social responsibility of businesses. Through substantial Saemaul spiritual education, they should establish new values and a new image of businesspeople, cultivate the ability to cope with an advanced industrial society, and take the lead in fostering international competitiveness without any selfish motives.

On the other hand, the era when workers, through labor unions, focused solely on external criticism and pressure is over. They must change their attitude to address and concretely solve the problems they face within the current political and economic systems. In other words, Korean labor-management relations should seek solutions to problems based on an equal relationship between the two parties.

Furthermore, managers should focus on forming an ideal model of labor-management relations based on Korean corporate ethics as workplace norms. They should promote the "Second Family" movement in the workplace effectively, fostering the modernization of values including national views, life views, and occupational views. They should also pay special attention to creating a workplace environment where employees can find joy and fulfillment through stable workplace life. Additionally, they should encourage the activities of Saemaul task groups to expand the scope of employee participation in management, ensuring that their creativity and knowledge are sufficiently reflected in management strategies.


--- (p. 580) ---

By promoting productivity and modernizing management through collective efforts and assigned activities, the new village incentive system was introduced to foster a stable labor-management relationship by directly returning the results of employees' efforts to them. This system aimed to provide tangible benefits through the factory Saemaul Undong, embodying "corporate ethics without trickery."

When both labor and management participate together in the factory Saemaul Undong, it is expected to sustain economic development on a new dimension, improve corporate management, and prepare for a new industrial revolution. This requires appropriate government policies, corporate social responsibility, and a strong foundation for joint labor-management operations, creating a workplace environment where those who do not contribute cannot coexist.

For the factory Saemaul Undong, which carries future-oriented and developmental elements, to avoid obstacles and interruptions, continuous organizational and material development must be achieved to maximize productivity on a stable labor-management foundation.

Ultimately, the tasks of the Saemaul Undong are such that as human living standards improve and develop, the movement's orientation shifts from environmental to human-centered, and its focus changes from material to spiritual and cultural well-being. Therefore, the Saemaul Undong is not a temporary movement, nor is it limited to specific classes or regions. It is a method chosen by us, the people living in this era, to pursue eternal happiness for the national community. Thus, the question of how to establish the foundation for the revitalization of the Saemaul Undong requires further careful consideration, especially in fulfilling the role of connecting the past and future generations.

## 3. School Saemaul Undong

### 가. Achievements of the School Saemaul Undong

#### (1) The Role of the Ministry of Education's Dedicated Department


--- (p. 581) ---

## Chapter 5 Contributions and Achievements of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The school Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) not only guided the direction to set more rational indicators for the nationwide Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) but also examined and analyzed cases of success and failure in the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to propose a development-oriented theoretical model. Moreover, the role of university personnel in establishing a systematic explanation of the results of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) from a developmental perspective holds significant meaning.

The support logic of the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development (文敎部 學術振興局), which served as the dedicated department, was ultimately aimed at the modernization of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement). This was to ensure that the movement did not end as a simple movement but rather established a developmental order system where theory and practice were harmoniously combined based on well-researched academic theories.

Thus, the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development's support activities for the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) focused on organizing and activating the following key directions: ① Promoting Saemaul education (敎育) for professors (敎授) and students (學生), ② Encouraging organized activities of Saemaul research societies (硏究會), ③ Inducing the establishment and operation of Saemaul research institutes (硏究所) to solidify the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) within academic institutions, ④ Connecting the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) with academia through presentations of outstanding Saemaul cases by university students, and ⑤ Developing a volunteer activity system to enhance the social learning effects of university students through on-site training.

### (2) Saemaul Education (敎育) for Professors (敎授) and Students (學生)

Saemaul education (敎育) for university professors (大學敎授) began in 1974, and for university students (大學生) in 1976.

In the early stages of Saemaul education (敎育), there was indeed some resistance, but during the one-week education period at the Saemaul Leadership Training Institute (指導者硏修院), almost all participants were somehow influenced.

The positive reactions from most of the educated indicated that the influence spread to their colleagues, who then recommended it to their peers, leading to an increase in the number of applicants. This also led university personnel to reflect on their role during a turning point in social atmosphere.

As a result, the number of professors (敎授) and university students (大學生) participating in the education increased each year. However, due to the limited capacity of the training institute (硏修院), the number of participants was adjusted accordingly.

(3) Activities of the Saemaul Research Society

The Saemaul Research Society aims to encourage participation in the Saemaul Undong and contribute to the development of local communities. It was established on August 8, 1975, centered around the first and second graduates of the Suwon Saemaul Leader Training Institute and university professors.

The society initially accepted graduates of the training institute as members, reaching a total of 620 members. As the organization grew, it established its own bylaws and set up branch offices to maintain a nationwide organic structure.

(a) Organization of the Saemaul Research Society

# (5) Excellent Case Presentation of University Saemaul Undong

To foster voluntary participation in the Saemaul Undong among university students and to establish a healthy academic atmosphere, while promoting and solidifying the Saemaul Undong in universities, the Excellent Case Presentation of University Saemaul Undong has been held since 1976. This event encourages students to uncover and research outstanding examples of Saemaul Undong activities from their respective universities and to present their findings.

The content of the Excellent Case Presentation of University Saemaul Undong includes various cases of volunteer activities or Saemaul Undong experiences, ranging from urban areas to rural villages, remote mountainous regions, and even isolated islands. These cases often highlight themes of overcoming numerous challenges and hardships to achieve meaningful results, earning praise and encouragement from university communities.

Initially, the Excellent Case Presentation of University Saemaul Undong was organized by the Saemaul Research Society. However, since 1979, it has been integrated with the National University Students' Excellent Case Presentation of Saemaul Undong, which had been organized by Konkuk University since 1978. Konkuk University now serves as the main organizer. Scholarships are awarded to the winners to stimulate their research enthusiasm.

# Chapter 5 (第5章) Achievements and Results of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

The establishment of the "Federation (聯合會)" led to the unification of student volunteer activities, which had been carried out sporadically, under the Ministry of Education's financial support, allowing for systematic promotion.

Following this, in 1975, with the establishment of the Student Corps for National Defense (學徒護國團), each university's Student Corps for National Defense established a "Saemaul Division (部)" to take charge of volunteer activities, bringing the university Saemaul Undong onto the right track.

Before the establishment of the Student Corps for National Defense, volunteer activities primarily focused on increasing income and improving living conditions in underdeveloped rural areas. However, as the Saemaul Undong spread nationwide, rural living conditions rapidly improved, making a shift in the direction of rural volunteer activities inevitable.

Starting in 1976, universities were encouraged to select one county per school for concentrated long-term development. This shift from rural volunteerism to urban and school-based Saemaul Undong yielded significant results in cleaning up school surroundings.

Additionally, universities implemented concentrated volunteer activities combined with on-site education at the university or department level, alongside the 1-school-1-county concentrated volunteer activities. This approach accelerated regional development while also achieving significant results in student training and on-site practical education.

Notably, among university student volunteer activities, medical services in villages without doctors received high praise and yielded substantial results.

Since 1973, medical services in villages without doctors have been provided not only during school breaks but also every weekend, with students and professors touring these areas to focus on disease prevention, treatment, and surgeries such as cleft lip repair, greatly contributing to national health improvement.

B. Achievements of School Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The School Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has been evaluated as having made significant contributions to social development as its implementation system was established. Its achievements can be summarized as follows:

First, university students themselves not only acquired methods of self-education but also created opportunities for self-discovery.

Second, it provided an opportunity to transform the previously theory-oriented academic approach into a more practical one.

Third, through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and volunteer activities, students could more clearly define their social roles.

Fourth, by experiencing and analyzing the issues of the local community, students developed new methods of understanding society.

Fifth, it promoted university-industry cooperation, allowing residents of any region to exchange opinions with university professors and students about current issues. This expanded the possibility of making specialized knowledge, which was previously concentrated among a few, more universal. It also demonstrated the potential for anyone's knowledge or experimental results to be openly utilized and applied as social nourishment.


--- (p. 587) ---

# Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

## Section 1 (第1節) Characteristic Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

### 1. Overview of the Developmental Stages (段階的發展內容의槪觀)

The Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) in our country has been progressing since its inception in 1970, undergoing deepening and expansion. The developmental process of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) can be divided into three stages.

First is the foundation-building stage (基盤造成的段階), which spans from 1971 to 1973. The year 1971 marked the decision to simultaneously promote the movement in all 33,267 villages across the nation by providing each with 335 bags of cement. In 1972, out of the 34,665 villages nationwide, 16,600 villages received support with 500 bags of cement and 1 ton of steel reinforcement each, leading to an expansion of self-participating villages to 6,108. This year was significant for expanding the ignition radius. The year 1973 saw all 34,665 villages across the nation participating voluntarily and autonomously, marking the year of foundation establishment.

Second is the self-help development stage (自助發展的段階), which spans from 1974 to 1976. In 1974, the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) greatly expanded, actively unfolding in every village nationwide. Participation from various sectors began, with the movement starting in 5,253 workplaces including schools, social organizations, and others. As key projects such as Saemaul income (새마을所得), Saemaul education (새마을敎育), and urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을운동) intensified, the movement matured into a three-dimensional participation system.

In 1975, the Private Sector Saemaul Undong (新村運動) Council (協議會) was established, leading to the initiation of the production increase movement (增產運動),


--- (p. 588) ---

The year was marked by a focus on establishing a solid foundation for overcoming economic difficulties through total participation, with emphasis on the Three Major Movements (근검운동(勤儉運動), 인보상조운동(隣保相助運動), and 삼대운동(三大運動)) and the Four Major Policies (소득사업(所得事業), 노역사업(勞力事業), 국민교육(國民敎育), and 도시새마을(都市새마을)).

In 1976, the momentum of the Four Major Policies and Three Major Movements, which had been building since the previous year, was further expanded and promoted. In rural communities, efforts were made to revitalize backward villages, while in urban areas, the Urban Saemaul Undong (都市새마을운동) began in earnest. Notably, cities across the nation designated the 25th of each month as the day for neighborhood meetings (반상회(班常會)), encouraging residents to voluntarily implement decisions made during these meetings. This spirit helped accelerate the deepening and development of the Saemaul Undong.

The third phase, from 1977 to 1981, was characterized by self-reliance and completion. Starting in 1977, efforts were focused on renovating the living environment for the construction of a cultural welfare society, improving the income structure to increase non-agricultural and circulation income, and transforming the consciousness structure to foster the Saemaul national character. If 1977 marked the entry into the self-reliance and completion phase, then from 1978 onward, it can be said that the process of advancing the self-reliance and completion system was repeated.

## 2. Characteristics of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동)

The Saemaul Undong in our country is unique as a Korean social development movement, distinct from community movements in other nations. Additionally, it differs from past social movements initiated by our ancestors, as it is unfolding in the social context in which our generation currently lives.

If we examine the characteristics of the Saemaul Undong from an international or chronological perspective, they can perhaps be explained based on the following key points. The first is its semantic characteristic.

The term "Saemaul Undong" originated from the President's directive during the Local Governors' Meeting on April 22, 1970, suggesting that the movement to beautify our villages with our own hands be called the "Saemaul Beautification Movement" (새마을가꾸기운동).


--- (p. 589) ---

## Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The origins of the Saemaul Undong can be traced back to the characteristics of a village as a small-scale society (小單位社會). The features of a village as a small-scale society can be found in the fact that ① residents (住民) sharing a small-scale living space (小單位生活空間) are ② assimilated into the same tradition (同一傳統性) and ③ commonly acknowledge customs (因襲). Among village residents, there is a strong sense of ① community consciousness (共同體意識) and (we feeling), ② role consciousness (役割意識) and (role feeling), and ③ mutual trust and dependence (相扶相助意識) and (depending feeling). Therefore, the joint effort (共同努力) to cultivate our village with our own hands is more easily induced than in any other unit society (單位社會).

The broad-area combination (廣域的結合) of such small-scale societies (小單位社會) is a regional society (地域社會), and when the concept (槪念) of this regional society (地域社會) expands to the national radius (全國的半徑), it can be called the entire nation (全國土). In this sense, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is a national movement (國民運動) with a national character (全國性) rooted in small-scale villages (小單位).

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is not a movement (運動) limited to rural regional societies (農村地域社會) but possesses the character of a national movement (國民運動) that simultaneously encompasses universality (汎民性) and broad-area characteristics (汎域性).

Secondly, there is the historical characteristic (歷史的特性).

While the Saemaul Undong (運動) is defined as a "movement (運動) to live well," the methods (方法) of how to live well depending on the situation (狀況) of the era (時代) differed. However, the desire (欲求) to live well has continued unbroken from the past to the present, which cannot be denied.

As mentioned in another chapter (章), within the long 5,000-year (5千年) history of our national customs (民族生活因襲), deeply rooted customs such as "Gosari (古事理)," "Dure (두레)," and "Hyangyak (郷約)" can be understood as historical contexts (歷史的脈絡) to achieve our desire (欲望) to live well. In this sense, today's Saemaul Undong (運動) can be seen as a movement (運動) that has found a method (方法) suitable for our current reality (實情) within the same historical flow (歷史的流れ).

Thirdly, there is the characteristic (特性) of the method of development (展開方法).

In the past, social movements (社會運動) in our ancestral society (祖上社會), such as Hyangyak (郷約), were movements (運動) centered around a few individuals (一部人士) belonging to the Yangban class (兩班階層) who joined Hyangyak (鄕約) and were limited to fellow villagers (同鄕民). Moreover, they were localized movements (限地的運動) focused on the hometowns (緣故地) of the Hyangyak members (鄕約者) and were temporary movements (一時的運動). Therefore, their


--- (p. 590) ---

It could not develop into a pan-citizen system (汎民化體制) nor spread nationwide (全國的) as a movement (運動), and it could not be sustained (永續的) as a continuous (持續) movement (運動). However, today's Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) possesses characteristics in its approach to development (展開方法面), including a full-participation system (全民參與體制), a nationwide deployment system (全域展開體制), and a commitment to sustained efforts (持續化).

The fourth characteristic is sociological (社會學的). Through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), we are fostering a new social consciousness (社會意識) and creating new social landscapes (社會象) in many areas. We have awakened from the idle dreams (閑夢) of the past, determined to forge our own destiny (運命) with our own strength (自身), and have taken an active (積極) approach to life. We are also challenging nature (自然), which was once only seen as a source of fear (對象), and organizing the future (未來) more rationally (合理的), fostering a sense of confidence (自信感) that we are not inferior to others.

The fifth characteristic is political-cultural (政治文化的). A notable political-cultural (政治文化的) phenomenon emerging from the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is the maturation (成熟) of a culture of village democracy (마을民主主義). Village leaders (指導者) are elected (選出) based on the consensus (總意) of the residents (住民), and the elected leaders (指導者) address the common concerns (共同關心事) of the village residents (住民) through united efforts (團結) based on consensus (總意). This can be seen as a desirable phenomenon (現象) where the foundation of Korean-style democracy (韓國的民主主義) is taking root in the small social units (小單位社會) of villages.

Previously, when we talked about democracy (民主主義), we only associated it with the political act (政治的行爲) of electing members of parliament (國會議員). The fact that this traditional (在來式) notion (觀念) has changed holds great significance (意味). The effort to seek methods (方法) for residents (住民) to solve their own real-life problems (現實的生活問題) through their own will (意思), where each resident (各者) presents their opinions (意見) and cooperates (協力) to improve (改善) by adjusting (調整) the presented opinions (意見) and finding solutions (發見), can be described as fostering a new political-cultural (政治文化的) environment (風土) that strengthens the foundation of democracy (民主主義).

One matured democratic (民主主義的) feature (特徵) through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) is, first, the realization (具現) of a new form (形態) of direct democracy (直接民主主義) method (方式); second, the development (開發) of a practical democracy (實踐民主主義) method (方式) based on the principle (原理) of concrete (具體的) execution (實行); and third, on-site democracy (現場民主).


--- (p. 591) ---

## Chapter 6 (第6章): Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The main characteristic of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is the "main signature method" (주회방식).

Originally, direct democracy (直接民主主義) refers to a method of direct participation by citizens led by a political figure, but in the case of the Saemaul Undong, direct democracy means setting development plans for small regional communities (e.g., villages) as models suitable for the right people and places, with the precondition of full participation by all village residents.

What does this imply? It means that all citizens directly participate in the process of discussing and deciding on regional community development plans.

Secondly, the practical democratic characteristic of the Saemaul Undong is that the decision-makers of policies are not separate from those who execute them. Instead, the same individuals—the residents—are the ones who raise issues, discuss and decide on them, and concretely implement them.

In other words, the planners, executors, and managers of development plans are the same entity: the residents themselves.

Thirdly, the characteristic of the Saemaul Undong being a form of on-site democracy is that there is no separate venue for discussions and no separate venue for work.

Discussions and work are carried out simultaneously, and development plans are advanced on-site through a system where discussions are held while working and work is done while discussing.

Sixth is the developmental characteristic.

We refer to the Saemaul Undong as a movement for living well forever, but it is clearly not a temporary movement. Nor is it a movement with temporary value as a means tied to any particular regime.

Rather, it is a people's movement with a non-partisan and supra-political nature, aimed at realizing the rise and fall of our nation's existence and paving the way for the infinite progress of the nation.

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong has the characteristic of being developed sustainably based on its own developmental logic.

Considering these main points, the Saemaul Undong is based on national self-awareness aimed at living well and the people's resolve to challenge the future.


--- (p. 592) ---

Diligence, self-help, and cooperation as practical principles, the Saemaul Undong can be defined as a self-reliance movement where Koreans proactively participate in constructing a self-reliant and strong community and society based on their daily lives.

## 3. Development and Promotion Elements of the Saemaul Undong

The Saemaul Undong is not merely a movement with a microscopic concept of renovating villages but should be understood as a movement that comprehensively addresses our human desires and pursues greater happiness. In this context, the Saemaul Undong is a movement system that develops through the interaction of at least the following four development and promotion elements.

First, it encompasses an educational element that enhances humans' latent abilities,

Second, it possesses an environmental change element that aims to improve living conditions,

Third, it has an element that expands the foundation for wealth to improve living conditions,

Fourth, it is based on a dynamic and creative element that pursues infinite possibilities.

### Ga. Continuation of Human Education

Human education is both the development of consciousness and the development of abilities.

The effects of human education not only enable individuals to perform human renewal themselves but also drive them to pursue new desires during the human renewal process. Moreover, it helps discover humans' infinite latent possibilities.

In other words, through education, humans acquire the desire to challenge nature, and the greater the value gained from nature through such challenges, the more they hasten the expansion of human abilities. The expansion of human abilities essentially means education. Therefore, the Saemaul Undong, as a movement that strengthens our living conditions socially, encompasses the principle of promoting the continuation of human education.

### Na. Continuation of Environmental Improvement

--- (p. 593) ---

## Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation (評價) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The environment (環境) not only provides functions (機能) for human (人間) living conditions (生活條件) but also possesses functions (機能) that transform (變革) human (人間) attitudes (態度) towards life (生活).
While it is true that the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) was promoted through a movement-first approach (運動先行方式), improved living environments (生活環境) demand attitude transformations (態度變革) that can adapt (適應) to them. In this process, human (人間) attitudes (態度) and living (生活) environments (環境) interact (相乘作用) and develop (發展) together.
In other words, as we continue to beautify our living environments (生活環境), we naturally become concerned (關心) with attitude transformations (態度變容) that can adapt (適應) to these improved environments (環境). Moreover, we strive (努力) to develop (體得) the ability (能力) to meet higher-dimensional needs (次元 높은 욕구대응) by establishing (定立) self-management systems (自己管理體系).
This can be seen as both training (訓練) to adapt (適應) oneself (自身) to social change (社會變動)(social change) and as the development (啓發) of the ability (能力) to preserve (保全) oneself (自身) from change (變動) while creating (創造) new changes (新しい變動).
In another sense, education (敎育) raises (提起) the formation of life (生活形成問題) as the main issue (主된 過題) before experience (經驗), whereas the environment (環境) continuously raises (提起) problem-solving (問題解決) as an ongoing issue (持續的 過題) during experience (經驗).
Thus, in a certain sense (某種意味), the environment (環境) can be seen as performing (遂行) the function (機能) of creating educational needs (敎育需要創造機能).
Since the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) prioritized (先行) environmental improvement (環境改善), the current reality (現實) that highlights (提起) the need (必要) for corresponding education (敎育) signifies (意味) that artificially created (造成的) nature (自然) prompts (促求) a spiritual (精神的) revolution (革命) in humans (人間), leading to a cyclical (循環機能的) development (發展) where active (活動的) humans (人間) continuously (持續) stimulate (刺戟) changes (變化) in natural (天然的) nature (自然).
Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) embodies (內包) the principle (原理) of sustained (持續) environmental improvement (環境改善).

### D. Continuation (持續化) of Resource Development (富源開發)

Wealth (富) is the first condition (第1의 조건) that guarantees (保障) future (未來) living (生活) while also allowing us to enjoy (享受) the present (現在) life (生活).
The reason why the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) emphasizes (重視) productivity (生産性) from one to ten and focuses (力點) on increasing income (所得增大) is to firmly establish (構築) the foundation (基調) for stable (安定) living (生活).
The idea of living well (잘 살아보자는 뜻) is not merely for our own well-being (우리만이 잘 살자는데 그 의미) but also to create (마련) a foundation (터전) where we can live well (잘 살아갈 수 있는) for generations to come (後孫萬代에 이르기까지), ensuring the well-being (잘 살아갈 수 있는) of our descendants (後孫).


--- (p. 594) ---

It instills a great sense of pride in having excellent ancestors, which holds significant meaning.

If a nation (民族) is to be clearly (分明) eternal and imperishable (永遠不滅), it must never repeat the countless historical (歷史的) trials (試鍊) it has endured in the past. To achieve this, we must break free from the poverty (貧困) that threatens our livelihood (民生威脅的) and find ways to overcome poverty (貧困克服). Our tangible and intangible (有形無形) potential resources (資源) must be realized (顯在化), and the system (體系) for utilizing all available resources (可用資源) must be advanced (高度化). This is precisely the essence of the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), which aims to develop limitless (無限的) potential (可能性) in resources (資源) and expand (擴充) income sources (所得源) through continuous innovation (開發).

### La. Continuing the Process of Change and Creation (變動創造的持續化)

The fundamental and ongoing condition (條件) for modernization (近代化) is not just one or two changes (變化) in human life (人間生活), but the ability to adapt (適應) to the changing environment (環境) every year (每年). To strive for a more dynamic society (動態的社會) (dynamic society), we must break free from the traditional (傳統的) (traditional), subsistence (生計維持的) (subsistence), backward (後進的) (backward), and primitive (原始的) (primitive) customs (因襲) that a static society (靜態的社會) (static society) possesses. We must independently pioneer (開拓) a process of self-renewal (自己革新過程) as a self-change factor (自體變化要因).

The Saemaul Undong (새마을운동) also addresses the issue of continuous change and creation (變動創造持續問題) as one of its core elements (內容要素) in its efforts to establish a more modern (近代的) (modern), commercial (商業的) (commercial), progressive (進步的) (progressive), and advanced (先進的) (advanced) society (社會形成).

Through the Saemaul Undong (새마을운동), our rural communities (農村地域社會) have indeed awakened from a long slumber of traditionalism (傳統主義的). The notion of merely being content (滿足) with having food to eat and a roof over one's head has given way to a new perspective on life (新生活觀) that seeks to live a life worthy of human dignity (人答게). Furthermore, the channels (通路) for the circulation (流通) of living culture (生活文化) have become diversified (多角化) not only to bridge the gap (隔差) with advanced urban societies (都市社會) but also to expand (擴大) the possibilities (可能性) for absorbing and accommodating (吸引受容) advanced cultural elements (文化要素). Consequently, the momentum (氣風) for improving (改善) one primitive societal habit (原始社會的非生產的惡習) after another has been growing (振作).

In the context of modernization (近代化), the process of change (變動的過程) can be understood as the journey from pre-human (人間以前) life forms (生物) (prehuman) to human (人間) existence, and from primitive societies (原始社會) (primitive societies) to civilized societies (文明社會) (civilized societies). However, this process of change (變動過程) is essentially about how humans (人間) deal with (處理) their environment (環境).


--- (p. 595) ---

# Chapter 6 Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was not only a great revolutionary transformation but also a more dynamic one. The specific working factors of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) all perform the functions of change acceptance or change creation. Therefore, the dynamic combination of such change factors transfers our society from a static to a dynamic state.

Under the premise that human developmental desires can be infinitely expanded, if change is consciously acknowledged, then that change must also unfold infinitely. Therefore, the proposition is that desires and change must proceed in parallel.

In this sense, the meaning of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in terms of creating and sustaining change is immense.

## Section 2 Overview of the Saemaul Undong's (New Community Movement) Achievements

The 1970s were undoubtedly a decade of significant national development and economic growth, a decade filled with accomplishment. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) greatly contributed to this, both directly and indirectly. Of course, it is very difficult to precisely define the exact limits of the influence the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) had in a strict sense. However, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) influenced everything from comprehensive national development plans to individual lifestyles and value realization. Thus, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) contributed to the spiritual foundation of our modernization, and at times, it also served as a development strategy for modernization.

### 1. Improvement of Rural Living Environments

The desire to create a cleaner, more comfortable, and healthier living environment, and to lead a more convenient and valuable life, is a fundamental human desire.

Our rural areas in the past were extremely unclean. They rejected any change in life, repeating the same daily routines mechanically. The roads were narrow, the sewers were clogged, and the walls were crumbling. Moreover, the villages were impoverished, and in such an environment, comfort and dignity in life could not flourish.


--- (p. 596) ---

A healthy life and creative ambition could not have sprouted any more. However, the Saemaul Undong over the past 10 years has clearly improved the living environment in rural areas. Village roads, including sewers, have been repaired, walls have been fixed, and roofs have been reconstructed. Every household has electricity, and simple water supply facilities have been installed. Public laundries and children's playgrounds have been created. Thus, our villages and hometowns have transformed into beautiful and livable places. In just 4-5 years since the start of the Saemaul Undong, over 2 million thatched roofs have been improved, and walls, kitchens, toilets, and auxiliary buildings have been neatly and cleanly organized.

## 2. Stimulating Development Ambition and Inducing Achievement Motivation

If it were not for the Saemaul Undong, our farmers would have settled in stagnation and regression, living in resignation. Fortunately, the Saemaul Undong brought significant change and reform to farmers and rural areas. The improvement of the living environment and the enhancement of living conditions awakened the farmers' consciousness. This gave rise to a firm belief that "We too must live well." In other words, it instilled the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. This was not abstract or ideological but was achieved through practical action and experiential learning, which was meaningful. Historically, we often fell into the trap of abstract and ideological wordplay rather than taking action.

While the Saemaul Undong sometimes suffered from being forced by external intentions or top-down guidance and instructions from authorities, many leaders and participants in the process of the movement came to realize the true meaning of increased income through diligence, the tremendous results and efficiency brought by cooperation, and the spiritual significance of self-help efforts in terms of autonomy and self-reliance. Village residents eagerly joined the ranks of benevolent competition. Thus, they worked harder, saved more frugally, enhanced the vitality of their lives, found fulfilling happiness, and enriched their lives.


--- (p. 597) ---

## Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) served as a catalyst for farmers to develop motivation for development and growth, and it became a significant driving force for fostering a sense of achievement.

### 3. The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) as a Catalyst for Increasing Rural Income

During the implementation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the focus was on how to link the visible and demonstrative achievements of improved living environments to substantial income growth.

Given that the ultimate goal of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was to improve living standards, it was essential to connect the movement to income growth, essentially making it a movement for increasing income.

The prosperity of rural areas was not only necessary for achieving economic balance between urban and rural areas, or for ensuring that increased food production in rural areas provided a fundamental condition for the healthy development of industries, including factories. It was also crucial because the backwardness and vulnerability of rural areas posed a significant internal threat to national stability and order. Therefore, attention had to be paid to agricultural modernization.

However, despite this, the rapid promotion of industrialization from the 1960s and the accompanying progress of urbanization led to the relative backwardness of rural areas and agriculture compared to the growth of cities and industry. This resulted in the overdevelopment of major cities and the decline of rural areas.

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) had to be concentrated on overcoming two fundamental elements of rural backwardness: the lack of scientific and rationalist spirit and the stagnation of traditional small-farming society. It aimed to achieve a significant increase in income. In this sense, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) greatly contributed to increasing rural income.

Firstly: The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) helped overcome chronic food shortages and cultivated the ability to achieve self-sufficiency in staple crops. It primarily contributed to establishing the technical and spiritual foundation for developing and disseminating new varieties such as IR 667. It also contributed to the development and self-sufficiency of fertilizers and pesticides. The expansion of all-weather irrigation and safety facilities was also an indispensable condition.

As income increased, food consumption patterns changed, reducing the demand for staple crops like rice and barley while increasing the demand for vegetables and fruits, as well as pork and beef.


--- (p. 598) ---

Secondly: Villages that had begun to realize the importance of income started to focus on the development of existing resources. In particular, businesses aimed at increasing income by utilizing idle labor in rural areas became lively. Sericulture, beekeeping, fish farming, and other agricultural sideline businesses were introduced to rural areas. Forest development through afforestation and the creation of orchards are examples of this. The mindset that any effort to increase farmers' income was necessary became a driving force for increasing farmers' income. This economic psychology also greatly helped to make consumption habits in rural areas more healthy. In particular, the frugality movement led by the Saemaul Women's Association instilled in farmers the habit of saving, and the frugal atmosphere of farmers made excellent contributions to the growth of Saemaul savings banks. Thus, the money collected was reinvested in other income-generating businesses, developing into a movement to promote production.

Thirdly: The improvement of conditions for increasing income. Through the Saemaul Undong, improved roads increased transportation and circulation efficiency and expanded marketability. In addition, the improvement of various circulation and storage facilities, including communal warehouses, collection centers, and transportation means, not only contributed to increasing the income of farmers and fishermen but also helped to compensate for the weaknesses of small-scale circulation economies. Moreover, farmers and fishermen, who had previously focused solely on production, actively participated in circulation economies, contributing greatly to the transformation and development of their thinking and behavior patterns into enterprise management capabilities.

Such results led to an increase in the income of farmers and fishermen, which, in the early 1970s, was only 67% of that of urban workers, to surpass their income by the years 1974 and 1975.

### 4. Expansion of the Production Base

The establishment of a production base in agriculture refers to increasing the yield per unit of given land, promoting mechanization to compensate for the lack of labor, and improving the economic efficiency of agricultural production through the rationalization of management. It also involves minimizing labor and management costs and investing them in the expansion and reproduction of agriculture.


--- (p. 599) ---

# Chapter 6: Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong

This is the case.

Such production infrastructure projects (生產基盤造成事業) are tasks that individual farmers (農民) or a few rural communities (農村) cannot resolve on their own. They require immense investment (投資), technological support (技術的支援), and coordinating bodies to manage conflicting interests (利害調整機構). Given the reality that 70-80% of public funds (公共財政) are concentrated in the two major cities of Seoul and Busan (釜山), the limited financial capacity of local governments (地方財政) makes it impossible to undertake large-scale infrastructure projects. Thus, large-scale infrastructure development must be based on a comprehensive national development plan (國土綜合開發計劃). This is also true from a technical perspective (技術的側面), as well as in coordinating interests (利害調整) among farmers (農民相互間) and regional communities (地域社會).

While the government (政府) has made concentrated investments (集中的投資) in various sectors (各分野別) considering the effects (效果) and nature (性格) of agricultural infrastructure expansion projects (農業基盤擴大事業), particularly in the 1970s (年代), significant achievements were made as part of the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) through joint efforts (合心) between the government (政府) and residents (住民) to expand infrastructure (基盤造成).

This is because the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) itself aims to maximize (極大化) and enhance the efficiency (效率化) of government (政府) investments (投資), which necessitates the participation (參與) and cooperation (協力) of residents (住民). Therefore, the government (政府) focused on:

* First: Expanding the production infrastructure (生產基盤擴大)

As industrialization (工業化) progresses and urbanization (都市化) accelerates, the outflow of rural labor (農村人力) to cities and industrial areas (工場地帶) is inevitable. Consequently, rural areas (農村) face severe labor shortages (人力不足). By the 1970s (年代), the ratio of rural (農村) to non-rural (非農村) populations (人口) became 50:50. Given our current agricultural production methods (農業生產樣式) that rely on human (人力) and animal labor (畜力), the outflow of young and middle-aged individuals (靑壯年) to cities exacerbates rural labor shortages (農村人力不足), making agricultural mechanization (農業機械化) inevitable.

Agricultural mechanization requires the consolidation of farmland (農耕地) into appropriate sizes (適正規模) and the improvement of farm roads (農路) and irrigation systems (水路). Such consolidation and development of farmland and irrigation systems necessitate land exchanges and readjustments (土地交換分合), which cannot be achieved without the participation and cooperation (協同) of farmers (農民). The spirit of cooperation (協同精神) emphasized in the Saemaul Undong (新村運動) is indeed aimed at achieving this.


--- (p. 600) ---

It was to establish a groundbreaking spiritual tone.

In the 1970s, projects to expand farmland and increase land productivity, alongside rural electrification, began to gain momentum. Of course, these projects were carried out in parallel with the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) in rural areas.

These included land reclamation and landfill (간척) for farmland expansion, large-scale agricultural infrastructure development, water management projects, small stream restoration, seed improvement, compost production, soil amendment, and soil acidification prevention. Large-scale water management projects in the Geumgang (錦江), Yeongsangang (榮山江), Nakdonggang (洛東江), and Hangang (漢江) basins, as well as mountain conservation and underutilized land development plans, were part of these efforts. The reclamation projects along the west coast were also indispensable. In 1978, 38.6 billion won was invested to complete the Yeongsangang (榮山江) irrigation project. Subsequently, the first phase of the Sapgyocheon (揷橋川) project, the development of the Changnyeong and Imjin (臨津) regions, and the development of the Mihocheon (美湖川) and Namgang (南江) regions were underway. A total of 49.4 billion won was invested in these agricultural water development projects, and 364 hectares of new irrigation-safe farmland was developed, increasing the irrigation-safe farmland ratio from 85% to 87%.

Secondly, in addition to the expansion of farmland consolidation and farmland preservation projects, mechanized farming, which replaces human and animal labor, will become even more necessary in the future. This is to liberate labor from the burden of labor, to compensate for the shortage of labor, and to increase productivity.

Therefore, mechanized production is a general trend in agriculture today, and for mechanization to take place, farmland must be consolidated and production scales must be large. In 1978, 17.5 billion won was invested to consolidate 164,000 hectares of farmland, bringing the total consolidated farmland area to 310,000 hectares. In addition, mountain development projects and drainage improvement projects centered on the paddy fields in the Honam (湖南) region are being actively promoted.

These projects, particularly when linked with river improvement, agricultural water development, and regional comprehensive development projects, are enhancing their interconnected effects.

These agricultural productivity infrastructure projects, both large and small, were deeply connected with the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) centered on rural and regional communities, which is why their effects were enhanced.


--- (p. 601) ---

## 5. Expansion to the Urban Saemaul Undong (Urban New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong, which originated in rural areas, gradually spread to urban societies. Despite the unique ecological conditions and social consciousness of urban societies, the Saemaul Undong, which began in rural areas, spread to urban areas and evoked sympathy among urban residents.

It spread through the following stages:

1. In 1973, urban leaders, including businesspeople, economists, educators, and civil servants from various regions, including Seoul and Gyeonggi, gathered to hold a forward march conference for workplace Saemaul Undong. At this conference, they formed the Promotion Council for Workplace Saemaul Undong.
2. In 1974, urban civilians also actively participated in the Saemaul Undong, which quickly spread to workplaces, schools, the military, and general companies.
3. In 1975, the government-led urban workplace Saemaul Undong was replaced and transformed into the private sector Saemaul Promotion Council, shifting to a private sector-led model.

Through these stages, the Urban Saemaul Undong developed into savings campaigns, neighborhood mutual aid campaigns, and consumer frugality campaigns. By 1977-1978, it had evolved into a nationwide movement to establish three major orders: spiritual order, behavioral order, and environmental order, as well as a movement to establish a new image of citizens, social ethics, and values.

Looking back, since 1945, our society, due to economic immaturity and social and cultural non-autonomy, has introduced and imitated Western culture without autonomous choice. Urban artifacts have resulted in the collapse of our traditional value system and ethical norms. Consequently, primary human relationships have collapsed, and secondary living relationships, rampant individualism, social fluidity, personal differentiation, and heterogeneity have made it difficult for urban residents to lead a rational urban life. On the other hand, it has fostered money worship, destruction of moral values, extravagance and waste, decadent trends, and gambling tendencies. As a result, community consciousness and the concept of order have been lost, and public morality and social ethics have deteriorated. Public conscience in commercial transactions has become hard to find, and practices such as profiteering, unfair charges, hoarding, substandard food, and substandard products have become rampant.


--- (p. 602) ---

It has become a matter of action.
When such social injustices prevail, even if material life becomes somewhat abundant, spiritual emptiness is inevitable, and it could potentially nullify growth and development itself. In truth, material abundance is necessary for us, but equally important was a corresponding spiritual revolution. The Urban Saemaul Undong aimed to establish the spiritual posture of urbanites and civic ethics, and in this sense, it undoubtedly carried the meaning of a spiritual revolution.

### 6. Pleasant Environment and Nature Conservation

Human beings cannot survive without nature. Water, air, the sun, forests, and every other element are essential to life. For our spiritual posture to be correctly established, a pleasant environment must first be created. The Urban Saemaul Undong also set significant goals for purifying the environment around our daily lives. First, we cleaned the fronts of our houses and the surrounding areas, tidied up the roadsides, vacant lots, and hills, and actively carried out the back-alley purification campaign.

For such environmental purification to truly achieve results, it was necessary to accompany facility improvements and systematic control. Temporary enlightenment or indirect stimulation alone could not achieve results in environmental purification and beautification projects that had almost become chronic. Inadequate facilities not only become the cause of unclean environments but also factors that loosen various orders and norms. This is why facilities for welfare, traffic safety, and public hygiene are necessary. To prevent acts that violate public morals, traffic regulations, commercial ethics, and juvenile delinquency, fundamental and sustained efforts must be carried out in parallel.

Environmental purification of parks, recreational areas, and tourist attractions is also necessary. This is not only to preserve the natural beauty but also to make our country appear beautiful and clean to many domestic and international tourists. To efficiently carry out these various projects, the Urban Saemaul Undong was linked with nature conservation efforts, leading our living environment to become clean, bright, and orderly.


--- (p. 603) ---

We have achieved this while creating a sound (健全) environment (環境) that leads to a sound (健全) spiritual life (精神生活).

## 7. The Ripple Effect of the Factory Saemaul Undong (運動)

The 1970s (年代) were a decade (年代) of economic growth (經濟成長), social development (社會開發), and national development (國家發展). We successfully laid the groundwork (基盤構築) for modernization (近代化), which took 1~2 centuries (世紀) in Western (歐美) societies, in just over 10 years (餘年). In particular, despite the oil shock (오일쇼크) of 1973 (年), we maintained a 7% growth rate (成長率) by overcoming zero growth (成長) in other advanced countries. This was achieved through cost reduction (原價節減), resource conservation (物資節約), and other performance (成果) improvements. Behind this was the significant contribution of labor-management cooperation (勞使協同) and production efficiency (生産能率化) through the Factory Saemaul Undong (運動).

In a capitalist (資本主義) society, conflict (對立) and imbalance (不均衡) of interests (利害) between labor (勞) and management (使) are almost inevitable. However, we cannot disregard the advantages (利點) of the competitive (競爭) mechanism, motivation (動機) devices, and distribution (配分) based on ability (能力) that capitalist (資本主義) societies possess, as they contribute to increased productivity (生産力提高) and technological development (技術開發).

Through the capitalist (資本主義) system, we must establish the foundation for enriching the country and strengthening the military (富國强兵), as aimed by modern nation-states (近代民族國家). Only then can a nation (國家) and its people (民族) achieve self-reliance (自立), autonomy (自主), and freedom (自由). Such self-reliance (自立), autonomy (自主), and freedom (自由) are not merely conceptual (觀念的) but substantial (實質的) and concrete.

Therefore, we are utilizing the institutional advantages (利點) of capitalism (資本主義) to accumulate (蓄積) and increase (增殖) capital (資本).

From this perspective, the Saemaul Undong (運動) is clearly a means (手段) and a process (過程).

In other words, it is a process (過程) of forming a wealthy and powerful modern nation-state (近代民族國家) through national development (國家發展) and development (開發). Given this premise (前提), what we need first is labor-management cooperation (勞使協調).

We must cooperate (協同) through dialogue (對話) and understanding (理解). In principle, labor's three rights (勞動三權) must be guaranteed (保障) based on the Constitution (憲法), and protection (保護) must be provided through labor relations laws (勞動關係法規). However, given the stage of maturity (成熟) of our capitalist (資本主義) system, we cannot pursue only such ideals (理想). In this process (過程), labor (勞動)


--- (p. 604) ---

A significant gap emerged between workers and enterprises, which deepened both qualitative and psychological disparities. This gap stemmed from workers' own perceptions of labor and their aspirations for life, as well as from the unbridled and irrational lifestyles of business owners. In this context, the latter posed a greater problem. The Factory Saemaul Undong, when traced to its origins, primarily aimed to rectify the consciousness, lifestyle orientation, and behavioral patterns of business owners.

As societies gradually transitioned into advanced industrial ones, there was a growing tendency to seek labor's value not in labor itself but in the satisfaction derived from private life and leisure activities. This shift marked the emergence of a "subjective human perspective" from a previously "mechanical human perspective." The issues of dehumanization in production processes were highlighted as a result. While some mature industrial societies sought to explore new human relationships through dialogue and mutual functions, such maladies and vicious cycles persisted. We endeavored to establish a Korean-style labor-management relationship based on the Saemaul spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation within our corporate culture.

Some argued that the Factory Saemaul Undong ultimately prioritized the profits of business owners over the sacrifices of workers, rather than establishing a normal labor-management relationship. However, as previously mentioned, the Factory Saemaul Undong encouraged business owners to improve workers' working environments and living conditions, including housing and meals, through a sense of public benefit and strong responsibility. It also fostered workers' dedicated service spirit and proactive participation consciousness, leading to labor-management cooperation. Consequently, this resulted in increased productivity and improved product quality.

It is not an overstatement to say that one of the reasons why we alone achieved such economic growth during the 1973 oil crisis was the Factory Saemaul Undong. The Factory Saemaul Undong undoubtedly contributed to maximizing efficiency.


--- (p. 605) ---

## Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

In this way, the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을운동) contributed to the internationalization (國際化) of our companies and greatly aided in the substantial increase (增大) in exports (輸出). While our fragile economic level (經濟水準) in 1960 (年) had a per capita (一人當) national income (國民所得) of $81 and export (輸出高) of only $330 million, the reason we were able to comfortably surpass a national income (國民所得) of $1,000 and export (輸出額) of $100 billion is largely due to the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動). In any case, when the key to corporate development (企業發展) lies in management (經營) and technological innovation (技術革新) as well as the development (開發) of human resources (人的資源), the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動) has also greatly contributed in terms of human resource development (人力資源開發).

First, let's examine the achievements seen on the part of businesspeople (企業人) through the Factory Saemaul Undong (工場새마을運動):

1. Many businesspeople (企業人) gained an opportunity (契機) to clearly recognize (認識) the reality (現實) we were facing through Saemaul training (硏修), and this became an important opportunity (契機) to foster a new national perspective (國家觀) and ethnic consciousness (民族意識). In other words, it became a good opportunity to hold new values (價値觀) and corporate perspectives (企業觀).
2. Not only business owners (企業主) but also mid-level managers (中堅幹部) were provided with an opportunity (機會) to think of innovative (獨創的) and proactive (能動的) management methods (經營方式) through the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) and education (敎育). In particular, exchanging opinions (意見交換) and division of tasks (分任討議) became good opportunities (契機) for mutual education (相互敎育).
3. It contributed to creating a new corporate culture (企業人風土). It became an opportunity (契機) to recognize (認識) and understand (理解) the ethics (倫理) of businesspeople (企業人), the responsibility (責任) of corporations (企業), the public benefit (公益性) of corporations (企業), and the mission (召命) of corporations (企業).
4. Companies realized that to increase corporate profits (利潤) and improve productivity (生產性), a cooperative system (協力體制) between labor and management (勞使間) must be established, and that human relations (人間) are important and that human resource development (人力開發) holds an absolute (絕對) large share (比重).
5. It became recognized that corporations (企業) should not focus solely on increasing profits (利潤增大) for businesspeople (企業人), but also recognize the social nature (社會性) it possesses. In other words, an opportunity (機會) for the germination (發芽) of a Korean-style (韓國的) capitalist (資本主義) spirit (精神) was created.

### On the other hand, the achievements seen on the part of workers (勤勞者) are as follows:

1. Workers (勤勞者) themselves realized that they are not merely existences (存在) that receive wages (賃金) and perform mechanical (機械的) labor (勞動), but existences (存在) that create production (生產) with high value (價値) and meaning (意義) on a national (國家的) and social (社會的) level.


--- (p. 606) ---

## 8. Saemaul Training and Spiritual Education

② Individual workers were instilled with a strong sense of mission to enhance labor productivity and contribute to national development, overcoming their previously fragmented and heterogeneous value systems.
③ Workers developed a positive and constructive attitude towards life.
④ Workers, who had previously devalued their own professions and doubted the worth of their labor, came to recognize the creative significance of their work and reaffirmed their own existence.
⑤ It sparked a sense of purpose and fulfillment in life, motivating individuals towards a better life.
⑥ It contributed to the establishment of new human relationships, fostering an environment where mutual understanding, cooperation, respect for personality, and appreciation for humanity were encouraged.

In this way, the Saemaul Undong made positive contributions to all aspects of our difficult economic situation, including energy conservation, material conservation, quality management, cost reduction, technological development, and personality cultivation. These achievements can be seen as unique and unprecedented in other countries.

The achievements of Saemaul education are manifold, but one of its significant accomplishments was the spiritual education it provided to the citizens, including fostering a new national consciousness, ethnic consciousness, value system, and life ethics. In this sense, Saemaul education should also be highly evaluated for its social educational aspects.

Generally, social education refers to all forms of education outside of formal school education, primarily targeting youth and adults through organized educational activities. Today, social education is widely spread alongside the concept of lifelong education. This is because the rapid social changes and developments of our time render even high school or university education outdated after a certain period, turning the knowledge, information, and technology it provides into relics of the past.

While differing in nature from other forms of social education that focus on new knowledge and science, Saemaul education significantly contributed to adult spiritual education. This aspect should not be overlooked.


--- (p. 607) ---

# Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The Saemaul education (새마을敎育), targeting civil servants (公務員), businesspeople (企業人), teachers (敎師), workers (勤勞者), farmers (農民), housewives (家庭主婦), students (學生), and soldiers (軍人), greatly contributed to instilling in the citizens (國民) the correct attitudes (生活姿勢) and behavioral norms (行動規範) for life.

While there were some criticisms (一部批判) regarding the educational process (敎育過程) and content (敎育內容), the Saemaul education (새마을敎育), as an irregular (非正規的) adult education (成人敎育), achieved significant resonance (共感) in a short period (短期的). Its achievements can be summarized as follows:

(1) Cultivation of the Spirit of Self-Reliance (自主精神)

As we have lived within our narrow territory (國土) and amidst the powers (强大國勢力) of great nations, we have managed to maintain our national (民族) uniqueness (獨自性) and inherent characteristics (固有性) for thousands of years (數千年). This resilience (底力) has been supported by the strong spirit of self-reliance (自主精神) passed down from our ancestors (祖上) to the present day.

If we had not possessed such a strong spirit of self-reliance (自主精神), we might have been annexed (併合) by a great power (强大國) due to the geopolitical situation (地政學的狀況) and the dynamics (力學關係) of power.

The Saemaul education (새마을敎育) provided an opportunity (契機) to re-recognize (再認識) and internalize (體得) such historical lessons (歷史的敎訓) and spirit (精神).

Through the Saemaul education (새마을敎育), we have instilled (體得) in the consciousness (意識) of the citizens (國民) the strong self-reliance consciousness (自主意識) possessed by our national history (民族史), and we have confirmed (確認) our re-recognition (再認識) of our history (歷史) and our traditions (傳統).

Based on such a spirit of self-reliance (自主精神), we must establish (定着) positive (肯定的) and rational (合理的) thinking (思考), maintain (維持) stability (安定) and order (秩序). If such self-reliance consciousness (自主意識) becomes blurred (流露), it may lead to prioritizing (優先) individual (個人) interests (利益) over the interests (利益) of the nation (國家) and the people (民族), and in extreme cases, it may even lead to supporting (擁護) or sympathizing (同調) with the interests (利益) of a great power (强大國).

Today, the implementation (實施) of education (敎育) with national dignity (國格), the establishment (確立) of the Juche idea (主體思想), the development (開發) of traditional culture (傳統文化) and national studies (國學), the excavation (發掘) and restoration (復元) of cultural properties (文化財) and historical evidence (考證), etc., are all opportunities (契機) to elevate (高揚) the self-reliance consciousness (自主意識) of the citizens (國民). Furthermore, when such self-reliance consciousness (自主意識) serves as the foundation (底), economic (經濟的) self-reliance (自立) and the consciousness (意識) of self-defense (自衛意識) in national defense (國防) are also stimulated (刺激). This is because we believe that the origin (根源) of our consciousness structure (意識構造) and values (價値) ultimately (歸着) lies in the self-reliance consciousness (自主意識).


--- (p. 608) ---

## (2) Cultivation of National Awareness

The Saemaul Undong was part of Korea's modernization movement, as previously mentioned. This movement encompassed two aspects: material revolution and spiritual revolution.

Spiritual revolution refers to the modernization of national consciousness. Saemaul education instilled national awareness in its participants. We came to realize the strong national will to escape poverty and form a prosperous nation, free from political, military, and social interference and constraints by powerful surrounding countries.

This realization sparked a belief in the necessity of diligence, cooperation, and the development of science and technology among all citizens. Through the Saemaul Undong process, we came to adopt a lifestyle orientation and attitude that discards pre-modern thinking, fosters confident productive capabilities, and promotes a frugal consumer lifestyle.

## (3) Sound Thinking and Normative Behavior

Saemaul education cultivated sound thinking in citizens and encouraged them to engage in normative behavior. Stability and order in human society can be expected from sound thinking and normative behavior.

In the past, our extreme poverty led us to resign and despair in life. Consequently, our lifestyle became tainted with laziness, complacency, lament, escapism, regression, and decadence.

Moreover, our life consciousness became occupied by dependence, cynicism, selfishness, and factionalism.

Our pressing task is to rid ourselves of decadent life ethics, unproductive value norms, and irrational behavior patterns.

We must cleanse ourselves of misguided life concepts and establish sound lifestyles suited to the new era. We need to establish and develop new value systems and ethical codes in our families, workplaces, businesses, and schools.

In this regard, the Saemaul Undong clearly provided an important impetus for spiritual revolution by establishing the spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation.

## (4) Respect for Public Interest and Increased Productivity

# Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

From the 1960s, the promotion of industrialization and modernization accelerated urbanization, and urbanization, along with the universalization of education, raised our relative consciousness. Individualism-based rationalism aimed at maximizing individual interests, and intense competition to maximize these interests gave birth to selfish individualism. This selfish individualism, which has permeated our society today, not only breaks the sense of coexistence in society but also, in extreme cases, creates a relationship of "enmity among all." This hinders social integration and could even lead to internal social division. Such phenomena have become common social problems in liberal societies, and how to harmonize individual differentiation and social integration has been their biggest challenge.

Saemaul education emphasized appropriate adjustments to pursue individual rational profit through efficiency and scientification without neglecting common public interests. Through Saemaul education, many trainees came to serve their neighbors, society, and the nation, and to cultivate a spirit of cooperation for the common good.

(5) Action and Practice, Not Concepts and Theories
Contributing to the cultivation of a personality of unity between words and deeds by mastering the philosophy of action and practice, not empty theories, and putting it into practice. The big task that remains is how to adjust and mutually complement Saemaul education and regular school education.

# Section 3 (第3節) Success Factors of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

The human desire to live well is fundamentally the same across all times, but the methods chosen to achieve this have not been the same. The type of collective activity of residents with regional social characteristics


--- (p. 610) ---
