From this perspective, during the Silla era, the method was presented as "Dure," and during the Joseon era, it was presented as the "Hyangyak Movement." Today, we are making efforts to live well through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Then, in what sense can we say that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is presenting a new direction for the development of national history? It is because it has challenged the history of national life, which had sought a path of self-comfort in a peaceful past, and achieved unprecedented developmental changes in a short period.

The attitude of self-management, which did not hesitate to find the principle of possibility in all aspects and did not shy away from practicing development-oriented will through action, has activated the developmental character of national history. Therefore, the historical significance of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is considered to be great.

### 1. National Awakening

The primary factor in the success of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is national awakening. When we look at the process of our national history, which has gone through many trials, we cannot deny that the dark aspects were more numerous than the bright ones.

Our self-reflective attitude, which does not hesitate to honestly admit the past that we were ashamed of in front of historical facts, has given us the courage to exhibit a more proactive and dynamic attitude.

A clear example of this is that, despite the insufficient realistic conditions, we have prepared an unprecedented economic development plan in history to challenge the future. Furthermore, we are equipping ourselves with a self-defense system, which was once thought to be an insurmountable means of strengthening self-defense conditions. We are also actively challenging the fatalistic notion that we have to live in poverty because we have always been poor, and we are building up our willpower and experience that "anything can be done if we try."

The term "can be done" is meaningful. If we look back, about 420 years ago, during the 16th year of King Seonjo's reign, Mr. Yulgok presented the "Ten Million Soldiers Theory" to King Seonjo, who said that there is nothing that cannot be done if one has a firm mind, meaning "where there is a will, there is a way." During the reign of King Yeongjo, Mr. Jeong Ja-seong said that there is nothing that cannot be done with effort, meaning "mountains can be moved and seas can be filled." Mr. Jeong Da-san also said that


--- (p. 611) ---

# Chapter 6 Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (Movement)

The idea that if a person decides to do something, they can overcome fate (運命) like one's saju (四柱八字) has been emphasized, advocating the view that humans can conquer nature (人定勝天觀).

In this regard, Yulgok (栗谷) advocated challenging the future (未來), Seong Sangjeong (鄭尙驄) emphasized challenging nature (自然), and Dasan (茶山) strongly argued against fate (運命). However, we have viewed the future (未來), nature (自然), and fate (運命) as objects of fear (恐怖) and have believed that we have had a longer historical (歷史的) experience (經驗) and superior talent (才質) than other nations. Yet, we have not been able to live as well as others because we have not actively challenged these three fears: the future (未來), nature (自然), and fate (運命).

Through the Saemaul Undong (運動), we have learned valuable lessons, such as making and executing plans for goals that consider decades into the future (未來), constructing and renovating houses (住宅) without relying on the advice of geomancers (地理風水家), and even completely redesigning villages (聚落). Moreover, we have adopted a popular (大衆的) lifestyle attitude (態度) of pursuing self-satisfaction (自己充足) through effort (努力) rather than leaving our lives (一生) to fate (運命), which we previously believed to be predetermined (先天的).

## 2. Motivation (動機賦與) and Stimulation (刺戟)

The second key factor (要因) in the success (成功) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) is motivation (動機賦與) and stimulation (刺戟).
While it is true that the Saemaul Undong (運動) began with self-improvement (自力改良) in rural (農村) communities (地域社會), the general economic (經濟) situation (實情) of farm households (農家) before the Saemaul Undong (運動) was marked by difficult periods such as the spring famine (春窮期) and the rice shortage (보리고개).

For the masses (大衆) who hate poverty (貧困), there can be no greater gift (膳物) than the phrase "Let's try to live well too." Efforts to rise above deep-rooted poverty (찌든 가난) began to emerge in various forms (各樣各色), but the most touching (눈물겨웠던) event was the rice-saving movement (節米運動) led by housewives (家庭主婦).

The rice saved in the "jomdori" jar (좀도리통) placed on the kitchen stove (부뚜막), measured by the number of family members (家族數) per meal (끼니마다), accumulated to become a unit of rice (한말) and then a sack (한가마). This primitive form of savings (原始貯蓄) became capital (資本) within the context of poverty (가난).

In the early stages (初期) of improving a three-room thatched house (三間草屋), the cost (斯레트의) was 50,000 won (萬원), and in the case of tiles (기와의 경우)


--- (p. 612) ---

Although 100,000 won was spent, a strong motivating factor, the desire for self-help, began to burn intensely. Furthermore, the cement and rebar allocated to each village in a certain amount served as a detonator for the new village beautification project, while also injecting vitality into the basic industries by creating demand and solving supply shortages. This function helped establish a "pipeline" that could inject social interest and enthusiasm for the Saemaul Undong into both rural areas and industrial society. The leading role of administrative functions actively contributed to expanding the radius of mutual interaction between various sectors, enhancing access to life information and opportunities to acquire production technologies. As a result, the Saemaul Undong could accelerate its expansion and deepening through measures to increase income.

### 3. Introduction of a New Type of Educational System

The third factor in the success of the Saemaul Undong was the introduction of a new pattern of social education system. Any form of education, with its traditional type, has been conducted with those who know teaching those who do not, or with those who have higher education teaching those with lower education. However, Saemaul education, unlike the traditional relic form, is characterized by being conducted in the opposite type. In other words, not only did the traditional theory-centered educational method change to a practitioner-centered educational method, but the hypothetical content-centered educational method also transformed into a factual, inquiry-based educational method focusing on qualities. While theories and hypotheses have the advantage of pursuing infinite content, they are not strong in inducing attitudes to solve current factual problems at the mass living level. The Saemaul Undong, as a practical movement aimed at expelling poverty deeply rooted in our daily lives, whether in conscious notions, lifestyle attitudes, or production techniques, had a system of movement execution methods before theoretical establishment and also had education in the method of pursuing theories.


--- (p. 613) ---

# Chapter 6 (第6章) Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

The Saemaul Undong adopted an educational system that addressed the problem-solving approach. Saemaul education was implemented across various sectors, regardless of social status or class distinctions. It involved education by farmers, education by those with firsthand experience, and education centered around case studies of success and failure. This broad implementation helped minimize trial-and-error in the execution of Saemaul projects, enabled full community participation in the Saemaul Undong, and established a nationwide expansion system for the movement.

## 4. Operation of Support Systems Suitable for the Situation

The fourth factor contributing to the success of the Saemaul Undong was the operation of support systems tailored to the situation. While the fundamental spiritual pillars of the Saemaul Undong are explained based on the three principles of diligence, self-help, and cooperation, we directly experienced and observed how the pace of village development was determined by how strongly these principles were manifested at the community level—through diligent daily attitudes, unyielding self-help will, and wise cooperative unity.

Evidence of this can be seen in the three-stage classification of villages: basic villages, self-help villages, and self-reliant villages. By 1978, basic villages had disappeared nationwide. (Initially, villages were classified into types A, B, and C based on three elements: leadership, capital mobilization ability, and resident cooperation. Later, they were reclassified into basic, self-help, and self-reliant villages, with self-reliant villages further divided into self-managed and welfare villages.)

Moreover, the initial target of achieving an average household income of 1.4 million won per farming household was not only met but exceeded. From 1974 onwards, the average income of farming households surpassed that of urban workers. By 1978, South Korea also comfortably recorded an export volume of $100 billion. The sustained upward trend in income and export figures can be attributed to the systematic and consistent implementation of support systems, such as prioritizing support for outstanding villages and promoting exports. This strategic approach likely contributed to these results.

Through these institutional operations, diverse and innovative ideas were inspired among the people, and residents or regional societies that had been stagnant due to backwardness were able to


--- (p. 614) ---

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) not only provided enterprises (企業體) with the stimulus (刺戟) to strive (奮發) but also aroused self-awareness (自覺) to promote (促求) their own development (發展). The concept (槪念) of support (支援) has generally been understood as providing assistance to those who are lacking (不足) or lagging behind (未洽), but in the case of the Saemaul Undong, the opposite (反對) concept (槪念) was used to operate (運用) the support system (支援制度), which was one of its distinctive features (特徵).

## 5. The Exercise of Leadership (指導力) with Tenacity (執念)

The fifth factor (要因) contributing to the success (成功) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is the exercise (發揮) of leadership (指導力) with tenacity (執念).

It is often said that the first prerequisite (要件) for a long-term (長期的) development plan (開發計劃) is social (社會的) stability (安定). However, our experience (體驗) has shown that the exercise (發揮) of leadership (指導力) with tenacity (執念) was even more important.

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) can be rephrased as a movement (運動) to alleviate (解) the long-standing (久) resentment (恨) of our people (我) who have suffered (苦) from poverty (貧) for a long time (久), aiming (志) to live (生) well (好) forever (永).

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is not a movement (運動) that only a specific stratum (階層) of people (人) can participate (參與) in, nor is it a movement (運動) limited (局限) to a particular region (地域). Moreover, it is not a time-bound (時限的) movement (運動) that ends in our contemporary (當代) era (代).

The question (問題) of how to promote (推進) the movement (運動) to live (生) well (好) in a certain way (方式) according to the social (社會的) development (發展) situation (狀況) should be decided (選擇) by the people (人) living in that era (時代). However, if our desire (欲望) to live (生) well (好) is infinitely (無限히) expanding (伸), the methods (方法), systems (體制), and scales (規模) of promoting (推進) the movement (運動) may change (變). But from the perspective (側面) of responding (對應) to the desire (欲求) to live (生) better (好), I am confident (確信) that there can be no different opinions (異說) that the movement (運動) has the character (性格) of perpetuity (永續性).

Therefore, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is understood as a perpetual (永續性) movement (運動) that should be promoted (推進) beyond (超越) the dimensions (次元) of political power (政權) and political parties (政黨), and a movement (運動) that should be inherited (承繼) by our descendants (後孫) in a more developed (發展的) form (形態) as a "baton" (巴頓).

Such inheritable (承繼可能性) nature (性質) has led to the establishment (定立) of a Korean (韓國的) pattern (模式) in which the functional (機能的) roles (役割) of resident organizations (住民組織) and social bodies (社會體) are interconnected (聯關) in a vertical and horizontal (縱横) structure (構造), centered around (求心) the central (中心的) leadership (指導力) and radiating (遠心的) secondary (次位) leadership (指導力). As a result, various types (類型) of activity systems (活動體系) have emerged (形成).


--- (p. 615) ---

## Chapter 6 Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

### Section 4 Problems and Their Resolution in the Development Process

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was not without its problems as it developed. In a certain sense, pursuing development means consciously orienting oneself toward the future, but in practical terms, it inevitably brings about anxiety. Moreover, it is a fact that farmers, who had long been engaged in the primary industry of agriculture, were reluctant to leave their comfortable homes where they had grown up.

Additionally, it was also a fact that there were many difficulties in obtaining agreement and cooperation from the literati.

However, one clear persuasive argument was the question of "How long will we endure the misfortune of living powerlessly in poverty?"

The three great fears of humanity— the future, nature, and fate—do not clearly guarantee that we will live happier lives, but nor do they predict that we will live unhappier ones.

Fortunately, humans can remember the past in detail but cannot foresee even an inch of the future. This is why we can harbor more hope for the future than fear, and we can possess the courage and wisdom to resolve past dissatisfactions within the future.

Therefore, we can pursue a more valuable tomorrow based on the principle of possibility.

While it is true that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) faced countless problems in its early stages, the collective national sentiment of hatred towards poverty and the sense of shame that our situation was relatively backward compared to overseas affairs, as conveyed through the mass media, served as a vital force to overcome these numerous problems.

Furthermore, an important factor that contributed to overcoming these problems was the tangible results achieved through the continuous promotion of the Five-Year Economic Development Plan.


--- (p. 616) ---

For a long time, we had only known poverty, but the Saemaul Undong brought us both a great shock and newfound confidence. Additionally, the Vietnam War dispatch provided many young people with the opportunity to broaden their horizons in overseas markets. Upon their return, they channeled their dissatisfaction with their living conditions into a driving force for development. These factors significantly contributed to overcoming and resolving the challenges faced during the development of the Saemaul Undong.

# Section 5: Reflection on the Saemaul Undong

While it is undeniable that the Saemaul Undong nurtured our national strength and promoted sustained economic development, we must also acknowledge that the process was not without its issues. Some of these points are worth noting for future improvements:

1. The Saemaul Undong was often government-led, fostering dependency and passivity among residents. This hindered residents' spontaneity and creativity, and there were instances of superficial displays aimed at showcasing results. In our haste to achieve results, we sometimes rushed things.

Given that the movement initially targeted around 36,000 villages simultaneously, it was inevitable that it was government and administration-led in its early stages. This was because there were no indigenous leaders, voluntary resident participation, or independent organizations at the outset. Farmers were mired in old poverty, complacency, and despair. Under these conditions, a privately-led Saemaul Undong was impossible from the start.

Therefore, in its initial stages, the government had to take the lead. The government and administration initiated resident participation and mobilized manpower. They organized division of labor, cooperation, and collaboration. Through numerous meetings and discussions, residents' awareness of participation was heightened, and they began to


--- (p. 617) ---

# Chapter 6 Evaluation of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

Through the Saemaul Undong, people have gained valuable experience.

However, over the past 10 years, new leaders have emerged in each region, and they have gained experience. In each region and workplace, organizations for the Saemaul Undong have been actively formed. Residents' responses and participation in the Saemaul Undong have become more autonomous compared to the beginning.

Now, we must use this experience to ensure that the Saemaul Undong moves beyond superficial displays and avoids focusing solely on achievements or results. We must develop this movement into a genuine effort for oneself, one's family, one's workplace, and one's local community.

Secondly, during the promotion of the Saemaul Undong, there has been a tendency towards non-autonomy. In other words, we have overly focused on support-driven projects. We must reflect on this. It is not about doing one's best and leaving the rest to fate; we have relied too much on official support and external help.

Therefore, when support is cut off, it often leads to the discontinuation of projects.

Moreover, we have realized that the traditional methods have limitations in promoting projects for income increase.

However, the limitations of income increase through the Saemaul Undong can be addressed in the future through university-industry cooperation.

In other words, we must explore not only the cooperation in production but also the communalization of distribution. By improving the distribution structure, we can connect producers and consumers, exclude intermediate profits, and enhance the benefits for both parties. Joint market development is also desirable. Cooperation and division of labor within the village should also be promoted.

Given the current population dynamics, where the rural population is decreasing and agricultural labor is aging and becoming more female, this is even more crucial.

We must also explore the mechanization and technologization of agriculture.

The development potential of the Saemaul Undong is limitless, depending on our creativity and cooperative efforts. We must develop various promotion techniques within democratic procedures and methods.

Thirdly, although the rural Saemaul Undong has been actively carried out and its results are evident, the urban Saemaul Undong, factory Saemaul Undong, and workplace Saemaul Undong are relatively insufficient.


--- (p. 618) ---

However, the most important problem was the lack of understanding about the Saemaul Undong among the intellectual and leadership classes.

In the 1980s, the Saemaul Undong must shed such misconceptions. The Saemaul Undong should truly become a nationwide movement. It is not a movement for any specific individual or class, but a movement for all of us to shed the accumulated chronic issues and old evils we share as a community of fate, and to build a healthy society.

Fourthly, the Saemaul Undong of the 1970s was largely a materialistic revolution. However, the Saemaul Undong of the 1980s must add qualitative movements to such quantitative movements. Efforts to transition quantitative movements to qualitative ones should not be neglected. The Saemaul Undong is a movement for the century-long planning of our nation and people.

Even in the construction of a single road or bridge, we must have a vision and consideration for the distant future. The Saemaul Undong should not be planned, organized, and promoted for the sake of showcasing immediate benefits or results.

Looking back, we admit that there were considerable waste and trial and error in the process of promoting the Saemaul Undong. Our lack of planning was not insignificant, nor was the lack of technical and scientific support. As it is a public enterprise, there was also a lack of responsibility in calculating profits and losses.

However, the Saemaul Undong of the upcoming 1980s must be a scientific and rational movement. This is because a scientific Saemaul Undong leads to the rationalization of life and the continuation of production.

Therefore, we must devise measures to elevate the spirit of the Saemaul Undong—diligence, self-help, and cooperation—into a scientific spirit.


--- (p. 619) ---

# Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

## Section 1: The Second Decade of the Saemaul Undong (運動)

If we refer to the Saemaul Undong (運動) of the 1970s as the first decade, then the Saemaul Undong (運動) of the 1980s becomes the second decade.
As the Saemaul Undong (運動) is a movement for better living, the logic that our efforts for better living cannot be interrupted can be found in the fact that the life of a human being with ideals cannot be separated from a life oriented towards the satisfaction of desires.
In other words, if we consider human life and human desires as separate entities, it becomes difficult to find the real meaning of human existence.
Of course, the question of how to live well and at what level to live well may vary depending on the conditions given to each individual, the content and methods of mobilizing means to satisfy desires, but one common thing for anyone living in any space or time is that they do not give up on the path to satisfying their own desires.
The greatest achievement we have made through the Saemaul Undong (運動) is self-discovery. The exploration of ways to resolve one's own dissatisfaction, the discovery of one's own potential, and the improvement of one's own possibilities and self-confidence in all aspects of self-diagnosis are believed to contribute to making the future of the Saemaul Undong (運動) even brighter.
It seems that the concept of self can be better defined when understood from four aspects.
First, there is the realistic self, second, the ideal self, third, the historical self, and fourth, the national self.
The realistic self is the self that exists in the present time, and dissatisfaction is


--- (p. 620) ---

More people, however, could manage self-regulation in an orderly manner because they had expectations and possibilities that all sorts of dissatisfaction would be resolved in the future. These expectations and possibilities signify an ideal self.

An ideal self refers to a self that implies the existence of a self in the future, which is a future of possibilities. Because of this, it not only serves as an outlet for all dissatisfaction felt by the realistic self but also acts as a protector of the realistic order that is easily shaken by dissatisfaction.

Looking back, we were able to endure and overcome the difficult situation of trials and poverty because we possessed the world of an ideal self that placed hope in the future.

Moreover, our proactive attitude towards life, which was significantly manifested during the 10 years of the Saemaul Undong, was not only a declaration of the will to rise above the trials and poverty of the past but also a strong manifestation of the desire to realize a future-oriented self that could definitely resolve realistic dissatisfaction.

In other words, the first decade of the Saemaul Undong was a period when the power to encourage and inspire the realistic self towards approaching the ideal self was immense.

Development and change are not synonymous concepts but have an inseparable interrelationship. Development without change is impossible, and change without development has little meaning.

Therefore, change is more desirable when it is development-oriented. The creation of development-oriented change is not only a path to pursue the ideal model envisioned in the future but also a method to realize the world of the ideal self.

The next historical self implies that it possesses the past, whether from the perspective of an individual or the position of a community.

A concrete individual has a career, and a national community has history.

History necessarily has both a proud bright side and a shameful dark side. The bright side of history instills pride, while the dark side of history prompts self-awareness with the meaning of


--- (p. 621) ---

## Chapter 7 The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) clearly possesses a dual nature, much like a double-sided mirror. It simultaneously declared an awareness of rising above past trials and a determination to plant great hopes in the future. This is particularly historically significant. The ultimate national self is meaningful as it allows concrete individuals to externalize their concepts.

As members of the vast national community, the inherent concept of self always has the opportunity for self-transcendence through contributions to the community. Through the Saemaul Undong, our collective efforts to improve household self-sufficiency, develop villages, and strengthen the foundation for national development are paths to realizing the ideal of national self. The Saemaul Undong, which should adorn the second decade, is given the proposition that it must harmoniously combine these four concepts of self to make the 1980s even more beautiful.

## Section 2 Resolving to Face the Future

Although the Saemaul Undong has not been around for a long time, as it has progressed, we have overcome the issues that arose and, based on our experiences, gained the confidence, courage, and pride to pursue the direction of national life with a more proactive attitude.

When examining the foundations of our 5,000-year history, we find that periods when the bright side of history stood out were times when the national lifestyle was more proactive. The invention of movable metal type in the 21st year of King Gojong of Goryeo, the invention of the rain gauge in the 24th and 28th years of King Sejong, the creation of Hangul, and Admiral Yi Sun-sin's construction of the Geobukseon, the world's first ironclad warship, in the 23rd year of King Seonjo, were all products of a proactive attitude based on the spirit of innovation and creativity. We deeply understand that the Saemaul Undong is also a challenge to our fate, nature, and the future, embodying a proactive attitude based on the spirit of innovation and creativity.


--- (p. 622) ---

Based on the dynamic principle of attitude, the future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), which is being promoted, must inevitably be bright, aiming at the inherent nature of this characteristic. It should not bring about any retrogressive change.

This is because, considering the developmental nature of human desires, which can make even today's satisfying reality lose its satisfaction tomorrow, humans always possess an inherent mentality that seeks to pursue higher-level desires beyond the current reality.

Like a tree standing against harsh winds, or water gathering on firmly compacted land, when faced with trials and tribulations, both big and small, we must display wisdom and courage to the fullest, using these trials as opportunities to strengthen our roots and compact the land further. In this regard, to promote the Saemaul Undong in the future more meaningfully, we must have a clear consensus on at least the following practical tasks and clearly define our individual social roles.

First, we must ensure that we have the endurance to maintain our will and the logic of consistent attitudes.

While we can cite numerous historical examples of the woes brought about by short-sightedness and the misfortunes born of prejudice, social change in any case does not mean a revolution or disruption of the essence and orthodoxy of that society.

No matter how fierce the waves may be, the surface of the sea may move, but the depths remain as calm as ever.

We have consistently proclaimed the Saemaul Undong as a movement that aims for eternal prosperity. However, if at this point we harbor any doubt about the Saemaul Undong, it is undoubtedly a clear case of self-betrayal and a self-contradiction of "beating one's own drum."

If we call societal destruction when the logic of history commits a contradiction, we can call it self-destruction when humans commit self-betrayal.

There is nothing more terrifying than societal destruction and self-destruction. Therefore, we must consistently pursue the desire to live well, which has been a part of the depths of our national life, both in the past and present.


--- (p. 623) ---

## Chapter 7 (第7章) The Future (未來) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

First, we must further emphasize the need for a clear logic (論理) in our mental attitude (精神姿勢面), one that is marked by enduring willpower (持久力意志) and consistent behavior (一貫性態度).

Second, we must demonstrate proactive (積極的) practical abilities (實踐力) by utilizing the valuable experiences (經驗) gained through a decade (10年間) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) as resources (資源) for future (未來) challenges (挑戰).

Reflecting on our past, it seems that our nation (民族) possessed immense potential (潛在力) yet found itself lagging behind others, living in poverty and powerlessness (無力). This was, as previously mentioned, due to an excessive fear (恐怖) of the future (未來), nature (自然), and fate (運命).

While it is true that the future (未來) offers humans (人間) infinite (無限的) possibilities (可能性), it also provides no guarantees (保障). Our past attitudes (態度) towards life (生活) focused more on the lack of guarantees (保障) rather than the possibilities (可能性), leading us to view the future (未來) as an object of fear (恐怖).

Similarly, we regarded nature (自然) as a terrifying (恐怖) entity (對象), which is why, despite being surrounded by the sea (3面이 바다) on three sides, we shied away from challenging (挑戰) it, neglecting the development of maritime culture (海洋文化發展). Moreover, although we were blessed with natural conditions (自然條件) and unique climates (氣候), we merely sang praises to our "land of golden mountains and rivers" (錦繡江山), without taking proactive (積極的) steps (態度) to transform (造成) this beautiful nature (自然) into a more comfortable environment (環境).

Furthermore, we were shackled by the belief in fate (運命) as determined by our birth (生年月日時) and the interpretation of the Four Pillars and Eight Characters (四柱八字解), entrusting our lives (生涯) to this predetermined fate (先天的運命) rather than challenging (挑戰) it. However, the decade (10年間) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) has shown us that we can overcome (克服) these fears (恐怖) of the future (未來), nature (自然), and fate (運命) through our own willpower (意志), opening up new horizons (局面).

This is encapsulated in the phrase "If we do it, we can do it" (하면된다), a belief (信念) that no endeavor (事) is impossible. Recognizing this as a priceless intangible resource (無形資源) that drives national self-reliance (民族自活), the task (課題) of cultivating (養成) practical abilities (實踐力) that surpass (倍前) the past holds immense significance (意味).


--- (p. 624) ---

The third point is that, in the process of implementing the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), it is essential to cultivate not only the external appearances that have already been refined but also the internal aspects beautifully.

Although it is true that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) began with fundamental improvements and was conducted in a manner that prioritized action, it is also crucial to consider deeply the spiritual and cultural aspects, as well as the purification of emotions, and to seek new developmental trajectories that are dimensionally transformative.

This is because even when living in a beautifully refined environment, one's attitude towards life may not necessarily be beautiful. In our society, where people say they have become prosperous through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), why do various crimes that attempt to fundamentally destroy social order occur? It seems to indicate a "gap" phenomenon where the system for establishing a humanistic order that can manage the material order as a primary concern fails to keep pace with the rapid material development trend.

Human desire to live well is not satisfied solely by material conditions such as food and clothing. It is not an exaggeration to say that the condition of having a mental environment where one can live comfortably is just as important, if not more so, than the conditions for sleeping and eating.

The fourth point is that the radius of activation of the cooperative principle should be further expanded to strengthen the foundation for national self-reliance.

Considering our realistic situation, the surrounding international situation does not necessarily develop in a way that is always favorable to us.

There may be no more important task than clearly defining our continuous development path in response to changes in the international situation.

If the direction of development is not clear, it becomes difficult to maintain the unity of national opinion, and the possibility of integrating various social forces towards a common goal becomes slim. In such cases, we may even fail to exert our own power.

People often talk about total unity and great unity, emphasizing national and social unity, but what we should realize first is that without cooperation among individuals and in primary human relationships, no unity can be achieved.


--- (p. 625) ---

## Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is a movement achieved based on the principle of cooperation (協同原理) between you and me.

Through the process of overcoming various difficulties such as dialogue (對話), compromise (妥協), and agreement (合意) among residents, the movement has evolved into a stage where village-level (單位) projects can be accomplished. In this process, people have learned and experienced what cooperation (協同) truly means in real life (實生活). Individuals who can appreciate the true value (眞價) of cooperation (協同) can become excellent members (成員) of a group (集團), but those whose emotions (感情) towards cooperation (協同) have dulled may possess individual (個人) self-governance (自治) capabilities, but in general (一般的), they lack the ability for collective (集團) self-governance (自治).

It is no exaggeration to say that humans are destined (運命的) to exist (存在) within the order (秩序) of a group (集團). The family (家庭) is a group (集團), the workplace (職場) is a group (集團), society (社會) is a group (集團), and the nation (民族) is a group (集團). Without cooperation (協同), a group (集團) cannot establish a self-strengthening (自强) foundation (基盤) based on its capacity (力量).

The cooperation (協同) method of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) style is based on the harmonious (調和) combination (配合) of social (社會的) elements (諸要素), with the principle (原則) of innovation (革新) rooted in the spirit (精神) of revolution (革命) (meaning self-innovation (自己革新)). It promotes movements across all sectors (部面), such as family (家庭) Saemaul, workplace (職場) Saemaul, factory (工場) Saemaul, school (學校) Saemaul, and urban (都市) Saemaul. On a smaller scale, it fosters neighborhood cooperation (隣保運動) among neighbors, and on a regional (地域社會) level, it implements the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) within cooperative (協同圈) circles to enhance regional (地域社會) self-reliance (自立度). It also elevates the spirit (氣像) of cooperation (協同) through collaborative (協力) methods, accelerating the establishment of a cooperative (協同的) self-strengthening (自强) foundation (基盤) across all sectors (部門).

Therefore, we must not weaken (弱化) our self-strengthening (自强化) plans (方案) for any reason, lest we invite external threats (外患) and make a foolish (愚) mistake. To this end, we must further solidify (確立) the lifestyle (生活) discipline (規律) based on the principle of cooperation (協同原理).

Fifthly, we must apply the wisdom (機智) of a group (集團) to agilely (機敏) respond (對處) to realistic (現實的) situations, drawing from the experiences (經驗) gained through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

We must exhibit outstanding wisdom (機智) to navigate concerns arising from the weaponization (武器化) of oil (石油) resources (資源), anxieties stemming from the disruption (破壞) of power (勢力) balances (均衡), and the potential (可能性) expansion (擴大) of peace (平和) threats (危脅) posed by local (局地戰) conflicts in certain regions (一部地域), which may lead to provocations (挑發) from North Korea (北傀). Amidst these numerous (多數) elements (要素) of uncertainty (不安), we must demonstrate our finest (最優秀) wisdom (機智).


--- (p. 626) ---

At this point, we must view it as something we have to do.

The more we are in a period of change (變動期), the more we must exercise self-restraint (自重). There is nothing more important than making accurate and careful judgments (判斷). Reflecting on the regrets (自悔度) that history's blemishes (汚點) have thrown at us, we must resolutely decide not to leave any blemishes in history. This is what I believe we must do.

As seen above, the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動) was not born out of a mere accidental motive (偶然의 동기), nor was its development a result of any social development logic (社會發展的인 필연성). It was a decision made amidst the conflicts (葛藤) of how to solve our struggles (苦憫) in the contemporary dimension (現時代的 차원) where we must live. It is an expression of determination (決斷) and a product of will (意志) filled with obsession (執念), as well as the price (代價) of persistent effort (努力).

In the growth and development (成長發展) of a nation (民族), there is no example in the history (民族史) of any nation, east or west, ancient or modern, where the bloodshed (出血) that must be endured is a result of mere accident (偶然). The degree (程度) may vary, but there is none.

From this perspective, when we revisit the essence (本質性) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動), we see that its development results leave much room for future efforts (努力) in how it should contribute to our national life history (民族生活史).

### Section 3 (第3節): Key Directions of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

#### 1. Cultivating the Driving Force for National Progress (民族史 進運의 동력培養)

In the 1970s (年代), the entire nation (全國民) cooperated and united, actively responding to the rapidly changing domestic and international situation (國內外情勢) with the Saemaul spirit (精神) of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. We boldly challenged and achieved growth (成長) and stability (安定) in the task (課業) of national revival (民族中興) through self-reliance (自主) and self-sufficiency (自立). This lifted our country to the top ranks among developing countries (開發途上國).

Now, we must not slow down the momentum of national development (國家發展) achieved in the brilliant 1970s (年代). We must sprint into the eagerly awaited 1980s (年代) and create a new historical mission (課題) to definitely become an advanced nation (先進國).


--- (p. 627) ---

# Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong

Given the significant changes in international conditions and the security threats we face, ensuring our survival and future prospects requires a solemn resolve and national unity.

The Saemaul Undong has been fostering a new national spirit of diligence, self-help, and cooperation on this land for nearly a decade. As this movement has spread like a relentless flame across the country, the achievements it has made are truly immense. Starting in rural areas during its initial phase, the Saemaul Undong has, over the past 10 years, expanded to all sectors of our society—rural and urban areas, homes and workplaces, factories and schools—becoming a driving force for national development. It has established a new ethics and correct values for national revitalization, forming a powerful force that propels the progress of our nation's history.

On this foundation, we are now entering a new era. As we welcome this new era, we are aiming for a new national goal: the construction of a democratic welfare state. Just as the Saemaul Undong of the 1970s played a pivotal role in fostering the spiritual attitude needed for rapid economic growth, the Saemaul Undong of the new era must contribute fully to building a just new society and a prosperous welfare state.

## 2. The Promotion of Democratic Culture

While democracy is universally revered as a human value, the methods of realizing this value cannot be identical across time and space. Western societies, which have a Christian cultural background and a long tradition of democratic politics, cannot achieve the same content of democratic politics as Eastern societies with entirely different cultural traditions. When Western democratic politics is directly transplanted into Eastern societies, it cannot take root properly. Such imitated democratic politics, lacking roots, is powerless in addressing the true expectations of society and only acknowledges social confusion, poverty, and stagnation. Therefore, in this new era, we must create and cultivate a democratic politics that can take root in our political climate.


--- (p. 628) ---

The necessity to indigenize various systems and behavioral patterns is not only recognized in politics but also in culture in general. It is not about blindly imitating Western models but about digesting and filtering them to make them our own. This is not about exclusivity but about the legitimate desire for national self-preservation.

Our national will to indigenize democracy should lead to overcoming communism and achieving national unification. Although it is painful that, over the past 35 years of division, the North Korean communist regime has intensified the alienation of our people, we must prevent any fratricidal war on this land and, while doing so, make every effort towards peaceful democratic unification. We must persevere with patience and strive for a unified, free, prosperous, and peaceful nation.

### 3. Building a True Welfare State

An important indicator for the new era is the implementation of genuine welfare policies to build a true welfare state. This arises from the era's demand that, despite rapid economic growth in the 1980s, qualitative improvements in the lives of the people should not forever be overshadowed by quantitative growth.

Social welfare policies are closely linked to the direction of sustained economic development. Continuous economic development is a fundamental precondition for creating the foundation of a welfare society. Moreover, sustained economic growth and development are not only the bedrock of building a welfare society but are also directly connected to the self-reliant national defense we have pursued and will continue to pursue.

However, from the perspective of national security, the most important aspect of the welfare society we aspire to is that all citizens should be able to share the benefits of development and growth. If the fruits of growth are concentrated in a few layers of society and a significant number of citizens are left behind in the shadows of growth, a sense of unity among the people cannot be fostered, and such a society cannot be called a welfare society. Given the situation of confronting the North Korean communist regime, all citizens must equally share the benefits of development to foster mutual trust.


--- (p. 629) ---

# Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

And it can be seen that creating a true welfare society where there is no sense of incongruity between classes is a core task that proves the superiority of our system over the communist system. Therefore, the realization of a welfare society is absolutely necessary even from a security perspective.

## 4. Implementation of Social Justice (社會正義)

A just society can be described in one word as a society where a fair reward is given for fair effort. In other words, it is about creating a society where honest, sincere, and diligent people are respected and treated well by society. In a society where justice is driven out by injustice, and honest and sincere people are treated as if they were foolish, there can be no expectation of national vitality and national development.

Our society has, to some extent, been swept up in material growth, causing our unique customs and moral dignity to fade, and materialistic values to prevail. In the shadow of this, corruption, injustice, and distrust have sprouted and deepened. Without eliminating such entrenched evils, we cannot uplift the correct national spirit in the 1980s, concretize our will for unification, or build a true welfare society. The formation of new values for creating a new era and new history is urgently needed. Previous social purification movements have only focused on removing negative factors with physical force, but from now on, they should continue to develop in a direction that encourages positive elements. This new direction for purification movements is a task for the 1980s that is directly connected to the new direction of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Since the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) began in our rural areas over ten years ago, this flame has continued to burn fiercely each year. It has now taken root as a nationwide movement, bringing about a great innovation in our national spirit. It has also stirred up a strong wind of spiritual revolution in politics, economy, and society, becoming the driving force behind the rapid changes and remarkable developments we see today.

With the accumulation over the past ten years, we are now facing a new era.


--- (p. 630) ---

# A Decade of the Saemaul Undong (1970-1979)

This is how it has become. And based on such exemplary totality, we have set a new historical creation of building a democratic welfare state and national indicators. Our Saemaul Undong should be promoted as a practical movement to achieve the newly set national indicators, meeting a new historical step.

*   First, our Saemaul Undong should contribute to localizing democracy suitable for our political climate.
*   Second, our Saemaul Undong should focus on being a nationwide practical movement to lay the foundation for realizing a just society and a true welfare state.
*   Finally, our Saemaul Undong should be promoted with a full focus on reforming the national spirit, which is a fundamental basis for achieving the national goal of "building a democratic welfare state."

In the 1980s, the goal of the Saemaul Undong is to build a democratic welfare state. We should localize democracy suitable for our political climate, build a true welfare society, realize a just society, and reform the national spirit through educational innovation and cultural development. Through these efforts, we can advance towards the new society and new history that we yearn for.

Such a new society will achieve a breakthrough in the process of unification based on cultural democracy, cultural industrial society, and national legitimacy.

The tasks of the Saemaul Undong in the new era are very significant in this context. To become a model for industrialization, democratization, and national unification for late-developing countries in modern history, and further, a global model, we must steadily address the tasks at hand. There must be a continuous effort to narrow the gap between ideals and reality, accompanied by constant consciousness revolution. Creation itself is difficult to achieve without endurance and labor pains. Just as life cannot be created without the pain of tearing flesh, we must also overcome the problems that arise in the process of striving for a democratic welfare society with bold decisions.


--- (p. 631) ---

# Chapter 7 The Future of Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

## Section 4 Major Development Tasks

### 1. Strengthening the Resident-Led System

#### a. Basic Understanding of the Leadership System

When discussing the leadership system of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), it seems that there is no consensus on where the basic perspective should be placed to hit the nail on the head. Those who respect the autonomous will of the residents criticize the involvement and leadership of the government (官), while those who view the residents' self-driven (自體) promotion capabilities as weak tend to take the government's (官) leadership approach for granted. Therefore, it is undeniable that the focus of the problem lies in the presence or absence, or the degree of strength and weakness, of the residents' autonomous will and self-driven promotion capabilities.

Looking back at the history of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), the basic unit concept as a promotion group was the village (with the exception of the Saemaul Undong (運動) in counties (도·농), factories (공장), workplaces (직장), and schools). The number of villages nationwide amounts to about 30,000, each with different geographical, industrial, and formational conditions. Therefore, each village has its own characteristics in terms of various conditions. However, despite this, the government (官) played a leading role through a uniform promotion method, which led to discussions about the pros and cons of government (官) leadership.

However, before we become fixated on the view that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) started with a government-led (官) approach, we need to consider why such an approach had to be mobilized. First, there is the general tendency of rural residents' dependence on the government (大官). Second, there is the question of at what level the residents' will to collectively and systematically pioneer the path of self-help (自助) efforts can be defined. Third, there is the general outcome of passive social movements.


--- (p. 632) ---

The level of awareness (自覺) among residents was a significant factor. While there could be discussions on whether the government-led approach (官主導方式) was entirely or partially dominant, or whether it would have been better to motivate residents without being tied to the concept of leadership (主導的 槪念), these are essentially theoretical issues (卓上理論) that are far removed from the practical realities (實質的) on the ground (現場).

Expectations for residents' (住民) autonomous consensus (自律合意) to be achieved autonomously were difficult to hold, as were hopes for their ability to formulate plans (計畫樹立能力). Additionally, identifying indigenous leaders (自生指導者) was no easy task. Despite this, the methodology that advocated for the nationwide spread and deepening (擴散深化) of resident movements based solely on the one-sided argument of democracy (民主方式) had an undeniably unrealistic aspect.

In other words, the general notion of comparing our situation to the resultant phenomena (結果的 現象) achieved through centuries of citizen training (市民訓練過程) in other countries might stem from an overly ambitious thought.

The most valuable outcomes (價値) of citizen training (市民訓練) are the spirit of autonomy (自律性) and the spirit of public participation (公共參與).

The spirit of autonomy (自律性) refers to a cultural and spiritual (精神文化的) sense of order (秩序意識) based on the ethics of self-management (自己管理), where one manages their own actions under their own responsibility. The spirit of public participation (公共參與) refers to a sense of public responsibility that arises from contributing to socially defined public values (共觀價値).

Group life (集團生活) clearly requires a system of behavior (行爲體系) where the concepts and value consciousness (價値意識) of individual self (個體的 自我) and collective self (集團的 自我) are harmoniously blended to be substantial, orderly, and successful.

Whether our country possessed such matured civic elements (市民的 要素) during the early stages of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動展開初期) is highly questionable. Given this logical framework (論理的 基調), the so-called government-led type (官主導型) of the Saemaul Undong was inevitably necessary.


--- (p. 633) ---

# Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)
## I. Prerequisites for the Formation of a Democratization (民主導化) System

So, what does the democratization of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) entail?

Even if the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is carried out under a democratic leadership (民主導) system, there are parts where active government (官) involvement cannot be excluded. Conversely, even if the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) is conducted under a government-led (官主導) system, it cannot evolve as a national movement (國民運動) without the cooperation of the citizens (民).

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) has developed into a national movement (國民運動) as it is today, not because it was a system where the government leads and the citizens follow (官主民從), nor because it was a system where the citizens lead and the government follows (民主官從).

Rather, it has progressed under a system of government-citizen cooperation (官民協調).

In what sense was this government-citizen cooperation (官民協調)? From the government's (官) perspective, it induced (誘導) citizen (住民) cooperation (協調) by presenting the contents of the plan, while from the citizens' (住民) perspective, they proceeded with a cooperative attitude (協調態度) by requesting government (官) support and guidance to pursue their basic objective of self-interest (自家利益).

In other words, the government (官) was a provider (給付的) of cooperation (協助者), and the citizens (民) were petitioners (請願的) for cooperation (協助者).

However, one point to note is that when conflicts (相互衝突) arose between the positions of the provider (給付者) and the petitioner (請願者), the government's (官) position was often dominant (優勢).

It might be an overstatement to conclude that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) was a government-led (官主導) system based solely on this aspect.

This is because the government (官) has a nationwide (全國的) scope of vision (視界半徑), while the citizens (住民) have a local (局地的) scope of vision (視界半徑).

When one has a local (局地的) scope of vision (視界半徑), it becomes difficult to have the insight (眼目) to understand how local (局地的) projects (事業) should harmonize with national development plans (開發計劃).

However, from the government's (官) perspective, which grasps the overall (全體的) contents of the development plan (開發計劃), it was easy to discover the errors (錯誤) and mistakes (誤謬) in local (局地的) development plans, and thus it could not help but exercise its dominance (優勢性) to prevent and correct them.


--- (p. 634) ---

It will be necessary to do so. For example, in the case of the New Town Formation Plan, there is a road network formation plan, but there are cases where landowners ask why the government cannot prevent them from building their own houses on their land. Or, in the case of the national food production plan, there is a policy that a certain percentage of new varieties must be planted, but when farmers refuse, the administration secures a certain amount of new variety planting through administrative power. Such cases have often been pointed out as examples of government-led initiatives.

In such situations, it is essential to point out why pre-enlightenment was not sufficiently carried out and why methods for voluntary cooperation from residents were not induced.

However, even here, there is another aspect to consider. Following the previous examples, ① the exercise of government authority to secure planned road network formation ultimately aims to beautify the living environment of the region's residents for the enhancement of public interest, and ② the exertion of administrative power to secure a certain rate of new variety planting area aims primarily to increase food production in agriculture and contribute to improving the level of national food self-sufficiency. These points cannot be denied.

From this perspective, if we accept the role of the government, there is no need to vaguely cause a definition of the final beneficiary of interests by necessarily calling the phenomenon of government action "government-led." However, one thing to note is that the technical issues in the process of government action being exercised need to be further developed.

Then, when it is viewed that the Saemaul Undong should transition to a so-called democratic leadership system, what should be understood as the prerequisite condition for this?

It might be summarized from the following aspects.

First, it is an issue of forming a popular consciousness type that values process over results. Since the generation of results without process is not possible, the popularization of consciousness that values process holds truly important significance.

Perhaps the general pains experienced by underdeveloped social groups come from such an inclination to belittle the internal aspects, and the results derived from it.


--- (p. 635) ---

## Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

For the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) to transition into a democratized (民主化) system (體制), it must be understood as democratization (民主化) methodologization (方法化). Additionally, to carry out the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) under such an understanding and adjustment, there must be a development of public consciousness that prioritizes process (過程) over results (結果).

Secondly, two value consciousnesses—self-oriented (自我指向) consciousness and community-oriented (共同體指向) consciousness—must form a public perception framework that exhibits duality (兩面性) from a third value criterion (價値基準). This framework should be established as a social value criterion (社會價値基準).

A principle of harmony (妙合) must be formed where the radius (半徑) of the self-concept (自我槪念) expands into a community concept (共同體概念), and the radius (半徑) of the community concept (共同體槪念) shrinks into a self-concept (自我概念).

Individuals and society are clearly like the two sides of a coin (銅錢) or the two wheels (兩輪) of a vehicle (車輛). However, the relationship between individuals and society is inherently difficult to form as a dual-value (兩價) relationship.

The degree of community cohesion (共同體凝結度) and the degree of harmony (和協度) towards common goals (共同目標) are indeed indicators of such metrics (尺度).

The value criterion (價値基準) discussing advanced and developing stages (先後進性) is perhaps a phenomenon based on the order (秩序) of the relationship (關係) between the community (共同體) and its members (成員).

The fact that the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement), despite starting under the same conditions, created more advanced (先進的) situations (狀況) in Village B than in Village A, as seen in many cases (事例), was perhaps a manifestation of such systemic order (體系秩序).

Thirdly, it is about enhancing the self-awareness (自覺度) of individuals regarding their social (社會的) responsibility (責任) in managing (管理) their own roles (自身).

The formation of a developed society, a prosperous society, and a welfare society is not achieved through external human (人間) conditions (條件) such as locational (立地的), resource-based (資源的), or environmental (環境的) conditions (條件). It is ultimately achieved through the creative (創造的) actions (作用) of humans, based on their intentional (作爲的) conditions (條件). To build a comprehensive happy society that embodies the meaning of living well, humans must take the lead in developing, utilizing, managing, and preserving conditions (條件) such as location (立地), resources (資源), and environment (環境).

Therefore, as humans (人間), every individual must be aware of their role in the community (共同體) to which they belong.


--- (p. 636) ---

Values and attitudes towards the future, organizational perspectives, perspectives on challenging nature, and pioneering attitudes towards self-management must be defined based on one's role. The Saemaul Undong is, to put it clearly, a task aimed at realizing the ideology of developing a complex community called a village, while actively challenging the future, nature, and fate—which we have feared—as a means to create a bright history that connects generations. To do this, we must be aware of actively responding to the calling that arises from the perspective of the members living in that era.

When a consciousness system is established from these three aspects, the concept of the role of the government will become clear, and the citizens will establish a sense of calling from the perspective of the citizens.

The development of society is not led by only a part of the members but is achieved through the harmony principle of all members with different characteristics, each doing their best based on their roles.

## II. Strengthening the Direction of Resident-Led Systems

To promote the Saemaul Undong more substantially in the 1980s, one method to enhance the leadership of residents is to explore the following directions for strengthening.

First, the government's attitude should shift from being the executor to being a supporter of the planning subject's function. Based on the residents' experiences over the past 10 years of the Saemaul Undong, we should focus more on motivating them to find and develop plans for dimensional changes.

Second, the process of setting goals for the Saemaul Undong should reflect the collective will of the residents within the organizational system. A consensus-building system model should be developed for this purpose. Methods where promotional plans are prepared by one-sided government consensus bodies and imposed through administrative directives should be avoided.

For example, a system should be developed where plans are formulated through discussion, analysis, and compromise among government-citizen dialogue bodies, from the Central Deliberation Council to the Neighborhood Development Committee.


--- (p. 637) ---

# Chapter 10 (第10章) Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) and the Future (未來)

Thirdly, the resident proposal system regarding the Saemaul Undong must be developed.

Previously, the development indicators and proposals for how to lead the Saemaul Undong were announced through occasions such as the Saemaul Implementation Leaders Conference.

In fact, the decision-making process for the content was often made based on one-sided materials adopted by officials from relevant departments at that time.

In the future, the previous method should be revised to open a window for all residents to utilize the proposal system. Institutional measures should be put in place so that residents' opinions can be conveyed through the channels of the deliberation system on one hand, and adopted and utilized through the proposal system on the other.

Fourthly, we must escape from uniformity and present a blueprint for short- and long-term plans.

Considering that each village has its own uniqueness and that conditions differ among factories, workplaces, schools, and urban areas, it is a fact that the development plans and achievement speeds of the Saemaul Undong can also differ.

By escaping from uniformity, we should maximize the advantage of acknowledging the uniqueness of the Saemaul Undong promotion units and supporting and guaranteeing the achievement speed through the presentation of short- and long-term plans.

Fifthly, we must enhance public understanding so that the national land development plan and the regional community development projects promoted through the Saemaul Undong can be recognized as a parallel system.

If the national land development plan exists separately and the regional community development plan through the Saemaul Undong also exists separately, there are often cases where friction and conflict arise between the two plans.

The more there are cases of friction and conflict, the more residents will hesitate to develop autonomous development plans.

For example, if the content of the two plans is revealed as a parallel system, even residents who are carrying out specific village business plans will be able to understand which part of the national land development plan this business corresponds to, which will make them even more lively.

In addition, support system, award system, successor leader cultivation, and Saemaul education plan.


--- (p. 638) ---

The development of evaluation systems (評價制度) and performance management methods (成果管理方法), as well as all other fields (分野), require a model that is suitable for implementing the ideology (理念) of a resident-led (住民主導) system (體制). This model must be carefully devised (講究).

## 2. Promotion of Spiritual and Cultural Education (精神文化敎育)

History (歷史) is based on the psychology (心理) and behavior (行動) of the people (國民), while theory (理論) is based on philosophical (哲學的) and psychological (心理學的) foundations. Policy (政策), on the other hand, aims to cultivate (育成) ethically sound (倫理的) and healthy (健全) citizens (國民). The view that history (歷史), theory (理論), and policy (政策) must be organically unified (有機的一體化) based on the psychology (心理) and philosophical (哲學的) awareness (認識) of the people (國民) holds great significance (重要意味).

History (歷史) is both the survival (生存) and growth (成長) story of a nation (民族), as well as its development (發展) story. Theory (理論), when understood from the perspective of historiography (史觀), is both a scholarly (論究的) tool (用具) for referencing the past (參攷) and a theorem (定理) that reveals the systematic nature (體系性) of the development process (發展過程). It is also a public (公理的) hypothesis (假說) that illuminates the future (未來) path (進路).

Policy (政策), meanwhile, uses referenced content (內容) as a mirror to solve current (顯在的) tasks (課題) and orient towards the future (未來). It is a means (手段) of implementing ideology (理念具顯) that concretizes (具體的) public (公理的) hypotheses (假說) into established (定說) theories, rationally (合理的) organizing social phenomena (社會的諸思象)(social phenomena) to guarantee (保證) facts (事實) and pursue (追求) infinite (無限) progress (追求).

In this sense, history (歷史) should have as few refractions (屈折)(prism) as possible in its development process (展開過程). Theory (理論) should develop (發展) with a systematic (體系)(logic) approach to reality (現實接近的), and policy (政策) should have the ability (能力) to solve tasks (課題). Looking back at the history (運動史) of regional society (地域社會) movements, many theories (理論) and ideas (構想) have been proposed to achieve social development (社會發展). However, policies (政策) as means (手단) to transform (轉換) these theoretical developments (發展定理) into reality (事實) have often been lacking. As a result, many excellent ideas (構想) and theories (理論) have withered away without being elevated (昇華) to historical facts (史實).

As we have already seen with the case of local agreements (鄕約), they either did not transcend (超越) human (限人的) or geographical (限地的) limitations (範圍性格), or they were not policyized (政策化) in a way that could dynamize (動態化) the entire (全體) society (社會)(total society). Additionally, they did not sufficiently contribute (寄與) to recording (記錄) the draft (草) of new history (新歷史). Upon closer examination, this is due to the fact that (歴)


--- (p. 639) ---

# Chapter 7 (第7章) The Future (未來) of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

It is understood that there were factors that prevented the integration of history (史), theory (理論), and policy (政策). To ensure the functional (順機能的) development (展開) of national history (民族史), we must establish a proactive system (能動體制) based on innovation (革新性) and creativity (創造性), forming a dynamic relationship (力學關係) that is both realistic (現實管理的) and idealistic (理想對應的). This will enable us to achieve development (發展) based on the accumulation (蓄積) of new facts (事實).

The Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) currently underway must clearly resolve (確然) not to repeat past mistakes (前非) and past regrets (前轍). Only then can it transcend (昇華) its historical (歷史性) significance (意義) and more greatly embody (意味) the meaning of developing (發展的) and inheriting (承繼) history (歷史).

If history (歷史) is an absolute (絶對的) continuum (斷絶) that cannot be broken, then the resolve (決意) to develop (發展的) and continue (承繼) that history (歷史) must be increasingly (日益) elevated (高揚). This is what is required (要請).

In other words, the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) holds historical (歷史的) significance (意義) in resolving (解消) the latent (潛在) national (民族的) dissatisfaction (不滿) embedded in past history (先代史), and in achieving (成就) the realization (實現) of desires (欲求) that could not be satisfied (充足) by internal and external (內外的) social (社會) conditions (條件). At the same time, it possesses a future-historical (未來史的) significance (意義) in that it can stretch infinitely (無限) into the future (未來) to:

1. Establish (創建) one's self-image (自我像)
2. Formulate (定立) the social image (社會像) of one's hometown (故鄕)
3. Emphasize (浮刻) the image (映像) of a sacred motherland (祖國)

From this perspective, today's Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement) can be said to possess a continuity of historical (續歷史性) development (發展指向的).

How the current facts (諸事實) will be evaluated in future society (後代社會) depends on where the ideology (理念) driving today's development (發展推進理念) is anchored (基點), and how we ourselves (自身) invest (投入) our roles (役割) in the process (過程) of realizing (具現) that ideology (理念). This is how we can respond (副應) to our historical (歷史的) mission (召命).

In this sense, the task (職務) imposed (賦課) on us today is to harmoniously (調和) connect (結付) the past (先代) and the future (後代). The wisdom (叡智) to achieve (發揮) this is the practical (實踐) manifestation (浮刻) of the will (意志) to link (連結) today's desires (欲求) to tomorrow's ideals (來日理想), even as we dig (파헤쳐) into the realistic (現實的) problems (問題) of a dissatisfying (不滿) past (지난날). This is the very essence of the inheritance (承繼) and development (發展) of national history (民族史) through the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement).

Humanity (人間) is a being (存在) that possesses ideals (理想), and at the same time, a being (存在) that strives (努力的) to realize (具現) those ideals (理想). Therefore, "Let us live well" is the setting (設定) of an ideal (理想), and "The effort (努力) to live well" is


--- (p. 640) ---

The pursuit of ideal realization (理想具顯) is an endeavor to expand the means-value system (手段慣値體). Therefore, the former (前者) is the goal (目的), and the latter (後者) is the means (手段). Since means (手段) follow the goal (目的) to achieve it, means (手段) always prioritize efficiency (能率) as their value content (價値內容). The necessity (必要性) to promote the Saemaul Undong (運動) in a more rational (合理的) and efficient (能率的) manner lies in addressing the shortcomings (缺點) of regional community movements (地域社會運動) observed in pre-modern history (先代史) and striving to achieve the realization (具顯) of purpose values (目的價値) more substantially.

All humans (人間) seek happiness (幸福)(happiness), which is measured (尺度) by the extent to which possessions (所有)(possessions) satisfy desires (欲望)(desires). However, to satisfy infinite (無限的) needs (欲求) with finite (有限的) possessions, the resource (資源) of "sustained effort (持續的努力)" holds the greatest significance (意味). Therefore, to achieve the Saemaul Undong (運動) with high intentionality (宿意度), we must:

1. Unify (統一) societal (社會的) perceptions (認識方法) of the Saemaul Undong (運動).
2. Establish (定立) the development principles (發展原理) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) on a popular (大衆的) consciousness base (意識基盤).
3. Model (模型化) the operational system (展開體系) of the Saemaul Undong (運動).
4. Clearly (確然히) present (提示) the historical (歷史的) value attribution (價値賦與) of the Saemaul Undong (運動).

Given that the Saemaul Undong (運動) is a sustained effort (持續的努力) to pursue a brighter aspect (面) of our new lifestyle society (生活社會), the Saemaul education system (敎育體系) must be developed (開發) dimensionally (次元變化的) to foster the development-oriented (發展指向的) philosophy (哲學) of the Saemaul Undong (運動) through spiritual education (精神化敎育) and embed it in the grassroots of national life (國民生活底邊).

## 3. Strengthening the Foundation for Rural Prosperity (農村富强基盤)

### a. Shifting Focus to Rural Areas (農村關心轉換)

Rural areas (農村) are, in a word, the homeland (故鄕) of humanity (人類). They are formed (形成) as clusters (集群) of old-fashioned villages (舊式村落).

The notion that rural areas (農村) themselves (自體) are old-fashioned is echoed in the words of "Morgan," a key figure (主役) in one of America's (美國) famous development cases (開發事例), the Tennessee River (江) development project (開發事業). He argued that rural areas (農村) have simultaneously (同時) fulfilled (遂行) the role (角色) of shaping (主宰) human destiny (人類運命) and serving (源泉) as the origin (源泉) of urban formation (都市形成), while also acting (養成所) as a breeding ground (養成所) for sound (健實) leaders (指導者).


--- (p. 641) ---

# Chapter 7: The Future of the Saemaul Undong (New Community Movement)

They say it's about the countryside and the village.
It is not an incorrect expression to say that the origin of cities is a product created to remove the inconveniences of trade between villages and to meet the commercial need for exchange.
However, it is a fact that today's countryside is aging due to urban factors, and the preference for places of human residence is urban-oriented. Moreover, in some regions, the progressive phenomenon of depopulation makes it difficult to even expect the possibility of rural reconstruction.
One ironic aspect is that, despite the fact that the countryside is the treasure trove of food, the primary good in human life, and the phenomenon of food weaponization is prominent in today's international society, just as important as weapons and oil resources, public interest continues to be sustained in cities rather than in the countryside, which is the original production site of food and is becoming impoverished.
The countryside is where the historical roots of humanity are deeply embedded, and it is also the concrete hometown of each individual emotionally. Therefore, at this point, we should reconsider our old-fashioned villages, the source of human growth and the wellspring of the heart, and explore directions for revitalization for the future.

## II. Phenomenological Problems of Rural Society

The first difficulty that today's countryside is facing is the instability of its self-reliance base.
First, the trend of urban migration, regardless of the reasons behind it, is revealing a new phase in the gap between urban and rural areas.
The migration of highly educated human resources from rural areas is causing an intellectual depopulation phenomenon in rural community societies, weakening their capacity to accept new culture. The migration of prime-aged labor force is leading to a structural imbalance in productive activity capacity, resulting in a depopulation phenomenon in terms of human resources, which in turn causes a decline in productivity. Additionally, the phenomenon of rural households migrating to cities, following their sons and husbands, raises the issue of population decrease at the village level.
These multifaceted factors promoting depopulation make it difficult to preserve the functional original form of villages, leading to the phenomenon of declining social investment return rates.


--- (p. 642) ---

The first point is that it is creating problems. For instance, the low utilization rate of arable land, the sharp decrease in the number of school-age children leading to the diminished effectiveness of educational facilities, and the unreasonable maintenance of health centers, post offices, and various agricultural-related agencies are all manifestations of the grim reality of rural areas.

Secondly, the degeneration of rural perspectives is shaking the traditional emotional foundation of rural society. The intensity of urban orientation is so strong that it makes us forget the warm and comforting taste of our hometown's mountains and rivers. At a time when the trend in living environment development is to create a harmonious beauty between nature, greenery, and humans, is it not something we should consider to leave the phenomenon of rural depopulation unattended? The neglect of rural depopulation is not only a sign of a dismissive attitude but also indicates a tendency towards the spread of rural alienation. The case of Free China, where rural revitalization policies are bearing fruit, and Japan, which is advancing research on local industry theories, are all understood as efforts to prevent rural depopulation.

Rural areas cannot merely be the romantic homeland of emotions. If rural areas were the original starting point of human communal life, they should become a place that is warmer, greener, and more abundant. In this sense, the degeneration of rural perspectives should not be a passive change but a reconstruction or a developmental change.

Thirdly, the discrepancy between the social image and the internal reality of rural areas could potentially become a threat to the future of rural society. It is a fact that the rural areas of our country have, based on the Saemaul Undong, shed the old shell that had continued for thousands of years and taken on a new appearance. Housing has been improved, villages have been structurally improved, village roads and the environment have been developed, physical aspects of the distribution network with markets have greatly changed, farmland has been organized, new farming methods have been developed, and barren mountains have been greened.


--- (p. 643) ---

# Chapter 7 (第7章) The Future (未來) of the Saemaul Undong (새마을運動)

It is a fact that enormous developmental changes have been achieved.
Moreover, it is also a fact that electric lights have been turned on in dark mountainous villages, and mass media such as TV have been widely disseminated, narrowing the temporal and spatial gaps in cultural life.
Furthermore, the paving of major national road networks has reformed the order of production and logistics, while expanding the possibility of more convenient social mobility between urban and rural areas.
In a word, while the conditions for development and modernization have been generally established, the problem lies in the fragility of the internal aspects, which are characterized by an imbalance with the external aspects.
There is an old saying, "Real in the middle and apparent on the outside" (實於中而形於外). The issue of ensuring the solidity of internal aspects is something that should never be neglected.
Of course, in the process of achieving rapid development and pioneering, there may be resistance, impracticality, and trial and error, but our desire is for such secondary damages to be absent, which is our honest feeling.
Even if there are beautifully renovated improved houses, if the owners of those houses are absent, or if there is no capable leading group to drive the development of the village within the improved settlement, this means that the external appearance of the village exists, but the internal aspects are lacking.
One of the current issues in rural society is that while the number of farm households remains the same, the structure of the farm labor force is almost aging.
As can be seen in the table, when taking 1962 as the base year, over 14 years, the change in the number of farm households was 4.5%, while the change in the farm population was 15.3%.
This indicates that, in a fragmented way, the external appearance of rural society is almost maintaining its old level, but the internal aspects are not.
