Through national industrialization, the Saemaul Undong also presents a definite and workable means of satisfying all the economic and social prerequisites for the development of Korean democracy, such as the accumulation of wealth, the enlargement of the middle class, the building of a sound and beneficial welfare state, etc. But, in implanting democracy, the most emphasized directions (points) of the Saemaul Undong are the creation of the spirit of a democratic citizen by means of spiritual development, the training of democratic leaders through the democratic process of the Saemaul Undong, and democratic training itself effected in achieving some of the Saemaul projects. And it should be added that the Saemaul Undong revives the traditional spirit of communal life and changes it.


--- (p. 680) ---

### (4) Based on the history of traditional nationalism, the Saemaul Undong promises the peaceful unification of the Korean peninsula by overcoming the obstacles which have been dividing the country since 1945, especially the Korean War. Unification is the most important stimulant for national revitalization and the main objective of modernization. Unification is an ultimate goal of the Korean people in order to overcome their tragic fate and agony caused by the division of the country, and it is also a prerequisite to overcoming other obstacles on the way to a welfare state. Since unification is a matter of life and death for Korea, it should be achieved by peaceful means; therefore, the first step should be a peaceful settlement by making self-defense its main point. The process of unification should also be steady, for it should not be simply a formal nor reactionary unification. It should be one where the divided people become truly united without any heterogeneity nor any ideological differences, so that it can really promise unified national development. Therefore, fostering a strong conviction in the identity of the Korean people, and knowing the historical mission of the country to preserve the national tradition, we should make it a heraldic main force of the unification that leads into a glorious national development. Thus, it is not an exaggeration to say that the Saemaul Undong is the key to the unification of Korea.

### (5) The Saemaul Undong presents a model of national development since it demonstrates its superiority in the methods of modernization as it is based on the traditions of national history and since it tries to bring peace to this country as the preconditions of the unification by means of self-defense. The so-called “economic development of socialism” in North Korea is not only a whirlpool of economic failure but also an anti-national heresy which annihilates the traditional


--- (p. 681) ---

Korean culture completely. And the so-called ^revolution of South Korea by the proletariats^ is also very far from the ideal unification based on the traditions of national history. In short, the Saemaul Undong is the only way to unify the country peacefully, preserving the national heritage and tradition. Now, the Saemaul Undong is marking a new era; the establishment of a democratic welfare-state which is one of the national goals of the new era, the realization of social justice through the eradication of all social evils and wrongdoings, the development of the national spirit by showing the potential powers of the nation, etc, are not far from the ideals of the Saemaul Undong. The Saemaul Undong is, in a sense, a new detonator to solidify nationalism which is directly linked with the goals of modernization, such as industrialization, democratization, unification, etc. In short, the Saemaul Undong is the main factor of building the material and spiritual basis for the unification and the development of the country, and it is the pronoun of modernization on its way to the nationalistic unification.

### (6) The idea of the Saemaul Undong can be summarised as follows: It

can be said that every culture has its own territory and has its own special meanings and interpretations of a ‘village’. Thus, when the idea of a village which has been formed in the minds of the Korean people, is defined in a general sense, two intrinsic qualities seem to appear: ① The village symbolizes an everlasting root of spiritual life connected with the long tradition of ancestor-worship rather than a mere living place. ② The village is not an artificial idea of collection formed in a supernatural sense, but traditionally it is formed geographically as an assimilated thing grown in natural environments. When these two meanings are put together, in the minds of the Korean people, the traditional idea about a village is the root of the spiritual bond and a resting place for the mind. Thus, it is based on the universal view of the benevolent village》whi^h is somewhat cor卜


--- (p. 682) ---

connected with the Confucian view of life. In other words, it idealizes a community where both the inner and the outer sides of the benevolent village can conjoin for benevolence. The inner side of it means the world of the mind, and the outer side means the physical world of the village. The basic idea of the new community, Saemaul, can be construed as a new integrated ideology where the traditional meaning of the village is added to the idea of scientific modernization, and the practical learning necessary for the formation of a modern country.

### (7) The main idea of the Saemaul Undong in another sense is an

ingenious integration of the transformation toward a benevolent village—a spiritual transformation and materialistic modernization as an industrial revolution. The guiding spirit of the Saemaul Undong is diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Among the three principle ideas, cooperation is based on the traditional idea of benevolent village where acts of kindness and moral justice are overflowing, and the other two, diligence and self-help, are based on the idea of capitalism necessary for modernization. Thus, the Saemaul Undong can be construed as a behaviorism based on the two ideas combined; the behavior of the patriotic and dedicated leaders of the Saemaul Undong is engrafted on the psychological structure of the general public of Korean people. Let us first consider the narrow sense of the grafted-relationship. The Korean people usually have an unconscious longing for the benevolent village based on human sentiment and righteousness. When we consider the broader and positive meaning of relationships there is a release or catharsis of the psychological tensions such as grudges, discontents, and rancors, the typical psychological phenomena found in the Korean people in the course of the successful implementation of the behaviorism of the Saemaul Undong. Throughout the long history of Korea, the Korean people have experienced lots of grudges or rancors such as poverty, ignorance, insult, contemptuous treatment, wars, and rebellions. When they were faced with such things, they had experienced only psychological defeatism. However, through the Saemaul Undong, they began to exercise their spiritual strength in


--- (p. 683) ---

66^ facing their fate,

### (8) When we consider the relation between the Saemaul Undong

and national security, we could not get rid of the idea of defeatism existent until the 1960s, that is, it was a dominant belief that it was impossible for the Korean people to have an economic independence for national self-defense. Following the Nixon doctrine, the U.S. Army stationed in Korea began to withdraw, and they claimed that the stationing of the U.S. Army in Korea was not an obligation but a right according to the mutual defense treaty between the Republic of Korea and the U.S.A.; thus, in 1977, Carter’s withdraw plan began with a one-way notice. In facing this hard reality, the Saemaul Undong has been playing an important role as a spiritual core factor in establishing a self-defense plan from the time of the Nixon doctrine. Under the new determination of the people that “We should defend our own country” stimulated by the new spirit of self-defense policy, the army equipment modernization plan which began in 1971, was a great success, and in 1975, the Korean people could bear all the defense expenses by means of a defense-tax system. The second army equipment modernization plan should be pushed ahead until 1985 through the Saemaul Undong, because the number of the North Korean army has increased from 400,000 to 700,000, and our G.N.P. cannot be expected to increase by more than 9% due to the oil crisis and the economic depression of the world; thus, it is very difficult to achieve the self-defense modernization project in a foreseeable short period of time. Therefore, in order to overcome all the unfavorable conditions for modernizing the army equipment, we should rely on the spirit of the Saemaul Undong—diligence, self-help, and cooperation. When the international situation around Korea became unfavorable to Russia because of the unexpected compromise among the three superpowers, that is, the U.S.A., Japan, and China, Russia exerted her efforts to exercise great influence over North Korea, and as a result there exists a great danger on the Korean peninsula threatening national security. In an atmosphere of such tension, the necessity of making the Saemaul Undong a part of daily life and activity is felt.


--- (p. 684) ---

more strongly than ever before.

### (9) When we consider the Saemaul Undong in connection with the

sense of a new society, the Saemaul Undong which started in 1970 is, in a sense, a social renewal movement on the structure of thought patterns, which have changed our way of thinking formed and petrified since the Liberation in 1945 after World War II. Before 1970 when the Saemaul Movement began to appear, there were many self-contradictory and negative factors in the value system and some confusions in establishing the true meaning of society because of the indiscriminate introduction of Western culture, especially the Western value system. The individualism and liberalism of the West were transformed into selfishness and led into defeatism when people were confronted with the traditional social value system of Korea. Thus, when seen from the socialistic point of view, the Saemaul Undong is a movement for the salvation of a decaying society because the negative cynical elements in the past traditional thought-pattern and the indifferent attitude of the people are changed into a positive and rational thought pattern by the powerful influence of the Saemaul Undong.

### (10) When we turn our attention to the Saemaul Undong in connection with the sense of politics, the Saemaul Undong has nothing to do with politics in a narrow sense of the political power. But, when seen from a broad sense, that is, when politics is connected with national existence, prosperity, and welfare as well as the social order, then the Saemaul Undong is a political movement. Through the spiritual revolution to revitalize the morals of the people, the Saemaul Undong, being a new national spirit, has crystallized its political nature with the establishment of the existentialism to accomplish the national revitalization and the development of Korean democracy through the self-expression of the pan-national movement.

### (11) Now let us observe the Saemaul Undong in the light of a new

sense of economics. After the Saemaul Undong became a success as a movement of better-living for the people in the rural areas, it moved into a new stage, that is, it became an urban renewal movement as


--- (p. 685) ---

## The Spirit of the Saemaul Undong

Through the improvement of environments, the Saemaul Undong has accomplished inner spiritual growth, and, through the spiritual revolution, it launched efforts to enhance economic standards and improve poor economic conditions. Thus, the new way of thinking about economics through the Saemaul Undong, overcoming the movement of better-living for an individual, has created a new movement of better-living for all, and established an atmosphere where every member of the community can live better through diligence, honesty, and cooperation. The idea of the Saemaul Undong in the sense of economics is best seen in communal life, communal prosperity, and communal cooperation.

### (12) When we see the Saemaul Undong from a historical point of view

Its main objective is the establishment of an ideal welfare-state unparalleled by any other country in the long history of the world. The Korean people have suffered from many unfavorable incidents such as the manipulation and the division of the country by the great powers, class-discrimination, the indiscriminate influx of foreign culture, shameful grudges that we had to bear, etc. The historical sense of the Saemaul Undong will alleviate these rancors accumulated in the past, and will implant a new historical sense of peace inherited in diligence, self-help, and cooperation. It will also find its true meaning in seeking the main underlying force to build a new nation, a democratic welfare-state, through the expansion of the Saemaul Undong.

### (13) If we consider the Saemaul Undong in connection with the sense of our traditional culture

We can easily find the fact that the underlying moving force of the spirit of social cooperation already existed in the traditional way of thinking, especially in the idea of the “Ke” and “Hyangyak,” which have a long history of social cooperative tradition. In this respect, the Saemaul Undong has no difference with the modernization of the traditional idea, because the “Ke” and “Hyangyak” are exactly the same idea as that of self-help, diligence, and cooperation.


--- (p. 686) ---

### (14) When the sense of new education in relation to the Saemaul Undong is considered, the Korean people had been trained under the educational system influenced by foreign culture, but a new educational system born out of the Saemaul Undong which places more emphasis on self-reliance, has been set up and put into force. Thus, the idea of existence emphasizing “here”，the idea of time-reference “now”， and the idea of self-assertion “we” are the result of the new educational goals of the Saemaul Undong. Finally, the Saemaul Undong has created a historical moment where a new image of self-reliant man, a new image of creative man, a new image of cooperative man, and a new image of lively man, can be set up with its mystical power.

### (1) Among the major factors which contributed to the successful Saemaul Movement, its organization has played the most important role. In this light, this chapter will analyze the whole program action system of the movement. The managerial function of the organization will be examined and described, focusing upon its function of structure in connection with various aspects of the Saemaul Undong such as human and material resources, technology, information, etc. Before entering into organizational analysis, there will be presented a framework, within which the organization is described. In other words, the action system of the movement could be described by dividing it into the operations system and the program structure for the purpose of affording a better understanding. And it should be noted that the operations system could be further divided into a motivation system and program action system, and the program structure, into various kinds and levels of the program. In addition, the analysis of the action system according to its characteristics will contribute to a better understanding of the whole system. Its characteristics can be defined to be ① integrated, ②


--- (p. 687) ---

pan-governmental, and ③ long-standing. Finally, the action system can also be divided into a ① program development system, ② program operation system, ③ support system, and ④ public liaison system.

### (2) Within the above-mentioned framework, this chapter will describe

the nature and characteristics of program development and program operation systems of the action program for individual Saemaul programs, and finally the problems intrinsic in the action program itself. First of all, the program development system plans and controls business projects, performing the function of a so-called conventional administrative system, and the results of its functions are to be transmitted to the operations system. The various levels of consultative meetings and committees perform functions equivalent to those of the program development system, and their respective organizational structures and functions will be described in detail. They are ① central consultative meetings, ② city or provincial consultative meetings, ③ city or county consultative meetings, ④ "eub" or "myon" consultative meetings, and ⑤ "ri" or "dong" consultative meetings. Let us proceed to the description of the program operations system. This system operates and manages the business planned by the program development system. And its role is to contribute to better planning by feeding back the results of the assistance provided by the program development system. In other words, its functions are divided and analyzed into two types: functions to be performed in the process of receiving support, and those to be performed in the process of feeding back the results. The functions performed in the receiving or transmission process are ① training for the Saemaul Movement, ② publicity of the Saemaul Movement, ③ administrative guidance, ④ material support, ⑤ technical assistance, and so on; and those in the feedback process are ① confirmation and analysis of the general situation and ② its evaluation by public officials on duty. Prior to the description of the program operations, the organizational


--- (p. 688) ---

### (3) Regarding the description of the action system for the implementation of individual Saemaul programs, primary emphasis was placed on program structure. The subdivisions of the action system for such programs are: ① production basis program, ② income increase program, ③ welfare program, ④ spiritual enlightenment program, ⑤ factory Saemaul Undong, and ⑥ urban Saemaul Undong. Several ministries take part in the Saemaul programs. Therefore, it naturally follows that the Saemaul Undong cannot be concerned only with the tasks and goals of a certain ministry or an institution, but it should rather incorporate into unified Saemaul programs in coordination with various ministries which have to do with the Saemaul Undong. Some of the programs used to be carried out separately by the ministries concerned had to be transferred to the Saemaul programs, since the nature of such programs were more Saemaul-oriented. It is worthwhile to point out that the structure of Saemaul programs are divided on the basis of three criteria: characteristics of a program, the ministry or the agency in charge of a program, and the level of development of the village concerned.

### (4) The action system of the Saemaul Undong which we have surveyed from different angles up to now has many characteristics and problems. The problems, most of which resulted from inappropriate conditions, should be taken into consideration in planning future programs and their solutions will lend great assistance for future Saemaul programs. Let us enumerate the problems.


--- (p. 689) ---

① The fundamental principle of the Saemaul Undong is voluntary participation. This means that villagers should actively engage in both planning and implementing programs of their own accord. However, current conditions often do not support voluntary participation, leading to a forced and standardized organizational structure. This does not necessarily mean the structure is outdated.

② As the Saemaul Undong expands across the country, more ministries and governmental agencies become involved. However, coordination and cooperation among these agencies and ministries are not always satisfactory.

③ While the complexity of the organizational operations system may be inevitable due to the movement's proliferation, working-level organizations with limited human resources and capabilities often struggle with complex and burdensome tasks imposed by the central government, leading to inefficiency and unproductivity.

@ The organization of the Saemaul Undong is multiple-branched, meaning it is divided according to functions and even specific business items, as seen in the program structure. Although this multiple-branching is somewhat unavoidable to leverage organizational characteristics, it is not desirable without an increase in personnel. It would be better to maximize the use of existing organizations rather than establish new ones.

⑤ The action system of the movement within the Home Ministry is comparatively well organized. However, those of other ministries are not in good shape. For instance, the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries has too many branched programs.

⑥ Organizations in name only are of no use. For example, village development committees should exercise general control over each program-specific organization, but they do not always perform their proper functions.

⑦ Because most program-specific organizations are hierarchically organized according to laws, administrative orders, or directions, their members are not well tied together, and the inhabitants


--- (p. 690) ---

tend to be indifferent. ⑧ The Saemaul Undong should shake off the simple-minded idea that a group of people can form an organization and father a project. An organization should be evaluated, not by its physical appearance, but by how it performs its proper managerial functions such as planning, coordination, and assessment on the basis of voluntary participation of its members. An organization, which does not discharge its proper functions or whose members do not even know where they belong, is not an organization but in name only. But unfortunately some of the organizations of the Saemaul Undong do not live up to their names.

### (5) In view of the above-mentioned problems, the action system of

the Saemaul Undong should be adapted to future programs of the movement. In other words, to usher in another successful decade, the action strategies should be readjusted and the action system should be reorganized. Up to now the action system has been controlled mainly by government, and encouraged by late President Park’s devoted interest in the movement. But now that the movement stands on a firm basis, the future action system should be based on grassroots' participation. A reorganization of the action system should take into consideration the fact that its premise is experiencing change. In other words, higher productivity, larger income and better living conditions have been the first concern of the system and its organizations have been managed to serve the purpose, but from now on it should be organized and managed in such a way as to improve the quality of both material and spiritual life. The slogan of welfare was much publicized but has never materialized satisfactorily. One of the greatest problems facing the Saemaul Undong is how to carve out a future action system which will help to insure satisfactory hygiene, public health, recreation, education, employment, and so on, in the rural area. Many other ideas will be suggested in the concluding part. The lesson we got from the 10 years’ history of the Saemaul Undong is that though any organization should not be overbearing, our goal under the present circumstances should be to achieve such kind of


--- (p. 691) ---

## IV. The Rural Saemaul Undong

An organization that can achieve “production and satisfaction.”

### (1) Background of the Rural Saemaul Undong

The rural communities of Korea were originally impoverished. To compound the issue, in the 1960s, while industry made remarkable progress, agriculture stagnated. This exacerbated the economic, social, and cultural disparities between urban and rural areas. The situation appeared to deteriorate, and if left unresolved, it threatened to create a dual social structure of urban wealth and rural poverty, which would further contribute to social instability. Increasingly, people recognized and advocated that the lagging rural communities needed development and that a self-sufficient economy was impossible without agricultural progress. To address these pressing needs, the late President Park Chung-hee initiated the Saemaul Undong as a rural development movement.

### (2) The Significance and Goal of the Movement

The rural Saemaul Undong aimed to enable rural inhabitants to enjoy comfortable living conditions, including better income, mutual aid, a richer and more modernized cultural life, and dignity. Underpinning the movement were activism and practical philosophy, as it was understood that strong will alone, without action, does not ensure an improved life. Indeed, the rural Saemaul Undong held significant importance in various aspects. First, in terms of its composition, it was a movement for a better life, primarily composed of and led by the farming population. Second, in terms of its programs, it was a movement to enhance living conditions and establish the foundations for higher productivity. Third, in terms of public participation, it was a movement that contributed to reforming the villagers' way of


--- (p. 692) ---

### (3) Motivation and Actions Taken for the Movement

The rural Saemaul Undong was launched in 1976 at 33,267 Li and Dong, each of which was supplied with 335 bags of cement, under the motto that “easy life with no hard work means indolence; dependence with no self-help is nothing more than subordination; society in which no cooperation can be found cannot expect any productivity but will only drive into factional strife.” Each village tentatively launched so-called “10 improvement programs,” among which were included widening the road leading to a village, putting small reservoirs in better condition, constructing storages of compost heaps, and so on. But the results reaped in the programs were much better than expected, infusing authorities and officials concerned and villagers with new hope and courage. Encouraged by the results, the government set short and long-range objectives, and set up plans to implement them. For successful implementation of these programs, villages were classified into several types according to their level of development and characteristics. In 1973, all the villages in the country were divided into three types according to their level of development: basic villages, self-help villages, and self-sufficient (or self-reliant) villages, because programs suitable to the level of a village were necessary. Along with these classifications, the Saemaul programs were classified into primary programs, support programs, and income-generating programs.


--- (p. 693) ---

## IV. The Rural Saemaul Undong

programs according to their functions and effects, so as to provide villages with suitable and necessary support. Meanwhile, there were set up standardized programs for each level of villages. The standardized programs for basic villages were mainly new village programs such as street-widening, roofing improvement, maintenance of the dams of streams, and so on. The government provided 500 bags of cement and a ton of reinforcing iron rods to support the programs. The standardized programs for self-help villages were, besides new village programs, job-producing programs, tree nursery programs, and programs for raising village funds of 50 million won to finance the Saemaul programs. In short, the programs for self-help villages were designed to increase the income of the farming population through subsidiary projects. The self-help villages, when they successfully complete their programs, develop into self-sufficient villages. The standardized programs for the self-sufficient villages were programs for laying foundations of productivity, income-wise programs, programs for cooperative production, and so on. For the successful implementation of the programs, a campaign to raise funds of more than 1 million won was launched at the same time. In short, a village which reached the level of self-sufficiency concentrated on income-wise programs and culture and welfare programs. But it was not always desirable to confine certain standardized programs to a certain level of villages. Therefore, the standardized programs for each level of villages were mainly suggested as exemplary programs.

### (4) Classification of Villages According to the Conditions of their Location and Their Upgrading

In the previous section, rural villages were classified according to the level of their development. They are also classified into 5 types according to the conditions of their location: plain villages, intermediary villages, mountain villages, fishing villages, and suburban villages.


--- (p. 694) ---

68. The aim of the classification was to contribute to the development of the rural villages by characterizing them on the basis of their geographical conditions, their historical background, and their social and cultural conditions. 8,104 villages were selected as plain villages. The major guided programs for the villages were those for farmland readjustment, establishment of agricultural appliances centers, establishment of farm product processing factories, and so on. 18,895 villages were to be developed into specialized agricultural villages and their major guided programs were those for the semi-livestock industry, development of specialized crops, fuel forestry, and so on. Business projects were also set up for intensive development of gardening, fruit trees, vegetables, and domestic manual industry in 4,330 suburban villages; in 1,583 fishing villages, modernization of fishing facilities was a major program; and lastly in 1,953 mountain villages, projects for the development of forest resources were undertaken. Of course, the village development plan on the basis of geographical conditions was part of the long-term development plan.

### (5) Higher Income and Higher Agricultural Productivity

Ever since it was launched in 1970, the Saemaul Undong successfully fulfilled its initial experimental programs and it was established on a solid foundation by the middle of the 1970s. By that time, the movement had concentrated mainly on income-generating business projects and programs to raise the self-reliance posture of rural villages. Income-generating programs mainly consisted of those for forming the main producing area of economical crops, improved distribution of farm produces, expansion of farm produces processing facilities, and forestation. In order to help build self-sufficient villages, special emphasis was put on the cultivation of a self-help spirit of the farming population and the establishment of an independent development system.

### (6) Community Development and Characterization

By the middle of the 1970s, the rural Saemaul Undong embarked


--- (p. 695) ---

## V. The Saemaul Undong in the City, Factory, and School

Upon new village infrastructure renovation programs based on past achievements, which involved the modernization of farmhouses and their surroundings, which had been carried out at random. The old villages were reshaped in such a way as to help modernization of agricultural and fishing villages, mechanization of farming, and cooperative farming. And in order to develop rural areas according to their characteristics and to increase side income sources of farmhouses, Saemaul factories were distributed to different rural areas. We have briefly traced the development of the rural Saemaul Undong. It may be safe to say that program planning and actions taken, which considered not only the characteristics and level of development of rural villages but also the ability of the farming and fishing population, together with correct judgment on given circumstances and situations, made it possible to achieve the remarkable success of the rural Saemaul Undong, though there were some trial and errors in setting up the program goals and a planning-action system.

### (1) The industrial development in urban areas in the 1960s and the

consequent growth shock necessitated the rural Saemaul Undong, which was launched under the slogan of the parallel advance of agriculture and industry. Now, since the Saemaul Undong in rural areas have become established on a solid basis, producing remarkable results, the movement has in turn ushered in the Saemaul Undong in the cities, enterprises, and schools. In view of the fact that the Saemaul movement was a spiritual support which made possible the prosperity of the 1970s, it is widely believed that the movement will provide the essential driving force to build a democratic welfare state and to realize social justice in the 1980s. The urban Saemaul Undong, in its first stage, embarked upon


--- (p. 696) ---

various projects in four different places: jobsite, local district, home, and school, with the motto, “diligence, frugality, neighborhood association, and cooperation.” The movement was successful in programs for urban environment improvement, Saemaul job-producing programs, and education programs for citizens. In its later stage, the urban Saemaul movement helped not only to establish a sound sense of value based on urbanite’s morality and public good, but also to build up a philosophy of life on the basis of principles and public morals. Various actions were taken to establish an orderly, pure, and dignified urban environment. For example, there were enlightenment efforts to persuade people to obey traffic rules, to pick up waste paper, to use refined language, and to observe good manners. To infuse the Saemaul spirit in citizens, voluntary participation in the movement by business organizations and other groups was greatly encouraged. Whether by holding meetings of neighborhood associations, or by launching campaigns for orderly streets, fair business dealings, public morality, and ethics, the urban Saemaul Undong led the way in social purification. Through the so-called “three order campaigns” for ① an environmentally pure city, ② a physically orderly city, and ③ a spiritually dignified city, the urban Saemaul Undong was placed on a solid foundation.

### (2) In 1980, the emphasis shifted from the three order campaigns to

“three civic campaigns,” whose goals are ① to habituate economy in spending, ② to cultivate a law-abiding spirit, and ③ to get accustomed to cooperation within the neighborhood. These campaigns cast a good reflection of ① a strong will to actively cope with business depression mainly caused by the second oil shock, ② the absolute necessity to reestablish social discipline utterly relaxed following President Park’s assassination on October 26, 1979, and ③ the importance of extending a helping hand and loving care to our poor neighbors. The factory Saemaul Undong was launched just after the first oil shock near the end of 1973, which dealt a most serious blow to Korean businesses on their way to rapid development.


--- (p. 697) ---

## V. The Saemaul Undong in the City, Factory, and School

The factory Saemaul Undong, which started under these unfavorable conditions, was actively carried on to re-arm with the Saemaul spirit the employees who were deeply discouraged by business recession, to cope with the recession, and to overhaul business management systems, under the slogan, “Save materials,” “Energy conservation,” “Better quality of produce,” and “Higher productivity.” The action center of the factory Saemaul Undong was established by the government. The Saemaul Undong of member enterprises of four economic bodies including the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, concentrated its efforts on planning, investigation, guidance, publicity, and education, successfully performing its functions at its stage of self-help and development. The outstanding program at the stage was the “working place as second home” movement under the slogan, “Treat the employee as one member of your family; do your job just as your private business.” The movement contributed to better relations between labor and management through giving joint birthday parties and operating bride school for employees; and helped to achieve higher productivity.

### (3) The second oil shock and the Y.H. Trade Company labor strike

which was one of the greatest domestic issues in 1979, drove home to the government the importance of the factory Saemaul Undong once again. At the early stage of capitalism, the relations between labor and management were taken to be antagonistic, but now at its stage of maturity, it is an indisputable truth that their relations should be improved into cooperative relations through mutual understanding and dialogue. Above all, on its spiritual side, the factory Saemaul Undong helped to establish the cooperative basis of joint management by working out the Korean version of business ethics; on the institutional side, it helped to improve the channel of dialogue and consultation by setting up a joint labor-management conference system; and as its future-oriented projects, it is undertaking various programs to ensure employees higher income by introducing Saemaul funds, joint commodity purchase and sale system and other Saemaul programs.


--- (p. 698) ---

### (4) The school Saemaul movement has been carried on as a form of

Saemaul education in that Saemaul as a whole cannot be perpetuated as a nation-wide campaign without educational support such as spiritual enlightenment and reformation. That is why the Ministry of Education has steadily carried on Saemaul education so that the whole Saemaul movement might be supported by education and the educational effect might extend to homes, local inhabitants, and the whole nation. Saemaul education has made steady progress. It found its way out of its disarrangement at its inception to its settled phase, insuring substantiality not only in school education but also in education of people for higher income and mental culture. Saemaul education made its way into education promotion policies in the form of promotion of living education, cultivation of cooperation and esprit de corps, building of the local community school, or socialization of education. In 1973, Saemaul education became one of the five policies for the promotion of education, representing a very important part of educational activities. The Saemaul movement, which started in the form of a rural Saemaul movement to build up affluent rural villages, has expanded its base until it comprises the urban Saemaul movement, the factory Saemaul movement, and finally the school Saemaul movement. In other words, the movement has empirically proved the fact that where there is wisdom and sagacity of our people, there can be launched the Saemaul movement; and it taught us the basic principles of national development. National development should be a balanced one comprising not only economic growth but also social and cultural development. Such development is possible only when preceded by modernization of human resources. In other words, national modernization programs can be successfully carried out only on the basis of reformation of people’s way of thinking. It is comparable to a high building built on a solid foundation. That is why we are not envious of Japanese modernization. It deserves


--- (p. 699) ---

<5忌5 special note that many foreigners who visit Korea are impressed not by the remarkable economic growth we made during the past one decade, but by the Saemaul spirit with which every citizen is armed. At this point in time when we are pushing our way toward national development, the tasks we have to take upon ourselves are: ① to get rid of poverty, to build a nation in which both rural and urban populations live in affluence, ② to establish national discipline by eliminating injustice and absurdities, and ③ to achieve peaceful national reunification by consolidating the basis of freedom and democracy. The Saemaul movement is believed to facilitate these tasks to a great extent. In that conviction, the Saemaul movement in urban areas, factories, and schools is moving in earnest toward its final goal, the building of a democratic welfare state.

### (1) Saemaul education has both general and historic characteristics.

Just as the education of any nation is influenced by historical and social circumstances, Saemaul education is no exception. Let us take a look at the general characteristics of Saemaul education. One of its most notable characteristics is that it involves every citizen from the president down to the grass-roots of society. Primarily, every Korean citizen is called on to participate in the Saemaul education program regardless of differences in occupation, sex, age, region, religion, or station in life, and is closely linked with both school and out-of-school education. It takes on a social context in school education by cultivating local and national patriotism through integrated studies in the form of social activities, field studies, etc. It can be considered as a life-long education since every citizen, including parents of students, participate in Saemaul education, which features a continuing all-time education in the all-social, all-regional, and all-class aspects. Secondly, we see it as an effort to revolutionize the human consciousness through arming it with the Saemaul spirit.


--- (p. 700) ---

It is essential and only natural that Saemaul education initially is conceived as a means to a “better life,” to create a new person, or at least a modern man out of a traditional and poor farmer or urban laborer. The term “new man” must be defined in relation to both historical and social aspects in view of our reality. The “new man” can be visualized when it stands at the juncture of time and space. It prescribes a profound patriotic sentiment, spirit of national security, implanting democracy in the soil of Korea, historical consciousness of subjecthood, establishment of national ethics, and the creation of modern man indigenous to the Korean idea. These can be considered urgent historical problems in Korea’s present circumstances, and they are closely related with spiritual education. The Saemaul spirit is a practical philosophy designed to express and practice the ideals of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. Within the Saemaul spirit, the problems of education must be solved in realization that the poverty of the past originated from the lack of a spiritual posture of diligence, self-help, and cooperation. These negative elements cannot serve to contribute to the solution of current social problems facing the nation. It is only feasible when all of our people are armed with the Saemaul spirit. Lastly, Saemaul education focuses on technical training. It is well-known that modern society is in an age of technical renovation. It is said that the social change of a year today is comparable to that of one thousand years in the past. Therefore, it is clear that it is impossible to build an affluent society, overcome abject poverty, and increase income without adequate agricultural management or construction techniques. Henceforth, the features of Saemaul education have been on harmonious development of intelligence, virtue, fitness, and techniques separate from those having general education characteristics. It is only common knowledge then that Saemaul education should give priority to technical training in view of the fact that the realization of industrial development, environmental improvement, public


--- (p. 701) ---

### (2) Let us examine the meaning of Saemaul education.

Firstly, Korea’s social education had been isolated for a long time due to rural stagnation and industrial backwardness. It underwent a slight, if not moderate, change towards the end of the 19th century when a group of people conscious of nationalism and a save-the-nation drive rather than a charity motivation launched an unsystematic, unplanned, manual labor industrial style program. It retained its vulnerability, however, under the circumstances of near lack of educational financing or policy vision. However, Saemaul education, in complete contrast to the past in regards to inculcation, is an organized and planned social education for every citizen. This can be construed as the creation of Korea’s life-long education in connection with the idea sponsored by UNESCO since 1965.

Secondly, we can point out wide-ranging educational objectives as another aspect of Saemaul education. One of the most universal aspects is the decision to involve everyone from students on up to ministers, deputy ministers, officials of every grade, university presidents and deans, professors, lawmakers, judges, prosecutors, business executives, employees, journalists, peasants, housewives, and people from all sectors of society. This resulted in the education of 28,571,700 persons as of the end of 1979 and financing over 1.94 billion won. This mass social education is unprecedented in history, and it is by no means exaggerated that it is substantially nationwide.

Thirdly, the educational contents and methods of Saemaul education are very characteristic. Spiritual education is common to all cooperative leaders, professors, and village women leaders, given at the same time, same place, with the same contents, and by the same instructors. It is not intellectual nor highbrow instruction, but is living and practical based upon everyday experience. Most characteristic is the “success cases,” and the heroes are the


--- (p. 702) ---

The sons and daughters of modest people in general, and they are usually not well-educated, nor high ranked or well-to-do. Their lifestyle is extraordinary. Voluntarily participating in the Saemaul education, motivated by their own desire for a better life and self-consciousness, they present cases of how they had overcome innumerable hardships for themselves and thereby moving the people who listen to their noble experiences with deep sentiment and who can hardly control the tears welling up, and thus leading them to reflect on their own lives. It rises above rank, intellect, or occupation, and it is a specific method of all-human education.

Fourthly, the independent form of Saemaul education is effective and characteristic, and it is noteworthy that the process of the Saemaul movement itself serves as an educational process. Villagers have established a discussion program among themselves with a village leader as a pivot where they discuss the village affairs, small or large, and have cultivated democratic discipline and consciousness concerning responsibilities while solving their own problems. We might also add the following factors as the results of Saemaul education: self-confidence that “we can make it, too,” a scientific processing method, ability to draw a line between public and private matters, a sense of accomplishment, a coordinating spirit of unity, and a spirit of sacrifice in terms of an educational system.

Fifthly, Saemaul education is not an idle, ideological education, but an education supported by demonstrative, material evidence such as income increase and environmental betterment. The traditional Confucian school of the Yi dynasty was a private, voluntary institution that served as a source for the establishment of Confucian ethics. It also cannot be neglected that the night school or enlightenment movement during Japanese rule played an important role in terms of educational value. Although education in the past could attach “head and heart” to the original meaning of education, it failed to give a “hand” to it. It is very sagacious that Saemaul education regarded technological education as a part of it, and in view of this, the ideas on the organization of a technical corps is very characteristic.


--- (p. 703) ---

and also unprecedented. Sixthly, it is highly noteworthy that the Saemaul movement placed emphasis on leaders' training in addition to nationwide and all-social education and that it purported to consolidate the “work unit” such as the occupation-unit or rank-unit along with it. It must also be highly assessed that when specialty is liable to be disregarded according as universality is emphasized, Saemaul education is duly heedful of this respect.

### (3) Let us enumerate the results of Saemaul education. Firstly, Saemaul education launched a structural innovation of consciousness, and enabled people to conceive the self-confidence that "We can make it, too." Secondly, Saemaul education is fully justified by the decisive factor that spiritual elements support all material, demonstrative changes. Thirdly, Saemaul education made an effort to achieve a consolidated integrity of technological and workshop education apart from ideology so that it could stimulate the strong will of accomplishment on the part of the people as a working factor for realizing a popular income increase. Fourthly, Saemaul education greatly contributed to the establishment of Korean democracy indigenous to its soil and economic construction, since it has been pragmatically oriented. Fifthly, it is only natural, therefore, that Saemaul education put emphasis on educating people who are able to become Saemaul leaders in order to perpetuate the Saemaul movement. Saemaul education is in its takeoff stage of ignition, and is taking form in a way indigenous to the Korean soil. It is not without trials and errors, or without problems in its pathway to cope with. But it is valuable for us to cherish with self-confidence that Korea has a promising future, as long as we keep on reflecting on ourselves, correcting errors and rounding off the movement.

## VII. Results of Promotion Projects for Productive Bases

### (1) Basic Promotion Projects for Agricultural Production


--- (p. 704) ---

6. One of the major factors responsible in large part for the slow development of both rural and fishing villages in some areas was the limitation and low productivity due to a poorly established productive base. For that very reason, from our point of view, it is most urgent and significant that something be done to stimulate this relatively stagnant sector by conceiving rural development programs on the basis of a productive promotion project. This project is designed to stimulate villagers into improving their living surroundings and boosting their incomes with the spirit of furthering extensive production per unit farming area, and to be instrumental in drastically raising the productive level, and recruiting lesser labor power and expenditures through modernized management. The government has thus far conceived and launched the project in the following sectors:

1. Irrigation development in coping with natural calamities
2. Integrated macro-unit agricultural development projects in four river basins along respective watersheds
3. Farm area renewal and drainage improvement for the betterment of agricultural mechanization
4. Controlling of urbanization envisaged by economic development and utilization of farming areas for other purposes caused by industrialization, along with work on extending farming areas through reclamation of wasteland and drainage on a larger scale

The nationwide agricultural water facilities amount to 72,000, benefiting 1,121,000 ha of farmland, thus covering 85 per cent of a total of 1,312,000 ha of rice paddy fields as of the end of 1978. The integrated macro-unit agricultural development project saw the completion of its initial stages in the Keum River, Pyongtaek, Kyongju areas, Keihwado Island, and in the Yongsan River as of the end of 1979. The cost to the government was 153.9 billion won, and an area of 69,000 ha was developed. This unprecedented beneficence on the part of villagers was greeted with the results of an extension of farming area reaching 110,000 ha, and farm renewal of 23,000 ha. The value of the project was the increase of food production of


--- (p. 705) ---

### (1) Results of Promotion Projects for Productive Bases

The project enabled the cultivation of approximately 135,000 suk (1 suk = 0.0001 ha) through the supply of agricultural water to an area of 82,000 ha. Indirect results of the project include a shift in farmers' consciousness towards positive and scientific agricultural management. The government thus facilitated the human and material growth of the respective areas and promoted community urbanization by fostering local tourism. The agricultural field renewal project cost the government 1.035 trillion won and achieved the renewal of 173,000 ha during the period of 1972 through 1979, completing the renewal of 322,000 ha, corresponding to 54.8 percent of the target area of 588,000 ha. The direct results of the project are increased productivity through a high ratio of land utilization and a reduction in production costs through decreased labor. The indirect results, on the other hand, include increased income for the farming populace aside from farming activities, through increased employment opportunities during the project period, as well as the preservation of agricultural land and visual improvements.

### (2) Basic Promotion Project for Fisheries Production

Frequent natural calamities left fishing villages devastated and hopeless, with people despondent over their cruel fate. This was largely due to the lack of basic, adequate facilities on boats and at fishing ports. However, the Saemaul movement in the fishing villages addressed and overcame these problems by motivating a spirit of mutual help rooted in the nation’s traditional ways of doing things and thinking, and by establishing a system of interdependent loans known as “Ke,” thus helping people refuse to submit to the inevitable and the challenges of nature. The Saemaul movement in fishing villages is characterized by the following four sectors:

1. Production basis
2. Income generation/growth
3. Welfare surroundings
4. Spiritual enlightenment

The production basis consists of projects such as the improvement of


--- (p. 706) ---

6^2 fishing ports, cooperative fishing boat construction, and the basic establishment of a fishing village interdependent loan system. From 1972, marking the year of the inception of the fishing village Saemaul movement, through 1979, out of a total expenditure for projects amounting to 25.9 billion won, including that of fishermen, 16.2 billion won, or 63 per cent of the total, was spent for income growth, and 5 billion won, 19 per cent of the total, in the sector of production. The fishing port improvement project which continued from 1975 through 1979, with a total expenditure of 9,440 million won, repaired 8,361 meters of breakwaters of ports. Cooperative construction of fishing boats including cooperative operation, cost the government 1.6 billion won, resulting in the construction of 42 new fishing boats. The basic production facilities project promoted by fishers’ interdependent loans, includes repair work on ferry and loading piers, simple processing and quick repair services. From 1972 through 1979, the project launched the construction of 418 ferries, 114 quays, 66 loading docks, 50 simple processing plants, 43 breakwaters, 36 commission sales facilities, and 114 other facilities with an investment of 6 billion won.

### (3) Saemaul Improvement Project

The Saemaul improvement project in itself is one of the fundamental works, and is characterized by the promotion of productive bases, income increase, and improvement of village surroundings. The Saemaul improvement project, in connection with the basic promotion of agricultural production, includes forming common compost piles, communal working areas, common stalls, construction of warehouses, repairing riverlets, bridges, and extension of intra-village roads. The project began in a modest fashion and covered infrastructure and income generating programs, selecting long desired projects first. In light of this, the Saemaul improvement project played a pivotal role in the Saemaul movement. This has resulted in the overly successful construction of intra-village roads by 65 per cent.


--- (p. 707) ---

Bridge construction reached 94 percent of its original goal, construction of communal warehouses, common compost piles, riverlet damage repairs, over 50 percent respectively, bringing about at the same time new community consciousness, diligence, self-help, and an idealistic environment. Villagers experienced high morale not to be likened to material reward through the movement, and this kind of example is by no means unique. Thousands of comparable cases demonstrate a degree of change as great as any brought about by any nation in the world.

### ⑷ Improvement Project for Cooperative Spheres

Improvement projects for cooperative spheres exemplify communal improvement of the intra-village environment and production bases. The project for promotion of production bases is categorized into the construction of roads, bridges, management of rivers, establishment of communal warehouses, and common workplaces. In its initial stage, the Saemaul movement began with small-scale projects and achieved as a whole more than expected. Thus, it dramatized and highlighted a period that we expect would lead to more ambitious projects. The difference between the Saemaul improvement project and that of the cooperative sphere lies within their individual scope; the former, an individual village as a unit, and the latter, the intra-village as a unit. Neighboring villages, therefore, when they have a common interest, launch relatively large-scale, long-desired projects, such as main intra-village thoroughfares and irrigation facilities. The most important of all among cooperative sphere projects was to maintain intra-village roads in good condition and to open up new roads in view of the fact that they have, with no exception, close relations in labor productivity. Secondly, constructing new roads and bridges were essential since it contributed to the speeding up of the movement of production materials and agricultural and livestock produce. The government financed 2.1 billion won during the period 1974 through 1979 for works in the cooperative sphere, which resulted in 1,007 cases of success in 836 spheres throughout the nation.


--- (p. 708) ---

### (1) Innovation of Living Style

① Progress in the "Revolution with Rising Expectation" and Spiritual Enlightenment. The most characteristic aspect of the Saemaul Undong has been noted as a substantial innovation of the farmers’ conscious structure, the so-called “The Revolution of Rising Expectations”. Through this, they experienced the surprising power of effective energy, of principle, and cooperative work and effective activities through environmental betterment such as extension of intra-village roads and fence mending. They came to realize that it was they who were to blame that they were poor, and that it was feasible for them to work in harmony under the slogans that “We can make it, too” and “we can live a better life through cooperation,” cherishing self-confidence, aspirations and expectations. It is analyzed that the "Revolution of Rising Expectations" was mainly led by low-educated farmers rather than the high-educated and became floriferous rapidly. And the continuous rising of expectation brought about the demand for liberation from the incurring shortage of supply, and there occurred a broader gap between aspirations and realizations, thus inviting mounting dissent and disbelief in the society. Furthermore, the better life movement or income growth movement was overrated in terms of quantitative and material growth, so it cannot be denied that it aggravated the fever of mammonism among farmers. There emerged therefore the task of renaissance of a national spirit of erasing out excessive expectation and aspirations and also, stamping out spiritual poverty.

② Rationalization of Consumptive Life and Savings Increase. The Saemaul Undong brought about great change in the rural life pattern and moral through the positive participation of the rural people, especially women, in the movement and through spiritual enlightenment drive.
